    blob_collection: &str,
    episodes_collection: &str,
) -> Result<()> {
    std::env::set_var("COGNITIVE_MCP_QDRANT_URL", url);
    std::env::set_var("COGNITIVE_MCP_USER_MEMORY_COLLECTION", memory_collection);
    std::env::set_var("COGNITIVE_MCP_BLOB_VECTORS_COLLECTION", blob_collection);
    std::env::set_var("COGNITIVE_MCP_QDRANT_COLLECTION", episodes_collection);

    let shuttle = QdrantSemanticShuttle::new()
        .await
        .context("QdrantSemanticShuttle::new() failed")?;

    // ── 1. Voyage vectorization ──────────────────────────────────────────
    let ovs_doc = "The rovs plugin drives Open vSwitch natively over OVSDB JSON-RPC: \
                   it creates bridges, attaches ports, and installs OpenFlow rules.";
    let mail_doc = "The mail-3tched container runs Postfix and Dovecot, exposing SMTP \
                    submission on 587 and IMAPS on 993 for mailbox delivery.";

    let ovs_vector = shuttle
        .embed_document(ovs_doc)
        .await
        .context("Voyage embed_document failed for the OVS document")?;
    let mail_vector = shuttle
        .embed_document(mail_doc)
        .await
        .context("Voyage embed_document failed for the mail document")?;

    assert_eq!(
        ovs_vector.len(),
        PROBE_DIMS as usize,
        "Voyage returned {} dims, expected the shared-space {PROBE_DIMS}",
        ovs_vector.len()
    );
    assert_eq!(mail_vector.len(), PROBE_DIMS as usize);
    let norm = ovs_vector.iter().map(|v| v * v).sum::<f32>().sqrt();
    assert!(
        norm > 0.5,
        "Voyage embedding looks degenerate (L2 norm {norm})"
    );
    println!("embed: 2 documents vectorized, {PROBE_DIMS} dims, L2 norm {norm:.4}");

    // ── 2. Qdrant upsert ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
    let container_id = format!("e2e-container-{}", uuid::Uuid::new_v4().simple());
    let ovs_point = uuid::Uuid::new_v4().to_string();
    let mail_point = uuid::Uuid::new_v4().to_string();

    shuttle
        .upsert_user_memory(&ovs_point, ovs_vector, &container_id, "ovs-note", ovs_doc)
        .await
        .context("upsert_user_memory failed for the OVS vector")?;
    shuttle
        .upsert_user_memory(
            &mail_point,
            mail_vector,
            &container_id,
            "mail-note",
            mail_doc,
        )
        .await
        .context("upsert_user_memory failed for the mail vector")?;
    println!("upsert: 2 points written to {memory_collection}");

    // ── 3. Query-side embedding + scoped semantic search ─────────────────
    let query_vector = shuttle
        .embed_query_text("how do I add a port to an Open vSwitch bridge?")
        .await
        .context("Voyage embed_query_text failed")?;
    assert_eq!(query_vector.len(), PROBE_DIMS as usize);

    let hits = shuttle
        .search_user_memory(query_vector, &container_id, 5)
        .await
        .context("search_user_memory failed")?;

    assert!(
        !hits.is_empty(),
        "scoped search returned nothing for container {container_id}"
    );
    let top = &hits[0];
    let top_key = top
        .payload
        .get("entry_key")
        .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
        .cloned()
        .unwrap_or_default();
    println!(
        "search: {} hits, top entry_key={top_key} score={:.4}",
        hits.len(),
        top.score
    );
    assert_eq!(
        top_key, "ovs-note",
        "OVS query ranked '{top_key}' first — vectors and payloads are misaligned"
    );
    assert!(
        top.score > 0.3,
        "top cosine score {} is implausibly low for a matching document",
        top.score
    );

    // Container scoping must exclude other containers' memory.
    let other_query = shuttle.embed_query_text("open vswitch bridge").await?;
    let leaked = shuttle
        .search_user_memory(other_query, "e2e-container-does-not-exist", 5)
        .await
        .context("scoped search for an unknown container failed")?;
    assert!(
        leaked.is_empty(),
        "container_id filter leaked {} points across containers",
        leaked.len()
    );

    // ── 4. blob_vectors refresh over the SHM sealed-blob catalog ─────────
    match op_blob::catalog::read_manifest_plugin_ids_shm() {
        Some(ids) if !ids.is_empty() => {
            let started = std::time::Instant::now();
            let summary = shuttle
                .refresh_blob_vectors()
                .await
                .context("refresh_blob_vectors failed")?;
            println!(
                "refresh: {} of {} catalog plugins embedded into {} in {:.1}s",
                summary.embedded,
                ids.len(),
                summary.collection,
                started.elapsed().as_secs_f64()
            );
            assert_eq!(summary.collection, blob_collection);
            assert!(
                summary.embedded > 0,
                "SHM catalog listed {} plugins but nothing was embedded",
                ids.len()
            );

            let results = shuttle
                .search_blob_vectors("open vswitch bridge ports configured over OVSDB", 5)
                .await
                .context("search_blob_vectors failed")?;
            assert!(
                !results.is_empty(),
                "blob_vectors search returned no plugins after embedding {} of them",
                summary.embedded
            );
            for point in &results {
                let plugin_id = point
                    .payload
                    .get("plugin_id")
                    .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
                    .cloned()
                    .unwrap_or_default();
                assert!(
                    !plugin_id.is_empty(),
                    "blob_vectors point is missing its plugin_id payload"
                );
                println!("  blob hit: {plugin_id} score={:.4}", point.score);
            }
        }
        _ => eprintln!("SKIP blob_vectors refresh: no SHM sealed-blob catalog on this host"),
    }

    Ok(())
}
</file>

<file path="op-cognitive-mcp/build.rs">
fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let proto_file = "proto/cognitive.proto";

    tonic_build::configure()
        .build_server(true)
        .build_client(true)
        .file_descriptor_set_path(
            std::path::PathBuf::from(std::env::var("OUT_DIR")?).join("cognitive_descriptor.bin"),
        )
        .compile_protos(&[proto_file], &["proto/"])?;

    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={}", proto_file);
    Ok(())
}
</file>

## Purpose

`op-cognitive-mcp` exposes code-aware retrieval over the Qdrant/Voyage indexes
used by local coding clients. Retrieval is intentionally split by embedding
space:

- Rust solo: `rust_lang_rust_lsp_voyage_code_3`, queried with `voyage-code-3`
  when `COGNITIVE_MCP_VOYAGE_MODEL=voyage-code-3`.
- Other LSP/spec groups: `repos_lsp_*_voyage_4_lite` and
  `repos_specs_docs_voyage_4_lite`, queried with the Voyage 4 family. These
  default to `voyage-4` at query time and are compatible with
  `voyage-4-lite` indexes.

For context-aware completion, the MCP path should ask Kiro/LSP for exact local
symbol and hover context first, then call `code_context` with
`retrieval_mode="completion"`. Completion retrieval embeds the query once,
queries the compatible configured collections, returns top-k vector hits, and
does not rerank unless `COGNITIVE_MCP_RERANK_MODE=always`.

Deep chat/edit context can use `retrieval_mode="deep"` with a larger fetch
window. Rerank is only enabled for deep mode when
`COGNITIVE_MCP_RERANK_MODE=auto` or `always`.

### Vector Environment

```sh
COGNITIVE_MCP_VOYAGE_API_KEY=<key>
# Falls back to VOYAGE_API_KEY, then VOYAGE_API_KEY_RUST, then key file.

COGNITIVE_MCP_COMPLETION_COLLECTIONS=repos_lsp_c_cpp_voyage_4_lite,repos_lsp_go_voyage_4_lite,repos_lsp_java_voyage_4_lite,repos_lsp_python_voyage_4_lite,repos_lsp_typescript_voyage_4_lite,repos_specs_docs_voyage_4_lite
COGNITIVE_MCP_RUST_COLLECTION=rust_lang_rust_lsp_voyage_code_3
COGNITIVE_MCP_COMPLETION_TOP_K=12
COGNITIVE_MCP_DEEP_TOP_K=50
COGNITIVE_MCP_RERANK_MODE=auto
COGNITIVE_MCP_KIRO_LSP_STATE_DIR=/home/jeremy/git/logs/kiro-lsp-state
```

//! The Compliance Engine: "The Law Firm"
//! Responsible for validating the PluginSchema against legal and security frameworks.

use serde_json::Value;

/// Strongly-typed error for compliance validation operations.
///
/// Keeps `anyhow` out of the public API surface while preserving
/// ergonomic `?` propagation inside the crate.
#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum ComplianceError {
    #[error("validation failed: {0}")]
    Validation(String),

    #[error("JSON error: {0}")]
    Json(#[from] serde_json::Error),
}

pub mod attorneys {
    use super::ComplianceError;
    use serde_json::Value;

    /// Olivia Scal: Managing Partner / OSCAL (Open Security Controls Assessment Language)
    pub struct OliviaScal;
    impl OliviaScal {
        pub fn validate_controls(schema: &Value) -> std::result::Result<(), ComplianceError> {
            // Check for security control metadata
            if let Some(caps) = schema.get("capabilities") {
                if caps.get("requires_root").and_then(|v| v.as_bool()) == Some(true) {
                    tracing::warn!("Plugin requires root; OSCAL assessment recommended");
                }
            }
            Ok(())
        }
    }

    /// E.U.gene Risk: EU AI Act Counsel
    pub struct EugeneRisk;
    impl EugeneRisk {
        pub fn validate_ai_risk(schema: &Value) -> std::result::Result<(), ComplianceError> {
            // If it's an AI/ML plugin, check for transparency requirements
            if schema.get("plugin_type").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) == Some("custom") {
                if let Some(meta) = schema.get("schema") {
                    if meta.get("model_name").is_some()
                        && meta.get("training_data_source").is_none()
                    {
                        return Err(ComplianceError::Validation(
                            "EU AI Act violation: Training data source must be declared for models"
                                .into(),
                        ));
                    }
                }
            }
            Ok(())
        }
    }

    /// Penny Privacy: GDPR Engine
    pub struct PennyPrivacy;
    impl PennyPrivacy {
        pub fn validate_privacy(schema: &Value) -> std::result::Result<(), ComplianceError> {
            // Check for PII handling without retention policy
            if let Some(s) = schema.get("schema") {
                let schema_str = s.to_string().to_lowercase();
                if (schema_str.contains("email")
                    || schema_str.contains("user_id")
                    || schema_str.contains("phone"))
                    && !schema_str.contains("retention")
                {
                    return Err(ComplianceError::Validation(
                        "GDPR violation: PII fields detected without retention policy".into(),
                    ));
                }
            }
            Ok(())
        }
    }

    /// Reggie O.P.A.: Cloud Prosecutor
    pub struct ReggieOpa;
    impl ReggieOpa {
        pub fn validate_policy(schema: &Value) -> std::result::Result<(), ComplianceError> {
            // Basic policy check: Versioning must be present
            if schema.get("version").is_none() {
                return Err(ComplianceError::Validation(
                    "OPA Policy failure: Missing version field".into(),
                ));
            }
            Ok(())
        }
    }
}

pub struct LawFirm;

impl LawFirm {
    /// Review the canonical typed plugin schema. The generated JSON schema is
    /// only a view for the attorney checks; no repository schema file is read.
    pub fn review_plugin_schema(
        schema: &op_state_store::PluginSchema,
    ) -> std::result::Result<(), ComplianceError> {
        let mut v = serde_json::to_value(schema)?;
        v["plugin_type"] = serde_json::Value::String(schema.category.clone());
        v["schema"] = serde_json::to_value(schema.to_json_schema())?;
        Self::validate_structure(&v)?;
        attorneys::OliviaScal::validate_controls(&v)?;
        attorneys::EugeneRisk::validate_ai_risk(&v)?;
        attorneys::PennyPrivacy::validate_privacy(&v)?;
        attorneys::ReggieOpa::validate_policy(&v)?;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub fn review_schema(schema_json: &str) -> std::result::Result<(), ComplianceError> {
        let v: Value = serde_json::from_str(schema_json)?;
        Self::validate_legacy_structure(&v)?;

        // 2. Attorney Reviews
        attorneys::OliviaScal::validate_controls(&v)?;
        attorneys::EugeneRisk::validate_ai_risk(&v)?;
        attorneys::PennyPrivacy::validate_privacy(&v)?;
        attorneys::ReggieOpa::validate_policy(&v)?;

        Ok(())
    }

    fn validate_structure(schema: &Value) -> std::result::Result<(), ComplianceError> {
        let object = schema.as_object().ok_or_else(|| {
            ComplianceError::Validation("Plugin schema must be a JSON object".into())
        })?;
        let name = object
            .get("name")
            .and_then(Value::as_str)
            .unwrap_or_default();
        if name.is_empty() {
            return Err(ComplianceError::Validation(
                "Plugin schema missing required field: name".into(),
            ));
        }
        let version = object
            .get("version")
            .and_then(Value::as_str)
            .unwrap_or_default();
        let valid_version = version.split('.').count() == 3
            && version
                .split('.')
                .all(|part| !part.is_empty() && part.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()));
        if !valid_version {
            return Err(ComplianceError::Validation(format!(
                "Invalid plugin schema version: {version}"
            )));
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Preserve the legacy JSON review contract while its source is migrated
    /// away from the deleted repository meta-schema file.
    fn validate_legacy_structure(schema: &Value) -> std::result::Result<(), ComplianceError> {
        Self::validate_structure(schema)?;
        let object = schema.as_object().expect("validated object");
        let name = object["name"].as_str().unwrap();
        if name.len() > 64
            || name.is_empty()
            || !name
                .chars()
                .all(|c| c.is_ascii_lowercase() || c.is_ascii_digit() || c == '_' || c == '-')
        {
            return Err(ComplianceError::Validation(
                "Invalid plugin schema name".into(),
            ));
        }
        let plugin_type = object
            .get("plugin_type")
            .and_then(Value::as_str)
            .ok_or_else(|| ComplianceError::Validation("Missing plugin_type".into()))?;
        if !matches!(
            plugin_type,
            "service" | "network" | "storage" | "system" | "custom"
        ) {
            return Err(ComplianceError::Validation("Invalid plugin_type".into()));
        }
        if let Some(caps) = object.get("capabilities") {
            let caps = caps.as_object().ok_or_else(|| {
                ComplianceError::Validation("capabilities must be an object".into())
            })?;
            for (key, value) in caps {
                if matches!(
                    key.as_str(),
                    "can_read"
                        | "can_write"
                        | "can_delete"
                        | "supports_rollback"
                        | "supports_checkpoints"
                        | "requires_root"
                ) && !value.is_boolean()
                {
                    return Err(ComplianceError::Validation(
                        "Invalid capabilities field".into(),
                    ));
                }
            }
        }
        if let Some(dependencies) = object.get("dependencies") {
            let dependencies = dependencies.as_array().ok_or_else(|| {
                ComplianceError::Validation("dependencies must be an array".into())
            })?;
            for dependency in dependencies {
                let dependency = dependency.as_object().ok_or_else(|| {
                    ComplianceError::Validation("dependency must be an object".into())
                })?;
                if dependency.get("name").and_then(Value::as_str).is_none() {
                    return Err(ComplianceError::Validation(
                        "dependency missing name".into(),
                    ));
                }
                for key in ["version", "required"] {
                    if let Some(value) = dependency.get(key) {
                        let valid = (key == "version" && value.is_string())
                            || (key == "required" && value.is_boolean());
                        if !valid {
                            return Err(ComplianceError::Validation(
                                "Invalid dependency field".into(),
                            ));
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        if let Some(plugin_schema) = object.get("schema") {
            if !plugin_schema.is_object() {
                return Err(ComplianceError::Validation(
                    "schema must be an object".into(),
                ));
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use serde_json::json;

    #[test]
    fn test_valid_schema_passes() {
        let schema = json!({
            "name": "test-plugin",
            "version": "1.0.0",
            "plugin_type": "service",
            "capabilities": {
                "can_read": true
            }
        });
        assert!(LawFirm::review_schema(&schema.to_string()).is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_invalid_version_fails() {
        let schema = json!({
            "name": "test-plugin",
            "version": "invalid",
            "plugin_type": "service"
        });
        assert!(LawFirm::review_schema(&schema.to_string()).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn legacy_shape_rules_are_preserved_without_a_meta_schema_file() {
        for (field, value) in [
            ("name", json!("BadName")),
            ("plugin_type", json!("unknown")),
            ("capabilities", json!({"can_read": "yes"})),
            ("dependencies", json!(["not-an-object"])),
            ("schema", json!("not-an-object")),
        ] {
            let mut schema = json!({
                "name": "valid-plugin",
                "version": "1.0.0",
                "plugin_type": "service"
            });
            schema[field] = value;
            assert!(
                LawFirm::review_schema(&schema.to_string()).is_err(),
                "legacy field {field} should be rejected"
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_gdpr_violation() {
        let schema = json!({
            "name": "pii-plugin",
            "version": "1.1.0",
            "plugin_type": "custom",
            "schema": {
                "user_email": "string"
            }
        });
        let result = LawFirm::review_schema(&schema.to_string());
        assert!(result.is_err());
        assert!(result.unwrap_err().to_string().contains("GDPR"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_ai_act_violation() {
        let schema = json!({
            "name": "ai-plugin",
            "version": "2.0.0",
            "plugin_type": "custom",
            "schema": {
                "model_name": "gpt-4"
            }
        });
        let result = LawFirm::review_schema(&schema.to_string());
        assert!(result.is_err());
        assert!(result.unwrap_err().to_string().contains("AI Act"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn typed_plugin_schema_is_reviewed_without_meta_schema_file() {
        let schema = op_state_store::PluginSchema::builder("typed-plugin")
            .version("1.0.0")
            .description("A typed test plugin")
            .build();
        assert!(LawFirm::review_plugin_schema(&schema).is_ok());
    }
}

<file path="op-core/src/config.rs">
//! Environment Configuration Loader
//!
//! Loads environment variables from the canonical location: `/etc/op-dbus/environment`
//! This ensures all op-dbus components share the same configuration.
//!
//! ## Usage
//!
//! Call `load_environment()` early in main() before accessing any config:
//!
//! ```rust
//! use op_core::config::load_environment;
//!
//! fn main() {
//!     load_environment();
//!     // Now all env vars from /etc/op-dbus/environment are available
//! }
//! ```

use std::fs;
use std::path::Path;
use tracing::{debug, info, warn};

/// Canonical D-Bus well-known bus name for the op-dbus system.
///
/// All components (op-dbus-mirror, projection_server, rovs_proxy, etc.)
/// must use this constant instead of hardcoding the string.
pub const OPDBUS_BUS_NAME: &str = "org.opdbus.v1.plugins";

/// Canonical base object path for the projected plugin tree.
///
/// This is the single stable root anchor; plugin leaves live at
/// `{PLUGIN_BASE_PATH}/<plugin_id>` and must be derived from it (or discovered
/// by introspection), never hardcoded with a different spelling. Consumers that
/// only depend on `op-core` use this; `op-plugins` exposes the richer
/// `canonical::plugin_path()` helper built on the same value.
pub const PLUGIN_BASE_PATH: &str = "/org/opdbus/v1/plugins";

/// D-Bus bus name for the op-dbus-mirror service.
///
/// The mirror publishes OVSDB, ObjectManager, and other non-plugin surfaces.
/// It MUST NOT request `OPDBUS_BUS_NAME` — the projection server is the sole
/// owner of that name. Consumers of the mirror's surfaces (OVSDB JSON-RPC,
/// ObjectManager) dial this name instead.
pub const MIRROR_BUS_NAME: &str = "org.opdbus.v1.mirror";

/// Canonical session bus socket path.  No dash — consistent with `opdbus`
/// used in D-Bus names, object paths, and shm directories.
pub const SESSION_BUS_SOCKET_PATH: &str = "/run/opdbus/session-bus.sock";

/// Canonical session bus address string (for `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`).
pub const SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS: &str = "unix:path=/run/opdbus/session-bus.sock";

/// Default path for the environment file
pub const DEFAULT_ENV_FILE: &str = "/etc/op-dbus/environment";

/// Alternative paths to check (in order of priority)
pub const ENV_FILE_PATHS: &[&str] = &["/etc/op-dbus/environment", "/etc/op-dbus.env", ".env"];

/// Load environment variables from the canonical configuration file.
///
/// This function:
/// 1. Checks `/etc/op-dbus/environment` first (system-wide)
/// 2. Falls back to `.env` in current directory (development)
/// 3. Does NOT override existing environment variables
///
/// Returns the path that was loaded, or None if no file was found.
pub fn load_environment() -> Option<String> {
    // Check if a custom path is specified
    if let Ok(custom_path) = std::env::var("OP_ENV_FILE") {
        if let Some(path) = try_load_env_file(&custom_path) {
            return Some(path);
        }
    }

    // Try each path in order
    for path in ENV_FILE_PATHS {
        if let Some(loaded_path) = try_load_env_file(path) {
            return Some(loaded_path);
        }
    }

    debug!("No environment file found, using existing environment");
    None
}

/// Try to load an environment file from the given path.
fn try_load_env_file(path: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let path_obj = Path::new(path);

    if !path_obj.exists() {
        return None;
    }

    match fs::read_to_string(path_obj) {
        Ok(content) => {
            let mut loaded_count = 0;
            let mut skipped_count = 0;

            for line in content.lines() {
                let line = line.trim();

                // Skip comments and empty lines
                if line.is_empty() || line.starts_with('#') {
                    continue;
                }

                // Parse KEY=VALUE
                if let Some((key, value)) = parse_env_line(line) {
                    // Don't override existing environment variables
                    if std::env::var(&key).is_err() {
                        std::env::set_var(&key, &value);
                        loaded_count += 1;
                        debug!(
                            "Loaded: {}={}",
                            key,
                            if key.contains("KEY")
                                || key.contains("TOKEN")
                                || key.contains("SECRET")
                            {
                                "***"
                            } else {
                                &value
                            }
                        );
                    } else {
                        skipped_count += 1;
                        debug!("Skipped (already set): {}", key);
                    }
                }
            }

            info!(
                "Loaded {} environment variables from {} ({} skipped - already set)",
                loaded_count, path, skipped_count
            );

            Some(path.to_string())
        }
        Err(e) => {
            warn!("Failed to read environment file {}: {}", path, e);
            None
        }
    }
}

/// Parse a single environment line into key-value pair.
fn parse_env_line(line: &str) -> Option<(String, String)> {
    // Handle: KEY=VALUE, KEY="VALUE", KEY='VALUE'
    let mut parts = line.splitn(2, '=');
    let key = parts.next()?.trim();
    let value = parts.next()?.trim();

    if key.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }

    // Remove surrounding quotes
    let value = value
        .strip_prefix('"')
        .and_then(|v| v.strip_suffix('"'))
        .or_else(|| value.strip_prefix('\'').and_then(|v| v.strip_suffix('\'')))
        .unwrap_or(value);

    Some((key.to_string(), value.to_string()))
}

/// Get a configuration value with a default.
pub fn get_config(key: &str, default: &str) -> String {
    std::env::var(key).unwrap_or_else(|_| default.to_string())
}

/// Get an optional configuration value.
pub fn get_config_opt(key: &str) -> Option<String> {
    std::env::var(key).ok().filter(|v| !v.is_empty())
}

/// Get a boolean configuration value.
pub fn get_config_bool(key: &str, default: bool) -> bool {
    std::env::var(key)
        .map(|v| matches!(v.to_lowercase().as_str(), "true" | "1" | "yes" | "on"))
        .unwrap_or(default)
}

/// Get an integer configuration value.
pub fn get_config_int(key: &str, default: i64) -> i64 {
    std::env::var(key)
        .ok()
        .and_then(|v| v.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(default)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn test_parse_env_line_simple() {
        let (k, v) = parse_env_line("FOO=bar").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(k, "FOO");
        assert_eq!(v, "bar");
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_parse_env_line_quoted() {
        let (k, v) = parse_env_line("FOO=\"bar baz\"").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(k, "FOO");
        assert_eq!(v, "bar baz");
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_parse_env_line_single_quoted() {
        let (k, v) = parse_env_line("FOO='bar'").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(k, "FOO");
        assert_eq!(v, "bar");
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_parse_env_line_empty() {
        assert!(parse_env_line("").is_none());
        assert!(parse_env_line("=value").is_none());
    }
}

<file path="op-core/src/error.rs">
//! Error types for op-dbus-v2

use thiserror::Error;

/// Main error type for op-dbus operations
#[derive(Error, Debug)]
pub enum Error {
    #[error("DBus error: {0}")]
    Dbus(#[from] zbus::Error),

    #[error("DBus FDO error: {0}")]
    DbusFdo(#[from] zbus::fdo::Error),

    #[error("Connection error: {0}")]
    Connection(String),

    #[error("Introspection error: {0}")]
    Introspection(String),

    #[error("Tool execution error: {0}")]
    ToolExecution(String),

    #[error("Plugin error: {0}")]
    Plugin(String),

    #[error("Agent error: {0}")]
    Agent(String),

    #[error("Serialization error: {0}")]
    Serialization(#[from] simd_json::Error),

    #[error("IO error: {0}")]
    Io(#[from] std::io::Error),

    #[error("Timeout: {0}")]
    Timeout(String),

    #[error("Not found: {0}")]
    NotFound(String),

    #[error("Invalid argument: {0}")]
    InvalidArgument(String),

    #[error("Permission denied: {0}")]
    PermissionDenied(String),

    #[error("Internal error: {0}")]
    Internal(String),
}

/// Result type alias using our Error type
pub type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, Error>;

impl Error {
    /// Create a connection error
    pub fn connection(msg: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Error::Connection(msg.into())
    }

    /// Create an introspection error
    pub fn introspection(msg: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Error::Introspection(msg.into())
    }

    /// Create a tool execution error
    pub fn tool_execution(msg: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Error::ToolExecution(msg.into())
    }

    /// Create a plugin error
    pub fn plugin(msg: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Error::Plugin(msg.into())
    }

    /// Create an agent error
    pub fn agent(msg: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Error::Agent(msg.into())
    }

    /// Create a not found error
    pub fn not_found(msg: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Error::NotFound(msg.into())
    }

    /// Create an internal error
    pub fn internal(msg: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Error::Internal(msg.into())
    }
}

impl From<anyhow::Error> for Error {
    fn from(err: anyhow::Error) -> Self {
        Error::Internal(err.to_string())
    }
}
</file>

//! Execution Tracking for Tool and Agent Operations
//!
//! Provides accountability and audit trail for all tool executions.

use chrono::{DateTime, Utc};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::sync::Arc;
use tokio::sync::RwLock;
use uuid::Uuid;

/// Execution status
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum ExecutionStatus {
    /// Request received, not yet started
    Pending,
    /// Currently executing
    Running,
    /// Completed successfully
    Completed,
    /// Failed with error
    Failed,
    /// Cancelled by user or system
    Cancelled,
    /// Timed out
    Timeout,
}

/// Record of a single tool/agent execution
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ExecutionRecord {
    /// Unique execution ID
    pub id: String,
    /// Trace ID for correlation across systems
    pub trace_id: String,
    /// Tool or agent name
    pub tool_name: String,
    /// Input arguments (sanitized)
    pub input_summary: Option<simd_json::OwnedValue>,
    /// Execution status
    pub status: ExecutionStatus,
    /// Start time
    pub started_at: DateTime<Utc>,
    /// End time (if completed)
    pub ended_at: Option<DateTime<Utc>>,
    /// Duration in milliseconds
    pub duration_ms: Option<u64>,
    /// Output summary (truncated if large)
    pub output_summary: Option<String>,
    /// Error message if failed
    pub error: Option<String>,
    /// Whether execution was successful
    pub success: bool,
    /// User/session that initiated execution
    pub initiated_by: Option<String>,
    /// Additional metadata
    pub metadata: HashMap<String, String>,
}

impl ExecutionRecord {
    /// Create a new execution record
    pub fn new(tool_name: &str, trace_id: Option<String>) -> Self {
        let id = Uuid::new_v4().to_string();
        Self {
            id: id.clone(),
            trace_id: trace_id.unwrap_or_else(|| id.clone()),
            tool_name: tool_name.to_string(),
            input_summary: None,
            status: ExecutionStatus::Pending,
            started_at: Utc::now(),
            ended_at: None,
            duration_ms: None,
            output_summary: None,
            error: None,
            success: false,
            initiated_by: None,
            metadata: HashMap::new(),
        }
    }

    /// Mark as running
    pub fn start(&mut self) {
        self.status = ExecutionStatus::Running;
        self.started_at = Utc::now();
    }

    /// Mark as completed successfully
    pub fn complete(&mut self, output: Option<String>) {
        let now = Utc::now();
        self.ended_at = Some(now);
        self.duration_ms = Some((now - self.started_at).num_milliseconds().max(0) as u64);
        self.status = ExecutionStatus::Completed;
        self.success = true;
        self.output_summary = output.map(|s| truncate_string(&s, 1000));
    }

    /// Mark as failed
    pub fn fail(&mut self, error: String) {
        let now = Utc::now();
        self.ended_at = Some(now);
        self.duration_ms = Some((now - self.started_at).num_milliseconds().max(0) as u64);
        self.status = ExecutionStatus::Failed;
        self.success = false;
        self.error = Some(error);
    }

    /// Mark as timed out
    pub fn timeout(&mut self) {
        let now = Utc::now();
        self.ended_at = Some(now);
        self.duration_ms = Some((now - self.started_at).num_milliseconds().max(0) as u64);
        self.status = ExecutionStatus::Timeout;
        self.success = false;
        self.error = Some("Execution timed out".to_string());
    }
}

/// Truncate string to max length
fn truncate_string(s: &str, max_len: usize) -> String {
    if s.len() <= max_len {
        s.to_string()
    } else {
        format!("{}... (truncated)", &s[..max_len])
    }
}

/// Execution tracker - maintains history of all executions
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct ExecutionTracker {
    /// Recent executions (ring buffer)
    records: Arc<RwLock<Vec<ExecutionRecord>>>,
    /// Maximum records to keep
    max_records: usize,
    /// Statistics
    stats: Arc<RwLock<ExecutionStats>>,
}

/// Execution statistics
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ExecutionStats {
    pub total_executions: u64,
    pub successful_executions: u64,
    pub failed_executions: u64,
    pub total_duration_ms: u64,
    pub executions_by_tool: HashMap<String, u64>,
    pub failures_by_tool: HashMap<String, u64>,
}

impl ExecutionStats {
    pub fn average_duration_ms(&self) -> f64 {
        if self.total_executions == 0 {
            0.0
        } else {
            self.total_duration_ms as f64 / self.total_executions as f64
        }
    }

    pub fn success_rate(&self) -> f64 {
        if self.total_executions == 0 {
            0.0
        } else {
            self.successful_executions as f64 / self.total_executions as f64 * 100.0
        }
    }
}

impl ExecutionTracker {
    /// Create a new tracker
    pub fn new(max_records: usize) -> Self {
        Self {
            records: Arc::new(RwLock::new(Vec::with_capacity(max_records))),
            max_records,
            stats: Arc::new(RwLock::new(ExecutionStats::default())),
        }
    }

    /// Start tracking a new execution
    pub async fn start_execution(
        &self,
        tool_name: &str,
        input: Option<simd_json::OwnedValue>,
        initiated_by: Option<String>,
    ) -> ExecutionRecord {
        let mut record = ExecutionRecord::new(tool_name, None);
        record.input_summary = input;
        record.initiated_by = initiated_by;
        record.start();

        let mut records = self.records.write().await;
        records.push(record.clone());

        // Trim if over limit
        if records.len() > self.max_records {
            records.remove(0);
        }

        tracing::info!(
            execution_id = %record.id,
            tool = %tool_name,
            "Execution started"
        );

        record
    }

    /// Complete an execution
    pub async fn complete_execution(&self, id: &str, output: Option<String>) {
        let mut records = self.records.write().await;
        if let Some(record) = records.iter_mut().find(|r| r.id == id) {
            record.complete(output);

            // Update stats
            let mut stats = self.stats.write().await;
            stats.total_executions += 1;
            stats.successful_executions += 1;
            if let Some(duration) = record.duration_ms {
                stats.total_duration_ms += duration;
            }
            *stats
                .executions_by_tool
                .entry(record.tool_name.clone())
                .or_insert(0) += 1;

            tracing::info!(
                execution_id = %id,
                tool = %record.tool_name,
                duration_ms = ?record.duration_ms,
                "Execution completed successfully"
            );
        }
    }

    /// Fail an execution
    pub async fn fail_execution(&self, id: &str, error: String) {
        let mut records = self.records.write().await;
        if let Some(record) = records.iter_mut().find(|r| r.id == id) {
            record.fail(error.clone());

            // Update stats
            let mut stats = self.stats.write().await;
            stats.total_executions += 1;
            stats.failed_executions += 1;
            if let Some(duration) = record.duration_ms {
                stats.total_duration_ms += duration;
            }
            *stats
                .executions_by_tool
                .entry(record.tool_name.clone())
                .or_insert(0) += 1;
            *stats
                .failures_by_tool
                .entry(record.tool_name.clone())
                .or_insert(0) += 1;

            tracing::error!(
                execution_id = %id,
                tool = %record.tool_name,
                error = %error,
                "Execution failed"
            );
        }
    }

    /// Get recent executions
    pub async fn get_recent(&self, limit: usize) -> Vec<ExecutionRecord> {
        let records = self.records.read().await;
        records.iter().rev().take(limit).cloned().collect()
    }

    /// Get execution by ID
    pub async fn get_execution(&self, id: &str) -> Option<ExecutionRecord> {
        let records = self.records.read().await;
        records.iter().find(|r| r.id == id).cloned()
    }

    /// Get executions for a specific tool
    pub async fn get_by_tool(&self, tool_name: &str, limit: usize) -> Vec<ExecutionRecord> {
        let records = self.records.read().await;
        records
            .iter()
            .filter(|r| r.tool_name == tool_name)
            .rev()
            .take(limit)
            .cloned()
            .collect()
    }

    /// Get statistics
    pub async fn get_stats(&self) -> ExecutionStats {
        self.stats.read().await.clone()
    }

    /// Get all pending/running executions
    pub async fn get_active(&self) -> Vec<ExecutionRecord> {
        let records = self.records.read().await;
        records
            .iter()
            .filter(|r| {
                r.status == ExecutionStatus::Running || r.status == ExecutionStatus::Pending
            })
            .cloned()
            .collect()
    }
}

impl Default for ExecutionTracker {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new(1000)
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn test_execution_tracking() {
        let tracker = ExecutionTracker::new(100);

        let record = tracker
            .start_execution("test_tool", Some(simd_json::json!({"arg": "value"})), None)
            .await;

        assert_eq!(record.status, ExecutionStatus::Running);
        assert_eq!(record.tool_name, "test_tool");

        tracker
            .complete_execution(&record.id, Some("success output".to_string()))
            .await;

        let completed = tracker.get_execution(&record.id).await.unwrap();
        assert_eq!(completed.status, ExecutionStatus::Completed);
        assert!(completed.success);
        assert!(completed.duration_ms.is_some());
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn test_execution_failure() {
        let tracker = ExecutionTracker::new(100);

        let record = tracker.start_execution("failing_tool", None, None).await;

        tracker
            .fail_execution(&record.id, "Something went wrong".to_string())
            .await;

        let failed = tracker.get_execution(&record.id).await.unwrap();
        assert_eq!(failed.status, ExecutionStatus::Failed);
        assert!(!failed.success);
        assert_eq!(failed.error, Some("Something went wrong".to_string()));
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn test_stats() {
        let tracker = ExecutionTracker::new(100);

        // Successful execution
        let r1 = tracker.start_execution("tool1", None, None).await;
        tracker.complete_execution(&r1.id, None).await;

        // Failed execution
        let r2 = tracker.start_execution("tool2", None, None).await;
        tracker.fail_execution(&r2.id, "error".to_string()).await;

        let stats = tracker.get_stats().await;
        assert_eq!(stats.total_executions, 2);
        assert_eq!(stats.successful_executions, 1);
        assert_eq!(stats.failed_executions, 1);
        assert!((stats.success_rate() - 50.0).abs() < 0.01);
    }
}

<file path="op-core/src/identity_projection_transaction_tests.rs">
use super::*;
use std::sync::{
    atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering},
    mpsc, Arc, Barrier,
};

fn root(dir: &tempfile::TempDir) -> &str {
    dir.path().to_str().unwrap()
}
fn gid() -> u32 {
    nix::unistd::getegid().as_raw()
}
fn pair(version: u64) -> Pair {
    Some((
        format!("{{\"version\":{version}}}").into_bytes(),
        format!("{{\"version\":{version},\"sealed_id\":\"private-{version}\"}}").into_bytes(),
    ))
}
fn seed(dir: &tempfile::TempDir) {
    update_projection_with_credentials_in(root(dir), IDENTITY, gid(), |_| Ok(pair(1))).unwrap();
}
fn unavailable(dir: &tempfile::TempDir) {
    assert!(read_credential_in(root(dir), IDENTITY).is_err());
    assert!(read_projection_snapshot_in(root(dir), &[IDENTITY.into()]).is_err());
    assert!(update_projection_in(root(dir), IDENTITY, |_| Ok(None)).is_err());
    assert!(
        update_projection_with_credentials_in(root(dir), IDENTITY, gid(), |_| Ok(None)).is_err()
    );
}
fn committed<T>(result: CredentialPublication<T>) -> ProjectionCommit {
    match result {
        CredentialPublication::Committed { projection, .. } => projection,
        CredentialPublication::Pending { error, .. } => panic!("unexpected pending: {error}"),
    }
}

#[test]
fn durable_callback_runs_after_synced_marker_and_sees_only_private_predecessor() {
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    seed(&dir);
    let receipt = committed(
        commit_identity_projection_durable_in(root(&dir), gid(), "op-two", |previous| {
            assert_eq!(
                previous,
                pair(1).as_ref().map(|(_, private)| private.as_slice())
            );
            // Fixture-only direct marker inspection avoids reentering the lock.
            let bytes = std::fs::read(dir.path().join(MANIFEST_NAME)).unwrap();
            let text = String::from_utf8(bytes).unwrap();
            assert!(text.contains("op-two"));
            Ok((pair(2), 2u64))
        })
        .unwrap(),
    );
    assert_eq!(receipt.generation, 2);
    assert_eq!(receipt.current, pair(2).map(|(public, _)| public));
    assert!(!receipt.current.unwrap().windows(7).any(|v| v == b"private"));
    assert!(pending_identity_publication_in(root(&dir))
        .unwrap()
        .is_none());
}

#[test]
fn uncertain_callback_blocks_identity_but_preserves_unrelated_transactions() {
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    seed(&dir);
    let result =
        commit_identity_projection_durable_in::<()>(root(&dir), gid(), "uncertain", |_| {
            bail!("native commit outcome uncertain")
        })
        .unwrap();
    assert!(matches!(
        result,
        CredentialPublication::Pending { durable: None, .. }
    ));
    unavailable(&dir);
    let other = update_projection_in(root(&dir), "other", |_| Ok(Some(b"{}".to_vec()))).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(other.generation, 2);
    assert_eq!(
        read_projection_snapshot_in(root(&dir), &["other".into()])
            .unwrap()
            .states["other"],
        b"{}"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        pending_identity_publication_in(root(&dir))
            .unwrap()
            .unwrap()
            .operation_id,
        "uncertain"
    );
    unavailable(&dir);
    let called = AtomicUsize::new(0);
    assert!(
        recover_identity_projection_in(root(&dir), gid(), "wrong", || {
            called.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
            Ok((pair(9), ()))
        })
        .is_err()
    );
    assert_eq!(called.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 0);
    let receipt = committed(
        recover_identity_projection_in(root(&dir), gid(), "uncertain", || Ok((pair(3), ())))
            .unwrap(),
    );
    assert_eq!(receipt.generation, 3);
    assert!(
        receipt.previous.is_none(),
        "recovery never certifies a potentially mixed old public file"
    );
}

#[test]
fn every_post_durable_file_failure_keeps_gate_until_exact_durable_recovery() {
    for (name, occurrence) in [(IDENTITY_FILE, 1), (IDENTITY_FILE, 2), (MANIFEST_NAME, 2)] {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        seed(&dir);
        super::super::tests::inject(name, occurrence, false);
        let result =
            commit_identity_projection_durable_in(root(&dir), gid(), "committed-db", |_| {
                Ok((pair(2), 42u64))
            })
            .unwrap();
        assert!(matches!(
            result,
            CredentialPublication::Pending {
                durable: Some(42),
                ..
            }
        ));
        unavailable(&dir);
        let receipt = committed(
            recover_identity_projection_in(root(&dir), gid(), "committed-db", || {
                Ok((pair(2), 42u64))
            })
            .unwrap(),
        );
        assert_eq!(receipt.current, pair(2).map(|(public, _)| public));
        assert_eq!(
            read_credential_in(root(&dir), IDENTITY).unwrap(),
            pair(2).map(|(_, private)| private)
        );
    }
}

#[test]
fn pre_intent_failure_and_generation_overflow_never_call_durable_writer() {
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    seed(&dir);
    let called = AtomicUsize::new(0);
    super::super::tests::inject(MANIFEST_NAME, 1, false);
    assert!(
        commit_identity_projection_durable_in(root(&dir), gid(), "not-called", |_| {
            called.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
            Ok((pair(2), ()))
        })
        .is_err()
    );
    assert_eq!(called.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 0);
    assert_eq!(
        read_credential_in(root(&dir), IDENTITY).unwrap(),
        pair(1).map(|(_, v)| v)
    );
    std::fs::write(
        dir.path().join(MANIFEST_NAME),
        format!("{{\"generation\":{},\"publishing\":false}}", u64::MAX),
    )
    .unwrap();
    assert!(
        commit_identity_projection_durable_in(root(&dir), gid(), "overflow", |_| {
            called.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
            Ok((pair(2), ()))
        })
        .is_err()
    );
    assert_eq!(called.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 0);
}

#[test]
fn directory_sync_failures_never_clear_pending_or_expose_old_credentials() {
    for phase in [
        "identity_marker_sync",
        "identity_private_sync",
        "identity_public_sync",
    ] {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        seed(&dir);
        let calls = AtomicUsize::new(0);
        super::super::tests::inject(phase, 1, false);
        let result =
            commit_identity_projection_durable_in(root(&dir), gid(), "sync-failed", |_| {
                calls.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
                Ok((pair(2), 2u64))
            })
            .unwrap();
        let expected_calls = usize::from(phase != "identity_marker_sync");
        assert_eq!(calls.load(Ordering::SeqCst), expected_calls);
        match result {
            CredentialPublication::Pending {
                durable,
                operation_id,
                ..
            } => {
                assert_eq!(durable, (expected_calls == 1).then_some(2));
                assert_eq!(operation_id, "sync-failed");
            }
            CredentialPublication::Committed { .. } => panic!("sync failure cannot commit"),
        }
        unavailable(&dir);
        // Recovery's fixture emulates exact durable reread: unchanged on marker
        // sync failure (the callback never ran), otherwise the new committed row.
        let version = if expected_calls == 0 { 1 } else { 2 };
        committed(
            recover_identity_projection_in(root(&dir), gid(), "sync-failed", || {
                Ok((pair(version), ()))
            })
            .unwrap(),
        );
        assert_eq!(
            read_credential_in(root(&dir), IDENTITY).unwrap(),
            pair(version).map(|(_, v)| v)
        );
    }
}

#[test]
fn panic_never_rolls_back_to_old_readable_credential_and_recovery_can_delete() {
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    seed(&dir);
    let result = std::panic::catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| {
        commit_identity_projection_durable_in::<()>(root(&dir), gid(), "panic", |_| {
            panic!("simulated cancellation/process unwind")
        })
    }));
    assert!(result.is_err());
    unavailable(&dir);
    let recovery = std::panic::catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| {
        recover_identity_projection_in::<()>(root(&dir), gid(), "panic", || {
            panic!("failed durable recovery")
        })
    }));
    assert!(recovery.is_err());
    unavailable(&dir);
    committed(
        recover_identity_projection_in(root(&dir), gid(), "panic", || Ok((None, ()))).unwrap(),
    );
    assert!(read_credential_in(root(&dir), IDENTITY).unwrap().is_none());
    assert!(!dir.path().join(IDENTITY_FILE).exists());
}

#[test]
fn concurrent_reader_waits_for_entire_durable_and_pair_boundary() {
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    seed(&dir);
    let path = root(&dir).to_string();
    let barrier = Arc::new(Barrier::new(2));
    let writer_barrier = barrier.clone();
    let (entered, inside) = mpsc::channel();
    let writer = std::thread::spawn(move || {
        commit_identity_projection_durable_in(&path, gid(), "concurrent", |_| {
            entered.send(()).unwrap();
            writer_barrier.wait();
            Ok((pair(2), ()))
        })
        .unwrap()
    });
    inside.recv().unwrap();
    let path = root(&dir).to_string();
    let (read_tx, read_rx) = mpsc::channel();
    let reader = std::thread::spawn(move || {
        read_tx.send(read_credential_in(&path, IDENTITY)).unwrap();
    });
    assert!(read_rx.try_recv().is_err());
    barrier.wait();
    committed(writer.join().unwrap());
    assert_eq!(read_rx.recv().unwrap().unwrap(), pair(2).map(|(_, v)| v));
    reader.join().unwrap();
}

#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]
async fn started_owned_blocking_commit_survives_waiter_cancellation() {
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    seed(&dir);
    let path = root(&dir).to_string();
    let (entered, inside) = tokio::sync::oneshot::channel();
    let (release, released) = mpsc::channel();
    let (finished, done) = tokio::sync::oneshot::channel();
    let worker = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
        let result =
            commit_identity_projection_durable_in(&path, gid(), "cancelled-waiter", |_| {
                entered.send(()).unwrap();
                released.recv().unwrap();
                Ok((pair(2), ()))
            });
        finished
            .send(result.is_ok_and(|r| matches!(r, CredentialPublication::Committed { .. })))
            .unwrap();
    });
    inside.await.unwrap();
    worker.abort();
    release.send(()).unwrap();
    assert!(done.await.unwrap());
    assert_eq!(
        read_credential_in(root(&dir), IDENTITY).unwrap(),
        pair(2).map(|(_, v)| v)
    );
}

//! Identity's durable-store boundary within the existing SHM manifest/lock.
//! These are trusted writer/recovery APIs, never caller-request entry points.
use super::*;

const IDENTITY: &str = "identity_sled";
const IDENTITY_FILE: &str = "identity_sled.json";
type Pair = Option<(Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>)>;

/// Only Committed may update the engine mirror or emit a state notification.
/// Pending retains the exact durable result when the callback completed, so
/// an owned lifecycle worker can distinguish that from an uncertain failure.
/// Neither path restores an old readable credential after the callback starts.
pub enum CredentialPublication<T> {
    Committed {
        projection: ProjectionCommit,
        durable: T,
    },
    Pending {
        operation_id: String,
        durable: Option<T>,
        error: anyhow::Error,
    },
}

pub(super) fn validate_operation_id(id: &str) -> Result<()> {
    ensure!(
        !id.is_empty()
            && id.len() <= 128
            && id
                .bytes()
                .all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(byte, b'-' | b'_')),
        "identity publication operation id is invalid"
    );
    Ok(())
}

fn credentials(locked: &LockedDirectory, state_dir: &str, gid: u32) -> Result<File> {
    locked.enable_credential_readers(gid)?;
    let path = super::super::credential_projection_dir_for_state_dir(state_dir);
    let private =
        directory(Path::new(&path), true, 0o750)?.context("credential directory missing")?;
    private.set_permissions(std::fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o750))?;
    nix::unistd::fchown(private.as_raw_fd(), None, Some(Gid::from_raw(gid)))?;
    Ok(private)
}

fn sync_boundary(directory: &File, phase: &str) -> Result<()> {
    #[cfg(test)]
    super::tests::write_fault(phase)?;
    let _ = phase;
    directory.sync_all()?;
    Ok(())
}

fn check_existing_pair_file(directory: &File, private: bool) -> Result<()> {
    match open_at(
        directory,
        IDENTITY_FILE.as_ref(),
        OFlag::O_RDONLY | OFlag::O_NONBLOCK,
        0,
    ) {
        Ok(file) => check_file(&file, private, directory.metadata()?.uid()),
        Err(Errno::ENOENT) => Ok(()),
        Err(error) => Err(error).context("identity recovery refuses unsafe existing file"),
    }
}

/// Read the existing pending marker without reading any credential bytes.
/// Operators use its exact token for a durable reread; it is not authority to
/// choose replacement state or recover a different operation.
pub fn pending_identity_publication_in(
    state_dir: &str,
) -> Result<Option<PendingCredentialPublication>> {
    let Some(locked) = LockedDirectory::open(state_dir, false)? else {
        return Ok(None);
    };
    Ok(locked
        .manifest()?
        .and_then(|(manifest, _)| manifest.credential_pending))
}

/// Synchronous durable callback under the same lock as every strict SHM reader.
/// The caller must run the whole helper in a cancellation-owned worker. The
/// callback must not reenter SHM helpers; it commits/syncs the authoritative
/// identity store and returns the exact full public/private pair to publish.
/// The callback receives the committed PRIVATE predecessor. Validate typed
/// edits/expected revision inside it; an error may mean a DB commit was
/// uncertain, so even a callback error leaves identity unavailable.
pub fn commit_identity_projection_durable_in<T>(
    state_dir: &str,
    credential_gid: u32,
    operation_id: &str,
    commit: impl FnOnce(Option<&[u8]>) -> Result<(Pair, T)>,
) -> Result<CredentialPublication<T>> {
    validate_operation_id(operation_id)?;
    let locked = LockedDirectory::open(state_dir, true)?.context("projection directory missing")?;
    let manifest = locked.manifest()?;
    let mut manifest = manifest.map_or_else(Manifest::default, |(manifest, _)| manifest);
    manifest.require_available(IDENTITY)?;
    // Reserve room before any durable effect, even for a potential no-op.
    manifest
        .generation
        .checked_add(1)
        .context("projection generation overflow")?;
    let private = credentials(&locked, state_dir, credential_gid)?;
    let previous = read_file(&locked.directory, IDENTITY_FILE, MAX_PROJECTION, false)?;
    let old_private = read_file(&private, IDENTITY_FILE, MAX_PROJECTION, true)?;
    // Existing pairs always require a commit manifest; a raw orphan is not input.
    ensure!(
        locked.manifest()?.is_some() || (previous.is_none() && old_private.is_none()),
        "uncommitted identity files exist without a manifest"
    );
    manifest.credential_pending = Some(PendingCredentialPublication {
        plugin_id: IDENTITY.into(),
        operation_id: operation_id.into(),
    });
    write_file(
        &locked.directory,
        MANIFEST_NAME,
        &simd_json::to_vec(&manifest)?,
        0o644,
        None,
    )?;
    // Marker file data was fsynced by write_file; sync the containing directory
    // BEFORE calling Cozo so a crash cannot recover the old readable marker.
    // Failure here never executes commit; a visible pending marker is retained.
    if let Err(error) = sync_boundary(&locked.directory, "identity_marker_sync") {
        return Ok(CredentialPublication::Pending {
            operation_id: operation_id.into(),
            durable: None,
            error: error.context("sync identity pending marker before durable callback"),
        });
    }
    match commit(old_private.as_deref()) {
        Ok((pair, durable)) => Ok(finish(
            &locked,
            &private,
            manifest,
            previous,
            old_private,
            pair,
            credential_gid,
            durable,
            false,
        )),
        Err(error) => Ok(CredentialPublication::Pending {
            operation_id: operation_id.into(),
            durable: None,
            error,
        }),
    }
}

/// Recover only the exact pending operation by rereading the authoritative
/// durable store. The callback never sees possibly mixed SHM files. There is
/// no "clear marker" or caller-supplied-old-state rollback API. Failure/panic
/// leaves the same token pending. Recovery is explicit, never a read fallback.
pub fn recover_identity_projection_in<T>(
    state_dir: &str,
    credential_gid: u32,
    operation_id: &str,
    load_durable: impl FnOnce() -> Result<(Pair, T)>,
) -> Result<CredentialPublication<T>> {
    validate_operation_id(operation_id)?;
    let locked = LockedDirectory::open(state_dir, true)?.context("projection directory missing")?;
    let (manifest, _) = locked
        .manifest()?
        .context("identity recovery requires a commit manifest")?;
    ensure!(
        manifest.credential_pending.as_ref().is_some_and(
            |pending| pending.plugin_id == IDENTITY && pending.operation_id == operation_id
        ),
        "identity recovery requires the exact pending operation id"
    );
    manifest
        .generation
        .checked_add(1)
        .context("projection generation overflow")?;
    let private = credentials(&locked, state_dir, credential_gid)?;
    check_existing_pair_file(&locked.directory, false)?;
    check_existing_pair_file(&private, true)?;
    match load_durable() {
        Ok((pair, durable)) => Ok(finish(
            &locked,
            &private,
            manifest,
            None,
            None,
            pair,
            credential_gid,
            durable,
            true,
        )),
        Err(error) => Ok(CredentialPublication::Pending {
            operation_id: operation_id.into(),
            durable: None,
            error,
        }),
    }
}

#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
fn finish<T>(
    locked: &LockedDirectory,
    private: &File,
    mut manifest: Manifest,
    previous: Option<Vec<u8>>,
    old_private: Option<Vec<u8>>,
    pair: Pair,
    gid: u32,
    durable: T,
    recovery: bool,
) -> CredentialPublication<T> {
    let operation_id = manifest
        .credential_pending
        .as_ref()
        .expect("pending intent")
        .operation_id
        .clone();
    let (current, credential) = pair.map_or((None, None), |(public, private)| {
        (Some(public), Some(private))
    });
    let result = (|| -> Result<ProjectionCommit> {
        ensure!(
            current
                .as_ref()
                .is_none_or(|bytes| bytes.len() as u64 <= MAX_PROJECTION),
            "identity public projection exceeds size limit"
        );
        ensure!(
            credential
                .as_ref()
                .is_none_or(|bytes| bytes.len() as u64 <= MAX_PROJECTION),
            "identity credential projection exceeds size limit"
        );
        if recovery || previous != current || old_private != credential {
            manifest.generation = manifest
                .generation
                .checked_add(1)
                .context("projection generation overflow")?;
        }
        restore_file(
            private,
            IDENTITY_FILE,
            credential.as_deref(),
            0o640,
            Some(gid),
        )?;
        restore_file(
            &locked.directory,
            IDENTITY_FILE,
            current.as_deref(),
            0o644,
            None,
        )?;
        // Persist both pair renames/deletions BEFORE the final clear-marker
        // rename. After power loss the manifest can be pending or committed;
        // either case can never certify the prior credential over new Cozo.
        sync_boundary(private, "identity_private_sync")?;
        sync_boundary(&locked.directory, "identity_public_sync")?;
        manifest.credential_pending = None;
        write_file(
            &locked.directory,
            MANIFEST_NAME,
            &simd_json::to_vec(&manifest)?,
            0o644,
            None,
        )?;
        // Final manifest rename is the commit point, with no fallible work
        // afterwards. A crash may retain the synced pending marker and require
        // conservative recovery; it cannot resurrect the pre-intent manifest.
        Ok(ProjectionCommit {
            generation: manifest.generation,
            previous,
            current,
        })
    })();
    match result {
        Ok(projection) => CredentialPublication::Committed {
            projection,
            durable,
        },
        Err(error) => CredentialPublication::Pending {
            operation_id,
            durable: Some(durable),
            error,
        },
    }
}

<file path="op-core/src/private_document_publication_tests.rs">
use super::*;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};

const PLUGIN: &str = "gemma_brain";
const OLD: &[u8] = br#"{"revision":1,"jobs":{"a":{"status":"running"}},"specs":{}}"#;
const NEW: &[u8] =
    br#"{"revision":2,"jobs":{"a":{"status":"complete"}},"specs":{"one":{"children":["a","b"]}}}"#;
fn seeded() -> (tempfile::TempDir, PrivateProjectionDirectory) {
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let owner = PrivateProjectionDirectory::prepare(&dir.path().join("owner")).unwrap();
    owner.update(PLUGIN, |_| Ok(Some(OLD.to_vec()))).unwrap();
    (dir, owner)
}
fn unavailable(owner: &PrivateProjectionDirectory) {
    assert!(owner.read_snapshot(&[PLUGIN.into()]).is_err());
    assert!(owner.update(PLUGIN, |_| Ok(None)).is_err());
}
fn committed<T>(result: PrivateDocumentPublication<T>) -> ProjectionCommit {
    match result {
        PrivateDocumentPublication::Committed { projection, .. } => projection,
        PrivateDocumentPublication::Pending { error, .. } => panic!("unexpected pending: {error}"),
    }
}

#[test]
fn complete_document_and_children_publish_after_durable_callback() {
    let (dir, owner) = seeded();
    let result = owner
        .commit_document_durable(PLUGIN, "op-two", |previous| {
            assert_eq!(previous, Some(OLD));
            // Fixture inspection only: production callbacks never read SHM.
            let manifest =
                std::fs::read_to_string(dir.path().join("owner/.manifest.json")).unwrap();
            assert!(manifest.contains("document_pending"));
            assert!(manifest.contains("op-two"));
            assert!(!manifest.contains("credential_pending"));
            Ok((Some(NEW.to_vec()), 2u64))
        })
        .unwrap();
    let projection = committed(result);
    assert_eq!(projection.generation, 2);
    assert_eq!(projection.previous.as_deref(), Some(OLD));
    assert_eq!(projection.current.as_deref(), Some(NEW));
    assert_eq!(
        owner.read_snapshot(&[PLUGIN.into()]).unwrap().states[PLUGIN],
        NEW
    );
    assert!(owner.pending_document().unwrap().is_none());
}

#[test]
fn uncertain_durable_work_blocks_stale_reads_and_requires_exact_recovery() {
    let (dir, owner) = seeded();
    let result = owner
        .commit_document_durable::<()>(PLUGIN, "uncertain", |_| bail!("durable uncertainty"))
        .unwrap();
    assert!(matches!(
        result,
        PrivateDocumentPublication::Pending { durable: None, .. }
    ));
    unavailable(&owner);
    let reopened = PrivateProjectionDirectory::open(&dir.path().join("owner"))
        .unwrap()
        .unwrap();
    unavailable(&reopened);
    let calls = AtomicUsize::new(0);
    for (plugin, operation) in [(PLUGIN, "wrong"), ("other", "uncertain")] {
        assert!(reopened
            .recover_document(plugin, operation, || {
                calls.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
                Ok((Some(OLD.to_vec()), ()))
            })
            .is_err());
    }
    assert_eq!(calls.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 0);
    // Unrelated publication must retain the pending metadata.
    owner.update("other", |_| Ok(Some(b"{}".to_vec()))).unwrap();
    unavailable(&owner);
    assert_eq!(
        owner.pending_document().unwrap().unwrap().operation_id,
        "uncertain"
    );
    let projection = committed(
        reopened
            .recover_document(PLUGIN, "uncertain", || Ok((Some(NEW.to_vec()), ())))
            .unwrap(),
    );
    assert_eq!(projection.generation, 3);
    assert!(projection.previous.is_none());
    assert_eq!(projection.current.as_deref(), Some(NEW));
}

#[test]
fn write_sync_and_final_manifest_failures_never_expose_old_state_after_durability() {
    for (phase, occurrence) in [
        ("gemma_brain.json", 1),
        ("private_document_data_sync", 1),
        (MANIFEST_NAME, 2),
    ] {
        let (_dir, owner) = seeded();
        super::super::super::tests::inject(phase, occurrence, false);
        let calls = AtomicUsize::new(0);
        let result = owner
            .commit_document_durable(PLUGIN, "durable-two", |_| {
                calls.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
                Ok((Some(NEW.to_vec()), 2u64))
            })
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(calls.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 1);
        assert!(matches!(
            result,
            PrivateDocumentPublication::Pending {
                durable: Some(2),
                ..
            }
        ));
        unavailable(&owner);
        let projection = committed(
            owner
                .recover_document(PLUGIN, "durable-two", || Ok((Some(NEW.to_vec()), 2u64)))
                .unwrap(),
        );
        assert_eq!(projection.current.as_deref(), Some(NEW));
    }
}

#[test]
fn marker_sync_failure_prevents_durable_callback() {
    let (_dir, owner) = seeded();
    super::super::super::tests::inject("private_document_marker_sync", 1, false);
    let calls = AtomicUsize::new(0);
    let result = owner
        .commit_document_durable(PLUGIN, "not-started", |_| {
            calls.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
            Ok((Some(NEW.to_vec()), ()))
        })
        .unwrap();
    assert!(matches!(
        result,
        PrivateDocumentPublication::Pending { durable: None, .. }
    ));
    assert_eq!(calls.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 0);
    unavailable(&owner);
    committed(
        owner
            .recover_document(PLUGIN, "not-started", || Ok((Some(OLD.to_vec()), ())))
            .unwrap(),
    );
    assert_eq!(
        owner.read_snapshot(&[PLUGIN.into()]).unwrap().states[PLUGIN],
        OLD
    );
}

#[test]
fn proven_pre_effect_rejection_clears_marker_without_changing_state() {
    let (_dir, owner) = seeded();
    let generation = owner.read_snapshot(&[PLUGIN.into()]).unwrap().generation;
    let error = owner
        .commit_document_durable_with_decision::<()>(PLUGIN, "rejected", |_| {
            Ok(PrivateDocumentCommit::Abort {
                error: anyhow::anyhow!("revision conflict"),
            })
        })
        .err()
        .expect("rejection must remain an error");
    assert_eq!(error.to_string(), "revision conflict");
    assert!(owner.pending_document().unwrap().is_none());
    let snapshot = owner.read_snapshot(&[PLUGIN.into()]).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(snapshot.generation, generation);
    assert_eq!(snapshot.states[PLUGIN], OLD);
}

#[test]
fn rejected_operation_cleanup_failure_retains_exact_pending_gate() {
    let (_dir, owner) = seeded();
    super::super::super::tests::inject(MANIFEST_NAME, 2, false);
    let result = owner
        .commit_document_durable_with_decision::<()>(PLUGIN, "rejected-cleanup", |_| {
            Ok(PrivateDocumentCommit::Abort {
                error: anyhow::anyhow!("revision conflict"),
            })
        })
        .unwrap();
    assert!(matches!(
        result,
        PrivateDocumentPublication::Pending { durable: None, .. }
    ));
    unavailable(&owner);
    let pending = owner.pending_document().unwrap().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(pending.plugin_id, PLUGIN);
    assert_eq!(pending.operation_id, "rejected-cleanup");
}

#[test]
fn panic_and_document_deletion_use_the_same_gate() {
    let (_dir, owner) = seeded();
    let result = std::panic::catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| {
        owner.commit_document_durable::<()>(PLUGIN, "interrupted", |_| {
            panic!("durable callback interrupted")
        })
    }));
    assert!(result.is_err());
    unavailable(&owner);
    let projection = committed(
        owner
            .recover_document(PLUGIN, "interrupted", || Ok((None, ())))
            .unwrap(),
    );
    assert!(projection.current.is_none());
    assert!(owner
        .read_snapshot(&[PLUGIN.into()])
        .unwrap()
        .states
        .is_empty());
    assert!(owner
        .commit_document_durable("identity_sled", "invalid", |_| Ok((None, ())))
        .is_err());
}

#[test]
fn post_durable_contract_rejection_retains_receipt_without_publishing() {
    let (dir, owner) = seeded();
    let result = owner
        .commit_document_durable_with_decision(PLUGIN, "changed-contract", |_| {
            Ok(PrivateDocumentCommit::RetainPending {
                durable: 2u64,
                error: anyhow::anyhow!("contract changed after durable commit"),
            })
        })
        .unwrap();
    assert!(matches!(
        result,
        PrivateDocumentPublication::Pending {
            durable: Some(2),
            ..
        }
    ));
    unavailable(&owner);
    assert_eq!(
        std::fs::read(dir.path().join("owner/gemma_brain.json")).unwrap(),
        OLD
    );
    let result = owner
        .recover_document_with_decision(PLUGIN, "changed-contract", || {
            Ok(PrivateDocumentCommit::RetainPending {
                durable: 2u64,
                error: anyhow::anyhow!("recovered row still lacks current render admission"),
            })
        })
        .unwrap();
    assert!(matches!(
        result,
        PrivateDocumentPublication::Pending {
            durable: Some(2),
            ..
        }
    ));
    unavailable(&owner);
    assert_eq!(
        owner.pending_document().unwrap().unwrap().operation_id,
        "changed-contract"
    );
    let final_projection = committed(
        owner
            .recover_document_with_decision(PLUGIN, "changed-contract", || {
                Ok(PrivateDocumentCommit::Publish {
                    current: Some(NEW.to_vec()),
                    durable: 2u64,
                })
            })
            .unwrap(),
    );
    assert_eq!(final_projection.current.as_deref(), Some(NEW));
    assert_eq!(final_projection.generation, 2);
}
