<file path="op-core/src/projection_shm.rs">
//! Shared-memory projection layer for the projected plugin tree.
//!
//! The projected plugin tree lives in tmpfs (`/dev/shm/opdbus/state/`).
//! The MutationEngine writes one file per plugin on every mutation (atomic
//! temp+rename). These helpers read the raw JSON files without a held cache or
//! polling, and cooperate through one private service-owned advisory lock
//! around data plus manifest access.
//!
//! This module is the shared contract between the **writer** (op-grpc-bridge
//! MutationEngine, the single write door) and the **readers**. The old
//! op-projection D-Bus server is deleted. Retired projection paths are never a
//! fallback or a source of plugin existence.
//!
//! General raw state files are service-only (0600). Their location does not
//! authorize outward disclosure: wire consumers must apply the exact sealed
//! plugin's state-exposure policy. Identity has a separately redacted public
//! file (0644) paired transactionally with its protected credential file.

use std::fs::{self, OpenOptions};
use std::io::Write;
use std::os::unix::fs::{OpenOptionsExt, PermissionsExt};
use std::path::Path;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};

#[path = "projection_transactions.rs"]
mod transactions;
pub use transactions::{
    commit_identity_projection_durable_in, pending_identity_publication_in,
    prepare_projection_directory_in, read_projection_snapshot, read_projection_snapshot_in,
    recover_identity_projection_in, restrict_projection_file_in, update_projection,
    update_projection_in, update_projection_with_credentials_in, CredentialPublication,
    PendingCredentialPublication, PendingDocumentPublication, PrivateDocumentCommit,
    PrivateDocumentPublication, PrivateProjectionDirectory, ProjectionCommit, ProjectionSnapshot,
};

/// Canonical directory for per-plugin present-state files (one JSON file per
/// plugin). This is the static tree that `write_projection` maintains and all
/// consumers read.
pub const SHM_STATE_DIR: &str = "/dev/shm/opdbus/state";
/// Private tmpfs directory for local possession credentials. Files here are
/// not part of the generic state tree and must never be served by schema
/// routing, state sync, snapshots, or web projection readers.
pub const SHM_CREDENTIAL_DIR: &str = "/dev/shm/opdbus/credentials";
/// Retired path constant retained only for source references. Never read as a
/// fallback by the current projection API.
pub const SHM_PROJECTION_DIR: &str = "/dev/shm/opdbus/projections";

/// Manifest carrying the monotonic `generation` counter. Written LAST as the
/// atomic commit point after each projection write. Readers hold a shared lock
/// across manifest and data reads and reject an in-progress transaction.
pub const SHM_PROJECTION_MANIFEST: &str = "/dev/shm/opdbus/state/.manifest.json";

static TEMP_SEQUENCE: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);

/// The state tree root: the canonical [`SHM_STATE_DIR`] in production.
/// `OP_SHM_STATE_DIR` overrides it so tests that drive the MutationEngine
/// never write the live projection tree.
pub fn shm_state_dir() -> String {
    std::env::var("OP_SHM_STATE_DIR").unwrap_or_else(|_| SHM_STATE_DIR.to_string())
}

/// Atomically publish `bytes` to a `/dev/shm` path via a sibling temp file +
/// rename, so readers see either the old or new content, never a torn write.
pub fn atomic_write_shm(path: &str, bytes: &[u8]) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    atomic_write_shm_with_permissions(path, bytes, 0o644, None)
}

/// Atomically publish a sensitive projection with an exact mode and optional
/// group owner. Permissions are applied to the sibling temporary file before
/// rename, so there is no world-readable interval at the destination.
pub fn atomic_write_shm_with_permissions(
    path: &str,
    bytes: &[u8],
    mode: u32,
    gid: Option<u32>,
) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let destination = Path::new(path);
    let parent = destination
        .parent()
        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("Projection path has no parent: {path}"))?;
    let filename = destination
        .file_name()
        .and_then(|value| value.to_str())
        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("Projection path has no UTF-8 filename: {path}"))?;

    // A deterministic `<destination>.tmp` races when two mutation tasks
    // publish the same plugin concurrently. Use O_EXCL and a process-unique
    // sibling name so each writer owns its bytes through the final rename.
    let (tmp, mut file) = (0..32)
        .find_map(|_| {
            let sequence = TEMP_SEQUENCE.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
            let candidate = parent.join(format!(
                ".{filename}.tmp.{}.{}",
                std::process::id(),
                sequence
            ));
            match OpenOptions::new()
                .write(true)
                .create_new(true)
                .mode(mode)
                .open(&candidate)
            {
                Ok(file) => Some(Ok((candidate, file))),
                Err(error) if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::AlreadyExists => None,
                Err(error) => Some(Err(anyhow::anyhow!(
                    "Cannot create {}: {}",
                    candidate.display(),
                    error
                ))),
            }
        })
        .transpose()?
        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("Could not allocate a unique temp file for {path}"))?;

    let publish = (|| -> anyhow::Result<()> {
        file.set_permissions(fs::Permissions::from_mode(mode))
            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!("Cannot set permissions on {}: {}", tmp.display(), e))?;
        file.write_all(bytes)
            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!("Failed to write {}: {}", tmp.display(), e))?;
        file.sync_all()
            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!("Failed to sync {}: {}", tmp.display(), e))?;
        drop(file);
        if let Some(gid) = gid {
            nix::unistd::chown(&tmp, None, Some(nix::unistd::Gid::from_raw(gid)))
                .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!("Cannot set group on {}: {}", tmp.display(), e))?;
        }
        fs::rename(&tmp, destination).map_err(|e| {
            anyhow::anyhow!(
                "Failed to rename {} -> {}: {}",
                tmp.display(),
                destination.display(),
                e
            )
        })?;
        Ok(())
    })();
    if publish.is_err() {
        let _ = fs::remove_file(&tmp);
    }
    publish
}

/// Sanitize a plugin id into a safe flat filename (no path separators or NUL).
fn safe_filename(plugin_id: &str) -> String {
    plugin_id
        .chars()
        .map(|c| {
            if c == '/' || c == '\\' || c == '\0' {
                '_'
            } else {
                c
            }
        })
        .collect()
}

/// File path for a specific plugin's projection (`<state_dir>/<plugin>.json`).
pub fn projection_file_path(plugin_id: &str) -> String {
    projection_file_path_in(&shm_state_dir(), plugin_id)
}

/// File path for a projection under one already-resolved state directory.
/// Writers use this form so a process-global test override cannot change
/// between resolving the directory and publishing the file.
pub fn projection_file_path_in(state_dir: &str, plugin_id: &str) -> String {
    format!("{state_dir}/{}.json", safe_filename(plugin_id))
}

/// Credential directory paired with one already-resolved state tree. Test
/// roots keep credentials beneath the same temporary root; production uses a
/// separate non-enumerated tmpfs directory.
pub fn credential_projection_dir_for_state_dir(state_dir: &str) -> String {
    if Path::new(state_dir) == Path::new(SHM_STATE_DIR) {
        SHM_CREDENTIAL_DIR.to_string()
    } else {
        format!("{state_dir}/.credentials")
    }
}

pub fn credential_projection_dir() -> String {
    credential_projection_dir_for_state_dir(&shm_state_dir())
}

/// Protected credential file for one plugin. This path is intentionally not
/// considered by generic projection readers or plugin enumeration.
pub fn credential_projection_file_path(plugin_id: &str) -> String {
    let directory = credential_projection_dir();
    format!("{directory}/{}.json", safe_filename(plugin_id))
}

pub fn credential_projection_file_path_in(state_dir: &str, plugin_id: &str) -> String {
    let directory = credential_projection_dir_for_state_dir(state_dir);
    format!("{directory}/{}.json", safe_filename(plugin_id))
}

/// Write a plugin's full projected state to shm and bump the manifest
/// generation.
///
/// Called by the MutationEngine for an already-completed state value. Opaque
/// configuration values remain service-only raw state until a schema-owned
/// projector explicitly selects the public wire view.
pub fn write_projection(plugin_id: &str, json_bytes: &[u8]) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let commit = update_projection(plugin_id, |_| Ok(Some(json_bytes.to_vec())))?;
    tracing::debug!(
        plugin_id,
        generation = commit.generation,
        "Projection committed to shm"
    );
    Ok(())
}

/// This former API cannot safely commit independently installed files. Callers
/// must use update_projection or update_projection_with_credentials_in.
pub fn bump_manifest_generation() -> anyhow::Result<u64> {
    bump_manifest_generation_in(&shm_state_dir())
}

/// Fail closed rather than certify state written outside a transaction.
pub fn bump_manifest_generation_in(_state_dir: &str) -> anyhow::Result<u64> {
    anyhow::bail!(
        "standalone projection generation bumps are unsafe; use the transactional projection API"
    )
}

/// Read the raw bytes of a plugin's projection from shm.
pub fn read_projection_bytes(plugin_id: &str) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
    read_projection_snapshot(&[plugin_id.to_string()])
        .ok()?
        .states
        .remove(plugin_id)
}

/// Read a protected local credential projection. There is deliberately no
/// legacy or public-state fallback: callers requesting possession material
/// must fail closed when the private projection is absent.
pub fn read_credential_projection_bytes(plugin_id: &str) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
    read_credential_projection_bytes_in(&shm_state_dir(), plugin_id)
        .ok()
        .flatten()
}

/// Strict privileged credential read under the shared transaction lock. The
/// caller resolves the state directory once; absence remains distinct from
/// unsafe or incomplete publication. Existing protected-group OS permissions
/// apply. Generic state readers never call this helper.
pub fn read_credential_projection_bytes_in(
    state_dir: &str,
    plugin_id: &str,
) -> anyhow::Result<Option<Vec<u8>>> {
    transactions::read_credential_in(state_dir, plugin_id)
}

/// Legacy best-effort generation read (0 on absence or error). Authoritative
/// consumers use read_projection_snapshot so malformed/incomplete publication
/// remains an error rather than looking like generation zero.
pub fn read_manifest_generation() -> u64 {
    read_projection_snapshot(&[])
        .map(|snapshot| snapshot.generation)
        .unwrap_or(0)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt;

    #[test]
    fn safe_filename_replaces_separators() {
        assert_eq!(safe_filename("wireguard"), "wireguard");
        assert_eq!(safe_filename("a/b"), "a_b");
        assert_eq!(safe_filename("a\\b"), "a_b");
    }

    #[test]
    fn projection_file_path_under_canonical_dir() {
        assert_eq!(
            projection_file_path("cognitive_mcp"),
            "/dev/shm/opdbus/state/cognitive_mcp.json"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn restricted_atomic_publish_never_uses_world_readable_mode() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let path = dir.path().join("identity_sled.json");
        atomic_write_shm_with_permissions(
            path.to_str().unwrap(),
            br#"{"sleds":[]}"#,
            0o640,
            Some(nix::unistd::Gid::current().as_raw()),
        )
        .unwrap();
        let metadata = std::fs::metadata(path).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(metadata.mode() & 0o777, 0o640);
        assert_eq!(metadata.gid(), nix::unistd::Gid::current().as_raw());
    }

    #[test]
    fn concurrent_atomic_publish_never_shares_a_temp_file() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let path = dir.path().join("state.json");
        let first_path = path.clone();
        let second_path = path.clone();
        let first = std::thread::spawn(move || {
            for _ in 0..64 {
                atomic_write_shm(first_path.to_str().unwrap(), br#"{"writer":"first"}"#).unwrap();
            }
        });
        let second = std::thread::spawn(move || {
            for _ in 0..64 {
                atomic_write_shm(second_path.to_str().unwrap(), br#"{"writer":"second"}"#).unwrap();
            }
        });
        first.join().unwrap();
        second.join().unwrap();

        let bytes = std::fs::read(&path).unwrap();
        assert!(bytes == br#"{"writer":"first"}"# || bytes == br#"{"writer":"second"}"#);
        assert!(std::fs::read_dir(dir.path()).unwrap().all(|entry| {
            !entry
                .unwrap()
                .file_name()
                .to_string_lossy()
                .contains(".tmp.")
        }));
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_state_roots_keep_credentials_out_of_the_public_tree() {
        assert_eq!(
            credential_projection_dir_for_state_dir("/tmp/example-state"),
            "/tmp/example-state/.credentials"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            credential_projection_file_path_in("/tmp/example-state", "identity_sled"),
            "/tmp/example-state/.credentials/identity_sled.json"
        );
    }
}
</file>

<file path="op-core/src/projection_transactions_tests.rs">
use super::*;
use std::{
    cell::RefCell,
    sync::{mpsc, Arc, Barrier},
    time::Duration,
};

// Inject a single native-write failure at the file/manifest boundary. This
// leaves rollback writes operational, exercising the public transaction API.
thread_local! {
    static FAILURE: RefCell<Option<(String, usize, bool)>> = const { RefCell::new(None) };
}

pub(super) fn write_fault(name: &str) -> Result<()> {
    let action = FAILURE.with(|fault| {
        let mut fault = fault.borrow_mut();
        match fault.as_mut() {
            Some((target, remaining, panic)) if target == name => {
                *remaining -= 1;
                if *remaining == 0 {
                    let panic = *panic;
                    *fault = None;
                    Some(panic)
                } else {
                    None
                }
            }
            _ => None,
        }
    });
    if let Some(panic) = action {
        if panic {
            panic!("simulated publisher interruption before commit");
        }
        bail!("injected file publication failure")
    }
    Ok(())
}

pub(super) fn inject(name: &str, occurrence: usize, panic: bool) {
    FAILURE.with(|fault| *fault.borrow_mut() = Some((name.into(), occurrence, panic)));
}

fn root(directory: &tempfile::TempDir) -> &str {
    directory.path().to_str().unwrap()
}

fn snapshot(directory: &tempfile::TempDir) -> ProjectionSnapshot {
    read_projection_snapshot_in(root(directory), &["plugin".into()]).unwrap()
}

fn write(directory: &tempfile::TempDir, bytes: &[u8]) -> ProjectionCommit {
    update_projection_in(root(directory), "plugin", |_| Ok(Some(bytes.to_vec()))).unwrap()
}

#[test]
fn raw_json_commit_update_delete_and_noop_keep_exact_generations() {
    let directory = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let first = write(&directory, br#"{"child":{"false":false,"zero":0}}"#);
    assert_eq!(first.generation, 1);
    assert_eq!(
        std::fs::metadata(directory.path().join("plugin.json"))
            .unwrap()
            .mode()
            & 0o777,
        0o600
    );
    assert_eq!(
        std::fs::read(directory.path().join("plugin.json")).unwrap(),
        first.current.clone().unwrap()
    );
    let before = snapshot(&directory);
    assert_eq!(before.states["plugin"], first.current.clone().unwrap());
    assert_eq!(
        write(&directory, first.current.as_ref().unwrap()).generation,
        1
    );
    let second = update_projection_in(root(&directory), "plugin", |old| {
        assert_eq!(old, first.current.as_deref());
        Ok(Some(br#"{"child":{"false":false,"zero":1}}"#.to_vec()))
    })
    .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(second.generation, 2);
    assert_eq!(second.previous, first.current);
    let deleted = update_projection_in(root(&directory), "plugin", |_| Ok(None)).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(deleted.generation, 3);
    assert!(deleted.current.is_none());
    assert!(!directory.path().join("plugin.json").exists());
    assert!(snapshot(&directory).states.is_empty());
}

#[test]
fn file_and_manifest_failures_restore_previous_committed_bytes() {
    for (name, occurrence) in [("plugin.json", 1), (MANIFEST_NAME, 1), (MANIFEST_NAME, 2)] {
        let directory = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        write(&directory, br#"{"value":"old"}"#);
        let manifest = std::fs::read(directory.path().join(MANIFEST_NAME)).unwrap();
        inject(name, occurrence, false);
        assert!(
            update_projection_in(root(&directory), "plugin", |_| Ok(Some(
                br#"{"value":"new"}"#.to_vec()
            )))
            .is_err()
        );
        assert_eq!(snapshot(&directory).generation, 1);
        assert_eq!(snapshot(&directory).states["plugin"], br#"{"value":"old"}"#);
        assert_eq!(
            std::fs::read(directory.path().join(MANIFEST_NAME)).unwrap(),
            manifest
        );
    }
}

#[test]
fn interrupted_publication_is_unreadable_and_never_certified_by_next_write() {
    let directory = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    write(&directory, br#"{"value":"old"}"#);
    inject(MANIFEST_NAME, 2, true);
    let interrupted = std::panic::catch_unwind(|| {
        let _ = update_projection_in(root(&directory), "plugin", |_| {
            Ok(Some(br#"{"value":"partial"}"#.to_vec()))
        });
    });
    assert!(interrupted.is_err());
    assert_eq!(
        std::fs::read(directory.path().join("plugin.json")).unwrap(),
        br#"{"value":"partial"}"#
    );
    assert!(
        read_projection_snapshot_in(root(&directory), &["plugin".into()])
            .unwrap_err()
            .to_string()
            .contains("incomplete")
    );
    assert!(
        update_projection_in(root(&directory), "plugin", |_| Ok(Some(b"{}".to_vec()))).is_err()
    );
}

#[test]
fn generation_overflow_rejects_before_changing_data() {
    let directory = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    write(&directory, b"{}");
    std::fs::write(
        directory.path().join(MANIFEST_NAME),
        format!("{{\"generation\":{}}}", u64::MAX),
    )
    .unwrap();
    let error = update_projection_in(root(&directory), "plugin", |_| {
        Ok(Some(br#"{"changed":true}"#.to_vec()))
    })
    .unwrap_err();
    assert!(error.to_string().contains("overflow"));
    assert_eq!(snapshot(&directory).generation, u64::MAX);
    assert_eq!(snapshot(&directory).states["plugin"], b"{}");
}

#[test]
fn readers_wait_until_the_entire_locked_fold_and_commit_finish() {
    let directory = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    write(&directory, b"0");
    let barrier = Arc::new(Barrier::new(2));
    let (release_tx, release_rx) = mpsc::channel();
    let writer_root = root(&directory).to_owned();
    let writer_barrier = barrier.clone();
    let writer = std::thread::spawn(move || {
        update_projection_in(&writer_root, "plugin", |_| {
            writer_barrier.wait();
            release_rx.recv().unwrap();
            Ok(Some(b"1".to_vec()))
        })
        .unwrap()
    });
    barrier.wait();
    let (read_tx, read_rx) = mpsc::channel();
    let reader_root = root(&directory).to_owned();
    let reader = std::thread::spawn(move || {
        read_tx
            .send(read_projection_snapshot_in(&reader_root, &["plugin".into()]).unwrap())
            .unwrap();
    });
    assert!(read_rx.recv_timeout(Duration::from_millis(30)).is_err());
    release_tx.send(()).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(writer.join().unwrap().generation, 2);
    let read = read_rx.recv_timeout(Duration::from_secs(3)).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(read.generation, 2);
    assert_eq!(read.states["plugin"], b"1");
    reader.join().unwrap();
}

#[test]
fn independent_handles_serialize_folds_without_lost_updates_or_mixed_reads() {
    let directory = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    write(&directory, b"0");
    let mut threads = Vec::new();
    for _ in 0..4 {
        let state_root = root(&directory).to_owned();
        threads.push(std::thread::spawn(move || {
            for _ in 0..24 {
                update_projection_in(&state_root, "plugin", |old| {
                    let number = std::str::from_utf8(old.unwrap())?.parse::<u64>()?;
                    Ok(Some((number + 1).to_string().into_bytes()))
                })
                .unwrap();
                let snapshot =
                    read_projection_snapshot_in(&state_root, &["plugin".into()]).unwrap();
                let number = std::str::from_utf8(&snapshot.states["plugin"])
                    .unwrap()
                    .parse::<u64>()
                    .unwrap();
                assert_eq!(snapshot.generation, number + 1);
            }
        }));
    }
    for thread in threads {
        thread.join().unwrap();
    }
    let final_state = snapshot(&directory);
    assert_eq!(final_state.generation, 97);
    assert_eq!(final_state.states["plugin"], b"96");
}

#[test]
fn generic_snapshot_never_contains_credentials_and_pair_rolls_back_together() {
    let directory = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let group = nix::unistd::getgid().as_raw();
    let commit =
        update_projection_with_credentials_in(root(&directory), "identity_sled", group, |old| {
            assert!(old.is_none());
            Ok(Some((
                br#"{"session_id":"one"}"#.to_vec(),
                br#"{"session_id":"one","sealed_id":"secret"}"#.to_vec(),
            )))
        })
        .unwrap();
    assert!(!String::from_utf8(commit.current.unwrap())
        .unwrap()
        .contains("sealed_id"));
    let public = read_projection_snapshot_in(root(&directory), &["identity_sled".into()]).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        std::fs::metadata(directory.path().join("identity_sled.json"))
            .unwrap()
            .mode()
            & 0o777,
        0o644
    );
    assert_eq!(public.states.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(public.states["identity_sled"], br#"{"session_id":"one"}"#);
    assert_eq!(
        read_credential_in(root(&directory), "identity_sled")
            .unwrap()
            .unwrap(),
        br#"{"session_id":"one","sealed_id":"secret"}"#
    );
    inject(MANIFEST_NAME, 2, false);
    assert!(update_projection_with_credentials_in(
        root(&directory),
        "identity_sled",
        group,
        |_| {
            Ok(Some((
                br#"{"session_id":"two"}"#.to_vec(),
                br#"{"sealed_id":"replacement"}"#.to_vec(),
            )))
        }
    )
    .is_err());
    assert_eq!(
        read_credential_in(root(&directory), "identity_sled")
            .unwrap()
            .unwrap(),
        br#"{"session_id":"one","sealed_id":"secret"}"#
    );
    assert_eq!(
        read_projection_snapshot_in(root(&directory), &["identity_sled".into()])
            .unwrap()
            .generation,
        1
    );
    assert!(
        read_projection_snapshot_in(root(&directory), &[".credentials/identity_sled".into()])
            .is_err()
    );
    let private_file = directory.path().join(".credentials/identity_sled.json");
    let lock_metadata = std::fs::metadata(directory.path().join(LOCK_NAME)).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(lock_metadata.mode() & 0o777, 0o640);
    assert_eq!(lock_metadata.gid(), group);
    assert_eq!(
        std::fs::metadata(&private_file).unwrap().mode() & 0o777,
        0o640
    );
    let unchanged =
        update_projection_with_credentials_in(root(&directory), "identity_sled", group, |old| {
            Ok(Some((
                br#"{"session_id":"one"}"#.to_vec(),
                old.unwrap().to_vec(),
            )))
        })
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(unchanged.generation, 1);
    inject(MANIFEST_NAME, 2, false);
    assert!(update_projection_with_credentials_in(
        root(&directory),
        "identity_sled",
        group,
        |_| Ok(None)
    )
    .is_err());
    assert!(private_file.exists());
    assert_eq!(
        read_credential_in(root(&directory), "identity_sled")
            .unwrap()
            .unwrap(),
        br#"{"session_id":"one","sealed_id":"secret"}"#
    );
    let deleted =
        update_projection_with_credentials_in(root(&directory), "identity_sled", group, |_| {
            Ok(None)
        })
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(deleted.generation, 2);
    assert!(deleted.current.is_none());
    assert!(!private_file.exists());
    assert!(!directory.path().join("identity_sled.json").exists());
    assert_eq!(
        update_projection_with_credentials_in(root(&directory), "identity_sled", group, |_| Ok(
            None
        ))
        .unwrap()
        .generation,
        2
    );
}

#[test]
fn old_raw_file_modes_are_restricted_without_content_or_generation_changes() {
    let directory = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    write(&directory, br#"{"opaque":"private"}"#);
    let path = directory.path().join("plugin.json");
    let old_manifest = std::fs::read(directory.path().join(MANIFEST_NAME)).unwrap();
    std::fs::set_permissions(&path, std::fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o644)).unwrap();
    let unchanged = write(&directory, br#"{"opaque":"private"}"#);
    assert_eq!(unchanged.generation, 1);
    assert_eq!(std::fs::metadata(&path).unwrap().mode() & 0o777, 0o600);
    std::fs::set_permissions(&path, std::fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o644)).unwrap();
    restrict_projection_file_in(root(&directory), "plugin").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(std::fs::metadata(&path).unwrap().mode() & 0o777, 0o600);
    assert_eq!(std::fs::read(path).unwrap(), br#"{"opaque":"private"}"#);
    assert_eq!(
        std::fs::read(directory.path().join(MANIFEST_NAME)).unwrap(),
        old_manifest
    );
    assert!(restrict_projection_file_in(root(&directory), "identity_sled").is_err());
}

#[test]
fn missing_manifest_or_unselected_files_never_become_state_authority() {
    let directory = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    std::fs::write(directory.path().join("orphan.json"), b"secret-orphan").unwrap();
    assert!(
        read_projection_snapshot_in(root(&directory), &["orphan".into()])
            .unwrap()
            .states
            .is_empty()
    );
    assert!(
        !directory.path().join(LOCK_NAME).exists(),
        "reader must not create lock files"
    );
    assert!(
        update_projection_in(root(&directory), "orphan", |_| Ok(Some(b"{}".to_vec()))).is_err()
    );
    assert_eq!(
        std::fs::read(directory.path().join("orphan.json")).unwrap(),
        b"secret-orphan"
    );
    write(&directory, b"{}");
    assert_eq!(snapshot(&directory).states.len(), 1);
    assert!(!snapshot(&directory).states.contains_key("orphan"));
}

#[test]
fn unsafe_lock_paths_links_permissions_and_plugin_paths_are_rejected() {
    let directory = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let target = directory.path().join("foreign");
    std::fs::write(&target, b"untouched").unwrap();
    std::os::unix::fs::symlink(&target, directory.path().join(LOCK_NAME)).unwrap();
    assert!(prepare_projection_directory_in(root(&directory)).is_err());
    assert_eq!(std::fs::read(&target).unwrap(), b"untouched");
    std::fs::remove_file(directory.path().join(LOCK_NAME)).unwrap();
    std::fs::hard_link(&target, directory.path().join(LOCK_NAME)).unwrap();
    assert!(prepare_projection_directory_in(root(&directory)).is_err());
    std::fs::remove_file(directory.path().join(LOCK_NAME)).unwrap();
    std::fs::write(directory.path().join(LOCK_NAME), b"").unwrap();
    for mode in [0o644, 0o660, 0o666, 0o604] {
        std::fs::set_permissions(
            directory.path().join(LOCK_NAME),
            std::fs::Permissions::from_mode(mode),
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert!(prepare_projection_directory_in(root(&directory)).is_err());
        assert!(read_projection_snapshot_in(root(&directory), &[]).is_err());
    }
    std::fs::remove_file(directory.path().join(LOCK_NAME)).unwrap();
    prepare_projection_directory_in(root(&directory)).unwrap();
    for id in ["../secret", "a/b", "a\\b", ".manifest", "", "bad\0id"] {
        assert!(update_projection_in(root(&directory), id, |_| Ok(Some(b"{}".to_vec()))).is_err());
    }
    let alias = directory.path().join("alias");
    std::os::unix::fs::symlink(directory.path(), &alias).unwrap();
    assert!(read_projection_snapshot_in(alias.to_str().unwrap(), &[]).is_err());
}

#[test]
fn root_owned_reader_source_does_not_grant_nonowner_writer_authority() {
    assert!(trusted_directory_owner(1000, 1000, true));
    assert!(trusted_directory_owner(0, 1000, false));
    assert!(!trusted_directory_owner(0, 1000, true));
    assert!(!trusted_directory_owner(1001, 1000, false));
    assert!(!trusted_directory_owner(1001, 1000, true));
}

#[test]
fn existing_generation_manifest_is_read_without_changes_after_writer_preparation() {
    let directory = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    std::fs::write(directory.path().join("plugin.json"), b"{\"existing\":true}").unwrap();
    std::fs::write(directory.path().join(MANIFEST_NAME), b"{\"generation\":9}").unwrap();
    assert!(read_projection_snapshot_in(root(&directory), &["plugin".into()]).is_err());
    prepare_projection_directory_in(root(&directory)).unwrap();
    let before = std::fs::metadata(directory.path().join(MANIFEST_NAME))
        .unwrap()
        .modified()
        .unwrap();
    let state = snapshot(&directory);
    assert_eq!(state.generation, 9);
    assert_eq!(state.states["plugin"], b"{\"existing\":true}");
    assert_eq!(
        std::fs::metadata(directory.path().join(MANIFEST_NAME))
            .unwrap()
            .modified()
            .unwrap(),
        before
    );
}
</file>

<file path="op-core/src/projection_transactions.rs">
//! Locked publication/read transactions for the canonical raw SHM state tree.
//!
//! The existing manifest is the commit marker. `publishing=true` means an
//! interrupted transaction is not readable; no reader may invent a committed
//! state from those files. This layer does not decide plugin existence: callers
//! select IDs using the manifest-pinned sealed catalog, never a directory scan.

use anyhow::{bail, ensure, Context, Result};
use nix::{
    errno::Errno,
    fcntl::{Flock, FlockArg, OFlag},
    sys::stat::Mode,
    unistd::{Gid, UnlinkatFlags},
};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::{
    collections::BTreeMap,
    fs::File,
    io::{Read, Write},
    os::{
        fd::{AsRawFd, FromRawFd},
        unix::fs::{MetadataExt, PermissionsExt},
    },
    path::{Component, Path},
    sync::atomic::Ordering,
};

#[path = "private_projection_directory.rs"]
mod private_directory;
pub use private_directory::{
    PrivateDocumentCommit, PrivateDocumentPublication, PrivateProjectionDirectory,
};

const LOCK_NAME: &str = ".projection.lock";
const MANIFEST_NAME: &str = ".manifest.json";
const MAX_MANIFEST: u64 = 4096;
const MAX_PROJECTION: u64 = 64 * 1024 * 1024;

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ProjectionSnapshot {
    pub generation: u64,
    pub states: BTreeMap<String, Vec<u8>>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ProjectionCommit {
    pub generation: u64,
    pub previous: Option<Vec<u8>>,
    pub current: Option<Vec<u8>>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
struct Manifest {
    generation: u64,
    #[serde(default)]
    publishing: bool,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    credential_pending: Option<PendingCredentialPublication>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    document_pending: Option<PendingDocumentPublication>,
}

/// Private document publication gate in the same manifest as committed state.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct PendingDocumentPublication {
    pub plugin_id: String,
    pub operation_id: String,
}

/// A commit gate in the existing manifest, never a credential or identity store.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct PendingCredentialPublication {
    pub plugin_id: String,
    pub operation_id: String,
}

impl Manifest {
    fn require_available(&self, plugin_id: &str) -> Result<()> {
        ensure!(
            !self
                .document_pending
                .as_ref()
                .is_some_and(|pending| pending.plugin_id == plugin_id),
            "private document publication is pending; exact-operation durable recovery is required"
        );
        ensure!(
            !self
                .credential_pending
                .as_ref()
                .is_some_and(|pending| pending.plugin_id == plugin_id),
            "identity publication is pending; exact-operation durable recovery is required"
        );
        Ok(())
    }
}

struct LockedDirectory {
    directory: File,
    _lock: Flock<File>,
}

fn open_at(directory: &File, name: &std::ffi::OsStr, flags: OFlag, mode: u32) -> nix::Result<File> {
    let raw = nix::fcntl::openat(
        Some(directory.as_raw_fd()),
        name,
        flags | OFlag::O_NOFOLLOW | OFlag::O_CLOEXEC,
        Mode::from_bits_truncate(mode),
    )?;
    // SAFETY: nix 0.28 returns a newly owned descriptor on success. Ownership
    // transfers exactly once to File, which closes it on every exit path.
    Ok(unsafe { File::from_raw_fd(raw) })
}

fn directory(path: &Path, create: bool, mode: u32) -> Result<Option<File>> {
    ensure!(
        path.is_absolute() && path != Path::new("/"),
        "projection directory must be absolute and not the filesystem root"
    );
    ensure!(
        !path
            .to_string_lossy()
            .split('/')
            .any(|part| part == "." || part == ".."),
        "projection directory must not contain dot components"
    );
    let mut current = File::open("/")?;
    for component in path.components() {
        match component {
            Component::RootDir => {}
            Component::Normal(name) => {
                let opened = open_at(&current, name, OFlag::O_RDONLY | OFlag::O_DIRECTORY, 0);
                current = match opened {
                    Ok(file) => file,
                    Err(Errno::ENOENT) if create => {
                        match nix::sys::stat::mkdirat(
                            Some(current.as_raw_fd()),
                            name,
                            Mode::from_bits_truncate(mode),
                        ) {
                            Ok(()) | Err(Errno::EEXIST) => {}
                            Err(error) => return Err(error.into()),
                        }
                        open_at(&current, name, OFlag::O_RDONLY | OFlag::O_DIRECTORY, 0)?
                    }
                    Err(Errno::ENOENT) => return Ok(None),
                    Err(error) => {
                        return Err(error)
                            .context("projection directory must have no symlink components")
                    }
                };
            }
            _ => bail!("projection directory must not contain dot components"),
        }
    }
    let metadata = current.metadata()?;
    ensure!(
        trusted_directory_owner(metadata.uid(), nix::unistd::geteuid().as_raw(), create),
        "projection directory must be owned by the writing service user or trusted root reader source"
    );
    ensure!(
        metadata.mode() & 0o022 == 0,
        "projection directory must not be writable by other users or groups"
    );
    Ok(Some(current))
}

fn trusted_directory_owner(owner: u32, caller: u32, writer: bool) -> bool {
    owner == caller || (!writer && owner == 0)
}

fn check_file(file: &File, private: bool, owner: u32) -> Result<()> {
    let metadata = file.metadata()?;
    ensure!(
        metadata.is_file() && metadata.nlink() == 1,
        "projection file must be a regular file with one link"
    );
    ensure!(
        metadata.uid() == owner,
        "projection file must be owned by its trusted service directory owner"
    );
    ensure!(
        metadata.mode() & 0o022 == 0,
        "projection file must not be group/world writable"
    );
    if private {
        ensure!(
            metadata.mode() & 0o007 == 0,
            "credential projection must not be world accessible"
        );
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn read_file(directory: &File, name: &str, maximum: u64, private: bool) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>> {
    let file = match open_at(
        directory,
        name.as_ref(),
        OFlag::O_RDONLY | OFlag::O_NONBLOCK,
        0,
    ) {
        Ok(file) => file,
        Err(Errno::ENOENT) => return Ok(None),
        Err(error) => return Err(error).context("open canonical projection file without symlinks"),
    };
    check_file(&file, private, directory.metadata()?.uid())?;
    ensure!(
        file.metadata()?.len() <= maximum,
        "projection file exceeds its size limit"
    );
    let mut bytes = Vec::new();
    file.take(maximum + 1).read_to_end(&mut bytes)?;
    ensure!(
        bytes.len() as u64 <= maximum,
        "projection file grew beyond its size limit"
    );
    Ok(Some(bytes))
}

impl LockedDirectory {
    fn open(state_dir: &str, exclusive: bool) -> Result<Option<Self>> {
        let Some(directory) = directory(Path::new(state_dir), exclusive, 0o755)? else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        Self::from_directory(directory, exclusive)
    }

    fn from_directory(directory: File, exclusive: bool) -> Result<Option<Self>> {
        let flags = if exclusive {
            OFlag::O_RDWR | OFlag::O_CREAT | OFlag::O_NONBLOCK
        } else {
            OFlag::O_RDONLY | OFlag::O_NONBLOCK
        };
        let lock = match open_at(&directory, LOCK_NAME.as_ref(), flags, 0o600) {
            Ok(file) => file,
            Err(Errno::ENOENT) if !exclusive => {
                ensure!(read_file(&directory, MANIFEST_NAME, MAX_MANIFEST, false)?.is_none(),
                    "projection manifest exists without its lock; writer must prepare the projection directory before readers start");
                return Ok(None);
            }
            Err(error) => return Err(error).context("open private projection lock"),
        };
        check_file(&lock, true, directory.metadata()?.uid())?;
        ensure!(
            matches!(lock.metadata()?.mode() & 0o777, 0o600 | 0o640),
            "projection lock must have service-private 0600 or protected-group 0640 permissions"
        );
        let inode = lock.metadata()?;
        let lock = Flock::lock(
            lock,
            if exclusive {
                FlockArg::LockExclusive
            } else {
                FlockArg::LockShared
            },
        )
        .map_err(|(_, error)| anyhow::anyhow!("lock projection transaction: {error}"))?;
        let current = open_at(
            &directory,
            LOCK_NAME.as_ref(),
            OFlag::O_RDONLY | OFlag::O_NONBLOCK,
            0,
        )?;
        let current = current.metadata()?;
        ensure!(
            inode.dev() == current.dev() && inode.ino() == current.ino(),
            "projection lock was replaced while waiting"
        );
        Ok(Some(Self {
            directory,
            _lock: lock,
        }))
    }

    fn manifest(&self) -> Result<Option<(Manifest, Vec<u8>)>> {
        let Some(bytes) = read_file(&self.directory, MANIFEST_NAME, MAX_MANIFEST, false)? else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        let mut parsed = bytes.clone();
        let manifest: Manifest =
            simd_json::from_slice(&mut parsed).context("invalid projection commit manifest")?;
        if let Some(pending) = &manifest.credential_pending {
            ensure!(
                pending.plugin_id == "identity_sled",
                "invalid pending credential plugin"
            );
            identity_transaction::validate_operation_id(&pending.operation_id)?;
        }
        if let Some(pending) = &manifest.document_pending {
            filename(&pending.plugin_id)?;
            ensure!(
                pending.plugin_id != "identity_sled",
                "identity cannot use the private document gate"
            );
            identity_transaction::validate_operation_id(&pending.operation_id)?;
        }
        ensure!(!manifest.publishing, "projection transaction is incomplete; operator recovery is required before reading or updating state");
        Ok(Some((manifest, bytes)))
    }

    fn enable_credential_readers(&self, credential_gid: u32) -> Result<()> {
        // Identity writers grant the existing protected group shared-lock
        // access; no second lock or credential authority is introduced.
        // Revoke the old group's access before changing group ownership.
        self._lock
            .set_permissions(std::fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o600))?;
        nix::unistd::fchown(
            self._lock.as_raw_fd(),
            None,
            Some(Gid::from_raw(credential_gid)),
        )?;
        self._lock
            .set_permissions(std::fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o640))?;
        Ok(())
    }
}

fn filename(plugin_id: &str) -> Result<String> {
    ensure!(
        !plugin_id.is_empty()
            && plugin_id.len() <= 200
            && plugin_id.as_bytes()[0].is_ascii_alphanumeric()
            && plugin_id
                .bytes()
                .all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(byte, b'_' | b'-' | b'.')),
        "invalid flat plugin identifier"
    );
    Ok(format!("{plugin_id}.json"))
}

fn remove_file(directory: &File, name: &str) -> Result<()> {
    match nix::unistd::unlinkat(
        Some(directory.as_raw_fd()),
        name,
        UnlinkatFlags::NoRemoveDir,
    ) {
        Ok(()) | Err(Errno::ENOENT) => Ok(()),
        Err(error) => Err(error.into()),
    }
}

fn write_file(
    directory: &File,
    name: &str,
    bytes: &[u8],
    mode: u32,
    gid: Option<u32>,
) -> Result<()> {
    #[cfg(test)]
    tests::write_fault(name)?;
    let mut allocated = None;
    for _ in 0..32 {
        let sequence = super::TEMP_SEQUENCE.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
        let candidate = format!(".{name}.tmp.{}.{}", std::process::id(), sequence);
        match open_at(
            directory,
            candidate.as_ref(),
            OFlag::O_WRONLY | OFlag::O_CREAT | OFlag::O_EXCL,
            mode,
        ) {
            Ok(file) => {
                allocated = Some((candidate, file));
                break;
            }
            Err(Errno::EEXIST) => {}
            Err(error) => return Err(error.into()),
        }
    }
    let (temporary, mut file) =
        allocated.context("cannot allocate private projection temporary file")?;
    let result = (|| -> Result<()> {
        file.set_permissions(std::fs::Permissions::from_mode(mode))?;
        if let Some(gid) = gid {
            nix::unistd::fchown(file.as_raw_fd(), None, Some(Gid::from_raw(gid)))?;
        }
        file.write_all(bytes)?;
        file.sync_all()?;
        drop(file);
        // Rename is the last fallible step. In particular, no error after a
        // successful commit-manifest rename may incorrectly trigger rollback.
        nix::fcntl::renameat(
            Some(directory.as_raw_fd()),
            temporary.as_str(),
            Some(directory.as_raw_fd()),
            name,
        )?;
        Ok(())
    })();
    if result.is_err() {
        let _ = remove_file(directory, &temporary);
    }
    result
}

fn restore_file(
    directory: &File,
    name: &str,
    previous: Option<&[u8]>,
    mode: u32,
    gid: Option<u32>,
) -> Result<()> {
    match previous {
        Some(bytes) => write_file(directory, name, bytes, mode, gid),
        None => remove_file(directory, name),
    }
}

/// Writer-startup preparation only. Generic readers never create the lock or
/// a directory. This also enables locked reads of existing canonical raw state
/// and generation manifests after upgrading from the previous implementation.
pub fn prepare_projection_directory_in(state_dir: &str) -> Result<()> {
    let _lock = LockedDirectory::open(state_dir, true)?.context("projection directory missing")?;
    Ok(())
}

/// Read a consistent raw state snapshot for IDs already selected by the
/// caller's sealed catalog. No enumeration, credential read or retired
/// fallback. Service readers must apply the sealed exposure policy before
/// sending these bytes over a public transport.
pub fn read_projection_snapshot_in(
    state_dir: &str,
    plugin_ids: &[String],
) -> Result<ProjectionSnapshot> {
    for plugin in plugin_ids {
        filename(plugin)?;
    }
    let Some(locked) = LockedDirectory::open(state_dir, false)? else {
        return Ok(ProjectionSnapshot {
            generation: 0,
            states: BTreeMap::new(),
        });
    };
    read_locked_snapshot(&locked, plugin_ids)
}

fn read_locked_snapshot(
    locked: &LockedDirectory,
    plugin_ids: &[String],
) -> Result<ProjectionSnapshot> {
    let Some((manifest, _)) = locked.manifest()? else {
        // Uncommitted files beside a missing manifest are not state authority.
        return Ok(ProjectionSnapshot {
            generation: 0,
            states: BTreeMap::new(),
        });
    };
    let mut states = BTreeMap::new();
    for plugin in plugin_ids {
        manifest.require_available(plugin)?;
        if let Some(bytes) =
            read_file(&locked.directory, &filename(plugin)?, MAX_PROJECTION, false)?
        {
            states.insert(plugin.clone(), bytes);
        }
    }
    Ok(ProjectionSnapshot {
        generation: manifest.generation,
        states,
    })
}

pub fn read_projection_snapshot(plugin_ids: &[String]) -> Result<ProjectionSnapshot> {
    read_projection_snapshot_in(&super::shm_state_dir(), plugin_ids)
}

type CredentialPairPublication<'a> = (&'a File, Option<Vec<u8>>, Option<Vec<u8>>, u32);

fn publish(
    locked: &LockedDirectory,
    old_manifest: Option<(Manifest, Vec<u8>)>,
    name: &str,
    previous: Option<Vec<u8>>,
    current: Option<Vec<u8>>,
    credential: Option<CredentialPairPublication<'_>>,
) -> Result<ProjectionCommit> {
    let projection_mode = if credential.is_some() { 0o644 } else { 0o600 };
    if let Some(bytes) = &current {
        ensure!(
            bytes.len() as u64 <= MAX_PROJECTION,
            "projection exceeds size limit"
        );
    }
    if let Some((_, _, Some(bytes), _)) = &credential {
        ensure!(
            bytes.len() as u64 <= MAX_PROJECTION,
            "credential projection exceeds size limit"
        );
    }
    let old_generation = old_manifest
        .as_ref()
        .map_or(0, |(manifest, _)| manifest.generation);
    let private_changed = credential
        .as_ref()
        .is_some_and(|(_, old, new, _)| old != new);
    if previous == current && !private_changed {
        return Ok(ProjectionCommit {
            generation: old_generation,
            previous,
            current,
        });
    }
    let generation = old_generation
        .checked_add(1)
        .context("projection generation overflow")?;
    let intent = simd_json::to_vec(&Manifest {
        generation: old_generation,
        publishing: true,
        credential_pending: old_manifest
            .as_ref()
            .and_then(|(manifest, _)| manifest.credential_pending.clone()),
        document_pending: old_manifest
            .as_ref()
            .and_then(|(manifest, _)| manifest.document_pending.clone()),
    })?;
    write_file(&locked.directory, MANIFEST_NAME, &intent, 0o644, None)?;
    let result = (|| -> Result<()> {
        if let Some((directory, _, bytes, gid)) = &credential {
            restore_file(directory, name, bytes.as_deref(), 0o640, Some(*gid))?;
        }
        restore_file(
            &locked.directory,
            name,
            current.as_deref(),
            projection_mode,
            None,
        )?;
        let committed = simd_json::to_vec(&Manifest {
            generation,
            publishing: false,
            credential_pending: old_manifest
                .as_ref()
                .and_then(|(manifest, _)| manifest.credential_pending.clone()),
            document_pending: old_manifest
                .as_ref()
                .and_then(|(manifest, _)| manifest.document_pending.clone()),
        })?;
        write_file(&locked.directory, MANIFEST_NAME, &committed, 0o644, None)?;
        Ok(())
    })();
    if let Err(error) = result {
        let restore_public = restore_file(
            &locked.directory,
            name,
            previous.as_deref(),
            projection_mode,
            None,
        );
        let restore_private = match &credential {
            Some((directory, previous, _, gid)) => {
                restore_file(directory, name, previous.as_deref(), 0o640, Some(*gid))
            }
            None => Ok(()),
        };
        if restore_public.is_ok() && restore_private.is_ok() {
            restore_file(&locked.directory, MANIFEST_NAME, old_manifest.as_ref().map(|(_, bytes)| bytes.as_slice()), 0o644, None)
                .context("projection rollback restored files but could not restore the manifest; state remains unreadable")?;
            return Err(error)
                .context("projection publication failed; previous committed state restored");
        }
        bail!("projection publication failed ({error}); rollback incomplete (public={restore_public:?}, private={restore_private:?}); in-progress manifest retained and state is unreadable")
    }
    Ok(ProjectionCommit {
        generation,
        previous,
        current,
    })
}

/// Fold opaque JSON bytes under the same exclusive filesystem lock used for
/// publication. The closure must be synchronous, side-effect-free, and must not
/// call another projection helper (locks are intentionally not reentrant).
/// Returning None deletes only this public projection; credential bytes are
/// never read or deleted by the generic API.
pub fn update_projection_in(
    state_dir: &str,
    plugin_id: &str,
    fold: impl FnOnce(Option<&[u8]>) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>>,
) -> Result<ProjectionCommit> {
    let name = filename(plugin_id)?;
    let locked = LockedDirectory::open(state_dir, true)?.context("projection directory missing")?;
    update_locked_projection(&locked, plugin_id, &name, fold)
}

fn update_locked_projection(
    locked: &LockedDirectory,
    plugin_id: &str,
    name: &str,
    fold: impl FnOnce(Option<&[u8]>) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>>,
) -> Result<ProjectionCommit> {
    let manifest = locked.manifest()?;
    if let Some((manifest, _)) = &manifest {
        manifest.require_available(plugin_id)?;
    }
    restrict_file_mode(&locked.directory, name)?;
    let previous = read_file(&locked.directory, name, MAX_PROJECTION, false)?;
    ensure!(
        manifest.is_some() || previous.is_none(),
        "uncommitted projection file exists without a manifest; refusing to overwrite it"
    );
    let current = fold(previous.as_deref())?;
    publish(locked, manifest, name, previous, current, None)
}

fn restrict_file_mode(directory: &File, name: &str) -> Result<()> {
    let file = match open_at(
        directory,
        name.as_ref(),
        OFlag::O_RDONLY | OFlag::O_NONBLOCK,
        0,
    ) {
        Ok(file) => file,
        Err(Errno::ENOENT) => return Ok(()),
        Err(error) => return Err(error).context("open raw state for service-only mode repair"),
    };
    check_file(&file, false, directory.metadata()?.uid())?;
    file.set_permissions(std::fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o600))?;
    Ok(())
}

/// Upgrade one caller-selected, manifest-pinned raw state file to service-only
/// access without changing bytes or generation. No scans or group changes.
/// The identity pair has a separate redacted public file and must use its
/// dedicated publication path instead.
pub fn restrict_projection_file_in(state_dir: &str, plugin_id: &str) -> Result<()> {
    ensure!(
        plugin_id != "identity_sled",
        "identity public metadata uses paired publication permissions"
    );
    let name = filename(plugin_id)?;
    let locked = LockedDirectory::open(state_dir, true)?.context("projection directory missing")?;
    locked.manifest()?;
    restrict_file_mode(&locked.directory, &name)
}

pub fn update_projection(
    plugin_id: &str,
    fold: impl FnOnce(Option<&[u8]>) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>>,
) -> Result<ProjectionCommit> {
    update_projection_in(&super::shm_state_dir(), plugin_id, fold)
}

/// Publish public redacted and protected credential projections as one commit.
/// The closure sees PRIVATE prior bytes and returns Some((public, private)),
/// or None to delete both files. The returned receipt and all generic readers
/// contain only public bytes. Identical pairs do not advance the generation.
pub fn update_projection_with_credentials_in(
    state_dir: &str,
    plugin_id: &str,
    credential_gid: u32,
    fold: impl FnOnce(Option<&[u8]>) -> Result<Option<(Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>)>>,
) -> Result<ProjectionCommit> {
    let name = filename(plugin_id)?;
    let locked = LockedDirectory::open(state_dir, true)?.context("projection directory missing")?;
    let manifest = locked.manifest()?;
    if let Some((manifest, _)) = &manifest {
        manifest.require_available(plugin_id)?;
    }
    let private_path = super::credential_projection_dir_for_state_dir(state_dir);
    locked.enable_credential_readers(credential_gid)?;
    let private = directory(Path::new(&private_path), true, 0o750)?
        .context("credential directory missing")?;
    private.set_permissions(std::fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o750))?;
    nix::unistd::fchown(
        private.as_raw_fd(),
        None,
        Some(Gid::from_raw(credential_gid)),
    )?;
    let previous = read_file(&locked.directory, &name, MAX_PROJECTION, false)?;
    let old_private = read_file(&private, &name, MAX_PROJECTION, true)?;
    ensure!(
        manifest.is_some() || (previous.is_none() && old_private.is_none()),
        "uncommitted identity projection exists without a manifest; refusing to overwrite it"
    );
    let (public, credential) = match fold(old_private.as_deref())? {
        Some((public, credential)) => (Some(public), Some(credential)),
        None => (None, None),
    };
    publish(
        &locked,
        manifest,
        &name,
        previous,
        public,
        Some((&private, old_private, credential, credential_gid)),
    )
}

pub(super) fn read_credential_in(state_dir: &str, plugin_id: &str) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>> {
    let name = filename(plugin_id)?;
    let Some(locked) = LockedDirectory::open(state_dir, false)? else {
        return Ok(None);
    };
    let Some((manifest, _)) = locked.manifest()? else {
        return Ok(None);
    };
    manifest.require_available(plugin_id)?;
    let private_path = super::credential_projection_dir_for_state_dir(state_dir);
    let Some(private) = directory(Path::new(&private_path), false, 0)? else {
        return Ok(None);
    };
    ensure!(
        private.metadata()?.mode() & 0o007 == 0,
        "credential directory must not be world accessible"
    );
    read_file(&private, &name, MAX_PROJECTION, true)
}

#[path = "identity_projection_transaction.rs"]

<file path="op-core/src/runit.rs">
//! Runit service-supervision paths — the single source of truth.
//!
//! This host boots **runit** as PID 1 and is controlled with `sv`. There is no
//! s6 installed: `s6-rc`, `s6-svc`, `s6-svstat` and `service6` are all absent,
//! so any code that spawns them fails at runtime. Import these constants
//! instead of hardcoding paths, so the layout is stated once.
//!
//! Verified layout:
//!
//! | Path | Meaning |
//! |---|---|
//! | `/etc/runit/sv/<svc>` | Service definition (`run`, optional `log/run`) |
//! | `/etc/runit/runsvdir/default/<svc>` | Symlink enabling the service at boot |
//! | `/run/runit/service` | Tree that `runsvdir -P` supervises |
//! | `/etc/runit/sv/<svc>/down` | Marker: do not auto-start when supervised |
//!
//! Runit has no compiled service database (unlike s6-rc): `runsvdir` picks up
//! directory changes on its own, so there is nothing to recompile after editing
//! a definition — edit the `run` script, then `sv restart <svc>`.
//!
//! OSCAL subid: `src.service.runit.paths@v1`

/// Service definitions live here, one directory per service.
pub const SV_DIR: &str = "/etc/runit/sv";

/// Enablement symlinks for the `default` runlevel (`current -> default`).
pub const RUNSVDIR_DEFAULT: &str = "/etc/runit/runsvdir/default";

/// The live supervised tree (`runsvdir -P /run/runit/service`).
pub const SERVICE_DIR: &str = "/run/runit/service";

/// The control binary. Requires root to read `supervise/ok`.
pub const SV_BIN: &str = "sv";

/// The supervisor process name, used for liveness probes.
pub const RUNSVDIR_PROC: &str = "runsvdir";

/// Definition directory for a service: `/etc/runit/sv/<service>`.
pub fn definition_path(service: &str) -> String {
    format!("{SV_DIR}/{service}")
}

/// Live supervised path for a service: `/run/runit/service/<service>`.
pub fn live_path(service: &str) -> String {
    format!("{SERVICE_DIR}/{service}")
}

/// Boot-persistent enablement symlink: `/etc/runit/runsvdir/default/<service>`.
pub fn enabled_path(service: &str) -> String {
    format!("{RUNSVDIR_DEFAULT}/{service}")
}

/// Supervise status file that `sv` and `runsv` maintain:
/// `/run/runit/service/<service>/supervise/stat`.
pub fn supervise_stat_path(service: &str) -> String {
    format!("{SERVICE_DIR}/{service}/supervise/stat")
}

/// Per-service log directory written by the `log/run` companion service.
pub fn log_current_path(service: &str) -> String {
    format!("/var/log/sv/{service}/current")
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn paths_match_the_verified_host_layout() {
        assert_eq!(definition_path("op-web"), "/etc/runit/sv/op-web");
        assert_eq!(live_path("op-web"), "/run/runit/service/op-web");
        assert_eq!(enabled_path("op-web"), "/etc/runit/runsvdir/default/op-web");
        assert_eq!(
            supervise_stat_path("op-web"),
            "/run/runit/service/op-web/supervise/stat"
        );
    }

    /// The s6 tree must never reappear in these constants.
    #[test]
    fn no_s6_paths() {
        for path in [SV_DIR, RUNSVDIR_DEFAULT, SERVICE_DIR] {
            assert!(!path.contains("s6"), "{path} still references s6");
        }
        assert_ne!(SERVICE_DIR, "/run/service", "that is the s6 tree");
    }
}
</file>

<file path="op-core/src/security.rs">
//! Core security types and access control logic
//!
//! Provides IP-based access zones and security levels used across the system.

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

/// Security level for resources/tools
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, Default)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum SecurityLevel {
    /// Safe, read-only operations - any IP
    #[default]
    Public,
    /// Normal operations - any IP
    Standard,
    /// System modifications - localhost or private network
    Elevated,
    /// Dangerous commands - localhost only
    Restricted,
}

impl SecurityLevel {
    pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Self {
        match s.to_lowercase().as_str() {
            "public" => Self::Public,
            "standard" => Self::Standard,
            "elevated" => Self::Elevated,
            "restricted" => Self::Restricted,
            _ => Self::Standard,
        }
    }
}

/// IP-based access control zones
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, Default)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum AccessZone {
    /// 127.0.0.1, ::1 - full access to everything
    Localhost,
    /// Trusted VPN/mesh networks (Netmaker, Tailscale, etc.) - full access
    TrustedMesh,
    /// 192.168.x.x, 10.x.x.x, 172.16-31.x.x - elevated access
    PrivateNetwork,
    /// Public IPs - restricted to safe tools only
    #[default]
    Public,
}

impl AccessZone {
    /// Detect access zone from IP address string
    pub fn from_ip(ip: &str) -> Self {
        Self::from_ip_with_config(ip, &NetworkConfig::default())
    }

    /// Detect access zone with custom network configuration
    pub fn from_ip_with_config(ip: &str, config: &NetworkConfig) -> Self {
        let ip = ip.trim();

        // 1. Localhost - always full access
        if Self::is_localhost(ip) {
            return Self::Localhost;
        }

        // 2. Check custom trusted networks first (from config or env)
        if config.is_trusted(ip) {
            return Self::TrustedMesh;
        }

        // 3. Known VPN/mesh networks - auto-detect common ranges
        if Self::is_mesh_network(ip) {
            return Self::TrustedMesh;
        }

        // 4. Standard private networks (RFC 1918)
        if Self::is_private_network(ip) {
            return Self::PrivateNetwork;
        }

        Self::Public
    }

    fn is_localhost(ip: &str) -> bool {
        ip == "127.0.0.1" || ip == "::1" || ip == "localhost" || ip.starts_with("127.")
    }

    /// Check for known VPN/mesh network ranges
    fn is_mesh_network(ip: &str) -> bool {
        // Netmaker default ranges (commonly 10.x.x.x but checking specific patterns)
        // Netmaker often uses: 10.101.0.0/16, 10.102.0.0/16, etc.
        if ip.starts_with("10.101.") || ip.starts_with("10.102.") || ip.starts_with("10.103.") {
            return true;
        }

        // Tailscale CGNAT range: 100.64.0.0/10 (100.64.x.x - 100.127.x.x)
        if let Some(first) = ip.split('.').next() {
            if first == "100" {
                if let Some(second) = ip.split('.').nth(1) {
                    if let Ok(n) = second.parse::<u8>() {
                        if (64..=127).contains(&n) {
                            return true;
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        // ZeroTier default range: often 10.147.x.x, 10.244.x.x
        if ip.starts_with("10.147.") || ip.starts_with("10.244.") {
            return true;
        }

        // WireGuard common ranges: often 10.0.0.x, 10.200.x.x, 10.66.66.x
        if ip.starts_with("10.0.0.") || ip.starts_with("10.200.") || ip.starts_with("10.66.66.") {
            return true;
        }

        // Nebula default: often 10.42.x.x
        if ip.starts_with("10.42.") {
            return true;
        }

        // IPv6 ULA for mesh (fd00::/8)
        if ip.starts_with("fd") {
            return true;
        }

        false
    }

    fn is_private_network(ip: &str) -> bool {
        // RFC 1918 private ranges
        if ip.starts_with("192.168.") || ip.starts_with("10.") {
            return true;
        }

        // 172.16.0.0 - 172.31.255.255
        if let Some(rest) = ip.strip_prefix("172.") {
            if let Some(second_octet) = rest.split('.').next() {
                if let Ok(n) = second_octet.parse::<u8>() {
                    if (16..=31).contains(&n) {
                        return true;
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        // IPv6 link-local
        if ip.starts_with("fe80") {
            return true;
        }

        false
    }

    /// Check if this zone can access a security level
    pub fn can_access(&self, level: SecurityLevel) -> bool {
        match (self, level) {
            // Localhost can access everything
            (Self::Localhost, _) => true,

            // Trusted mesh (Netmaker, Tailscale, etc.) - full access like localhost
            (Self::TrustedMesh, _) => true,

            // Private network: public, standard, elevated (not restricted)
            (Self::PrivateNetwork, SecurityLevel::Public) => true,
            (Self::PrivateNetwork, SecurityLevel::Standard) => true,
            (Self::PrivateNetwork, SecurityLevel::Elevated) => true,
            (Self::PrivateNetwork, SecurityLevel::Restricted) => false,

            // Public: only public and standard
            (Self::Public, SecurityLevel::Public) => true,
            (Self::Public, SecurityLevel::Standard) => true,
            (Self::Public, _) => false,
        }
    }

    /// Get human-readable description
    pub fn description(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Localhost => "localhost (full access)",
            Self::TrustedMesh => "trusted mesh/VPN (full access)",
            Self::PrivateNetwork => "private network (elevated access)",
            Self::Public => "public network (limited access)",
        }
    }
}

/// Network configuration for trusted ranges
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct NetworkConfig {
    /// Custom trusted CIDR ranges (e.g., "10.50.0.0/16")
    #[serde(default)]
    pub trusted_cidrs: Vec<String>,

    /// Custom trusted IP prefixes (e.g., "10.50.")
    #[serde(default)]
    pub trusted_prefixes: Vec<String>,

    /// Exact trusted IPs
    #[serde(default)]
    pub trusted_ips: Vec<String>,

    /// Auto-detect Tailscale networks  
    #[serde(default = "default_true")]
    pub auto_tailscale: bool,

    /// Auto-detect ZeroTier networks
    #[serde(default = "default_true")]
    pub auto_zerotier: bool,

    /// Auto-detect WireGuard common ranges
    #[serde(default = "default_true")]
    pub auto_wireguard: bool,
}

fn default_true() -> bool {
    true
}

impl Default for NetworkConfig {
    fn default() -> Self {
        // Also check environment variable for additional trusted networks
        let env_trusted: Vec<String> = std::env::var("OP_TRUSTED_NETWORKS")
            .unwrap_or_default()
            .split(',')
            .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
            .map(|s| s.trim().to_string())
            .collect();

        Self {
            trusted_cidrs: env_trusted,
            trusted_prefixes: vec![],
            trusted_ips: vec![],
            auto_tailscale: true,
            auto_zerotier: true,
            auto_wireguard: true,
        }
    }
}

impl NetworkConfig {
    /// Create new network config
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self::default()
    }

    /// Add a trusted CIDR range (e.g., "10.50.0.0/16")
    pub fn trust_cidr(mut self, cidr: &str) -> Self {
        self.trusted_cidrs.push(cidr.to_string());
        self
    }

    /// Add a trusted prefix (e.g., "10.50." for 10.50.x.x)
    pub fn trust_prefix(mut self, prefix: &str) -> Self {
        self.trusted_prefixes.push(prefix.to_string());
        self
    }

    /// Add a trusted IP
    pub fn trust_ip(mut self, ip: &str) -> Self {
        self.trusted_ips.push(ip.to_string());
        self
    }

    /// Check if an IP is in trusted networks
    pub fn is_trusted(&self, ip: &str) -> bool {
        // Check exact IPs
        if self.trusted_ips.contains(&ip.to_string()) {
            return true;
        }

        // Check prefixes
        for prefix in &self.trusted_prefixes {
            if ip.starts_with(prefix) {
                return true;
            }
        }

        // Check CIDRs (simplified - just checks prefix for now)
        for cidr in &self.trusted_cidrs {
            if let Some(network) = cidr.split('/').next() {
                // Simple prefix match based on CIDR
                let prefix = Self::cidr_to_prefix(network, cidr);
                if ip.starts_with(&prefix) {
                    return true;
                }
            }
        }

        false
    }

    /// Convert CIDR to prefix for simple matching
    fn cidr_to_prefix(network: &str, cidr: &str) -> String {
        let mask: u8 = cidr
            .split('/')
            .nth(1)
            .and_then(|m| m.parse().ok())
            .unwrap_or(24);

        let octets: Vec<&str> = network.split('.').collect();

        match mask {
            0..=8 => octets
                .first()
                .map(|s| format!("{}.", s))
                .unwrap_or_default(),
            9..=16 => {
                if octets.len() >= 2 {
                    format!("{}.{}.", octets[0], octets[1])
                } else {
                    network.to_string()
                }
            }
            17..=24 => {
                if octets.len() >= 3 {
                    format!("{}.{}.{}.", octets[0], octets[1], octets[2])
                } else {
                    network.to_string()
                }
            }
            _ => network.to_string(),
        }
    }
}

/// Quick helper to create trusted network config
pub fn trust_networks(prefixes: &[&str]) -> NetworkConfig {
    let mut config = NetworkConfig::new();
    for prefix in prefixes {
        config = config.trust_prefix(prefix);
    }
    config
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn test_ip_detection() {
        // Localhost
        assert_eq!(AccessZone::from_ip("127.0.0.1"), AccessZone::Localhost);
        assert_eq!(AccessZone::from_ip("::1"), AccessZone::Localhost);
        assert_eq!(AccessZone::from_ip("localhost"), AccessZone::Localhost);

        // Tailscale (100.64.0.0/10)
        assert_eq!(AccessZone::from_ip("100.64.1.1"), AccessZone::TrustedMesh);
        assert_eq!(AccessZone::from_ip("100.100.50.1"), AccessZone::TrustedMesh);
        assert_eq!(
            AccessZone::from_ip("100.127.255.255"),
            AccessZone::TrustedMesh
        );

        // Netmaker common ranges
        assert_eq!(AccessZone::from_ip("10.101.0.5"), AccessZone::TrustedMesh);
        assert_eq!(AccessZone::from_ip("10.102.1.1"), AccessZone::TrustedMesh);

        // ZeroTier
        assert_eq!(AccessZone::from_ip("10.147.20.1"), AccessZone::TrustedMesh);

        // WireGuard common
        assert_eq!(AccessZone::from_ip("10.0.0.5"), AccessZone::TrustedMesh);
        assert_eq!(AccessZone::from_ip("10.66.66.1"), AccessZone::TrustedMesh);

        // Private networks (non-mesh)
        assert_eq!(
            AccessZone::from_ip("192.168.1.100"),
            AccessZone::PrivateNetwork
        );
        assert_eq!(AccessZone::from_ip("10.1.0.1"), AccessZone::PrivateNetwork); // Generic 10.x
        assert_eq!(
            AccessZone::from_ip("172.16.0.1"),
            AccessZone::PrivateNetwork
        );
        assert_eq!(
            AccessZone::from_ip("172.31.255.255"),
            AccessZone::PrivateNetwork
        );

        // Public
        assert_eq!(AccessZone::from_ip("8.8.8.8"), AccessZone::Public);
        assert_eq!(AccessZone::from_ip("172.15.0.1"), AccessZone::Public); // Not in 172.16-31
        assert_eq!(AccessZone::from_ip("172.32.0.1"), AccessZone::Public);
        assert_eq!(AccessZone::from_ip("100.63.0.1"), AccessZone::Public); // Just below Tailscale range
        assert_eq!(AccessZone::from_ip("100.128.0.1"), AccessZone::Public); // Just above Tailscale range
    }
}
</file>

<file path="op-core/src/self_identity.rs">
//! Self-Repository Identity
//!
//! Provides awareness of the chatbot's own source code repository.

use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::process::Command;
use tracing::info;

/// Get the self-repository path from environment
pub fn get_self_repo_path() -> Option<PathBuf> {
    std::env::var("OP_SELF_REPO_PATH")
        .ok()
        .map(PathBuf::from)
        .filter(|p| p.exists())
}

/// Check if self-repository is configured
pub fn is_self_repo_configured() -> bool {
    get_self_repo_path().is_some()
}

/// Information about the self-repository
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct SelfRepositoryInfo {
    pub path: PathBuf,
    pub name: String,
    pub branch: Option<String>,
    pub commit: Option<String>,
    pub has_changes: bool,
    pub has_git: bool,
}

impl SelfRepositoryInfo {
    /// Gather information about the self-repository
    pub fn gather() -> Option<Self> {
        let path = get_self_repo_path()?;

        let name = path
            .file_name()
            .map(|n| n.to_string_lossy().to_string())
            .unwrap_or_else(|| "unknown".to_string());

        let has_git = path.join(".git").exists();

        let (branch, commit, has_changes) = if has_git {
            (
                Self::get_git_branch(&path),
                Self::get_git_commit(&path),
                Self::check_git_changes(&path),
            )
        } else {
            (None, None, false)
        };

        info!(
            "Self-repository: {} at {:?} (branch: {:?}, commit: {:?})",
            name, path, branch, commit
        );

        Some(Self {
            path,
            name,
            branch,
            commit,
            has_changes,
            has_git,
        })
    }

    fn get_git_branch(path: &PathBuf) -> Option<String> {
        let output = Command::new("git")
            .args(["branch", "--show-current"])
            .current_dir(path)
            .output()
            .ok()?;

        if output.status.success() {
            let branch = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).trim().to_string();
            if !branch.is_empty() {
                return Some(branch);
            }
        }
        None
    }

    fn get_git_commit(path: &PathBuf) -> Option<String> {
        let output = Command::new("git")
            .args(["rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD"])
            .current_dir(path)
            .output()
            .ok()?;

        if output.status.success() {
            let commit = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).trim().to_string();
            if !commit.is_empty() {
                return Some(commit);
            }
        }
        None
    }

    fn check_git_changes(path: &PathBuf) -> bool {
        Command::new("git")
            .args(["status", "--porcelain"])
            .current_dir(path)
            .output()
            .ok()
            .map(|o| !String::from_utf8_lossy(&o.stdout).trim().is_empty())
            .unwrap_or(false)
    }

    /// Generate system prompt context for self-awareness
    pub fn to_system_prompt_context(&self) -> String {
        let git_info = if self.has_git {
            format!(
                "**Branch**: `{}`\n**Commit**: `{}`\n**Uncommitted Changes**: {}",
                self.branch.as_deref().unwrap_or("unknown"),
                self.commit.as_deref().unwrap_or("unknown"),
                if self.has_changes {
                    "Yes ⚠️"
                } else {
                    "No ✓"
                }
            )
        } else {
            "Not a git repository".to_string()
        };

        format!(
            r#"## 🔮 SELF-AWARENESS: YOUR OWN SOURCE CODE

You have access to your own source code. This IS you.

**Repository Path**: `{}`
**Repository Name**: `{}`
{}

### Self-Modification Tools
| Tool | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `self_read_file` | Read your source files |
| `self_write_file` | Modify your source files |
| `self_list_directory` | Explore your codebase |
| `self_search_code` | Search your code |
| `self_git_status` | Check git status |
| `self_git_diff` | View pending changes |
| `self_git_commit` | Commit changes |
| `self_git_log` | View history |
| `self_build` | Build yourself |
| `self_deploy` | Deploy yourself |

**⚠️ Changes to your code affect your own capabilities!**"#,
            self.path.display(),
            self.name,
            git_info
        )
    }
}
</file>

use anyhow::Result;
use async_trait::async_trait;
use simd_json::OwnedValue as Value;
use std::fmt::Debug;

    PropertySet,
    Signal,
    Deleted,

    async fn publish_change(
        &self,

        change_type: ChangeType,
