<file path="op-grpc-bridge/src/dynamic_reflection.rs">
//! Active blob-backed gRPC reflection.
//!
//! `tonic_reflection::server::Builder` freezes its descriptor index at build
//! time. This module keeps the descriptor files indexed, but advertises service
//! names from the active plugin object blobs so discovery follows D-Bus object
//! lifetime.

use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet, HashMap};
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::sync::Arc;

use prost::Message;
use prost_types::{
    DescriptorProto, EnumDescriptorProto, FieldDescriptorProto, FileDescriptorProto,
    FileDescriptorSet,
};
use tokio::sync::{mpsc, RwLock};
use tokio_stream::{wrappers::ReceiverStream, StreamExt};
use tonic::{Request, Response, Status, Streaming};
use tonic_reflection::pb::v1::server_reflection_request::MessageRequest;
use tonic_reflection::pb::v1::server_reflection_response::MessageResponse;
use tonic_reflection::pb::v1::server_reflection_server::{
    ServerReflection, ServerReflectionServer,
};
use tonic_reflection::pb::v1::{
    ExtensionNumberResponse, FileDescriptorResponse, ListServiceResponse, ServerReflectionRequest,
    ServerReflectionResponse, ServiceResponse,
};

use crate::plugin_object_blob::PluginObjectBlob;

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ActiveReflectionCatalog {
    inner: Arc<RwLock<ActiveReflectionInner>>,
    shm_dir: PathBuf,
}

impl Default for ActiveReflectionCatalog {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::with_dir(crate::sealed_schema_reader::blob_catalog_dir_from_env())
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
struct ActiveReflectionInner {
    descriptor_sets: Vec<Vec<u8>>,
    blobs: BTreeMap<String, PluginObjectBlob>,
    index: ReflectionIndex,
    /// Last stored catalog hash, used only for change logging. Schema hashes
    /// do not cover descriptor/manifest producer revisions, so this must not
    /// suppress arrival-triggered replacement of the pinned artifacts.
    catalog_hash: Option<String>,
}

impl Default for ActiveReflectionInner {
    fn default() -> Self {
        let mut inner = Self {
            descriptor_sets: Vec::new(),
            blobs: BTreeMap::new(),
            index: ReflectionIndex::default(),
            catalog_hash: None,
        };
        inner
            .descriptor_sets
            .push(crate::proto::FILE_DESCRIPTOR_SET.to_vec());
        inner
            .descriptor_sets
            .push(tonic_reflection::pb::v1::FILE_DESCRIPTOR_SET.to_vec());
        inner.rebuild_index();
        inner
    }
}

impl ActiveReflectionCatalog {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self::default()
    }

    pub fn with_dir(shm_dir: PathBuf) -> Self {
        Self {
            inner: Arc::new(RwLock::new(ActiveReflectionInner::default())),
            shm_dir,
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn catalog_dir(&self) -> &std::path::Path {
        &self.shm_dir
    }

    /// Arrival-triggered resync reads the complete manifest-pinned artifacts.
    /// The sealer commits its manifest last. Every arrival replaces the index,
    /// even when schema/catalog hashes are unchanged: a producer revision can
    /// change descriptor or manifest bytes without changing schema JSON. No
    /// watcher, polling loop, consumer hash, or parallel revision authority.
    pub async fn sync_from_shm(&self) -> usize {
        // Serialize snapshot loads so an older concurrent reader cannot
        // overwrite newer advertisements. Even an unchanged manifest is
        // checked for missing/corrupt pinned files; no directory is scanned.
        let mut inner = self.inner.write().await;
        let directory = self.shm_dir.clone();
        let loaded = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
            crate::sealed_schema_reader::read_manifest_pinned_catalog(&directory)
        })
        .await
        .map_err(anyhow::Error::from)
        .and_then(|result| result);
        let catalog = match loaded {
            Ok(catalog) => catalog,
            Err(error) => {
                tracing::warn!(%error, "sealed reflection catalog unavailable or invalid; clearing plugin advertisements");
                inner.blobs.clear();
                inner.catalog_hash = None;
                inner.rebuild_index();
                return 0;
            }
        };
        let count = catalog.plugins.len();
        if inner.catalog_hash.as_deref() != Some(catalog.catalog_hash.as_str()) {
            tracing::info!(count, "reflection loaded committed sealed catalog");
        }
        inner.blobs = catalog
            .plugins
            .into_iter()
            .map(|(id, document)| (id, document.blob))
            .collect();
        inner.catalog_hash = Some(catalog.catalog_hash);
        inner.rebuild_index();
        count
    }

    pub async fn list_services(&self) -> Vec<String> {
        self.inner.read().await.index.service_names.clone()
    }

    async fn file_by_filename(&self, filename: &str) -> Result<Vec<u8>, Status> {
        self.inner.read().await.index.file_by_filename(filename)
    }

    async fn symbol_by_name(&self, symbol: &str) -> Result<Vec<u8>, Status> {
        self.inner.read().await.index.symbol_by_name(symbol)
    }
}

impl ActiveReflectionInner {
    fn rebuild_index(&mut self) {
        // A sealed blob proves plugin presence, not that every descriptor in
        // it has a mounted RPC handler. The blob's operation.method.* entries
        // are schema metadata; add_routes mounts operation.plugin.v1.* instead.
        // Advertise only those mounted services, gated by live blob presence.
        // This table is generated alongside add_routes, not an existence check
        // against the Rust plugin registry. Blob descriptors remain readable.
        let active_services = crate::grpc_server::LEGACY_PLUGIN_METHOD_SERVICES
            .iter()
            .filter(|(plugin_id, _)| self.blobs.contains_key(*plugin_id))
            .map(|(_, service)| service.to_string())
            .collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();

        let mut index = ReflectionIndex::new(active_services);

        for encoded in self
            .descriptor_sets
            .iter()
            .chain(self.blobs.values().map(|blob| &blob.descriptor_set))
        {
            let Ok(file_set) = FileDescriptorSet::decode(encoded.as_slice()) else {
                continue;
            };
            index.add_file_descriptor_set(file_set);
        }

        self.index = index;
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
struct ReflectionIndex {
    active_services: BTreeSet<String>,
    service_names: Vec<String>,
    files: HashMap<String, Arc<FileDescriptorProto>>,
    symbols: HashMap<String, Arc<FileDescriptorProto>>,
}

impl ReflectionIndex {
    fn new(active_services: BTreeSet<String>) -> Self {
        Self {
            active_services,
            service_names: Vec::new(),
            files: HashMap::new(),
            symbols: HashMap::new(),
        }
    }

    fn add_file_descriptor_set(&mut self, file_set: FileDescriptorSet) {
        for file in file_set.file {
            let Some(name) = file.name.clone() else {
                continue;
            };
            if self.files.contains_key(&name) {
                continue;
            }

            let file = Arc::new(file);
            self.files.insert(name, file.clone());
            self.process_file(file);
        }

        self.service_names.sort();
        self.service_names.dedup();
    }

    fn process_file(&mut self, file: Arc<FileDescriptorProto>) {
        let prefix = file.package.clone().unwrap_or_default();

        for message in &file.message_type {
            self.process_message(file.clone(), &prefix, message);
        }
        for enum_type in &file.enum_type {
            self.process_enum(file.clone(), &prefix, enum_type);
        }
        for service in &file.service {
            let Some(service_name) = extract_name(&prefix, service.name.as_ref()) else {
                continue;
            };
            if self.active_services.contains(&service_name)
                || service_name == "grpc.reflection.v1.ServerReflection"
            {
                self.service_names.push(service_name.clone());
            }
            self.symbols.insert(service_name.clone(), file.clone());

            for method in &service.method {
                if let Some(method_name) = extract_name(&service_name, method.name.as_ref()) {
                    self.symbols.insert(method_name, file.clone());
                }
            }
        }
    }

    fn process_message(
        &mut self,
        file: Arc<FileDescriptorProto>,
        prefix: &str,
        message: &DescriptorProto,
    ) {
        let Some(message_name) = extract_name(prefix, message.name.as_ref()) else {
            return;
        };
        self.symbols.insert(message_name.clone(), file.clone());

        for nested in &message.nested_type {
            self.process_message(file.clone(), &message_name, nested);
        }
        for enum_type in &message.enum_type {
            self.process_enum(file.clone(), &message_name, enum_type);
        }
        for field in &message.field {
            self.process_field(file.clone(), &message_name, field);
        }
        for oneof in &message.oneof_decl {
            if let Some(oneof_name) = extract_name(&message_name, oneof.name.as_ref()) {
                self.symbols.insert(oneof_name, file.clone());
            }
        }
    }

    fn process_enum(
        &mut self,
        file: Arc<FileDescriptorProto>,
        prefix: &str,
        enum_type: &EnumDescriptorProto,
    ) {
        let Some(enum_name) = extract_name(prefix, enum_type.name.as_ref()) else {
            return;
        };
        self.symbols.insert(enum_name.clone(), file.clone());

        for value in &enum_type.value {
            if let Some(value_name) = extract_name(&enum_name, value.name.as_ref()) {
                self.symbols.insert(value_name, file.clone());
            }
        }
    }

    fn process_field(
        &mut self,
        file: Arc<FileDescriptorProto>,
        prefix: &str,
        field: &FieldDescriptorProto,
    ) {
        if let Some(field_name) = extract_name(prefix, field.name.as_ref()) {
            self.symbols.insert(field_name, file);
        }
    }

    // tonic::Status is 176 bytes; Boxing the error would ripple through the
    // shared reflection surface for zero runtime benefit, so the large Err is
    // the deliberate disposition on these three lookup helpers.
    #[allow(clippy::result_large_err)]
    fn symbol_by_name(&self, symbol: &str) -> Result<Vec<u8>, Status> {
        self.encode_file(symbol, self.symbols.get(symbol), "symbol")
    }

    #[allow(clippy::result_large_err)]
    fn file_by_filename(&self, filename: &str) -> Result<Vec<u8>, Status> {
        self.encode_file(filename, self.files.get(filename), "file")
    }

    #[allow(clippy::result_large_err)]
    fn encode_file(
        &self,
        name: &str,
        file: Option<&Arc<FileDescriptorProto>>,
        kind: &str,
    ) -> Result<Vec<u8>, Status> {
        let Some(file) = file else {
            return Err(Status::not_found(format!("{kind} '{name}' not found")));
        };
        let mut encoded = Vec::new();
        file.encode(&mut encoded)
            .map_err(|_| Status::internal("failed to encode descriptor"))?;
        Ok(encoded)
    }
}

fn extract_name(prefix: &str, name: Option<&String>) -> Option<String> {
    let name = name?;
    if prefix.is_empty() {
        Some(name.to_string())
    } else {
        Some(format!("{prefix}.{name}"))
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct DynamicReflectionService {
    catalog: ActiveReflectionCatalog,
}

impl DynamicReflectionService {
    pub fn new(catalog: ActiveReflectionCatalog) -> Self {
        Self { catalog }
    }

    pub fn into_v1_server(self) -> ServerReflectionServer<Self> {
        ServerReflectionServer::new(self)
    }
}

#[tonic::async_trait]
impl ServerReflection for DynamicReflectionService {
    type ServerReflectionInfoStream = ReceiverStream<Result<ServerReflectionResponse, Status>>;

    async fn server_reflection_info(
        &self,
        request: Request<Streaming<ServerReflectionRequest>>,
    ) -> Result<Response<Self::ServerReflectionInfoStream>, Status> {
        let mut request_rx = request.into_inner();
        let (response_tx, response_rx) =
            mpsc::channel::<Result<ServerReflectionResponse, Status>>(1);
        let catalog = self.catalog.clone();

        tokio::spawn(async move {
            while let Some(request) = request_rx.next().await {
                let Ok(request) = request else {
                    return;
                };

                // Arrival-triggered: pick up blobs sealed by the op-blob
                // binary since startup (no-op when the manifest is unchanged).
                catalog.sync_from_shm().await;

                let response = match request.message_request.clone() {
                    None => Err(Status::invalid_argument("invalid MessageRequest")),
                    Some(MessageRequest::FileByFilename(filename)) => catalog
                        .file_by_filename(&filename)
                        .await
                        .map(file_descriptor_response),
                    Some(MessageRequest::FileContainingSymbol(symbol)) => catalog
                        .symbol_by_name(&symbol)
                        .await
                        .map(file_descriptor_response),
                    Some(MessageRequest::FileContainingExtension(_)) => {
                        Err(Status::not_found("extensions are not supported"))
                    }
                    Some(MessageRequest::AllExtensionNumbersOfType(_)) => {
                        Ok(MessageResponse::AllExtensionNumbersResponse(
                            ExtensionNumberResponse::default(),
                        ))
                    }
                    Some(MessageRequest::ListServices(_)) => {
                        let services = catalog
                            .list_services()
                            .await
                            .into_iter()
                            .map(|name| ServiceResponse { name })
                            .collect();
                        Ok(MessageResponse::ListServicesResponse(ListServiceResponse {
                            service: services,
                        }))
                    }
                };

                let send_result = match response {
                    Ok(message_response) => {
                        response_tx
                            .send(Ok(ServerReflectionResponse {
                                valid_host: request.host.clone(),
                                original_request: Some(request),
                                message_response: Some(message_response),
                            }))
                            .await
                    }
                    Err(status) => response_tx.send(Err(status)).await,
                };

                if send_result.is_err() {
                    return;
                }
            }
        });

        Ok(Response::new(ReceiverStream::new(response_rx)))
    }
}

fn file_descriptor_response(file: Vec<u8>) -> MessageResponse {
    MessageResponse::FileDescriptorResponse(FileDescriptorResponse {
        file_descriptor_proto: vec![file],
    })
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn retired_plugin_pinned_by_a_stale_manifest_is_not_advertised() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let seal = |id: &str| {
            let schema = op_state_store::PluginSchema::builder(id)
                .version("1.0.0")
                .method(op_state_store::MethodDecl {
                    name: "Read".into(),
                    args: simd_json::json!({"type":"object", "properties":{}}),
                    returns: Some(simd_json::json!({"type":"object", "properties":{}})),
                    side_effect: op_state_store::SideEffect::Read,
                    idempotent: true,
                    required_capability: Some("fixture.read".into()),
                    subid: "obs.service.fixture.read@v1".into(),
                })
                .build();
            op_blob::blobify_plugin_schema(id, schema)
        };
        let mut producer = op_blob::BlobStore::open(dir.path()).unwrap();
        producer.write(&seal("tched_router")).unwrap();
        // Simulates a catalog sealed before `factory` was retired.
        producer.write(&seal("factory")).unwrap();

        // The manifest pins both blobs; the manifest-pinned reader drops the
        // retired id before reflection ever sees it (sealed_schema_reader).
        let catalog = ActiveReflectionCatalog::with_dir(dir.path().into());
        assert_eq!(
            catalog.sync_from_shm().await,
            1,
            "only the live plugin is loaded"
        );
        let services = catalog.list_services().await;
        assert!(
            services.iter().any(|s| s.contains("TchedRouter")),
            "live plugin advertised: {services:?}"
        );
        assert!(
            !services
                .iter()
                .any(|s| s.to_ascii_lowercase().contains("factory")),
            "retired plugin must not be advertised: {services:?}"
        );
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn same_schema_and_catalog_hash_refreshes_changed_valid_descriptor_artifacts() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let schema = op_state_store::PluginSchema::builder("tched_router")
            .version("1.0.0")
            .method(op_state_store::MethodDecl {
                name: "Read".into(),
                args: simd_json::json!({"type":"object", "properties":{}}),
                returns: Some(simd_json::json!({"type":"object", "properties":{}})),
                side_effect: op_state_store::SideEffect::Read,
                idempotent: true,
                required_capability: Some("fixture.read".into()),
                subid: "obs.service.fixture.read@v1".into(),
            })
            .build();
        let template = op_blob::blobify_plugin_schema("tched_router", schema);
        // Model two valid sealer code-generation revisions. The source schema
        // stays identical while a generated helper message changes. Only the
        // local producer fixture writes artifacts and the committed manifest.
        let revision = |helper: &str| {
            let mut blob = template.clone();
            let mut descriptors =
                FileDescriptorSet::decode(blob.descriptor_set.as_slice()).unwrap();
            let file = &mut descriptors.file[0];
            let symbol = format!("{}.{}", file.package.as_deref().unwrap(), helper);
            file.message_type.push(DescriptorProto {
                name: Some(helper.into()),
                ..Default::default()
            });
            blob.manifest.methods[0].symbols.push(symbol.clone());
            blob.descriptor_set = descriptors.encode_to_vec();
            (blob, symbol)
        };
        let (first, old_symbol) = revision("ArtifactRevisionOne");
        let (second, new_symbol) = revision("ArtifactRevisionTwo");
        assert_eq!(first.schema_json, second.schema_json);
        assert_eq!(first.manifest.schema_hash, second.manifest.schema_hash);
        assert_eq!(first.file_name(), second.file_name());
        assert_ne!(first.descriptor_set, second.descriptor_set);

        let mut producer = op_blob::BlobStore::open(dir.path()).unwrap();
        producer.write(&first).unwrap();
        let manifest_path = dir.path().join(op_blob::catalog::MANIFEST_FILENAME);
        let first_manifest: serde_json::Value =
            serde_json::from_slice(&std::fs::read(&manifest_path).unwrap()).unwrap();
        let catalog = ActiveReflectionCatalog::with_dir(dir.path().into());
        assert_eq!(catalog.sync_from_shm().await, 1);
        assert!(catalog.symbol_by_name(&old_symbol).await.is_ok());
        assert!(catalog.symbol_by_name(&new_symbol).await.is_err());

        producer.write(&second).unwrap();
        let second_manifest: serde_json::Value =
            serde_json::from_slice(&std::fs::read(&manifest_path).unwrap()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            first_manifest["catalog_hash"],
            second_manifest["catalog_hash"]
        );
        assert!(
            second_manifest["generation"].as_u64().unwrap()
                > first_manifest["generation"].as_u64().unwrap()
        );
        assert_eq!(catalog.sync_from_shm().await, 1);
        assert!(catalog.symbol_by_name(&old_symbol).await.is_err());
        let indexed = catalog.symbol_by_name(&new_symbol).await.unwrap();
        let expected = FileDescriptorSet::decode(second.descriptor_set.as_slice())
            .unwrap()
            .file
            .remove(0)
            .encode_to_vec();
        assert_eq!(indexed, expected);
        assert_eq!(
            catalog
                .file_by_filename(&second.manifest.methods[0].grpc_file)
                .await
                .unwrap(),
            expected
        );
        assert!(catalog
            .list_services()
            .await
            .iter()
            .any(|service| service == "operation.plugin.v1.TchedRouterPluginMethods"));
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn active_reflection_advertises_only_active_blob_services() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let catalog = ActiveReflectionCatalog::with_dir(dir.path().into());
        let before = catalog.list_services().await;
        assert!(before
            .iter()
            .any(|service| service == "grpc.reflection.v1.ServerReflection"));
        assert!(!before
            .iter()
            .any(|service| service == "operation.plugin.v1.TchedRouterPluginMethods"));

        let mut sealer = op_blob::BlobStore::open(dir.path()).unwrap();
        sealer
            .write(&crate::tched_router_object_blob::from_plugin_schema())
            .unwrap();
        catalog.sync_from_shm().await;
        let after = catalog.list_services().await;
        // Legacy service (mounted via build.rs) is advertised.
        assert!(after
            .iter()
            .any(|service| service == "operation.plugin.v1.TchedRouterPluginMethods"));
        assert!(after.iter().all(|service| {
            service == "grpc.reflection.v1.ServerReflection"
                || service == "operation.plugin.v1.TchedRouterPluginMethods"
        }));

        sealer.remove_blob("tched_router").unwrap();
        catalog.sync_from_shm().await;
        let removed = catalog.list_services().await;
        assert!(!removed
            .iter()
            .any(|service| service == "operation.plugin.v1.TchedRouterPluginMethods"));
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn sync_from_shm_picks_up_blobs_sealed_by_external_writer() {
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("op-reflection-sync-{}", std::process::id()));
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();

        let catalog = ActiveReflectionCatalog::with_dir(dir.clone());
        let before = catalog.list_services().await;
        assert_eq!(
            before,
            vec!["grpc.reflection.v1.ServerReflection".to_string()]
        );

        // External sealer (the op-blob binary's role): seals the blob and
        // commits the manifest — no call into the bridge.
        let blob = crate::tched_router_object_blob::from_plugin_schema();
        let descriptor_only_services = blob.manifest.grpc.services.clone();
        assert!(!descriptor_only_services.is_empty());
        {
            let mut store = op_blob::BlobStore::open(&dir).unwrap();
            store.write(&blob).unwrap();
        }

        catalog.sync_from_shm().await;
        let after = catalog.list_services().await;
        assert!(after
            .iter()
            .any(|service| service == "operation.plugin.v1.TchedRouterPluginMethods"));
        for service in &descriptor_only_services {
            assert!(
                !after.iter().any(|s| s == service),
                "unmounted descriptor {service} advertised after SHM resync"
            );
        }

        // Removal by the external sealer propagates on the next arrival too.
        {
            let mut store = op_blob::BlobStore::open(&dir).unwrap();
            store.remove_blob("tched_router").unwrap();
        }
        catalog.sync_from_shm().await;
        let removed = catalog.list_services().await;
        assert_eq!(
            removed,
            vec!["grpc.reflection.v1.ServerReflection".to_string()]
        );

        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
    }
}
</file>

<file path="op-grpc-bridge/src/emqx_hook_provider.rs">
//! EMQX ExHook v3 HookProvider gRPC service implementation.
//!
//! EMQX acts as a gRPC client, calling this service for MQTT events
//! The pinned EMQX 6.2.2 broker requires `emqx.exhook.v3`.
//! The implementation records events through MutationEngine for
//! accountability. Publish decisions are left to the broker (`IGNORE`) — the
//! hook is an audit tap; identity gating stays with the Ghostbridge
//! interceptor on the plugin surface. The one exception is the doorbell
//! (`wake_doorbell`): clients whose id is an owner key must prove the
//! matching SID1 against the identity sled, and may only subscribe to their
//! own `opdbus/wake/<owner-key>` topic. Every other client is kept out of
//! the `opdbus/` namespace and otherwise left to the broker's own rules.

use std::sync::Arc;

use tonic::{Request, Response, Status};
use tracing::{debug, info};

use op_plugins::state_plugins::emqx::{
    BrokerEvent, BROKER_EVENT_SIGNAL, BROKER_EVENT_SUBID, REGISTERED_HOOKS,
};

use crate::mutation_engine::{ChangeSource, ChangeType, MutationEngine};
use crate::proto::emqx_exhook::{
    self as exhook, hook_provider_server::HookProvider, valued_response, EmptySuccess, HookSpec,
    LoadedResponse, ValuedResponse,
};

/// HookProvider service implementation for EMQX MQTT event hooks.
///
/// All EMQX hook events are recorded as signals through the MutationEngine,
/// providing accountability and persistence without direct SQL storage.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct HookProviderService {
    mutation_engine: Arc<MutationEngine>,
    /// Doorbell OIA1 verification: the same validator family as the door
    /// (trust store, replay store, source binding from the environment).
    assertion_validator: Arc<crate::oracle_assertion::AssertionValidator>,
    /// Event-triggered agent runs (OD-63): match + enqueue on publish.
    triggers: crate::agent_triggers::TriggerMatcher,
}

impl HookProviderService {
    pub fn new(mutation_engine: Arc<MutationEngine>) -> Self {
        let queue = crate::agent_runs::RunQueue::spawn(
            mutation_engine.clone(),
            crate::agent_runs::DEFAULT_CAPACITY,
            crate::agent_runs::DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY,
        );
        Self::with_queue(mutation_engine, queue)
    }

    pub(crate) fn with_queue(
        mutation_engine: Arc<MutationEngine>,
        queue: crate::agent_runs::RunQueue,
    ) -> Self {
        let assertion_validator = Arc::new(crate::oracle_assertion::AssertionValidator::from_env(
            crate::oracle_assertion::DecoyTrustStore::load(),
        ));
        Self {
            mutation_engine,
            assertion_validator,
            triggers: crate::agent_triggers::TriggerMatcher::new(queue),
        }
    }

    /// Record a broker observation, never a fictitious mutation/tool call.
    async fn record_event(
        &self,
        event_type: &str,
        client_id: &str,
        topic: Option<&str>,
        detail: Option<&str>,
    ) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
        let event_data = broker_event(event_type, client_id, topic, detail);
        let result = self
            .mutation_engine
            .process_authoritative_change(
                "emqx".into(),
                "/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/emqx".into(),
                ChangeType::Signal,
                Some(BROKER_EVENT_SIGNAL.into()),
                None,
                simd_json::serde::to_owned_value(event_data)?,
                vec![BROKER_EVENT_SUBID.into()],
                "grpc:emqx.exhook.v3".into(),
                None,
                ChangeSource::Grpc,
            )
            .await;
        if let Err(error) = result {
            tracing::error!(%error, event_type, "could not record broker observation");
            return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(error));
        }

        Ok(())
    }
}

fn broker_event(
    event_type: &str,
    client: &str,
    topic: Option<&str>,
    detail: Option<&str>,
) -> BrokerEvent {
    let digest = |value: &str| {
        blake3::Hash::from(blake3::derive_key(
            "opdbus broker observation v1",
            value.as_bytes(),
        ))
        .to_hex()
        .to_string()
    };
    BrokerEvent {
        event_type: event_type.to_owned(),
        client_ref: digest(client),
        topic_ref: topic.map(digest),
        detail_ref: detail.map(digest),
    }
}

fn client_id(info: &Option<exhook::ClientInfo>) -> &str {
    info.as_ref()
        .map(|c| c.clientid.as_str())
        .unwrap_or("unknown")
}

fn empty() -> Response<EmptySuccess> {
    Response::new(EmptySuccess {})
}

/// A doorbell verdict as the broker expects it: `Ignore` keeps the chain,
/// `Allow`/`Deny` stop it with a boolean.
fn respond(verdict: crate::wake_doorbell::Verdict) -> Response<ValuedResponse> {
    match verdict {
        crate::wake_doorbell::Verdict::Ignore => ignore(),
        crate::wake_doorbell::Verdict::Allow => stop_with(true),
        crate::wake_doorbell::Verdict::Deny => stop_with(false),
    }
}

fn stop_with(result: bool) -> Response<ValuedResponse> {
    Response::new(ValuedResponse {
        r#type: valued_response::ResponsedType::StopAndReturn as i32,
        value: Some(valued_response::Value::BoolResult(result)),
    })
}

/// Leave the broker's own decision in place.
fn ignore() -> Response<ValuedResponse> {
    Response::new(ValuedResponse {
        r#type: valued_response::ResponsedType::Ignore as i32,
        value: None,
    })
}

#[tonic::async_trait]
impl HookProvider for HookProviderService {
    async fn on_provider_loaded(
        &self,
        request: Request<exhook::ProviderLoadedRequest>,
    ) -> Result<Response<LoadedResponse>, Status> {
        let req = request.into_inner();
        info!(
            broker = %req.broker.as_ref().map(|b| b.version.as_str()).unwrap_or("unknown"),
            "EMQX exhook provider loaded"
        );
        let hooks = REGISTERED_HOOKS
            .iter()
            .map(|name| HookSpec {
                name: (*name).to_string(),
                topics: if name.starts_with("message.") {
                    vec!["#".to_string()]
                } else {
                    Vec::new()
                },
            })
            .collect();
        Ok(Response::new(LoadedResponse { hooks }))
    }

    async fn on_provider_unloaded(
        &self,
        _request: Request<exhook::ProviderUnloadedRequest>,
    ) -> Result<Response<EmptySuccess>, Status> {
        info!("EMQX exhook provider unloaded");
        Ok(empty())
    }

    async fn on_client_connect(
        &self,
        request: Request<exhook::ClientConnectRequest>,
    ) -> Result<Response<EmptySuccess>, Status> {
        let req = request.into_inner();
        let client = req
            .conninfo
            .as_ref()
            .map(|c| c.clientid.as_str())
            .unwrap_or("unknown");
        debug!(client_id = %client, "EMQX OnClientConnect");
        let _ = self
            .record_event("on_client_connect", client, None, None)
            .await;
        Ok(empty())
    }

    async fn on_client_connack(
        &self,
        _request: Request<exhook::ClientConnackRequest>,
    ) -> Result<Response<EmptySuccess>, Status> {
        Ok(empty())
    }

    async fn on_client_connected(
        &self,
        request: Request<exhook::ClientConnectedRequest>,
    ) -> Result<Response<EmptySuccess>, Status> {
        let req = request.into_inner();
        let client = client_id(&req.clientinfo);
        info!(client_id = %client, "EMQX OnClientConnected");
        let _ = self
            .record_event("on_client_connected", client, None, None)
            .await;
        Ok(empty())
    }

    async fn on_client_disconnected(
        &self,
        request: Request<exhook::ClientDisconnectedRequest>,
    ) -> Result<Response<EmptySuccess>, Status> {
        let req = request.into_inner();
        let client = client_id(&req.clientinfo);
        info!(client_id = %client, reason = %req.reason, "EMQX OnClientDisconnected");
        let _ = self
            .record_event("on_client_disconnected", client, None, Some(&req.reason))
            .await;
        Ok(empty())
    }

    async fn on_client_authenticate(
        &self,
        request: Request<exhook::ClientAuthenticateRequest>,
    ) -> Result<Response<ValuedResponse>, Status> {
        let req = request.into_inner();
        let client = client_id(&req.clientinfo);
        debug!(client_id = %client, result = req.result, "EMQX OnClientAuthenticate");
        let (password, peer) = req
            .clientinfo
            .as_ref()
            .map(|info| {
                (
                    info.password.as_str(),
                    format!("{}:{}", info.peerhost, info.peerport)
                        .parse::<std::net::SocketAddr>()
                        .ok(),
                )
            })
            .unwrap_or_default();
        let verdict = crate::wake_doorbell::authenticate(
            &self.mutation_engine,
            &self.assertion_validator,
            client,
            password,
            peer,
        )
        .await;
        let _ = self
            .record_event(
                "on_client_authenticate",
                client,
                None,
                Some(match verdict {
                    crate::wake_doorbell::Verdict::Ignore if req.result => "pass",
                    crate::wake_doorbell::Verdict::Ignore => "fail",
                    crate::wake_doorbell::Verdict::Allow => "doorbell-pass",
                    crate::wake_doorbell::Verdict::Deny => "doorbell-fail",
                }),
            )
            .await;
        Ok(respond(verdict))
    }

    async fn on_client_authorize(
        &self,
        request: Request<exhook::ClientAuthorizeRequest>,
    ) -> Result<Response<ValuedResponse>, Status> {
        let req = request.into_inner();
        let client = client_id(&req.clientinfo);
        debug!(client_id = %client, topic = %req.topic, "EMQX OnClientAuthorize");
        let subscribe =
            req.r#type == exhook::client_authorize_request::AuthorizeReqType::Subscribe as i32;
        let verdict =
            crate::wake_doorbell::authorize(&self.mutation_engine, client, subscribe, &req.topic)
                .await;
        let _ = self
            .record_event(
                "on_client_authorize",
                client,
                Some(&req.topic),
                Some(match verdict {
                    crate::wake_doorbell::Verdict::Ignore => "broker",
                    crate::wake_doorbell::Verdict::Allow => "doorbell-allow",
                    crate::wake_doorbell::Verdict::Deny => "doorbell-deny",
                }),
            )
            .await;
        Ok(respond(verdict))
    }

    async fn on_client_subscribe(
        &self,
        request: Request<exhook::ClientSubscribeRequest>,
    ) -> Result<Response<EmptySuccess>, Status> {
        let req = request.into_inner();
        let client = client_id(&req.clientinfo);
        let topics = req
            .topic_filters
            .iter()
            .map(|f| f.name.as_str())
            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
            .join(",");
        debug!(client_id = %client, topics = %topics, "EMQX OnClientSubscribe");
        let _ = self
            .record_event("on_client_subscribe", client, Some(&topics), None)
            .await;
        Ok(empty())
    }

    async fn on_client_unsubscribe(
        &self,
        request: Request<exhook::ClientUnsubscribeRequest>,
    ) -> Result<Response<EmptySuccess>, Status> {
        let req = request.into_inner();
        let client = client_id(&req.clientinfo);
        let topics = req
            .topic_filters
            .iter()
            .map(|f| f.name.as_str())
            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
            .join(",");
        debug!(client_id = %client, topics = %topics, "EMQX OnClientUnsubscribe");
        let _ = self
            .record_event("on_client_unsubscribe", client, Some(&topics), None)
            .await;
        Ok(empty())
    }

    async fn on_session_created(
        &self,
        request: Request<exhook::SessionCreatedRequest>,
    ) -> Result<Response<EmptySuccess>, Status> {
        let req = request.into_inner();
        let client = client_id(&req.clientinfo);
        debug!(client_id = %client, "EMQX OnSessionCreated");
        let _ = self
            .record_event("on_session_created", client, None, None)
            .await;
        Ok(empty())
    }

    async fn on_session_subscribed(
        &self,
        request: Request<exhook::SessionSubscribedRequest>,
    ) -> Result<Response<EmptySuccess>, Status> {
        let req = request.into_inner();
        let client = client_id(&req.clientinfo);
        debug!(client_id = %client, topic = %req.topic, "EMQX OnSessionSubscribed");
        let _ = self
            .record_event("on_session_subscribed", client, Some(&req.topic), None)
            .await;
        Ok(empty())
    }

    async fn on_session_unsubscribed(
        &self,
        request: Request<exhook::SessionUnsubscribedRequest>,
    ) -> Result<Response<EmptySuccess>, Status> {
        let req = request.into_inner();
        let client = client_id(&req.clientinfo);
        debug!(client_id = %client, topic = %req.topic, "EMQX OnSessionUnsubscribed");
        let _ = self
            .record_event("on_session_unsubscribed", client, Some(&req.topic), None)
            .await;
        Ok(empty())
    }

    async fn on_session_resumed(
        &self,
        _request: Request<exhook::SessionResumedRequest>,
    ) -> Result<Response<EmptySuccess>, Status> {
        Ok(empty())
    }

    async fn on_session_discarded(
        &self,
        _request: Request<exhook::SessionDiscardedRequest>,
    ) -> Result<Response<EmptySuccess>, Status> {
        Ok(empty())
    }

    async fn on_session_takenover(
        &self,
        _request: Request<exhook::SessionTakenoverRequest>,
    ) -> Result<Response<EmptySuccess>, Status> {
        Ok(empty())
    }

    async fn on_session_terminated(
        &self,
        request: Request<exhook::SessionTerminatedRequest>,
    ) -> Result<Response<EmptySuccess>, Status> {
        let req = request.into_inner();
        let client = client_id(&req.clientinfo);
        debug!(client_id = %client, reason = %req.reason, "EMQX OnSessionTerminated");
        let _ = self
            .record_event("on_session_terminated", client, None, Some(&req.reason))
            .await;
        Ok(empty())
    }

    async fn on_message_publish(
        &self,
        request: Request<exhook::MessagePublishRequest>,
    ) -> Result<Response<ValuedResponse>, Status> {
        let req = request.into_inner();
        if let Some(message) = req.message.as_ref() {
            info!(from = %message.from, topic = %message.topic, "EMQX OnMessagePublish");
            let _ = self
                .record_event(
                    "on_message_publish",
                    &message.from,
                    Some(&message.topic),
                    None,
                )
                .await;
            // OD-63: a matching trigger enqueues a run; the payload is read
            // only for a match and bounded by the trigger. The verdict is
            // still the broker's.
            let enqueued = self
                .triggers
                .on_publish(&message.topic, &message.payload)
                .await;
            if enqueued > 0 {
                debug!(enqueued, topic = %message.topic, "agent runs enqueued");
            }
        }
        Ok(ignore())
    }

    async fn on_message_delivered(
        &self,
        _request: Request<exhook::MessageDeliveredRequest>,
    ) -> Result<Response<EmptySuccess>, Status> {
        Ok(empty())
    }

    async fn on_message_dropped(
        &self,
        _request: Request<exhook::MessageDroppedRequest>,
    ) -> Result<Response<EmptySuccess>, Status> {
        Ok(empty())
    }

    async fn on_message_acked(
        &self,
        _request: Request<exhook::MessageAckedRequest>,
    ) -> Result<Response<EmptySuccess>, Status> {
        Ok(empty())
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn broker_events_are_metadata_only_and_digest_all_external_values() {
        let event = broker_event(
            "message.publish",
            "client-secret",
            Some("private/project/topic"),
            Some("message body must not be retained"),
        );
        assert_eq!(event.event_type, "message.publish");
        assert_ne!(event.client_ref, "client-secret");
        assert_ne!(event.topic_ref.as_deref(), Some("private/project/topic"));
        assert_ne!(
            event.detail_ref.as_deref(),
            Some("message body must not be retained")
        );
        let encoded = serde_json::to_string(&event).unwrap();
        assert!(!encoded.contains("client-secret"));
        assert!(!encoded.contains("private/project/topic"));
        assert!(!encoded.contains("message body must not be retained"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn auth_and_authorize_responses_leave_broker_decisions_unchanged() {
        let response = ignore().into_inner();
        assert_eq!(
            response.r#type,
            valued_response::ResponsedType::Ignore as i32
        );
        assert!(response.value.is_none());
    }
}

<file path="op-grpc-bridge/src/event_chain_access.rs">
//! Authorization for the existing privileged audit metadata transport.
//!
//! Full ledger payloads remain internal. These aliases exercise existing
//! sealed Snowball declarations; they do not create a public audit policy.
use std::{pin::Pin, sync::Arc};

use futures::Stream;
use tonic::{Request, Status};

use crate::{
    grpc_server::{proto_chain_event, DECLARED_CAPABILITY_HEADER},
    interceptor::load_capability_grants,
    method_contract_admission::admit_compiled_invocation,
    mutation_engine::MutationEngine,
    oracle_assertion::HumanPrincipalIdentity,
    proto::{ChainEvent, GetEventsRequest, GetEventsResponse, SubscribeEventsRequest},
};

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) enum AuditMethod {
    QueryEvents,
    VerifyChain,
    GetSnapshot,
    CreateSnapshot,
}

impl AuditMethod {
    fn canonical(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::QueryEvents => "query_events",
            Self::VerifyChain => "verify_chain",
            Self::GetSnapshot => "get_snapshot",
            Self::CreateSnapshot => "create_snapshot",
        }
    }
}

pub(crate) struct AuditAccess {
    identity: HumanPrincipalIdentity,
    method: AuditMethod,
    capability: String,
}

/// Only the strict SID1/OIA1 interceptor authors this extension. Legacy
/// genesis/trace metadata is deliberately insufficient for audit access.
pub(crate) async fn verified_identity<T>(
    engine: &MutationEngine,
    request: &Request<T>,
) -> Result<HumanPrincipalIdentity, Status> {
    let identity = request
        .extensions()
        .get::<HumanPrincipalIdentity>()
        .cloned()
        .ok_or_else(|| Status::unauthenticated("verified SID1/OIA1 identity is required"))?;
    validate_identity(engine, &identity).await?;
    Ok(identity)
}

pub(crate) async fn validate_identity(
    engine: &MutationEngine,
    identity: &HumanPrincipalIdentity,
) -> Result<(), Status> {
    if identity.expires_at != 0 && identity.expires_at <= chrono::Utc::now().timestamp() {
        return Err(Status::unauthenticated("identity credential has expired"));
    }
    crate::project_dispatch::verified_session(
        engine,
        &identity.principal_id,
        Some(&identity.session_id),
        Some(&identity.session_genesis),
    )
    .await
    .map_err(|_| Status::unauthenticated("principal/session is no longer valid"))?;
    Ok(())
}

impl AuditAccess {
    pub(crate) async fn admit<T>(
        engine: &MutationEngine,
        request: &Request<T>,
        method: AuditMethod,
    ) -> Result<Self, Status> {
        let identity = verified_identity(engine, request).await?;
        let declared: Vec<_> = request
            .metadata()
            .get_all(DECLARED_CAPABILITY_HEADER)
            .into_iter()
            .collect();
        if declared.len() != 1 {
            return Err(Status::permission_denied(
                "one exact audit capability declaration is required",
            ));
        }
        let capability = declared[0]
            .to_str()
            .map_err(|_| Status::permission_denied("invalid audit capability declaration"))?
            .to_owned();
        let access = Self {
            identity,
            method,
            capability,
        };
        access.check_contract_and_grant()?;
        Ok(access)
    }

    // Keep the native tonic status used by the surrounding RPC boundary.
    #[allow(clippy::result_large_err)]
    fn check_contract_and_grant(&self) -> Result<(), Status> {
        if !load_capability_grants(&self.identity.principal_id).contains(&self.capability) {
            return Err(Status::permission_denied(
                "exact-principal audit capability grant is required",
            ));
        }
        // Same pinned method supplies compatibility evidence and its exact
        // required capability. The compiled registry is never existence authority.
        admit_compiled_invocation("snowball", self.method.canonical(), Some(&self.capability))
            .map_err(|_| Status::permission_denied("present Snowball method must match the exercised audit capability and compiled contract"))?;
        Ok(())
    }

    pub(crate) async fn revalidate(&self, engine: &MutationEngine) -> Result<(), Status> {
        validate_identity(engine, &self.identity).await?;
        self.check_contract_and_grant()
    }
}

const PAGE_LIMIT: usize = 100;
const REPLAY_LIMIT: usize = 1000;

// This RPC helper returns tonic's concrete status, preserving code/details.
#[allow(clippy::result_large_err)]
pub(crate) fn get_events(
    events: &[op_state_store::ChainEvent],
    request: &GetEventsRequest,
) -> Result<GetEventsResponse, Status> {
    if request.to_event_id != 0 && request.from_event_id > request.to_event_id {
        return Err(Status::invalid_argument("audit event range is reversed"));
    }
    if !matches!(request.decision_filter, 0..=2) {
        return Err(Status::invalid_argument("unknown audit decision filter"));
    }
    let limit = if request.limit == 0 {
        50
    } else {
        request.limit as usize
    }
    .min(PAGE_LIMIT);
    let mut found = events
        .iter()
        .filter(|event| request.from_event_id == 0 || event.event_id >= request.from_event_id)
        .filter(|event| request.to_event_id == 0 || event.event_id <= request.to_event_id)
        .filter(|event| matches_filters(event, &request.plugin_id, &request.tags))
        .filter(|event| match request.decision_filter {
            1 => event.decision == op_state_store::Decision::Allow,
            2 => event.decision == op_state_store::Decision::Deny,
            _ => true,
        });
    let page = found.by_ref().take(limit).map(proto_chain_event).collect();
    let has_more = found.next().is_some();
    Ok(GetEventsResponse {
        events: page,
        has_more,
    })
}

fn matches_filters(event: &op_state_store::ChainEvent, plugin: &str, tags: &[String]) -> bool {
    (plugin.is_empty() || event.plugin_id == plugin)
        && (tags.is_empty() || event.tags_touched.iter().any(|tag| tags.contains(tag)))
}

/// Read ordered ledger metadata after a wakeup. Broadcast payloads are never
/// trusted for ordering: concurrent appenders can send notifications out of order.
#[allow(clippy::result_large_err)] // Native tonic error contract for the stream.
fn replay_after(
    events: &[op_state_store::ChainEvent],
    cursor: u64,
    plugin: &str,
    tags: &[String],
) -> Result<(u64, Vec<ChainEvent>), Status> {
    let head = events.last().map_or(0, |event| event.event_id);
    if let Some(first) = events.first() {
        if first.event_id.saturating_sub(1) > cursor {
            return Err(Status::out_of_range(
                "requested audit history is no longer retained",
            ));
        }
    }
    let pending = events.iter().filter(|event| event.event_id > cursor);
    let mut count = 0;
    let mut result = Vec::new();
    for event in pending {
        count += 1;
        if count > REPLAY_LIMIT {
            return Err(Status::resource_exhausted("audit replay exceeds 1000 events; page GetEvents then resume from the next event id"));
        }
        if matches_filters(event, plugin, tags) {
            result.push(proto_chain_event(event));
        }
    }
    Ok((head.max(cursor), result))
}

pub(crate) type AuditStream = Pin<Box<dyn Stream<Item = Result<ChainEvent, Status>> + Send>>;

pub(crate) async fn subscribe(
    engine: Arc<MutationEngine>,
    request: SubscribeEventsRequest,
    access: AuditAccess,
) -> Result<AuditStream, Status> {
    // Subscribe before taking the replay snapshot to close the handoff gap.
    let mut receiver = engine.chain_tx().subscribe();
    let (mut cursor, initial) = {
        let chain = engine.event_chain.read().await;
        let head = chain.events().last().map_or(0, |event| event.event_id);
        if request.from_event_id == 0 {
            (head, Vec::new())
        } else {
            let cursor = request.from_event_id - 1;
            if cursor > head {
                return Err(Status::out_of_range(
                    "requested audit cursor is beyond the current chain",
                ));
            }
            replay_after(chain.events(), cursor, &request.plugin_id, &request.tags)?
        }
    };
    Ok(Box::pin(async_stream::stream! {
        let mut pending = initial;
        loop {
            for event in pending.drain(..) {
                if let Err(error) = access.revalidate(&engine).await {
                    yield Err(error); return;
                }
                yield Ok(event);
            }
            match receiver.recv().await {
                Ok(_) => {
                    if let Err(error) = access.revalidate(&engine).await {
                        yield Err(error); return;
                    }
                    let next = {
                        let chain = engine.event_chain.read().await;
                        replay_after(chain.events(), cursor, &request.plugin_id, &request.tags)
                    };
                    match next {
                        Ok((head, events)) => { cursor = head; pending = events; }
                        Err(error) => { yield Err(error); return; }
                    }
                }
                Err(tokio::sync::broadcast::error::RecvError::Lagged(_)) => {
                    yield Err(Status::out_of_range("audit notification history lagged; page GetEvents and resume explicitly"));
                    return;
                }
                Err(tokio::sync::broadcast::error::RecvError::Closed) => return,
            }
        }
    }))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use op_state_store::{Decision, OperationType};

    fn event(id: u64, plugin: &str) -> op_state_store::ChainEvent {
        op_state_store::ChainEvent::new(
            id,
            "prior".into(),
            "actor".into(),
            plugin.into(),
            "2.0.0".into(),
            OperationType::MethodCall,
            "private-target".into(),
            vec!["tag".into()],
            Decision::Allow,
            &simd_json::json!({"private_fixture":"never-on-audit-wire"}),
        )
    }

    #[test]
    fn bounded_pages_preserve_ledger_and_metadata_only() {
        let events: Vec<_> = (1..=103).map(|id| event(id, "demo")).collect();
        let input_before = events[0].input_payload.clone();
        let result = get_events(&events, &GetEventsRequest::default()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(result.events.len(), 50);
        assert!(result.has_more);
        let result = get_events(
            &events,
            &GetEventsRequest {
                limit: u32::MAX,
                ..Default::default()
            },
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(result.events.len(), 100);
        assert!(result.has_more);
        let result = get_events(
            &events,
            &GetEventsRequest {
                from_event_id: 100,
                limit: 4,
                ..Default::default()
            },
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(result.events.len(), 4);
        assert!(!result.has_more);
        let bytes = prost::Message::encode_to_vec(&result);
        assert!(!bytes
            .windows(b"never-on-audit-wire".len())
            .any(|bytes| bytes == b"never-on-audit-wire"));
        assert_eq!(events[0].input_payload, input_before);
        assert_eq!(events[0].event_hash, events[0].compute_hash());
    }

    #[test]
    fn replay_orders_by_ledger_and_advances_across_filtered_events() {
        let events = vec![event(1, "demo"), event(2, "other"), event(3, "demo")];
        let (cursor, replay) = replay_after(&events, 1, "demo", &[]).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(cursor, 3);
        assert_eq!(
            replay
                .iter()
                .map(|event| event.event_id)
                .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
            [3]
        );
        assert!(replay_after(&events, cursor, "demo", &[])
            .unwrap()
            .1
            .is_empty());
        assert!(replay_after(&events, 0, "demo", &["missing".into()])
            .unwrap()
            .1
            .is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn replay_rejects_lost_history_and_excessive_backlog() {
        assert_eq!(
            replay_after(&[event(3, "demo")], 0, "", &[])
                .unwrap_err()
                .code(),
            tonic::Code::OutOfRange
        );
        let events: Vec<_> = (1..=1001).map(|id| event(id, "demo")).collect();
        assert_eq!(
            replay_after(&events, 0, "", &[]).unwrap_err().code(),
            tonic::Code::ResourceExhausted
        );
        assert_eq!(
            get_events(
                &events,
                &GetEventsRequest {
                    from_event_id: 5,
                    to_event_id: 2,
                    ..Default::default()
                }
            )
            .unwrap_err()
            .code(),
            tonic::Code::InvalidArgument
        );
    }
}
