<file path="op-plugins/src/state_plugins/gcloud_adc.rs">
use anyhow::Result;
use async_trait::async_trait;
use op_state::{ApplyResult, Checkpoint, DiffMetadata, PluginCapabilities, StateDiff, StatePlugin};
use op_state_store::PluginSchema;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use simd_json::prelude::*;
use simd_json::OwnedValue as Value;

const CLOUD_PLATFORM_SCOPE: &str = "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform";
const ADC_PROBE_TIMEOUT: std::time::Duration = std::time::Duration::from_secs(15);

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum AdcValidationState {
    /// The SDK could not construct a usable ADC credential configuration.
    NotConfigured,
    ConfiguredUnverified,
    ProviderUnavailable,
    Rejected,
    Validated,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum AdcFailureKind {
    Configuration,
    ProviderUnavailable,
    ProviderRejected,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct AdcProbeFailure {
    pub kind: AdcFailureKind,
    pub retryable: bool,
    pub message: String,
}

/// Provider-backed ADC status. Tokens and credential fields are intentionally
/// absent from this public contract.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct AdcAuthStatus {
    pub provider: String,
    pub configured: bool,
    /// True only after Google issued an access token.
    pub authenticated: bool,
    pub validation: AdcValidationState,
    pub failure: Option<AdcProbeFailure>,
}

impl AdcAuthStatus {
    fn not_configured(failure: AdcProbeFailure) -> Self {
        Self {
            provider: "google_application_default_credentials".to_string(),
            configured: false,
            authenticated: false,
            validation: AdcValidationState::NotConfigured,
            failure: Some(failure),
        }
    }

    fn validation_failed(state: AdcValidationState, failure: AdcProbeFailure) -> Self {
        Self {
            provider: "google_application_default_credentials".to_string(),
            configured: true,
            authenticated: false,
            validation: state,
            failure: Some(failure),
        }
    }

    fn validated() -> Self {
        Self {
            provider: "google_application_default_credentials".to_string(),
            configured: true,
            authenticated: true,
            validation: AdcValidationState::Validated,
            failure: None,
        }
    }
}

pub(crate) fn provider_timeout_status() -> AdcAuthStatus {
    AdcAuthStatus::validation_failed(
        AdcValidationState::ProviderUnavailable,
        AdcProbeFailure {
            kind: AdcFailureKind::ProviderUnavailable,
            retryable: true,
            message: "Google credential validation timed out".to_string(),
        },
    )
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "sch.software.plugin.gcloud-adc.schema@v2"))]
#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-category" = "software"))]
pub struct GcloudAdcState {
    pub status: AdcAuthStatus,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct CheckAuthStatusInput {}

#[async_trait]
pub(crate) trait AdcStatusProvider: Send + Sync {
    async fn check_auth_status(&self) -> Result<AdcAuthStatus>;
}

pub(crate) struct GoogleCloudAuthProvider;

#[async_trait]
impl AdcStatusProvider for GoogleCloudAuthProvider {
    async fn check_auth_status(&self) -> Result<AdcAuthStatus> {
        use google_cloud_auth::credentials::Builder;

        // The official SDK owns ADC file and metadata-service discovery.
        let credentials = match Builder::default()
            .with_scopes([CLOUD_PLATFORM_SCOPE])
            .build_access_token_credentials()
        {
            Ok(credentials) => credentials,
            Err(error) => {
                let message = if error.is_loading() {
                    "ADC credentials could not be loaded"
                } else if error.is_parsing() {
                    "ADC credentials could not be parsed"
                } else if error.is_unknown_type() {
                    "ADC credential type is unknown"
                } else if error.is_missing_field() {
                    "ADC credentials are missing a required field"
                } else if error.is_not_supported() {
                    "ADC credential type is unsupported"
                } else {
                    "ADC credentials could not be configured"
                };
                return Ok(AdcAuthStatus::not_configured(AdcProbeFailure {
                    kind: AdcFailureKind::Configuration,
                    retryable: false,
                    message: message.to_string(),
                }));
            }
        };

        match credentials.access_token().await {
            Ok(token) if !token.token.is_empty() => {
                drop(token);
                Ok(AdcAuthStatus::validated())
            }
            Ok(token) => {
                drop(token);
                Ok(AdcAuthStatus::validation_failed(
                    AdcValidationState::Rejected,
                    AdcProbeFailure {
                        kind: AdcFailureKind::ProviderRejected,
                        retryable: false,
                        message: "Google returned an unusable credential response".to_string(),
                    },
                ))
            }
            Err(error) => {
                let retryable = error.is_transient();
                let (kind, message) = if retryable {
                    (
                        AdcFailureKind::ProviderUnavailable,
                        "Google credential validation is temporarily unavailable",
                    )
                } else {
                    (
                        AdcFailureKind::ProviderRejected,
                        "Google did not validate the configured ADC credential",
                    )
                };
                // SDK errors may contain response bodies. Never format them.
                drop(error);
                let state = if retryable {
                    AdcValidationState::ProviderUnavailable
                } else {
                    AdcValidationState::Rejected
                };
                Ok(AdcAuthStatus::validation_failed(
                    state,
                    AdcProbeFailure {
                        kind,
                        retryable,
                        message: message.to_string(),
                    },
                ))
            }
        }
    }
}

pub struct GcloudAdcPlugin;

impl Default for GcloudAdcPlugin {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self
    }
}

impl GcloudAdcPlugin {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl StatePlugin for GcloudAdcPlugin {
    fn name(&self) -> &str {
        "gcloud_adc"
    }
    fn version(&self) -> &str {
        "2.0.0"
    }
    fn schema(&self) -> Option<PluginSchema> {
        Some(gcloud_adc_schema())
    }

    async fn calculate_diff(&self, _current: &Value, _desired: &Value) -> Result<StateDiff> {
        Ok(StateDiff {
            plugin: self.name().to_string(),
            actions: vec![],
            metadata: DiffMetadata {
                timestamp: chrono::Utc::now().timestamp(),
                current_hash: "unknown".to_string(),
                desired_hash: "unknown".to_string(),
            },
        })
    }
    async fn apply_state(&self, _diff: &StateDiff) -> Result<ApplyResult> {
        Ok(ApplyResult {
            success: true,
            changes_applied: vec![],
            errors: vec![],
            checkpoint: None,
        })
    }
    async fn verify_state(&self, _desired: &Value) -> Result<bool> {
        Ok(true)
    }
    async fn create_checkpoint(&self) -> Result<Checkpoint> {
        Ok(Checkpoint {
            id: uuid::Uuid::new_v4().to_string(),
            plugin: self.name().to_string(),
            timestamp: chrono::Utc::now().timestamp(),
            state_snapshot: Value::null(),
            backend_checkpoint: None,
        })
    }
    async fn rollback(&self, _checkpoint: &Checkpoint) -> Result<()> {
        Ok(())
    }
    fn capabilities(&self) -> PluginCapabilities {
        PluginCapabilities {
            supports_rollback: false,
            supports_checkpoints: true,
            supports_verification: true,
            atomic_operations: false,
        }
    }
}

pub fn gcloud_adc_schema() -> PluginSchema {
    let root =
        serde_json::to_value(schemars::schema_for!(GcloudAdcState)).expect("schema serializes");
    let mut schema = super::schemars_adapter::plugin_schema_from_json(
        "gcloud_adc",
        "2.0.0",
        "Google Cloud ADC provider validation state",
        &root,
    );
    use super::plugin_scaffold_helpers::method_decl_from_schemars_with_output;
    use op_state_store::SideEffect;
    schema.methods.insert(
        "check_auth_status".to_string(),
        method_decl_from_schemars_with_output::<CheckAuthStatusInput, AdcAuthStatus>(
            "check_auth_status",
            SideEffect::Read,
            true,
            "gcloud_adc.read",
            "obs.software.plugin.gcloud-adc.auth-status.check@v2",
        ),
    );
    schema.capabilities.insert(
        "gcloud_adc.read".to_string(),
        op_state_store::CapabilityDecl {
            id: "gcloud_adc.read".to_string(),
            description: "Grants: check_auth_status.".to_string(),
        },
    );
    schema
}

pub(crate) async fn dispatch_gcloud_adc_with_provider(
    provider: &dyn AdcStatusProvider,
    method: &str,
    args: &serde_json::Value,
) -> Result<serde_json::Value> {
    dispatch_gcloud_adc_with_provider_timeout(provider, method, args, ADC_PROBE_TIMEOUT).await
}

async fn dispatch_gcloud_adc_with_provider_timeout(
    provider: &dyn AdcStatusProvider,
    method: &str,
    args: &serde_json::Value,
    timeout: std::time::Duration,
) -> Result<serde_json::Value> {
    match method {
        "check_auth_status" => {
            serde_json::from_value::<CheckAuthStatusInput>(args.clone())?;
            let status = match tokio::time::timeout(timeout, provider.check_auth_status()).await {
                Ok(result) => result?,
                Err(_) => provider_timeout_status(),
            };
            Ok(serde_json::to_value(status)?)
        }
        other => Err(anyhow::anyhow!("unknown gcloud_adc method: {other}")),
    }
}

pub async fn dispatch_gcloud_adc_method(
    method: &str,
    args: &serde_json::Value,
) -> Result<serde_json::Value> {
    dispatch_gcloud_adc_with_provider(&GoogleCloudAuthProvider, method, args).await
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::state_plugins::common::oscal::validate_subid;

    struct FakeProvider(std::result::Result<AdcAuthStatus, &'static str>);
    #[async_trait]
    impl AdcStatusProvider for FakeProvider {
        async fn check_auth_status(&self) -> Result<AdcAuthStatus> {
            self.0.clone().map_err(anyhow::Error::msg)
        }
    }

    fn failure_status(kind: AdcFailureKind, retryable: bool) -> AdcAuthStatus {
        let failure = AdcProbeFailure {
            kind,
            retryable,
            message: "sanitized".to_string(),
        };
        if kind == AdcFailureKind::Configuration {
            AdcAuthStatus::not_configured(failure)
        } else {
            let state = if retryable {
                AdcValidationState::ProviderUnavailable
            } else {
                AdcValidationState::Rejected
            };
            AdcAuthStatus::validation_failed(state, failure)
        }
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn validated_status_contains_no_credential_fields() {
        let value = dispatch_gcloud_adc_with_provider(
            &FakeProvider(Ok(AdcAuthStatus::validated())),
            "check_auth_status",
            &serde_json::json!({}),
        )
        .await
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(value["authenticated"], true);
        assert_eq!(value["validation"], "validated");
        let encoded = serde_json::to_string(&value).unwrap();
        for name in [
            "access_token",
            "refresh_token",
            "private_key",
            "client_secret",
        ] {
            assert!(!encoded.contains(name));
        }
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn failure_classes_remain_distinct_and_unprobed() {
        for (kind, retryable) in [
            (AdcFailureKind::Configuration, false),
            (AdcFailureKind::ProviderUnavailable, true),
            (AdcFailureKind::ProviderRejected, false),
        ] {
            let value = dispatch_gcloud_adc_with_provider(
                &FakeProvider(Ok(failure_status(kind, retryable))),
                "check_auth_status",
                &serde_json::json!({}),
            )
            .await
            .unwrap();
            assert_eq!(value["authenticated"], false);
            let expected_validation = match kind {
                AdcFailureKind::Configuration => "not_configured",
                AdcFailureKind::ProviderUnavailable => "provider_unavailable",
                AdcFailureKind::ProviderRejected => "rejected",
            };
            assert_eq!(value["validation"], expected_validation);
            assert_eq!(value["failure"]["retryable"], retryable);
            assert_eq!(
                serde_json::from_value::<AdcFailureKind>(value["failure"]["kind"].clone()).unwrap(),
                kind
            );
        }
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn input_and_provider_errors_are_reported() {
        let provider = FakeProvider(Err("offline provider failed"));
        let err = dispatch_gcloud_adc_with_provider(
            &provider,
            "check_auth_status",
            &serde_json::json!({"unexpected": true}),
        )
        .await
        .unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.to_string().contains("unknown field"));
        let err = dispatch_gcloud_adc_with_provider(
            &provider,
            "check_auth_status",
            &serde_json::json!({}),
        )
        .await
        .unwrap_err();
        assert_eq!(err.to_string(), "offline provider failed");
    }

    struct PendingProvider;

    #[async_trait]
    impl AdcStatusProvider for PendingProvider {
        async fn check_auth_status(&self) -> Result<AdcAuthStatus> {
            std::future::pending().await
        }
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn provider_probe_has_a_bounded_deadline() {
        let value = dispatch_gcloud_adc_with_provider_timeout(
            &PendingProvider,
            "check_auth_status",
            &serde_json::json!({}),
            std::time::Duration::from_millis(1),
        )
        .await
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(value["validation"], "provider_unavailable");
        assert_eq!(value["authenticated"], false);
        assert_eq!(value["failure"]["retryable"], true);
    }

    #[test]
    fn method_schema_has_typed_input_and_output() {
        let method = &gcloud_adc_schema().methods["check_auth_status"];
        assert_eq!(method.args["type"], "object");
        assert_eq!(method.returns.as_ref().unwrap()["type"], "object");
    }

    #[test]
    fn all_subids_are_valid() {
        let raw = serde_json::to_value(schemars::schema_for!(GcloudAdcState)).unwrap();
        let mut stack = vec![&raw];
        while let Some(node) = stack.pop() {
            if let Some(subid) = node.get("x-oscal-subid").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) {
                validate_subid(subid).unwrap();
            }
            if let Some(props) = node.get("properties").and_then(|v| v.as_object()) {
                stack.extend(props.values());
            }
            if let Some(defs) = node
                .get("$defs")
                .or_else(|| node.get("definitions"))
                .and_then(|v| v.as_object())
            {
                stack.extend(defs.values());
            }
        }
    }
}

inventory::submit! {
    crate::default_registry::PluginReg::new("gcloud_adc", |_ctx| std::sync::Arc::new(GcloudAdcPlugin::new()))
}
</file>

<file path="op-plugins/src/state_plugins/gemma_brain_methods.rs">
//! Model-agnostic intent taxonomy for the private Gemma workspace.

use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};

use anyhow::{ensure, Result};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

const MAX_TAGS: usize = 256;
const MAX_KEYWORDS: usize = 64;
const MAX_TEXT_BYTES: usize = 64 * 1024;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct GemmaTaxonomy {
    pub revision: u64,
    pub tags: BTreeMap<String, GemmaTag>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct GemmaTag {
    pub id: String,
    pub label: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub description: String,
    pub keywords: Vec<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub perspectives: Vec<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct ClassifyInput {
    pub text: String,
    #[serde(default = "default_limit")]
    pub limit: u32,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct TagMatch {
    pub tag_id: String,
    pub score: u32,
    pub matched_keywords: Vec<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct ClassifyOutput {
    pub taxonomy_revision: u64,
    pub classification: Option<String>,
    pub matches: Vec<TagMatch>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct ListTaxonomyInput {}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct PerspectiveSummary {
    pub id: String,
    pub tag_count: u32,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct ListPerspectivesOutput {
    pub taxonomy_revision: u64,
    pub perspectives: Vec<PerspectiveSummary>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct ListTagsOutput {
    pub taxonomy_revision: u64,
    pub tags: Vec<GemmaTag>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct RegisterTagInput {
    pub expected_taxonomy_revision: u64,
    pub tag: GemmaTag,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct RegisterTagOutput {
    pub taxonomy_revision: u64,
    pub created: bool,
    pub tag: GemmaTag,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct AnalyzeIntentInput {
    pub text: String,
    #[serde(default = "default_limit")]
    pub limit: u32,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct AnalyzeIntentOutput {
    pub taxonomy_revision: u64,
    pub intent: Option<String>,
    pub matches: Vec<TagMatch>,
    pub perspectives: Vec<String>,
}

fn default_limit() -> u32 {
    8
}

fn valid_id(value: &str) -> bool {
    !value.is_empty()
        && value.len() <= 64
        && value.bytes().all(|byte| {
            byte.is_ascii_lowercase() || byte.is_ascii_digit() || matches!(byte, b'_' | b'-')
        })
}

pub fn validate_taxonomy(taxonomy: &GemmaTaxonomy) -> Result<()> {
    ensure!(
        taxonomy.tags.len() <= MAX_TAGS,
        "Gemma taxonomy exceeds tag capacity"
    );
    for (id, tag) in &taxonomy.tags {
        validate_tag(tag)?;
        ensure!(id == &tag.id, "Gemma taxonomy key differs from tag id");
    }
    Ok(())
}

pub fn validate_tag(tag: &GemmaTag) -> Result<()> {
    ensure!(valid_id(&tag.id), "Gemma tag id is invalid");
    ensure!(
        !tag.label.trim().is_empty() && tag.label.len() <= 128,
        "Gemma tag label is invalid"
    );
    ensure!(
        tag.description.len() <= 2048,
        "Gemma tag description is too large"
    );
    ensure!(
        !tag.keywords.is_empty() && tag.keywords.len() <= MAX_KEYWORDS,
        "Gemma tag requires 1..=64 keywords"
    );
    let mut keywords = BTreeSet::new();
    for keyword in &tag.keywords {
        ensure!(
            !keyword.trim().is_empty()
                && keyword.trim() == keyword
                && keyword.len() <= 128
                && !keyword.chars().any(char::is_control),
            "Gemma tag keyword is invalid"
        );
        ensure!(
            keywords.insert(keyword.to_lowercase()),
            "Gemma tag repeats a keyword"
        );
    }
    ensure!(
        tag.perspectives.len() <= 16,
        "Gemma tag has too many perspectives"
    );
    let mut perspectives = BTreeSet::new();
    for perspective in &tag.perspectives {
        ensure!(valid_id(perspective), "Gemma perspective id is invalid");
        ensure!(
            perspectives.insert(perspective),
            "Gemma tag repeats a perspective"
        );
    }
    Ok(())
}

pub fn register_tag(
    taxonomy: &mut GemmaTaxonomy,
    input: RegisterTagInput,
) -> Result<RegisterTagOutput> {
    validate_taxonomy(taxonomy)?;
    validate_tag(&input.tag)?;
    ensure!(
        taxonomy.revision == input.expected_taxonomy_revision,
        "stale Gemma taxonomy revision"
    );
    let created = !taxonomy.tags.contains_key(&input.tag.id);
    ensure!(
        !created || taxonomy.tags.len() < MAX_TAGS,
        "Gemma taxonomy tag capacity reached"
    );
    taxonomy.revision = taxonomy
        .revision
        .checked_add(1)
        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("Gemma taxonomy revision overflow"))?;
    taxonomy
        .tags
        .insert(input.tag.id.clone(), input.tag.clone());
    Ok(RegisterTagOutput {
        taxonomy_revision: taxonomy.revision,
        created,
        tag: input.tag,
    })
}

pub fn list_tags(taxonomy: &GemmaTaxonomy) -> Result<ListTagsOutput> {
    validate_taxonomy(taxonomy)?;
    Ok(ListTagsOutput {
        taxonomy_revision: taxonomy.revision,
        tags: taxonomy.tags.values().cloned().collect(),
    })
}

pub fn list_perspectives(taxonomy: &GemmaTaxonomy) -> Result<ListPerspectivesOutput> {
    validate_taxonomy(taxonomy)?;
    let mut counts = BTreeMap::<String, u32>::new();
    for tag in taxonomy.tags.values() {
        for perspective in &tag.perspectives {
            *counts.entry(perspective.clone()).or_default() += 1;
        }
    }
    Ok(ListPerspectivesOutput {
        taxonomy_revision: taxonomy.revision,
        perspectives: counts
            .into_iter()
            .map(|(id, tag_count)| PerspectiveSummary { id, tag_count })
            .collect(),
    })
}

fn matches(taxonomy: &GemmaTaxonomy, text: &str, limit: u32) -> Result<Vec<TagMatch>> {
    validate_taxonomy(taxonomy)?;
    ensure!(
        !text.trim().is_empty() && text.len() <= MAX_TEXT_BYTES,
        "Gemma input text must be 1..=65536 bytes"
    );
    ensure!(
        (1..=64).contains(&limit),
        "Gemma result limit must be 1..=64"
    );
    let normalized = text.to_lowercase();
    let mut matches = taxonomy
        .tags
        .values()
        .filter_map(|tag| {
            let matched_keywords: Vec<_> = tag
                .keywords
                .iter()
                .filter(|keyword| normalized.contains(&keyword.to_lowercase()))
                .cloned()
                .collect();
            (!matched_keywords.is_empty()).then(|| TagMatch {
                tag_id: tag.id.clone(),
                score: u32::try_from(matched_keywords.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX),
                matched_keywords,
            })
        })
        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
    matches.sort_by(|left, right| {
        right
            .score
            .cmp(&left.score)
            .then_with(|| left.tag_id.cmp(&right.tag_id))
    });
    matches.truncate(limit as usize);
    Ok(matches)
}

pub fn classify(taxonomy: &GemmaTaxonomy, input: ClassifyInput) -> Result<ClassifyOutput> {
    let matches = matches(taxonomy, &input.text, input.limit)?;
    Ok(ClassifyOutput {
        taxonomy_revision: taxonomy.revision,
        classification: matches.first().map(|entry| entry.tag_id.clone()),
        matches,
    })
}

pub fn analyze_intent(
    taxonomy: &GemmaTaxonomy,
    input: AnalyzeIntentInput,
) -> Result<AnalyzeIntentOutput> {
    let matches = matches(taxonomy, &input.text, input.limit)?;
    let perspectives = matches
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|entry| taxonomy.tags.get(&entry.tag_id))
        .flat_map(|tag| tag.perspectives.iter().cloned())
        .collect::<BTreeSet<_>>()
        .into_iter()
        .collect();
    Ok(AnalyzeIntentOutput {
        taxonomy_revision: taxonomy.revision,
        intent: matches.first().map(|entry| entry.tag_id.clone()),
        matches,
        perspectives,
    })
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn tag(id: &str, keywords: &[&str], perspectives: &[&str]) -> GemmaTag {
        GemmaTag {
            id: id.into(),
            label: id.into(),
            description: String::new(),
            keywords: keywords.iter().map(|value| (*value).into()).collect(),
            perspectives: perspectives.iter().map(|value| (*value).into()).collect(),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn registered_taxonomy_drives_deterministic_classification_and_intent() {
        let mut taxonomy = GemmaTaxonomy::default();
        register_tag(
            &mut taxonomy,
            RegisterTagInput {
                expected_taxonomy_revision: 0,
                tag: tag("deploy", &["release", "deploy"], &["operational"]),
            },
        )
        .unwrap();
        register_tag(
            &mut taxonomy,
            RegisterTagInput {
                expected_taxonomy_revision: 1,
                tag: tag("review", &["review"], &["analytical"]),
            },
        )
        .unwrap();
        let result = classify(
            &taxonomy,
            ClassifyInput {
                text: "Review the release before deploy".into(),
                limit: 8,
            },
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(result.classification.as_deref(), Some("deploy"));
        let intent = analyze_intent(
            &taxonomy,
            AnalyzeIntentInput {
                text: "review release".into(),
                limit: 8,
            },
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(intent.perspectives, vec!["analytical", "operational"]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn invalid_or_stale_registration_never_mutates_taxonomy() {
        let mut taxonomy = GemmaTaxonomy::default();
        let before = taxonomy.clone();
        assert!(register_tag(
            &mut taxonomy,
            RegisterTagInput {
                expected_taxonomy_revision: 1,
                tag: tag("deploy", &["deploy"], &[]),
            },
        )
        .is_err());
        assert_eq!(taxonomy, before);
    }
}
</file>

<file path="op-plugins/src/state_plugins/gemma_brain.rs">
//! Gemma brain — the umbrella cognitive plugin.
//!
//! Gemma does multiple things, so this is a "brain", not a "router": it owns the
//! tag-routing / subid-classification configuration, the four reasoning
//! perspectives, and the UI-spec gallery surface. It is the WHAT-to-decide
//! surface; it **consumes** the generic [`super::large_language_model`] plugin
//! for inference and embeds no model of its own ("gemma" here is a brand for the
//! brain, not a model binding — swap the underlying model via the
//! `large_language_model` plugin).
//!
//! The MutationEngine owns the canonical private workspace methods and commits
//! their full state to owner-scoped SHM before streaming wakeups. The retained
//! legacy generator is not the authority for this plugin's existence or state.

#[path = "gemma_brain_methods.rs"]
pub mod methods;
#[path = "ui_workspace_methods.rs"]
pub mod workspace;

use anyhow::Result;
use async_trait::async_trait;
use op_state::{ApplyResult, Checkpoint, PluginCapabilities, StateDiff, StatePlugin};
use op_state_store::PluginSchema;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use simd_json::OwnedValue as Value;

/// Tag-routing / subid-classification configuration owned by the brain.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "sch.software.gemma-brain.routing.schema@v1"))]
pub struct GemmaRouting {
    /// Whether Gemma performs OSCAL subid classification.
    #[serde(default)]
    #[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "mut.service.gemma-brain.subid-classification@v1"))]
    pub subid_classification: bool,
    /// Whether Gemma performs xray/OpenFlow tag routing.
    #[serde(default)]
    #[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "mut.service.gemma-brain.tag-routing@v1"))]
    pub tag_routing: bool,
    /// xray config the routing decisions are written into.
    #[serde(default)]
    #[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "src.service.gemma-brain.xray-config@v1"))]
    pub xray_config_path: String,
}

/// UI-spec gallery surface (the artifact the lovable SPA renders).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "sch.software.gemma-brain.gallery.schema@v1"))]
pub struct GemmaGallery {
    /// Tmpfs path of the gallery JSON (formerly produced by the retired `op-gemma` binary).
    #[serde(default)]
    #[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "exp.service.gemma-brain.gallery-path@v1"))]
    pub specs_path: String,
    /// Target number of specs the gallery is topped up to.
    #[serde(default)]
    #[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "mut.service.gemma-brain.target-count@v1"))]
    pub target_count: u32,
    /// Current number of specs present (observed live).
    #[serde(default)]
    #[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "obs.software.gemma-brain.spec-count@v1"))]
    pub spec_count: u32,
}

/// Top-level state for the Gemma brain.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "sch.software.plugin.gemma-brain.schema@v1"))]
#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-category" = "llm"))]
pub struct GemmaBrainState {
    /// Committed private workspace revision; not public_state-authorized.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    #[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "obs.service.gemma.ui-workspace.revision@v2"))]
    pub document_revision: Option<u64>,
    /// Stored json_render schema hash, not a recomputed/global catalog hash.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    #[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "src.service.gemma.ui-renderer.schema-hash@v2"))]
    pub catalog_hash: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    #[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "obs.service.gemma.ui-workspace.jobs@v2"))]
    pub jobs: Option<std::collections::BTreeMap<String, workspace::UiGenerationJob>>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    #[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "obs.service.gemma.ui-workspace.specs@v2"))]
    pub specs: Option<std::collections::BTreeMap<String, workspace::UiSpecRecord>>,
    /// Derived operational status (observed): `unavailable` (no gallery
    /// producer present), `empty`, `partial`, or `ready`.
    #[serde(default)]
    #[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "obs.software.gemma-brain.status@v1"))]
    pub status: String,
    /// The generic LLM plugin this brain consumes for inference. Not a model —
    /// the model is selected inside that plugin.
    #[serde(default)]
    #[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "mut.service.gemma-brain.llm-plugin@v1"))]
    pub llm_plugin: String,
    /// Enabled reasoning perspectives (the four axes).
    #[serde(default)]
    #[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "mut.service.gemma-brain.perspectives@v1"))]
    pub perspectives: Vec<String>,
    /// Registered model-agnostic routing tags in this private workspace.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub tags: Option<std::collections::BTreeMap<String, methods::GemmaTag>>,
    /// Monotonic revision of the private tag taxonomy.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub taxonomy_revision: Option<u64>,
    /// Routing / subid-classification configuration.
    #[serde(default)]
    #[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "mut.service.gemma-brain.routing@v1"))]
    pub routing: GemmaRouting,
    /// UI-spec gallery surface.
    #[serde(default)]
    #[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "sch.software.gemma-brain.gallery@v1"))]
    pub gallery: GemmaGallery,
}

pub struct GemmaBrainPlugin;

impl Default for GemmaBrainPlugin {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self
    }
}

impl GemmaBrainPlugin {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl StatePlugin for GemmaBrainPlugin {
    fn name(&self) -> &str {
        "gemma_brain"
    }

    fn version(&self) -> &str {
        "4.0.0"
    }

    fn schema(&self) -> Option<PluginSchema> {
        let mut schema = gemma_brain_schema();
        super::common::oscal::ensure_category_metadata_fields(&mut schema);
        Some(schema)
    }

    async fn calculate_diff(&self, _current: &Value, _desired: &Value) -> Result<StateDiff> {
        anyhow::bail!("Gemma reconciliation requires canonical owner-scoped method dispatch")
    }

    async fn apply_state(&self, _diff: &StateDiff) -> Result<ApplyResult> {
        anyhow::bail!("Gemma mutation requires canonical owner-scoped method dispatch")
    }

    async fn verify_state(&self, _desired: &Value) -> Result<bool> {
        anyhow::bail!("Gemma verification requires a committed owner-scoped projection")
    }

    async fn create_checkpoint(&self) -> Result<Checkpoint> {
        anyhow::bail!("Gemma has no generic checkpoint owner")
    }

    async fn rollback(&self, _checkpoint: &Checkpoint) -> Result<()> {
        anyhow::bail!("Gemma has no generic rollback owner")
    }

    fn capabilities(&self) -> PluginCapabilities {
        PluginCapabilities {
            supports_rollback: false,
            supports_checkpoints: false,
            supports_verification: false,
            atomic_operations: false,
        }
    }
}

/// Canonical `gemma_brain` schema derived from [`GemmaBrainState`] via schemars.
pub(crate) fn gemma_brain_schema() -> PluginSchema {
    let root = serde_json::to_value(schemars::schema_for!(GemmaBrainState))
        .expect("schemars schema serializes to JSON");
    let mut schema = super::schemars_adapter::plugin_schema_from_json(
        "gemma_brain",
        "4.0.0",
        "Gemma cognitive brain: tag routing, subid classification, reasoning perspectives, and UI-spec gallery; consumes the large_language_model plugin for inference",
        &root,
    );

    // Add methods
    use super::plugin_scaffold_helpers::method_decl_from_schemars_with_output;
    use op_state_store::SideEffect;

    schema.methods.insert(
        "classify".to_string(),
        method_decl_from_schemars_with_output::<methods::ClassifyInput, methods::ClassifyOutput>(
            "classify",
            SideEffect::Read,
            true,
            "gemma.invoke",
            "mut.service.gemma.classify@v1",
        ),
    );
    let router = super::tched_router::tched_router_schema();
    let mut route = router.methods["ResolveRoute"].clone();
    route.name = "route".into();
    route.required_capability = Some("gemma.invoke".into());
    route.subid = "obs.service.gemma.route@v2".into();
    schema.methods.insert("route".into(), route);
    schema.methods.insert(
        "list_perspectives".to_string(),
        method_decl_from_schemars_with_output::<
            methods::ListTaxonomyInput,
            methods::ListPerspectivesOutput,
        >(
            "list_perspectives",
            SideEffect::Read,
            true,
            "gemma.read",
            "obs.service.gemma.perspective.list@v1",
        ),
    );
    schema.methods.insert(
        "list_tags".to_string(),
        method_decl_from_schemars_with_output::<methods::ListTaxonomyInput, methods::ListTagsOutput>(
            "list_tags",
            SideEffect::Read,
            true,
            "gemma.read",
            "obs.service.gemma.tag.list@v1",
        ),
    );
    schema.methods.insert(
        "register_tag".to_string(),
        method_decl_from_schemars_with_output::<
            methods::RegisterTagInput,
            methods::RegisterTagOutput,
        >(
            "register_tag",
            SideEffect::Mutation,
            false,
            "gemma.invoke",
            "mut.service.gemma.tag.register@v1",
        ),
    );
    schema.methods.insert(
        "analyze_intent".to_string(),
        method_decl_from_schemars_with_output::<
            methods::AnalyzeIntentInput,
            methods::AnalyzeIntentOutput,
        >(
            "analyze_intent",
            SideEffect::Read,
            true,
            "gemma.invoke",
            "mut.service.gemma.intent.analyze@v1",
        ),
    );

    workspace::declare_methods(&mut schema);
    schema.dependencies = vec!["large_language_model".into(), "json_render".into()];

    schema.capabilities.insert(
        "gemma.invoke".to_string(),
        op_state_store::CapabilityDecl {
            id: "gemma.invoke".to_string(),
            description: "Grants: classify, route, register_tag, analyze_intent and canonical private UI workspace mutations/recovery.".to_string(),
        },
    );
    schema.capabilities.insert(
        "gemma.read".to_string(),
        op_state_store::CapabilityDecl {
            id: "gemma.read".to_string(),
            description: "Grants: list_perspectives, list_tags and canonical private UI workspace/spec/job reads.".to_string(),
        },
    );

    schema
}

// Self-registration: the plugin registry discovers this via inventory
// (single source of the catalog; no central dispatch list).
inventory::submit! {
    crate::default_registry::PluginReg::new("gemma_brain", |_ctx| std::sync::Arc::new(GemmaBrainPlugin::new()))
}
</file>

<file path="op-plugins/src/state_plugins/ghostbridge.rs">
//! Ghostbridge plugin — bridge identity, TLS management, and Ghostrunner surface.
//!
//! Ghostbridge is the inward-facing bridge that extends zeroclaw's routing with
//! TLS-backed gRPC-Web connectivity, wireguard-pubkey identity, and the
//! Ghostrunner browser UI surface. It follows the same
//! `PluginSchema`/`StatePlugin` pattern as every other state plugin — no
//! centralized registry, no JSON-RPC, no SQL — just a 1:1 schema declaration.

use super::plugin_scaffold_helpers::method_decl_from_schemars_with_output;
use anyhow::Result;
use async_trait::async_trait;
use op_state::{ApplyResult, Checkpoint, DiffMetadata, PluginCapabilities, StateDiff, StatePlugin};
use op_state_store::PluginSchema;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use serde_json::Value as JsonValue;
use simd_json::OwnedValue as Value;

// =============================================================================
// PLUGIN ENTRY: identity and typed schema seed
// =============================================================================

const PLUGIN_NAME: &str = "ghostbridge";
const PLUGIN_VERSION: &str = "1.0.0";
const PLUGIN_CATEGORY: &str = "network";
const PLUGIN_DESCRIPTION: &str =
    "Ghostbridge TLS/identity bridge for Ghostrunner UI, gRPC-Web surface, and WireGuard pubkey transport";
const PLUGIN_DISPLAY_NAME: &str = "Ghostbridge";

/// TLS certificate identity carried by the bridge.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "sch.service.ghostbridge.identity.schema@v1"))]
pub struct BridgeIdentity {
    /// WireGuard public key identifying this bridge.
    #[serde(default)]
    #[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "src.network.ghostbridge.identity.wireguard-pubkey@v1"))]
    pub wireguard_pubkey: String,
    /// TLS certificate subject (CN/SAN).
    #[serde(default)]
    #[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "src.service.ghostbridge.identity.tls-subject@v1"))]
    pub tls_subject: String,
    /// TLS certificate DNS SANs.
    #[serde(default)]
    #[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "src.service.ghostbridge.identity.tls-sans@v1"))]
    pub tls_sans: Vec<String>,
    /// TLS certificate expiration timestamp (ISO 8601).
    #[serde(default)]
    #[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "src.service.ghostbridge.identity.tls-expires@v1"))]
    pub tls_expires: String,
    /// Whether the TLS cert was self-signed or CA-issued.
    #[serde(default)]
    #[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "sch.service.ghostbridge.identity.tls-self-signed@v1"))]
    pub tls_self_signed: bool,
}

/// Ghostrunner — the browser-based bridge administration UI surface.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "sch.service.ghostbridge.ghostrunner.schema@v1"))]
pub struct GhostrunnerSurface {
    /// TCP port the Ghostrunner web UI listens on.
    #[serde(default)]
    #[schemars(extend(
        "x-oscal-subid" = "mut.service.ghostbridge.ghostrunner.port@v1"
    ))]
    pub port: u16,
    /// Bind address for the Ghostrunner web UI.
    #[serde(default)]
    #[schemars(extend(
        "x-oscal-subid" = "mut.service.ghostbridge.ghostrunner.bind-addr@v1"
    ))]
    pub bind_addr: String,
    /// Base URL path prefix (e.g. "/ghostrunner").
    #[serde(default)]
    #[schemars(extend(
        "x-oscal-subid" = "mut.service.ghostbridge.ghostrunner.path@v1"
    ))]
    pub path: String,
    /// True when the Ghostrunner UI is enabled.
    #[serde(default)]
    #[schemars(extend(
        "x-oscal-subid" = "obs.service.ghostbridge.ghostrunner.enabled@v1"
    ))]
    pub enabled: bool,
}

/// A connected bridge endpoint.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "sch.network.ghostbridge.endpoint.schema@v1"))]
pub struct BridgeEndpoint {
    /// Unique endpoint identifier.
    #[serde(default)]
    #[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "obs.network.ghostbridge.endpoint.id@v1"))]
    pub id: String,
    /// Remote address (IP:port).
    #[serde(default)]
    #[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "obs.network.ghostbridge.endpoint.address@v1"))]
    pub address: String,
    /// Endpoint status: active, connecting, disconnected.
    #[serde(default)]
    #[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "obs.network.ghostbridge.endpoint.status@v1"))]
    pub status: String,
    /// Peer WireGuard public key.
    #[serde(default)]
    #[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "src.network.ghostbridge.endpoint.peer-pubkey@v1"))]
    pub peer_pubkey: String,
    /// Connection uptime in seconds.
    #[serde(default)]
    #[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "obs.network.ghostbridge.endpoint.uptime@v1"))]
    pub uptime_secs: u64,
}

/// Root state for the Ghostbridge plugin.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "sch.service.ghostbridge.state.schema@v1"))]
#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-category" = "network"))]
pub struct GhostbridgeState {
    /// Operational status: active, connecting, error.
    #[serde(default)]
    #[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "obs.service.ghostbridge.status@v1"))]
    pub status: String,
    /// Observed bridge identity (aggregates TLS + WireGuard state).
    #[serde(default)]
    #[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "obs.service.ghostbridge.identity@v1"))]
    pub bridge_identity: BridgeIdentity,
    /// Ghostrunner web UI surface config.
    #[serde(default)]
    #[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "exp.service.ghostbridge.ghostrunner@v1"))]
    pub ghostrunner: GhostrunnerSurface,
    /// Connected bridge endpoints.
    #[serde(default)]
    #[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "obs.network.ghostbridge.endpoints@v1"))]
    pub endpoints: Vec<BridgeEndpoint>,
}

// =============================================================================
// Input / Output types for D-Bus / gRPC methods
// =============================================================================

/// Empty input for read-only Ghostbridge methods.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
pub struct EmptyGhostbridgeInput {}

/// Full Ghostbridge state output.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "exp.service.ghostbridge.state.result@v1"))]
pub struct GetStateOutput {
    pub state: GhostbridgeState,
}

/// Bridge identity output.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "obs.service.ghostbridge.identity.result@v1"))]
pub struct GetIdentityOutput {
    pub identity: BridgeIdentity,
}

/// Endpoints list output.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "obs.network.ghostbridge.endpoints.result@v1"))]
pub struct ListEndpointsOutput {
    pub endpoints: Vec<BridgeEndpoint>,
}

/// Ghostrunner surface output.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "obs.service.ghostbridge.ghostrunner.result@v1"))]
pub struct GetGhostrunnerOutput {
    pub ghostrunner: GhostrunnerSurface,
}

// =============================================================================
// PLUGIN BODY
// =============================================================================

pub struct GhostbridgePlugin;

impl Default for GhostbridgePlugin {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self
    }
}

impl GhostbridgePlugin {
    const DEFAULT_GHOSTRUNNER_PORT: u16 = 8091;
    const DEFAULT_GHOSTRUNNER_BIND: &'static str = "127.0.0.1";
    const DEFAULT_GHOSTRUNNER_PATH: &'static str = "/ghostrunner";

    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self
    }

    fn env_or(key: &str, fallback: &str) -> String {
        std::env::var(key).unwrap_or_else(|_| fallback.to_string())
    }

    pub fn current_state() -> GhostbridgeState {
        let wg_pubkey = Self::env_or("GHOSTBRIDGE_WG_PUBKEY", "");
        let tls_subject = Self::env_or("GHOSTBRIDGE_TLS_SUBJECT", "ghostbridge.tech");
        let tls_sans = Self::env_or(
            "GHOSTBRIDGE_TLS_SANS",
            "localhost,ghostbridge.tech,3tched.com",
        );
        let tls_expires = Self::env_or("GHOSTBRIDGE_TLS_EXPIRES", "");
        let tls_self_signed = std::env::var("GHOSTBRIDGE_TLS_SELF_SIGNED")
            .map(|v| v == "1" || v == "true")
            .unwrap_or(true);
        let ghostrunner_port: u16 = std::env::var("GHOSTBRIDGE_UI_PORT")
            .ok()
            .and_then(|v| v.parse().ok())
            .unwrap_or(Self::DEFAULT_GHOSTRUNNER_PORT);
        let ghostrunner_bind = Self::env_or("GHOSTBRIDGE_UI_BIND", Self::DEFAULT_GHOSTRUNNER_BIND);
        let ghostrunner_path = Self::env_or("GHOSTBRIDGE_UI_PATH", Self::DEFAULT_GHOSTRUNNER_PATH);
        let ghostrunner_enabled = std::env::var("GHOSTBRIDGE_UI_ENABLED")
            .map(|v| v == "1" || v == "true")
            .unwrap_or(true);

        GhostbridgeState {
            status: "declared".to_string(),
            bridge_identity: BridgeIdentity {
                wireguard_pubkey: wg_pubkey,
                tls_subject,
                tls_sans: tls_sans.split(',').map(|s| s.trim().to_string()).collect(),
                tls_expires,
                tls_self_signed,
            },
            ghostrunner: GhostrunnerSurface {
                port: ghostrunner_port,
                bind_addr: ghostrunner_bind,
                path: ghostrunner_path,
                enabled: ghostrunner_enabled,
            },
            endpoints: vec![],
        }
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl StatePlugin for GhostbridgePlugin {
    fn name(&self) -> &str {
        PLUGIN_NAME
    }

    fn version(&self) -> &str {
        PLUGIN_VERSION
    }

    fn schema(&self) -> Option<PluginSchema> {
        let schema = ghostbridge_schema();
        Some(schema)
    }

    async fn calculate_diff(&self, _current: &Value, _desired: &Value) -> Result<StateDiff> {
        Ok(StateDiff {
            plugin: PLUGIN_NAME.to_string(),
            actions: vec![],
            metadata: DiffMetadata {
                timestamp: chrono::Utc::now().timestamp(),
                current_hash: "schema-declared".to_string(),
                desired_hash: "schema-declared".to_string(),
            },
        })
    }

    async fn apply_state(&self, _diff: &StateDiff) -> Result<ApplyResult> {
        Ok(ApplyResult {
            success: true,
            changes_applied: vec![],
            errors: vec![],
            checkpoint: None,
        })
    }

    async fn verify_state(&self, _desired: &Value) -> Result<bool> {
        Ok(true)
    }

    async fn create_checkpoint(&self) -> Result<Checkpoint> {
        Ok(Checkpoint {
            id: uuid::Uuid::new_v4().to_string(),
            plugin: PLUGIN_NAME.to_string(),
            timestamp: chrono::Utc::now().timestamp(),
            state_snapshot: simd_json::serde::to_owned_value(Self::current_state())?,
            backend_checkpoint: None,
        })
    }

    async fn rollback(&self, _checkpoint: &Checkpoint) -> Result<()> {
        Ok(())
    }

    fn capabilities(&self) -> PluginCapabilities {
        PluginCapabilities {
            supports_rollback: false,
            supports_checkpoints: true,
            supports_verification: true,
            atomic_operations: false,
        }
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// PLUGIN EXIT: publish the single PluginSchema contract
// =============================================================================

/// Canonical `ghostbridge` schema derived from [`GhostbridgeState`] via schemars.
pub(crate) fn ghostbridge_schema() -> PluginSchema {
    let root = serde_json::to_value(schemars::schema_for!(GhostbridgeState))
        .expect("schemars schema serializes to JSON");
    let mut schema = super::schemars_adapter::plugin_schema_from_json(
        PLUGIN_NAME,
        PLUGIN_VERSION,
        PLUGIN_DESCRIPTION,
        &root,
    );
    schema.category = PLUGIN_CATEGORY.to_string();
    schema.display_name = Some(PLUGIN_DISPLAY_NAME.to_string());

    if let Ok(state) = simd_json::serde::to_owned_value(GhostbridgePlugin::current_state()) {
        super::schemars_adapter::apply_state_defaults(&mut schema, &state);
        schema.example = Some(state);
    }

    schema.methods.insert(
        "GetState".to_string(),
        method_decl_from_schemars_with_output::<EmptyGhostbridgeInput, GetStateOutput>(
            "GetState",
            op_state_store::SideEffect::Read,
            true,
            "cap.service.ghostbridge.state.read@v1",
            "obs.service.ghostbridge.state.get@v1",
        ),
    );
    schema.methods.insert(
        "GetIdentity".to_string(),
        method_decl_from_schemars_with_output::<EmptyGhostbridgeInput, GetIdentityOutput>(
            "GetIdentity",
            op_state_store::SideEffect::Read,
            true,
            "cap.service.ghostbridge.identity.read@v1",
            "obs.service.ghostbridge.identity.get@v1",
        ),
    );
    schema.methods.insert(
        "ListEndpoints".to_string(),
        method_decl_from_schemars_with_output::<EmptyGhostbridgeInput, ListEndpointsOutput>(
            "ListEndpoints",
            op_state_store::SideEffect::Read,
            true,
            "cap.service.ghostbridge.endpoints.read@v1",
            "obs.network.ghostbridge.endpoints.list@v1",
        ),
    );
    schema.methods.insert(
        "GetGhostrunner".to_string(),
        method_decl_from_schemars_with_output::<EmptyGhostbridgeInput, GetGhostrunnerOutput>(
            "GetGhostrunner",
            op_state_store::SideEffect::Read,
            true,
            "cap.service.ghostbridge.ghostrunner.read@v1",
            "obs.service.ghostbridge.ghostrunner.get@v1",
        ),
    );

    schema.capabilities.insert(
        "cap.service.ghostbridge.state.read@v1".to_string(),
        op_state_store::CapabilityDecl {
            id: "cap.service.ghostbridge.state.read@v1".to_string(),
            description: "Grants: GetState.".to_string(),
        },
    );
    schema.capabilities.insert(
        "cap.service.ghostbridge.identity.read@v1".to_string(),
        op_state_store::CapabilityDecl {
            id: "cap.service.ghostbridge.identity.read@v1".to_string(),
            description: "Grants: GetIdentity.".to_string(),
        },
    );
    schema.capabilities.insert(
        "cap.service.ghostbridge.endpoints.read@v1".to_string(),
        op_state_store::CapabilityDecl {
            id: "cap.service.ghostbridge.endpoints.read@v1".to_string(),
            description: "Grants: ListEndpoints.".to_string(),
        },
    );
    schema.capabilities.insert(
        "cap.service.ghostbridge.ghostrunner.read@v1".to_string(),
        op_state_store::CapabilityDecl {
            id: "cap.service.ghostbridge.ghostrunner.read@v1".to_string(),
            description: "Grants: GetGhostrunner.".to_string(),
        },
    );

    schema
}

/// Public accessor for crates that embed the Ghostbridge plugin contract.
pub fn ghostbridge_plugin_schema() -> PluginSchema {
    ghostbridge_schema()
}

/// Plugin-owned method dispatch for the Ghostbridge D-Bus/gRPC surface.
///
/// Keeping these handlers beside the schema makes the contract executable:
/// every method declared by [`ghostbridge_schema`] has a domain result instead
/// of falling through to the bridge's generic argument echo.
pub fn dispatch_ghostbridge_method(method: &str, state: &GhostbridgeState) -> Result<JsonValue> {
    match method {
        "GetState" => Ok(serde_json::json!({ "state": state })),
        "GetIdentity" => Ok(serde_json::json!({
            "identity": &state.bridge_identity
        })),
        "ListEndpoints" => Ok(serde_json::json!({
            "endpoints": &state.endpoints
        })),
        "GetGhostrunner" => Ok(serde_json::json!({
            "ghostrunner": &state.ghostrunner
        })),
        other => Err(anyhow::anyhow!(
            "ghostbridge method is not declared: {other}"
        )),
    }
}

// Self-registration: the plugin registry discovers this via inventory
// (single source of the catalog; no central dispatch list).
inventory::submit! {
    crate::default_registry::PluginReg::new(PLUGIN_NAME, |_ctx| std::sync::Arc::new(GhostbridgePlugin::new()))
}

// =============================================================================
// TESTS
// =============================================================================

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::state_plugins::common::oscal::validate_subid;

    fn collect_subids(node: &serde_json::Value, out: &mut Vec<String>) {
        if let Some(subid) = node
            .get("x-oscal-subid")
            .and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str)
        {
            out.push(subid.to_string());
        }
        if let Some(obj) = node.as_object() {
            for v in obj.values() {
                collect_subids(v, out);
            }
        }
        if let Some(arr) = node.as_array() {
            for v in arr {
                collect_subids(v, out);
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn all_subids_are_valid() {
        let raw = serde_json::to_value(schemars::schema_for!(GhostbridgeState)).unwrap();
        let mut subids = Vec::new();
        collect_subids(&raw, &mut subids);
        assert!(!subids.is_empty(), "expected at least one x-oscal-subid");
        for subid in subids {
            validate_subid(&subid).unwrap_or_else(|_| panic!("invalid subid: {subid}"));
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn public_schema_accessor_returns_ghostbridge_schema() {
        let schema = ghostbridge_plugin_schema();
        assert_eq!(schema.name, PLUGIN_NAME);
        assert_eq!(schema.version, PLUGIN_VERSION);
        assert_eq!(schema.display_name, Some(PLUGIN_DISPLAY_NAME.to_string()));
        assert_eq!(schema.methods.len(), 4);
    }

    #[test]
    fn current_state_has_defaults() {
        let state = GhostbridgePlugin::current_state();
        assert_eq!(state.status, "declared");
        assert_eq!(state.ghostrunner.port, 8091);
        assert_eq!(state.ghostrunner.path, "/ghostrunner");
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_declared_method_returns_concrete_state_values() {
        let mut state = GhostbridgePlugin::current_state();
        state.bridge_identity.wireguard_pubkey = "warp-decoy-pubkey".to_string();
        state.bridge_identity.tls_expires = "2026-12-31T00:00:00Z".to_string();
        state.endpoints.push(BridgeEndpoint {
            id: "endpoint-1".to_string(),
            address: "198.51.100.10:443".to_string(),
            status: "active".to_string(),
            peer_pubkey: "peer-key".to_string(),
            uptime_secs: 42,
        });

        let get_state = dispatch_ghostbridge_method("GetState", &state).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(get_state["state"]["status"], "declared");
        assert_eq!(
            get_state["state"]["bridge_identity"]["wireguard_pubkey"],
            "warp-decoy-pubkey"
        );
        assert_eq!(get_state["state"]["endpoints"][0]["id"], "endpoint-1");

        let identity = dispatch_ghostbridge_method("GetIdentity", &state).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            identity["identity"]["wireguard_pubkey"],
            "warp-decoy-pubkey"
        );
        assert_eq!(identity["identity"]["tls_subject"], "ghostbridge.tech");
        assert_eq!(identity["identity"]["tls_expires"], "2026-12-31T00:00:00Z");

        let endpoints = dispatch_ghostbridge_method("ListEndpoints", &state).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(endpoints["endpoints"].as_array().unwrap().len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(endpoints["endpoints"][0]["address"], "198.51.100.10:443");
        assert_eq!(endpoints["endpoints"][0]["status"], "active");
        assert_eq!(endpoints["endpoints"][0]["uptime_secs"], 42);

        let ghostrunner = dispatch_ghostbridge_method("GetGhostrunner", &state).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(ghostrunner["ghostrunner"]["port"], 8091);
        assert_eq!(ghostrunner["ghostrunner"]["bind_addr"], "127.0.0.1");
        assert_eq!(ghostrunner["ghostrunner"]["path"], "/ghostrunner");
        assert_eq!(ghostrunner["ghostrunner"]["enabled"], true);
    }

    #[test]
    fn undeclared_method_is_rejected() {
        let error = dispatch_ghostbridge_method("NotDeclared", &GhostbridgePlugin::current_state())
            .unwrap_err();
        assert!(error.to_string().contains("not declared"));
    }
}

<file path="op-plugins/src/state_plugins/hardware.rs">
use anyhow::{bail, Result};
use async_trait::async_trait;
use op_state::{ApplyResult, Checkpoint, DiffMetadata, PluginCapabilities, StateDiff, StatePlugin};
use op_state_store::PluginSchema;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use simd_json::prelude::*;
use simd_json::OwnedValue as Value;
use sysinfo::{Disks, System};

/// Hardware inventory snapshot.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, Default, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "sch.software.plugin.hardware.schema@v1"))]
#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-category" = "hardware"))]
pub struct HardwareState {
    /// CPU information.
    #[serde(default)]
    #[schemars(
        description = "CPU information",
        extend("x-oscal-subid" = "exp.service.hardware.cpu.render@v1")
    )]
    pub cpu: CpuInfo,

    /// Memory information.
    #[serde(default)]
    #[schemars(
        description = "Memory information",
        extend("x-oscal-subid" = "exp.service.hardware.memory.render@v1")
    )]
    pub memory: MemoryInfo,

    /// Disk inventory.
    #[serde(default)]
    #[schemars(
        description = "Disk inventory",
        extend("x-oscal-subid" = "exp.service.hardware.disks.render@v1")
    )]
    pub disks: Vec<DiskInfo>,
}

/// CPU information.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, Default, schemars::JsonSchema)]
pub struct CpuInfo {
    /// CPU model name.
    #[schemars(
        description = "CPU model name",
        example = &"AMD Ryzen 9 7950X",
        extend("x-oscal-subid" = "exp.service.hardware.cpu.model.declare@v1")
    )]
    pub model: Option<String>,

    /// Number of CPU cores.
    #[schemars(
        description = "Number of CPU cores",
        example = 16,
        extend("x-oscal-subid" = "exp.service.hardware.cpu.cores.declare@v1")
    )]
    pub cores: usize,
}

/// Memory information.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, Default, schemars::JsonSchema)]
pub struct MemoryInfo {
    /// Total memory in kilobytes.
    #[schemars(
        description = "Total memory in kilobytes",
        example = 33554432,
        extend("x-oscal-subid" = "exp.service.hardware.memory.total-kb.declare@v1")
    )]
    pub total_kb: u64,

    /// Available memory in kilobytes.
    #[schemars(
        description = "Available memory in kilobytes",
        example = 16777216,
        extend("x-oscal-subid" = "exp.service.hardware.memory.available-kb.declare@v1")
    )]
    pub available_kb: u64,
}

/// Disk information.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
pub struct DiskInfo {
    /// Disk device name.
    #[schemars(
        description = "Disk device name",
        example = &"nvme0n1",
        extend("x-oscal-subid" = "exp.service.hardware.disk.name.declare@v1")
    )]
    pub name: String,

    /// Capacity of the mounted filesystem in bytes.
    #[schemars(
        description = "Mounted filesystem capacity in bytes",
        example = 1000204886016_i64,
        extend("x-oscal-subid" = "exp.service.hardware.disk.capacity-bytes.declare@v1")
    )]
    pub capacity_bytes: u64,

    /// Currently available space on the mounted filesystem in bytes.
    pub available_bytes: u64,

    /// Mount point, if any.
    #[serde(default)]
    #[schemars(
        description = "Mount point, if any",
        example = &"/",
        extend("x-oscal-subid" = "exp.service.hardware.disk.mountpoint.declare@v1")
    )]
    pub mountpoint: Option<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
pub struct ScanHardwareOutput {
    pub observed_at: String,
    pub inventory: HardwareState,
    /// `observed` means this request took a fresh native snapshot; it does not
    /// claim a kernel hotplug rescan or a mutation.
    pub disposition: String,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
pub struct RefreshInventoryOutput {
    pub observed_at: String,
    pub inventory: HardwareState,
    /// `observed` means this request took a fresh native snapshot; it does not
    /// claim a kernel hotplug rescan or a mutation.
    pub disposition: String,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
pub struct ListDevicesOutput {
    pub observed_at: String,
    pub devices: Vec<DiskInfo>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
pub struct GetDeviceInput {
    pub name: String,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
pub struct GetDeviceOutput {
    pub observed_at: String,
    pub device: Option<DiskInfo>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
pub struct GetStatsOutput {
    pub observed_at: String,
    pub cpu: CpuInfo,
    pub memory: MemoryInfo,
    pub disk_count: usize,
}

/// Method output paired with the inventory captured by the same native
/// snapshot. The caller commits `state` before returning `output`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct HardwareObservedDispatch {
    pub output: serde_json::Value,
    pub state: HardwareState,
}

pub struct HardwarePlugin;

impl Default for HardwarePlugin {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self
    }
}

impl HardwarePlugin {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self
    }

    fn snapshot() -> Result<(String, HardwareState)> {
        let mut system = System::new();
        system.refresh_memory();
        system.refresh_cpu();
        validate_native_inventory(
            system.total_memory(),
            system.available_memory(),
            system.cpus().len(),
        )?;
        let cpu = system.cpus().first();
        let disks = Disks::new_with_refreshed_list();
        let inventory = HardwareState {
            cpu: CpuInfo {
                model: cpu.and_then(|cpu| nonempty(cpu.brand())),
                cores: system.cpus().len(),
            },
            memory: MemoryInfo {
                total_kb: bytes_to_kib(system.total_memory()),
                available_kb: bytes_to_kib(system.available_memory()),
            },
            disks: disks
                .list()
                .iter()
                .map(|disk| DiskInfo {
                    name: disk.name().to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
                    capacity_bytes: disk.total_space(),
                    available_bytes: disk.available_space(),
                    mountpoint: nonempty(&disk.mount_point().to_string_lossy()),
                })
                .collect(),
        };
        Ok((chrono::Utc::now().to_rfc3339(), inventory))
    }

    pub fn dispatch_hardware_method(
        method: &str,
        args: &serde_json::Value,
    ) -> Result<serde_json::Value> {
        Ok(Self::dispatch_hardware_method_observed(method, args)?.output)
    }

    pub fn dispatch_hardware_method_observed(
        method: &str,
        args: &serde_json::Value,
    ) -> Result<HardwareObservedDispatch> {
        let (observed_at, inventory) = Self::snapshot()?;
        Self::dispatch_snapshot_observed(method, args, observed_at, inventory)
    }

    fn dispatch_snapshot_observed(
        method: &str,
        args: &serde_json::Value,
        observed_at: String,
        inventory: HardwareState,
    ) -> Result<HardwareObservedDispatch> {
        validate_hardware_state(&inventory)?;
        let output = Self::dispatch_snapshot(method, args, observed_at, inventory.clone())?;
        Ok(HardwareObservedDispatch {
            output,
            state: inventory,
        })
    }

    fn dispatch_snapshot(
        method: &str,
        args: &serde_json::Value,
        observed_at: String,
        inventory: HardwareState,
    ) -> Result<serde_json::Value> {
        match method {
            "list_devices" => Ok(serde_json::to_value(ListDevicesOutput {
                observed_at,
                devices: inventory.disks.clone(),
            })?),
            "get_device" => {
                let input: GetDeviceInput = serde_json::from_value(args.clone())?;
                if input.name.trim().is_empty() {
                    bail!("device name must not be empty");
                }
                Ok(serde_json::to_value(GetDeviceOutput {
                    observed_at,
                    device: inventory
                        .disks
                        .iter()
                        .find(|disk| disk.name == input.name)
                        .cloned(),
                })?)
            }
            "get_stats" => Ok(serde_json::to_value(GetStatsOutput {
                observed_at,
                cpu: inventory.cpu,
                memory: inventory.memory,
                disk_count: inventory.disks.len(),
            })?),
            "scan_hardware" => Ok(serde_json::to_value(ScanHardwareOutput {
                observed_at,
                inventory,
                disposition: "observed".to_string(),
            })?),
            "refresh_inventory" => Ok(serde_json::to_value(RefreshInventoryOutput {
                observed_at,
                inventory,
                disposition: "observed".to_string(),
            })?),
            _ => bail!("unsupported hardware method: {method}"),
        }
    }
}

fn validate_native_inventory(
    total_memory_bytes: u64,
    available_memory_bytes: u64,
    cpu_count: usize,
) -> Result<()> {
    if total_memory_bytes == 0 {
        bail!("native hardware snapshot reported zero total memory");
    }
    if available_memory_bytes > total_memory_bytes {
        bail!("native hardware snapshot reported available memory greater than total memory");
    }
    if cpu_count == 0 {
        bail!("native hardware snapshot reported no CPUs");
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn validate_hardware_state(inventory: &HardwareState) -> Result<()> {
    if inventory.memory.total_kb == 0 {
        bail!("hardware observation reported zero total memory");
    }
    if inventory.memory.available_kb > inventory.memory.total_kb {
        bail!("hardware observation reported available memory greater than total memory");
    }
    if inventory.cpu.cores == 0 {
        bail!("hardware observation reported no CPU cores");
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn nonempty(value: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let value = value.trim();
    (!value.is_empty()).then(|| value.to_string())
}

fn bytes_to_kib(bytes: u64) -> u64 {
    bytes / 1024
}
