//! GB.Persona plugin — schemars-seeded, D-Bus-backed agent persona catalog.
//!
//! Projects the live agent-persona catalog from `op-agents` through the
//! `org.opdbus.v1.plugins` surface. The catalog is live, not mocked.

use super::plugin_scaffold_helpers::{method_decl_from_schemars_with_output, AckOutput};
use anyhow::Result;
use async_trait::async_trait;
use op_agents::builtin_agent_descriptors;
use op_state::{
    ApplyResult, Checkpoint, DiffMetadata, PluginCapabilities, StateAction, StateDiff, StatePlugin,
};
use op_state_store::{PluginSchema, SideEffect};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use simd_json::OwnedValue as Value;

// =============================================================================
// PLUGIN ENTRY: identity and typed schema seed
// =============================================================================

const PLUGIN_NAME: &str = "persona";
const PLUGIN_VERSION: &str = "1.1.0";
const PLUGIN_CATEGORY: &str = "agents";
const PLUGIN_DESCRIPTION: &str =
    "Agent persona catalog — built-in agent types, names, descriptions, operations";
const PLUGIN_DISPLAY_NAME: &str = "GB.Persona";

/// A single agent persona.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "exp.agent.persona.persona.render@v1"))]
pub struct Persona {
    /// Agent type identifier.
    #[schemars(
        description = "Agent type identifier",
        extend("x-oscal-subid" = "exp.agent.persona.agent-type.render@v1")
    )]
    pub agent_type: String,

    /// Display name.
    #[schemars(
        description = "Display name",
        extend("x-oscal-subid" = "exp.agent.persona.name.render@v1")
    )]
    pub name: String,

    /// Description of the persona.
    #[schemars(
        description = "Description of the persona",
        extend("x-oscal-subid" = "exp.agent.persona.description.render@v1")
    )]
    pub description: String,

    /// Agent category: execution | persona | orchestration.
    #[schemars(
        description = "Agent category (execution, persona, orchestration)",
        extend("x-oscal-subid" = "exp.agent.persona.category.render@v1")
    )]
    pub category: String,

    /// Supported operations.
    #[serde(default)]
    #[schemars(
        description = "Supported operations",
        extend("x-oscal-subid" = "exp.agent.persona.operations.render@v1")
    )]
    pub operations: Vec<String>,

    /// Per-operation JSON Schemas (input + output).
    #[serde(default)]
    #[schemars(
        description = "Per-operation JSON Schemas",
        extend("x-oscal-subid" = "sch.agent.persona.operation-schemas.render@v1")
    )]
    pub operation_schemas: Vec<PersonaOperationSchema>,
}

/// JSON Schema contract for one agent operation.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "sch.agent.persona.operation.schema@v1"))]
pub struct PersonaOperationSchema {
    pub name: String,
    pub description: String,
    /// JSON Schema for operation arguments.
    #[schemars(with = "serde_json::Value")]
    pub input_schema: serde_json::Value,
    /// JSON Schema for operation results.
    #[schemars(with = "serde_json::Value")]
    pub output_schema: serde_json::Value,
}

/// Persona catalog live state.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "sch.agent.plugin.persona.schema@v2"))]
#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-category" = "agents"))]
pub struct PersonaState {
    /// Current status.
    #[schemars(
        description = "Current status",
        extend("x-oscal-subid" = "obs.agent.persona.status.observe@v1")
    )]
    pub status: String,

    /// Number of personas in the catalog.
    #[schemars(
        description = "Number of personas in the catalog",
        extend("x-oscal-subid" = "obs.agent.persona.count.observe@v1")
    )]
    pub persona_count: usize,

    /// Available personas.
    #[serde(default)]
    #[schemars(
        description = "Available personas",
        extend("x-oscal-subid" = "exp.agent.persona.catalog.render@v1")
    )]
    pub personas: Vec<Persona>,
}

// =============================================================================
// METHOD INPUT/OUTPUT TYPES
// =============================================================================

/// Input for GetIdentity method.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "obs.agent.persona.identity.get.input@v1"))]
pub struct GetIdentityInput {
    /// Agent type to get identity for.
    pub agent_type: String,
}

/// Output for GetIdentity method.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "obs.agent.persona.identity.get.output@v1"))]
pub struct GetIdentityOutput {
    /// The persona identity, if found.
    pub persona: Option<Persona>,
}

/// Input for SetIdentity method.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "mut.agent.persona.identity.set.input@v1"))]
pub struct SetIdentityInput {
    /// Agent type to set identity for.
    pub agent_type: String,
    /// New name.
    pub name: String,
    /// New description (optional).
    #[serde(default)]
    pub description: Option<String>,
}

/// Input for Authenticate method.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "mut.agent.persona.authenticate.input@v1"))]
pub struct AuthenticateInput {
    /// Agent type to authenticate.
    pub agent_type: String,
    /// Credentials map.
    pub credentials: std::collections::HashMap<String, String>,
}

/// Output for Authenticate method.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "obs.agent.persona.authenticate.output@v1"))]
pub struct AuthenticateOutput {
    /// Whether authentication succeeded.
    pub authenticated: bool,
    /// Auth token, if successful.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub token: Option<String>,
}

/// Input for Execute — run a catalog agent operation.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "mut.agent.persona.execute.input@v1"))]
pub struct ExecuteInput {
    /// Agent type from the catalog (e.g. rust-pro, memory).
    pub agent_type: String,
    /// Operation name advertised by that agent.
    pub operation: String,
    /// Optional working path.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub path: Option<String>,
    /// Free-form query (persona agents).
    #[serde(default)]
    pub query: Option<String>,
    /// Operation arguments object.
    #[serde(default)]
    #[schemars(with = "serde_json::Value")]
    pub args: Option<serde_json::Value>,
}

/// Output for Execute.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "obs.agent.persona.execute.output@v1"))]
pub struct ExecuteOutput {
    pub success: bool,
    pub agent_type: String,
    pub operation: String,
    #[schemars(with = "serde_json::Value")]
    pub data: serde_json::Value,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub message: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    #[schemars(with = "serde_json::Value")]
    pub metadata: Option<serde_json::Value>,
}

// =============================================================================
// PLUGIN BODY: D-Bus-backed behavior only
// =============================================================================

pub struct PersonaPlugin;

impl Default for PersonaPlugin {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

impl PersonaPlugin {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self
    }

    /// Enumerate the live persona catalog from the real agent implementations.
    fn live() -> PersonaState {
        let personas: Vec<Persona> = builtin_agent_descriptors()
            .into_iter()
            .map(|d| {
                let category = format!("{:?}", d.category).to_lowercase();
                let operation_schemas = d
                    .operation_schemas
                    .iter()
                    .map(|op| PersonaOperationSchema {
                        name: op.name.clone(),
                        description: op.description.clone(),
                        input_schema: serde_json::from_str(
                            &simd_json::to_string(&op.input_schema).unwrap_or_else(|_| "{}".into()),
                        )
                        .unwrap_or(serde_json::json!({})),
                        output_schema: serde_json::from_str(
                            &simd_json::to_string(&op.output_schema)
                                .unwrap_or_else(|_| "{}".into()),
                        )
                        .unwrap_or(serde_json::json!({})),
                    })
                    .collect();
                Persona {
                    agent_type: d.agent_type,
                    name: d.name,
                    description: d.description,
                    category,
                    operations: d.operations,
                    operation_schemas,
                }
            })
            .collect();
        PersonaState {
            status: "active".to_string(),
            persona_count: personas.len(),
            personas,
        }
    }
}

/// Dispatch persona plugin methods (catalog + execute).
pub async fn dispatch_persona_method(
    method: &str,
    args: &serde_json::Value,
) -> anyhow::Result<serde_json::Value> {
    match method {
        "get_identity" | "GetIdentity" => {
            let agent_type = args
                .get("agent_type")
                .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
                .unwrap_or("");
            let persona = PersonaPlugin::live()
                .personas
                .into_iter()
                .find(|p| p.agent_type == agent_type);
            Ok(serde_json::to_value(GetIdentityOutput { persona })?)
        }
        "set_identity" | "SetIdentity" => {
            anyhow::bail!("persona catalog is read-only (code-defined in op-agents)")
        }
        "list_triggers" => {
            let _: super::agent_triggers::ListTriggersInput = serde_json::from_value(args.clone())
                .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!("invalid list_triggers args: {e}"))?;
            let documents = super::runtime_documents::runtime_documents().await?;
            Ok(serde_json::to_value(
                super::agent_triggers::list_triggers(&documents).await?,
            )?)
        }
        "set_trigger" => {
            let input: super::agent_triggers::SetTriggerInput =
                serde_json::from_value(args.clone())
                    .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!("invalid set_trigger args: {e}"))?;
            let documents = super::runtime_documents::runtime_documents().await?;
            Ok(serde_json::to_value(
                super::agent_triggers::set_trigger(&documents, input).await?,
            )?)
        }
        "delete_trigger" => {
            let input: super::agent_triggers::DeleteTriggerInput =
                serde_json::from_value(args.clone())
                    .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!("invalid delete_trigger args: {e}"))?;
            let documents = super::runtime_documents::runtime_documents().await?;
            Ok(serde_json::to_value(
                super::agent_triggers::delete_trigger(&documents, input).await?,
            )?)
        }
        "authenticate" | "Authenticate" => Ok(serde_json::to_value(AuthenticateOutput {
            authenticated: false,
            token: None,
        })?),
        "execute" | "Execute" => {
            let input: ExecuteInput = serde_json::from_value(args.clone())
                .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!("invalid execute args: {e}"))?;
            let mut task = op_agents::AgentTask::new(&input.agent_type, &input.operation);
            if let Some(path) = &input.path {
                task = task.with_path(path);
            }
            let mut arg_obj = serde_json::Map::new();
            if let Some(serde_json::Value::Object(map)) = input.args.clone() {
                arg_obj.extend(map);
            }
            if let Some(query) = &input.query {
                arg_obj.insert("query".into(), serde_json::Value::String(query.clone()));
            }
            if !arg_obj.is_empty() {
                task = task.with_args(&serde_json::Value::Object(arg_obj).to_string());
            }

            let agent =
                op_agents::create_agent(&input.agent_type, format!("persona-{}", input.agent_type))
                    .map_err(anyhow::Error::msg)?;
            match agent.execute(task).await {
                Ok(result) => {
                    let data: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&result.data)
                        .unwrap_or_else(|_| serde_json::Value::String(result.data.clone()));
                    let metadata = serde_json::to_value(&result.metadata).ok();
                    Ok(serde_json::to_value(ExecuteOutput {
                        success: result.success,
                        agent_type: input.agent_type,
                        operation: result.operation,
                        data,
                        message: metadata
                            .as_ref()
                            .and_then(|m| m.get("message"))
                            .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
                            .map(str::to_string),
                        metadata,
                    })?)
                }
                Err(e) => Ok(serde_json::to_value(ExecuteOutput {
                    success: false,
                    agent_type: input.agent_type,
                    operation: input.operation,
                    data: serde_json::Value::Null,
                    message: Some(e),
                    metadata: None,
                })?),
            }
        }
        other => anyhow::bail!("unknown persona method: {other}"),
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl StatePlugin for PersonaPlugin {
    fn name(&self) -> &str {
        PLUGIN_NAME
    }

    fn version(&self) -> &str {
        PLUGIN_VERSION
    }

    fn schema(&self) -> Option<PluginSchema> {
        Some(persona_schema())
    }

    async fn calculate_diff(&self, _current: &Value, _desired: &Value) -> Result<StateDiff> {
        Ok(StateDiff {
            plugin: PLUGIN_NAME.to_string(),
            actions: vec![StateAction::NoOp {
                resource: "personas".to_string(),
            }],
            metadata: DiffMetadata {
                timestamp: chrono::Utc::now().timestamp(),
                current_hash: String::new(),
                desired_hash: String::new(),
            },
        })
    }

    async fn apply_state(&self, diff: &StateDiff) -> Result<ApplyResult> {
        let mut errors = Vec::new();
        for action in &diff.actions {
            match action {
                StateAction::NoOp { .. } => {}
                other => errors.push(format!(
                    "persona catalog is code-defined (op-agents) and read-only; \
                     cannot apply {:?}",
                    other
                )),
            }
        }
        Ok(ApplyResult {
            success: errors.is_empty(),
            changes_applied: Vec::new(),
            errors,
            checkpoint: None,
        })
    }

    async fn verify_state(&self, desired: &Value) -> Result<bool> {
        let current = simd_json::serde::to_owned_value(Self::live())?;
        Ok(&current == desired)
    }

    async fn create_checkpoint(&self) -> Result<Checkpoint> {
        Ok(Checkpoint {
            id: uuid::Uuid::new_v4().to_string(),
            plugin: PLUGIN_NAME.to_string(),
            timestamp: chrono::Utc::now().timestamp(),
            state_snapshot: simd_json::serde::to_owned_value(Self::live())?,
            backend_checkpoint: None,
        })
    }

    async fn rollback(&self, _checkpoint: &Checkpoint) -> Result<()> {
        Ok(())
    }

    fn capabilities(&self) -> PluginCapabilities {
        PluginCapabilities {
            supports_rollback: false,
            supports_checkpoints: true,
            supports_verification: true,
            atomic_operations: false,
        }
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// PLUGIN EXIT: publish the single PluginSchema contract
// =============================================================================

pub fn persona_schema() -> PluginSchema {
    let root = serde_json::to_value(schemars::schema_for!(PersonaState))
        .expect("schemars schema serializes to JSON");
    let mut schema = super::schemars_adapter::plugin_schema_from_json(
        PLUGIN_NAME,
        PLUGIN_VERSION,
        PLUGIN_DESCRIPTION,
        &root,
    );
    schema.category = PLUGIN_CATEGORY.to_string();
    schema.display_name = Some(PLUGIN_DISPLAY_NAME.to_string());

    // GetIdentity method
    schema.methods.insert(
        "get_identity".to_string(),
        method_decl_from_schemars_with_output::<GetIdentityInput, GetIdentityOutput>(
            "get_identity",
            SideEffect::Read,
            true,
            "persona.read",
            "obs.agent.persona.identity.get@v1",
        ),
    );

    // SetIdentity method
    schema.methods.insert(
        "set_identity".to_string(),
        method_decl_from_schemars_with_output::<SetIdentityInput, AckOutput>(
            "set_identity",
            SideEffect::Mutation,
            false,
            "persona.write",
            "mut.agent.persona.identity.set@v1",
        ),
    );

    // Authenticate method
    schema.methods.insert(
        "authenticate".to_string(),
        method_decl_from_schemars_with_output::<AuthenticateInput, AuthenticateOutput>(
            "authenticate",
            SideEffect::Mutation,
            false,
            "persona.write",
            "mut.agent.persona.authenticate@v1",
        ),
    );

    // Execute — run a catalog agent operation (schema-validated entrypoint)
    schema.methods.insert(
        "execute".to_string(),
        method_decl_from_schemars_with_output::<ExecuteInput, ExecuteOutput>(
            "execute",
            SideEffect::Mutation,
            false,
            "persona.execute",
            "mut.agent.persona.execute@v1",
        ),
    );

    // Event triggers (OD-63): durable, revisioned, sealed here.
    {
        use super::agent_triggers::{
            DeleteTriggerInput, DeleteTriggerOutput, ListTriggersInput, ListTriggersOutput,
            SetTriggerInput, SetTriggerOutput,
        };
        schema.methods.insert(
            "list_triggers".to_string(),
            method_decl_from_schemars_with_output::<ListTriggersInput, ListTriggersOutput>(
                "list_triggers",
                SideEffect::Read,
                true,
                "persona.read",
                "obs.agent.persona.triggers.list@v1",
            ),
        );
        schema.methods.insert(
            "set_trigger".to_string(),
            method_decl_from_schemars_with_output::<SetTriggerInput, SetTriggerOutput>(
                "set_trigger",
                SideEffect::Mutation,
                true,
                "persona.write",
                "mut.agent.persona.triggers.set@v1",
            ),
        );
        schema.methods.insert(
            "delete_trigger".to_string(),
            method_decl_from_schemars_with_output::<DeleteTriggerInput, DeleteTriggerOutput>(
                "delete_trigger",
                SideEffect::Mutation,
                true,
                "persona.write",
                "mut.agent.persona.triggers.delete@v1",
            ),
        );
    }

    schema.capabilities.insert(
        "persona.read".to_string(),
        op_state_store::CapabilityDecl {
            id: "persona.read".to_string(),
            description: "Grants: get_identity, list_triggers.".to_string(),
        },
    );
    schema.capabilities.insert(
        "persona.write".to_string(),
        op_state_store::CapabilityDecl {
            id: "persona.write".to_string(),
            description: "Grants: set_identity, authenticate, set_trigger, delete_trigger."
                .to_string(),
        },
    );
    schema.capabilities.insert(
        "persona.execute".to_string(),
        op_state_store::CapabilityDecl {
            id: "persona.execute".to_string(),
            description: "Grants: execute.".to_string(),
        },
    );

    schema
}

// Self-registration: the plugin registry discovers this via inventory
// (single source of the catalog; no central dispatch list).
inventory::submit! {
    crate::default_registry::PluginReg::new(PLUGIN_NAME, |_ctx| std::sync::Arc::new(PersonaPlugin::new()))
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod methods_tests {
    use super::*;
    use serde_json::json;

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn identity_lookup_and_execute_use_registered_persona_operations() {
        let identity = dispatch_persona_method("get_identity", &json!({"agent_type":"rust-pro"}))
            .await
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(identity["persona"]["agent_type"], "rust-pro");
        assert!(identity["persona"]["name"]
            .as_str()
            .unwrap()
            .contains("Rust"));
        assert!(identity["persona"]["operations"]
            .as_array()
            .unwrap()
            .iter()
            .any(|operation| operation == "check"));
        assert!(!identity["persona"]["operation_schemas"]
            .as_array()
            .unwrap()
            .is_empty());
        let expert =
            dispatch_persona_method("get_identity", &json!({"agent_type":"backend-architect"}))
                .await
                .unwrap();
        assert!(expert["persona"]["operations"]
            .as_array()
            .unwrap()
            .iter()
            .any(|operation| operation == "consult"));
        let query = "How should API design handle retries?";
        let executed = dispatch_persona_method(
            "execute",
            &json!({
                "agent_type":"backend-architect", "operation":"consult", "query":query
            }),
        )
        .await
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(executed["success"], true);
        assert_eq!(executed["agent_type"], "backend-architect");
        assert_eq!(executed["operation"], "consult");
        assert_eq!(executed["data"]["query"], query);
        assert_eq!(executed["data"]["source"], "embedded_knowledge");
        assert!(!executed["data"]["recommendations"]
            .as_array()
            .unwrap()
            .is_empty());
        assert!(executed["data"]["answer"]
            .as_str()
            .unwrap()
            .contains("API design"));
        let unknown =
            dispatch_persona_method("get_identity", &json!({"agent_type":"absent-persona"}))
                .await
                .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(unknown["persona"], serde_json::Value::Null);
        assert!(dispatch_persona_method(
            "execute",
            &json!({
                "agent_type":"absent-persona", "operation":"consult", "query":query
            })
        )
        .await
        .is_err());
    }
}

//! Plugin scaffold helpers.
//!
//! THE PLUGIN IS THE SCHEMA. Every schema is defined in its own plugin file.
//! This module only provides shared helpers used by the ENTRY/EXIT scaffold:
//! projection seeds, method declarations, and legacy cross-plugin discovery.
//!
//! For the expected top-to-bottom plugin shape, start from
//! `plugin_scaffold.rs.template`. Do not add new plugin schema bodies here.

// ── Shared utility functions (not schemas) ─────────────────────────────────────

use op_state_store::{FieldSchema, FieldType, MethodDecl, PluginSchema, SideEffect};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use simd_json::{json, OwnedValue as Value};

/// Materialize a deterministic initial live state from a plugin schema.
///
/// This is the schema-side bootstrap for D-Bus projection creation. It never
/// queries a plugin backend and never invents data outside the contract:
/// field defaults win, then examples, then an empty value matching the field
/// type. The MutationEngine writes this once when no projection exists yet;
/// later mutations replace it through the normal `/dev/shm/opdbus/state`
/// write door.
pub(crate) fn materialize_state_from_schema(schema: &PluginSchema) -> Value {
    if let Some(example) = &schema.example {
        return example.clone();
    }

    let mut state = simd_json::value::owned::Object::new();
    let mut fields = schema.fields.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>();
    fields.sort_by_key(|(a, _)| *a);

    for (name, field) in fields {
        state.insert(name.clone(), materialize_field(field));
    }

    Value::Object(Box::new(state))
}

fn materialize_field(field: &FieldSchema) -> Value {
    if let Some(value) = &field.default {
        return value.clone();
    }
    if let Some(value) = &field.example {
        return value.clone();
    }

    materialize_field_type(&field.field_type)
}

fn materialize_field_type(field_type: &FieldType) -> Value {
    match field_type {
        FieldType::String => json!(""),
        FieldType::Integer => json!(0),
        FieldType::Float => json!(0.0),
        FieldType::Boolean => json!(false),
        FieldType::Array(_) => json!([]),
        FieldType::Object(fields) => {
            let mut object = simd_json::value::owned::Object::new();
            let mut fields = fields.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>();
            fields.sort_by_key(|(a, _)| *a);
            for (name, field) in fields {
                object.insert(name.clone(), materialize_field(field));
            }
            Value::Object(Box::new(object))
        }
        FieldType::Enum(values) => values
            .first()
            .map(|value| json!(value))
            .unwrap_or_else(|| json!(null)),
        FieldType::OneOf(types) => types
            .first()
            .map(materialize_field_type)
            .unwrap_or_else(|| json!(null)),
        FieldType::Map(_) => json!({}),
        FieldType::JsonSchema(_) | FieldType::Any => json!(null),
    }
}

/// Format a plugin's live state into a `PluginSchema`.
///
/// This is a *formatter*, not a schema authority — nothing here is indexed. The
/// plugin's live state (its `*State` struct) is the single source
/// of truth; field types are inferred from that state, so the schema can never
/// drift from what the plugin actually reports. To add a field, add it to the
/// plugin state — never hand-write a field definition.
pub(crate) fn schema_from_state(
    name: &str,
    category: &str,
    version: &str,
    description: &str,
    state: &Value,
) -> PluginSchema {
    use simd_json::prelude::*;

    let mut builder = PluginSchema::builder(name)
        .version(version)
        .category(category)
        .description(description);

    if let Some(obj) = state.as_object() {
        for (key, value) in obj.iter() {
            builder = builder.field(&key.to_string(), field_from_value(value));
        }
    }

    builder.example(state.clone()).build()
}

/// Infer a `FieldSchema` (type + example) from a live state value.
pub(crate) fn field_from_value(value: &Value) -> FieldSchema {
    FieldSchema {
        field_type: infer_field_type(value),
        required: false,
        description: String::new(),
        default: None,
        example: Some(value.clone()),
        constraints: Vec::new(),
        read_only: false,
        read_only_when: None,
    }
}

/// Infer a `FieldType` from a live state value, recursing into arrays/objects.
pub(crate) fn infer_field_type(value: &Value) -> FieldType {
    use simd_json::prelude::*;

    if value.is_null() {
        FieldType::Any
    } else if value.as_bool().is_some() {
        FieldType::Boolean
    } else if value.as_i64().is_some() || value.as_u64().is_some() {
        FieldType::Integer
    } else if value.as_f64().is_some() {
        FieldType::Float
    } else if value.as_str().is_some() {
        FieldType::String
    } else if let Some(arr) = value.as_array() {
        let inner = arr.first().map(infer_field_type).unwrap_or(FieldType::Any);
        FieldType::Array(Box::new(inner))
    } else if let Some(obj) = value.as_object() {
        let fields = obj
            .iter()
            .map(|(k, v)| (k.to_string(), field_from_value(v)))
            .collect();
        FieldType::Object(fields)
    } else {
        FieldType::Any
    }
}

pub(crate) fn any_field(required: bool, description: &str, default: Option<Value>) -> FieldSchema {
    FieldSchema {
        field_type: FieldType::Any,
        required,
        description: description.to_string(),
        default,
        example: None,
        constraints: Vec::new(),
        read_only: false,
        read_only_when: None,
    }
}

pub(crate) fn cap_method(
    name: &str,
    side_effect: SideEffect,
    idempotent: bool,
    required_capability: &str,
    subid: &str,
) -> MethodDecl {
    MethodDecl {
        name: name.to_string(),
        args: json!({"type": "object", "additionalProperties": true}),
        returns: Some(json!({"type": "object", "additionalProperties": true})),
        side_effect,
        idempotent,
        required_capability: Some(required_capability.to_string()),
        subid: subid.to_string(),
    }
}

use super::common::oscal::is_component_type;
use std::collections::HashMap;

/// Category used when a plugin declares nothing to infer one from.
const DEFAULT_CATEGORY: &str = "software";

/// Build the schema-level subid for a plugin.
///
/// Declared in one place so every plugin gets one without copy-pasting a
/// `#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = ...))]` attribute onto its state struct
/// — that duplication is why 20 of 65 plugins ended up with no schema subid at
/// all, while their methods (which route through the helpers here) always had
/// theirs.
///
/// `declared_category` is the plugin stating what it is, and always wins — it is
/// the one fact here that cannot be derived from anything else. Failing that,
/// the category is inferred from the plugin's own field subids, so a plugin
/// cannot contradict itself. Ties break lexicographically: this value feeds the
/// schema hash, so it must not depend on `HashMap` iteration order.
///
/// The subject segment is kebab-cased — `SUBID_CATEGORIES`' grammar allows no
/// underscores, so `agent_config` has to become `agent-config`.
pub fn derive_schema_subid(
    plugin_name: &str,
    declared_category: Option<&str>,
    declared: &HashMap<String, String>,
) -> String {
    let inferred = || {
        let mut counts: HashMap<&str, usize> = HashMap::new();
        for subid in declared.values() {
            if let Some(category) = subid.split('.').nth(1) {
                if is_component_type(category) {
                    *counts.entry(category).or_default() += 1;
                }
            }
        }

        let mut ranked: Vec<(&str, usize)> = counts.into_iter().collect();
        ranked.sort_by(|a, b| b.1.cmp(&a.1).then_with(|| a.0.cmp(b.0)));
        ranked
            .first()
            .map(|(c, _)| c.to_string())
            .unwrap_or_else(|| DEFAULT_CATEGORY.to_string())
    };

    // An unusable declared category is ignored rather than trusted: emitting it
    // would produce a subid that fails validation at the gate.
    let category = declared_category
        .filter(|c| is_component_type(c))
        .map(str::to_string)
        .unwrap_or_else(inferred);

    format!(
        "sch.{category}.plugin.{}.schema@v1",
        plugin_name.replace('_', "-")
    )
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
pub struct EmptyInput {}

/// Create a MethodDecl from a schemars-typed input struct.
///
/// This is the canonical pattern for all plugins: define method inputs as
/// Rust structs with `#[derive(schemars::JsonSchema)]`, then use this function
/// to generate typed method declarations. The resulting schema drives D-Bus method
/// validation and gRPC proto generation.
///
/// For methods with typed outputs, use `method_decl_from_schemars_with_output`.
/// For methods with no meaningful return (just success/failure), use `AckOutput`.
#[deprecated(
    since = "0.2.0",
    note = "Use method_decl_from_schemars_with_output for typed returns"
)]
pub fn method_decl_from_schemars<Input: schemars::JsonSchema>(
    name: &str,
    side_effect: SideEffect,
    idempotent: bool,
    required_capability: &str,
    subid: &str,
) -> MethodDecl {
    method_decl_from_schemars_with_output::<Input, AckOutput>(
        name,
        side_effect,
        idempotent,
        required_capability,
        subid,
    )
}

/// Dual-generic helper that generates method declarations with typed input AND output schemas.
/// The returns schema is derived from `Output` via schemars - NO hardcoded `{"type": "object"}`.
pub fn method_decl_from_schemars_with_output<
    Input: schemars::JsonSchema,
    Output: schemars::JsonSchema,
>(
    name: &str,
    side_effect: SideEffect,
    idempotent: bool,
    required_capability: &str,
    subid: &str,
) -> MethodDecl {
    // Generate input schema
    let serde_input_schema = serde_json::to_value(schemars::schema_for!(Input)).unwrap();
    let input_bytes = serde_json::to_vec(&serde_input_schema).unwrap();
    let mut input_bytes = input_bytes;
    let args = simd_json::to_owned_value(&mut input_bytes).unwrap();

    // Generate output schema
    let serde_output_schema = serde_json::to_value(schemars::schema_for!(Output)).unwrap();
    let output_bytes = serde_json::to_vec(&serde_output_schema).unwrap();
    let mut output_bytes = output_bytes;
    let returns = simd_json::to_owned_value(&mut output_bytes).unwrap();

    MethodDecl {
        name: name.to_string(),
        args,
        returns: Some(returns),
        side_effect,
        idempotent,
        required_capability: Some(required_capability.to_string()),
        subid: subid.to_string(),
    }
}

/// Standard acknowledgment response for methods that only need success/failure.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
pub struct AckOutput {
    pub success: bool,
}

pub(crate) fn simple_schema(
    name: &str,
    description: &str,
    dependencies: &[&str],
    fields: Vec<(&str, FieldSchema)>,
) -> PluginSchema {
    let mut builder = PluginSchema::builder(name)
        .version("1.0.0")
        .description(description);
    for dep in dependencies {
        builder = builder.dependency(dep);
    }
    for (field_name, schema) in fields {
        builder = builder.field(field_name, schema);
    }
    builder.build()
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::collections::HashMap;

    fn field(field_type: FieldType, default: Option<Value>, example: Option<Value>) -> FieldSchema {
        FieldSchema {
            field_type,
            required: false,
            description: String::new(),
            default,
            example,
            constraints: Vec::new(),
            read_only: false,
            read_only_when: None,
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn materializes_seed_state_from_schema_defaults_examples_and_types() {
        let schema = PluginSchema::builder("example")
            .field(
                "enabled",
                field(FieldType::Boolean, Some(json!(true)), Some(json!(false))),
            )
            .field("label", field(FieldType::String, None, Some(json!("demo"))))
            .field(
                "mode",
                field(
                    FieldType::Enum(vec!["active".to_string(), "passive".to_string()]),
                    None,
                    None,
                ),
            )
            .field(
                "choice",
                field(
                    FieldType::OneOf(vec![FieldType::Integer, FieldType::String]),
                    None,
                    None,
                ),
            )
            .field(
                "nested",
                field(
                    FieldType::Object(HashMap::from([(
                        "count".to_string(),
                        field(FieldType::Integer, None, None),
                    )])),
                    None,
                    None,
                ),
            )
            .build();

        let state = materialize_state_from_schema(&schema);

        assert_eq!(state["enabled"], json!(true));
        assert_eq!(state["label"], json!("demo"));
        assert_eq!(state["mode"], json!("active"));
        assert_eq!(state["choice"], json!(0));
        assert_eq!(state["nested"]["count"], json!(0));
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod derive_schema_subid_tests {
    use super::derive_schema_subid;
    use crate::state_plugins::common::oscal::validate_subid;
    use std::collections::HashMap;

    fn declared(pairs: &[(&str, &str)]) -> HashMap<String, String> {
        pairs
            .iter()
            .map(|(k, v)| (k.to_string(), v.to_string()))
            .collect()
    }

    #[test]
    fn takes_the_category_the_plugins_own_fields_use() {
        // procfs declares `service` on every field but `software` on its struct;
        // the fields are the plugin describing itself, so they win.
        let subids = declared(&[
            ("memory", "obs.service.procfs.memory.query@v2"),
            ("cpuinfo", "obs.service.procfs.cpuinfo.query@v1"),
        ]);
        let got = derive_schema_subid("procfs", None, &subids);
        assert_eq!(got, "sch.service.plugin.procfs.schema@v1");
        assert!(validate_subid(&got).is_ok(), "derived subid must validate");
    }

    #[test]
    fn kebab_cases_underscored_plugin_names() {
        // The grammar allows no underscores, so `agent_config` must not appear
        // verbatim or the result fails validation.
        let got = derive_schema_subid("agent_config", None, &declared(&[]));
        assert_eq!(got, "sch.software.plugin.agent-config.schema@v1");
        assert!(validate_subid(&got).is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn accepts_internal_categories_not_just_oscal_ones() {
        let subids = declared(&[("subvolumes", "obs.storage.btrfs.subvolume.list@v1")]);
        let got = derive_schema_subid("btrfs", None, &subids);
        assert_eq!(got, "sch.storage.plugin.btrfs.schema@v1");
        assert!(validate_subid(&got).is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn is_deterministic_because_the_result_feeds_the_schema_hash() {
        let subids = declared(&[
            ("a", "obs.service.x.a.query@v1"),
            ("b", "obs.network.x.b.query@v1"),
            ("c", "obs.network.x.c.query@v1"),
        ]);
        let first = derive_schema_subid("x", None, &subids);
        for _ in 0..50 {
            assert_eq!(derive_schema_subid("x", None, &subids), first);
        }
        assert_eq!(first, "sch.network.plugin.x.schema@v1");
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod declared_category_tests {
    use super::derive_schema_subid;
    use crate::state_plugins::common::oscal::validate_subid;
    use std::collections::HashMap;

    #[test]
    fn a_declared_category_beats_inference() {
        // openflow's fields say nothing, but the plugin knows it is network.
        let got = derive_schema_subid("openflow", Some("network"), &HashMap::new());
        assert_eq!(got, "sch.network.plugin.openflow.schema@v1");
        assert!(validate_subid(&got).is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_unusable_declared_category_is_ignored_not_emitted() {
        // Emitting an unknown category would fail the subid gate, so the
        // derivation must fall back rather than trust the declaration.
        for bogus in ["nonsense", "replace_me", ""] {
            let got = derive_schema_subid("x", Some(bogus), &HashMap::new());
            assert_eq!(got, "sch.software.plugin.x.schema@v1");
            assert!(validate_subid(&got).is_ok(), "{bogus} produced {got}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_domain_terms_real_plugins_declare_are_usable() {
        // `llm` and `agents` are declared by live plugins. They are aliases, so
        // they survive into the subid verbatim and resolve to OSCAL elsewhere.
        for (category, plugin) in [("llm", "large-language-model"), ("agents", "agent-config")] {
            let got = derive_schema_subid(plugin, Some(category), &HashMap::new());
            assert_eq!(got, format!("sch.{category}.plugin.{plugin}.schema@v1"));
            assert!(validate_subid(&got).is_ok(), "{category} produced {got}");
        }
    }
}
</file>

<file path="op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_scaffold.rs.template">
//! Plugin scaffold template.
//!
//! Copy this file when rebuilding a plugin from scratch. Keep the ENTRY and
//! EXIT blocks intact so every plugin has the same audit shape:
//! - ENTRY owns identity, typed state, and typed method contracts.
//! - EXIT publishes the PluginSchema contract consumed by D-Bus, The Sled,
//!   gRPC, reflection, MCP, and the GUI renderer.
//!
//! Do not put this file in `mod.rs`; it is a template, not compiled source.

use anyhow::Result;
use async_trait::async_trait;
use op_state::{ApplyResult, Checkpoint, DiffMetadata, PluginCapabilities, StateDiff, StatePlugin};
use op_state_store::{PluginSchema, SideEffect};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use simd_json::{json, OwnedValue as Value};

use super::plugin_scaffold_helpers::{
    method_decl_from_schemars_with_output, schema_from_state, AckOutput,
};

// =============================================================================
// PLUGIN ENTRY: identity and typed schema seed
// =============================================================================

const PLUGIN_NAME: &str = "replace_me";
const PLUGIN_VERSION: &str = "1.0.0";
const PLUGIN_CATEGORY: &str = "replace_me";
const PLUGIN_DESCRIPTION: &str = "Replace with the plugin's D-Bus contract purpose.";

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct ReplaceMePlugin;

impl ReplaceMePlugin {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self
    }
}

/// The plugin's published live-state contract.
///
/// This struct is the schemars seed. Add fields here first, with OSCAL subids,
/// then let schema-output-processor turn it into PluginSchema output.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "sch.software.plugin.replace-me.schema@v1"))]
#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-category" = "replace_me"))]
pub struct ReplaceMeState {
    #[serde(default)]
    #[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "obs.software.plugin.replace-me.status@v1"))]
    pub status: String,
}

impl Default for ReplaceMeState {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            status: "ready".to_string(),
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "obs.software.plugin.replace-me.get-status.input@v1"))]
pub struct GetStatusInput {}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "obs.software.plugin.replace-me.get-status.output@v1"))]
pub struct GetStatusOutput {
    pub status: String,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "mut.software.plugin.replace-me.set-status.input@v1"))]
pub struct SetStatusInput {
    pub status: String,
}

// =============================================================================
// PLUGIN BODY: D-Bus-backed behavior only
// =============================================================================

#[async_trait]
impl StatePlugin for ReplaceMePlugin {
    fn name(&self) -> &str {
        PLUGIN_NAME
    }

    fn version(&self) -> &str {
        PLUGIN_VERSION
    }

    fn schema(&self) -> Option<PluginSchema> {
        Some(replace_me_schema())
    }

    async fn calculate_diff(&self, _current: &Value, _desired: &Value) -> Result<StateDiff> {
        Ok(StateDiff {
            plugin: PLUGIN_NAME.to_string(),
            actions: vec![],
            metadata: DiffMetadata {
                timestamp: chrono::Utc::now().timestamp(),
                current_hash: String::new(),
                desired_hash: String::new(),
            },
        })
    }

    async fn apply_state(&self, _diff: &StateDiff) -> Result<ApplyResult> {
        Ok(ApplyResult {
            success: true,
            changes_applied: vec![],
            errors: vec![],
            checkpoint: None,
        })
    }

    async fn verify_state(&self, _desired: &Value) -> Result<bool> {
        Ok(true)
    }

    async fn create_checkpoint(&self) -> Result<Checkpoint> {
        Ok(Checkpoint {
            id: format!("{}-checkpoint", PLUGIN_NAME),
            plugin: PLUGIN_NAME.to_string(),
            timestamp: chrono::Utc::now().timestamp(),
            state_snapshot: json!({}),
            backend_checkpoint: None,
        })
    }

    async fn rollback(&self, _checkpoint: &Checkpoint) -> Result<()> {
        Ok(())
    }

    fn capabilities(&self) -> PluginCapabilities {
        PluginCapabilities {
            supports_rollback: false,
            supports_checkpoints: true,
            supports_verification: true,
            atomic_operations: true,
        }
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// PLUGIN EXIT: publish the single PluginSchema contract
// =============================================================================

pub(crate) fn replace_me_schema() -> PluginSchema {
    let state = serde_json::to_value(ReplaceMeState::default())
        .expect("plugin state serializes")
        .to_string();
    let mut state = state.into_bytes();
    let state = simd_json::to_owned_value(&mut state).expect("plugin state is valid JSON");

    let mut schema = schema_from_state(
        PLUGIN_NAME,
        PLUGIN_CATEGORY,
        PLUGIN_VERSION,
        PLUGIN_DESCRIPTION,
        &state,
    );

    schema.methods.insert(
        "get_status".to_string(),
        method_decl_from_schemars_with_output::<GetStatusInput, GetStatusOutput>(
            "get_status",
            SideEffect::Read,
            true,
            "replace_me.read",
            "obs.software.plugin.replace-me.status.get@v1",
        ),
    );

    schema.methods.insert(
        "set_status".to_string(),
        method_decl_from_schemars_with_output::<SetStatusInput, AckOutput>(
            "set_status",
            SideEffect::Mutation,
            false,
            "replace_me.invoke",
            "mut.software.plugin.replace-me.status.set@v1",
        ),
    );

    schema
}

inventory::submit! {
    crate::default_registry::PluginReg::new(PLUGIN_NAME, |_ctx| std::sync::Arc::new(ReplaceMePlugin::new()))
}
</file>

  Key consequence of code-3 being exhausted

  Embeddings are only comparable within the same model. A search query against a
  collection must be embedded with the same model that built it. So:

  - rust_lang_rust_lsp_voyage_code_3 (429k chunks) is now stranded. With code-3
  at 0, you can't embed new queries against it → that collection is effectively
  unsearchable until you either get more code-3 tokens or re-embed it under
  another model. That's the single biggest thing to flag.
  - The 6 sibling collections (go/python/java/c-cpp/ts/specs) are all
  voyage-4-lite — fine, you have 122M left there.

  On "interchangeable": true at the infra level (any voyage-4 / code-2 model is
  1024-dim and drops into Qdrant the same way), but not at the vector-space
  level — you can't cross-query between two collections built with different
  models, and you can't query a collection with a different model than built it.

● Yes — multi-collection retrieval is a first-class design feature, not a
  workaround.

  How it works

  Two ways to target multiple collections:
  1. Pass a collections: ["a","b",...] array in the tool args (the singular
  collection forces one; plural fans out).
  2. Pass nothing — and it uses per-mode defaults. For code_search/code_context
  (Search/Completion modes) the default is the whole
  DEFAULT_VOYAGE4_LITE_COLLECTIONS set — all 6 language collections fused
  automatically (rag_pipeline.rs:830). Overridable via env:
  COGNITIVE_MCP_SEARCH_COLLECTIONS, COGNITIVE_MCP_COMPLETION_COLLECTIONS,
  COGNITIVE_MCP_RAG_COLLECTIONS.

  Fusion mechanics (query_fused_collections, rag_pipeline.rs:501): embed the
  query once → search every collection with that one vector → merge → sort by
  score → dedupe by file → truncate to limit. Per-collection failures are
  non-fatal (logged and skipped), so one missing collection won't break the
  query.

  The one hard rule (and why it drives the rust-crate model choice)

  Because the query is embedded once with a single model and that vector is
  reused against every collection, fusion is only meaningful across collections 
  built with the same model. The code already enforces this by separating:
  - DEFAULT_VOYAGE4_LITE_COLLECTIONS → the fused set (6 collections, all
  voyage-4-lite)
  - DEFAULT_RUST_SOLO_COLLECTION = rust_lang_rust_lsp_voyage_code_3 →
  deliberately solo, with the source comment: "Keep voyage-code-3 Rust indexes 
  in a separate retrieval profile unless both indexing and querying use 
  voyage-code-3."

  Footgun: mixing the code-3 rust collection into the voyage-4-lite fused query
  wouldn't error (both are 1024-dim) — it'd silently return garbage scores.
  That's the whole reason it's kept solo.

  → This confirms the plan: build the 44 crates under voyage-4-lite and they
  drop straight into the fused set alongside go/python/etc. Under code-3 they'd
  be stranded solo (and code-3 is exhausted anyway).

  Two gaps I noticed in the deployed service

  1. Query model is unset → defaults to voyage-4, but your collections were
  built with voyage-4-lite. Those are different models/spaces — you should set
  COGNITIVE_MCP_VOYAGE_MODEL=voyage-4-lite in /etc/s6/sv/op-cognitive-mcp/env/
  so query embeddings match the index.
  2. The running binary looks older than the working tree — my earlier
  code_search returned the single-collection: repomix_rag shape, while current
  source emits the plural collections: [...] fused shape. So this
  multi-collection behavior is in the source but needs a rebuild/redeploy to

● Research done. Here's the conclusion.

  What codex got wrong

  1. vectorize_lsp_group.py never used LSP at all. It blind-chunks files by
  character count (chunk_text) and writes a hollow kiro_lsp payload (state_dir +
  expected_done_file strings) that nothing reads or produces. The
  go/python/java/c-cpp/ts/specs collections are naive char-chunks wearing a fake
  "LSP" label.
  2. run_kiro_lsp_groups.sh ran /code init but nothing consumed it. Only
  rust-lang/rust got real symbol-aware chunks — via export_rust_lsp_symbols.py,
  which drives rust-analyzer directly over the LSP wire (documentSymbol) and
  chunks along symbol boundaries (lsp_symbol_ranges). That's the one piece done
  right.

  Why "just use kiro" doesn't work for batch vectorization

  Kiro's code intelligence is tree-sitter-based (18 languages, no LSP install
  needed) — but it's interactive/agent-only with no JSON symbol export (docs
  (https://kiro.dev/docs/cli/code-intelligence/)). You can't script kiro-cli to
  dump symbols for a vectorizer. That's the trap: /code init builds kiro's
  internal index, but there's no export path, so codex fell back to naive
  chunking. Confirmed locally — kiro-cli only exposes chat/agent, no symbol
  subcommand.

  The key simplification

  Everything left to vectorize is 100% Rust (44 deps + the rust-lang/rust
  re-do). And rust-analyzer is installed and already proven via the symbol-aware
  path. The other LSP servers (gopls, pyright, ts-ls, jdtls) are all missing —
  but I don't need them for the rust scope.

  So the correct, low-risk fix is to generalize the working rust-analyzer LSP 
  path (currently hardcoded to rust-lang/rust) into one script that walks a repo
  list, extracts real rust-analyzer symbols per repo, chunks along symbol
  boundaries, and embeds under voyage-4-large @ 1024. No kiro, no tree-sitter,
  no missing servers.

  The genuine fork is scope:
● User answered Claude's questions:
  ⎿  · What should the unified LSP vectorization script cover? → is 
     rust-analyzer kiro?

● Good question — no, they're different things, but they're connected in a way
  that matters here.

  - rust-analyzer = the official standalone Rust LSP server (from the rust-lang
  project, /usr/bin/rust-analyzer). It speaks the Language Server Protocol. It
  is not kiro and doesn't depend on kiro.//
  - kiro = an AI coding CLI. Its "code intelligence" is two layers: a built-in
  tree-sitter engine (18 languages, no install) plus optional external LSP 
  servers you configure in .kiro/settings/lsp.json for deeper analysis.

  The link: for Rust, kiro's LSP layer is rust-analyzer. That's literally what
  the existing .kiro/settings/lsp.json does — it points kiro at rust-analyzer as
  the Rust backend. The export_rust_lsp_symbols.py script even reads that same
  kiro config (load_command()) to find the command, then talks to rust-analyzer
  directly over the LSP wire.

  So:

  ▎ Driving rust-analyzer directly produces the exact same documentSymbol data 
  ▎ kiro's LSP engine would produce for Rust — it's kiro's Rust backend, just 
  ▎ invoked directly so it's scriptable.

  That's actually more correct than trying to use kiro-cli itself, because
  kiro-cli has no way to export symbols to a file (interactive-only). codex's
  mistake wasn't "didn't use kiro" — it's that the group vectorizer skipped
  symbols entirely and faked the kiro_lsp payload, while the real symbol path
  existed only for rust-lang/rust.

  Bottom line: since everything left is Rust, using rust-analyzer is faithful to
  "use the kiro LSP engine" — same engine, same symbols, just batch-scriptable.
  The tree-sitter side only becomes relevant if/when you re-do the non-Rust
  languages (where the LSP servers are missing and kiro's tree-sitter would be
  the fallback).

  Does that resolve it? If so, I'd proceed with the recommended option — one
  rust-analyzer-driven script to finish the Rust corpus under voyage-4-large.

❯ you switch api keys auto matically/?                                          

● No — and that's worth being clear about. The current run uses a single key:
  the runner hardcodes VOYAGE_API_KEY=$VOYAGE_API_KEY_RUST (…JCUSug). It does
  not fall over to the other account's key.

  Here's exactly what happens at limits:
  - Soft stop: my --max-input-tokens 100000000 guard halts cleanly at 100M (a
  local estimate of that account's ~110M 4-large headroom) → exit 75, resumable.
  - Hard quota: if the real account balance runs dry before 100M, Voyage returns
  an error. The script retries rate-limits/429 with backoff, but a true
  quota-exhausted error isn't caught as transient — it would crash the current
  group (still resumable, but it stalls, not switches).

  So no automatic account rotation today. Given you have two accounts with
  4-large (…JCUSug ~110M + …XAT585 ~200M ≈ 310M combined), auto-failover is a
  genuinely useful addition: rotate RUST → LITE when one account hits quota, so
  the run uses the full pool and survives one account draining.

  Want me to add it? It's a contained change:
  1. Pass a comma-separated key list to the script
  (VOYAGE_API_KEY_RUST,VOYAGE_API_KEY_LITE).
  2. On a quota-exhausted error (distinct from rate-limit), re-init the Voyage
  client with the next key and continue; raise only when all keys are exhausted.

  The currently-running process won't pick up the change mid-flight (Python's
  already loaded), but since it's resumable I can either let it finish on the
  single key or restart it with failover enabled. Your call — add failover +
  restart, add it for next time only, or leave as-is?

❯ it will stop if hits budget?                                                  

● Let me verify the actual stop logic in the code rather than just assert it.

  Read 1 file (ctrl+o to expand)

● Yes — verified in the code, here's exactly how:

  Per-batch, before each embed call (_pick, line 455-464):
  1. It checks used + estimated_tokens <= budget for the current key before
  calling Voyage. So it never fires a request it can't afford on that account.
  2. If the current key would go over, it logs "budget reached -> rotating" and
  advances to the next key (RUST → LITE).
  3. When all keys are exhausted, it raise SystemExit(75).

  Propagation:
  - SystemExit is explicitly re-raised in upsert_batch (line 644-645), so it
  isn't swallowed by the rate-limit/retry handling.
  - It bubbles through main() → sys.exit(main()) → process exits with code 75.
  - The runner's run() checks if status -eq 75 → logs "token budget exhausted"
  and exit 75, stopping the whole chain (no advancing to the next group).

  Two caveats worth being precise about:
  - The pre-call gate uses the estimated token count; the budget is then debited
  by the real billed count (result.total_tokens) after the call. So the stop is
  driven by real usage, but the trigger-point is checked against the estimate —
  meaning it can overshoot a budget by at most one batch's worth of
  real-vs-estimate drift. That's why the budgets are set conservatively
  (105M/190M, under your ~110M/~200M actual balances).
  - It's resumable: budgets persist in voyage-4-large-budget.json and done-repos
  in state files, so re-running after a stop picks up where it left off without
  re-spending.

  So: it stops cleanly when the local budget is hit — which is the only reliable
  signal, since Voyage itself won't error when your free quota runs out.

  The model: containers shouldn't each get their own incus proxy device (what I
  was doing). They share one socket; zbusctl createsocket --name <x> --port 
  <ports> --path <SHARED> registers each service against that shared --path, and
  xray/OpenFlow demux by the identity wristband — not by per-service sockets.

  creates the UnixListener), and the entry lands in /dev/shm as the single
  source of truth.

  Before I build it, one design choice I don't want to guess on — how the shared

● User answered Claude's questions:
  ⎿  · No shared socket exists. How should I create the shared socket that all 
     containers' `createsocket --path` will point at? → what is your opinion on 
     the dummmy owner container?

● My honest opinion: a truly "dummy" owner container is the weakest of the 
  options — for one specific reason. An Incus proxy device is listen → connect;
  it must forward to a real target. A dummy that forwards nowhere just
  materializes an inert socket file. And a single unix socket is one endpoint —
  you can't fan it out to netmaker + qdrant + op-web through one bare socket
  unless something behind it demuxes by identity/Host/SNI. A dummy container
  can't route, so the "shared socket" would have nothing to dispatch with.

  Where the dummy idea is really pointing, though, is sound — and there are two
  clean ways to get it:

  1. The demux already exists — it's xray. The genuine "one shared door for all
  containers" is the identity-gated ingress that routes by the wristband/SNI.
  That's exactly what xray is now doing on :443/:80. So the shared socket should
  terminate at xray, not a dummy. In unix_socket terms: xray listens on the
  per-service TCP ports and proxies into sockets — xray is the shared router.
  You don't need a new container for that.
  2. If you mean a shared location (not one multiplexed socket): a shared socket
  directory (e.g. /run/op-sockets/) bind-mounted into every container, with
  per-service socket files inside it. That gives you "one shared path all
  containers see" while each service still has a real endpoint. That's the same
  pattern as the existing host-shm mount (/dev/shm → /var/lib/host-shm). A tiny
  owner container could own that dir — but a bind-mounted tmpfs is simpler.

  And note: the unix_socket plugin's ensure_bound already creates/owns the 
  socket itself (it binds the UnixListener). So you don't need a container just
  to make the socket exist — zbusctl createsocket → plugin binds it.

  My recommendation: skip the dummy container. Use a shared socket directory as
  the canonical --path root (e.g. /run/op-sockets/<name>.sock), let the
  unix_socket plugin bind the sockets, and let xray be the shared
  identity-router in front. If you specifically want a container to own the
  shared dir for lifecycle/persistence, a 5MB Alpine owner is fine — but it's
  owning a directory, not routing traffic.

  What's the shared socket actually fronting in your design — is it one 
  identity-multiplexed ingress (then it's xray), or a shared directory of 
  per-service sockets (then it's a mount)? That determines whether we provision
  an OVS ovsbr0-sock + OpenFlow, or just a tmpfs mount.

  — includes the populated openclaw.json (+ .bak / .last-good), credentials,
  agents, flows, tasks, memory, identity, workspace, cron, devices. So the

  Your schema-isolation question: yes, zeroclaw's schema is already isolated and
  plugin-owned. The zeroclaw plugin writes the canonical schema to
  /dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json and is the only writer; consumers (the
  op-grpc-bridge Axum host) read it and never write. So "point to the plugin for
  the schema zeroclaw uses" is literally how it's built.

  On the direction you flipped to — my honest take: it's not either/or. Schema 
  and config have opposite natural owners, so split them:

  - Schema (the contract: fields, models, transports, UI routes) → plugin owns 
  it, published to /dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json, mounted read-only into
  the container (the existing host-shm pattern). This is your "easier to mount
  to incus" side — and it's correct for schema, because schema is code-derived
  and should regenerate on every upgrade. You don't want stale schema surviving
  an upgrade.
  - Config/state (the populated values: credentials, agents, flows, memory) →
  persistent volume the plugin points to. This is your "survive upgrades" side —
  and it's correct for config, because that data must outlive any
  container/code rebuild. The plugin references it; it isn't baked into the
  image.

  So the tradeoff dissolves: schema flows container ← plugin (mount); config 
  flows plugin → container (reference to a persistent volume). Upgrade the code
  → schema refreshes automatically; recreate the container → config persists on
  the volume.

  That also makes your teardown plan clean: the new container is disposable —
  schema arrives via the read-only /dev/shm mount, config arrives from a
  persistent volume holding the ported openclaw→zeroclaw values. Only real work
  is mapping the captured openclaw.json into zeroclaw's config::schema::Config
  shape.

● Confirmed the key fact that decides this. There are two separable things in
  zeroclaw's schema system, and only one of them is cleanly tappable:

  1. schemars::JsonSchema — decoupled, the real reusable win. That's the
  #[cfg_attr(feature="schema-export", derive(schemars::JsonSchema))] line.
  Standard crate, zero zeroclaw coupling. You write the struct + field attrs,
  you get JSON Schema out. This is exactly what would replace op-plugins'
  hand-rolled PluginSchema/FieldSchema builders, codebase-wide.

  2. Configurable (zeroclaw-macros) — NOT cleanly tappable. The proc-macro crate
  itself is standalone (only syn/quote), but the code it generates hardwires 
  crate::config::HasPropKind, crate::config::PropKind, 
  crate::security::SecretStore — paths that only exist inside zeroclaw-config.
  So the derive assumes it's compiled within zeroclaw-config's trait/module
  ecosystem. To "tap into" it, op-dbus would have to adopt that whole ecosystem
  (the prop model, the secret store, the tabs/groups/map-key-CRUD runtime).
  That's a framework adoption, not a borrow.

  So what Configurable buys beyond schemars (and what you'd be signing up for):
  secret encrypt/decrypt/mask, snake→kebab CLI paths, dashboard tabs/groups, and
  auto-discovered map-key CRUD ("+ Add entry" with no hand-maintained dispatch
  list — which is very on-brand with your single-source-of-truth principle).
  Powerful, but it comes bundled with zeroclaw-config as a dependency.

  My recommendation — split the ambition:

  - Now, low-risk, codebase-wide: adopt schemars::JsonSchema in op-plugins.
  Define each plugin's config as an annotated struct, derive the schema, emit to
  /dev/shm (the projection already writes JSON there). Add a thin JsonSchema → 
  PluginSchema adapter so your existing schema consumers (UI/schema_renderer)
  keep working. This kills the hand-rolled builders and the drift, with no
  zeroclaw coupling.
  - Strategic, only if converging: pull in zeroclaw-config + zeroclaw-macros as
  a shared foundation to get secrets + dashboard sections + map-key CRUD for
  free. This only makes sense if op-dbus is going to converge its 
  config/secrets/UI model onto zeroclaw's — which is plausible because zeroclaw
  is becoming your assistant/gateway and its schema is already bridged into
  /dev/shm/opdbus/schemas/zeroclaw.json. But treat it as a merge project, not a
  quick win.

  The honest one-liner: the pattern is 100% worth copying; the specific 
  Configurable macro is zeroclaw-internal, so borrow schemars now and reserve 
  full zeroclaw-config adoption for a deliberate convergence.

  schedules: Value, config: Value } — but cron_schema() hand-encodes rich
  structure for jobs/schedules/config. The struct uses opaque Value blobs where 
  the schema spells out the detail. So deriving from CronState would lose the
  schema — they don't mirror.

  That changes the honest scope of "roll across plugins." It's a spectrum, not a
  mechanical sweep:

  Class: Struct already mirrors schema
  Count (approx): few
  Effort: mechanical — derive + flip
  Example: unix_socket ✓
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Class: Struct exists but opaque (Value fields)
  Count (approx): most of the 42
  Effort: must fully type the struct first (real work, touches runtime
  read/write
     code)
  Example: cron, and many others
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Class: No struct at all
  Count (approx): 5
  Effort: author a struct from the schema
  Example: oscal_subid_registry, lxc, procfs

  So a blind 42-plugin sweep isn't safe — for the opaque ones, converting means
  replacing Value fields with real nested types, which is independently valuable
  (it kills the untyped blobs and makes the struct authoritative) but is a
  deliberate per-plugin refactor with runtime implications, not a
  find-and-replace.
