use anyhow::{Context, Result};
use async_trait::async_trait;
use op_state::{ApplyResult, Checkpoint, DiffMetadata, PluginCapabilities, StateDiff, StatePlugin};
use op_state_store::{CapabilityDecl, PluginSchema};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use serde_json::Value as JsonValue;
use simd_json::prelude::*;
use simd_json::OwnedValue as Value;

use super::plugin_scaffold_helpers::method_decl_from_schemars_with_output;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, Default, schemars::JsonSchema)]
pub struct SoftwareState {
    #[serde(default)]
    pub packages: Vec<PackageInfo>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
pub struct PackageInfo {
    pub name: String,
    pub version: String,
    pub architecture: String,
    pub package_id: String,
    pub status: String,
    pub manager: String,
}

/// Input struct for Install method.
/// See: https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/org.freedesktop.systemd1.html
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
pub struct InstallInput {
    /// Package name to install
    pub name: String,
    /// Package version (optional)
    pub version: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub architecture: Option<String>,
}

/// Input struct for Uninstall method.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
pub struct UninstallInput {
    /// Package name to uninstall
    pub name: String,
    /// Force removal even if dependent
    #[serde(default)]
    pub force: bool,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub architecture: Option<String>,
}

/// Input struct for Update method.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
pub struct UpdateInput {
    /// Package name to update
    pub name: String,
    /// Target version (optional, defaults to latest)
    pub version: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub architecture: Option<String>,
}

/// Input struct for GetInfo method.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
pub struct GetInfoInput {
    /// Package name to query
    pub name: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub architecture: Option<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
pub struct PackageMutationOutput {
    pub operation: String,
    pub package_id: String,
    pub transaction: String,
    pub exit_code: u32,
    pub runtime_ms: u32,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
pub struct GetInfoOutput {
    pub packages: Vec<PackageInfo>,
    pub candidates: Vec<String>,
    pub transaction: String,
}

/// Published schema state for the `software` plugin.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "sch.software.plugin.software.schema@v1"))]
#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-category" = "software"))]
pub struct SoftwareSchemaState {
    #[schemars(
        description = "Package list",
        extend("x-oscal-subid" = "obs.software.plugin.software.packages@v1")
    )]
    pub packages: Vec<PackageInfo>,
}

pub struct SoftwarePlugin;

impl Default for SoftwarePlugin {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self
    }
}

impl SoftwarePlugin {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self
    }
}

#[async_trait]
impl StatePlugin for SoftwarePlugin {
    fn name(&self) -> &str {
        "software"
    }

    fn version(&self) -> &str {
        "2.0.0"
    }

    fn schema(&self) -> Option<op_state_store::PluginSchema> {
        Some(software_schema())
    }

    async fn calculate_diff(&self, _current: &Value, _desired: &Value) -> Result<StateDiff> {
        Ok(StateDiff {
            plugin: self.name().to_string(),
            actions: vec![],
            metadata: DiffMetadata {
                timestamp: chrono::Utc::now().timestamp(),
                current_hash: "unknown".to_string(),
                desired_hash: "unknown".to_string(),
            },
        })
    }

    async fn apply_state(&self, _diff: &StateDiff) -> Result<ApplyResult> {
        Ok(ApplyResult {
            success: true,
            changes_applied: vec![],
            errors: vec![],
            checkpoint: None,
        })
    }

    async fn verify_state(&self, _desired: &Value) -> Result<bool> {
        Ok(true)
    }

    async fn create_checkpoint(&self) -> Result<Checkpoint> {
        Ok(Checkpoint {
            id: uuid::Uuid::new_v4().to_string(),
            plugin: self.name().to_string(),
            timestamp: chrono::Utc::now().timestamp(),
            state_snapshot: Value::null(),
            backend_checkpoint: None,
        })
    }

    async fn rollback(&self, _checkpoint: &Checkpoint) -> Result<()> {
        Ok(())
    }

    fn capabilities(&self) -> PluginCapabilities {
        PluginCapabilities {
            supports_rollback: true,
            supports_checkpoints: true,
            supports_verification: true,
            atomic_operations: false,
        }
    }
}

// PackageKit filter values are bitfields: each PkFilterEnum ordinal selects a bit.
// Source: PackageKit lib/pk-enum.h and org.freedesktop.PackageKit.Transaction.xml.
const FILTER_NONE: u64 = 1 << 1;
const FILTER_INSTALLED: u64 = 1 << 2;
const FILTER_NOT_INSTALLED: u64 = 1 << 3;
const FILTER_NEWEST: u64 = 1 << 16;

const INFO_INSTALLED: u32 = 1;
const INFO_AVAILABLE: u32 = 2;
const INFO_LOW: u32 = 3;
const INFO_ENHANCEMENT: u32 = 4;
const INFO_NORMAL: u32 = 5;
const INFO_BUGFIX: u32 = 6;
const INFO_IMPORTANT: u32 = 7;
const INFO_SECURITY: u32 = 8;
const INFO_BLOCKED: u32 = 9;
const INFO_CRITICAL: u32 = 25;

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
struct PackageIdParts {
    name: String,
    version: String,
    architecture: String,
    data: String,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
enum CandidateKind {
    Installed,
    Available,
    Update,
}

fn validate_name(name: &str) -> Result<()> {
    if name.is_empty()
        || name.contains(';')
        || name.chars().any(char::is_control)
        || name.trim() != name
    {
        anyhow::bail!("invalid package name")
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn package_parts(id: &str) -> Result<PackageIdParts> {
    let fields = id.split(';').collect::<Vec<_>>();
    if fields.len() != 4
        || fields[0].is_empty()
        || fields[1].is_empty()
        || fields[2].is_empty()
        || fields[3].is_empty()
        || fields
            .iter()
            .any(|field| field.chars().any(char::is_control))
    {
        anyhow::bail!("invalid PackageKit package ID: {id:?}")
    }
    Ok(PackageIdParts {
        name: fields[0].to_string(),
        version: fields[1].to_string(),
        architecture: fields[2].to_string(),
        data: fields[3].to_string(),
    })
}

fn is_update_info(info: u32) -> bool {
    matches!(
        info,
        INFO_LOW
            | INFO_ENHANCEMENT
            | INFO_NORMAL
            | INFO_BUGFIX
            | INFO_IMPORTANT
            | INFO_SECURITY
            | INFO_CRITICAL
    )
}

fn candidate_matches(
    candidate: &super::packagekit::PackageKitPackage,
    parts: &PackageIdParts,
    kind: CandidateKind,
) -> bool {
    match kind {
        CandidateKind::Installed => {
            candidate.info == INFO_INSTALLED && parts.data.starts_with("installed")
        }
        CandidateKind::Available => {
            candidate.info == INFO_AVAILABLE && !parts.data.starts_with("installed")
        }
        CandidateKind::Update => is_update_info(candidate.info),
    }
}

async fn resolve_one(
    conn: &zbus::Connection,
    name: &str,
    version: Option<&str>,
    architecture: Option<&str>,
    filter: u64,
    kind: CandidateKind,
) -> Result<String> {
    validate_name(name)?;
    let response = super::packagekit::dispatch_packagekit_method_with_connection(
        conn,
        "resolve",
        &serde_json::json!({"filter": filter, "packages": [name]}),
    )
    .await?;
    let response: super::packagekit::PackageKitResult =
        serde_json::from_value(response).context("decode PackageKit resolve result")?;
    select_package_id(&response.package_details, name, version, architecture, kind)
}

fn select_package_id(
    candidates: &[super::packagekit::PackageKitPackage],
    name: &str,
    version: Option<&str>,
    architecture: Option<&str>,
    kind: CandidateKind,
) -> Result<String> {
    validate_name(name)?;
    let mut matches = Vec::new();
    for candidate in candidates {
        let parts = package_parts(&candidate.package_id)?;
        if parts.name == name
            && version.is_none_or(|value| value == parts.version)
            && architecture.is_none_or(|value| value == parts.architecture)
            && candidate_matches(candidate, &parts, kind)
        {
            matches.push(candidate.package_id.clone());
        }
    }
    matches.sort();
    matches.dedup();
    if matches.len() != 1 {
        anyhow::bail!("PackageKit selection for {name} is ambiguous or unavailable")
    }
    Ok(matches.remove(0))
}

fn mutation_output(operation: &str, package_id: String, response: JsonValue) -> Result<JsonValue> {
    let receipt: super::packagekit::PackageKitResult =
        serde_json::from_value(response).context("decode completed PackageKit transaction")?;
    Ok(serde_json::to_value(PackageMutationOutput {
        operation: operation.to_string(),
        package_id,
        transaction: receipt.transaction,
        exit_code: receipt.exit_code,
        runtime_ms: receipt.runtime_ms,
    })?)
}

pub async fn dispatch_software_method(method: &str, args: &JsonValue) -> Result<JsonValue> {
    let conn = zbus::Connection::system()
        .await
        .context("connect to PackageKit system bus")?;
    dispatch_software_method_with_connection(&conn, method, args).await
}

pub(crate) async fn dispatch_software_method_with_connection(
    conn: &zbus::Connection,
    method: &str,
    args: &JsonValue,
) -> Result<JsonValue> {
    match method {
        "get_info" => {
            let input: GetInfoInput = serde_json::from_value(args.clone())?;
            validate_name(&input.name)?;
            let response = super::packagekit::dispatch_packagekit_method_with_connection(
                conn,
                "resolve",
                &serde_json::json!({"filter": FILTER_NONE, "packages": [input.name]}),
            )
            .await?;
            let response: super::packagekit::PackageKitResult =
                serde_json::from_value(response).context("decode PackageKit resolve result")?;
            let mut packages = Vec::new();
            let mut candidates = Vec::new();
            for candidate in response.package_details {
                let parts = package_parts(&candidate.package_id)?;
                if parts.name == input.name
                    && input
                        .architecture
                        .as_deref()
                        .is_none_or(|value| value == parts.architecture)
                {
                    let status = if candidate.info == INFO_INSTALLED
                        && parts.data.starts_with("installed")
                    {
                        "installed"
                    } else if candidate.info == INFO_AVAILABLE
                        && !parts.data.starts_with("installed")
                    {
                        "available"
                    } else if candidate.info == INFO_BLOCKED {
                        "blocked"
                    } else if is_update_info(candidate.info) {
                        "update"
                    } else {
                        "other"
                    };
                    candidates.push(candidate.package_id.clone());
                    packages.push(PackageInfo {
                        name: parts.name,
                        version: parts.version,
                        architecture: parts.architecture,
                        package_id: candidate.package_id,
                        status: status.to_string(),
                        manager: "packagekit".into(),
                    });
                }
            }
            if packages.is_empty() {
                anyhow::bail!("PackageKit returned no matching package")
            }
            packages.sort_by(|left, right| left.package_id.cmp(&right.package_id));
            candidates.sort();
            candidates.dedup();
            Ok(serde_json::to_value(GetInfoOutput {
                packages,
                candidates,
                transaction: response.transaction,
            })?)
        }
        "install" => {
            let input: InstallInput = serde_json::from_value(args.clone())?;
            let filter = if input.version.is_some() {
                FILTER_NOT_INSTALLED
            } else {
                FILTER_NOT_INSTALLED | FILTER_NEWEST
            };
            let id = resolve_one(
                conn,
                &input.name,
                input.version.as_deref(),
                input.architecture.as_deref(),
                filter,
                CandidateKind::Available,
            )
            .await?;
            let receipt = super::packagekit::dispatch_packagekit_method_with_connection(
                conn,
                "install_packages",
                &serde_json::json!({"transaction_flags":0u64,"package_ids":[id]}),
            )
            .await?;
            mutation_output(method, id, receipt)
        }
        "uninstall" => {
            let input: UninstallInput = serde_json::from_value(args.clone())?;
            let id = resolve_one(
                conn,
                &input.name,
                None,
                input.architecture.as_deref(),
                FILTER_INSTALLED,
                CandidateKind::Installed,
            )
            .await?;
            let receipt = super::packagekit::dispatch_packagekit_method_with_connection(conn, "remove_packages", &serde_json::json!({"transaction_flags":0u64,"package_ids":[id],"allow_deps":input.force,"autoremove":false})).await?;
            mutation_output(method, id, receipt)
        }
        "update" => {
            let input: UpdateInput = serde_json::from_value(args.clone())?;
            validate_name(&input.name)?;
            let response = super::packagekit::dispatch_packagekit_method_with_connection(
                conn,
                "get_updates",
                &serde_json::json!({"filter": FILTER_NONE}),
            )
            .await?;
            let response: super::packagekit::PackageKitResult =
                serde_json::from_value(response).context("decode PackageKit update result")?;
            let id = select_package_id(
                &response.package_details,
                &input.name,
                input.version.as_deref(),
                input.architecture.as_deref(),
                CandidateKind::Update,
            )?;
            let receipt = super::packagekit::dispatch_packagekit_method_with_connection(
                conn,
                "update_packages",
                &serde_json::json!({"transaction_flags":0u64,"package_ids":[id]}),
            )
            .await?;
            mutation_output(method, id, receipt)
        }
        _ => anyhow::bail!("unknown software method: {method}"),
    }
}

pub(crate) fn software_schema() -> PluginSchema {
    let mut schema = super::schemars_adapter::plugin_schema_from_json(
        "software",
        "2.0.0",
        "Software package inventory",
        &serde_json::to_value(schemars::schema_for!(SoftwareSchemaState)).unwrap(),
    );
    schema.subids.insert(
        "__schema__".to_string(),
        "sch.software.plugin.software.schema@v1".to_string(),
    );
    super::schemars_adapter::apply_state_defaults(
        &mut schema,
        &simd_json::serde::to_owned_value(&SoftwareState::default()).unwrap(),
    );

    // Package operations are backed by org.freedesktop.PackageKit transactions.
    schema.methods.insert(
        "install".to_string(),
        method_decl_from_schemars_with_output::<InstallInput, PackageMutationOutput>(
            "Install",
            op_state_store::SideEffect::Mutation,
            false,
            "software.write",
            "mut.software.plugin.software.install@v1",
        ),
    );

    // Uninstall method
    schema.methods.insert(
        "uninstall".to_string(),
        method_decl_from_schemars_with_output::<UninstallInput, PackageMutationOutput>(
            "Uninstall",
            op_state_store::SideEffect::Mutation,
            false,
            "software.write",
            "mut.software.plugin.software.uninstall@v1",
        ),
    );

    // Update method
    schema.methods.insert(
        "update".to_string(),
        method_decl_from_schemars_with_output::<UpdateInput, PackageMutationOutput>(
            "Update",
            op_state_store::SideEffect::Mutation,
            false,
            "software.write",
            "mut.software.plugin.software.update@v1",
        ),
    );

    // GetInfo method
    schema.methods.insert(
        "get_info".to_string(),
        method_decl_from_schemars_with_output::<GetInfoInput, GetInfoOutput>(
            "GetInfo",
            op_state_store::SideEffect::Read,
            true,
            "software.read",
            "obs.software.plugin.software.get-info@v1",
        ),
    );

    schema.capabilities.insert(
        "software.write".to_string(),
        CapabilityDecl {
            id: "software.write".to_string(),
            description: "Grants: install, uninstall, update.".to_string(),
        },
    );
    schema.capabilities.insert(
        "software.read".to_string(),
        CapabilityDecl {
            id: "software.read".to_string(),
            description: "Grants: get_info.".to_string(),
        },
    );

    schema
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use serde_json::json;
    use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
    use tokio::time::{timeout, Duration};
    use zbus::{
        connection::Builder, object_server::SignalContext, zvariant::OwnedObjectPath, Guid,
    };

    const TX_PATH: &str = "/org/freedesktop/PackageKit/transactions/software_test";
    type Calls = Arc<Mutex<Vec<RecordedCall>>>;

    #[derive(Clone, Copy)]
    enum FixtureMode {
        Normal,
        Ambiguous,
        Malformed,
        BackendError,
    }

    #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
    struct RecordedCall {
        method: String,
        flags: u64,
        package_ids: Vec<String>,
        allow_deps: bool,
        autoremove: bool,
    }

    #[derive(Clone)]
    struct FixtureState {
        mode: FixtureMode,
        calls: Calls,
    }

    #[derive(Clone)]
    struct RootFixture {
        _state: FixtureState,
    }

    #[derive(Clone)]
    struct TransactionFixture {
        state: FixtureState,
    }

    impl TransactionFixture {
        fn record(
            &self,
            method: &str,
            flags: u64,
            package_ids: Vec<String>,
            allow_deps: bool,
            autoremove: bool,
        ) {
            self.state.calls.lock().unwrap().push(RecordedCall {
                method: method.to_string(),
                flags,
                package_ids,
                allow_deps,
                autoremove,
            });
        }

        async fn finish(ctxt: &SignalContext<'_>) -> zbus::fdo::Result<()> {
            Self::finished(ctxt, 1, 17).await?;
            Ok(())
        }

        async fn emit_package(
            ctxt: &SignalContext<'_>,
            info: u32,
            package_id: &str,
        ) -> zbus::fdo::Result<()> {
            Self::package(ctxt, info, package_id, "fixture package").await?;
            Ok(())
        }
    }

    #[zbus::interface(name = "org.freedesktop.PackageKit")]
    impl RootFixture {
        async fn create_transaction(&self) -> OwnedObjectPath {
            OwnedObjectPath::try_from(TX_PATH).unwrap()
        }
    }

    #[zbus::interface(name = "org.freedesktop.PackageKit.Transaction")]
    impl TransactionFixture {
        async fn resolve(
            &self,
            #[zbus(signal_context)] ctxt: SignalContext<'_>,
            filter: u64,
            packages: Vec<String>,
        ) -> zbus::fdo::Result<()> {
            self.record("Resolve", filter, packages, false, false);
            match self.state.mode {
                FixtureMode::Malformed => {
                    Self::emit_package(&ctxt, INFO_AVAILABLE, "malformed").await?;
                }
                FixtureMode::Ambiguous => {
                    Self::emit_package(&ctxt, INFO_AVAILABLE, "demo;2.0;x86_64;repo-a").await?;
                    Self::emit_package(&ctxt, INFO_AVAILABLE, "demo;2.0;x86_64;repo-b").await?;
                }
                FixtureMode::Normal | FixtureMode::BackendError => {
                    if filter == FILTER_INSTALLED {
                        Self::emit_package(
                            &ctxt,
                            INFO_INSTALLED,
                            "demo;1.0;x86_64;installed:fixture",
                        )
                        .await?;
                    } else if filter & FILTER_NOT_INSTALLED != 0 {
                        if filter & FILTER_NEWEST == 0 {
                            Self::emit_package(&ctxt, INFO_AVAILABLE, "demo;1.0;x86_64;fixture")
                                .await?;
                        }
                        Self::emit_package(&ctxt, INFO_AVAILABLE, "demo;2.0;x86_64;fixture")
                            .await?;
                        Self::emit_package(&ctxt, INFO_AVAILABLE, "demo;2.0;aarch64;fixture")
                            .await?;
                    } else {
                        Self::emit_package(
                            &ctxt,
                            INFO_INSTALLED,
                            "demo;1.0;x86_64;installed:fixture",
                        )
                        .await?;
                        Self::emit_package(&ctxt, INFO_AVAILABLE, "demo;2.0;x86_64;fixture")
                            .await?;
                    }
                }
            }
            Self::finish(&ctxt).await
        }

        async fn get_updates(
            &self,
            #[zbus(signal_context)] ctxt: SignalContext<'_>,
            filter: u64,
        ) -> zbus::fdo::Result<()> {
            self.record("GetUpdates", filter, Vec::new(), false, false);
            Self::emit_package(&ctxt, INFO_SECURITY, "demo;2.0;x86_64;updates").await?;
            Self::emit_package(&ctxt, INFO_BLOCKED, "demo;3.0;x86_64;updates").await?;
            Self::finish(&ctxt).await
        }

        async fn install_packages(
            &self,
            #[zbus(signal_context)] ctxt: SignalContext<'_>,
            flags: u64,
            package_ids: Vec<String>,
        ) -> zbus::fdo::Result<()> {
            self.record("InstallPackages", flags, package_ids, false, false);
            if matches!(self.state.mode, FixtureMode::BackendError) {
                Self::error_code(&ctxt, 42, "installation failed").await?;
            } else {
                Self::finish(&ctxt).await?;
            }
            Ok(())
        }

        async fn remove_packages(
            &self,
            #[zbus(signal_context)] ctxt: SignalContext<'_>,
            flags: u64,
            package_ids: Vec<String>,
            allow_deps: bool,
            autoremove: bool,
        ) -> zbus::fdo::Result<()> {
            self.record("RemovePackages", flags, package_ids, allow_deps, autoremove);
            Self::finish(&ctxt).await
        }

        async fn update_packages(
            &self,
            #[zbus(signal_context)] ctxt: SignalContext<'_>,
            flags: u64,
            package_ids: Vec<String>,
        ) -> zbus::fdo::Result<()> {
            self.record("UpdatePackages", flags, package_ids, false, false);
            Self::finish(&ctxt).await
        }

        #[zbus(signal)]
        async fn package(
            ctxt: &SignalContext<'_>,
            info: u32,
            package_id: &str,
            summary: &str,
        ) -> zbus::Result<()>;

        #[zbus(signal)]
        async fn error_code(ctxt: &SignalContext<'_>, code: u32, details: &str)
            -> zbus::Result<()>;

        #[zbus(signal)]
        async fn finished(ctxt: &SignalContext<'_>, exit: u32, runtime: u32) -> zbus::Result<()>;
    }

    async fn fixture(mode: FixtureMode) -> (zbus::Connection, zbus::Connection, Calls) {
        let (server_stream, client_stream) = tokio::net::UnixStream::pair().unwrap();
        let calls = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::new()));
        let state = FixtureState {
            mode,
            calls: calls.clone(),
        };
        let server = Builder::unix_stream(server_stream)
            .server(Guid::generate())
            .unwrap()
            .p2p()
            .serve_at(
                "/org/freedesktop/PackageKit",
                RootFixture {
                    _state: state.clone(),
                },
            )
            .unwrap()
            .serve_at(TX_PATH, TransactionFixture { state })
            .unwrap()
            .build();
        let client = Builder::unix_stream(client_stream).p2p().build();
        let (_server, client) = timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), async {
            tokio::try_join!(server, client)
        })
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .unwrap();
        (_server, client, calls)
    }

    #[test]
    fn package_selection_requires_one_valid_exact_candidate() {
        let candidates = vec![
            super::super::packagekit::PackageKitPackage {
                info: INFO_AVAILABLE,
                package_id: "demo;1.0;x86_64;repo".to_string(),
                summary: String::new(),
            },
            super::super::packagekit::PackageKitPackage {
                info: INFO_AVAILABLE,
                package_id: "demo;2.0;x86_64;repo".to_string(),
                summary: String::new(),
            },
        ];
        assert!(
            select_package_id(&candidates, "demo", None, None, CandidateKind::Available).is_err()
        );
        assert_eq!(
            select_package_id(
                &candidates,
                "demo",
                Some("2.0"),
                Some("x86_64"),
                CandidateKind::Available
            )
            .unwrap(),
            "demo;2.0;x86_64;repo"
        );
        let malformed = [super::super::packagekit::PackageKitPackage {
            info: INFO_AVAILABLE,
            package_id: "corrupt".to_string(),
            summary: String::new(),
        }];
        assert!(
            select_package_id(&malformed, "demo", None, None, CandidateKind::Available).is_err()
        );
        assert!(select_package_id(&[], "demo", None, None, CandidateKind::Available).is_err());
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn all_four_methods_use_exact_packagekit_transactions() {
        let (_server, conn, calls) = fixture(FixtureMode::Normal).await;
        let info: GetInfoOutput = serde_json::from_value(
            dispatch_software_method_with_connection(
                &conn,
                "get_info",
                &json!({"name":"demo", "architecture":"x86_64"}),
            )
            .await
            .unwrap(),
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(info.packages.len(), 2);
        assert_eq!(info.packages[0].status, "installed");
        assert_eq!(info.packages[0].architecture, "x86_64");
        assert_eq!(info.packages[1].status, "available");

        let install: PackageMutationOutput = serde_json::from_value(
            dispatch_software_method_with_connection(
                &conn,
                "install",
                &json!({"name":"demo", "version":null, "architecture":"x86_64"}),
            )
            .await
            .unwrap(),
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(install.package_id, "demo;2.0;x86_64;fixture");
        assert_eq!(install.exit_code, 1);

        let uninstall: PackageMutationOutput = serde_json::from_value(
            dispatch_software_method_with_connection(
                &conn,
                "uninstall",
                &json!({"name":"demo", "force":true, "architecture":"x86_64"}),
            )
            .await
            .unwrap(),
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(uninstall.package_id, "demo;1.0;x86_64;installed:fixture");

        let update: PackageMutationOutput = serde_json::from_value(
            dispatch_software_method_with_connection(
                &conn,
                "update",
                &json!({"name":"demo", "version":null, "architecture":"x86_64"}),
            )
            .await
            .unwrap(),
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(update.package_id, "demo;2.0;x86_64;updates");

        let calls = calls.lock().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(calls[0].method, "Resolve");
        assert_eq!(calls[0].flags, FILTER_NONE);
        assert_eq!(calls[1].flags, FILTER_NOT_INSTALLED | FILTER_NEWEST);
        assert_eq!(calls[2].method, "InstallPackages");
        assert_eq!(calls[3].flags, FILTER_INSTALLED);
        assert_eq!(calls[4].method, "RemovePackages");
        assert!(calls[4].allow_deps);
        assert!(!calls[4].autoremove);
        assert_eq!(calls[5].method, "GetUpdates");
        assert_eq!(calls[5].flags, FILTER_NONE);
        assert_eq!(calls[6].method, "UpdatePackages");
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn exact_version_and_architecture_select_before_install() {
        let (_server, conn, calls) = fixture(FixtureMode::Normal).await;
        let result: PackageMutationOutput = serde_json::from_value(
            dispatch_software_method_with_connection(
                &conn,
                "install",
                &json!({"name":"demo", "version":"1.0", "architecture":"x86_64"}),
            )
            .await
            .unwrap(),
        )
        .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(result.package_id, "demo;1.0;x86_64;fixture");
        let calls = calls.lock().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(calls[0].flags, FILTER_NOT_INSTALLED);
        assert_eq!(calls[1].package_ids, ["demo;1.0;x86_64;fixture"]);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn ambiguous_and_malformed_candidates_never_reach_mutation() {
        for mode in [FixtureMode::Ambiguous, FixtureMode::Malformed] {
            let (_server, conn, calls) = fixture(mode).await;
            let result = dispatch_software_method_with_connection(
                &conn,
                "install",
                &json!({"name":"demo", "version":null, "architecture":"x86_64"}),
            )
            .await;
            assert!(result.is_err());
            let calls = calls.lock().unwrap();
            assert_eq!(calls.len(), 1);
            assert_eq!(calls[0].method, "Resolve");
        }
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn backend_error_is_not_reported_as_completed_install() {
        let (_server, conn, calls) = fixture(FixtureMode::BackendError).await;
        let error = dispatch_software_method_with_connection(
            &conn,
            "install",
            &json!({"name":"demo", "version":null, "architecture":"x86_64"}),
        )
        .await
        .unwrap_err();
        assert!(error.to_string().contains("PackageKit error 42"));
        assert_eq!(calls.lock().unwrap().len(), 2);
    }

    #[test]
    fn all_subids_are_valid() {
        let raw = serde_json::to_value(schemars::schema_for!(SoftwareSchemaState)).unwrap();
        let mut subids = Vec::new();
        collect_subids(&raw, &mut subids);
        for subid in subids {
            assert!(
                crate::state_plugins::common::oscal::validate_subid(&subid).is_ok(),
                "invalid subid: {subid}"
            );
        }
    }

    fn collect_subids(value: &serde_json::Value, out: &mut Vec<String>) {
        if let Some(obj) = value.as_object() {
            if let Some(subid) = obj.get("x-oscal-subid").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) {
                out.push(subid.to_string());
            }
            for v in obj.values() {
                collect_subids(v, out);
            }
        }
        if let Some(arr) = value.as_array() {
            for v in arr {
                collect_subids(v, out);
            }
        }
    }
}

// Self-registration: the plugin registry discovers this via inventory
// (single source of the catalog; no central dispatch list).
inventory::submit! {
    crate::default_registry::PluginReg::new("software", |_ctx| std::sync::Arc::new(SoftwarePlugin::new()))
}

/// Where a config section is read from.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum SectionSource {
    /// The native tched_router configuration, described by the imported plugin-owned contract.
    Upstream,
    /// Local 3tched Router state (a plain configuration).
    Local,
}

/// Register every config method and its declared capability on the schema.
///
/// The plugin is the single declaration point: each method's
/// `required_capability` has a matching `schema.capabilities` entry
/// (closure-clean under `validate_capability_closure`).
pub fn register_config_methods(schema: &mut PluginSchema) {
    schema.methods.insert(
        "GetConfig".to_string(),
        method_decl_from_schemars_with_output::<ConfigMethodInput, GetConfigOutput>(
            "GetConfig",
            SideEffect::Read,
            true,
            "cap.software.3tched-router.config.read@v1",
            "obs.service.3tched-router.config.get@v1",
        ),
    );
    schema.capabilities.insert(
        "cap.software.3tched-router.config.read@v1".to_string(),
        CapabilityDecl {
            id: "cap.software.3tched-router.config.read@v1".to_string(),
            description: "Read the full 3tched Router configuration (secrets masked).".to_string(),
        },
    );
    schema.methods.insert(
        "PatchConfig".to_string(),
        method_decl_from_schemars_with_output::<PatchConfigInput, PatchConfigOutput>(
            "PatchConfig",
            SideEffect::Mutation,
            false,
            "cap.software.3tched-router.config.write@v1",
            "mut.service.3tched-router.config.patch@v2",
        ),
    );
    schema.capabilities.insert(
        "cap.software.3tched-router.config.write@v1".to_string(),
        CapabilityDecl {
            id: "cap.software.3tched-router.config.write@v1".to_string(),
            description: "Apply bounded typed 3tched Router configuration property operations."
                .to_string(),
        },
    );
    schema.methods.insert(
        "GetA2aConfig".to_string(),
        method_decl_from_schemars_with_output::<ConfigMethodInput, GetA2aConfigOutput>(
            "GetA2aConfig",
            SideEffect::Read,
            true,
            "cap.software.3tched-router.a2a-config.read@v1",
            "obs.service.3tched-router.a2a-config.get@v1",
        ),
    );
    schema.capabilities.insert(
        "cap.software.3tched-router.a2a-config.read@v1".to_string(),

// ── Native dispatch metadata ───────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// This generated module owns schemas and routing metadata only. Async provider
// I/O and committed-state reads belong to the bridge after canonical admission.

/// The authoritative backing required by one retained config-surface method.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ConfigMethodBacking {
    /// Masked `GET /api/config` from the pinned v0.8.4 loopback gateway.
    WholeNativeConfig,
    /// One top-level value selected from the masked native config response.
    NativeSection(&'static str),
    /// A field in the committed protected tched_router state. The native
    /// v0.8.4 config document does not contain these plugin-owned fields.
    CommittedPluginStateSection(&'static str),
    /// Bounded typed property operations sent to native `PATCH /api/config`.
    NativePropertyPatch,
}

/// Resolve a canonical method name to its backing without reading state or
/// consulting the Rust registry for plugin existence.
pub fn config_method_backing(method: &str) -> Option<ConfigMethodBacking> {
    match method {
        "GetConfig" => Some(ConfigMethodBacking::WholeNativeConfig),
        "PatchConfig" => Some(ConfigMethodBacking::NativePropertyPatch),
        other => SECTIONS
            .iter()
            .find(|(name, _, _)| *name == other)
            .map(|(_, key, source)| match source {
                SectionSource::Upstream => ConfigMethodBacking::NativeSection(key),
                SectionSource::Local => ConfigMethodBacking::CommittedPluginStateSection(key),
            }),
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod backing_tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn all_declared_config_methods_have_one_explicit_backing() {
        for method in CONFIG_METHODS {
            assert!(
                config_method_backing(method).is_some(),
                "missing backing metadata for {method}"
            );
        }
        assert_eq!(config_method_backing("unknown"), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn native_and_plugin_owned_sections_are_not_conflated() {
        assert_eq!(
            config_method_backing("GetGatewayConfig"),
            Some(ConfigMethodBacking::NativeSection("gateway"))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            config_method_backing("GetIdentityChainConfig"),
            Some(ConfigMethodBacking::CommittedPluginStateSection(
                "identity_chain"
            ))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            config_method_backing("PatchConfig"),
            Some(ConfigMethodBacking::NativePropertyPatch)
        );
    }
}

//! The plugin-owned upstream configuration contract for tched_router.
//! Imported from `zeroclaw config schema`; all section/method schemas derive here.
//! Upgrade explicitly with gen_tched_router_config_surface --import-json PATH --version VERSION.

// BEGIN UPSTREAM IMPORT
pub const BINARY_SCHEMA_VERSION: &str = "0.8.4";
const CONFIG_SCHEMA: &str = r####"{
  "$defs": {
    "A2aServerConfig": {
      "description": "Inbound A2A discovery server configuration.",
      "properties": {
        "bind": {
          "description": "Optional advertise-only host override for card endpoint URLs. The\nroutes always serve on the gateway's own listener; this only changes\nthe host printed in advertised endpoints when A2A is fronted at a\ndifferent address. `None` derives from the gateway host.",
          "type": [

          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"

        "public_base_url": {

    "A2aServerSection": {

          "$ref": "#/$defs/A2aServerConfig",
          "default": {
            "enabled": false,

          "description": "Inbound A2A discovery server (`[a2a.server]`)."
        }

      "type": "object"

    "AccessMode": {

      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "read",
          "description": "Read access only. Cross-agent `file_read` is permitted; writes are not.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "write",
          "description": "Write access only. Cross-agent `file_write` is permitted; reads are not.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "read_write",
          "description": "Both read and write. The agent can `file_read` and `file_write` against\nthe target's workspace.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    },
    "AcpConfig": {
      "description": "ACP (Agent Client Protocol) server configuration (`[acp]` section).",
      "properties": {
        "default_agent": {
          "description": "Agent alias to use when `session/new` omits `agentAlias` and more than\none agent is configured. When exactly one agent exists it is\nauto-selected regardless of this field.",
          "type": [

            "null"

        },
        "max_sessions": {

          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "session_timeout_secs": {
          "default": 3600,
          "description": "Idle session timeout in seconds. Sessions with no activity for this\nduration are eligible for eviction. Default: `3600` (1 hour).",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"

      "type": "string"
    },
    "AgentMemoryConfig": {
      "description": "Per-agent memory backend selection and its persistence contract.",
      "properties": {
        "backend": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/MemoryBackendKind",
          "default": "sqlite",
          "description": "The backend kind this agent uses. Defaults to `Sqlite` for new\nagents; once an agent has on-disk data the value is locked."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "AgentWorkspaceConfig": {

          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "chat_template_kwargs": {
          "description": "Arbitrary key/value pairs forwarded verbatim as `chat_template_kwargs`\nin the request body (llama.cpp-specific).         },
        "context_window": {
          "description": "Context window size (max input tokens) for this model.\nAuto-populated on setup from provider's /models endpoint if available.\nOverride manually for custom endpoints or when auto-detection fails.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "extra_headers": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "description": "Extra HTTP headers sent with every request. Niche: used for auth bridges, corporate proxies, or custom gateways that demand a tracing header. Most users never touch this; edit `config.toml` directly if you need it.",
          "type": "object",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "fallback": {
          "description": "Ordered list of other provider aliases to try when every model on this\nalias has failed. Each entry is a dotted `<type>.<alias>` reference into\n`providers.models` and resolves with its own credentials, endpoint, and\nmodel. A fallback never inherits this alias's key. The walk is\ndepth-first: this alias's models are exhausted first, then each fallback\nalias is descended in turn (applying its own `fallback_models` and\n`fallback`). Empty means no provider-level fallback.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/ModelProviderRef"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "fallback_models": {
          "description": "Ordered alternate models to try on THIS provider before falling over to\nthe `fallback` aliases. Same endpoint, key, and headers as the primary\n`model`. Only the model identifier changes. Use this when a provider\nserves a backup model (e.g. a smaller or older variant) that should be\ntried before leaving the provider entirely. Empty means only `model` is\ntried.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "kind": {
          "description": "Provider implementation to instantiate for this profile. Use this\nwhen a canonical typed slot should run through a compatible\nimplementation, e.g. `[providers.models.openai.proxy] kind =\n\"openai-compatible\"`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "live_pricing": {
          "description": "Pull live token prices for this provider's models from its own\nOpenAI-compatible `/models` listing (the gateway is the source of truth\nfor its prices), filling cost-tracking rates for models the operator\nhas NOT priced under `[cost.rates]` / `pricing`. Models the gateway does\nnot price (or providers with no HTTP `/models` listing at all, such as\na subprocess gateway like `kilocli`) fall back to the public models.dev\ncatalog. Configured rates always win; live prices only fill gaps. A\nbackground task refreshes the price snapshot hourly; the cost-recording\npath reads the cached snapshot and never blocks on the network. Default\n`false`: off means no fetching and behavior identical to a build\nwithout the feature.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "max_tokens": {
          "description": "Hard cap on response length in tokens. Most models enforce sensible built-in limits already; leave unset unless you specifically need to clip long outputs for cost or latency reasons.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "merge_system_into_user": {
          "description": "ModelProvider-specific quirk: fold the system prompt into the first user message instead of sending a separate system role. Only needed for models that reject (or mishandle) a standalone system role, e.g. certain older Mistral variants.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "model": {
          "description": "Model identifier to send with each request: the ID string from the model_provider's catalog (e.g. `gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `llama-3.3-70b`). Must match a model the model_provider actually serves on this account.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "native_tools": {
          "description": "Override the provider's default for native tool calling.\n`None` (default) honors the provider's built-in choice. `Some(true)`\nforces native tool calls on, `Some(false)` forces text-fallback.\nCurrently consulted only by the Groq factory, which defaults to\ntext-fallback because llama-family Groq models reject native tool\ncalls with HTTP 400. Setting `native_tools = true` re-enables native\ntool calling for Groq models that support it.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "pricing": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "format": "double",
            "type": "number"
          },
          "description": "Per-model pricing for cost tracking, USD per 1M tokens.\n\nFree-form key/value map. Keys are user-defined model identifiers; an\noptional `.input` / `.output` suffix encodes pricing dimension when\nthe operator wants to split rates. A bare key without a suffix is\nused as a flat per-token rate when neither dimension is specified.\nDefault is empty: cost tracking falls back to \"unknown\" rates and\nonly token usage is recorded.\n\nExample: `pricing = { opus = 15.0, sonnet = 3.0 }`\nOr split: `pricing = { \"opus.input\" = 15.0, \"opus.output\" = 75.0 }`",
          "type": "object"
        },
        "provider_extra": {
          "description": "Extra JSON parameters to include in API requests.\nMerged at the top level of the request body, allowing provider-specific\nfeatures (routing, transforms, etc.) without code changes.\nExample: `provider_extra = { model_provider = { only = [\"Anthropic\"] } }`"
        },
        "replay_assistant_reasoning": {
          "description": "Whether stored assistant reasoning should be replayed on outbound\nassistant history messages. `Some(false)` strips `reasoning_content`\nand `reasoning` before sending. `None` (default) honours the provider's\nbuilt-in default (true for most compat providers, false for Groq).",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "requires_openai_auth": {
          "description": "When true, the client pulls credentials from ZeroClaw's stored `openai-codex` auth profile instead of the `api_key` field above. Import an existing Codex CLI login with `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json`, or run `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex`. Turn on only for the OpenAI Codex model_provider; leave off for standard API-key model_providers.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "temperature": {
          "description": "Sampling temperature passed to the model. Lower values (0.0–0.3) give\ndeterministic, near-verbatim output, which fits code, routing, summarization.\nHigher values (0.7–1.2) give more varied output, which fits open-ended chat.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "think": {
          "description": "Enable or disable chain-of-thought thinking for models that support it\n(e.g. Qwen3, GLM-4). `true` turns thinking on, `false` turns it off.\n`None` (default) lets the model decide. Forwarded as `enable_thinking`\nin the request body; mirrors the Ollama provider's `think` field.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "description": "HTTP request timeout in seconds. Bump this for slow local model_providers (Ollama on CPU, big local models) or high-latency networks; leave unset otherwise.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "tls_ca_cert_path": {
          "description": "Path to a PEM-encoded CA certificate for TLS connections to this provider.\nMust be an absolute path; shell expansion (e.g. `~`) is not performed.\nLeave unset to use the system's default trust store.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "uri": {
          "description": "Endpoint URI the client hits. Override the family's default endpoint when pointing at a self-hosted gateway (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama), a custom proxy, or any non-standard URL. Leave unset to use the family's default URI from its `ModelEndpoint` impl. Set this to the FULL endpoint URL; there is no separate path-suffix field.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "vision": {
          "description": "Override the provider's vision (image input) capability.\n`None` (default) uses the provider family's built-in default. Several\nfamilies (llama.cpp, the generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint, etc.)\nassume vision-capable because they can serve multimodal models. Set\n`vision = false` for a text-only model served by such a family (e.g. a\ntext LLM behind llama.cpp) so image messages are routed to a configured\n`[multimodal] vision_model_provider` instead of being sent to a model\nthat rejects them. `Some(true)` forces vision on.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "wire_api": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/WireApi"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Wire protocol flavor: `responses` for OpenAI's Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`), `chat_completions` for the legacy chat wire and most OpenAI-compatible gateways. New OpenAI provider slots default to `responses`; other families default to chat-completions (or ignore the field). Only override if you're forcing an unusual combination."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },

        "api_key": {

    "AliasedAgentConfig": {
      "description": "Configuration for an aliased agent. Each `[agents.<alias>]` TOML\nblock deserializes into one of these. The `DelegateTool` looks up\nentries here to dispatch a subtask to a named sibling agent.",
      "properties": {
        "a2a": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/AgentA2aConfig",
          "default": {
            "exposed_skills": [],
            "published": false
          },
          "description": "Per-agent A2A publication block (`[agents.<alias>.a2a]`). Gates\nwhether this alias is discoverable as a spec-conforming A2A agent\nand which resolved skills appear on its card. Default-closed\n(`published = false`, no exposed skills). See\n`crate::multi_agent::AgentA2aConfig`."
        },
        "acp_enable_mcp": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Initialize this agent's `mcp_bundles` tools when it serves an ACP\n(`session/new`) session.\n\nOff by default: MCP servers are external processes/services that can\nblock startup while they connect, and ACP `session/new` is expected to\nreturn promptly. Enable it when this agent must call its `mcp_bundles`\ntools over ACP; `session/new` then pays the one-time MCP connection cost\n(bounded and non-fatal per server). Set per agent so each ACP profile\nopts in independently; when this agent is the ACP default\n(`acp.default_agent`, or the sole configured agent), the flag is picked\nup automatically for sessions that omit `agentAlias`.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "channels": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Channel aliases this agent handles (e.g. `[\"telegram.<alias>\", \"discord.<alias>\"]`).\nEach entry is a `ChannelRef` resolving through `[channels.<type>.<alias>]`;\n`Config::validate()` fails loud on dangling references.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/ChannelRef"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "classifier_provider": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/ModelProviderRef",
          "default": "",
          "description": "Optional override for the per-message LLM reply-intent classifier\n(`classify_channel_reply_intent` in zeroclaw-channels). When non-empty,\nthe channel orchestrator routes the \"should this message be replied to?\"\nclassification call to `[providers.models.<type>.<alias>]` referenced\nhere, instead of reusing the main agent's `model_provider`.\n\nSource of truth for api_key / uri / model / temperature etc. is the\nreferenced `[providers.models.<type>.<alias>]` entry. This field is\na reference only (NEVER a copy), per AGENTS.md SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH.\n\nEmpty (`Default`) = inherit the main agent's resolved provider+model\n(preserves pre-PR behavior; backward compatible).\n\nUse case: classification is a cheap REPLY/NO_REPLY decision, doesn't\nneed a high-end model. Point this at a fast/free small model\n(e.g. `kimi-k2.5`, `qwen-turbo`) while `model_provider` stays on the\nexpensive answering model (e.g. `qwen3.6-plus`).\n\nNote: TOML table names cannot contain `.`, so alias `kimi-k2.5`\nmust be written as `[providers.models.custom.kimi-k2-5]`. The\nunderlying `model = \"kimi-k2.5\"` string can still contain dots.\n\nACP channels (IDE-direct) always reply and skip the classifier\nentirely, so this field has no effect on ACP traffic."
        },
        "cron_jobs": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Cron job aliases. Each entry references `cron[key]`, a declarative\nscheduled job invoked by the scheduler on its configured trigger.\nWhen the cron fires, this agent is the actor that executes the job.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "delegate_same_risk_profile": {
          "default": true,
          "description": "Auto-allow delegation to every agent sharing this agent's risk\nprofile. Default `true` preserves the historical reach where any\nsame-profile peer is a delegation target. Set `false` to opt this\nagent out so only the explicit `delegates` list is reachable.\nGating (whether delegation is permitted at all) still lives on the\nrisk profile's `delegation_policy.mode`; this only narrows reach.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "delegates": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Explicit delegate roster: additional agent aliases this agent may\ndelegate to, beyond same-profile peers. Possibly empty. String\nentries are accepted for concise manual editing and load as bounded\ndelegates; saved config emits object entries with explicit modes.\nEntries may name agents on a different risk profile. `Config::validate()`\nfails loud on a dangling alias, duplicate alias, or self-reference.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/DelegateTargetConfig"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": true,
          "description": "Whether this agent is active. Set false to disable without removing the definition.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "identity": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/IdentityConfig",
          "default": {
            "aieos_inline": null,
            "aieos_path": null,
            "format": "openclaw"
          },
          "description": "Per-agent identity format (`[agents.<alias>.identity]`). Each\nagent renders its own IDENTITY.md / SOUL.md inside its\nper-agent workspace; this block selects the format (OpenClaw or\nAIEOS) and optional inline/file source for the agent's identity\ndocument."
        },
        "knowledge_bundles": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Knowledge bundle aliases. Additive: the agent loads every listed\nbundle.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "mcp_bundles": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "MCP bundle aliases. Each entry references `mcp_bundles[key]`, a named\ngroup of MCP servers. Secure by default: an agent is granted only the\nservers named by its bundles. An agent with no `mcp_bundles` receives\nno MCP servers (omission is not a grant). See\n`Config::mcp_servers_for_agent`.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "memory": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/AgentMemoryConfig",
          "default": {
            "backend": "sqlite"
          },
          "description": "Per-agent memory backend selection (`[agents.<alias>.memory]`).\nThe `backend` field is locked at agent creation and immutable on\nsubsequent loads. Defaults to `Sqlite`. See\n`crate::multi_agent::AgentMemoryConfig`."
        },
        "model_provider": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/ModelProviderRef",
          "default": "",
          "description": "Dotted model-provider alias (e.g. `\"anthropic.<alias>\"`).\nResolves through `model_providers.<type>.<alias>` at runtime;\n`Config::validate()` fails loud on dangling references."
        },
        "precheck": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/ChannelPrecheckConfig",
          "default": {
            "enabled": true,
            "timeout_secs": 5
          },
          "description": "Per-agent reply-intent precheck controls. The classifier call reads\nthis block at message time; model/provider selection stays on\n`classifier_provider` so there is only one routing source of truth."
        },
        "risk_profile": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/RiskProfileRef",
          "default": "",
          "description": "Risk profile alias (e.g. `\"default\"`). Resolves delegation guardrails at runtime."
        },
        "runtime_profile": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/RuntimeProfileRef",
          "default": "",
          "description": "Runtime profile alias (e.g. `\"default\"`). Resolves agentic/iteration settings."
        },
        "skill_bundles": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Skill bundle aliases. Each entry resolves to\n`skill_bundles[key].directory` at runtime; the agent loads every\nlisted bundle.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "summary_provider": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/ModelProviderRef",
          "default": "",
          "description": "Per-agent override for the context-compression summarizer provider, as\na `providers.models.<type>.<alias>` reference. Empty (Default) = inherit\nthe runtime profile's `context_compression.summary_provider`, else the\nagent's own resolved provider+model. Reference only, never a copy;\nresolved by [`Config::effective_summary_provider`]. Validated in\n`Config::validate()`."
        },
        "transcription_provider": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/TranscriptionProviderRef",
          "default": "",
          "description": "Transcription / STT provider as a dotted alias reference\n(`<type>.<alias>`, e.g. `\"groq.<alias>\"`). Resolves through\n`transcription_providers.<type>.<alias>`. Empty = agent has no\ntranscription preference; channels that ingest voice still need a\nresolved provider (there is no global default), so an inbound voice\nflow into an agent with empty `transcription_provider` errors loudly\nat the channel boundary."
        },
        "tts_provider": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/TtsProviderRef",
          "default": "",
          "description": "TTS provider as a dotted alias reference (`<type>.<alias>`,\ne.g. `\"openai.<alias>\"`). Resolves through `tts_providers.<type>.<alias>`.\nEmpty = no TTS for this agent (there is no global default-provider concept;\nevery agent that wants TTS sets its own `tts_provider`)."
        },
        "workspace": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/AgentWorkspaceConfig",
          "default": {
            "access": {},
            "read_memory_from": [],
            "unrestricted_filesystem": false
          },
          "description": "Per-agent workspace block (`[agents.<alias>.workspace]`).\nHolds the agent's filesystem path, cross-agent access allowlist,\nfilesystem-escape boolean, and cross-agent memory allowlist.\nDefault is fully jailed (no cross-agent access). See\n`crate::multi_agent::AgentWorkspaceConfig`."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "AmqpConfig": {
      "properties": {
        "amqp_url": {
          "description": "AMQP broker URL. Use `amqp://` for plain or `amqps://` for TLS\n(e.g. `amqps://fedora:@rabbitmq.fedoraproject.org/%2Fpublic_pubsub`).",
          "type": "string",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "ca_cert": {
          "description": "Path to the CA certificate bundle for `amqps://` connections.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "client_cert": {
          "description": "Path to the client certificate for broker mutual-TLS auth\n(Fedora Messaging requires a client cert).",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "client_key": {
          "description": "Path to the client private key matching `client_cert`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "content_template": {
          "default": "",
          "description": "Template for the inbound message content. `{field}` placeholders are\ninterpolated from the JSON delivery body's top-level keys. When empty,\nthe raw delivery body is used verbatim.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "dispatch": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/SopDispatch",
          "default": "agent_loop",
          "description": "Where consumed deliveries are routed: drive an agent turn\n(`agent_loop`, default), dispatch to the SOP engine (`sop`), or both\n(`sop_and_agent_loop`). The `sop` and `sop_and_agent_loop` modes match\nthe delivery against SOP `amqp` triggers by routing key."
        },
        "durable_ack": {
          "default": true,
          "description": "Acknowledgement mode. When `true` (default), deliveries are acked only\nafter the message is durably handed to the agent loop, giving\nat-least-once semantics: a crash before hand-off redelivers the event.\nSet `false` for at-most-once (broker acks on dispatch), which silently\ndrops in-flight events on crash and is only appropriate for\nnon-side-effecting, drop-on-overload consumers.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Whether this channel is active. The runtime only loads channels whose\n`enabled = true`. Default: `false` so an operator who pastes a partial\n`[channels.<type>.<alias>]` block doesn't accidentally bring a channel\nlive before the rest of its config is filled in.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "exchange": {
          "description": "Exchange to bind the consumer queue to (e.g. `amq.topic`).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "excluded_tools": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Tools excluded from this channel's tool spec. When set, these tools\nare not exposed to the model when responding via this channel.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "queue": {
          "description": "Queue name. Leave unset for a server-generated, transient,\nauto-deleted, exclusive queue. Set a stable name (UUID recommended)\nonly when durable delivery across reconnects is required.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "routing_keys": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Routing keys to bind. Scope these to the topics of interest; binding\n`#` consumes the entire exchange and is almost never what you want.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "sender_label": {
          "default": "amqp",
          "description": "Value placed in `ChannelMessage.sender` for every delivery from this\nsource (e.g. `anitya`). Lets the orchestrator's self-loop guard and\nper-channel routing identify the origin.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "thread_id_field": {
          "default": "",
          "description": "Dotted path into the JSON delivery body whose value becomes the\nmessage `thread_ts`, correlating replies to the originating event\n(e.g. `message.project.name`). Empty disables threading.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "amqp_url",
        "exchange"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    "AnthropicModelProviderConfig": {
      "description": "Anthropic model model_provider config. No family-specific extras yet — typed\nslot reserved for future Anthropic-only knobs (cache_control, beta\nheaders) so they land cleanly without another schema rework.",
      "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "description": "Secret API token for this model_provider. Grab it from the model_provider's dashboard (OpenAI platform, Anthropic console, OpenRouter keys page, etc.). Stored via the OS keyring when possible; never commit it to config.toml directly.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "chat_template_kwargs": {
          "description": "Arbitrary key/value pairs forwarded verbatim as `chat_template_kwargs`\nin the request body (llama.cpp-specific). Use this to pass model-family\ntemplate variables that control behaviour not exposed by other fields.\nExample (Qwen3 thinking suppression):\n  `chat_template_kwargs = { enable_thinking = false }`"
        },
        "context_window": {
          "description": "Context window size (max input tokens) for this model.\nAuto-populated on setup from provider's /models endpoint if available.\nOverride manually for custom endpoints or when auto-detection fails.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "extra_headers": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "description": "Extra HTTP headers sent with every request. Niche: used for auth bridges, corporate proxies, or custom gateways that demand a tracing header. Most users never touch this; edit `config.toml` directly if you need it.",
          "type": "object",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "fallback": {
          "description": "Ordered list of other provider aliases to try when every model on this\nalias has failed. Each entry is a dotted `<type>.<alias>` reference into\n`providers.models` and resolves with its own credentials, endpoint, and\nmodel. A fallback never inherits this alias's key. The walk is\ndepth-first: this alias's models are exhausted first, then each fallback\nalias is descended in turn (applying its own `fallback_models` and\n`fallback`). Empty means no provider-level fallback.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/ModelProviderRef"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "fallback_models": {
          "description": "Ordered alternate models to try on THIS provider before falling over to\nthe `fallback` aliases. Same endpoint, key, and headers as the primary\n`model`. Only the model identifier changes. Use this when a provider\nserves a backup model (e.g. a smaller or older variant) that should be\ntried before leaving the provider entirely. Empty means only `model` is\ntried.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "kind": {
          "description": "Provider implementation to instantiate for this profile. Use this\nwhen a canonical typed slot should run through a compatible\nimplementation, e.g. `[providers.models.openai.proxy] kind =\n\"openai-compatible\"`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "live_pricing": {
          "description": "Pull live token prices for this provider's models from its own\nOpenAI-compatible `/models` listing (the gateway is the source of truth\nfor its prices), filling cost-tracking rates for models the operator\nhas NOT priced under `[cost.rates]` / `pricing`. Models the gateway does\nnot price (or providers with no HTTP `/models` listing at all, such as\na subprocess gateway like `kilocli`) fall back to the public models.dev\ncatalog. Configured rates always win; live prices only fill gaps. A\nbackground task refreshes the price snapshot hourly; the cost-recording\npath reads the cached snapshot and never blocks on the network. Default\n`false`: off means no fetching and behavior identical to a build\nwithout the feature.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "max_tokens": {
          "description": "Hard cap on response length in tokens. Most models enforce sensible built-in limits already; leave unset unless you specifically need to clip long outputs for cost or latency reasons.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "merge_system_into_user": {
          "description": "ModelProvider-specific quirk: fold the system prompt into the first user message instead of sending a separate system role. Only needed for models that reject (or mishandle) a standalone system role, e.g. certain older Mistral variants.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "model": {
          "description": "Model identifier to send with each request: the ID string from the model_provider's catalog (e.g. `gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `llama-3.3-70b`). Must match a model the model_provider actually serves on this account.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "native_tools": {
          "description": "Override the provider's default for native tool calling.\n`None` (default) honors the provider's built-in choice. `Some(true)`\nforces native tool calls on, `Some(false)` forces text-fallback.\nCurrently consulted only by the Groq factory, which defaults to\ntext-fallback because llama-family Groq models reject native tool\ncalls with HTTP 400. Setting `native_tools = true` re-enables native\ntool calling for Groq models that support it.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "pricing": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "format": "double",
            "type": "number"
          },
          "description": "Per-model pricing for cost tracking, USD per 1M tokens.\n\nFree-form key/value map. Keys are user-defined model identifiers; an\noptional `.input` / `.output` suffix encodes pricing dimension when\nthe operator wants to split rates. A bare key without a suffix is\nused as a flat per-token rate when neither dimension is specified.\nDefault is empty: cost tracking falls back to \"unknown\" rates and\nonly token usage is recorded.\n\nExample: `pricing = { opus = 15.0, sonnet = 3.0 }`\nOr split: `pricing = { \"opus.input\" = 15.0, \"opus.output\" = 75.0 }`",
          "type": "object"
        },
        "provider_extra": {
          "description": "Extra JSON parameters to include in API requests.\nMerged at the top level of the request body, allowing provider-specific\nfeatures (routing, transforms, etc.) without code changes.\nExample: `provider_extra = { model_provider = { only = [\"Anthropic\"] } }`"
        },
        "replay_assistant_reasoning": {
          "description": "Whether stored assistant reasoning should be replayed on outbound\nassistant history messages. `Some(false)` strips `reasoning_content`\nand `reasoning` before sending. `None` (default) honours the provider's\nbuilt-in default (true for most compat providers, false for Groq).",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "requires_openai_auth": {
          "description": "When true, the client pulls credentials from ZeroClaw's stored `openai-codex` auth profile instead of the `api_key` field above. Import an existing Codex CLI login with `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json`, or run `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex`. Turn on only for the OpenAI Codex model_provider; leave off for standard API-key model_providers.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "temperature": {
          "description": "Sampling temperature passed to the model. Lower values (0.0–0.3) give\ndeterministic, near-verbatim output, which fits code, routing, summarization.\nHigher values (0.7–1.2) give more varied output, which fits open-ended chat.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "think": {
          "description": "Enable or disable chain-of-thought thinking for models that support it\n(e.g. Qwen3, GLM-4). `true` turns thinking on, `false` turns it off.\n`None` (default) lets the model decide. Forwarded as `enable_thinking`\nin the request body; mirrors the Ollama provider's `think` field.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "description": "HTTP request timeout in seconds. Bump this for slow local model_providers (Ollama on CPU, big local models) or high-latency networks; leave unset otherwise.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "tls_ca_cert_path": {
          "description": "Path to a PEM-encoded CA certificate for TLS connections to this provider.\nMust be an absolute path; shell expansion (e.g. `~`) is not performed.\nLeave unset to use the system's default trust store.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "uri": {
          "description": "Endpoint URI the client hits. Override the family's default endpoint when pointing at a self-hosted gateway (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama), a custom proxy, or any non-standard URL. Leave unset to use the family's default URI from its `ModelEndpoint` impl. Set this to the FULL endpoint URL; there is no separate path-suffix field.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "vision": {
          "description": "Override the provider's vision (image input) capability.\n`None` (default) uses the provider family's built-in default. Several\nfamilies (llama.cpp, the generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint, etc.)\nassume vision-capable because they can serve multimodal models. Set\n`vision = false` for a text-only model served by such a family (e.g. a\ntext LLM behind llama.cpp) so image messages are routed to a configured\n`[multimodal] vision_model_provider` instead of being sent to a model\nthat rejects them. `Some(true)` forces vision on.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "wire_api": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/WireApi"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Wire protocol flavor: `responses` for OpenAI's Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`), `chat_completions` for the legacy chat wire and most OpenAI-compatible gateways. New OpenAI provider slots default to `responses`; other families default to chat-completions (or ignore the field). Only override if you're forcing an unusual combination."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
