    "ApprovalGroupConfig": {
      "description": "A named approver group (`[sop.approval.groups.<name>]`).",
      "properties": {
        "members": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Identity labels that belong to this group.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "ApprovalMode": {
      "description": "WHO may clear a SOP approval gate. Layered with execution_mode / priority /\nrequires_confirmation (all of which still apply). Closed set => serde enum.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "both",
          "description": "Agent `sop_approve` OR an out-of-band principal both clear. Backward-compat default.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "out_of_band_required",
          "description": "Only out-of-band principals (CLI / WS / HTTP / timeout) clear; `sop_approve`\nbecomes a no-op. Lets an operator require a separate approver without bricking runs.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "agent_tool",
          "description": "Only the agent tool clears; out-of-band surfaces are read-only pending lists. Niche.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    },
    "ApprovalPolicyConfig": {
      "description": "A named approval policy (`[sop.approval.policies.<name>]`) the broker enforces.",
      "properties": {
        "escalation_route": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Route to escalate to on timeout (the distinct \"second route\"). `None`/empty\nre-surfaces to the same route (today's `Escalate` behavior). When configured,\nthe route must use the `channel:recipient` format.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "quorum": {
          "default": 0,
          "description": "Distinct approvers required before the gate clears. `0`/`1` both mean a\nsingle approval; `>= 2` requires a quorum of distinct approver identities.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "request_route": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Channel to deliver the INITIAL approval request to when a run parks at a\ngate this policy governs, formatted `channel:recipient` (e.g.\n`discord.ops:123456789012345678`). The `channel` names a configured channel\n(the `<channel>.<alias>` / bare-`<channel>` key from the channel map); the\n`recipient` is that channel's addressee (a Discord channel id, a chat id,\netc.). Delivery is best-effort - the gate is the source of truth and a\ndelivery failure never blocks or clears it; approvals still come back\nthrough the normal HTTP/WS/tool surfaces. `None`/empty = no out-of-band\nrequest notice (today's behavior: only the originating surface is notified).\nThis is a DISTINCT lifecycle event from `escalation_route`: the request goes\nout when the run parks; the escalation goes out only if it later times out.\nWhen configured, the route must use the `channel:recipient` format.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "required_group": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Group whose members may satisfy this policy's gate. `None`/empty = any\nprincipal permitted by `approval_mode` (back-compat, no membership gate).",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "ApprovalRoute": {
      "description": "Routes tool approvals to a distinct approver channel with fail-closed defaults.",
      "properties": {
        "approver_channel": {
          "description": "A registered channel name (NOT the originator) — the distinct-approver hop.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "on_no_approver": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/OnNoApprover",
          "default": "deny",
          "description": "Behavior when the approver is unreachable. Fail-closed by default."
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "default": 120,
          "description": "Bound the approver's response window; a timeout denies (DoS guard). Default 120s.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "approver_channel"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    "ApprovalTimeoutAction": {
      "description": "What happens to a SOP approval gate when it times out. Default is fail-closed:\nthe gate never self-approves. Closed set => serde enum.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "escalate",
          "description": "Re-surface to the out-of-band approver and keep waiting; never self-approve.\nDefault, fail-closed.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "cancel",
          "description": "Terminate the run (fail-safe cancel). Strict mode.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "auto_approve",
          "description": "LEGACY: auto-approve on timeout. The ONLY path to the old fail-open behavior;\nopt-in only.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    },
    "ArceeModelProviderConfig": {
      "description": "Named model_provider profile definition.",
      "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "description": "Secret API token for this model_provider. Grab it from the model_provider's dashboard (OpenAI platform, Anthropic console, OpenRouter keys page, etc.). Stored via the OS keyring when possible; never commit it to config.toml directly.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "chat_template_kwargs": {
          "description": "Arbitrary key/value pairs forwarded verbatim as `chat_template_kwargs`\nin the request body (llama.cpp-specific). Use this to pass model-family\ntemplate variables that control behaviour not exposed by other fields.\nExample (Qwen3 thinking suppression):\n  `chat_template_kwargs = { enable_thinking = false }`"
        },
        "context_window": {
          "description": "Context window size (max input tokens) for this model.\nAuto-populated on setup from provider's /models endpoint if available.\nOverride manually for custom endpoints or when auto-detection fails.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "extra_headers": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "description": "Extra HTTP headers sent with every request. Niche: used for auth bridges, corporate proxies, or custom gateways that demand a tracing header. Most users never touch this; edit `config.toml` directly if you need it.",
          "type": "object",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "fallback": {
          "description": "Ordered list of other provider aliases to try when every model on this\nalias has failed. Each entry is a dotted `<type>.<alias>` reference into\n`providers.models` and resolves with its own credentials, endpoint, and\nmodel. A fallback never inherits this alias's key. The walk is\ndepth-first: this alias's models are exhausted first, then each fallback\nalias is descended in turn (applying its own `fallback_models` and\n`fallback`). Empty means no provider-level fallback.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/ModelProviderRef"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "fallback_models": {
          "description": "Ordered alternate models to try on THIS provider before falling over to\nthe `fallback` aliases. Same endpoint, key, and headers as the primary\n`model`. Only the model identifier changes. Use this when a provider\nserves a backup model (e.g. a smaller or older variant) that should be\ntried before leaving the provider entirely. Empty means only `model` is\ntried.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "kind": {
          "description": "Provider implementation to instantiate for this profile. Use this\nwhen a canonical typed slot should run through a compatible\nimplementation, e.g. `[providers.models.openai.proxy] kind =\n\"openai-compatible\"`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "live_pricing": {
          "description": "Pull live token prices for this provider's models from its own\nOpenAI-compatible `/models` listing (the gateway is the source of truth\nfor its prices), filling cost-tracking rates for models the operator\nhas NOT priced under `[cost.rates]` / `pricing`. Models the gateway does\nnot price (or providers with no HTTP `/models` listing at all, such as\na subprocess gateway like `kilocli`) fall back to the public models.dev\ncatalog. Configured rates always win; live prices only fill gaps. A\nbackground task refreshes the price snapshot hourly; the cost-recording\npath reads the cached snapshot and never blocks on the network. Default\n`false`: off means no fetching and behavior identical to a build\nwithout the feature.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "max_tokens": {
          "description": "Hard cap on response length in tokens. Most models enforce sensible built-in limits already; leave unset unless you specifically need to clip long outputs for cost or latency reasons.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "merge_system_into_user": {
          "description": "ModelProvider-specific quirk: fold the system prompt into the first user message instead of sending a separate system role. Only needed for models that reject (or mishandle) a standalone system role, e.g. certain older Mistral variants.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "model": {
          "description": "Model identifier to send with each request: the ID string from the model_provider's catalog (e.g. `gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `llama-3.3-70b`). Must match a model the model_provider actually serves on this account.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "native_tools": {
          "description": "Override the provider's default for native tool calling.\n`None` (default) honors the provider's built-in choice. `Some(true)`\nforces native tool calls on, `Some(false)` forces text-fallback.\nCurrently consulted only by the Groq factory, which defaults to\ntext-fallback because llama-family Groq models reject native tool\ncalls with HTTP 400. Setting `native_tools = true` re-enables native\ntool calling for Groq models that support it.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "pricing": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "format": "double",
            "type": "number"
          },
          "description": "Per-model pricing for cost tracking, USD per 1M tokens.\n\nFree-form key/value map. Keys are user-defined model identifiers; an\noptional `.input` / `.output` suffix encodes pricing dimension when\nthe operator wants to split rates. A bare key without a suffix is\nused as a flat per-token rate when neither dimension is specified.\nDefault is empty: cost tracking falls back to \"unknown\" rates and\nonly token usage is recorded.\n\nExample: `pricing = { opus = 15.0, sonnet = 3.0 }`\nOr split: `pricing = { \"opus.input\" = 15.0, \"opus.output\" = 75.0 }`",
          "type": "object"
        },
        "provider_extra": {
          "description": "Extra JSON parameters to include in API requests.\nMerged at the top level of the request body, allowing provider-specific\nfeatures (routing, transforms, etc.) without code changes.\nExample: `provider_extra = { model_provider = { only = [\"Anthropic\"] } }`"
        },
        "replay_assistant_reasoning": {
          "description": "Whether stored assistant reasoning should be replayed on outbound\nassistant history messages. `Some(false)` strips `reasoning_content`\nand `reasoning` before sending. `None` (default) honours the provider's\nbuilt-in default (true for most compat providers, false for Groq).",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "requires_openai_auth": {
          "description": "When true, the client pulls credentials from ZeroClaw's stored `openai-codex` auth profile instead of the `api_key` field above. Import an existing Codex CLI login with `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json`, or run `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex`. Turn on only for the OpenAI Codex model_provider; leave off for standard API-key model_providers.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "temperature": {
          "description": "Sampling temperature passed to the model. Lower values (0.0–0.3) give\ndeterministic, near-verbatim output, which fits code, routing, summarization.\nHigher values (0.7–1.2) give more varied output, which fits open-ended chat.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "think": {
          "description": "Enable or disable chain-of-thought thinking for models that support it\n(e.g. Qwen3, GLM-4). `true` turns thinking on, `false` turns it off.\n`None` (default) lets the model decide. Forwarded as `enable_thinking`\nin the request body; mirrors the Ollama provider's `think` field.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "description": "HTTP request timeout in seconds. Bump this for slow local model_providers (Ollama on CPU, big local models) or high-latency networks; leave unset otherwise.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "tls_ca_cert_path": {
          "description": "Path to a PEM-encoded CA certificate for TLS connections to this provider.\nMust be an absolute path; shell expansion (e.g. `~`) is not performed.\nLeave unset to use the system's default trust store.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "uri": {
          "description": "Endpoint URI the client hits. Override the family's default endpoint when pointing at a self-hosted gateway (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama), a custom proxy, or any non-standard URL. Leave unset to use the family's default URI from its `ModelEndpoint` impl. Set this to the FULL endpoint URL; there is no separate path-suffix field.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "vision": {
          "description": "Override the provider's vision (image input) capability.\n`None` (default) uses the provider family's built-in default. Several\nfamilies (llama.cpp, the generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint, etc.)\nassume vision-capable because they can serve multimodal models. Set\n`vision = false` for a text-only model served by such a family (e.g. a\ntext LLM behind llama.cpp) so image messages are routed to a configured\n`[multimodal] vision_model_provider` instead of being sent to a model\nthat rejects them. `Some(true)` forces vision on.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "wire_api": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/WireApi"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Wire protocol flavor: `responses` for OpenAI's Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`), `chat_completions` for the legacy chat wire and most OpenAI-compatible gateways. New OpenAI provider slots default to `responses`; other families default to chat-completions (or ignore the field). Only override if you're forcing an unusual combination."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "AssemblyAiSttConfig": {
      "description": "AssemblyAI STT model_provider configuration (`[transcription.assemblyai]`).",
      "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "AssemblyAI API key.",

        "initial_prompt": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Whisper-style initial prompt to bias the model toward expected\nvocabulary (proper nouns, technical terms). Provider-specific support;\nsilently ignored where not applicable.",

            "string",
            "null"
          ]

            "string",

      "type": "object"

Only the model identifier changes. Use this when a provider\nserves a backup model (e.g. a smaller or older variant) that should be\ntried before leaving the provider entirely. Empty means only `model` is\ntried.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "kind": {
          "description": "Provider implementation to instantiate for this profile. Use this\nwhen a canonical typed slot should run through a compatible\nimplementation, e.g. `[providers.models.openai.proxy] kind =\n\"openai-compatible\"`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "live_pricing": {
          "description": "Pull live token prices for this provider's models from its own\nOpenAI-compatible `/models` listing (the gateway is the source of truth\nfor its prices), filling cost-tracking rates for models the operator\nhas NOT priced under `[cost.rates]` / `pricing`. Models the gateway does\nnot price (or providers with no HTTP `/models` listing at all, such as\na subprocess gateway like `kilocli`) fall back to the public models.dev\ncatalog. Configured rates always win; live prices only fill gaps. A\nbackground task refreshes the price snapshot hourly; the cost-recording\npath reads the cached snapshot and never blocks on the network. Default\n`false`: off means no fetching and behavior identical to a build\nwithout the feature.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "max_tokens": {
          "description": "Hard cap on response length in tokens. Most models enforce sensible built-in limits already; leave unset unless you specifically need to clip long outputs for cost or latency reasons.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "merge_system_into_user": {
          "description": "ModelProvider-specific quirk: fold the system prompt into the first user message instead of sending a separate system role. Only needed for models that reject (or mishandle) a standalone system role, e.g. certain older Mistral variants.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "model": {
          "description": "Model identifier to send with each request: the ID string from the model_provider's catalog (e.g. `gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `llama-3.3-70b`). Must match a model the model_provider actually serves on this account.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "native_tools": {
          "description": "Override the provider's default for native tool calling.\n`None` (default) honors the provider's built-in choice. `Some(true)`\nforces native tool calls on, `Some(false)` forces text-fallback.\nCurrently consulted only by the Groq factory, which defaults to\ntext-fallback because llama-family Groq models reject native tool\ncalls with HTTP 400. Setting `native_tools = true` re-enables native\ntool calling for Groq models that support it.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "pricing": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "format": "double",
            "type": "number"
          },
          "description": "Per-model pricing for cost tracking, USD per 1M tokens.\n\nFree-form key/value map. Keys are user-defined model identifiers; an\noptional `.input` / `.output` suffix encodes pricing dimension when\nthe operator wants to split rates. A bare key without a suffix is\nused as a flat per-token rate when neither dimension is specified.\nDefault is empty: cost tracking falls back to \"unknown\" rates and\nonly token usage is recorded.\n\nExample: `pricing = { opus = 15.0, sonnet = 3.0 }`\nOr split: `pricing = { \"opus.input\" = 15.0, \"opus.output\" = 75.0 }`",
          "type": "object"
        },
        "provider_extra": {
          "description": "Extra JSON parameters to include in API requests.\nMerged at the top level of the request body, allowing provider-specific\nfeatures (routing, transforms, etc.) without code changes.\nExample: `provider_extra = { model_provider = { only = [\"Anthropic\"] } }`"
        },
        "replay_assistant_reasoning": {
          "description": "Whether stored assistant reasoning should be replayed on outbound\nassistant history messages. `Some(false)` strips `reasoning_content`\nand `reasoning` before sending. `None` (default) honours the provider's\nbuilt-in default (true for most compat providers, false for Groq).",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "requires_openai_auth": {
          "description": "When true, the client pulls credentials from ZeroClaw's stored `openai-codex` auth profile instead of the `api_key` field above. Import an existing Codex CLI login with `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json`, or run `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex`. Turn on only for the OpenAI Codex model_provider; leave off for standard API-key model_providers.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "temperature": {
          "description": "Sampling temperature passed to the model. Lower values (0.0–0.3) give\ndeterministic, near-verbatim output, which fits code, routing, summarization.\nHigher values (0.7–1.2) give more varied output, which fits open-ended chat.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "think": {
          "description": "Enable or disable chain-of-thought thinking for models that support it\n(e.g. Qwen3, GLM-4). `true` turns thinking on, `false` turns it off.\n`None` (default) lets the model decide. Forwarded as `enable_thinking`\nin the request body; mirrors the Ollama provider's `think` field.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "description": "HTTP request timeout in seconds. Bump this for slow local model_providers (Ollama on CPU, big local models) or high-latency networks; leave unset otherwise.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "tls_ca_cert_path": {
          "description": "Path to a PEM-encoded CA certificate for TLS connections to this provider.\nMust be an absolute path; shell expansion (e.g. `~`) is not performed.\nLeave unset to use the system's default trust store.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "uri": {
          "description": "Endpoint URI the client hits. Override the family's default endpoint when pointing at a self-hosted gateway (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama), a custom proxy, or any non-standard URL. Leave unset to use the family's default URI from its `ModelEndpoint` impl. Set this to the FULL endpoint URL; there is no separate path-suffix field.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "vision": {
          "description": "Override the provider's vision (image input) capability.\n`None` (default) uses the provider family's built-in default. Several\nfamilies (llama.cpp, the generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint, etc.)\nassume vision-capable because they can serve multimodal models. Set\n`vision = false` for a text-only model served by such a family (e.g. a\ntext LLM behind llama.cpp) so image messages are routed to a configured\n`[multimodal] vision_model_provider` instead of being sent to a model\nthat rejects them. `Some(true)` forces vision on.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "wire_api": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/WireApi"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Wire protocol flavor: `responses` for OpenAI's Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`), `chat_completions` for the legacy chat wire and most OpenAI-compatible gateways. New OpenAI provider slots default to `responses`; other families default to chat-completions (or ignore the field). Only override if you're forcing an unusual combination."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "AuditConfig": {
      "description": "Audit logging configuration",
      "properties": {
        "enabled": {
          "default": true,
          "description": "Enable audit logging",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "log_path": {
          "default": "audit.log",
          "description": "Path to audit log file (relative to zeroclaw dir)",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "max_size_mb": {
          "default": 100,
          "description": "Maximum log size in MB before rotation",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "sign_events": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Sign events with HMAC for tamper evidence",
          "type": "boolean"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "AuthMode": {
      "description": "Authentication mode for model model_provider families that support more than one\n(e.g. Qwen, Minimax can use API key OR OAuth). Families that only support a\nsingle auth flow simply omit this field from their config struct.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "api_key",
          "description": "Standard API key authentication via the `api_key` field.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "o_auth",
          "description": "OAuth flow — credential resolution defers to the family runtime impl\n(typically reading a vendor-specific token cache or env var).",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    },
    "AutoClassifyConfig": {
      "properties": {
        "complex_hint": {
          "default": null,
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "cost_optimized_hint": {
          "default": "cost-optimized",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "simple_hint": {
          "default": null,
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "standard_hint": {
          "default": null,
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "AutonomyLevel": {
      "description": "The agent's autonomy level, ordered from least to most autonomous.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "readonly",
          "description": "Read-only: can observe but not act",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "supervised",
          "description": "Supervised: acts but requires approval for risky operations",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "full",
          "description": "Full: autonomous execution within policy bounds",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    },

          "description": "Per-model pricing for cost tracking, USD per 1M tokens.\n\nFree-form key/value map. A bare key without a suffix is\nused as a flat per-token rate when neither dimension is specified.\nDefault is empty: cost tracking falls back to \"unknown\" rates and\nonly token usage is recorded.\n\nExample: `pricing = { opus = 15.0, sonnet = 3.0 }`\nOr split: `pricing = { \"opus.input\" = 15.0, \"opus.output\" = 75.0 }`",
          "type": "object"
        },
        "provider_extra": {
          "description": "Extra JSON parameters to include in API requests.\nMerged at the top level of the request body, allowing provider-specific\nfeatures (routing, transforms, etc.) without code changes.\nExample: `provider_extra = { model_provider = { only = [\"Anthropic\"] } }`"
        },
        "replay_assistant_reasoning": {
          "description": "Whether stored assistant reasoning should be replayed on outbound\nassistant history messages. `Some(false)` strips `reasoning_content`\nand `reasoning` before sending. `None` (default) honours the provider's\nbuilt-in default (true for most compat providers, false for Groq).",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "requires_openai_auth": {
          "description": "When true, the client pulls credentials from ZeroClaw's stored `openai-codex` auth profile instead of the `api_key` field above. Import an existing Codex CLI login with `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json`, or run `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex`. Turn on only for the OpenAI Codex model_provider; leave off for standard API-key model_providers.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "resource": {
          "description": "Azure resource name (the `<resource>` part of `<resource>.openai.azure.com`).",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "temperature": {
          "description": "Sampling temperature passed to the model. Lower values (0.0–0.3) give\ndeterministic, near-verbatim output, which fits code, routing, summarization.\nHigher values (0.7–1.2) give more varied output, which fits open-ended chat.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "think": {
          "description": "Enable or disable chain-of-thought thinking for models that support it\n(e.g. Qwen3, GLM-4). `true` turns thinking on, `false` turns it off.\n`None` (default) lets the model decide. Forwarded as `enable_thinking`\nin the request body; mirrors the Ollama provider's `think` field.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "description": "HTTP request timeout in seconds. Bump this for slow local model_providers (Ollama on CPU, big local models) or high-latency networks; leave unset otherwise.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "tls_ca_cert_path": {
          "description": "Path to a PEM-encoded CA certificate for TLS connections to this provider.\nMust be an absolute path; shell expansion (e.g. `~`) is not performed.\nLeave unset to use the system's default trust store.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "uri": {
          "description": "Endpoint URI the client hits. Override the family's default endpoint when pointing at a self-hosted gateway (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama), a custom proxy, or any non-standard URL. Leave unset to use the family's default URI from its `ModelEndpoint` impl. Set this to the FULL endpoint URL; there is no separate path-suffix field.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "vision": {
          "description": "Override the provider's vision (image input) capability.\n`None` (default) uses the provider family's built-in default. Several\nfamilies (llama.cpp, the generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint, etc.)\nassume vision-capable because they can serve multimodal models. Set\n`vision = false` for a text-only model served by such a family (e.g. a\ntext LLM behind llama.cpp) so image messages are routed to a configured\n`[multimodal] vision_model_provider` instead of being sent to a model\nthat rejects them. `Some(true)` forces vision on.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "wire_api": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/WireApi"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Wire protocol flavor: `responses` for OpenAI's Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`), `chat_completions` for the legacy chat wire and most OpenAI-compatible gateways. New OpenAI provider slots default to `responses`; other families default to chat-completions (or ignore the field). Only override if you're forcing an unusual combination."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "BackupConfig": {
      "description": "Backup tool configuration (`[backup]` section).",
      "properties": {
        "compress": {
          "default": true,
          "description": "Compress backup archives.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "destination_dir": {
          "default": "state/backups",
          "description": "Output directory for backup archives (relative to workspace root).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": true,
          "description": "Enable the `backup` tool.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "encrypt": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Encrypt backup archives (requires a configured secret store key).",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "include_dirs": {
          "default": [
            "config",
            "memory",
            "audit",
            "knowledge"
          ],
          "description": "Workspace subdirectories to include in backups.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "max_keep": {
          "default": 10,
          "description": "Maximum number of backups to keep (oldest are pruned).",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "schedule_cron": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Optional cron expression for scheduled automatic backups.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "schedule_timezone": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "IANA timezone for `schedule_cron`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "BaichuanModelProviderConfig": {
      "description": "Named model_provider profile definition.",
      "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "description": "Secret API token for this model_provider. Grab it from the model_provider's dashboard (OpenAI platform, Anthropic console, OpenRouter keys page, etc.). Stored via the OS keyring when possible; never commit it to config.toml directly.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "chat_template_kwargs": {
          "description": "Arbitrary key/value pairs forwarded verbatim as `chat_template_kwargs`\nin the request body (llama.cpp-specific). Use this to pass model-family\ntemplate variables that control behaviour not exposed by other fields.\nExample (Qwen3 thinking suppression):\n  `chat_template_kwargs = { enable_thinking = false }`"
        },
        "context_window": {
          "description": "Context window size (max input tokens) for this model.\nAuto-populated on setup from provider's /models endpoint if available.\nOverride manually for custom endpoints or when auto-detection fails.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "extra_headers": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "description": "Extra HTTP headers sent with every request. Niche: used for auth bridges, corporate proxies, or custom gateways that demand a tracing header. Most users never touch this; edit `config.toml` directly if you need it.",
          "type": "object",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "fallback": {
          "description": "Ordered list of other provider aliases to try when every model on this\nalias has failed. Each entry is a dotted `<type>.<alias>` reference into\n`providers.models` and resolves with its own credentials, endpoint, and\nmodel. A fallback never inherits this alias's key. The walk is\ndepth-first: this alias's models are exhausted first, then each fallback\nalias is descended in turn (applying its own `fallback_models` and\n`fallback`). Empty means no provider-level fallback.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/ModelProviderRef"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "fallback_models": {
          "description": "Ordered alternate models to try on THIS provider before falling over to\nthe `fallback` aliases. Same endpoint, key, and headers as the primary\n`model`. Only the model identifier changes. Use this when a provider\nserves a backup model (e.g. a smaller or older variant) that should be\ntried before leaving the provider entirely. Empty means only `model` is\ntried.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "kind": {
          "description": "Provider implementation to instantiate for this profile. Use this\nwhen a canonical typed slot should run through a compatible\nimplementation, e.g. `[providers.models.openai.proxy] kind =\n\"openai-compatible\"`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "live_pricing": {
          "description": "Pull live token prices for this provider's models from its own\nOpenAI-compatible `/models` listing (the gateway is the source of truth\nfor its prices), filling cost-tracking rates for models the operator\nhas NOT priced under `[cost.rates]` / `pricing`. Models the gateway does\nnot price (or providers with no HTTP `/models` listing at all, such as\na subprocess gateway like `kilocli`) fall back to the public models.dev\ncatalog. Configured rates always win; live prices only fill gaps. A\nbackground task refreshes the price snapshot hourly; the cost-recording\npath reads the cached snapshot and never blocks on the network. Default\n`false`: off means no fetching and behavior identical to a build\nwithout the feature.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "max_tokens": {
          "description": "Hard cap on response length in tokens. Most models enforce sensible built-in limits already; leave unset unless you specifically need to clip long outputs for cost or latency reasons.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "merge_system_into_user": {
          "description": "ModelProvider-specific quirk: fold the system prompt into the first user message instead of sending a separate system role. Only needed for models that reject (or mishandle) a standalone system role, e.g. certain older Mistral variants.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "model": {
          "description": "Model identifier to send with each request: the ID string from the model_provider's catalog (e.g. `gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `llama-3.3-70b`). Must match a model the model_provider actually serves on this account.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "native_tools": {
          "description": "Override the provider's default for native tool calling.\n`None` (default) honors the provider's built-in choice. `Some(true)`\nforces native tool calls on, `Some(false)` forces text-fallback.\nCurrently consulted only by the Groq factory, which defaults to\ntext-fallback because llama-family Groq models reject native tool\ncalls with HTTP 400. Setting `native_tools = true` re-enables native\ntool calling for Groq models that support it.",

    "BedrockModelProviderConfig": {
      "description": "AWS Bedrock model model_provider config. Carries the AWS region (the URI\ntemplate substitutes `{region}` from this field). Bedrock auth is\nSigV4 — credentials come from the standard AWS credential chain\n(env vars, instance metadata, profile), not from `api_key`.",
      "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "description": "Secret API token for this model_provider. Grab it from the model_provider's dashboard (OpenAI platform, Anthropic console, OpenRouter keys page, etc.). Stored via the OS keyring when possible; never commit it to config.toml directly.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "chat_template_kwargs": {
          "description": "Arbitrary key/value pairs forwarded verbatim as `chat_template_kwargs`\nin the request body (llama.cpp-specific). Use this to pass model-family\ntemplate variables that control behaviour not exposed by other fields.\nExample (Qwen3 thinking suppression):\n  `chat_template_kwargs = { enable_thinking = false }`"
        },
        "context_window": {
          "description": "Context window size (max input tokens) for this model.\nAuto-populated on setup from provider's /models endpoint if available.\nOverride manually for custom endpoints or when auto-detection fails.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "extra_headers": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "description": "Extra HTTP headers sent with every request. Niche: used for auth bridges, corporate proxies, or custom gateways that demand a tracing header. Most users never touch this; edit `config.toml` directly if you need it.",
          "type": "object",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "fallback": {
          "description": "Ordered list of other provider aliases to try when every model on this\nalias has failed. Each entry is a dotted `<type>.<alias>` reference into\n`providers.models` and resolves with its own credentials, endpoint, and\nmodel. A fallback never inherits this alias's key. The walk is\ndepth-first: this alias's models are exhausted first, then each fallback\nalias is descended in turn (applying its own `fallback_models` and\n`fallback`). Empty means no provider-level fallback.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/ModelProviderRef"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "fallback_models": {
          "description": "Ordered alternate models to try on THIS provider before falling over to\nthe `fallback` aliases. Same endpoint, key, and headers as the primary\n`model`. Only the model identifier changes. Use this when a provider\nserves a backup model (e.g. a smaller or older variant) that should be\ntried before leaving the provider entirely. Empty means only `model` is\ntried.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "kind": {
          "description": "Provider implementation to instantiate for this profile. Use this\nwhen a canonical typed slot should run through a compatible\nimplementation, e.g. `[providers.models.openai.proxy] kind =\n\"openai-compatible\"`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "live_pricing": {
          "description": "Pull live token prices for this provider's models from its own\nOpenAI-compatible `/models` listing (the gateway is the source of truth\nfor its prices), filling cost-tracking rates for models the operator\nhas NOT priced under `[cost.rates]` / `pricing`. Models the gateway does\nnot price (or providers with no HTTP `/models` listing at all, such as\na subprocess gateway like `kilocli`) fall back to the public models.dev\ncatalog. Configured rates always win; live prices only fill gaps. A\nbackground task refreshes the price snapshot hourly; the cost-recording\npath reads the cached snapshot and never blocks on the network. Default\n`false`: off means no fetching and behavior identical to a build\nwithout the feature.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "max_tokens": {
          "description": "Hard cap on response length in tokens. Most models enforce sensible built-in limits already; leave unset unless you specifically need to clip long outputs for cost or latency reasons.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "merge_system_into_user": {
          "description": "ModelProvider-specific quirk: fold the system prompt into the first user message instead of sending a separate system role. Only needed for models that reject (or mishandle) a standalone system role, e.g. certain older Mistral variants.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "model": {
          "description": "Model identifier to send with each request: the ID string from the model_provider's catalog (e.g. `gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `llama-3.3-70b`). Must match a model the model_provider actually serves on this account.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "native_tools": {
          "description": "Override the provider's default for native tool calling.\n`None` (default) honors the provider's built-in choice. `Some(true)`\nforces native tool calls on, `Some(false)` forces text-fallback.\nCurrently consulted only by the Groq factory, which defaults to\ntext-fallback because llama-family Groq models reject native tool\ncalls with HTTP 400. Setting `native_tools = true` re-enables native\ntool calling for Groq models that support it.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "pricing": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "format": "double",
            "type": "number"
          },
          "description": "Per-model pricing for cost tracking, USD per 1M tokens.\n\nFree-form key/value map. Keys are user-defined model identifiers; an\noptional `.input` / `.output` suffix encodes pricing dimension when\nthe operator wants to split rates. A bare key without a suffix is\nused as a flat per-token rate when neither dimension is specified.\nDefault is empty: cost tracking falls back to \"unknown\" rates and\nonly token usage is recorded.\n\nExample: `pricing = { opus = 15.0, sonnet = 3.0 }`\nOr split: `pricing = { \"opus.input\" = 15.0, \"opus.output\" = 75.0 }`",
          "type": "object"
        },
        "provider_extra": {
          "description": "Extra JSON parameters to include in API requests.\nMerged at the top level of the request body, allowing provider-specific\nfeatures (routing, transforms, etc.) without code changes.\nExample: `provider_extra = { model_provider = { only = [\"Anthropic\"] } }`"
        },
        "region": {
          "description": "AWS region for the Bedrock endpoint (e.g. `us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`).",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "replay_assistant_reasoning": {
          "description": "Whether stored assistant reasoning should be replayed on outbound\nassistant history messages. `Some(false)` strips `reasoning_content`\nand `reasoning` before sending. `None` (default) honours the provider's\nbuilt-in default (true for most compat providers, false for Groq).",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "requires_openai_auth": {
          "description": "When true, the client pulls credentials from ZeroClaw's stored `openai-codex` auth profile instead of the `api_key` field above. Import an existing Codex CLI login with `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json`, or run `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex`. Turn on only for the OpenAI Codex model_provider; leave off for standard API-key model_providers.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "temperature": {
          "description": "Sampling temperature passed to the model. Lower values (0.0–0.3) give\ndeterministic, near-verbatim output, which fits code, routing, summarization.\nHigher values (0.7–1.2) give more varied output, which fits open-ended chat.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "think": {
          "description": "Enable or disable chain-of-thought thinking for models that support it\n(e.g. Qwen3, GLM-4). `true` turns thinking on, `false` turns it off.\n`None` (default) lets the model decide. Forwarded as `enable_thinking`\nin the request body; mirrors the Ollama provider's `think` field.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "description": "HTTP request timeout in seconds. Bump this for slow local model_providers (Ollama on CPU, big local models) or high-latency networks; leave unset otherwise.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "tls_ca_cert_path": {
          "description": "Path to a PEM-encoded CA certificate for TLS connections to this provider.\nMust be an absolute path; shell expansion (e.g. `~`) is not performed.\nLeave unset to use the system's default trust store.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "uri": {
          "description": "Endpoint URI the client hits. Override the family's default endpoint when pointing at a self-hosted gateway (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama), a custom proxy, or any non-standard URL. Leave unset to use the family's default URI from its `ModelEndpoint` impl. Set this to the FULL endpoint URL; there is no separate path-suffix field.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "vision": {
          "description": "Override the provider's vision (image input) capability.\n`None` (default) uses the provider family's built-in default. Several\nfamilies (llama.cpp, the generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint, etc.)\nassume vision-capable because they can serve multimodal models. Set\n`vision = false` for a text-only model served by such a family (e.g. a\ntext LLM behind llama.cpp) so image messages are routed to a configured\n`[multimodal] vision_model_provider` instead of being sent to a model\nthat rejects them. `Some(true)` forces vision on.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "wire_api": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/WireApi"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Wire protocol flavor: `responses` for OpenAI's Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`), `chat_completions` for the legacy chat wire and most OpenAI-compatible gateways. New OpenAI provider slots default to `responses`; other families default to chat-completions (or ignore the field). Only override if you're forcing an unusual combination."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "BlueskyConfig": {
      "description": "Bluesky channel configuration (AT Protocol).",
      "properties": {
        "app_password": {
          "description": "App-specific password (from Bluesky settings).",
          "type": "string",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Whether this channel is active. The runtime only loads channels whose\n`enabled = true`. Default: `false` so an operator who pastes a partial\n`[channels.<type>.<alias>]` block doesn't accidentally bring a channel\nlive before the rest of its config is filled in.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "excluded_tools": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Tools excluded from this channel's tool spec. When set, these tools\nare not exposed to the model when responding via this channel.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "handle": {
          "description": "Bluesky handle (e.g. `\"mybot.bsky.social\"`).",
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "handle",
        "app_password"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    "BrowserComputerUseConfig": {
      "description": "Computer-use sidecar configuration (`[browser.computer_use]` section).\n\nDelegates OS-level mouse, keyboard, and screenshot actions to a local sidecar.",
      "properties": {
        "allow_remote_endpoint": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Allow remote/public endpoint for computer-use sidecar (default: false)",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "api_key": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Optional bearer token for computer-use sidecar",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "endpoint": {
          "default": "http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1/actions",
          "description": "Sidecar endpoint for computer-use actions (OS-level mouse/keyboard/screenshot)",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "max_coordinate_x": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Optional X-axis boundary for coordinate-based actions",
          "format": "int64",
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "max_coordinate_y": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Optional Y-axis boundary for coordinate-based actions",
          "format": "int64",
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "timeout_ms": {
          "default": 15000,
          "description": "Per-action request timeout in milliseconds",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "window_allowlist": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Optional window title/process allowlist forwarded to sidecar policy",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "BrowserConfig": {
      "description": "Browser automation configuration (`[browser]` section).\n\nControls the `browser_open` tool and browser automation backends.",
      "properties": {
        "allowed_domains": {
          "default": [
            "*"
          ],
          "description": "Allowed domains for `browser_open` (exact or subdomain match)",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "allowed_private_hosts": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Private/internal hosts allowed to bypass SSRF protection.\nExact and subdomain matches are supported; `[\"*\"]` permits **all** private/local\nhosts (RFC 1918, loopback, link-local, `.local`). Default: empty (deny).\nListed hosts also bypass `allowed_domains`. Both the `browser` tool and\n`browser_open` accept `http://` for listed hosts — internal services\nfrequently lack a public TLS cert.\nWarning: `[\"*\"]` also reaches link-local addresses, including the cloud metadata\nendpoint (`169.254.169.254`) — list specific hosts unless you accept that exposure.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "backend": {
          "default": "agent_browser",
          "description": "Browser automation backend: \"agent_browser\" | \"rust_native\" | \"computer_use\" | \"auto\"",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "computer_use": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/BrowserComputerUseConfig",
          "default": {
            "allow_remote_endpoint": false,
            "api_key": null,
            "endpoint": "http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1/actions",
            "max_coordinate_x": null,
            "max_coordinate_y": null,
            "timeout_ms": 15000,
            "window_allowlist": []
          },
          "description": "Computer-use sidecar configuration"
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": true,
          "description": "Enable `browser_open` tool (opens URLs in the system browser without scraping)",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "headed": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Show browser window for agent_browser backend. When unset, inherits AGENT_BROWSER_HEADED.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "native_chrome_path": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Optional Chrome/Chromium executable path for rust-native backend",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "native_headless": {
          "default": true,
          "description": "Headless mode for rust-native backend",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "native_webdriver_url": {
          "default": "http://127.0.0.1:9515",
          "description": "WebDriver endpoint URL for rust-native backend (e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:9515`)",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "session_name": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Browser session name (for agent-browser automation)",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "BrowserDelegateConfig": {
      "properties": {
        "allowed_domains": {
          "default": [],
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "blocked_domains": {
          "default": [],
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "chrome_profile_dir": {
          "default": "",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "cli_binary": {
          "default": "claude",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "task_timeout_secs": {
          "default": 120,
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "BuiltinHooksConfig": {
      "properties": {
        "command_logger": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Enable the command-logger hook (logs tool calls for auditing).",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "webhook_audit": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/WebhookAuditConfig",
          "default": {
            "enabled": false,
            "include_args": false,
            "max_args_bytes": 4096,
            "tool_patterns": [],
            "url": ""
          },
          "description": "Configuration for the webhook-audit hook.\n\nWhen enabled, POSTs a JSON payload to `url` for every tool invocation\nthat matches one of `tool_patterns`."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },

        "uri": {

Leave unset to use the family's default URI from its `ModelEndpoint` impl. Set this to the FULL endpoint URL; there is no separate path-suffix field.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "vision": {
          "description": "Override the provider's vision (image input) capability.\n`None` (default) uses the provider family's built-in default. Several\nfamilies (llama.cpp, the generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint, etc.)\nassume vision-capable because they can serve multimodal models. Set\n`vision = false` for a text-only model served by such a family (e.g. a\ntext LLM behind llama.cpp) so image messages are routed to a configured\n`[multimodal] vision_model_provider` instead of being sent to a model\nthat rejects them. `Some(true)` forces vision on.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "wire_api": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/WireApi"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Wire protocol flavor: `responses` for OpenAI's Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`), `chat_completions` for the legacy chat wire and most OpenAI-compatible gateways. New OpenAI provider slots default to `responses`; other families default to chat-completions (or ignore the field). Only override if you're forcing an unusual combination."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "ChannelPrecheckConfig": {
      "description": "Per-channel reply-intent precheck configuration.",
      "properties": {
        "enabled": {
          "default": true,
          "description": "When false, the precheck is skipped entirely for this agent and every\naccepted channel message triggers the full agent loop. Default: `true`.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "default": 5,
          "description": "Hard ceiling (seconds) on the precheck LLM call. On timeout the\nprecheck fails open to REPLY. Default: `5`.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"

    "ChannelRef": {
      "description": "Reference to a configured `[channels.<type>.<alias>]` entry.\nEmpty value means \"no preference\" (opt-out). Non-empty values must\nresolve to a configured alias; `Config::validate()` enforces this.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "ChannelsConfig": {
      "description": "Top-level channel configurations (`[channels]` section).\n\neach channel type is a keyed table of named instances (aliases).\n`[channels.telegram.default]` is the conventional single-instance key.\nAccess via `config.channels.telegram.get(\"default\")`.",
