    "ClassificationRule": {
      "description": "A single classification rule mapping message patterns to a model hint.",
      "properties": {
        "hint": {
          "description": "Must match a `[[model_routes]]` hint value.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "keywords": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Case-insensitive substring matches.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "max_length": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Only match if message length <= N chars.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "min_length": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Only match if message length >= N chars.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "patterns": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Case-sensitive literal matches (for \"```\", \"fn \", etc.).",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "priority": {
          "default": 0,
          "description": "Higher priority rules are checked first.",
          "format": "int32",
          "type": "integer"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "hint"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    "ClaudeCodeConfig": {
      "description": "Claude Code CLI tool configuration (`[claude_code]` section).\n\nDelegates coding tasks to the `claude -p` CLI. Authentication uses the\nbinary's own OAuth session (Max subscription) by default — no API key\nneeded unless `env_passthrough` includes `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.",
      "properties": {
        "allowed_tools": {
          "default": [
            "Read",
            "Edit",
            "Bash",
            "Write"
          ],
          "description": "Claude Code tools the subprocess is allowed to use",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Enable the `claude_code` tool",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "env_passthrough": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Extra env vars passed to the claude subprocess (e.g. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY for API-key billing)",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "max_output_bytes": {
          "default": 2097152,
          "description": "Maximum output size in bytes (2MB default)",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "system_prompt": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Optional system prompt appended to Claude Code invocations",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "default": 600,
          "description": "Maximum execution time in seconds (coding tasks can be long)",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "ClaudeCodeRunnerConfig": {
      "description": "Claude Code task runner configuration (`[claude_code_runner]` section).\n\nSpawns Claude Code in a tmux session with HTTP hooks that POST tool\nexecution events back to ZeroClaw's gateway, updating a Slack message\nin-place with progress plus an SSH handoff link.",
      "properties": {
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Enable the `claude_code_runner` tool",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "session_ttl": {
          "default": 3600,
          "description": "Session time-to-live in seconds before auto-cleanup (default: 3600)",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "ssh_host": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "SSH host for session handoff links (e.g. \"myhost.example.com\")",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "tmux_prefix": {
          "default": "zc-claude-",
          "description": "Prefix for tmux session names (default: \"zc-claude-\")",
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "ClawdTalkConfig": {
      "properties": {
        "allowed_destinations": {
          "default": [],
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "api_key": {
          "type": "string"
        },
        "connection_id": {
          "type": "string"
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Whether this channel is active. The runtime only loads channels whose\n`enabled = true`. Default: `false` so an operator who pastes a partial\n`[channels.<type>.<alias>]` block doesn't accidentally bring a channel\nlive before the rest of its config is filled in.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "excluded_tools": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Tools excluded from this channel's tool spec. When set, these tools\nare not exposed to the model when responding via this channel.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "from_number": {
          "type": "string"
        },
        "webhook_secret": {
          "default": null,
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "api_key",
        "connection_id",
        "from_number"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    "CloudOpsConfig": {
      "description": "Controls the read-only cloud transformation analysis tools:\nIaC review, migration assessment, cost analysis, and architecture review.",
      "properties": {
        "cost_threshold_monthly_usd": {
          "default": 100.0,
          "description": "Monthly USD threshold to flag cost items. Default: 100.0.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        },
        "default_cloud": {
          "default": "aws",
          "description": "Default cloud model_provider for analysis context. Default: \"aws\".",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Enable cloud operations tools. Default: false.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "iac_tools": {
          "default": [
            "terraform"
          ],
          "description": "Supported IaC tools for review. Default: \\[`terraform`\\].",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "supported_clouds": {
          "default": [
            "aws",
            "azure",
            "gcp"
          ],
          "description": "Supported cloud model_providers. Default: [`aws`, `azure`, `gcp`].",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "well_architected_frameworks": {
          "default": [
            "aws-waf"
          ],
          "description": "Well-Architected Frameworks to check against. Default: \\[`aws-waf`\\].",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "CloudflareModelProviderConfig": {
      "description": "Named model_provider profile definition.",
      "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "description": "Secret API token for this model_provider. Grab it from the model_provider's dashboard (OpenAI platform, Anthropic console, OpenRouter keys page, etc.). Stored via the OS keyring when possible; never commit it to config.toml directly.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "chat_template_kwargs": {
          "description": "Arbitrary key/value pairs forwarded verbatim as `chat_template_kwargs`\nin the request body (llama.cpp-specific). Use this to pass model-family\ntemplate variables that control behaviour not exposed by other fields.\nExample (Qwen3 thinking suppression):\n  `chat_template_kwargs = { enable_thinking = false }`"
        },
        "context_window": {
          "description": "Context window size (max input tokens) for this model.\nAuto-populated on setup from provider's /models endpoint if available.\nOverride manually for custom endpoints or when auto-detection fails.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "extra_headers": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "description": "Extra HTTP headers sent with every request. Niche: used for auth bridges, corporate proxies, or custom gateways that demand a tracing header. Most users never touch this; edit `config.toml` directly if you need it.",
          "type": "object",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "fallback": {
          "description": "Ordered list of other provider aliases to try when every model on this\nalias has failed. Each entry is a dotted `<type>.<alias>` reference into\n`providers.models` and resolves with its own credentials, endpoint, and\nmodel. A fallback never inherits this alias's key. The walk is\ndepth-first: this alias's models are exhausted first, then each fallback\nalias is descended in turn (applying its own `fallback_models` and\n`fallback`). Empty means no provider-level fallback.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/ModelProviderRef"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "fallback_models": {
          "description": "Ordered alternate models to try on THIS provider before falling over to\nthe `fallback` aliases. Same endpoint, key, and headers as the primary\n`model`. Only the model identifier changes. Use this when a provider\nserves a backup model (e.g. a smaller or older variant) that should be\ntried before leaving the provider entirely. Empty means only `model` is\ntried.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "kind": {
          "description": "Provider implementation to instantiate for this profile. Use this\nwhen a canonical typed slot should run through a compatible\nimplementation, e.g. `[providers.models.openai.proxy] kind =\n\"openai-compatible\"`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "live_pricing": {
          "description": "Pull live token prices for this provider's models from its own\nOpenAI-compatible `/models` listing (the gateway is the source of truth\nfor its prices), filling cost-tracking rates for models the operator\nhas NOT priced under `[cost.rates]` / `pricing`. Models the gateway does\nnot price (or providers with no HTTP `/models` listing at all, such as\na subprocess gateway like `kilocli`) fall back to the public models.dev\ncatalog. Configured rates always win; live prices only fill gaps. A\nbackground task refreshes the price snapshot hourly; the cost-recording\npath reads the cached snapshot and never blocks on the network. Default\n`false`: off means no fetching and behavior identical to a build\nwithout the feature.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "max_tokens": {
          "description": "Hard cap on response length in tokens. Most models enforce sensible built-in limits already; leave unset unless you specifically need to clip long outputs for cost or latency reasons.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "merge_system_into_user": {
          "description": "ModelProvider-specific quirk: fold the system prompt into the first user message instead of sending a separate system role. Only needed for models that reject (or mishandle) a standalone system role, e.g. certain older Mistral variants.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "model": {
          "description": "Model identifier to send with each request: the ID string from the model_provider's catalog (e.g. `gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `llama-3.3-70b`). Must match a model the model_provider actually serves on this account.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "native_tools": {
          "description": "Override the provider's default for native tool calling.\n`None` (default) honors the provider's built-in choice. `Some(true)`\nforces native tool calls on, `Some(false)` forces text-fallback.\nCurrently consulted only by the Groq factory, which defaults to\ntext-fallback because llama-family Groq models reject native tool\ncalls with HTTP 400. Setting `native_tools = true` re-enables native\ntool calling for Groq models that support it.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "pricing": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "format": "double",
            "type": "number"
          },
          "description": "Per-model pricing for cost tracking, USD per 1M tokens.\n\nFree-form key/value map. Keys are user-defined model identifiers; an\noptional `.input` / `.output` suffix encodes pricing dimension when\nthe operator wants to split rates. A bare key without a suffix is\nused as a flat per-token rate when neither dimension is specified.\nDefault is empty: cost tracking falls back to \"unknown\" rates and\nonly token usage is recorded.\n\nExample: `pricing = { opus = 15.0, sonnet = 3.0 }`\nOr split: `pricing = { \"opus.input\" = 15.0, \"opus.output\" = 75.0 }`",
          "type": "object"
        },
        "provider_extra": {
          "description": "Extra JSON parameters to include in API requests.\nMerged at the top level of the request body, allowing provider-specific\nfeatures (routing, transforms, etc.) without code changes.\nExample: `provider_extra = { model_provider = { only = [\"Anthropic\"] } }`"
        },
        "replay_assistant_reasoning": {
          "description": "Whether stored assistant reasoning should be replayed on outbound\nassistant history messages. `Some(false)` strips `reasoning_content`\nand `reasoning` before sending. `None` (default) honours the provider's\nbuilt-in default (true for most compat providers, false for Groq).",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "requires_openai_auth": {
          "description": "When true, the client pulls credentials from ZeroClaw's stored `openai-codex` auth profile instead of the `api_key` field above. Import an existing Codex CLI login with `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json`, or run `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex`. Turn on only for the OpenAI Codex model_provider; leave off for standard API-key model_providers.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "temperature": {
          "description": "Sampling temperature passed to the model. Lower values (0.0–0.3) give\ndeterministic, near-verbatim output, which fits code, routing, summarization.\nHigher values (0.7–1.2) give more varied output, which fits open-ended chat.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "think": {
          "description": "Enable or disable chain-of-thought thinking for models that support it\n(e.g. Qwen3, GLM-4). `true` turns thinking on, `false` turns it off.\n`None` (default) lets the model decide. Forwarded as `enable_thinking`\nin the request body; mirrors the Ollama provider's `think` field.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "description": "HTTP request timeout in seconds. Bump this for slow local model_providers (Ollama on CPU, big local models) or high-latency networks; leave unset otherwise.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "tls_ca_cert_path": {
          "description": "Path to a PEM-encoded CA certificate for TLS connections to this provider.\nMust be an absolute path; shell expansion (e.g. `~`) is not performed.\nLeave unset to use the system's default trust store.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "uri": {
          "description": "Endpoint URI the client hits. Override the family's default endpoint when pointing at a self-hosted gateway (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama), a custom proxy, or any non-standard URL. Leave unset to use the family's default URI from its `ModelEndpoint` impl. Set this to the FULL endpoint URL; there is no separate path-suffix field.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "vision": {
          "description": "Override the provider's vision (image input) capability.\n`None` (default) uses the provider family's built-in default. Several\nfamilies (llama.cpp, the generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint, etc.)\nassume vision-capable because they can serve multimodal models. Set\n`vision = false` for a text-only model served by such a family (e.g. a\ntext LLM behind llama.cpp) so image messages are routed to a configured\n`[multimodal] vision_model_provider` instead of being sent to a model\nthat rejects them. `Some(true)` forces vision on.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "wire_api": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/WireApi"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Wire protocol flavor: `responses` for OpenAI's Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`), `chat_completions` for the legacy chat wire and most OpenAI-compatible gateways. New OpenAI provider slots default to `responses`; other families default to chat-completions (or ignore the field). Only override if you're forcing an unusual combination."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "CloudflareTunnelConfig": {
      "properties": {
        "token": {
          "default": "",
          "description": "Cloudflare Tunnel token (from Zero Trust dashboard)",
          "type": "string",
          "x-secret": true
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "CodexCliConfig": {
      "description": "Codex CLI tool configuration (`[codex_cli]` section).\n\nDelegates coding tasks to the `codex exec` CLI. Authentication uses the\nbinary's own session by default — no API key needed unless\n`env_passthrough` includes `OPENAI_API_KEY`.",
      "properties": {
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Enable the `codex_cli` tool",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "env_passthrough": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Extra env vars passed to the codex subprocess (e.g. OPENAI_API_KEY)",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "extra_args": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Extra CLI arguments appended to `codex exec` before the prompt.\n\nValues come from operator-controlled config (same trust level as\n`env_passthrough`) and are not validated — the operator is responsible\nfor understanding the implications of flags passed here.\n\n**Warning:** `--sandbox=danger-full-access` disables Codex's bubblewrap\nisolation; only use in environments where the container itself provides\nisolation (e.g. Kubernetes pods with restricted PSS).\n\nExample: `[\"--sandbox=danger-full-access\", \"--skip-git-repo-check\"]`",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "max_output_bytes": {
          "default": 2097152,
          "description": "Maximum output size in bytes (2MB default)",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "default": 600,
          "description": "Maximum execution time in seconds (coding tasks can be long)",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "CohereModelProviderConfig": {
      "description": "Named model_provider profile definition.",
      "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "description": "Secret API token for this model_provider. Grab it from the model_provider's dashboard (OpenAI platform, Anthropic console, OpenRouter keys page, etc.). Stored via the OS keyring when possible; never commit it to config.toml directly.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "chat_template_kwargs": {
          "description": "Arbitrary key/value pairs forwarded verbatim as `chat_template_kwargs`\nin the request body (llama.cpp-specific).           "description": "Context window size (max input tokens) for this model.\nAuto-populated on setup from provider's /models endpoint if available.\nOverride manually for custom endpoints or when auto-detection fails.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "extra_headers": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "description": "Extra HTTP headers sent with every request. Niche: used for auth bridges, corporate proxies, or custom gateways that demand a tracing header. Most users never touch this; edit `config.toml` directly if you need it.",
          "type": "object",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "fallback": {
          "description": "Ordered list of other provider aliases to try when every model on this\nalias has failed. The walk is\ndepth-first: this alias's models are exhausted first, then each fallback\nalias is descended in turn (applying its own `fallback_models` and\n`fallback`). Empty means no provider-level fallback.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/ModelProviderRef"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "fallback_models": {
          "description": "Ordered alternate models to try on THIS provider before falling over to\nthe `fallback` aliases. Same endpoint, key, and headers as the primary\n`model`. Only the model identifier changes. Use this when a provider\nserves a backup model (e.g. a smaller or older variant) that should be\ntried before leaving the provider entirely. Empty means only `model` is\ntried.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "kind": {
          "description": "Provider implementation to instantiate for this profile. Use this\nwhen a canonical typed slot should run through a compatible\nimplementation, e.g. `[providers.models.openai.proxy] kind =\n\"openai-compatible\"`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "live_pricing": {
          "description": "Pull live token prices for this provider's models from its own\nOpenAI-compatible `/models` listing (the gateway is the source of truth\nfor its prices), filling cost-tracking rates for models the operator\nhas NOT priced under `[cost.rates]` / `pricing`. Models the gateway does\nnot price (or providers with no HTTP `/models` listing at all, such as\na subprocess gateway like `kilocli`) fall back to the public models.dev\ncatalog. Configured rates always win; live prices only fill gaps. A\nbackground task refreshes the price snapshot hourly; the cost-recording\npath reads the cached snapshot and never blocks on the network. Default\n`false`: off means no fetching and behavior identical to a build\nwithout the feature.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "max_tokens": {
          "description": "Hard cap on response length in tokens. Most models enforce sensible built-in limits already; leave unset unless you specifically need to clip long outputs for cost or latency reasons.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "merge_system_into_user": {

          "type": "boolean"

          "description": "Model identifier to send with each request: the ID string from the model_provider's catalog (e.g. `gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `llama-3.3-70b`). Must match a model the model_provider actually serves on this account.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "native_tools": {
          "description": "Override the provider's default for native tool calling.\n`None` (default) honors the provider's built-in choice. `Some(true)`\nforces native tool calls on, `Some(false)` forces text-fallback.\nCurrently consulted only by the Groq factory, which defaults to\ntext-fallback because llama-family Groq models reject native tool\ncalls with HTTP 400. Setting `native_tools = true` re-enables native\ntool calling for Groq models that support it.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "pricing": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "format": "double",
            "type": "number"
          },
          "description": "Per-model pricing for cost tracking, USD per 1M tokens.\n\nFree-form key/value map. Keys are user-defined model identifiers; an\noptional `.input` / `.output` suffix encodes pricing dimension when\nthe operator wants to split rates. A bare key without a suffix is\nused as a flat per-token rate when neither dimension is specified.\nDefault is empty: cost tracking falls back to \"unknown\" rates and\nonly token usage is recorded.\n\nExample: `pricing = { opus = 15.0, sonnet = 3.0 }`\nOr split: `pricing = { \"opus.input\" = 15.0, \"opus.output\" = 75.0 }`",
          "type": "object"
        },
        "provider_extra": {
          "description": "Extra JSON parameters to include in API requests.\nMerged at the top level of the request body, allowing provider-specific\nfeatures (routing, transforms, etc.) without code changes.\nExample: `provider_extra = { model_provider = { only = [\"Anthropic\"] } }`"
        },
        "replay_assistant_reasoning": {
          "description": "Whether stored assistant reasoning should be replayed on outbound\nassistant history messages. `Some(false)` strips `reasoning_content`\nand `reasoning` before sending. `None` (default) honours the provider's\nbuilt-in default (true for most compat providers, false for Groq).",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "requires_openai_auth": {
          "description": "When true, the client pulls credentials from ZeroClaw's stored `openai-codex` auth profile instead of the `api_key` field above. Import an existing Codex CLI login with `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json`, or run `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex`. Turn on only for the OpenAI Codex model_provider; leave off for standard API-key model_providers.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "temperature": {
          "description": "Sampling temperature passed to the model. Lower values (0.0–0.3) give\ndeterministic, near-verbatim output, which fits code, routing, summarization.\nHigher values (0.7–1.2) give more varied output, which fits open-ended chat.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "think": {
          "description": "Enable or disable chain-of-thought thinking for models that support it\n(e.g. Qwen3, GLM-4). `true` turns thinking on, `false` turns it off.\n`None` (default) lets the model decide. Forwarded as `enable_thinking`\nin the request body; mirrors the Ollama provider's `think` field.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "description": "HTTP request timeout in seconds. Bump this for slow local model_providers (Ollama on CPU, big local models) or high-latency networks; leave unset otherwise.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "tls_ca_cert_path": {
          "description": "Path to a PEM-encoded CA certificate for TLS connections to this provider.\nMust be an absolute path; shell expansion (e.g. `~`) is not performed.\nLeave unset to use the system's default trust store.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "uri": {
          "description": "Endpoint URI the client hits. Override the family's default endpoint when pointing at a self-hosted gateway (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama), a custom proxy, or any non-standard URL. Leave unset to use the family's default URI from its `ModelEndpoint` impl. Set this to the FULL endpoint URL; there is no separate path-suffix field.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "vision": {
          "description": "Override the provider's vision (image input) capability.\n`None` (default) uses the provider family's built-in default. Several\nfamilies (llama.cpp, the generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint, etc.)\nassume vision-capable because they can serve multimodal models. Set\n`vision = false` for a text-only model served by such a family (e.g. a\ntext LLM behind llama.cpp) so image messages are routed to a configured\n`[multimodal] vision_model_provider` instead of being sent to a model\nthat rejects them. `Some(true)` forces vision on.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "wire_api": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/WireApi"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Wire protocol flavor: `responses` for OpenAI's Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`), `chat_completions` for the legacy chat wire and most OpenAI-compatible gateways. New OpenAI provider slots default to `responses`; other families default to chat-completions (or ignore the field). Only override if you're forcing an unusual combination."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "CostConfig": {
      "description": "Cost tracking and budget enforcement configuration (`[cost]` section).",
      "properties": {
        "allow_override": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Allow requests to exceed budget with --override flag (default: false)",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "daily_limit_usd": {
          "default": 10.0,
          "description": "Daily spending limit in USD (default: 10.00)",
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": true,
          "description": "Enable cost tracking (default: true)",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "enforcement": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/CostEnforcementConfig",
          "default": {
            "mode": "warn",
            "reserve_percent": 10,
            "route_down_model": null
          },
          "description": "Cost enforcement behavior when budget limits are approached or exceeded."
        },
        "monthly_limit_usd": {
          "default": 100.0,
          "description": "Monthly spending limit in USD (default: 100.00)",
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        },
        "rates": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/CostRatesConfig",
          "default": {
            "providers": {
              "models": {},
              "transcription": {},
              "tts": {}
            },
            "tools": {}
          },
          "description": "Operator-managed rate sheet at `[cost.rates.*]`. Sections mirror\nthe `[providers.*]` dotted-path exactly with the trailing `alias`\nsegment replaced by the resource the rate applies to (model id,\ntool name, …). Layout:\n\n```toml\n[cost.rates.providers.models.anthropic.\"claude-opus-4-7\"]\ninput_per_mtok = 15.0\noutput_per_mtok = 75.0\ncached_input_per_mtok = 1.5\n\n[cost.rates.providers.tts.openai.\"tts-1-hd\"]\nper_mchar = 30.0\n\n[cost.rates.providers.transcription.openai.whisper-1]\nper_minute = 0.006\n\n[cost.rates.tools.web_search]\nper_call = 0.005\n```"
        },
        "track_per_agent": {
          "default": true,
          "description": "Stamp each recorded cost entry with the originating agent alias so\n`/api/cost?agent=<alias>` and CLI rollups can attribute spend to a\nspecific agent. Disable on high-volume deployments if the extra\nHashMap aggregation shows up in profiles (default: true).",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "warn_at_percent": {
          "default": 80,
          "description": "Warn when spending reaches this percentage of limit (default: 80)",
          "format": "uint8",
          "maximum": 255,
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "CostEnforcementConfig": {
      "description": "Configuration for cost enforcement behavior when budget limits are reached.",
      "properties": {
        "mode": {
          "default": "warn",
          "description": "Enforcement mode: \"warn\", \"block\", or \"route_down\".",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "reserve_percent": {
          "default": 10,
          "description": "Reserve this percentage of budget for critical operations.",
          "format": "uint8",
          "maximum": 255,
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "route_down_model": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Model hint to route to when budget is exceeded (used with \"route_down\" mode).",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "CostRatesConfig": {
      "description": "`[cost.rates]` — top-level rate-sheet namespace. Mirrors the\n`[providers.*]` shape so each subsection here points at the same\nkind of resource its `[providers.*]` counterpart configures.",
      "properties": {
        "providers": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/ProviderCostRates",
          "default": {
            "models": {},
            "transcription": {},
            "tts": {}
          },
          "description": "`[cost.rates.providers.*]` — rates for everything under\n`[providers.*]` (models, TTS, transcription, …)."
        },
        "tools": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/ToolCostRates"
          },
          "default": {},
          "description": "`[cost.rates.tools.<name>]` — per-call rates for tools that\nhit paid APIs. Keyed by the tool's registered name.",
          "type": "object"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "CronJobDecl": {
      "description": "A declarative cron job definition (`[cron.<alias>]`).\n\nStored alias-keyed on `Config.cron`. The map key serves as the stable job id.\nSynced into the database at scheduler startup with `source = \"declarative\"`,\ndistinguishing them from jobs created imperatively via CLI or API.\nDeclarative config takes precedence on each sync: if the config changes,\nthe DB is updated to match. Imperative jobs are never deleted by sync.",
      "properties": {
        "allowed_tools": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Optional allowlist of tool names for agent jobs. When omitted, scheduler\ndefaults may still exclude scheduler mutation tools for cron agent jobs.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": [
            "array",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "command": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Shell command to run (required when `job_type = \"shell\"`).",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "delivery": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/DeliveryConfigDecl"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "default": null,
          "description": "Delivery configuration."
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": true,
          "description": "Whether the job is enabled. Default: `true`.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "job_type": {
          "default": "shell",
          "description": "Job type: `\"shell\"` (default) or `\"agent\"`.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "model": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Model override for agent jobs.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "name": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Human-readable name.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "prompt": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Agent prompt (required when `job_type = \"agent\"`).",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "schedule": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/CronScheduleDecl",
          "default": {
            "expr": "",
            "kind": "cron",
            "tz": null
          },
          "description": "Schedule for the job."
        },
        "session_target": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Session target: `\"isolated\"` (default) or `\"main\"`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "shell_output_format": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/CronShellOutputFormat",
          "default": "wrapped",
          "description": "Output format for shell jobs: `\"wrapped\"` (default) or `\"raw\"`.\n\n- `\"wrapped\"` (default): returns stdout and stderr wrapped in a\n  `status=... / stdout: / stderr:` envelope.\n- `\"raw\"`: returns trimmed stdout when the process exits zero. A\n  non-zero process exit still gets the wrapped status/stdout/stderr\n  envelope for diagnosis. Failures that never reach a process exit —\n  a security-policy denial, a shell setup/spawn failure, or a\n  timeout — return a plain error string in either format."
        },
        "uses_memory": {
          "default": true,
          "description": "Whether to recall and inject memory context before this agent job runs.\nDefaults to `true`; set to `false` for stateless digest jobs.",
          "type": "boolean"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "CronScheduleDecl": {
      "description": "Schedule variant for declarative cron jobs.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "description": "Classic cron expression.",
          "properties": {
            "expr": {
              "type": "string"
            },
            "kind": {
              "const": "cron",
              "type": "string"
            },
            "tz": {
              "default": null,
              "type": [
                "string",
                "null"
              ]
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind",
            "expr"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        },
        {
          "description": "Interval in milliseconds.",
          "properties": {
            "every_ms": {
              "format": "uint64",
              "minimum": 0,
              "type": "integer"
            },
            "kind": {
              "const": "every",
              "type": "string"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind",
            "every_ms"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        },
        {
          "description": "One-shot at an RFC 3339 timestamp.",
          "properties": {
            "at": {
              "type": "string"
            },
            "kind": {
              "const": "at",
              "type": "string"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind",
            "at"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        }
      ]
    },
    "CronShellOutputFormat": {
      "description": "Output format for shell cron job stdout.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "wrapped",
          "description": "Wrapped format: `status=...\\nstdout:\\n...\\nstderr:\\n...` (default).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "raw",
          "description": "Raw stdout on a zero process exit; wrapped status/stdout/stderr on a\nnon-zero exit; a plain error string for failures that never reach a\nprocess exit (security denial, spawn/setup failure, timeout).",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    },
    "CustomModelProviderConfig": {
      "description": "Named model_provider profile definition.",
      "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "description": "Secret API token for this model_provider. Grab it from the model_provider's dashboard (OpenAI platform, Anthropic console, OpenRouter keys page, etc.). Stored via the OS keyring when possible; never commit it to config.toml directly.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "chat_template_kwargs": {
          "description": "Arbitrary key/value pairs forwarded verbatim as `chat_template_kwargs`\nin the request body (llama.cpp-specific). Use this to pass model-family\ntemplate variables that control behaviour not exposed by other fields.\nExample (Qwen3 thinking suppression):\n  `chat_template_kwargs = { enable_thinking = false }`"
        },
        "context_window": {
          "description": "Context window size (max input tokens) for this model.\nAuto-populated on setup from provider's /models endpoint if available.\nOverride manually for custom endpoints or when auto-detection fails.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "extra_headers": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "description": "Extra HTTP headers sent with every request. Niche: used for auth bridges, corporate proxies, or custom gateways that demand a tracing header. Most users never touch this; edit `config.toml` directly if you need it.",
          "type": "object",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "fallback": {
          "description": "Ordered list of other provider aliases to try when every model on this\nalias has failed. Each entry is a dotted `<type>.<alias>` reference into\n`providers.models` and resolves with its own credentials, endpoint, and\nmodel. A fallback never inherits this alias's key. The walk is\ndepth-first: this alias's models are exhausted first, then each fallback\nalias is descended in turn (applying its own `fallback_models` and\n`fallback`). Empty means no provider-level fallback.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/ModelProviderRef"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "fallback_models": {
          "description": "Ordered alternate models to try on THIS provider before falling over to\nthe `fallback` aliases. Same endpoint, key, and headers as the primary\n`model`. Only the model identifier changes. Use this when a provider\nserves a backup model (e.g. a smaller or older variant) that should be\ntried before leaving the provider entirely. Empty means only `model` is\ntried.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "kind": {
          "description": "Provider implementation to instantiate for this profile. Use this\nwhen a canonical typed slot should run through a compatible\nimplementation, e.g. `[providers.models.openai.proxy] kind =\n\"openai-compatible\"`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "live_pricing": {
          "description": "Pull live token prices for this provider's models from its own\nOpenAI-compatible `/models` listing (the gateway is the source of truth\nfor its prices), filling cost-tracking rates for models the operator\nhas NOT priced under `[cost.rates]` / `pricing`. Models the gateway does\nnot price (or providers with no HTTP `/models` listing at all, such as\na subprocess gateway like `kilocli`) fall back to the public models.dev\ncatalog. Configured rates always win; live prices only fill gaps. A\nbackground task refreshes the price snapshot hourly; the cost-recording\npath reads the cached snapshot and never blocks on the network. Default\n`false`: off means no fetching and behavior identical to a build\nwithout the feature.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "max_tokens": {
          "description": "Hard cap on response length in tokens. Most models enforce sensible built-in limits already; leave unset unless you specifically need to clip long outputs for cost or latency reasons.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "merge_system_into_user": {
          "description": "ModelProvider-specific quirk: fold the system prompt into the first user message instead of sending a separate system role. Only needed for models that reject (or mishandle) a standalone system role, e.g. certain older Mistral variants.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "model": {
          "description": "Model identifier to send with each request: the ID string from the model_provider's catalog (e.g. `gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `llama-3.3-70b`). Must match a model the model_provider actually serves on this account.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },

Setting `native_tools = true` re-enables native\ntool calling for Groq models that support it.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "pricing": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "format": "double",
            "type": "number"
          },
          "description": "Per-model pricing for cost tracking, USD per 1M tokens.\n\nFree-form key/value map. Keys are user-defined model identifiers; an\noptional `.input` / `.output` suffix encodes pricing dimension when\nthe operator wants to split rates. A bare key without a suffix is\nused as a flat per-token rate when neither dimension is specified.\nDefault is empty: cost tracking falls back to \"unknown\" rates and\nonly token usage is recorded.\n\nExample: `pricing = { opus = 15.0, sonnet = 3.0 }`\nOr split: `pricing = { \"opus.input\" = 15.0, \"opus.output\" = 75.0 }`",

        },

Import an existing Codex CLI login with `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json`, or run `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex`.           "type": "boolean"

          "format": "double",

      "type": "object"
    },
    "DataRetentionConfig": {
      "description": "Data retention and purge configuration (`[data_retention]` section).",
      "properties": {
        "categories": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Limit retention enforcement to specific data categories (empty = all).",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "dry_run": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Preview what would be deleted without actually removing anything.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Enable the `data_management` tool.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "retention_days": {
          "default": 90,
          "description": "Days of data to retain before purge eligibility.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "DeepgramSttConfig": {
      "description": "Deepgram STT model_provider configuration (`[transcription.deepgram]`).",
      "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Deepgram API key.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "model": {
          "default": "nova-2",
          "description": "Deepgram model name (default: \"nova-2\").",
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "DeepgramTranscriptionProviderConfig": {
      "description": "Shared base for cloud transcription providers. Each cloud family\ncomposes this via `#[serde(flatten)] base: TranscriptionProviderConfig`.",
      "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "API key for the transcription provider.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "initial_prompt": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Whisper-style initial prompt to bias the model toward expected\nvocabulary (proper nouns, technical terms). Provider-specific support;\nsilently ignored where not applicable.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "language": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Optional language hint passed to the provider (ISO-639-1 like `\"en\"` /\n`\"ru\"`, or BCP-47 like `\"en-US\"` for Google). Most providers auto-detect\nwhen this is unset.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "model": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Deepgram model name (default: `\"nova-2\"`).",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "DeepinfraModelProviderConfig": {
      "description": "Named model_provider profile definition.",
      "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "description": "Secret API token for this model_provider. Grab it from the model_provider's dashboard (OpenAI platform, Anthropic console, OpenRouter keys page, etc.). Stored via the OS keyring when possible; never commit it to config.toml directly.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "chat_template_kwargs": {
          "description": "Arbitrary key/value pairs forwarded verbatim as `chat_template_kwargs`\nin the request body (llama.cpp-specific). Use this to pass model-family\ntemplate variables that control behaviour not exposed by other fields.\nExample (Qwen3 thinking suppression):\n  `chat_template_kwargs = { enable_thinking = false }`"
        },
        "context_window": {
          "description": "Context window size (max input tokens) for this model.\nAuto-populated on setup from provider's /models endpoint if available.\nOverride manually for custom endpoints or when auto-detection fails.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "extra_headers": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "description": "Extra HTTP headers sent with every request. Niche: used for auth bridges, corporate proxies, or custom gateways that demand a tracing header. Most users never touch this; edit `config.toml` directly if you need it.",
          "type": "object",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "fallback": {
          "description": "Ordered list of other provider aliases to try when every model on this\nalias has failed. Each entry is a dotted `<type>.<alias>` reference into\n`providers.models` and resolves with its own credentials, endpoint, and\nmodel. A fallback never inherits this alias's key. The walk is\ndepth-first: this alias's models are exhausted first, then each fallback\nalias is descended in turn (applying its own `fallback_models` and\n`fallback`). Empty means no provider-level fallback.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/ModelProviderRef"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "fallback_models": {
          "description": "Ordered alternate models to try on THIS provider before falling over to\nthe `fallback` aliases. Same endpoint, key, and headers as the primary\n`model`. Only the model identifier changes. Use this when a provider\nserves a backup model (e.g. a smaller or older variant) that should be\ntried before leaving the provider entirely. Empty means only `model` is\ntried.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "kind": {
          "description": "Provider implementation to instantiate for this profile. Use this\nwhen a canonical typed slot should run through a compatible\nimplementation, e.g. `[providers.models.openai.proxy] kind =\n\"openai-compatible\"`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "live_pricing": {
          "description": "Pull live token prices for this provider's models from its own\nOpenAI-compatible `/models` listing (the gateway is the source of truth\nfor its prices), filling cost-tracking rates for models the operator\nhas NOT priced under `[cost.rates]` / `pricing`. Models the gateway does\nnot price (or providers with no HTTP `/models` listing at all, such as\na subprocess gateway like `kilocli`) fall back to the public models.dev\ncatalog. Configured rates always win; live prices only fill gaps. A\nbackground task refreshes the price snapshot hourly; the cost-recording\npath reads the cached snapshot and never blocks on the network. Default\n`false`: off means no fetching and behavior identical to a build\nwithout the feature.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "max_tokens": {
          "description": "Hard cap on response length in tokens. Most models enforce sensible built-in limits already; leave unset unless you specifically need to clip long outputs for cost or latency reasons.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "merge_system_into_user": {
          "description": "ModelProvider-specific quirk: fold the system prompt into the first user message instead of sending a separate system role. Only needed for models that reject (or mishandle) a standalone system role, e.g. certain older Mistral variants.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "model": {
          "description": "Model identifier to send with each request: the ID string from the model_provider's catalog (e.g. `gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `llama-3.3-70b`). Must match a model the model_provider actually serves on this account.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "native_tools": {
          "description": "Override the provider's default for native tool calling.\n`None` (default) honors the provider's built-in choice. `Some(true)`\nforces native tool calls on, `Some(false)` forces text-fallback.\nCurrently consulted only by the Groq factory, which defaults to\ntext-fallback because llama-family Groq models reject native tool\ncalls with HTTP 400. Setting `native_tools = true` re-enables native\ntool calling for Groq models that support it.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "pricing": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "format": "double",
            "type": "number"
          },
          "description": "Per-model pricing for cost tracking, USD per 1M tokens.\n\nFree-form key/value map. Keys are user-defined model identifiers; an\noptional `.input` / `.output` suffix encodes pricing dimension when\nthe operator wants to split rates. A bare key without a suffix is\nused as a flat per-token rate when neither dimension is specified.\nDefault is empty: cost tracking falls back to \"unknown\" rates and\nonly token usage is recorded.\n\nExample: `pricing = { opus = 15.0, sonnet = 3.0 }`\nOr split: `pricing = { \"opus.input\" = 15.0, \"opus.output\" = 75.0 }`",
          "type": "object"
        },
        "provider_extra": {
          "description": "Extra JSON parameters to include in API requests.\nMerged at the top level of the request body, allowing provider-specific\nfeatures (routing, transforms, etc.) without code changes.\nExample: `provider_extra = { model_provider = { only = [\"Anthropic\"] } }`"
        },
        "replay_assistant_reasoning": {
          "description": "Whether stored assistant reasoning should be replayed on outbound\nassistant history messages. `Some(false)` strips `reasoning_content`\nand `reasoning` before sending. `None` (default) honours the provider's\nbuilt-in default (true for most compat providers, false for Groq).",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "requires_openai_auth": {
          "description": "When true, the client pulls credentials from ZeroClaw's stored `openai-codex` auth profile instead of the `api_key` field above. Import an existing Codex CLI login with `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json`, or run `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex`. Turn on only for the OpenAI Codex model_provider; leave off for standard API-key model_providers.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "temperature": {
          "description": "Sampling temperature passed to the model. Lower values (0.0–0.3) give\ndeterministic, near-verbatim output, which fits code, routing, summarization.\nHigher values (0.7–1.2) give more varied output, which fits open-ended chat.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "think": {
          "description": "Enable or disable chain-of-thought thinking for models that support it\n(e.g. Qwen3, GLM-4). `true` turns thinking on, `false` turns it off.\n`None` (default) lets the model decide. Forwarded as `enable_thinking`\nin the request body; mirrors the Ollama provider's `think` field.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "description": "HTTP request timeout in seconds. Bump this for slow local model_providers (Ollama on CPU, big local models) or high-latency networks; leave unset otherwise.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "tls_ca_cert_path": {
          "description": "Path to a PEM-encoded CA certificate for TLS connections to this provider.\nMust be an absolute path; shell expansion (e.g. `~`) is not performed.\nLeave unset to use the system's default trust store.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "uri": {
          "description": "Endpoint URI the client hits. Override the family's default endpoint when pointing at a self-hosted gateway (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama), a custom proxy, or any non-standard URL. Leave unset to use the family's default URI from its `ModelEndpoint` impl. Set this to the FULL endpoint URL; there is no separate path-suffix field.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "vision": {
          "description": "Override the provider's vision (image input) capability.\n`None` (default) uses the provider family's built-in default. Several\nfamilies (llama.cpp, the generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint, etc.)\nassume vision-capable because they can serve multimodal models. Set\n`vision = false` for a text-only model served by such a family (e.g. a\ntext LLM behind llama.cpp) so image messages are routed to a configured\n`[multimodal] vision_model_provider` instead of being sent to a model\nthat rejects them. `Some(true)` forces vision on.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "wire_api": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/WireApi"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Wire protocol flavor: `responses` for OpenAI's Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`), `chat_completions` for the legacy chat wire and most OpenAI-compatible gateways. New OpenAI provider slots default to `responses`; other families default to chat-completions (or ignore the field). Only override if you're forcing an unusual combination."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
