          ],
          "description": "Wire protocol flavor: `responses` for OpenAI's Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`), `chat_completions` for the legacy chat wire and most OpenAI-compatible gateways. New OpenAI provider slots default to `responses`; other families default to chat-completions (or ignore the field). Only override if you're forcing an unusual combination."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "FriendliModelProviderConfig": {
      "description": "Named model_provider profile definition.",
      "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "description": "Secret API token for this model_provider. Grab it from the model_provider's dashboard (OpenAI platform, Anthropic console, OpenRouter keys page, etc.). Stored via the OS keyring when possible; never commit it to config.toml directly.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "chat_template_kwargs": {
          "description": "Arbitrary key/value pairs forwarded verbatim as `chat_template_kwargs`\nin the request body (llama.cpp-specific). Use this to pass model-family\ntemplate variables that control behaviour not exposed by other fields.\nExample (Qwen3 thinking suppression):\n  `chat_template_kwargs = { enable_thinking = false }`"
        },
        "context_window": {
          "description": "Context window size (max input tokens) for this model.\nAuto-populated on setup from provider's /models endpoint if available.\nOverride manually for custom endpoints or when auto-detection fails.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "extra_headers": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "description": "Extra HTTP headers sent with every request. Niche: used for auth bridges, corporate proxies, or custom gateways that demand a tracing header. Most users never touch this; edit `config.toml` directly if you need it.",
          "type": "object",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "fallback": {
          "description": "Ordered list of other provider aliases to try when every model on this\nalias has failed. Each entry is a dotted `<type>.<alias>` reference into\n`providers.models` and resolves with its own credentials, endpoint, and\nmodel. A fallback never inherits this alias's key. The walk is\ndepth-first: this alias's models are exhausted first, then each fallback\nalias is descended in turn (applying its own `fallback_models` and\n`fallback`). Empty means no provider-level fallback.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/ModelProviderRef"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "fallback_models": {
          "description": "Ordered alternate models to try on THIS provider before falling over to\nthe `fallback` aliases. Same endpoint, key, and headers as the primary\n`model`. Only the model identifier changes. Use this when a provider\nserves a backup model (e.g. a smaller or older variant) that should be\ntried before leaving the provider entirely. Empty means only `model` is\ntried.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "kind": {
          "description": "Provider implementation to instantiate for this profile. Use this\nwhen a canonical typed slot should run through a compatible\nimplementation, e.g. `[providers.models.openai.proxy] kind =\n\"openai-compatible\"`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "live_pricing": {
          "description": "Pull live token prices for this provider's models from its own\nOpenAI-compatible `/models` listing (the gateway is the source of truth\nfor its prices), filling cost-tracking rates for models the operator\nhas NOT priced under `[cost.rates]` / `pricing`. Models the gateway does\nnot price (or providers with no HTTP `/models` listing at all, such as\na subprocess gateway like `kilocli`) fall back to the public models.dev\ncatalog. Configured rates always win; live prices only fill gaps. A\nbackground task refreshes the price snapshot hourly; the cost-recording\npath reads the cached snapshot and never blocks on the network. Default\n`false`: off means no fetching and behavior identical to a build\nwithout the feature.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "max_tokens": {
          "description": "Hard cap on response length in tokens. Most models enforce sensible built-in limits already; leave unset unless you specifically need to clip long outputs for cost or latency reasons.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "merge_system_into_user": {
          "description": "ModelProvider-specific quirk: fold the system prompt into the first user message instead of sending a separate system role. Only needed for models that reject (or mishandle) a standalone system role, e.g. certain older Mistral variants.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "model": {
          "description": "Model identifier to send with each request: the ID string from the model_provider's catalog (e.g. `gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `llama-3.3-70b`). Must match a model the model_provider actually serves on this account.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "native_tools": {
          "description": "Override the provider's default for native tool calling.\n`None` (default) honors the provider's built-in choice. `Some(true)`\nforces native tool calls on, `Some(false)` forces text-fallback.\nCurrently consulted only by the Groq factory, which defaults to\ntext-fallback because llama-family Groq models reject native tool\ncalls with HTTP 400. Setting `native_tools = true` re-enables native\ntool calling for Groq models that support it.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "pricing": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "format": "double",
            "type": "number"
          },
          "description": "Per-model pricing for cost tracking, USD per 1M tokens.\n\nFree-form key/value map. Keys are user-defined model identifiers; an\noptional `.input` / `.output` suffix encodes pricing dimension when\nthe operator wants to split rates. A bare key without a suffix is\nused as a flat per-token rate when neither dimension is specified.\nDefault is empty: cost tracking falls back to \"unknown\" rates and\nonly token usage is recorded.\n\nExample: `pricing = { opus = 15.0, sonnet = 3.0 }`\nOr split: `pricing = { \"opus.input\" = 15.0, \"opus.output\" = 75.0 }`",
          "type": "object"
        },
        "provider_extra": {
          "description": "Extra JSON parameters to include in API requests.\nMerged at the top level of the request body, allowing provider-specific\nfeatures (routing, transforms, etc.) without code changes.\nExample: `provider_extra = { model_provider = { only = [\"Anthropic\"] } }`"
        },
        "replay_assistant_reasoning": {
          "description": "Whether stored assistant reasoning should be replayed on outbound\nassistant history messages. `Some(false)` strips `reasoning_content`\nand `reasoning` before sending. `None` (default) honours the provider's\nbuilt-in default (true for most compat providers, false for Groq).",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "requires_openai_auth": {
          "description": "When true, the client pulls credentials from ZeroClaw's stored `openai-codex` auth profile instead of the `api_key` field above. Import an existing Codex CLI login with `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json`, or run `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex`. Turn on only for the OpenAI Codex model_provider; leave off for standard API-key model_providers.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "temperature": {
          "description": "Sampling temperature passed to the model. Lower values (0.0–0.3) give\ndeterministic, near-verbatim output, which fits code, routing, summarization.\nHigher values (0.7–1.2) give more varied output, which fits open-ended chat.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "think": {
          "description": "Enable or disable chain-of-thought thinking for models that support it\n(e.g. Qwen3, GLM-4). `true` turns thinking on, `false` turns it off.\n`None` (default) lets the model decide. Forwarded as `enable_thinking`\nin the request body; mirrors the Ollama provider's `think` field.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "description": "HTTP request timeout in seconds. Bump this for slow local model_providers (Ollama on CPU, big local models) or high-latency networks; leave unset otherwise.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "tls_ca_cert_path": {
          "description": "Path to a PEM-encoded CA certificate for TLS connections to this provider.\nMust be an absolute path; shell expansion (e.g. `~`) is not performed.\nLeave unset to use the system's default trust store.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "uri": {
          "description": "Endpoint URI the client hits. Override the family's default endpoint when pointing at a self-hosted gateway (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama), a custom proxy, or any non-standard URL. Leave unset to use the family's default URI from its `ModelEndpoint` impl. Set this to the FULL endpoint URL; there is no separate path-suffix field.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "vision": {
          "description": "Override the provider's vision (image input) capability.\n`None` (default) uses the provider family's built-in default. Several\nfamilies (llama.cpp, the generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint, etc.)\nassume vision-capable because they can serve multimodal models. Set\n`vision = false` for a text-only model served by such a family (e.g. a\ntext LLM behind llama.cpp) so image messages are routed to a configured\n`[multimodal] vision_model_provider` instead of being sent to a model\nthat rejects them. `Some(true)` forces vision on.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "wire_api": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/WireApi"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Wire protocol flavor: `responses` for OpenAI's Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`), `chat_completions` for the legacy chat wire and most OpenAI-compatible gateways. New OpenAI provider slots default to `responses`; other families default to chat-completions (or ignore the field). Only override if you're forcing an unusual combination."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "GatewayClientAuthConfig": {
      "description": "Client certificate authentication (mTLS) configuration (`[gateway.tls.client_auth]`).",
      "properties": {
        "ca_cert_path": {
          "default": "",
          "description": "Path to the PEM-encoded CA certificate used to verify client certs.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Enable client certificate verification (default: false).",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "pinned_certs": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Optional SHA-256 fingerprints for certificate pinning.\nWhen non-empty, only client certs matching one of these fingerprints are accepted.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "require_client_cert": {
          "default": true,
          "description": "Reject connections that do not present a valid client certificate (default: true).",
          "type": "boolean"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "GatewayConfig": {
      "description": "Gateway server configuration (`[gateway]` section).\n\nControls the HTTP gateway for webhook and pairing endpoints.",
      "properties": {
        "allow_public_bind": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Allow binding to non-localhost without a tunnel (default: false)",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "allow_remote_admin": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Allow authenticated remote callers to use admin endpoints that are\notherwise localhost-only. Currently this gates `POST /admin/reload`.\nWhen false (default), those endpoints reject any non-loopback peer.\nWhen true, a non-loopback request is accepted only if it also passes\npairing authentication — which requires `require_pairing = true`; with\npairing off a remote caller cannot be authenticated and is rejected, so\nthis flag never exposes an anonymous remote reload. `/admin/shutdown`\nand the pairing-code endpoints stay localhost-only regardless.\n(default: false)",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "allow_self_upgrade": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Allow triggering a self-upgrade (binary swap via `zeroclaw update`) from\nthe dashboard. This is a remote-code-execution-adjacent surface: any\nauthenticated dashboard user could replace the running binary. Keep off\nunless you trust every paired client. (default: false)",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "check_updates": {
          "default": true,
          "description": "Poll GitHub for newer releases and show an \"update available\" indicator\non the dashboard version tag. Read-only; does not install anything.\n(default: true)",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "host": {
          "default": "127.0.0.1",
          "description": "Gateway host (default: 127.0.0.1)",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "idempotency_max_keys": {
          "default": 10000,
          "description": "Maximum distinct idempotency keys retained in memory.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "idempotency_ttl_secs": {
          "default": 300,
          "description": "TTL for webhook idempotency keys.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "long_running_request_timeout_secs": {
          "default": 600,
          "description": "HTTP request timeout (seconds) for `POST /api/cron/{id}/run`, which\nruns jobs synchronously and routinely exceeds the 30s default.\nDefault: 600s (10 minutes).",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "pair_rate_limit_per_minute": {
          "default": 10,
          "description": "Max `/pair` requests per minute per client key.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "paired_tokens": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Paired bearer tokens (managed automatically, not user-edited)",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "pairing_dashboard": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/PairingDashboardConfig",
          "default": {
            "code_length": 8,
            "code_ttl_secs": 3600,
            "lockout_secs": 300,
            "max_failed_attempts": 5,
            "max_pending_codes": 3
          },
          "description": "Pairing dashboard configuration"
        },
        "path_prefix": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Optional URL path prefix for reverse-proxy deployments.\nWhen set, all gateway routes are served under this prefix.\nMust start with `/` and must not end with `/`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "port": {
          "default": 42617,
          "description": "Gateway port (default: 42617)",
          "format": "uint16",
          "maximum": 65535,
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "rate_limit_max_keys": {
          "default": 10000,
          "description": "Maximum distinct client keys tracked by gateway rate limiter maps.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "request_timeout_secs": {
          "default": 30,
          "description": "HTTP request timeout (seconds) for gateway routes other than the\nlong-running cron-trigger endpoint. Default: 30s.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "require_pairing": {
          "default": true,
          "description": "Require pairing before accepting requests (default: true)",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "session_persistence": {
          "default": true,
          "description": "Persist gateway WebSocket chat sessions to SQLite. Default: true.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "session_ttl_hours": {
          "default": 0,
          "description": "Auto-archive stale gateway sessions older than N hours. 0 = disabled. Default: 0.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "tls": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/GatewayTlsConfig"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "default": null,
          "description": "TLS configuration for the gateway server (`[gateway.tls]`)."
        },
        "trust_forwarded_headers": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Trust proxy-forwarded client IP headers (`X-Forwarded-For`, `X-Real-IP`).\nDisabled by default; enable only behind a trusted reverse proxy.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "web_dist_dir": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Path to the web dashboard `dist` directory. When set, the gateway\nserves the compiled frontend from the filesystem instead of requiring\nit to be embedded in the binary. Accepts absolute paths or paths\nrelative to the working directory. When omitted the gateway runs in\nAPI-only mode (no web dashboard) unless auto-detection finds it.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "webhook_rate_limit_per_minute": {
          "default": 60,
          "description": "Max `/webhook` requests per minute per client key.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "GatewayTlsConfig": {
      "description": "TLS configuration for the gateway server (`[gateway.tls]`).",
      "properties": {
        "cert_path": {
          "description": "Path to the PEM-encoded server certificate file.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "client_auth": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/GatewayClientAuthConfig"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "default": null,
          "description": "Client certificate authentication (mutual TLS) settings."
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Enable TLS for the gateway (default: false).",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "key_path": {
          "description": "Path to the PEM-encoded server private key file.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "cert_path",
        "key_path"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    "GeminiCliConfig": {
      "description": "Gemini CLI tool configuration (`[gemini_cli]` section).\n\nDelegates coding tasks to the `gemini -p` CLI. Authentication uses the\nbinary's own session by default — no API key needed unless\n`env_passthrough` includes `GOOGLE_API_KEY`.",
      "properties": {
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Enable the `gemini_cli` tool",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "env_passthrough": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Extra env vars passed to the gemini subprocess (e.g. GOOGLE_API_KEY)",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "max_output_bytes": {
          "default": 2097152,
          "description": "Maximum output size in bytes (2MB default)",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "default": 600,
          "description": "Maximum execution time in seconds (coding tasks can be long)",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },

Import an existing Codex CLI login with `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json`, or run `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex`. Turn on only for the OpenAI Codex model_provider; leave off for standard API-key model_providers.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "temperature": {
          "description": "Sampling temperature passed to the model. Lower values (0.0–0.3) give\ndeterministic, near-verbatim output, which fits code, routing, summarization.\nHigher values (0.7–1.2) give more varied output, which fits open-ended chat.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "think": {
          "description": "Enable or disable chain-of-thought thinking for models that support it\n(e.g. Qwen3, GLM-4). `true` turns thinking on, `false` turns it off.\n`None` (default) lets the model decide. Forwarded as `enable_thinking`\nin the request body; mirrors the Ollama provider's `think` field.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "description": "HTTP request timeout in seconds. Bump this for slow local model_providers (Ollama on CPU, big local models) or high-latency networks; leave unset otherwise.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "tls_ca_cert_path": {
          "description": "Path to a PEM-encoded CA certificate for TLS connections to this provider.\nMust be an absolute path; shell expansion (e.g. `~`) is not performed.\nLeave unset to use the system's default trust store.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "uri": {
          "description": "Endpoint URI the client hits. Override the family's default endpoint when pointing at a self-hosted gateway (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama), a custom proxy, or any non-standard URL. Leave unset to use the family's default URI from its `ModelEndpoint` impl. Set this to the FULL endpoint URL; there is no separate path-suffix field.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "vision": {
          "description": "Override the provider's vision (image input) capability.\n`None` (default) uses the provider family's built-in default. Several\nfamilies (llama.cpp, the generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint, etc.)\nassume vision-capable because they can serve multimodal models. Set\n`vision = false` for a text-only model served by such a family (e.g. a\ntext LLM behind llama.cpp) so image messages are routed to a configured\n`[multimodal] vision_model_provider` instead of being sent to a model\nthat rejects them. `Some(true)` forces vision on.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "wire_api": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/WireApi"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Wire protocol flavor: `responses` for OpenAI's Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`), `chat_completions` for the legacy chat wire and most OpenAI-compatible gateways. New OpenAI provider slots default to `responses`; other families default to chat-completions (or ignore the field). Only override if you're forcing an unusual combination."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "GeminiModelProviderConfig": {
      "description": "Named model_provider profile definition.",
      "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "description": "Secret API token for this model_provider. Grab it from the model_provider's dashboard (OpenAI platform, Anthropic console, OpenRouter keys page, etc.). Stored via the OS keyring when possible; never commit it to config.toml directly.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "auth_mode": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/AuthMode"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Auth flow. Defaults to `api_key`; `oauth` uses GeminiModelProvider's\nOAuth-cache integration instead of the `api_key` field."
        },
        "chat_template_kwargs": {
          "description": "Arbitrary key/value pairs forwarded verbatim as `chat_template_kwargs`\nin the request body (llama.cpp-specific). Use this to pass model-family\ntemplate variables that control behaviour not exposed by other fields.\nExample (Qwen3 thinking suppression):\n  `chat_template_kwargs = { enable_thinking = false }`"
        },
        "context_window": {
          "description": "Context window size (max input tokens) for this model.\nAuto-populated on setup from provider's /models endpoint if available.\nOverride manually for custom endpoints or when auto-detection fails.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "extra_headers": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "description": "Extra HTTP headers sent with every request. Niche: used for auth bridges, corporate proxies, or custom gateways that demand a tracing header. Most users never touch this; edit `config.toml` directly if you need it.",
          "type": "object",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "fallback": {
          "description": "Ordered list of other provider aliases to try when every model on this\nalias has failed. Each entry is a dotted `<type>.<alias>` reference into\n`providers.models` and resolves with its own credentials, endpoint, and\nmodel. A fallback never inherits this alias's key. The walk is\ndepth-first: this alias's models are exhausted first, then each fallback\nalias is descended in turn (applying its own `fallback_models` and\n`fallback`). Empty means no provider-level fallback.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/ModelProviderRef"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "fallback_models": {
          "description": "Ordered alternate models to try on THIS provider before falling over to\nthe `fallback` aliases. Same endpoint, key, and headers as the primary\n`model`. Only the model identifier changes. Use this when a provider\nserves a backup model (e.g. a smaller or older variant) that should be\ntried before leaving the provider entirely. Empty means only `model` is\ntried.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "kind": {
          "description": "Provider implementation to instantiate for this profile. Use this\nwhen a canonical typed slot should run through a compatible\nimplementation, e.g. `[providers.models.openai.proxy] kind =\n\"openai-compatible\"`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "live_pricing": {
          "description": "Pull live token prices for this provider's models from its own\nOpenAI-compatible `/models` listing (the gateway is the source of truth\nfor its prices), filling cost-tracking rates for models the operator\nhas NOT priced under `[cost.rates]` / `pricing`. Models the gateway does\nnot price (or providers with no HTTP `/models` listing at all, such as\na subprocess gateway like `kilocli`) fall back to the public models.dev\ncatalog. Configured rates always win; live prices only fill gaps. A\nbackground task refreshes the price snapshot hourly; the cost-recording\npath reads the cached snapshot and never blocks on the network. Default\n`false`: off means no fetching and behavior identical to a build\nwithout the feature.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "max_tokens": {
          "description": "Hard cap on response length in tokens. Most models enforce sensible built-in limits already; leave unset unless you specifically need to clip long outputs for cost or latency reasons.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "merge_system_into_user": {
          "description": "ModelProvider-specific quirk: fold the system prompt into the first user message instead of sending a separate system role. Only needed for models that reject (or mishandle) a standalone system role, e.g. certain older Mistral variants.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "model": {
          "description": "Model identifier to send with each request: the ID string from the model_provider's catalog (e.g. `gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `llama-3.3-70b`). Must match a model the model_provider actually serves on this account.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "native_tools": {
          "description": "Override the provider's default for native tool calling.\n`None` (default) honors the provider's built-in choice. `Some(true)`\nforces native tool calls on, `Some(false)` forces text-fallback.\nCurrently consulted only by the Groq factory, which defaults to\ntext-fallback because llama-family Groq models reject native tool\ncalls with HTTP 400. Setting `native_tools = true` re-enables native\ntool calling for Groq models that support it.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "oauth_client_id": {
          "description": "Google OAuth app `client_id`, used when this alias drives ZeroClaw's\nown browser/device-code login flow (`zeroclaw auth login\n--model-provider gemini --profile <alias>`). Operators relying on\nthe upstream `gemini login` tool don't need this; that tool writes\nits own client_id / client_secret into `~/.gemini/oauth_creds.json`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "oauth_client_secret": {
          "description": "Google OAuth app `client_secret`. Set alongside `oauth_client_id`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "oauth_project": {
          "description": "Pin a specific GCP project ID for the OAuth `loadCodeAssist`\ndiscovery call. When unset, the discovery probes for an\nalready-onboarded project on the credential's account. Replaces\n`GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` / `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT_ID` env vars.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "pricing": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "format": "double",
            "type": "number"
          },
          "description": "Per-model pricing for cost tracking, USD per 1M tokens.\n\nFree-form key/value map. Keys are user-defined model identifiers; an\noptional `.input` / `.output` suffix encodes pricing dimension when\nthe operator wants to split rates. A bare key without a suffix is\nused as a flat per-token rate when neither dimension is specified.\nDefault is empty: cost tracking falls back to \"unknown\" rates and\nonly token usage is recorded.\n\nExample: `pricing = { opus = 15.0, sonnet = 3.0 }`\nOr split: `pricing = { \"opus.input\" = 15.0, \"opus.output\" = 75.0 }`",
          "type": "object"
        },
        "provider_extra": {
          "description": "Extra JSON parameters to include in API requests.\nMerged at the top level of the request body, allowing provider-specific\nfeatures (routing, transforms, etc.) without code changes.\nExample: `provider_extra = { model_provider = { only = [\"Anthropic\"] } }`"
        },
        "replay_assistant_reasoning": {
          "description": "Whether stored assistant reasoning should be replayed on outbound\nassistant history messages. `Some(false)` strips `reasoning_content`\nand `reasoning` before sending. `None` (default) honours the provider's\nbuilt-in default (true for most compat providers, false for Groq).",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "requires_openai_auth": {
          "description": "When true, the client pulls credentials from ZeroClaw's stored `openai-codex` auth profile instead of the `api_key` field above. Import an existing Codex CLI login with `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json`, or run `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex`. Turn on only for the OpenAI Codex model_provider; leave off for standard API-key model_providers.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "temperature": {
          "description": "Sampling temperature passed to the model. Lower values (0.0–0.3) give\ndeterministic, near-verbatim output, which fits code, routing, summarization.\nHigher values (0.7–1.2) give more varied output, which fits open-ended chat.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "think": {
          "description": "Enable or disable chain-of-thought thinking for models that support it\n(e.g. Qwen3, GLM-4). `true` turns thinking on, `false` turns it off.\n`None` (default) lets the model decide. Forwarded as `enable_thinking`\nin the request body; mirrors the Ollama provider's `think` field.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "description": "HTTP request timeout in seconds. Bump this for slow local model_providers (Ollama on CPU, big local models) or high-latency networks; leave unset otherwise.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "tls_ca_cert_path": {
          "description": "Path to a PEM-encoded CA certificate for TLS connections to this provider.\nMust be an absolute path; shell expansion (e.g. `~`) is not performed.\nLeave unset to use the system's default trust store.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "uri": {
          "description": "Endpoint URI the client hits. Override the family's default endpoint when pointing at a self-hosted gateway (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama), a custom proxy, or any non-standard URL. Leave unset to use the family's default URI from its `ModelEndpoint` impl. Set this to the FULL endpoint URL; there is no separate path-suffix field.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "vision": {
          "description": "Override the provider's vision (image input) capability.\n`None` (default) uses the provider family's built-in default. Several\nfamilies (llama.cpp, the generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint, etc.)\nassume vision-capable because they can serve multimodal models. Set\n`vision = false` for a text-only model served by such a family (e.g. a\ntext LLM behind llama.cpp) so image messages are routed to a configured\n`[multimodal] vision_model_provider` instead of being sent to a model\nthat rejects them. `Some(true)` forces vision on.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "wire_api": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/WireApi"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Wire protocol flavor: `responses` for OpenAI's Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`), `chat_completions` for the legacy chat wire and most OpenAI-compatible gateways. New OpenAI provider slots default to `responses`; other families default to chat-completions (or ignore the field). Only override if you're forcing an unusual combination."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "GitConfig": {
      "description": "Git-forge channel configuration (polling-based; no webhook required).\n\nA `provider` selects the forge. GitHub authenticates as a GitHub App:\na short-lived RS256 JWT signed with the app's private key is exchanged\nfor per-installation access tokens. Gitea and Forgejo use a personal\naccess token against the instance's `/api/v1` endpoint, named by the\nrequired `api_base_url`. Inbound issue/PR comments are polled from the\nforge REST API, so the daemon needs no inbound network exposure.",
      "properties": {
        "access_token": {
          "default": "",
          "description": "Personal access token for Gitea/Forgejo API requests. The token needs\nrepository read access plus issue/PR comment write access for replies\nand reactions. Gitea/Forgejo provider only.",
          "type": "string",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "api_base_url": {
          "description": "Gitea/Forgejo API base URL, including `/api/v1`, for example\n`https://git.example.org/api/v1` (for the public Gitea service:\n`https://gitea.com/api/v1`). Required when `provider` is `\"gitea\"`\nor `\"forgejo\"` - there is no default host, because every API\nrequest carries `access_token`; the channel fails closed at\nstartup rather than send the token to an endpoint the operator\nnever named. Gitea/Forgejo provider only.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "app_id": {
          "default": 0,
          "description": "GitHub App ID (shown on the app's settings page). GitHub provider only.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Whether this channel is active. The runtime only loads channels whose\n`enabled = true`. Default: `false` so an operator who pastes a partial\n`[channels.<type>.<alias>]` block doesn't accidentally bring a channel\nlive before the rest of its config is filled in.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "events": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/GitEventRoute"
          },
          "default": {},
          "description": "Per-event routing table, keyed by normalized event type\n(`\"issue_comment.created\"`, `\"pull_request.opened\"`,\n`\"workflow_run.failed\"`, …). Event types absent from the table fall\nback to the conversational default: `issue_comment.created`,\n`issues.opened`, and `pull_request.opened` are delivered as\nmessages (mention-gated); everything else is ignored. Which API\nendpoints are polled is derived from this table; routing an event\ntype is also subscribing to it.",
          "type": "object"
        },
        "events_backbone": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Also poll the repository Events API (`/repos/{owner}/{repo}/events`)\nas a broad backbone transport: one conditional (ETag) request per\nrepository per tick, so an idle repo costs almost nothing. Caveats:\nevents arrive with a delay of up to ~5 minutes and the feed carries\nno Actions/check events (workflow runs always use their dedicated\nendpoint). Items also surfaced by a targeted endpoint are\nde-duplicated. Default: `false`.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "excluded_tools": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Tools excluded from this channel's tool spec. When set, these tools\nare not exposed to the model when responding via this channel.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "installation_id": {
          "description": "Installation ID to act as. When unset, the app's installations are\nlisted on first use and a sole installation is auto-selected;\nstartup fails if the app has zero or multiple installations.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "listen_to_bots": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Process comments authored by other bot accounts. The app's own\ncomments are always ignored. Default: `false`.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "mention_only": {
          "default": true,
          "description": "Only respond to comments that @-mention the app's bot login.\nDefault: `true`.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "poll_interval_secs": {
          "default": 30,
          "description": "Poll interval in seconds for new issues and comments. Values below\n15 are clamped to 15. Default: `30`.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "private_key": {
          "description": "RS256 private key PEM, the contents of the `.pem` file GitHub\ngenerates on the app's settings page, inline and encrypted at rest.\nInclude the BEGIN/END lines. GitHub provider only.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "private_key_path": {
          "description": "Filesystem path to the RS256 private key `.pem` file, read at startup\nwhen `private_key` (inline PEM) is unset. Backward-compatible fallback\nfor configs that predate the inline-PEM field. GitHub provider only.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "provider": {
          "default": "github",
          "description": "Git forge provider. Supported: `\"github\"`, `\"gitea\"`, and\n`\"forgejo\"` (Forgejo uses the Gitea-compatible REST provider).\nDefault: `\"github\"`.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "proxy_url": {
          "description": "Per-channel proxy override for GitHub API requests.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "repos": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Repositories to poll, as `owner/repo`. Empty = every repository\nvisible to the installation.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "GitEventRoute": {
      "description": "Routing for one normalized git-forge event type, keyed in\n`[channels.git.<alias>.events]` by the event type string\n(`\"pull_request.opened\" = { sop = \"pr-triage\" }`).\n\nAn entry with neither `message = true` nor a `sop` explicitly ignores the\nevent type (overriding the conversational default).",
      "properties": {
        "message": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Deliver the event into the agent loop as a normal channel message.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "sop": {
          "description": "Route the event to the named SOP through channel-sourced SOP ingress.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },

          "description": "Per-model pricing for cost tracking, USD per 1M tokens.\n\nFree-form key/value map. Keys are user-defined model identifiers; an\noptional `.input` / `.output` suffix encodes pricing dimension when\nthe operator wants to split rates. A bare key without a suffix is\nused as a flat per-token rate when neither dimension is specified.\nDefault is empty: cost tracking falls back to \"unknown\" rates and\nonly token usage is recorded.\n\nExample: `pricing = { opus = 15.0, sonnet = 3.0 }`\nOr split: `pricing = { \"opus.input\" = 15.0, \"opus.output\" = 75.0 }`",
          "type": "object"
        },
        "provider_extra": {
          "description": "Extra JSON parameters to include in API requests.\nMerged at the top level of the request body, allowing provider-specific\nfeatures (routing, transforms, etc.) without code changes.\nExample: `provider_extra = { model_provider = { only = [\"Anthropic\"] } }`"
        },
        "replay_assistant_reasoning": {
          "description": "Whether stored assistant reasoning should be replayed on outbound\nassistant history messages. `Some(false)` strips `reasoning_content`\nand `reasoning` before sending. `None` (default) honours the provider's\nbuilt-in default (true for most compat providers, false for Groq).",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "requires_openai_auth": {
          "description": "When true, the client pulls credentials from ZeroClaw's stored `openai-codex` auth profile instead of the `api_key` field above. Import an existing Codex CLI login with `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json`, or run `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex`. Turn on only for the OpenAI Codex model_provider; leave off for standard API-key model_providers.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "temperature": {
          "description": "Sampling temperature passed to the model. Lower values (0.0–0.3) give\ndeterministic, near-verbatim output, which fits code, routing, summarization.\nHigher values (0.7–1.2) give more varied output, which fits open-ended chat.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "think": {
          "description": "Enable or disable chain-of-thought thinking for models that support it\n(e.g. Qwen3, GLM-4). `true` turns thinking on, `false` turns it off.\n`None` (default) lets the model decide. Forwarded as `enable_thinking`\nin the request body; mirrors the Ollama provider's `think` field.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "description": "HTTP request timeout in seconds. Bump this for slow local model_providers (Ollama on CPU, big local models) or high-latency networks; leave unset otherwise.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "tls_ca_cert_path": {
          "description": "Path to a PEM-encoded CA certificate for TLS connections to this provider.\nMust be an absolute path; shell expansion (e.g. `~`) is not performed.\nLeave unset to use the system's default trust store.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "uri": {
          "description": "Endpoint URI the client hits. Override the family's default endpoint when pointing at a self-hosted gateway (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama), a custom proxy, or any non-standard URL. Leave unset to use the family's default URI from its `ModelEndpoint` impl. Set this to the FULL endpoint URL; there is no separate path-suffix field.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "vision": {
          "description": "Override the provider's vision (image input) capability.\n`None` (default) uses the provider family's built-in default. Several\nfamilies (llama.cpp, the generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint, etc.)\nassume vision-capable because they can serve multimodal models. Set\n`vision = false` for a text-only model served by such a family (e.g. a\ntext LLM behind llama.cpp) so image messages are routed to a configured\n`[multimodal] vision_model_provider` instead of being sent to a model\nthat rejects them. `Some(true)` forces vision on.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "wire_api": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/WireApi"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Wire protocol flavor: `responses` for OpenAI's Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`), `chat_completions` for the legacy chat wire and most OpenAI-compatible gateways. New OpenAI provider slots default to `responses`; other families default to chat-completions (or ignore the field). Only override if you're forcing an unusual combination."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "GlmEndpoint": {
      "enum": [
        "cn",
        "global"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    },
    "GlmModelProviderConfig": {
      "description": "Named model_provider profile definition.",
      "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "description": "Secret API token for this model_provider. Grab it from the model_provider's dashboard (OpenAI platform, Anthropic console, OpenRouter keys page, etc.). Stored via the OS keyring when possible; never commit it to config.toml directly.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "chat_template_kwargs": {
          "description": "Arbitrary key/value pairs forwarded verbatim as `chat_template_kwargs`\nin the request body (llama.cpp-specific).         },

          "description": "Context window size (max input tokens) for this model.\nAuto-populated on setup from provider's /models endpoint if available.\nOverride manually for custom endpoints or when auto-detection fails.",

          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",

          "default": "global"
        },
        "extra_headers": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "description": "Extra HTTP headers sent with every request. Niche: used for auth bridges, corporate proxies, or custom gateways that demand a tracing header. Most users never touch this; edit `config.toml` directly if you need it.",
          "type": "object",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "fallback": {
          "description": "Ordered list of other provider aliases to try when every model on this\nalias has failed. Each entry is a dotted `<type>.<alias>` reference into\n`providers.models` and resolves with its own credentials, endpoint, and\nmodel. A fallback never inherits this alias's key. The walk is\ndepth-first: this alias's models are exhausted first, then each fallback\nalias is descended in turn (applying its own `fallback_models` and\n`fallback`). Empty means no provider-level fallback.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/ModelProviderRef"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "fallback_models": {
          "description": "Ordered alternate models to try on THIS provider before falling over to\nthe `fallback` aliases. Same endpoint, key, and headers as the primary\n`model`. Only the model identifier changes. Use this when a provider\nserves a backup model (e.g. a smaller or older variant) that should be\ntried before leaving the provider entirely. Empty means only `model` is\ntried.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "kind": {
          "description": "Provider implementation to instantiate for this profile. Use this\nwhen a canonical typed slot should run through a compatible\nimplementation, e.g. `[providers.models.openai.proxy] kind =\n\"openai-compatible\"`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "live_pricing": {
          "description": "Pull live token prices for this provider's models from its own\nOpenAI-compatible `/models` listing (the gateway is the source of truth\nfor its prices), filling cost-tracking rates for models the operator\nhas NOT priced under `[cost.rates]` / `pricing`. Models the gateway does\nnot price (or providers with no HTTP `/models` listing at all, such as\na subprocess gateway like `kilocli`) fall back to the public models.dev\ncatalog. Configured rates always win; live prices only fill gaps. A\nbackground task refreshes the price snapshot hourly; the cost-recording\npath reads the cached snapshot and never blocks on the network. Default\n`false`: off means no fetching and behavior identical to a build\nwithout the feature.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "max_tokens": {
          "description": "Hard cap on response length in tokens. Most models enforce sensible built-in limits already; leave unset unless you specifically need to clip long outputs for cost or latency reasons.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "merge_system_into_user": {
          "description": "ModelProvider-specific quirk: fold the system prompt into the first user message instead of sending a separate system role. Only needed for models that reject (or mishandle) a standalone system role, e.g. certain older Mistral variants.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "model": {
          "description": "Model identifier to send with each request: the ID string from the model_provider's catalog (e.g. `gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `llama-3.3-70b`). Must match a model the model_provider actually serves on this account.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "native_tools": {
          "description": "Override the provider's default for native tool calling.\n`None` (default) honors the provider's built-in choice. `Some(true)`\nforces native tool calls on, `Some(false)` forces text-fallback.\nCurrently consulted only by the Groq factory, which defaults to\ntext-fallback because llama-family Groq models reject native tool\ncalls with HTTP 400. Setting `native_tools = true` re-enables native\ntool calling for Groq models that support it.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "pricing": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "format": "double",
            "type": "number"
          },
          "description": "Per-model pricing for cost tracking, USD per 1M tokens.\n\nFree-form key/value map. A bare key without a suffix is\nused as a flat per-token rate when neither dimension is specified.\nDefault is empty: cost tracking falls back to \"unknown\" rates and\nonly token usage is recorded.\n\nExample: `pricing = { opus = 15.0, sonnet = 3.0 }`\nOr split: `pricing = { \"opus.input\" = 15.0, \"opus.output\" = 75.0 }`",
          "type": "object"
        },
        "provider_extra": {

        },
        "replay_assistant_reasoning": {
          "description": "Whether stored assistant reasoning should be replayed on outbound\nassistant history messages. `Some(false)` strips `reasoning_content`\nand `reasoning` before sending. `None` (default) honours the provider's\nbuilt-in default (true for most compat providers, false for Groq).",
          "type": [

        "requires_openai_auth": {

Import an existing Codex CLI login with `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json`, or run `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex`. Turn on only for the OpenAI Codex model_provider; leave off for standard API-key model_providers.",
          "type": "boolean"

        "temperature": {

          "format": "double",

        },
        "think": {

Forwarded as `enable_thinking`\nin the request body; mirrors the Ollama provider's `think` field.",

          ]
        },

          "format": "uint64",

Set\n`vision = false` for a text-only model served by such a family (e.g. a\ntext LLM behind llama.cpp) so image messages are routed to a configured\n`[multimodal] vision_model_provider` instead of being sent to a model\nthat rejects them. `Some(true)` forces vision on.",

    "GmailPushConfig": {
      "properties": {
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Whether this channel is active. The runtime only loads channels whose\n`enabled = true`. Default: `false` so an operator who pastes a partial\n`[channels.<type>.<alias>]` block doesn't accidentally bring a channel\nlive before the rest of its config is filled in.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "excluded_tools": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Tools excluded from this channel's tool spec. When set, these tools\nare not exposed to the model when responding via this channel.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "label_filter": {
          "default": [
            "INBOX"
          ],
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "oauth_token": {
          "default": "",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "topic": {
          "type": "string"
        },
        "webhook_secret": {
          "default": "",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "webhook_url": {
          "default": "",
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "topic"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    "GoogleSttConfig": {
      "description": "Google Cloud Speech-to-Text model_provider configuration (`[transcription.google]`).",
      "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Google Cloud API key.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "language_code": {
          "default": "en-US",
          "description": "BCP-47 language code (default: \"en-US\").",
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "GoogleTranscriptionProviderConfig": {
      "description": "Shared base for cloud transcription providers. Each cloud family\ncomposes this via `#[serde(flatten)] base: TranscriptionProviderConfig`.",
      "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "API key for the transcription provider.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "initial_prompt": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Whisper-style initial prompt to bias the model toward expected\nvocabulary (proper nouns, technical terms). Provider-specific support;\nsilently ignored where not applicable.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "language": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Optional language hint passed to the provider (ISO-639-1 like `\"en\"` /\n`\"ru\"`, or BCP-47 like `\"en-US\"` for Google). Most providers auto-detect\nwhen this is unset.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "GoogleTtsProviderConfig": {
      "description": "Per-instance TTS model_provider configuration (`[tts_providers.<type>.<alias>]`).\n\nMirrors `ModelProviderConfig` in shape — one struct holds the union of\nfields across backends. Only the fields relevant to the selected backend\n(determined by the outer `<type>` map key) are read at runtime; others\nare quietly ignored.",
      "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "API key (openai, elevenlabs, google).",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "binary_path": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Path to backend binary (edge-tts subprocess; piper local server).",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "language_code": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Language code for google (e.g. `en-US`).",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "model": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Model name. OpenAI uses this for `tts-1`/`tts-1-hd`; elevenlabs uses\nit as the model_id (e.g. `eleven_monolingual_v1`).",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "response_format": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Audio response format sent to the TTS backend (e.g. `\"opus\"`, `\"mp3\"`,\n`\"wav\"`). Defaults to `\"opus\"` for the OpenAI family. Override to\n`\"wav\"` for Orpheus-class models (e.g. `canopylabs/orpheus-v1-english`\non Groq) or `\"mp3\"` for broader compatibility.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "similarity_boost": {
          "default": null,

          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "speed": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Playback speed multiplier (openai only; default `1.0`).",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "stability": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Voice stability for elevenlabs (0.0-1.0; default `0.5`).",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "uri": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Endpoint URI for HTTP-based backends. Overrides the family default\nwhen pointing at a compatible third-party API (Groq, Azure, self-hosted\nproxies). Set to the **full** URL — there is no separate path-suffix\nfield. Renamed from `api_url` for parity with `ModelProviderConfig.uri`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "voice": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Voice override for this instance. When empty, falls back to\n`[tts].default_voice`.",
          "type": [
