            "null"
          ]
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "GoogleWorkspaceAllowedOperation": {
      "description": "Google Workspace CLI (`gws`) tool configuration (`[google_workspace]` section).\n\n## Defaults\n- `enabled`: `false` (tool is not registered unless explicitly opted-in).\n- `allowed_services`: empty vector, which grants access to the full default\n  service set: `drive`, `sheets`, `gmail`, `calendar`, `docs`, `slides`,\n  `tasks`, `people`, `chat`, `classroom`, `forms`, `keep`, `meet`, `events`.\n- `credentials_path`: `None` (uses default `gws` credential discovery).\n- `default_account`: `None` (uses the `gws` active account).\n- `rate_limit_per_minute`: `60`.\n- `timeout_secs`: `30`.\n- `audit_log`: `false`.\n- `credentials_path`: `None` (uses default `gws` credential discovery).\n- `default_account`: `None` (uses the `gws` active account).\n- `rate_limit_per_minute`: `60`.\n- `timeout_secs`: `30`.\n- `audit_log`: `false`.\n\n## Compatibility\nConfigs that omit the `[google_workspace]` section entirely are treated as\n`GoogleWorkspaceConfig::default()` (disabled, all defaults allowed). Adding\nthe section is purely opt-in and does not affect other config sections.\n\n## Rollback / Migration\nTo revert, remove the `[google_workspace]` section from the config file (or\nset `enabled = false`). No data migration is required; the tool simply stops\nbeing registered.",
      "properties": {
        "methods": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Allowed methods for the service/resource/sub_resource combination.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "resource": {
          "description": "Top-level resource name for the service (for example `users` for Gmail or `files` for Drive).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "service": {
          "description": "Google Workspace service ID (for example `gmail` or `drive`).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "sub_resource": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Optional sub-resource for 4-segment gws commands\n(for example `messages` or `drafts` under `gmail users`).\nWhen present, the entry only matches calls that include this exact sub_resource.\nWhen absent, the entry only matches calls with no sub_resource.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "service",
        "resource"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    "GoogleWorkspaceConfig": {
      "description": "Google Workspace CLI (`gws`) tool configuration (`[google_workspace]` section).\n\n## Defaults\n- `enabled`: `false` (tool is not registered unless explicitly opted-in).\n- `allowed_services`: empty vector, which grants access to the full default\n  service set: `drive`, `sheets`, `gmail`, `calendar`, `docs`, `slides`,\n  `tasks`, `people`, `chat`, `classroom`, `forms`, `keep`, `meet`, `events`.\n- `allowed_operations`: empty vector, which preserves the legacy behavior of\n  allowing any resource/method under the allowed service set.\n- `credentials_path`: `None` (uses default `gws` credential discovery).\n- `default_account`: `None` (uses the `gws` active account).\n- `rate_limit_per_minute`: `60`.\n- `timeout_secs`: `30`.\n- `audit_log`: `false`.\n\n## Compatibility\nConfigs that omit the `[google_workspace]` section entirely are treated as\n`GoogleWorkspaceConfig::default()` (disabled, all defaults allowed). Adding\nthe section is purely opt-in and does not affect other config sections.\n\n## Rollback / Migration\nTo revert, remove the `[google_workspace]` section from the config file (or\nset `enabled = false`). No data migration is required; the tool simply stops\nbeing registered.",
      "properties": {
        "allowed_operations": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Restrict which resource/method combinations the agent can access.\n\nWhen empty (the default), all methods under `allowed_services` remain\navailable for backward compatibility. When non-empty, the runtime denies\nany `(service, resource, sub_resource, method)` combination that is not\nexplicitly listed. `sub_resource` is optional per entry: an entry without\nit matches only 3-segment `gws` calls; an entry with it matches only calls\nthat supply that exact sub_resource value.\n\nEach entry's `service` must appear in `allowed_services` when that list is\nnon-empty; config validation rejects entries that would never match at\nruntime.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/GoogleWorkspaceAllowedOperation"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "allowed_services": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Restrict which Google Workspace services the agent can access.\n\nWhen empty (the default), the full default service set is allowed (see\nstruct-level docs). When non-empty, only the listed service IDs are\npermitted. Each entry must be non-empty, lowercase alphanumeric with\noptional underscores/hyphens, and unique.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "audit_log": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Enable audit logging of every `gws` invocation (service, resource,\nmethod, timestamp). Default: `false`.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "credentials_path": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Path to service account JSON or OAuth client credentials file.\n\nWhen `None`, the tool relies on the default `gws` credential discovery\n(`gws auth login`). Set this to point at a service-account key or an\nOAuth client-secrets JSON for headless / CI environments.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "default_account": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Default Google account email to pass to `gws --account`.\n\nWhen `None`, the currently active `gws` account is used.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Enable the `google_workspace` tool. Default: `false`.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "rate_limit_per_minute": {
          "default": 60,
          "description": "Maximum number of `gws` API calls allowed per minute. Default: `60`.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "default": 30,
          "description": "Command execution timeout in seconds. Default: `30`.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "GroqModelProviderConfig": {
      "description": "Named model_provider profile definition.",
      "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "description": "Secret API token for this model_provider. Grab it from the model_provider's dashboard (OpenAI platform, Anthropic console, OpenRouter keys page, etc.). Stored via the OS keyring when possible; never commit it to config.toml directly.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "chat_template_kwargs": {
          "description": "Arbitrary key/value pairs forwarded verbatim as `chat_template_kwargs`\nin the request body (llama.cpp-specific). Use this to pass model-family\ntemplate variables that control behaviour not exposed by other fields.\nExample (Qwen3 thinking suppression):\n  `chat_template_kwargs = { enable_thinking = false }`"
        },
        "context_window": {
          "description": "Context window size (max input tokens) for this model.\nAuto-populated on setup from provider's /models endpoint if available.\nOverride manually for custom endpoints or when auto-detection fails.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "extra_headers": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "description": "Extra HTTP headers sent with every request. Niche: used for auth bridges, corporate proxies, or custom gateways that demand a tracing header. Most users never touch this; edit `config.toml` directly if you need it.",
          "type": "object",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "fallback": {
          "description": "Ordered list of other provider aliases to try when every model on this\nalias has failed. Each entry is a dotted `<type>.<alias>` reference into\n`providers.models` and resolves with its own credentials, endpoint, and\nmodel. A fallback never inherits this alias's key. The walk is\ndepth-first: this alias's models are exhausted first, then each fallback\nalias is descended in turn (applying its own `fallback_models` and\n`fallback`). Empty means no provider-level fallback.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/ModelProviderRef"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "fallback_models": {
          "description": "Ordered alternate models to try on THIS provider before falling over to\nthe `fallback` aliases. Same endpoint, key, and headers as the primary\n`model`. Only the model identifier changes. Use this when a provider\nserves a backup model (e.g. a smaller or older variant) that should be\ntried before leaving the provider entirely. Empty means only `model` is\ntried.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "kind": {
          "description": "Provider implementation to instantiate for this profile. Use this\nwhen a canonical typed slot should run through a compatible\nimplementation, e.g. `[providers.models.openai.proxy] kind =\n\"openai-compatible\"`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "live_pricing": {
          "description": "Pull live token prices for this provider's models from its own\nOpenAI-compatible `/models` listing (the gateway is the source of truth\nfor its prices), filling cost-tracking rates for models the operator\nhas NOT priced under `[cost.rates]` / `pricing`. Models the gateway does\nnot price (or providers with no HTTP `/models` listing at all, such as\na subprocess gateway like `kilocli`) fall back to the public models.dev\ncatalog. Configured rates always win; live prices only fill gaps. A\nbackground task refreshes the price snapshot hourly; the cost-recording\npath reads the cached snapshot and never blocks on the network. Default\n`false`: off means no fetching and behavior identical to a build\nwithout the feature.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "max_tokens": {
          "description": "Hard cap on response length in tokens. Most models enforce sensible built-in limits already; leave unset unless you specifically need to clip long outputs for cost or latency reasons.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "merge_system_into_user": {
          "description": "ModelProvider-specific quirk: fold the system prompt into the first user message instead of sending a separate system role. Only needed for models that reject (or mishandle) a standalone system role, e.g. certain older Mistral variants.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "model": {
          "description": "Model identifier to send with each request: the ID string from the model_provider's catalog (e.g. `gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `llama-3.3-70b`). Must match a model the model_provider actually serves on this account.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "native_tools": {
          "description": "Override the provider's default for native tool calling.\n`None` (default) honors the provider's built-in choice. `Some(true)`\nforces native tool calls on, `Some(false)` forces text-fallback.\nCurrently consulted only by the Groq factory, which defaults to\ntext-fallback because llama-family Groq models reject native tool\ncalls with HTTP 400. Setting `native_tools = true` re-enables native\ntool calling for Groq models that support it.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "pricing": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "format": "double",
            "type": "number"
          },
          "description": "Per-model pricing for cost tracking, USD per 1M tokens.\n\nFree-form key/value map. Keys are user-defined model identifiers; an\noptional `.input` / `.output` suffix encodes pricing dimension when\nthe operator wants to split rates. A bare key without a suffix is\nused as a flat per-token rate when neither dimension is specified.\nDefault is empty: cost tracking falls back to \"unknown\" rates and\nonly token usage is recorded.\n\nExample: `pricing = { opus = 15.0, sonnet = 3.0 }`\nOr split: `pricing = { \"opus.input\" = 15.0, \"opus.output\" = 75.0 }`",
          "type": "object"
        },
        "provider_extra": {
          "description": "Extra JSON parameters to include in API requests.\nMerged at the top level of the request body, allowing provider-specific\nfeatures (routing, transforms, etc.) without code changes.\nExample: `provider_extra = { model_provider = { only = [\"Anthropic\"] } }`"
        },
        "replay_assistant_reasoning": {
          "description": "Whether stored assistant reasoning should be replayed on outbound\nassistant history messages. `Some(false)` strips `reasoning_content`\nand `reasoning` before sending. `None` (default) honours the provider's\nbuilt-in default (true for most compat providers, false for Groq).",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "requires_openai_auth": {
          "description": "When true, the client pulls credentials from ZeroClaw's stored `openai-codex` auth profile instead of the `api_key` field above. Import an existing Codex CLI login with `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json`, or run `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex`. Turn on only for the OpenAI Codex model_provider; leave off for standard API-key model_providers.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "temperature": {
          "description": "Sampling temperature passed to the model. Lower values (0.0–0.3) give\ndeterministic, near-verbatim output, which fits code, routing, summarization.\nHigher values (0.7–1.2) give more varied output, which fits open-ended chat.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "think": {
          "description": "Enable or disable chain-of-thought thinking for models that support it\n(e.g. Qwen3, GLM-4). `true` turns thinking on, `false` turns it off.\n`None` (default) lets the model decide. Forwarded as `enable_thinking`\nin the request body; mirrors the Ollama provider's `think` field.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "description": "HTTP request timeout in seconds. Bump this for slow local model_providers (Ollama on CPU, big local models) or high-latency networks; leave unset otherwise.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "tls_ca_cert_path": {
          "description": "Path to a PEM-encoded CA certificate for TLS connections to this provider.\nMust be an absolute path; shell expansion (e.g. `~`) is not performed.\nLeave unset to use the system's default trust store.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "uri": {
          "description": "Endpoint URI the client hits. Override the family's default endpoint when pointing at a self-hosted gateway (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama), a custom proxy, or any non-standard URL. Leave unset to use the family's default URI from its `ModelEndpoint` impl. Set this to the FULL endpoint URL; there is no separate path-suffix field.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "vision": {
          "description": "Override the provider's vision (image input) capability.\n`None` (default) uses the provider family's built-in default. Several\nfamilies (llama.cpp, the generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint, etc.)\nassume vision-capable because they can serve multimodal models. Set\n`vision = false` for a text-only model served by such a family (e.g. a\ntext LLM behind llama.cpp) so image messages are routed to a configured\n`[multimodal] vision_model_provider` instead of being sent to a model\nthat rejects them. `Some(true)` forces vision on.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "wire_api": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/WireApi"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Wire protocol flavor: `responses` for OpenAI's Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`), `chat_completions` for the legacy chat wire and most OpenAI-compatible gateways. New OpenAI provider slots default to `responses`; other families default to chat-completions (or ignore the field). Only override if you're forcing an unusual combination."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "GroqTranscriptionProviderConfig": {
      "description": "Shared base for cloud transcription providers. Each cloud family\ncomposes this via `#[serde(flatten)] base: TranscriptionProviderConfig`.",
      "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "API key for the transcription provider.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "initial_prompt": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Whisper-style initial prompt to bias the model toward expected\nvocabulary (proper nouns, technical terms). Provider-specific support;\nsilently ignored where not applicable.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "language": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Optional language hint passed to the provider (ISO-639-1 like `\"en\"` /\n`\"ru\"`, or BCP-47 like `\"en-US\"` for Google). Most providers auto-detect\nwhen this is unset.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "model": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Whisper model name (default: `\"whisper-large-v3-turbo\"`).",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "HardwareConfig": {
      "description": "Wizard-driven hardware configuration for physical world interaction.",
      "properties": {
        "baud_rate": {
          "default": 115200,
          "description": "Baud rate negotiated on the serial link. 115200 matches the common Arduino / ESP32 bootloader default; bump to 230400+ when your firmware explicitly supports faster rates and you need the throughput.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Opt in to direct physical-hardware control — GPIO pins, USB-tethered microcontrollers (Arduino, ESP32, Nucleo), or SWD/JTAG debug probes. Leave off for software-only use; turning it on without the right transport configured does nothing.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "probe_target": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Target chip identifier for `transport = probe` (e.g. `STM32F401RE`, `nRF52840_xxAA`). Passed straight to probe-rs for flash/debug operations; must match a chip probe-rs recognizes.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "serial_port": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "TTY path for the `serial` transport — e.g. `/dev/ttyACM0` on Linux, `/dev/tty.usbmodem1` on macOS, `COM3` on Windows. Ignored for other transports.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "transport": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/HardwareTransport",
          "default": "None",
          "description": "How ZeroClaw reaches the hardware: `native` = Linux SBC with direct GPIO access (Raspberry Pi, Orange Pi); `serial` = USB-tethered microcontroller speaking over a TTY; `probe` = SWD/JTAG debug probe driving a target chip via probe-rs; `none` = disabled."
        },
        "workspace_datasheets": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Index pre-converted `.md` and `.txt` datasheets from the workspace into\na local RAG store, so the agent can look up pin assignments and\nelectrical specs inline when you ask hardware questions. PDFs are not\nparsed as text; download or convert them to `.md`/`.txt` first. Off by\ndefault — turn on once the workspace has relevant text datasheets.",
          "type": "boolean"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "HardwareTransport": {
      "description": "Hardware transport mode.",
      "enum": [
        "None",
        "Native",
        "Serial",
        "Probe"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    },
    "HeartbeatConfig": {
      "description": "Heartbeat configuration for periodic health pings (`[heartbeat]` section).",
      "properties": {
        "adaptive": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Enable adaptive intervals that back off on failures and speed up for\nhigh-priority tasks. Default: `false`.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "agent": {
          "default": "",
          "description": "Configured agent alias the heartbeat worker runs as. Required\nwhen `enabled = true`; refers to a `[agents.<alias>]` entry.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "deadman_channel": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Channel for dead-man's switch alerts (e.g. `telegram`). Falls back to\nthe heartbeat delivery channel.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "deadman_timeout_minutes": {
          "default": 0,
          "description": "Dead-man's switch timeout in minutes. If the heartbeat has not ticked\nwithin this window, an alert is sent. `0` disables. Default: `0`.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "deadman_to": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Recipient for dead-man's switch alerts. Falls back to `to`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Enable periodic heartbeat pings. Default: `false`. When enabled,\n`agent` must name a configured agent — there is no default agent\nfor heartbeat to fall through to.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "interval_minutes": {
          "default": 30,
          "description": "Interval in minutes between heartbeat pings. Minimum: `1`. Default: `30`.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "load_session_context": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Load the channel session history before each heartbeat task execution so\nthe LLM has conversational context. Default: `false`.\n\nWhen `true`, the session file for the configured `target`/`to` is passed\nto the agent as `session_state_file`, giving it access to the recent\nconversation history — just as if the user had sent a message.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "max_interval_minutes": {
          "default": 120,
          "description": "Maximum interval in minutes when adaptive mode backs off. Default: `120`.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "max_run_history": {
          "default": 100,
          "description": "Maximum number of heartbeat run history records to retain. Default: `100`.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "message": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Optional fallback task text when `HEARTBEAT.md` has no task entries.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "min_interval_minutes": {
          "default": 5,
          "description": "Minimum interval in minutes when adaptive mode is enabled. Default: `5`.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "target": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Optional delivery channel for heartbeat output (for example: `telegram`).\nWhen omitted, auto-selects the first configured channel.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "task_timeout_secs": {
          "default": 600,
          "description": "Maximum wall-clock seconds allowed for a single agent invocation\n(Phase 1 decision or Phase 2 task execution). `0` disables.\nDefault: `600` (10 minutes).",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "to": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Optional delivery recipient/chat identifier (required when `target` is\nexplicitly set).",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "two_phase": {
          "default": true,
          "description": "Enable two-phase heartbeat: Phase 1 asks LLM whether to run, Phase 2\nexecutes only when the LLM decides there is work to do. Saves API cost\nduring quiet periods. Default: `true`.",
          "type": "boolean"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "HistoryPrunerConfig": {
      "properties": {
        "collapse_tool_results": {
          "default": true,
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "keep_recent": {
          "default": 4,
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "max_tokens": {
          "default": 8192,
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "HooksConfig": {
      "properties": {
        "builtin": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/BuiltinHooksConfig",
          "default": {
            "command_logger": false,
            "webhook_audit": {
              "enabled": false,
              "include_args": false,
              "max_args_bytes": 4096,
              "tool_patterns": [],
              "url": ""
            }
          }
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": true,
          "description": "Enable lifecycle hook execution.\n\nHooks run in-process with the same privileges as the main runtime.\nKeep enabled hook handlers narrowly scoped and auditable.",
          "type": "boolean"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "HttpRequestConfig": {
      "description": "HTTP request tool configuration (`[http_request]` section).\n\nDomain filtering: `allowed_domains` controls which hosts are reachable (use `[\"*\"]`\nfor all public hosts, which is the default). If `allowed_domains` is empty, all\nrequests are rejected.",
      "properties": {
        "allow_private_hosts": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Allow requests to private/LAN hosts (RFC 1918, loopback, link-local, .local).\nDefault: false (deny private hosts for SSRF protection).",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "allowed_domains": {
          "default": [
            "*"
          ],
          "description": "Allowed domains for HTTP requests (exact or subdomain match)",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "allowed_private_hosts": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Private/internal hosts explicitly allowed to bypass SSRF protection.\nExact and subdomain matches are supported; `*` permits all private/local hosts.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": true,
          "description": "Enable `http_request` tool for API interactions",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "max_response_size": {
          "default": 1000000,
          "description": "Maximum response size in bytes (default: 1MB, 0 = unlimited)",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "secrets": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "default": {},
          "description": "Named authorization secrets for `auth_secret` requests.",
          "type": "object",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "default": 30,
          "description": "Request timeout in seconds (default: 30)",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },

        },
        "merge_system_into_user": {
          "description": "ModelProvider-specific quirk: fold the system prompt into the first user message instead of sending a separate system role. Only needed for models that reject (or mishandle) a standalone system role, e.g. certain older Mistral variants.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "model": {
          "description": "Model identifier to send with each request: the ID string from the model_provider's catalog (e.g. `gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `llama-3.3-70b`). Must match a model the model_provider actually serves on this account.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "native_tools": {
          "description": "Override the provider's default for native tool calling.\n`None` (default) honors the provider's built-in choice. `Some(true)`\nforces native tool calls on, `Some(false)` forces text-fallback.\nCurrently consulted only by the Groq factory, which defaults to\ntext-fallback because llama-family Groq models reject native tool\ncalls with HTTP 400. Setting `native_tools = true` re-enables native\ntool calling for Groq models that support it.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "pricing": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "format": "double",
            "type": "number"
          },
          "description": "Per-model pricing for cost tracking, USD per 1M tokens.\n\nFree-form key/value map. Keys are user-defined model identifiers; an\noptional `.input` / `.output` suffix encodes pricing dimension when\nthe operator wants to split rates. A bare key without a suffix is\nused as a flat per-token rate when neither dimension is specified.\nDefault is empty: cost tracking falls back to \"unknown\" rates and\nonly token usage is recorded.\n\nExample: `pricing = { opus = 15.0, sonnet = 3.0 }`\nOr split: `pricing = { \"opus.input\" = 15.0, \"opus.output\" = 75.0 }`",
          "type": "object"
        },
        "provider_extra": {
          "description": "Extra JSON parameters to include in API requests.\nMerged at the top level of the request body, allowing provider-specific\nfeatures (routing, transforms, etc.) without code changes.\nExample: `provider_extra = { model_provider = { only = [\"Anthropic\"] } }`"
        },
        "replay_assistant_reasoning": {
          "description": "Whether stored assistant reasoning should be replayed on outbound\nassistant history messages. `Some(false)` strips `reasoning_content`\nand `reasoning` before sending. `None` (default) honours the provider's\nbuilt-in default (true for most compat providers, false for Groq).",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "requires_openai_auth": {
          "description": "When true, the client pulls credentials from ZeroClaw's stored `openai-codex` auth profile instead of the `api_key` field above. Import an existing Codex CLI login with `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json`, or run `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex`. Turn on only for the OpenAI Codex model_provider; leave off for standard API-key model_providers.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "temperature": {
          "description": "Sampling temperature passed to the model. Lower values (0.0–0.3) give\ndeterministic, near-verbatim output, which fits code, routing, summarization.\nHigher values (0.7–1.2) give more varied output, which fits open-ended chat.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "think": {
          "description": "Enable or disable chain-of-thought thinking for models that support it\n(e.g. Qwen3, GLM-4). `true` turns thinking on, `false` turns it off.\n`None` (default) lets the model decide. Forwarded as `enable_thinking`\nin the request body; mirrors the Ollama provider's `think` field.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "description": "HTTP request timeout in seconds. Bump this for slow local model_providers (Ollama on CPU, big local models) or high-latency networks; leave unset otherwise.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "tls_ca_cert_path": {
          "description": "Path to a PEM-encoded CA certificate for TLS connections to this provider.\nMust be an absolute path; shell expansion (e.g. `~`) is not performed.\nLeave unset to use the system's default trust store.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "uri": {
          "description": "Endpoint URI the client hits. Override the family's default endpoint when pointing at a self-hosted gateway (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama), a custom proxy, or any non-standard URL. Leave unset to use the family's default URI from its `ModelEndpoint` impl. Set this to the FULL endpoint URL; there is no separate path-suffix field.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "vision": {
          "description": "Override the provider's vision (image input) capability.\n`None` (default) uses the provider family's built-in default. Several\nfamilies (llama.cpp, the generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint, etc.)\nassume vision-capable because they can serve multimodal models. Set\n`vision = false` for a text-only model served by such a family (e.g. a\ntext LLM behind llama.cpp) so image messages are routed to a configured\n`[multimodal] vision_model_provider` instead of being sent to a model\nthat rejects them. `Some(true)` forces vision on.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "wire_api": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/WireApi"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Wire protocol flavor: `responses` for OpenAI's Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`), `chat_completions` for the legacy chat wire and most OpenAI-compatible gateways. New OpenAI provider slots default to `responses`; other families default to chat-completions (or ignore the field). Only override if you're forcing an unusual combination."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "HunyuanModelProviderConfig": {
      "description": "Named model_provider profile definition.",
      "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "description": "Secret API token for this model_provider. Grab it from the model_provider's dashboard (OpenAI platform, Anthropic console, OpenRouter keys page, etc.). Stored via the OS keyring when possible; never commit it to config.toml directly.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "chat_template_kwargs": {
          "description": "Arbitrary key/value pairs forwarded verbatim as `chat_template_kwargs`\nin the request body (llama.cpp-specific).         },

          "description": "Context window size (max input tokens) for this model.\nAuto-populated on setup from provider's /models endpoint if available.\nOverride manually for custom endpoints or when auto-detection fails.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "extra_headers": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "description": "Extra HTTP headers sent with every request. Niche: used for auth bridges, corporate proxies, or custom gateways that demand a tracing header. Most users never touch this; edit `config.toml` directly if you need it.",
          "type": "object",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "fallback": {
          "description": "Ordered list of other provider aliases to try when every model on this\nalias has failed. Empty means no provider-level fallback.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/ModelProviderRef"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "fallback_models": {
          "description": "Ordered alternate models to try on THIS provider before falling over to\nthe `fallback` aliases. Same endpoint, key, and headers as the primary\n`model`.           "type": "array"

        "kind": {

          "type": "boolean"

    "IMessageConfig": {
      "description": "iMessage channel configuration (macOS only).",
      "properties": {
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Whether this channel is active. The runtime only loads channels whose\n`enabled = true`. Default: `false` so an operator who pastes a partial\n`[channels.<type>.<alias>]` block doesn't accidentally bring a channel\nlive before the rest of its config is filled in.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "excluded_tools": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Tools excluded from this channel's tool spec. When set, these tools\nare not exposed to the model when responding via this channel.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "reply_min_interval_secs": {
          "default": 0,
          "description": "Per-(channel, recipient) outbound pacing floor in seconds.\nRange: `0..=REPLY_MIN_INTERVAL_MAX_SECS` (0 disables).",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "reply_queue_depth_max": {
          "default": 0,
          "description": "Per-(channel, recipient) outbound pacing queue depth.\nRange: `0..=REPLY_QUEUE_DEPTH_CEILING`. When `reply_min_interval_secs > 0`\nand this value is `0`, the pacing wrapper substitutes\n`DEFAULT_REPLY_QUEUE_DEPTH` (16). When the queue is full, the\nnewest send is dropped and a `WARN` is logged.",
          "format": "uint16",
          "maximum": 65535,
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },

    "InceptionModelProviderConfig": {
      "description": "Named model_provider profile definition.",
      "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "description": "Secret API token for this model_provider. Grab it from the model_provider's dashboard (OpenAI platform, Anthropic console, OpenRouter keys page, etc.). Stored via the OS keyring when possible; never commit it to config.toml directly.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "chat_template_kwargs": {
          "description": "Arbitrary key/value pairs forwarded verbatim as `chat_template_kwargs`\nin the request body (llama.cpp-specific). Use this to pass model-family\ntemplate variables that control behaviour not exposed by other fields.\nExample (Qwen3 thinking suppression):\n  `chat_template_kwargs = { enable_thinking = false }`"
        },
        "context_window": {
          "description": "Context window size (max input tokens) for this model.\nAuto-populated on setup from provider's /models endpoint if available.\nOverride manually for custom endpoints or when auto-detection fails.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "extra_headers": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "description": "Extra HTTP headers sent with every request. Niche: used for auth bridges, corporate proxies, or custom gateways that demand a tracing header. Most users never touch this; edit `config.toml` directly if you need it.",
          "type": "object",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "fallback": {
          "description": "Ordered list of other provider aliases to try when every model on this\nalias has failed. Each entry is a dotted `<type>.<alias>` reference into\n`providers.models` and resolves with its own credentials, endpoint, and\nmodel. A fallback never inherits this alias's key. The walk is\ndepth-first: this alias's models are exhausted first, then each fallback\nalias is descended in turn (applying its own `fallback_models` and\n`fallback`). Empty means no provider-level fallback.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/ModelProviderRef"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "fallback_models": {
          "description": "Ordered alternate models to try on THIS provider before falling over to\nthe `fallback` aliases. Same endpoint, key, and headers as the primary\n`model`. Only the model identifier changes. Use this when a provider\nserves a backup model (e.g. a smaller or older variant) that should be\ntried before leaving the provider entirely. Empty means only `model` is\ntried.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "kind": {
          "description": "Provider implementation to instantiate for this profile. Use this\nwhen a canonical typed slot should run through a compatible\nimplementation, e.g. `[providers.models.openai.proxy] kind =\n\"openai-compatible\"`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "live_pricing": {
          "description": "Pull live token prices for this provider's models from its own\nOpenAI-compatible `/models` listing (the gateway is the source of truth\nfor its prices), filling cost-tracking rates for models the operator\nhas NOT priced under `[cost.rates]` / `pricing`. Models the gateway does\nnot price (or providers with no HTTP `/models` listing at all, such as\na subprocess gateway like `kilocli`) fall back to the public models.dev\ncatalog. Configured rates always win; live prices only fill gaps. A\nbackground task refreshes the price snapshot hourly; the cost-recording\npath reads the cached snapshot and never blocks on the network. Default\n`false`: off means no fetching and behavior identical to a build\nwithout the feature.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "max_tokens": {
          "description": "Hard cap on response length in tokens. Most models enforce sensible built-in limits already; leave unset unless you specifically need to clip long outputs for cost or latency reasons.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "merge_system_into_user": {
          "description": "ModelProvider-specific quirk: fold the system prompt into the first user message instead of sending a separate system role. Only needed for models that reject (or mishandle) a standalone system role, e.g. certain older Mistral variants.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "model": {
          "description": "Model identifier to send with each request: the ID string from the model_provider's catalog (e.g. `gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `llama-3.3-70b`). Must match a model the model_provider actually serves on this account.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "native_tools": {
          "description": "Override the provider's default for native tool calling.\n`None` (default) honors the provider's built-in choice. `Some(true)`\nforces native tool calls on, `Some(false)` forces text-fallback.\nCurrently consulted only by the Groq factory, which defaults to\ntext-fallback because llama-family Groq models reject native tool\ncalls with HTTP 400. Setting `native_tools = true` re-enables native\ntool calling for Groq models that support it.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "pricing": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "format": "double",
            "type": "number"
          },
          "description": "Per-model pricing for cost tracking, USD per 1M tokens.\n\nFree-form key/value map. Keys are user-defined model identifiers; an\noptional `.input` / `.output` suffix encodes pricing dimension when\nthe operator wants to split rates. A bare key without a suffix is\nused as a flat per-token rate when neither dimension is specified.\nDefault is empty: cost tracking falls back to \"unknown\" rates and\nonly token usage is recorded.\n\nExample: `pricing = { opus = 15.0, sonnet = 3.0 }`\nOr split: `pricing = { \"opus.input\" = 15.0, \"opus.output\" = 75.0 }`",
          "type": "object"
        },
        "provider_extra": {
          "description": "Extra JSON parameters to include in API requests.\nMerged at the top level of the request body, allowing provider-specific\nfeatures (routing, transforms, etc.) without code changes.\nExample: `provider_extra = { model_provider = { only = [\"Anthropic\"] } }`"
        },
        "replay_assistant_reasoning": {
          "description": "Whether stored assistant reasoning should be replayed on outbound\nassistant history messages. `Some(false)` strips `reasoning_content`\nand `reasoning` before sending. `None` (default) honours the provider's\nbuilt-in default (true for most compat providers, false for Groq).",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "requires_openai_auth": {
          "description": "When true, the client pulls credentials from ZeroClaw's stored `openai-codex` auth profile instead of the `api_key` field above. Import an existing Codex CLI login with `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json`, or run `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex`. Turn on only for the OpenAI Codex model_provider; leave off for standard API-key model_providers.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "temperature": {
          "description": "Sampling temperature passed to the model. Lower values (0.0–0.3) give\ndeterministic, near-verbatim output, which fits code, routing, summarization.\nHigher values (0.7–1.2) give more varied output, which fits open-ended chat.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "think": {
          "description": "Enable or disable chain-of-thought thinking for models that support it\n(e.g. Qwen3, GLM-4). `true` turns thinking on, `false` turns it off.\n`None` (default) lets the model decide. Forwarded as `enable_thinking`\nin the request body; mirrors the Ollama provider's `think` field.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "description": "HTTP request timeout in seconds. Bump this for slow local model_providers (Ollama on CPU, big local models) or high-latency networks; leave unset otherwise.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "tls_ca_cert_path": {
          "description": "Path to a PEM-encoded CA certificate for TLS connections to this provider.\nMust be an absolute path; shell expansion (e.g. `~`) is not performed.\nLeave unset to use the system's default trust store.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "uri": {
          "description": "Endpoint URI the client hits. Override the family's default endpoint when pointing at a self-hosted gateway (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama), a custom proxy, or any non-standard URL. Leave unset to use the family's default URI from its `ModelEndpoint` impl. Set this to the FULL endpoint URL; there is no separate path-suffix field.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "vision": {
          "description": "Override the provider's vision (image input) capability.\n`None` (default) uses the provider family's built-in default. Several\nfamilies (llama.cpp, the generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint, etc.)\nassume vision-capable because they can serve multimodal models. Set\n`vision = false` for a text-only model served by such a family (e.g. a\ntext LLM behind llama.cpp) so image messages are routed to a configured\n`[multimodal] vision_model_provider` instead of being sent to a model\nthat rejects them. `Some(true)` forces vision on.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "wire_api": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/WireApi"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Wire protocol flavor: `responses` for OpenAI's Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`), `chat_completions` for the legacy chat wire and most OpenAI-compatible gateways. New OpenAI provider slots default to `responses`; other families default to chat-completions (or ignore the field). Only override if you're forcing an unusual combination."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "IrcConfig": {
      "description": "IRC channel configuration.",
      "properties": {
        "channels": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Channels to join on connect",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Whether this channel is active. The runtime only loads channels whose\n`enabled = true`. Default: `false` so an operator who pastes a partial\n`[channels.<type>.<alias>]` block doesn't accidentally bring a channel\nlive before the rest of its config is filled in.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "excluded_tools": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Tools excluded from this channel's tool spec. When set, these tools\nare not exposed to the model when responding via this channel.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "mention_only": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "When true, only respond to messages that mention the bot.\nOther messages in the channel are silently ignored.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "nickname": {
          "description": "Bot nickname",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "nickserv_password": {
          "description": "NickServ IDENTIFY password",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "port": {
          "default": 6697,
          "description": "IRC server port (default: 6697 for TLS)",
          "format": "uint16",
          "maximum": 65535,
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "sasl_password": {
          "description": "SASL PLAIN password (IRCv3)",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "server": {
          "description": "IRC server hostname",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "server_password": {
          "description": "Server password (for bouncers like ZNC)",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "username": {
          "description": "Username (defaults to nickname if not set)",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "verify_tls": {
          "description": "Verify TLS certificate (default: true)",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "server",
        "nickname"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    "JiraConfig": {
      "description": "Jira integration configuration (`[jira]`).\n\nWhen `enabled = true`, registers the `jira` tool which can get tickets,\nsearch with JQL, and add comments. Requires `base_url` and `api_token`\n(or the `JIRA_API_TOKEN` env var).\n\n## Defaults\n- `enabled`: `false`\n- `allowed_actions`: `[\"get_ticket\"]` — read-only by default.\n  Add `\"search_tickets\"` or `\"comment_ticket\"` to unlock them.\n- `timeout_secs`: `30`\n\n## Auth\nJira Cloud uses HTTP Basic auth: `email` + `api_token`.\nJira Server/Data Center uses Bearer token auth: omit `email` and set\n`api_token` to a personal access token.\n`api_token` is stored encrypted at rest; set it here or via `JIRA_API_TOKEN`.",
      "properties": {
        "allowed_actions": {
          "default": [
            "get_ticket"
          ],
          "description": "Actions the agent is permitted to call.\nValid values: `\"get_ticket\"`, `\"search_tickets\"`, `\"comment_ticket\"`,\n`\"list_projects\"`, `\"myself\"`, `\"list_transitions\"`,\n`\"transition_ticket\"`, `\"create_ticket\"`.\nDefaults to `[\"get_ticket\"]` (read-only).",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "api_token": {
          "default": "",
          "description": "Jira API token. Encrypted at rest. Falls back to `JIRA_API_TOKEN` env var.",
          "type": "string",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "base_url": {
          "default": "",
          "description": "Atlassian instance base URL, e.g. `https://yourco.atlassian.net`.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "email": {
          "description": "Jira account email used for Basic auth (Cloud).\nOmit for Server/DC deployments using Bearer token auth.\nAn empty string (`email = \"\"`) deserializes as `None`. Configs\nthat round-tripped the empty default to disk would otherwise\nsilently regress to Basic auth with empty username, since the\nemail-required validation was dropped when Server/DC Bearer-token\nsupport landed.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Enable the `jira` tool. Default: `false`.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "default": 30,
          "description": "Request timeout in seconds. Default: `30`.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },

          "description": "Whether stored assistant reasoning should be replayed on outbound\nassistant history messages. `Some(false)` strips `reasoning_content`\nand `reasoning` before sending. `None` (default) honours the provider's\nbuilt-in default (true for most compat providers, false for Groq).",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "requires_openai_auth": {
          "description": "When true, the client pulls credentials from ZeroClaw's stored `openai-codex` auth profile instead of the `api_key` field above. Import an existing Codex CLI login with `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json`, or run `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex`. Turn on only for the OpenAI Codex model_provider; leave off for standard API-key model_providers.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "temperature": {
          "description": "Sampling temperature passed to the model. Lower values (0.0–0.3) give\ndeterministic, near-verbatim output, which fits code, routing, summarization.\nHigher values (0.7–1.2) give more varied output, which fits open-ended chat.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "think": {
          "description": "Enable or disable chain-of-thought thinking for models that support it\n(e.g. Qwen3, GLM-4). `true` turns thinking on, `false` turns it off.\n`None` (default) lets the model decide. Forwarded as `enable_thinking`\nin the request body; mirrors the Ollama provider's `think` field.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "description": "HTTP request timeout in seconds. Bump this for slow local model_providers (Ollama on CPU, big local models) or high-latency networks; leave unset otherwise.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "tls_ca_cert_path": {
          "description": "Path to a PEM-encoded CA certificate for TLS connections to this provider.\nMust be an absolute path; shell expansion (e.g. `~`) is not performed.\nLeave unset to use the system's default trust store.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "uri": {
          "description": "Endpoint URI the client hits. Override the family's default endpoint when pointing at a self-hosted gateway (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama), a custom proxy, or any non-standard URL. Leave unset to use the family's default URI from its `ModelEndpoint` impl. Set this to the FULL endpoint URL; there is no separate path-suffix field.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "vision": {
          "description": "Override the provider's vision (image input) capability.\n`None` (default) uses the provider family's built-in default. Several\nfamilies (llama.cpp, the generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint, etc.)\nassume vision-capable because they can serve multimodal models. Set\n`vision = false` for a text-only model served by such a family (e.g. a\ntext LLM behind llama.cpp) so image messages are routed to a configured\n`[multimodal] vision_model_provider` instead of being sent to a model\nthat rejects them. `Some(true)` forces vision on.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "wire_api": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/WireApi"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Wire protocol flavor: `responses` for OpenAI's Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`), `chat_completions` for the legacy chat wire and most OpenAI-compatible gateways. New OpenAI provider slots default to `responses`; other families default to chat-completions (or ignore the field). Only override if you're forcing an unusual combination."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "KiloEndpoint": {
      "description": "Kilo AI Gateway endpoint. Single canonical endpoint at kilo.ai.",
      "enum": [
        "gateway"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    },
    "KiloModelProviderConfig": {
      "description": "Named model_provider profile definition.",
      "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "description": "Secret API token for this model_provider. Grab it from the model_provider's dashboard (OpenAI platform, Anthropic console, OpenRouter keys page, etc.). Stored via the OS keyring when possible; never commit it to config.toml directly.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "chat_template_kwargs": {
          "description": "Arbitrary key/value pairs forwarded verbatim as `chat_template_kwargs`\nin the request body (llama.cpp-specific). Use this to pass model-family\ntemplate variables that control behaviour not exposed by other fields.\nExample (Qwen3 thinking suppression):\n  `chat_template_kwargs = { enable_thinking = false }`"
        },
        "context_window": {
          "description": "Context window size (max input tokens) for this model.\nAuto-populated on setup from provider's /models endpoint if available.\nOverride manually for custom endpoints or when auto-detection fails.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "endpoint": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/KiloEndpoint",
          "description": "Kilo endpoint variant. Defaults to the canonical Kilo AI Gateway."
        },
        "extra_headers": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "description": "Extra HTTP headers sent with every request. Niche: used for auth bridges, corporate proxies, or custom gateways that demand a tracing header. Most users never touch this; edit `config.toml` directly if you need it.",
          "type": "object",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "fallback": {
          "description": "Ordered list of other provider aliases to try when every model on this\nalias has failed. Each entry is a dotted `<type>.<alias>` reference into\n`providers.models` and resolves with its own credentials, endpoint, and\nmodel. A fallback never inherits this alias's key. The walk is\ndepth-first: this alias's models are exhausted first, then each fallback\nalias is descended in turn (applying its own `fallback_models` and\n`fallback`). Empty means no provider-level fallback.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/ModelProviderRef"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "fallback_models": {
          "description": "Ordered alternate models to try on THIS provider before falling over to\nthe `fallback` aliases. Same endpoint, key, and headers as the primary\n`model`. Only the model identifier changes. Use this when a provider\nserves a backup model (e.g. a smaller or older variant) that should be\ntried before leaving the provider entirely. Empty means only `model` is\ntried.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "kind": {
          "description": "Provider implementation to instantiate for this profile. Use this\nwhen a canonical typed slot should run through a compatible\nimplementation, e.g. `[providers.models.openai.proxy] kind =\n\"openai-compatible\"`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "live_pricing": {
          "description": "Pull live token prices for this provider's models from its own\nOpenAI-compatible `/models` listing (the gateway is the source of truth\nfor its prices), filling cost-tracking rates for models the operator\nhas NOT priced under `[cost.rates]` / `pricing`. Models the gateway does\nnot price (or providers with no HTTP `/models` listing at all, such as\na subprocess gateway like `kilocli`) fall back to the public models.dev\ncatalog. Configured rates always win; live prices only fill gaps. A\nbackground task refreshes the price snapshot hourly; the cost-recording\npath reads the cached snapshot and never blocks on the network. Default\n`false`: off means no fetching and behavior identical to a build\nwithout the feature.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "max_tokens": {
          "description": "Hard cap on response length in tokens. Most models enforce sensible built-in limits already; leave unset unless you specifically need to clip long outputs for cost or latency reasons.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "merge_system_into_user": {
          "description": "ModelProvider-specific quirk: fold the system prompt into the first user message instead of sending a separate system role. Only needed for models that reject (or mishandle) a standalone system role, e.g. certain older Mistral variants.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "model": {
          "description": "Model identifier to send with each request: the ID string from the model_provider's catalog (e.g. `gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `llama-3.3-70b`). Must match a model the model_provider actually serves on this account.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "native_tools": {
          "description": "Override the provider's default for native tool calling.\n`None` (default) honors the provider's built-in choice. `Some(true)`\nforces native tool calls on, `Some(false)` forces text-fallback.\nCurrently consulted only by the Groq factory, which defaults to\ntext-fallback because llama-family Groq models reject native tool\ncalls with HTTP 400. Setting `native_tools = true` re-enables native\ntool calling for Groq models that support it.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "pricing": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "format": "double",
            "type": "number"
          },
          "description": "Per-model pricing for cost tracking, USD per 1M tokens.\n\nFree-form key/value map.           "type": "object"

        "provider_extra": {

      "description": "Named knowledge bundle (`[knowledge_bundles.<alias>]`).\n\nA reusable set of knowledge sources (documents, URLs, or RAG corpus paths)\nthat can be attached to an agent by alias.",

        "suggest_on_query": {

          "type": "boolean"

      "type": "object"
