        },
        "replay_assistant_reasoning": {
          "description": "Whether stored assistant reasoning should be replayed on outbound\nassistant history messages. `Some(false)` strips `reasoning_content`\nand `reasoning` before sending. `None` (default) honours the provider's\nbuilt-in default (true for most compat providers, false for Groq).",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "requires_openai_auth": {
          "description": "When true, the client pulls credentials from ZeroClaw's stored `openai-codex` auth profile instead of the `api_key` field above. Import an existing Codex CLI login with `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json`, or run `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex`. Turn on only for the OpenAI Codex model_provider; leave off for standard API-key model_providers.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "temperature": {
          "description": "Sampling temperature passed to the model. Lower values (0.0–0.3) give\ndeterministic, near-verbatim output, which fits code, routing, summarization.\nHigher values (0.7–1.2) give more varied output, which fits open-ended chat.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "think": {
          "description": "Enable or disable chain-of-thought thinking for models that support it\n(e.g. Qwen3, GLM-4). `true` turns thinking on, `false` turns it off.\n`None` (default) lets the model decide. Forwarded as `enable_thinking`\nin the request body; mirrors the Ollama provider's `think` field.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "description": "HTTP request timeout in seconds. Bump this for slow local model_providers (Ollama on CPU, big local models) or high-latency networks; leave unset otherwise.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "tls_ca_cert_path": {
          "description": "Path to a PEM-encoded CA certificate for TLS connections to this provider.\nMust be an absolute path; shell expansion (e.g. `~`) is not performed.\nLeave unset to use the system's default trust store.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "uri": {
          "description": "Endpoint URI the client hits. Override the family's default endpoint when pointing at a self-hosted gateway (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama), a custom proxy, or any non-standard URL. Leave unset to use the family's default URI from its `ModelEndpoint` impl. Set this to the FULL endpoint URL; there is no separate path-suffix field.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "vision": {
          "description": "Override the provider's vision (image input) capability.\n`None` (default) uses the provider family's built-in default. Several\nfamilies (llama.cpp, the generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint, etc.)\nassume vision-capable because they can serve multimodal models. Set\n`vision = false` for a text-only model served by such a family (e.g. a\ntext LLM behind llama.cpp) so image messages are routed to a configured\n`[multimodal] vision_model_provider` instead of being sent to a model\nthat rejects them. `Some(true)` forces vision on.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "wire_api": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/WireApi"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Wire protocol flavor: `responses` for OpenAI's Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`), `chat_completions` for the legacy chat wire and most OpenAI-compatible gateways. New OpenAI provider slots default to `responses`; other families default to chat-completions (or ignore the field). Only override if you're forcing an unusual combination."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "MochatConfig": {
      "description": "Mochat channel configuration (Mochat customer service API)",
      "properties": {
        "api_token": {
          "description": "Mochat API token",
          "type": "string",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "api_url": {
          "description": "Mochat API base URL",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Whether this channel is active. The runtime only loads channels whose\n`enabled = true`. Default: `false` so an operator who pastes a partial\n`[channels.<type>.<alias>]` block doesn't accidentally bring a channel\nlive before the rest of its config is filled in.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "excluded_tools": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Tools excluded from this channel's tool spec. When set, these tools\nare not exposed to the model when responding via this channel.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "poll_interval_secs": {
          "default": 5,
          "description": "Poll interval in seconds for new messages. Default: 5",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "api_url",
        "api_token"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    "ModelCostRates": {
      "description": "Token-cost rates for a single chat / completion model, in USD per\n1M tokens. Every field optional so partial sheets work without\nceremony (an operator who only knows the input rate can record it).",

          "description": "Cached input tokens (USD per 1M). Optional — leave unset on\nproviders that don't charge separately for prompt cache hits.",

          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "input_per_mtok": {

          "type": [

            "null"

      "type": "object"

    "ModelRouteConfig": {
      "description": "Route a task hint to a specific model_provider + model.\n\n```toml\n[[model_routes]]\nhint = \"reasoning\"\nmodel_provider = \"openrouter.default\"\nmodel = \"anthropic/claude-opus-4-20250514\"\n\n[[model_routes]]\nhint = \"fast\"\nmodel_provider = \"groq.low-latency\"\nmodel = \"llama-3.3-70b-versatile\"\n```\n\nUsage: pass `hint:reasoning` as the model parameter to route the request.",
      "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Optional API key override for this route's model provider",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "hint": {
          "default": "",
          "description": "Task hint name (e.g. \"reasoning\", \"fast\", \"code\", \"summarize\")\n`#[serde(default)]` lets the `create_map_key` macro default-construct\nfrom `{}` before the hint gets injected via `set_prop`. Empty strings\nare rejected by `Config::validate()`.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "model": {
          "default": "",
          "description": "Provider-local model identifier to use with that provider profile\n`#[serde(default)]` is required for `Default` + `create_map_key` construction.\nEmpty strings are rejected by `Config::validate()`.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "model_provider": {
          "default": "",
          "description": "Dotted provider profile ref to route to (must resolve to `providers.models.<type>.<alias>`)\n`#[serde(default)]` is required for `Default` + `create_map_key` construction.\nEmpty strings are rejected by `Config::validate()`.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "MoonshotEndpoint": {
      "description": "Moonshot endpoint variants. Operators pick the region that matches their\naccount; the runtime resolves the URI from the chosen variant unless\noverridden by `base.uri`. Code variant is intl-only.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "cn",
          "description": "Mainland China endpoint.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "intl",
          "description": "International endpoint.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "code",
          "description": "Code-specialist endpoint (intl).",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    },
    "MoonshotModelProviderConfig": {
      "description": "Moonshot model model_provider config. The `endpoint` field is required (no\nimplicit default) — operators must pick a region explicitly. Migration\nfills it in from collapsed `moonshot-cn` / `moonshot-intl` outer keys.",
      "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "description": "Secret API token for this model_provider. Grab it from the model_provider's dashboard (OpenAI platform, Anthropic console, OpenRouter keys page, etc.). Stored via the OS keyring when possible; never commit it to config.toml directly.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "chat_template_kwargs": {
          "description": "Arbitrary key/value pairs forwarded verbatim as `chat_template_kwargs`\nin the request body (llama.cpp-specific). Use this to pass model-family\ntemplate variables that control behaviour not exposed by other fields.\nExample (Qwen3 thinking suppression):\n  `chat_template_kwargs = { enable_thinking = false }`"
        },
        "context_window": {
          "description": "Context window size (max input tokens) for this model.\nAuto-populated on setup from provider's /models endpoint if available.\nOverride manually for custom endpoints or when auto-detection fails.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "endpoint": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/MoonshotEndpoint",
          "default": "intl",
          "description": "Required: pick `cn`, `intl`, or `code`. Defaults to `intl` when omitted\nto ease transition; operators on the China endpoint should set\n`endpoint = \"cn\"` explicitly."
        },
        "extra_headers": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "description": "Extra HTTP headers sent with every request. Niche: used for auth bridges, corporate proxies, or custom gateways that demand a tracing header. Most users never touch this; edit `config.toml` directly if you need it.",
          "type": "object",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "fallback": {
          "description": "Ordered list of other provider aliases to try when every model on this\nalias has failed. Each entry is a dotted `<type>.<alias>` reference into\n`providers.models` and resolves with its own credentials, endpoint, and\nmodel. A fallback never inherits this alias's key. The walk is\ndepth-first: this alias's models are exhausted first, then each fallback\nalias is descended in turn (applying its own `fallback_models` and\n`fallback`). Empty means no provider-level fallback.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/ModelProviderRef"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "fallback_models": {
          "description": "Ordered alternate models to try on THIS provider before falling over to\nthe `fallback` aliases. Same endpoint, key, and headers as the primary\n`model`. Only the model identifier changes. Use this when a provider\nserves a backup model (e.g. a smaller or older variant) that should be\ntried before leaving the provider entirely. Empty means only `model` is\ntried.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "kind": {
          "description": "Provider implementation to instantiate for this profile. Use this\nwhen a canonical typed slot should run through a compatible\nimplementation, e.g. `[providers.models.openai.proxy] kind =\n\"openai-compatible\"`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "live_pricing": {
          "description": "Pull live token prices for this provider's models from its own\nOpenAI-compatible `/models` listing (the gateway is the source of truth\nfor its prices), filling cost-tracking rates for models the operator\nhas NOT priced under `[cost.rates]` / `pricing`. Models the gateway does\nnot price (or providers with no HTTP `/models` listing at all, such as\na subprocess gateway like `kilocli`) fall back to the public models.dev\ncatalog. Configured rates always win; live prices only fill gaps. A\nbackground task refreshes the price snapshot hourly; the cost-recording\npath reads the cached snapshot and never blocks on the network. Default\n`false`: off means no fetching and behavior identical to a build\nwithout the feature.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "max_tokens": {
          "description": "Hard cap on response length in tokens. Most models enforce sensible built-in limits already; leave unset unless you specifically need to clip long outputs for cost or latency reasons.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "merge_system_into_user": {
          "description": "ModelProvider-specific quirk: fold the system prompt into the first user message instead of sending a separate system role. Only needed for models that reject (or mishandle) a standalone system role, e.g. certain older Mistral variants.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "model": {
          "description": "Model identifier to send with each request: the ID string from the model_provider's catalog (e.g. `gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `llama-3.3-70b`). Must match a model the model_provider actually serves on this account.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "native_tools": {
          "description": "Override the provider's default for native tool calling.\n`None` (default) honors the provider's built-in choice. `Some(true)`\nforces native tool calls on, `Some(false)` forces text-fallback.\nCurrently consulted only by the Groq factory, which defaults to\ntext-fallback because llama-family Groq models reject native tool\ncalls with HTTP 400. Setting `native_tools = true` re-enables native\ntool calling for Groq models that support it.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "pricing": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "format": "double",
            "type": "number"
          },
          "description": "Per-model pricing for cost tracking, USD per 1M tokens.\n\nFree-form key/value map. Keys are user-defined model identifiers; an\noptional `.input` / `.output` suffix encodes pricing dimension when\nthe operator wants to split rates. A bare key without a suffix is\nused as a flat per-token rate when neither dimension is specified.\nDefault is empty: cost tracking falls back to \"unknown\" rates and\nonly token usage is recorded.\n\nExample: `pricing = { opus = 15.0, sonnet = 3.0 }`\nOr split: `pricing = { \"opus.input\" = 15.0, \"opus.output\" = 75.0 }`",
          "type": "object"
        },
        "provider_extra": {
          "description": "Extra JSON parameters to include in API requests.\nMerged at the top level of the request body, allowing provider-specific\nfeatures (routing, transforms, etc.) without code changes.\nExample: `provider_extra = { model_provider = { only = [\"Anthropic\"] } }`"
        },
        "replay_assistant_reasoning": {
          "description": "Whether stored assistant reasoning should be replayed on outbound\nassistant history messages. `Some(false)` strips `reasoning_content`\nand `reasoning` before sending. `None` (default) honours the provider's\nbuilt-in default (true for most compat providers, false for Groq).",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "requires_openai_auth": {
          "description": "When true, the client pulls credentials from ZeroClaw's stored `openai-codex` auth profile instead of the `api_key` field above. Import an existing Codex CLI login with `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json`, or run `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex`. Turn on only for the OpenAI Codex model_provider; leave off for standard API-key model_providers.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "temperature": {
          "description": "Sampling temperature passed to the model. Lower values (0.0–0.3) give\ndeterministic, near-verbatim output, which fits code, routing, summarization.\nHigher values (0.7–1.2) give more varied output, which fits open-ended chat.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "think": {
          "description": "Enable or disable chain-of-thought thinking for models that support it\n(e.g. Qwen3, GLM-4). `true` turns thinking on, `false` turns it off.\n`None` (default) lets the model decide. Forwarded as `enable_thinking`\nin the request body; mirrors the Ollama provider's `think` field.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "description": "HTTP request timeout in seconds. Bump this for slow local model_providers (Ollama on CPU, big local models) or high-latency networks; leave unset otherwise.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "tls_ca_cert_path": {
          "description": "Path to a PEM-encoded CA certificate for TLS connections to this provider.\nMust be an absolute path; shell expansion (e.g. `~`) is not performed.\nLeave unset to use the system's default trust store.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "uri": {
          "description": "Endpoint URI the client hits. Override the family's default endpoint when pointing at a self-hosted gateway (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama), a custom proxy, or any non-standard URL. Leave unset to use the family's default URI from its `ModelEndpoint` impl. Set this to the FULL endpoint URL; there is no separate path-suffix field.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "vision": {
          "description": "Override the provider's vision (image input) capability.\n`None` (default) uses the provider family's built-in default. Several\nfamilies (llama.cpp, the generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint, etc.)\nassume vision-capable because they can serve multimodal models. Set\n`vision = false` for a text-only model served by such a family (e.g. a\ntext LLM behind llama.cpp) so image messages are routed to a configured\n`[multimodal] vision_model_provider` instead of being sent to a model\nthat rejects them. `Some(true)` forces vision on.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "wire_api": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/WireApi"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Wire protocol flavor: `responses` for OpenAI's Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`), `chat_completions` for the legacy chat wire and most OpenAI-compatible gateways. New OpenAI provider slots default to `responses`; other families default to chat-completions (or ignore the field). Only override if you're forcing an unusual combination."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },

        "vision": {
          "description": "Override the provider's vision (image input) capability.\n`None` (default) uses the provider family's built-in default. Several\nfamilies (llama.cpp, the generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint, etc.)\nassume vision-capable because they can serve multimodal models. Set\n`vision = false` for a text-only model served by such a family (e.g. a\ntext LLM behind llama.cpp) so image messages are routed to a configured\n`[multimodal] vision_model_provider` instead of being sent to a model\nthat rejects them. `Some(true)` forces vision on.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "wire_api": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/WireApi"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Wire protocol flavor: `responses` for OpenAI's Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`), `chat_completions` for the legacy chat wire and most OpenAI-compatible gateways. New OpenAI provider slots default to `responses`; other families default to chat-completions (or ignore the field). Only override if you're forcing an unusual combination."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "MqttConfig": {
      "description": "MQTT channel configuration (SOP listener).\n\nSubscribes to MQTT topics and dispatches incoming messages\nto the SOP engine for processing.",
      "properties": {
        "broker_url": {
          "description": "MQTT broker URL (e.g., `mqtt://localhost:1883` or `mqtts://broker.example.com:8883`).\nUse `mqtt://` for plain connections or `mqtts://` for TLS.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "client_id": {
          "description": "MQTT client ID (must be unique per broker).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Whether this channel is active. The runtime only loads channels whose\n`enabled = true`. Default: `false` so an operator who pastes a partial\n`[channels.<type>.<alias>]` block doesn't accidentally bring a channel\nlive before the rest of its config is filled in.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "excluded_tools": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Tools excluded from this channel's tool spec. When set, these tools\nare not exposed to the model when responding via this channel.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "keep_alive_secs": {
          "default": 30,
          "description": "Keep-alive interval in seconds (default: 30). Prevents broker disconnect on idle.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "password": {
          "description": "Password for authentication (optional).",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "qos": {
          "default": 1,
          "description": "MQTT QoS level (0 = at-most-once, 1 = at-least-once, 2 = exactly-once). Default: 1.",
          "format": "uint8",
          "maximum": 255,
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "topics": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Topics to subscribe to (e.g., `sensors/#`, `alerts/+/critical`).\nAt least one topic is required.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "use_tls": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Enable TLS encryption. Must match the broker_url scheme:\n- `mqtt://` → `use_tls: false`\n- `mqtts://` → `use_tls: true`",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "username": {
          "description": "Username for authentication (optional).",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "broker_url",
        "client_id"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    "MultimodalConfig": {
      "description": "Multimodal (image) handling configuration (`[multimodal]` section).\n\n# Privacy and cost note\n\nTool results that print real local image paths (e.g. shell tools doing\n`ls /pictures` or `find . -name '*.png'`) are canonicalized into\n`[IMAGE:...]` markers and base64-inlined into the next provider request.\nThis means image bytes that previously stayed local will be uploaded to\nthe configured provider when surfaced by a tool.\n\n`max_images` (and the `trim_old_images` LRU policy) bounds the per-request\nimage budget, but operators running shell-style tools over directories of\npersonal or sensitive images should be aware of the upload semantics. See\n`docs/book/src/contributing/privacy.md` for the project's privacy stance.",
      "properties": {
        "allow_remote_fetch": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Allow fetching remote image URLs (http/https). Disabled by default.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "max_image_size_mb": {
          "default": 5,
          "description": "Maximum image payload size in MiB before base64 encoding.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "max_image_turns": {
          "default": 0,
          "description": "Maximum age of images in conversation turns.\n\nWhen non-zero, images in user messages that are more than this many\nturns back from the end of history are stripped before the request is\nsent to the provider. This prevents a single screenshot from being\nre-encoded and re-uploaded on every subsequent turn indefinitely.\nTool-result images are already managed by the stale-tool-result\nmechanism and are not affected by this setting.\n\n`0` (the default) disables age-based trimming entirely — images are\nonly evicted by the `max_images` count cap.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "max_images": {
          "default": 4,
          "description": "Maximum number of image attachments accepted per request.\n\nCaps the total number of `[IMAGE:...]` markers that survive into the\nprovider request after multimodal preprocessing. Older images are\ndropped first when the cumulative count exceeds this limit. Acts as\nthe upper bound on per-turn upload cost when tool outputs surface\nlocal image paths.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "vision_model": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Model to use when routing to the vision model_provider (e.g. `\"llava:7b\"`).\nOnly used when `vision_model_provider` is set.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "vision_model_provider": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "ModelProvider name to use for vision/image messages (e.g. `\"ollama\"`).\nWhen set, messages containing `[IMAGE:]` markers are routed to this\nmodel_provider instead of the default text model_provider.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "NearaiModelProviderConfig": {
      "description": "Named model_provider profile definition.",
      "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "description": "Secret API token for this model_provider. Grab it from the model_provider's dashboard (OpenAI platform, Anthropic console, OpenRouter keys page, etc.). Stored via the OS keyring when possible; never commit it to config.toml directly.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "chat_template_kwargs": {
          "description": "Arbitrary key/value pairs forwarded verbatim as `chat_template_kwargs`\nin the request body (llama.cpp-specific). Use this to pass model-family\ntemplate variables that control behaviour not exposed by other fields.\nExample (Qwen3 thinking suppression):\n  `chat_template_kwargs = { enable_thinking = false }`"
        },
        "context_window": {
          "description": "Context window size (max input tokens) for this model.\nAuto-populated on setup from provider's /models endpoint if available.\nOverride manually for custom endpoints or when auto-detection fails.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "extra_headers": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "description": "Extra HTTP headers sent with every request. Niche: used for auth bridges, corporate proxies, or custom gateways that demand a tracing header. Most users never touch this; edit `config.toml` directly if you need it.",
          "type": "object",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "fallback": {
          "description": "Ordered list of other provider aliases to try when every model on this\nalias has failed. Each entry is a dotted `<type>.<alias>` reference into\n`providers.models` and resolves with its own credentials, endpoint, and\nmodel. A fallback never inherits this alias's key. The walk is\ndepth-first: this alias's models are exhausted first, then each fallback\nalias is descended in turn (applying its own `fallback_models` and\n`fallback`). Empty means no provider-level fallback.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/ModelProviderRef"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "fallback_models": {
          "description": "Ordered alternate models to try on THIS provider before falling over to\nthe `fallback` aliases. Same endpoint, key, and headers as the primary\n`model`. Only the model identifier changes. Use this when a provider\nserves a backup model (e.g. a smaller or older variant) that should be\ntried before leaving the provider entirely. Empty means only `model` is\ntried.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "kind": {
          "description": "Provider implementation to instantiate for this profile. Use this\nwhen a canonical typed slot should run through a compatible\nimplementation, e.g. `[providers.models.openai.proxy] kind =\n\"openai-compatible\"`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "live_pricing": {
          "description": "Pull live token prices for this provider's models from its own\nOpenAI-compatible `/models` listing (the gateway is the source of truth\nfor its prices), filling cost-tracking rates for models the operator\nhas NOT priced under `[cost.rates]` / `pricing`. Models the gateway does\nnot price (or providers with no HTTP `/models` listing at all, such as\na subprocess gateway like `kilocli`) fall back to the public models.dev\ncatalog. Configured rates always win; live prices only fill gaps. A\nbackground task refreshes the price snapshot hourly; the cost-recording\npath reads the cached snapshot and never blocks on the network. Default\n`false`: off means no fetching and behavior identical to a build\nwithout the feature.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "max_tokens": {
          "description": "Hard cap on response length in tokens. Most models enforce sensible built-in limits already; leave unset unless you specifically need to clip long outputs for cost or latency reasons.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "merge_system_into_user": {
          "description": "ModelProvider-specific quirk: fold the system prompt into the first user message instead of sending a separate system role. Only needed for models that reject (or mishandle) a standalone system role, e.g. certain older Mistral variants.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "model": {
          "description": "Model identifier to send with each request: the ID string from the model_provider's catalog (e.g. `gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `llama-3.3-70b`). Must match a model the model_provider actually serves on this account.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "native_tools": {
          "description": "Override the provider's default for native tool calling.\n`None` (default) honors the provider's built-in choice. `Some(true)`\nforces native tool calls on, `Some(false)` forces text-fallback.\nCurrently consulted only by the Groq factory, which defaults to\ntext-fallback because llama-family Groq models reject native tool\ncalls with HTTP 400. Setting `native_tools = true` re-enables native\ntool calling for Groq models that support it.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "pricing": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "format": "double",
            "type": "number"
          },
          "description": "Per-model pricing for cost tracking, USD per 1M tokens.\n\nFree-form key/value map. Keys are user-defined model identifiers; an\noptional `.input` / `.output` suffix encodes pricing dimension when\nthe operator wants to split rates. A bare key without a suffix is\nused as a flat per-token rate when neither dimension is specified.\nDefault is empty: cost tracking falls back to \"unknown\" rates and\nonly token usage is recorded.\n\nExample: `pricing = { opus = 15.0, sonnet = 3.0 }`\nOr split: `pricing = { \"opus.input\" = 15.0, \"opus.output\" = 75.0 }`",
          "type": "object"
        },
        "provider_extra": {
          "description": "Extra JSON parameters to include in API requests.\nMerged at the top level of the request body, allowing provider-specific\nfeatures (routing, transforms, etc.) without code changes.\nExample: `provider_extra = { model_provider = { only = [\"Anthropic\"] } }`"
        },
        "replay_assistant_reasoning": {
          "description": "Whether stored assistant reasoning should be replayed on outbound\nassistant history messages. `Some(false)` strips `reasoning_content`\nand `reasoning` before sending. `None` (default) honours the provider's\nbuilt-in default (true for most compat providers, false for Groq).",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "requires_openai_auth": {
          "description": "When true, the client pulls credentials from ZeroClaw's stored `openai-codex` auth profile instead of the `api_key` field above. Import an existing Codex CLI login with `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json`, or run `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex`. Turn on only for the OpenAI Codex model_provider; leave off for standard API-key model_providers.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "temperature": {
          "description": "Sampling temperature passed to the model. Lower values (0.0–0.3) give\ndeterministic, near-verbatim output, which fits code, routing, summarization.\nHigher values (0.7–1.2) give more varied output, which fits open-ended chat.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "think": {
          "description": "Enable or disable chain-of-thought thinking for models that support it\n(e.g. Qwen3, GLM-4). `true` turns thinking on, `false` turns it off.\n`None` (default) lets the model decide. Forwarded as `enable_thinking`\nin the request body; mirrors the Ollama provider's `think` field.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "description": "HTTP request timeout in seconds. Bump this for slow local model_providers (Ollama on CPU, big local models) or high-latency networks; leave unset otherwise.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "tls_ca_cert_path": {
          "description": "Path to a PEM-encoded CA certificate for TLS connections to this provider.\nMust be an absolute path; shell expansion (e.g. `~`) is not performed.\nLeave unset to use the system's default trust store.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "uri": {
          "description": "Endpoint URI the client hits. Override the family's default endpoint when pointing at a self-hosted gateway (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama), a custom proxy, or any non-standard URL. Leave unset to use the family's default URI from its `ModelEndpoint` impl. Set this to the FULL endpoint URL; there is no separate path-suffix field.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "vision": {
          "description": "Override the provider's vision (image input) capability.\n`None` (default) uses the provider family's built-in default. Several\nfamilies (llama.cpp, the generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint, etc.)\nassume vision-capable because they can serve multimodal models. Set\n`vision = false` for a text-only model served by such a family (e.g. a\ntext LLM behind llama.cpp) so image messages are routed to a configured\n`[multimodal] vision_model_provider` instead of being sent to a model\nthat rejects them. `Some(true)` forces vision on.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "wire_api": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/WireApi"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Wire protocol flavor: `responses` for OpenAI's Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`), `chat_completions` for the legacy chat wire and most OpenAI-compatible gateways. New OpenAI provider slots default to `responses`; other families default to chat-completions (or ignore the field). Only override if you're forcing an unusual combination."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },

      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "NevisConfig": {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "Nevis IAM integration configuration.\n\nWhen `enabled` is true, ZeroClaw validates incoming requests against a Nevis\nSecurity Suite instance and maps Nevis roles to tool/workspace permissions.",
      "properties": {
        "client_id": {
          "default": "",
          "description": "OAuth2 client ID registered in Nevis.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "client_secret": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "OAuth2 client secret. Encrypted via SecretStore when stored on disk.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Enable Nevis IAM integration. Defaults to false for backward compatibility.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "instance_url": {
          "default": "",
          "description": "Base URL of the Nevis instance (e.g. `https://nevis.example.com`).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "jwks_url": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "JWKS endpoint URL for local token validation.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "realm": {
          "default": "master",
          "description": "Nevis realm to authenticate against.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "require_mfa": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Require MFA verification for all Nevis-authenticated requests.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "role_mapping": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Nevis role to ZeroClaw permission mappings.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/NevisRoleMappingConfig"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "session_timeout_secs": {
          "default": 3600,
          "description": "Session timeout in seconds.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "token_validation": {
          "default": "local",
          "description": "Token validation strategy: `\"local\"` (JWKS) or `\"remote\"` (introspection).",
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "NevisRoleMappingConfig": {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "Maps a Nevis role to ZeroClaw tool permissions and workspace access.",
      "properties": {
        "nevis_role": {
          "description": "Nevis role name (case-insensitive).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "workspace_access": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Workspace names this role can access. Use `\"all\"` for unrestricted.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "zeroclaw_permissions": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Tool names this role can access. Use `\"all\"` for unrestricted tool access.",

            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        }
      },
      "required": [

      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    "NextcloudTalkConfig": {
      "description": "Nextcloud Talk bot configuration (webhook receive + signed bot send API).",
      "properties": {
        "app_token": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Deprecated, unused. Nextcloud Talk sends do not authenticate via\nOCS bearer auth (see `webhook_secret`); this field is only accepted so\nexisting configs that set it don't fail to parse. Safe to remove\nfrom your config.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "base_url": {
          "description": "Nextcloud base URL (e.g. `\"https://cloud.example.com\"`).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "bot_name": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Display name of the bot in Nextcloud Talk (e.g. \"zeroclaw\").\nUsed to filter out the bot's own messages and prevent feedback loops.\nIf not set, defaults to an empty string (no self-message filtering by name).",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "bot_token": {
          "description": "DEPRECATED alias for `webhook_secret`, kept for migration.\n\nNextcloud issues ONE secret per installed bot and uses it for both\ndirections, so this cannot hold a different outbound secret. When both\nare set to different non-empty values the channel logs the conflict and\nfails closed as unconfigured: inbound `401` and no outbound send.\nPrefer `webhook_secret`; this alias will be removed.\n\nUpgrade from a `bot_token`-only configuration: copy the installed bot\nsecret to `webhook_secret`, verify replies still send, then delete\n`bot_token`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "draft_update_interval_ms": {
          "default": 1000,
          "description": "Retained for configuration compatibility. Currently inert while draft\nupdates are disabled for this channel. Default: 1000 ms.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Whether this channel is active. The runtime only loads channels whose\n`enabled = true`. Default: `false` so an operator who pastes a partial\n`[channels.<type>.<alias>]` block doesn't accidentally bring a channel\nlive before the rest of its config is filled in.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "excluded_tools": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Tools excluded from this channel's tool spec. When set, these tools\nare not exposed to the model when responding via this channel.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "proxy_url": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Per-channel proxy URL (http, https, socks5, socks5h).\nOverrides the global `[proxy]` setting for this channel only.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "stream_mode": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/StreamMode",
          "default": "off",
          "description": "Retained for configuration compatibility. Nextcloud Talk's bot API does\nnot provide message IDs or edit/delete operations, so draft updates are\ndisabled and responses are currently sent as one final message for every\nvalue."
        },
        "webhook_secret": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "The bot secret Nextcloud installed for this bot. Canonical field.\n\nUsed for BOTH directions: verifying inbound webhook signatures and\nsigning outbound bot-API requests. When it is unset, inbound webhooks\nare rejected and no outbound request is sent (fail closed).\n\nCan also be set via `ZEROCLAW_NEXTCLOUD_TALK_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "base_url"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    "NgrokTunnelConfig": {
      "properties": {
        "auth_token": {
          "default": "",
          "description": "ngrok auth token",
          "type": "string",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "domain": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Optional custom domain",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },

        },

      "properties": {

    "NovitaModelProviderConfig": {
      "description": "Named model_provider profile definition.",
      "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "description": "Secret API token for this model_provider. Grab it from the model_provider's dashboard (OpenAI platform, Anthropic console, OpenRouter keys page, etc.). Stored via the OS keyring when possible; never commit it to config.toml directly.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "chat_template_kwargs": {
          "description": "Arbitrary key/value pairs forwarded verbatim as `chat_template_kwargs`\nin the request body (llama.cpp-specific). Use this to pass model-family\ntemplate variables that control behaviour not exposed by other fields.\nExample (Qwen3 thinking suppression):\n  `chat_template_kwargs = { enable_thinking = false }`"
        },
        "context_window": {
          "description": "Context window size (max input tokens) for this model.\nAuto-populated on setup from provider's /models endpoint if available.\nOverride manually for custom endpoints or when auto-detection fails.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "extra_headers": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "description": "Extra HTTP headers sent with every request. Niche: used for auth bridges, corporate proxies, or custom gateways that demand a tracing header. Most users never touch this; edit `config.toml` directly if you need it.",
          "type": "object",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "fallback": {
          "description": "Ordered list of other provider aliases to try when every model on this\nalias has failed. Each entry is a dotted `<type>.<alias>` reference into\n`providers.models` and resolves with its own credentials, endpoint, and\nmodel. A fallback never inherits this alias's key. The walk is\ndepth-first: this alias's models are exhausted first, then each fallback\nalias is descended in turn (applying its own `fallback_models` and\n`fallback`). Empty means no provider-level fallback.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/ModelProviderRef"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "fallback_models": {
          "description": "Ordered alternate models to try on THIS provider before falling over to\nthe `fallback` aliases. Same endpoint, key, and headers as the primary\n`model`. Only the model identifier changes. Use this when a provider\nserves a backup model (e.g. a smaller or older variant) that should be\ntried before leaving the provider entirely. Empty means only `model` is\ntried.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "kind": {
          "description": "Provider implementation to instantiate for this profile. Use this\nwhen a canonical typed slot should run through a compatible\nimplementation, e.g. `[providers.models.openai.proxy] kind =\n\"openai-compatible\"`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "live_pricing": {
          "description": "Pull live token prices for this provider's models from its own\nOpenAI-compatible `/models` listing (the gateway is the source of truth\nfor its prices), filling cost-tracking rates for models the operator\nhas NOT priced under `[cost.rates]` / `pricing`. Models the gateway does\nnot price (or providers with no HTTP `/models` listing at all, such as\na subprocess gateway like `kilocli`) fall back to the public models.dev\ncatalog. Configured rates always win; live prices only fill gaps. A\nbackground task refreshes the price snapshot hourly; the cost-recording\npath reads the cached snapshot and never blocks on the network. Default\n`false`: off means no fetching and behavior identical to a build\nwithout the feature.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "max_tokens": {
          "description": "Hard cap on response length in tokens. Most models enforce sensible built-in limits already; leave unset unless you specifically need to clip long outputs for cost or latency reasons.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "merge_system_into_user": {
          "description": "ModelProvider-specific quirk: fold the system prompt into the first user message instead of sending a separate system role. Only needed for models that reject (or mishandle) a standalone system role, e.g. certain older Mistral variants.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "model": {
          "description": "Model identifier to send with each request: the ID string from the model_provider's catalog (e.g. `gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `llama-3.3-70b`). Must match a model the model_provider actually serves on this account.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "native_tools": {
          "description": "Override the provider's default for native tool calling.\n`None` (default) honors the provider's built-in choice. `Some(true)`\nforces native tool calls on, `Some(false)` forces text-fallback.\nCurrently consulted only by the Groq factory, which defaults to\ntext-fallback because llama-family Groq models reject native tool\ncalls with HTTP 400. Setting `native_tools = true` re-enables native\ntool calling for Groq models that support it.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "pricing": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "format": "double",
            "type": "number"
          },
          "description": "Per-model pricing for cost tracking, USD per 1M tokens.\n\nFree-form key/value map. Keys are user-defined model identifiers; an\noptional `.input` / `.output` suffix encodes pricing dimension when\nthe operator wants to split rates. A bare key without a suffix is\nused as a flat per-token rate when neither dimension is specified.\nDefault is empty: cost tracking falls back to \"unknown\" rates and\nonly token usage is recorded.\n\nExample: `pricing = { opus = 15.0, sonnet = 3.0 }`\nOr split: `pricing = { \"opus.input\" = 15.0, \"opus.output\" = 75.0 }`",
          "type": "object"
        },
        "provider_extra": {
          "description": "Extra JSON parameters to include in API requests.\nMerged at the top level of the request body, allowing provider-specific\nfeatures (routing, transforms, etc.) without code changes.\nExample: `provider_extra = { model_provider = { only = [\"Anthropic\"] } }`"
        },
        "replay_assistant_reasoning": {
          "description": "Whether stored assistant reasoning should be replayed on outbound\nassistant history messages. `Some(false)` strips `reasoning_content`\nand `reasoning` before sending. `None` (default) honours the provider's\nbuilt-in default (true for most compat providers, false for Groq).",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "requires_openai_auth": {
          "description": "When true, the client pulls credentials from ZeroClaw's stored `openai-codex` auth profile instead of the `api_key` field above. Import an existing Codex CLI login with `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json`, or run `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex`. Turn on only for the OpenAI Codex model_provider; leave off for standard API-key model_providers.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "temperature": {
          "description": "Sampling temperature passed to the model. Lower values (0.0–0.3) give\ndeterministic, near-verbatim output, which fits code, routing, summarization.\nHigher values (0.7–1.2) give more varied output, which fits open-ended chat.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "think": {
          "description": "Enable or disable chain-of-thought thinking for models that support it\n(e.g. Qwen3, GLM-4). `true` turns thinking on, `false` turns it off.\n`None` (default) lets the model decide. Forwarded as `enable_thinking`\nin the request body; mirrors the Ollama provider's `think` field.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "description": "HTTP request timeout in seconds. Bump this for slow local model_providers (Ollama on CPU, big local models) or high-latency networks; leave unset otherwise.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "tls_ca_cert_path": {
          "description": "Path to a PEM-encoded CA certificate for TLS connections to this provider.\nMust be an absolute path; shell expansion (e.g. `~`) is not performed.\nLeave unset to use the system's default trust store.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "uri": {
          "description": "Endpoint URI the client hits. Override the family's default endpoint when pointing at a self-hosted gateway (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama), a custom proxy, or any non-standard URL. Leave unset to use the family's default URI from its `ModelEndpoint` impl. Set this to the FULL endpoint URL; there is no separate path-suffix field.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "vision": {
          "description": "Override the provider's vision (image input) capability.\n`None` (default) uses the provider family's built-in default. Several\nfamilies (llama.cpp, the generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint, etc.)\nassume vision-capable because they can serve multimodal models. Set\n`vision = false` for a text-only model served by such a family (e.g. a\ntext LLM behind llama.cpp) so image messages are routed to a configured\n`[multimodal] vision_model_provider` instead of being sent to a model\nthat rejects them. `Some(true)` forces vision on.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "wire_api": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/WireApi"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Wire protocol flavor: `responses` for OpenAI's Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`), `chat_completions` for the legacy chat wire and most OpenAI-compatible gateways. New OpenAI provider slots default to `responses`; other families default to chat-completions (or ignore the field). Only override if you're forcing an unusual combination."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },

Models the gateway does\nnot price (or providers with no HTTP `/models` listing at all, such as\na subprocess gateway like `kilocli`) fall back to the public models.dev\ncatalog. Configured rates always win; live prices only fill gaps. A\nbackground task refreshes the price snapshot hourly; the cost-recording\npath reads the cached snapshot and never blocks on the network. Default\n`false`: off means no fetching and behavior identical to a build\nwithout the feature.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "max_tokens": {
          "description": "Hard cap on response length in tokens. Most models enforce sensible built-in limits already; leave unset unless you specifically need to clip long outputs for cost or latency reasons.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "merge_system_into_user": {
          "description": "ModelProvider-specific quirk: fold the system prompt into the first user message instead of sending a separate system role. Only needed for models that reject (or mishandle) a standalone system role, e.g. certain older Mistral variants.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "model": {
          "description": "Model identifier to send with each request: the ID string from the model_provider's catalog (e.g. `gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `llama-3.3-70b`). Must match a model the model_provider actually serves on this account.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "native_tools": {
          "description": "Override the provider's default for native tool calling.\n`None` (default) honors the provider's built-in choice. `Some(true)`\nforces native tool calls on, `Some(false)` forces text-fallback.\nCurrently consulted only by the Groq factory, which defaults to\ntext-fallback because llama-family Groq models reject native tool\ncalls with HTTP 400. Setting `native_tools = true` re-enables native\ntool calling for Groq models that support it.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "pricing": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "format": "double",
            "type": "number"
          },
          "description": "Per-model pricing for cost tracking, USD per 1M tokens.\n\nFree-form key/value map. Keys are user-defined model identifiers; an\noptional `.input` / `.output` suffix encodes pricing dimension when\nthe operator wants to split rates. A bare key without a suffix is\nused as a flat per-token rate when neither dimension is specified.\nDefault is empty: cost tracking falls back to \"unknown\" rates and\nonly token usage is recorded.\n\nExample: `pricing = { opus = 15.0, sonnet = 3.0 }`\nOr split: `pricing = { \"opus.input\" = 15.0, \"opus.output\" = 75.0 }`",
          "type": "object"
        },
        "provider_extra": {
          "description": "Extra JSON parameters to include in API requests.\nMerged at the top level of the request body, allowing provider-specific\nfeatures (routing, transforms, etc.) without code changes.\nExample: `provider_extra = { model_provider = { only = [\"Anthropic\"] } }`"
        },
        "replay_assistant_reasoning": {
          "description": "Whether stored assistant reasoning should be replayed on outbound\nassistant history messages. `Some(false)` strips `reasoning_content`\nand `reasoning` before sending. `None` (default) honours the provider's\nbuilt-in default (true for most compat providers, false for Groq).",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "requires_openai_auth": {
          "description": "When true, the client pulls credentials from ZeroClaw's stored `openai-codex` auth profile instead of the `api_key` field above. Import an existing Codex CLI login with `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json`, or run `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex`. Turn on only for the OpenAI Codex model_provider; leave off for standard API-key model_providers.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "temperature": {
          "description": "Sampling temperature passed to the model. Lower values (0.0–0.3) give\ndeterministic, near-verbatim output, which fits code, routing, summarization.\nHigher values (0.7–1.2) give more varied output, which fits open-ended chat.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "think": {
          "description": "Enable or disable chain-of-thought thinking for models that support it\n(e.g. Qwen3, GLM-4). `true` turns thinking on, `false` turns it off.\n`None` (default) lets the model decide. Forwarded as `enable_thinking`\nin the request body; mirrors the Ollama provider's `think` field.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "description": "HTTP request timeout in seconds. Bump this for slow local model_providers (Ollama on CPU, big local models) or high-latency networks; leave unset otherwise.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "tls_ca_cert_path": {
          "description": "Path to a PEM-encoded CA certificate for TLS connections to this provider.\nMust be an absolute path; shell expansion (e.g. `~`) is not performed.\nLeave unset to use the system's default trust store.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "uri": {
          "description": "Endpoint URI the client hits. Override the family's default endpoint when pointing at a self-hosted gateway (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama), a custom proxy, or any non-standard URL. Leave unset to use the family's default URI from its `ModelEndpoint` impl. Set this to the FULL endpoint URL; there is no separate path-suffix field.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "vision": {
          "description": "Override the provider's vision (image input) capability.\n`None` (default) uses the provider family's built-in default. Several\nfamilies (llama.cpp, the generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint, etc.)\nassume vision-capable because they can serve multimodal models. Set\n`vision = false` for a text-only model served by such a family (e.g. a\ntext LLM behind llama.cpp) so image messages are routed to a configured\n`[multimodal] vision_model_provider` instead of being sent to a model\nthat rejects them. `Some(true)` forces vision on.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "wire_api": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/WireApi"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Wire protocol flavor: `responses` for OpenAI's Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`), `chat_completions` for the legacy chat wire and most OpenAI-compatible gateways. New OpenAI provider slots default to `responses`; other families default to chat-completions (or ignore the field). Only override if you're forcing an unusual combination."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },

    "ObservabilityBackend": {
      "description": "Observability sink backend.",
      "enum": [
        "none",
        "log",
        "verbose",
        "prometheus",
        "otel"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    },
    "ObservabilityConfig": {
      "description": "Observability backend configuration (`[observability]` section).",
      "properties": {
        "backend": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/ObservabilityBackend",
          "default": "none",
          "description": "Observability sink: none | log | verbose | prometheus | otel."
        },
        "log_llm_request_payload": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/LogLlmRequestPayload",
          "default": "off",
          "description": "LLM request payload capture: \"off\" | \"redacted\" | \"full\".\n- `off` (default): only `messages_count` lands on the `llm_request`\n  event. No prompt or conversation content is persisted.\n- `redacted`: the full message history (role + content) is leak-scanned\n  and truncated at `log_tool_io_truncate_bytes` before persisting.\n- `full`: full message history, still leak-scanned, untruncated. For\n  operators who need replay fidelity and accept the disk cost.\n\nOpt-in (default off) because `full`/`redacted` capture the entire system\nprompt and conversation on every turn."
        },
        "log_persistence": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/LogPersistence",
          "default": "rolling",
          "description": "Log persistence mode: \"none\" | \"rolling\" | \"full\".\nControls whether every event passing through `zeroclaw_log::record!`\nis appended to the on-disk JSONL log."
        },
        "log_persistence_max_bytes": {
          "default": 0,
          "description": "Size threshold in bytes that triggers an archive rotation when\n`log_persistence = \"rotating\"`. The active file is rotated once an\nappend leaves it at or above this size. `0` disables size-based\nrotation. Ignored unless `log_persistence = \"rotating\"`.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "log_persistence_max_entries": {
          "default": 200,
          "description": "Maximum entries retained when `log_persistence = \"rolling\"`.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "log_persistence_path": {
          "default": "state/runtime-trace.jsonl",
          "description": "Log persistence file path. Relative paths resolve under workspace_dir.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "log_persistence_retention_max_age_days": {
          "default": 0,
          "description": "Retention cap on the age (in days) of rotated archive files when\n`log_persistence = \"rotating\"`. After a rotation, archives older than\nthis many days are deleted. `0` disables age-based cleanup. Ignored\nunless `log_persistence = \"rotating\"`.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "log_persistence_retention_max_files": {
          "default": 7,
          "description": "Retention cap on the number of rotated archive files kept alongside the\nactive file when `log_persistence = \"rotating\"`. After a rotation the\noldest archives beyond this count are deleted. `0` keeps all archives.\nIgnored unless `log_persistence = \"rotating\"`.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "log_persistence_rotate_daily": {
          "default": true,
          "description": "Rotate the active file to an archive on a UTC day boundary when\n`log_persistence = \"rotating\"`: before the first event of a new day is\nappended, a file whose last write fell on an earlier day is archived.\nIgnored unless `log_persistence = \"rotating\"`.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "log_tool_io": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/LogToolIo",
          "default": "redacted",
          "description": "Tool I/O capture policy: \"off\" | \"redacted\" | \"full\".\n- `off`: only tool name + outcome + duration land in the log.\n- `redacted` (default): tool input + output are leak-scanned and\n  truncated at `log_tool_io_truncate_bytes` before persisting.\n- `full`: full input + output, still leak-scanned. For operators\n  who need replay fidelity and accept the disk cost."
        },
        "log_tool_io_denylist": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Tool names whose I/O is never logged beyond name + outcome + duration\nregardless of `log_tool_io`. Use for tools whose I/O is intrinsically\nsensitive (e.g. memory recall against personal namespaces, agent\nsecret reads). Empty by default.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "log_tool_io_truncate_bytes": {
          "default": 40960,
          "description": "Truncate the captured tool input and output at this many bytes when\n`log_tool_io = \"redacted\"`. Truncated events carry an explicit\n`tool_output_truncated: true` flag plus `tool_output_original_bytes`.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "otel_endpoint": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "OTLP endpoint (e.g. `\"http://localhost:4318\"`). Only used when backend = `\"otel\"`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "otel_genai_content": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/OtelContentPolicy",
          "default": "off",
          "description": "OTel GenAI content capture: \"off\" | \"redacted\" | \"full\".\nControls whether `gen_ai.system_instructions`, `gen_ai.input.messages`,\nand `gen_ai.output.messages` are emitted on OTel spans.\n- `off` (default): no content attributes, only metadata.\n- `redacted`: content is leak-scanned and truncated at `otel_genai_content_max_chars`.\n- `full`: content is leak-scanned but not truncated."
        },
        "otel_genai_content_max_chars": {
          "default": 1000,
          "description": "Per-field character truncation limit for OTel GenAI content when\n`otel_genai_content = \"redacted\"`. Each string field is truncated\nindependently. `0` is treated as `off`.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "otel_headers": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "default": null,
          "description": "Optional HTTP headers sent with every OTLP export request (e.g. authorization).\nSpecified as key-value pairs in TOML:\n```toml\n[observability.otel_headers]\nAuthorization = \"Bearer sk-...\"\n```",
          "type": [
            "object",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "otel_service_name": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Service name reported to the OTel collector. Defaults to \"zeroclaw\".",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "otel_tool_io": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/OtelContentPolicy",
          "default": "off",
          "description": "OTel tool I/O capture: \"off\" | \"redacted\" | \"full\".\nControls whether `gen_ai.tool.arguments`, `input.value`,\n`gen_ai.tool.result`, and `output.value` are emitted on OTel spans.\n- `off` (default): no content attributes, only tool name + outcome.\n- `redacted`: content is leak-scanned and truncated at `otel_tool_io_max_chars`.\n- `full`: content is leak-scanned but not truncated."
        },
        "otel_tool_io_max_chars": {
          "default": 1000,
          "description": "Per-field character truncation limit for OTel tool I/O when\n`otel_tool_io = \"redacted\"`. Each string field is truncated\nindependently. `0` is treated as `off`.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
