The walk is\ndepth-first: this alias's models are exhausted first, then each fallback\nalias is descended in turn (applying its own `fallback_models` and\n`fallback`). Empty means no provider-level fallback.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/ModelProviderRef"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "fallback_models": {
          "description": "Ordered alternate models to try on THIS provider before falling over to\nthe `fallback` aliases. Same endpoint, key, and headers as the primary\n`model`. Only the model identifier changes. Use this when a provider\nserves a backup model (e.g. a smaller or older variant) that should be\ntried before leaving the provider entirely. Empty means only `model` is\ntried.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "kind": {
          "description": "Provider implementation to instantiate for this profile. Use this\nwhen a canonical typed slot should run through a compatible\nimplementation, e.g. `[providers.models.openai.proxy] kind =\n\"openai-compatible\"`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "live_pricing": {
          "description": "Pull live token prices for this provider's models from its own\nOpenAI-compatible `/models` listing (the gateway is the source of truth\nfor its prices), filling cost-tracking rates for models the operator\nhas NOT priced under `[cost.rates]` / `pricing`. Models the gateway does\nnot price (or providers with no HTTP `/models` listing at all, such as\na subprocess gateway like `kilocli`) fall back to the public models.dev\ncatalog. Configured rates always win; live prices only fill gaps. A\nbackground task refreshes the price snapshot hourly; the cost-recording\npath reads the cached snapshot and never blocks on the network. Default\n`false`: off means no fetching and behavior identical to a build\nwithout the feature.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "max_tokens": {
          "description": "Hard cap on response length in tokens. Most models enforce sensible built-in limits already; leave unset unless you specifically need to clip long outputs for cost or latency reasons.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "merge_system_into_user": {
          "description": "ModelProvider-specific quirk: fold the system prompt into the first user message instead of sending a separate system role. Only needed for models that reject (or mishandle) a standalone system role, e.g. certain older Mistral variants.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "model": {
          "description": "Model identifier to send with each request: the ID string from the model_provider's catalog (e.g. `gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `llama-3.3-70b`). Must match a model the model_provider actually serves on this account.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "native_tools": {
          "description": "Override the provider's default for native tool calling.\n`None` (default) honors the provider's built-in choice. `Some(true)`\nforces native tool calls on, `Some(false)` forces text-fallback.\nCurrently consulted only by the Groq factory, which defaults to\ntext-fallback because llama-family Groq models reject native tool\ncalls with HTTP 400. Setting `native_tools = true` re-enables native\ntool calling for Groq models that support it.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "num_ctx": {
          "description": "Override the Ollama `num_ctx` (context window, in tokens) sent on\nevery `/api/chat` request. Defaults to the framework constant\n(`OLLAMA_DEFAULT_NUM_CTX`) when unset.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "num_predict": {
          "description": "Override the Ollama `num_predict` (max output tokens) sent on every\n`/api/chat` request. Defaults to the framework constant\n(`OLLAMA_DEFAULT_NUM_PREDICT`) when unset.",
          "format": "int32",
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "pricing": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "format": "double",
            "type": "number"
          },
          "description": "Per-model pricing for cost tracking, USD per 1M tokens.\n\nFree-form key/value map. Keys are user-defined model identifiers; an\noptional `.input` / `.output` suffix encodes pricing dimension when\nthe operator wants to split rates. A bare key without a suffix is\nused as a flat per-token rate when neither dimension is specified.\nDefault is empty: cost tracking falls back to \"unknown\" rates and\nonly token usage is recorded.\n\nExample: `pricing = { opus = 15.0, sonnet = 3.0 }`\nOr split: `pricing = { \"opus.input\" = 15.0, \"opus.output\" = 75.0 }`",
          "type": "object"
        },
        "provider_extra": {
          "description": "Extra JSON parameters to include in API requests.\nMerged at the top level of the request body, allowing provider-specific\nfeatures (routing, transforms, etc.) without code changes.\nExample: `provider_extra = { model_provider = { only = [\"Anthropic\"] } }`"
        },
        "replay_assistant_reasoning": {
          "description": "Whether stored assistant reasoning should be replayed on outbound\nassistant history messages. `Some(false)` strips `reasoning_content`\nand `reasoning` before sending. `None` (default) honours the provider's\nbuilt-in default (true for most compat providers, false for Groq).",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "requires_openai_auth": {
          "description": "When true, the client pulls credentials from ZeroClaw's stored `openai-codex` auth profile instead of the `api_key` field above. Import an existing Codex CLI login with `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json`, or run `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex`. Turn on only for the OpenAI Codex model_provider; leave off for standard API-key model_providers.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "temperature": {
          "description": "Sampling temperature passed to the model. Lower values (0.0–0.3) give\ndeterministic, near-verbatim output, which fits code, routing, summarization.\nHigher values (0.7–1.2) give more varied output, which fits open-ended chat.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "temperature_override": {
          "description": "Force every Ollama `/api/chat` request to use this temperature,\noverriding the per-call value passed through\n`ModelProvider::chat_with_system(.., temperature)`. When unset\n(`None`, the default), the per-call temperature wins: full\nbackward compatibility.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "think": {
          "description": "Enable or disable chain-of-thought thinking for models that support it\n(e.g. Qwen3, GLM-4). `true` turns thinking on, `false` turns it off.\n`None` (default) lets the model decide. Forwarded as `enable_thinking`\nin the request body; mirrors the Ollama provider's `think` field.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "description": "HTTP request timeout in seconds. Bump this for slow local model_providers (Ollama on CPU, big local models) or high-latency networks; leave unset otherwise.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "tls_ca_cert_path": {
          "description": "Path to a PEM-encoded CA certificate for TLS connections to this provider.\nMust be an absolute path; shell expansion (e.g. `~`) is not performed.\nLeave unset to use the system's default trust store.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "uri": {
          "description": "Endpoint URI the client hits. Override the family's default endpoint when pointing at a self-hosted gateway (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama), a custom proxy, or any non-standard URL. Leave unset to use the family's default URI from its `ModelEndpoint` impl. Set this to the FULL endpoint URL; there is no separate path-suffix field.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "vision": {
          "description": "Override the provider's vision (image input) capability.\n`None` (default) uses the provider family's built-in default. Several\nfamilies (llama.cpp, the generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint, etc.)\nassume vision-capable because they can serve multimodal models. Set\n`vision = false` for a text-only model served by such a family (e.g. a\ntext LLM behind llama.cpp) so image messages are routed to a configured\n`[multimodal] vision_model_provider` instead of being sent to a model\nthat rejects them. `Some(true)` forces vision on.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "wire_api": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/WireApi"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Wire protocol flavor: `responses` for OpenAI's Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`), `chat_completions` for the legacy chat wire and most OpenAI-compatible gateways. New OpenAI provider slots default to `responses`; other families default to chat-completions (or ignore the field). Only override if you're forcing an unusual combination."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "OnNoApprover": {
      "description": "What to do when a configured approver cannot be reached. Default FAIL-CLOSED.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "deny",
          "description": "Fail-closed: deny when the approver is unreachable / declines / times out.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "inherit-originator",
          "description": "Explicit opt-in: fall back to the originating channel (today's behavior).",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    },
    "OnboardStateConfig": {
      "description": "Multi-client workspace isolation configuration.\n\nWhen enabled, each client engagement gets an isolated workspace with\nseparate memory, audit, secrets, and tool restrictions.\nOpaque state the Quickstart flow writes so it can tell, on a\nre-run, which sections the user has already walked through at least\nonce — which lets it offer \"Reconfigure? [y/N]\" skip gates instead of\nforcing users through every field again.\n\nThis is meta-state about the Quickstart flow, not user-facing config.",
      "properties": {
        "completed_sections": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Section keys the user has completed at least once.\nValues are the lowercased Section variant names\n(`\"workspace\"`, `\"model_providers\"`, …).",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "quickstart_completed": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "`true` once the Quickstart has applied a `BuilderSubmission`\nsuccessfully on this install. Web gateway and TUI auto-launch\nthe Quickstart on startup iff this is `false` **and** no\n`agents.*` entries exist (the implicit-completion rule covers\nupgrades). The flag is flipped in the same atomic write that\nlands the Quickstart submission; re-entering the Quickstart\nlater to add another agent does not flip it back to `false`.",
          "type": "boolean"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "OpenAIModelProviderConfig": {
      "description": "OpenAI model model_provider config. OpenAI-compatible families\n(`custom`, `llamacpp`, branded vendors, …) keep the shared\n`ModelProviderConfig` default of unset / chat-completions.\n\nThis default governs **persisted slot creation only**.       "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "description": "Secret API token for this model_provider. Grab it from the model_provider's dashboard (OpenAI platform, Anthropic console, OpenRouter keys page, etc.). Stored via the OS keyring when possible; never commit it to config.toml directly.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "chat_template_kwargs": {
          "description": "Arbitrary key/value pairs forwarded verbatim as `chat_template_kwargs`\nin the request body (llama.cpp-specific). Use this to pass model-family\ntemplate variables that control behaviour not exposed by other fields.\nExample (Qwen3 thinking suppression):\n  `chat_template_kwargs = { enable_thinking = false }`"
        },
        "context_window": {
          "description": "Context window size (max input tokens) for this model.\nAuto-populated on setup from provider's /models endpoint if available.\nOverride manually for custom endpoints or when auto-detection fails.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "extra_headers": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "description": "Extra HTTP headers sent with every request. Niche: used for auth bridges, corporate proxies, or custom gateways that demand a tracing header. Most users never touch this; edit `config.toml` directly if you need it.",
          "type": "object",
          "x-secret": true
        },

          "description": "Ordered list of other provider aliases to try when every model on this\nalias has failed. Each entry is a dotted `<type>.<alias>` reference into\n`providers.models` and resolves with its own credentials, endpoint, and\nmodel. A fallback never inherits this alias's key. The walk is\ndepth-first: this alias's models are exhausted first, then each fallback\nalias is descended in turn (applying its own `fallback_models` and\n`fallback`). Empty means no provider-level fallback.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/ModelProviderRef"

Only the model identifier changes. Use this when a provider\nserves a backup model (e.g. a smaller or older variant) that should be\ntried before leaving the provider entirely. Empty means only `model` is\ntried.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "kind": {
          "description": "Provider implementation to instantiate for this profile. Use this\nwhen a canonical typed slot should run through a compatible\nimplementation, e.g. `[providers.models.openai.proxy] kind =\n\"openai-compatible\"`.",
          "type": [

          ]

          "description": "Pull live token prices for this provider's models from its own\nOpenAI-compatible `/models` listing (the gateway is the source of truth\nfor its prices), filling cost-tracking rates for models the operator\nhas NOT priced under `[cost.rates]` / `pricing`. Models the gateway does\nnot price (or providers with no HTTP `/models` listing at all, such as\na subprocess gateway like `kilocli`) fall back to the public models.dev\ncatalog. Configured rates always win; live prices only fill gaps. A\nbackground task refreshes the price snapshot hourly; the cost-recording\npath reads the cached snapshot and never blocks on the network. Default\n`false`: off means no fetching and behavior identical to a build\nwithout the feature.",
          "type": "boolean"

          "format": "uint32",

    "OpenAITtsProviderConfig": {
      "description": "Per-instance TTS model_provider configuration (`[tts_providers.<type>.<alias>]`).\n\nMirrors `ModelProviderConfig` in shape — one struct holds the union of\nfields across backends. Only the fields relevant to the selected backend\n(determined by the outer `<type>` map key) are read at runtime; others\nare quietly ignored.",
      "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "API key (openai, elevenlabs, google).",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "binary_path": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Path to backend binary (edge-tts subprocess; piper local server).",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "language_code": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Language code for google (e.g. `en-US`).",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "model": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Model name. OpenAI uses this for `tts-1`/`tts-1-hd`; elevenlabs uses\nit as the model_id (e.g. `eleven_monolingual_v1`).",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "response_format": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Audio response format sent to the TTS backend (e.g. `\"opus\"`, `\"mp3\"`,\n`\"wav\"`). Defaults to `\"opus\"` for the OpenAI family. Override to\n`\"wav\"` for Orpheus-class models (e.g. `canopylabs/orpheus-v1-english`\non Groq) or `\"mp3\"` for broader compatibility.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "similarity_boost": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Similarity boost for elevenlabs (0.0-1.0; default `0.5`).",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "speed": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Playback speed multiplier (openai only; default `1.0`).",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "stability": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Voice stability for elevenlabs (0.0-1.0; default `0.5`).",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "uri": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Endpoint URI for HTTP-based backends. Overrides the family default\nwhen pointing at a compatible third-party API (Groq, Azure, self-hosted\nproxies). Set to the **full** URL — there is no separate path-suffix\nfield. Renamed from `api_url` for parity with `ModelProviderConfig.uri`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "voice": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Voice override for this instance. When empty, falls back to\n`[tts].default_voice`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "OpenAiSttConfig": {
      "description": "OpenAI Whisper STT model_provider configuration (`[transcription.openai]`).",
      "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "OpenAI API key for Whisper transcription.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "model": {

          "description": "Whisper model name (default: \"whisper-1\").",

    },
    "OpenAiTranscriptionProviderConfig": {
      "description": "Shared base for cloud transcription providers. Each cloud family\ncomposes this via `#[serde(flatten)] base: TranscriptionProviderConfig`.",
      "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "API key for the transcription provider.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "initial_prompt": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Whisper-style initial prompt to bias the model toward expected\nvocabulary (proper nouns, technical terms). Provider-specific support;\nsilently ignored where not applicable.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "language": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Optional language hint passed to the provider (ISO-639-1 like `\"en\"` /\n`\"ru\"`, or BCP-47 like `\"en-US\"` for Google). Most providers auto-detect\nwhen this is unset.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "model": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Whisper model name (default: `\"whisper-1\"`).",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "OpenCodeCliConfig": {
      "description": "OpenCode CLI tool configuration (`[opencode_cli]` section).\n\nDelegates coding tasks to the `opencode run` CLI. Authentication uses the\nbinary's own session by default — no API key needed unless\n`env_passthrough` includes provider-specific keys.",
      "properties": {
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Enable the `opencode_cli` tool",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "env_passthrough": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Extra env vars passed to the opencode subprocess",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "max_output_bytes": {
          "default": 2097152,
          "description": "Maximum output size in bytes (2MB default)",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "default": 600,
          "description": "Maximum execution time in seconds (coding tasks can be long)",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "OpenRouterModelProviderConfig": {
      "description": "Named model_provider profile definition.",
      "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "description": "Secret API token for this model_provider. Grab it from the model_provider's dashboard (OpenAI platform, Anthropic console, OpenRouter keys page, etc.). Stored via the OS keyring when possible; never commit it to config.toml directly.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "chat_template_kwargs": {
          "description": "Arbitrary key/value pairs forwarded verbatim as `chat_template_kwargs`\nin the request body (llama.cpp-specific). Use this to pass model-family\ntemplate variables that control behaviour not exposed by other fields.\nExample (Qwen3 thinking suppression):\n  `chat_template_kwargs = { enable_thinking = false }`"
        },
        "context_window": {
          "description": "Context window size (max input tokens) for this model.\nAuto-populated on setup from provider's /models endpoint if available.\nOverride manually for custom endpoints or when auto-detection fails.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "extra_headers": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "description": "Extra HTTP headers sent with every request. Niche: used for auth bridges, corporate proxies, or custom gateways that demand a tracing header. Most users never touch this; edit `config.toml` directly if you need it.",
          "type": "object",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "fallback": {
          "description": "Ordered list of other provider aliases to try when every model on this\nalias has failed. Each entry is a dotted `<type>.<alias>` reference into\n`providers.models` and resolves with its own credentials, endpoint, and\nmodel. A fallback never inherits this alias's key. The walk is\ndepth-first: this alias's models are exhausted first, then each fallback\nalias is descended in turn (applying its own `fallback_models` and\n`fallback`). Empty means no provider-level fallback.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/ModelProviderRef"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "fallback_models": {
          "description": "Ordered alternate models to try on THIS provider before falling over to\nthe `fallback` aliases. Same endpoint, key, and headers as the primary\n`model`. Only the model identifier changes. Use this when a provider\nserves a backup model (e.g. a smaller or older variant) that should be\ntried before leaving the provider entirely. Empty means only `model` is\ntried.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "kind": {
          "description": "Provider implementation to instantiate for this profile. Use this\nwhen a canonical typed slot should run through a compatible\nimplementation, e.g. `[providers.models.openai.proxy] kind =\n\"openai-compatible\"`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "live_pricing": {
          "description": "Pull live token prices for this provider's models from its own\nOpenAI-compatible `/models` listing (the gateway is the source of truth\nfor its prices), filling cost-tracking rates for models the operator\nhas NOT priced under `[cost.rates]` / `pricing`. Models the gateway does\nnot price (or providers with no HTTP `/models` listing at all, such as\na subprocess gateway like `kilocli`) fall back to the public models.dev\ncatalog. Configured rates always win; live prices only fill gaps. A\nbackground task refreshes the price snapshot hourly; the cost-recording\npath reads the cached snapshot and never blocks on the network. Default\n`false`: off means no fetching and behavior identical to a build\nwithout the feature.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "max_tokens": {
          "description": "Hard cap on response length in tokens. Most models enforce sensible built-in limits already; leave unset unless you specifically need to clip long outputs for cost or latency reasons.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "merge_system_into_user": {
          "description": "ModelProvider-specific quirk: fold the system prompt into the first user message instead of sending a separate system role. Only needed for models that reject (or mishandle) a standalone system role, e.g. certain older Mistral variants.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "model": {
          "description": "Model identifier to send with each request: the ID string from the model_provider's catalog (e.g. `gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `llama-3.3-70b`). Must match a model the model_provider actually serves on this account.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "native_tools": {
          "description": "Override the provider's default for native tool calling.\n`None` (default) honors the provider's built-in choice. `Some(true)`\nforces native tool calls on, `Some(false)` forces text-fallback.\nCurrently consulted only by the Groq factory, which defaults to\ntext-fallback because llama-family Groq models reject native tool\ncalls with HTTP 400. Setting `native_tools = true` re-enables native\ntool calling for Groq models that support it.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "pricing": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "format": "double",
            "type": "number"
          },
          "description": "Per-model pricing for cost tracking, USD per 1M tokens.\n\nFree-form key/value map. Keys are user-defined model identifiers; an\noptional `.input` / `.output` suffix encodes pricing dimension when\nthe operator wants to split rates. A bare key without a suffix is\nused as a flat per-token rate when neither dimension is specified.\nDefault is empty: cost tracking falls back to \"unknown\" rates and\nonly token usage is recorded.\n\nExample: `pricing = { opus = 15.0, sonnet = 3.0 }`\nOr split: `pricing = { \"opus.input\" = 15.0, \"opus.output\" = 75.0 }`",
          "type": "object"
        },
        "provider_extra": {
          "description": "Extra JSON parameters to include in API requests.\nMerged at the top level of the request body, allowing provider-specific\nfeatures (routing, transforms, etc.) without code changes.\nExample: `provider_extra = { model_provider = { only = [\"Anthropic\"] } }`"
        },
        "replay_assistant_reasoning": {
          "description": "Whether stored assistant reasoning should be replayed on outbound\nassistant history messages. `Some(false)` strips `reasoning_content`\nand `reasoning` before sending. `None` (default) honours the provider's\nbuilt-in default (true for most compat providers, false for Groq).",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "requires_openai_auth": {
          "description": "When true, the client pulls credentials from ZeroClaw's stored `openai-codex` auth profile instead of the `api_key` field above. Import an existing Codex CLI login with `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json`, or run `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex`. Turn on only for the OpenAI Codex model_provider; leave off for standard API-key model_providers.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "temperature": {
          "description": "Sampling temperature passed to the model. Lower values (0.0–0.3) give\ndeterministic, near-verbatim output, which fits code, routing, summarization.\nHigher values (0.7–1.2) give more varied output, which fits open-ended chat.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "think": {
          "description": "Enable or disable chain-of-thought thinking for models that support it\n(e.g. Qwen3, GLM-4). `true` turns thinking on, `false` turns it off.\n`None` (default) lets the model decide. Forwarded as `enable_thinking`\nin the request body; mirrors the Ollama provider's `think` field.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "description": "HTTP request timeout in seconds. Bump this for slow local model_providers (Ollama on CPU, big local models) or high-latency networks; leave unset otherwise.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "tls_ca_cert_path": {
          "description": "Path to a PEM-encoded CA certificate for TLS connections to this provider.\nMust be an absolute path; shell expansion (e.g. `~`) is not performed.\nLeave unset to use the system's default trust store.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "uri": {
          "description": "Endpoint URI the client hits. Override the family's default endpoint when pointing at a self-hosted gateway (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama), a custom proxy, or any non-standard URL. Leave unset to use the family's default URI from its `ModelEndpoint` impl. Set this to the FULL endpoint URL; there is no separate path-suffix field.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "vision": {
          "description": "Override the provider's vision (image input) capability.\n`None` (default) uses the provider family's built-in default. Several\nfamilies (llama.cpp, the generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint, etc.)\nassume vision-capable because they can serve multimodal models. Set\n`vision = false` for a text-only model served by such a family (e.g. a\ntext LLM behind llama.cpp) so image messages are routed to a configured\n`[multimodal] vision_model_provider` instead of being sent to a model\nthat rejects them. `Some(true)` forces vision on.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "wire_api": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/WireApi"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Wire protocol flavor: `responses` for OpenAI's Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`), `chat_completions` for the legacy chat wire and most OpenAI-compatible gateways. New OpenAI provider slots default to `responses`; other families default to chat-completions (or ignore the field). Only override if you're forcing an unusual combination."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "OpenVpnTunnelConfig": {
      "description": "OpenVPN tunnel configuration (`[tunnel.openvpn]`).\n\nRequired when `tunnel.tunnel_provider = \"openvpn\"`. Omitting this section entirely\npreserves previous behavior. Setting `tunnel.tunnel_provider = \"none\"` (or removing\nthe `[tunnel.openvpn]` block) cleanly reverts to no-tunnel mode.\n\nDefaults: `connect_timeout_secs = 30`.",
      "properties": {
        "advertise_address": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Advertised address once VPN is connected (e.g., `\"10.8.0.2:42617\"`).\nWhen omitted the tunnel falls back to `http://{local_host}:{local_port}`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "auth_file": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Optional path to auth credentials file (`--auth-user-pass`).",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "config_file": {
          "description": "Path to `.ovpn` configuration file (must not be empty).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "connect_timeout_secs": {
          "default": 30,
          "description": "Connection timeout in seconds (default: 30, must be > 0).",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "extra_args": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Extra openvpn CLI arguments forwarded verbatim.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "config_file"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },

          "description": "Provider implementation to instantiate for this profile. Use this\nwhen a canonical typed slot should run through a compatible\nimplementation, e.g. `[providers.models.openai.proxy] kind =\n\"openai-compatible\"`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "live_pricing": {
          "description": "Pull live token prices for this provider's models from its own\nOpenAI-compatible `/models` listing (the gateway is the source of truth\nfor its prices), filling cost-tracking rates for models the operator\nhas NOT priced under `[cost.rates]` / `pricing`. Models the gateway does\nnot price (or providers with no HTTP `/models` listing at all, such as\na subprocess gateway like `kilocli`) fall back to the public models.dev\ncatalog. Configured rates always win; live prices only fill gaps. A\nbackground task refreshes the price snapshot hourly; the cost-recording\npath reads the cached snapshot and never blocks on the network. Default\n`false`: off means no fetching and behavior identical to a build\nwithout the feature.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "max_tokens": {
          "description": "Hard cap on response length in tokens. Most models enforce sensible built-in limits already; leave unset unless you specifically need to clip long outputs for cost or latency reasons.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "merge_system_into_user": {
          "description": "ModelProvider-specific quirk: fold the system prompt into the first user message instead of sending a separate system role. Only needed for models that reject (or mishandle) a standalone system role, e.g. certain older Mistral variants.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "model": {
          "description": "Model identifier to send with each request: the ID string from the model_provider's catalog (e.g. `gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `llama-3.3-70b`). Must match a model the model_provider actually serves on this account.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "native_tools": {
          "description": "Override the provider's default for native tool calling.\n`None` (default) honors the provider's built-in choice. `Some(true)`\nforces native tool calls on, `Some(false)` forces text-fallback.\nCurrently consulted only by the Groq factory, which defaults to\ntext-fallback because llama-family Groq models reject native tool\ncalls with HTTP 400. Setting `native_tools = true` re-enables native\ntool calling for Groq models that support it.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "pricing": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "format": "double",
            "type": "number"
          },
          "description": "Per-model pricing for cost tracking, USD per 1M tokens.\n\nFree-form key/value map. Keys are user-defined model identifiers; an\noptional `.input` / `.output` suffix encodes pricing dimension when\nthe operator wants to split rates. A bare key without a suffix is\nused as a flat per-token rate when neither dimension is specified.\nDefault is empty: cost tracking falls back to \"unknown\" rates and\nonly token usage is recorded.\n\nExample: `pricing = { opus = 15.0, sonnet = 3.0 }`\nOr split: `pricing = { \"opus.input\" = 15.0, \"opus.output\" = 75.0 }`",
          "type": "object"
        },
        "provider_extra": {
          "description": "Extra JSON parameters to include in API requests.\nMerged at the top level of the request body, allowing provider-specific\nfeatures (routing, transforms, etc.) without code changes.\nExample: `provider_extra = { model_provider = { only = [\"Anthropic\"] } }`"
        },
        "replay_assistant_reasoning": {
          "description": "Whether stored assistant reasoning should be replayed on outbound\nassistant history messages. `Some(false)` strips `reasoning_content`\nand `reasoning` before sending. `None` (default) honours the provider's\nbuilt-in default (true for most compat providers, false for Groq).",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "requires_openai_auth": {
          "description": "When true, the client pulls credentials from ZeroClaw's stored `openai-codex` auth profile instead of the `api_key` field above. Import an existing Codex CLI login with `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json`, or run `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex`. Turn on only for the OpenAI Codex model_provider; leave off for standard API-key model_providers.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "temperature": {
          "description": "Sampling temperature passed to the model. Lower values (0.0–0.3) give\ndeterministic, near-verbatim output, which fits code, routing, summarization.\nHigher values (0.7–1.2) give more varied output, which fits open-ended chat.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "think": {
          "description": "Enable or disable chain-of-thought thinking for models that support it\n(e.g. Qwen3, GLM-4). `true` turns thinking on, `false` turns it off.\n`None` (default) lets the model decide. Forwarded as `enable_thinking`\nin the request body; mirrors the Ollama provider's `think` field.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "description": "HTTP request timeout in seconds. Bump this for slow local model_providers (Ollama on CPU, big local models) or high-latency networks; leave unset otherwise.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "tls_ca_cert_path": {
          "description": "Path to a PEM-encoded CA certificate for TLS connections to this provider.\nMust be an absolute path; shell expansion (e.g. `~`) is not performed.\nLeave unset to use the system's default trust store.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "uri": {
          "description": "Endpoint URI the client hits. Override the family's default endpoint when pointing at a self-hosted gateway (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama), a custom proxy, or any non-standard URL. Leave unset to use the family's default URI from its `ModelEndpoint` impl. Set this to the FULL endpoint URL; there is no separate path-suffix field.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "vision": {
          "description": "Override the provider's vision (image input) capability.\n`None` (default) uses the provider family's built-in default. Several\nfamilies (llama.cpp, the generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint, etc.)\nassume vision-capable because they can serve multimodal models. Set\n`vision = false` for a text-only model served by such a family (e.g. a\ntext LLM behind llama.cpp) so image messages are routed to a configured\n`[multimodal] vision_model_provider` instead of being sent to a model\nthat rejects them. `Some(true)` forces vision on.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "wire_api": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/WireApi"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Wire protocol flavor: `responses` for OpenAI's Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`), `chat_completions` for the legacy chat wire and most OpenAI-compatible gateways. New OpenAI provider slots default to `responses`; other families default to chat-completions (or ignore the field). Only override if you're forcing an unusual combination."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "OtelContentPolicy": {
      "description": "OTel content capture policy. Mirrors [`LogToolIo`] but gates OTel span\nattribute emission, not log persistence. Defaults to `Off` for privacy.",
      "enum": [
        "off",
        "redacted",
        "full"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    },
    "OtpConfig": {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "Security OTP configuration.",
      "properties": {
        "cache_valid_secs": {
          "default": 300,
          "description": "Reuse window for recently validated OTP codes.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "challenge_max_attempts": {
          "default": 3,
          "description": "Maximum number of OTP challenge attempts before lockout.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Enable OTP gating. Defaults to disabled for backward compatibility.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "gated_actions": {
          "default": [
            "shell",
            "file_write",
            "browser_open",
            "browser",
            "memory_forget"
          ],
          "description": "Tool/action names gated by OTP. Empty or malformed entries are rejected\nat config load; an entry that does not match a known gated action is\naccepted but logged at WARN, since it cannot be enforced.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "gated_domain_categories": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Domain-category presets expanded into `gated_domains`.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "gated_domains": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Explicit domain patterns gated by OTP.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "method": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/OtpMethod",
          "default": "totp",
          "description": "OTP method."
        },
        "token_ttl_secs": {
          "default": 30,
          "description": "TOTP time-step in seconds.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "OtpMethod": {
      "description": "OTP validation strategy.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "totp",
          "description": "Time-based one-time password (RFC 6238).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "pairing",
          "description": "Future method for paired-device confirmations.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "cli-prompt",
          "description": "Future method for local CLI challenge prompts.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    },
    "OutputModality": {
      "description": "Preferred output modality for a peer group.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "mirror",
          "description": "Always reply in kind — voice note if user sent voice, text otherwise.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "voice",
          "description": "Always deliver via TTS as a voice note, regardless of input modality.\nApplies to proactive messages (cron, announces) as well as replies.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "text",
          "description": "Always deliver as text, even if user sent a voice note.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    },

    "PacingConfig": {
      "description": "Pacing controls for slow/local LLM workloads (`[pacing]` section).\n\nAll fields are optional and default to values that preserve existing\nbehavior. When set, they extend — not replace — the existing timeout\nand loop-detection subsystems.",
      "properties": {
        "loop_detection_enabled": {
          "default": true,
          "description": "Enable pattern-based loop detection (exact repeat, ping-pong,\nno-progress). Defaults to `true`.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "loop_detection_max_repeats": {
          "default": 3,
          "description": "Number of consecutive identical tool+args calls before the first\nescalation (Warning). Defaults to 3.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "loop_detection_min_elapsed_secs": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Minimum elapsed seconds before loop detection activates.\nTasks completing under this threshold get aggressive loop protection;\nlonger-running tasks receive a grace period before the detector starts\ncounting. `None` means loop detection is always active (existing behavior).",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "loop_detection_window_size": {
          "default": 20,
          "description": "Sliding window size for the pattern-based loop detector.\nDefaults to 20.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "loop_ignore_tools": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Tool names excluded from identical-output / alternating-pattern loop\ndetection. Useful for browser workflows where `browser_screenshot`\nstructurally resembles a loop even when making progress.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "message_timeout_scale_max": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Override for the hardcoded timeout scaling cap (default: 4).\nThe channel message timeout budget is computed as:\n  `message_timeout_secs * min(max_tool_iterations, message_timeout_scale_max)`\nRaising this value lets long multi-step tasks with slow local models\nreceive a proportionally larger budget without inflating the base timeout.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "step_timeout_secs": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Per-step timeout in seconds: the maximum time allowed for a single\nLLM inference turn, independent of the total message budget.\n`None` means no per-step timeout (existing behavior).",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "PairingDashboardConfig": {
      "description": "Pairing dashboard configuration (`[gateway.pairing_dashboard]`).",
      "properties": {
        "code_length": {
          "default": 8,
          "description": "Length of pairing codes (default: 8)",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "code_ttl_secs": {
          "default": 3600,
          "description": "Time-to-live for pending pairing codes in seconds (default: 3600)",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "lockout_secs": {
          "default": 300,
          "description": "Lockout duration in seconds after max attempts (default: 300)",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "max_failed_attempts": {
          "default": 5,
          "description": "Maximum failed pairing attempts before lockout (default: 5)",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "max_pending_codes": {
          "default": 3,
          "description": "Maximum concurrent pending pairing codes (default: 3)",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "PeerGroupConfig": {
      "description": "`[peer_groups.<name>]` — mutual-opt-in peer group on a channel type.",
      "properties": {
        "admin_for_agent_scope": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "When `true`, members of this peer group are authorized to issue\n`/model --agent <model>` on the agent this group is bound to.\nDefault `false` (deny-by-default). The runtime resolves this live\nfrom `Config::peer_groups` at command-dispatch time via\n`Config::channel_agent_scope_admins`; no cache, no per-channel\nduplicate sender list.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "agents": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Member agents by alias.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/AgentAlias"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "channel": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/ChannelRef",
          "default": "",
          "description": "Either a channel type (`\"telegram\"`) or a dotted channel alias\n(`\"telegram.work\"`). A bare type applies to every alias of that\ntype; a dotted form scopes the group to that single instance."
        },
        "external_peers": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Non-agent members by channel-native username.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/PeerUsername"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "ignore": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Per-group blocklist; subtracts from the resolved peer set.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/PeerUsername"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "output_modality": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/OutputModality",
          "default": "mirror",
          "description": "Preferred output modality for all peers in this group.\nDefaults to `mirror` (input-driven). Set to `voice` to have the\nagent always reply and deliver proactive messages (cron, announces)\nas TTS voice notes on channels that support audio output."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "PeerUsername": {
      "description": "Reference to a configured `[channels.peers.<type>.<alias>]` entry.\nEmpty value means \"no preference\" (opt-out). Non-empty values must\nresolve to a configured alias; `Config::validate()` enforces this.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "PeripheralBoardConfig": {
      "description": "Configuration for a single peripheral board (e.g. STM32, RPi GPIO).",
      "properties": {
        "baud": {
          "default": 115200,
          "description": "Baud rate for serial (default: 115200)",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "board": {
          "description": "Board type: \"nucleo-f401re\", \"rpi-gpio\", \"esp32\", etc.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "path": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Path for serial: \"/dev/ttyACM0\", \"/dev/ttyUSB0\"",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "transport": {
          "default": "serial",
          "description": "Transport: \"serial\", \"native\", \"websocket\"",
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "board"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    "PeripheralsConfig": {
      "description": "Peripheral board integration configuration (`[peripherals]` section).\n\nBoards become agent tools when enabled.",
      "properties": {
        "boards": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Board configurations (nucleo-f401re, rpi-gpio, etc.)",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/PeripheralBoardConfig"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "datasheet_dir": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Path to datasheet docs (relative to workspace) for RAG retrieval.\nPlace .md/.txt files named by board (e.g. nucleo-f401re.md, rpi-gpio.md).",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Enable peripheral support (boards become agent tools)",
          "type": "boolean"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "PerplexityModelProviderConfig": {
      "description": "Named model_provider profile definition.",
      "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "description": "Secret API token for this model_provider. Grab it from the model_provider's dashboard (OpenAI platform, Anthropic console, OpenRouter keys page, etc.). Stored via the OS keyring when possible; never commit it to config.toml directly.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "chat_template_kwargs": {
          "description": "Arbitrary key/value pairs forwarded verbatim as `chat_template_kwargs`\nin the request body (llama.cpp-specific). Use this to pass model-family\ntemplate variables that control behaviour not exposed by other fields.\nExample (Qwen3 thinking suppression):\n  `chat_template_kwargs = { enable_thinking = false }`"
        },
        "context_window": {
          "description": "Context window size (max input tokens) for this model.\nAuto-populated on setup from provider's /models endpoint if available.\nOverride manually for custom endpoints or when auto-detection fails.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "extra_headers": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "description": "Extra HTTP headers sent with every request. Niche: used for auth bridges, corporate proxies, or custom gateways that demand a tracing header. Most users never touch this; edit `config.toml` directly if you need it.",
          "type": "object",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "fallback": {
          "description": "Ordered list of other provider aliases to try when every model on this\nalias has failed. Each entry is a dotted `<type>.<alias>` reference into\n`providers.models` and resolves with its own credentials, endpoint, and\nmodel. A fallback never inherits this alias's key. The walk is\ndepth-first: this alias's models are exhausted first, then each fallback\nalias is descended in turn (applying its own `fallback_models` and\n`fallback`). Empty means no provider-level fallback.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/ModelProviderRef"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "fallback_models": {
          "description": "Ordered alternate models to try on THIS provider before falling over to\nthe `fallback` aliases. Same endpoint, key, and headers as the primary\n`model`. Only the model identifier changes. Use this when a provider\nserves a backup model (e.g. a smaller or older variant) that should be\ntried before leaving the provider entirely. Empty means only `model` is\ntried.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "kind": {
          "description": "Provider implementation to instantiate for this profile. Use this\nwhen a canonical typed slot should run through a compatible\nimplementation, e.g. `[providers.models.openai.proxy] kind =\n\"openai-compatible\"`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "live_pricing": {
          "description": "Pull live token prices for this provider's models from its own\nOpenAI-compatible `/models` listing (the gateway is the source of truth\nfor its prices), filling cost-tracking rates for models the operator\nhas NOT priced under `[cost.rates]` / `pricing`. Models the gateway does\nnot price (or providers with no HTTP `/models` listing at all, such as\na subprocess gateway like `kilocli`) fall back to the public models.dev\ncatalog. Configured rates always win; live prices only fill gaps. A\nbackground task refreshes the price snapshot hourly; the cost-recording\npath reads the cached snapshot and never blocks on the network. Default\n`false`: off means no fetching and behavior identical to a build\nwithout the feature.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "max_tokens": {
          "description": "Hard cap on response length in tokens. Most models enforce sensible built-in limits already; leave unset unless you specifically need to clip long outputs for cost or latency reasons.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "merge_system_into_user": {
          "description": "ModelProvider-specific quirk: fold the system prompt into the first user message instead of sending a separate system role. Only needed for models that reject (or mishandle) a standalone system role, e.g. certain older Mistral variants.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "model": {
          "description": "Model identifier to send with each request: the ID string from the model_provider's catalog (e.g. `gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `llama-3.3-70b`). Must match a model the model_provider actually serves on this account.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "native_tools": {
          "description": "Override the provider's default for native tool calling.\n`None` (default) honors the provider's built-in choice. `Some(true)`\nforces native tool calls on, `Some(false)` forces text-fallback.\nCurrently consulted only by the Groq factory, which defaults to\ntext-fallback because llama-family Groq models reject native tool\ncalls with HTTP 400. Setting `native_tools = true` re-enables native\ntool calling for Groq models that support it.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "pricing": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "format": "double",
            "type": "number"
          },
          "description": "Per-model pricing for cost tracking, USD per 1M tokens.\n\nFree-form key/value map. Keys are user-defined model identifiers; an\noptional `.input` / `.output` suffix encodes pricing dimension when\nthe operator wants to split rates. A bare key without a suffix is\nused as a flat per-token rate when neither dimension is specified.\nDefault is empty: cost tracking falls back to \"unknown\" rates and\nonly token usage is recorded.\n\nExample: `pricing = { opus = 15.0, sonnet = 3.0 }`\nOr split: `pricing = { \"opus.input\" = 15.0, \"opus.output\" = 75.0 }`",
          "type": "object"
        },
        "provider_extra": {
          "description": "Extra JSON parameters to include in API requests.\nMerged at the top level of the request body, allowing provider-specific\nfeatures (routing, transforms, etc.) without code changes.\nExample: `provider_extra = { model_provider = { only = [\"Anthropic\"] } }`"
        },
        "replay_assistant_reasoning": {
          "description": "Whether stored assistant reasoning should be replayed on outbound\nassistant history messages. `Some(false)` strips `reasoning_content`\nand `reasoning` before sending. `None` (default) honours the provider's\nbuilt-in default (true for most compat providers, false for Groq).",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "requires_openai_auth": {
          "description": "When true, the client pulls credentials from ZeroClaw's stored `openai-codex` auth profile instead of the `api_key` field above. Import an existing Codex CLI login with `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json`, or run `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex`. Turn on only for the OpenAI Codex model_provider; leave off for standard API-key model_providers.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "temperature": {
          "description": "Sampling temperature passed to the model. Lower values (0.0–0.3) give\ndeterministic, near-verbatim output, which fits code, routing, summarization.\nHigher values (0.7–1.2) give more varied output, which fits open-ended chat.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "think": {
          "description": "Enable or disable chain-of-thought thinking for models that support it\n(e.g. Qwen3, GLM-4). `true` turns thinking on, `false` turns it off.\n`None` (default) lets the model decide. Forwarded as `enable_thinking`\nin the request body; mirrors the Ollama provider's `think` field.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "description": "HTTP request timeout in seconds. Bump this for slow local model_providers (Ollama on CPU, big local models) or high-latency networks; leave unset otherwise.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "tls_ca_cert_path": {
          "description": "Path to a PEM-encoded CA certificate for TLS connections to this provider.\nMust be an absolute path; shell expansion (e.g. `~`) is not performed.\nLeave unset to use the system's default trust store.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "uri": {
          "description": "Endpoint URI the client hits. Override the family's default endpoint when pointing at a self-hosted gateway (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama), a custom proxy, or any non-standard URL. Leave unset to use the family's default URI from its `ModelEndpoint` impl. Set this to the FULL endpoint URL; there is no separate path-suffix field.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "vision": {
          "description": "Override the provider's vision (image input) capability.\n`None` (default) uses the provider family's built-in default. Several\nfamilies (llama.cpp, the generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint, etc.)\nassume vision-capable because they can serve multimodal models. Set\n`vision = false` for a text-only model served by such a family (e.g. a\ntext LLM behind llama.cpp) so image messages are routed to a configured\n`[multimodal] vision_model_provider` instead of being sent to a model\nthat rejects them. `Some(true)` forces vision on.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "wire_api": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/WireApi"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Wire protocol flavor: `responses` for OpenAI's Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`), `chat_completions` for the legacy chat wire and most OpenAI-compatible gateways. New OpenAI provider slots default to `responses`; other families default to chat-completions (or ignore the field). Only override if you're forcing an unusual combination."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },

    "PiperTtsProviderConfig": {
      "description": "Per-instance TTS model_provider configuration (`[tts_providers.<type>.<alias>]`).\n\nMirrors `ModelProviderConfig` in shape — one struct holds the union of\nfields across backends. Only the fields relevant to the selected backend\n(determined by the outer `<type>` map key) are read at runtime; others\nare quietly ignored.",

            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "model": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Model name. OpenAI uses this for `tts-1`/`tts-1-hd`; elevenlabs uses\nit as the model_id (e.g. `eleven_monolingual_v1`).",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "response_format": {

          "type": [

          ]
        },

            "null"
          ]
        },
        "speed": {

            "null"
          ]
        },
        "stability": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Voice stability for elevenlabs (0.0-1.0; default `0.5`).",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "uri": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Endpoint URI for HTTP-based backends. Overrides the family default\nwhen pointing at a compatible third-party API (Groq, Azure, self-hosted\nproxies). Set to the **full** URL — there is no separate path-suffix\nfield. Renamed from `api_url` for parity with `ModelProviderConfig.uri`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "voice": {

          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "PluginEntryConfig": {
      "description": "Per-plugin config section keyed by plugin alias; values are secret so they\nencrypt at rest under the same adjacent `.secret_key` as every other secret.",
      "properties": {
        "config": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "default": {},
          "type": "object",

        },

          "default": "",
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "PluginLimitsConfig": {
      "description": "Per-call WASM execution limits (`[plugins.limits]`).\n\nBounds a single plugin call so a runaway or malicious component traps\ninstead of hanging the host or exhausting memory. `call_fuel` caps\ninstructions per call; the memory, table, and instance ceilings bound a\nstore's growth. Every value is operator-tunable and validated as non-zero.",
      "properties": {
        "call_fuel": {
          "default": 1000000000,
          "description": "Fuel budget per plugin call (wasmtime instruction units).",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "max_instances": {
          "default": 64,
          "description": "Maximum component instances a plugin store may create.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "max_memory_mb": {
          "default": 256,
          "description": "Maximum linear memory a plugin store may grow to, in megabytes.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "max_table_elements": {
          "default": 100000,
          "description": "Maximum table elements a plugin store may allocate.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "PluginSecurityConfig": {
      "description": "Plugin signature verification configuration (`[plugins.security]`).\n\nControls Ed25519 signature verification for plugin manifests.\nIn `strict` mode, only plugins signed by a trusted publisher key are loaded.\nIn `permissive` mode, unsigned or untrusted plugins produce warnings but are\nstill loaded. In `disabled` mode (the default), no signature checking occurs.",
      "properties": {
        "signature_mode": {
          "default": "disabled",
          "description": "Signature enforcement mode: \"disabled\", \"permissive\", or \"strict\".",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "trusted_publisher_keys": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Hex-encoded Ed25519 public keys of trusted plugin publishers.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
