    "ProxyConfig": {
      "description": "Proxy configuration for outbound HTTP/HTTPS/SOCKS5 traffic (`[proxy]` section).",
      "properties": {
        "all_proxy": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Fallback proxy URL for all schemes.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Enable proxy support for selected scope.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "http_proxy": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Proxy URL for HTTP requests (supports http, https, socks5, socks5h).",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "https_proxy": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Proxy URL for HTTPS requests (supports http, https, socks5, socks5h).",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "no_proxy": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "No-proxy bypass list. Same format as NO_PROXY.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "scope": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/ProxyScope",
          "default": "zeroclaw",
          "description": "Proxy application scope."
        },
        "services": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Service selectors used when scope = \"services\".",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "ProxyScope": {
      "description": "Proxy application scope — determines which outbound traffic uses the proxy.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "environment",
          "description": "Use system environment proxy variables only.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "zeroclaw",
          "description": "Apply proxy to all ZeroClaw-managed HTTP traffic (default).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "services",
          "description": "Apply proxy only to explicitly listed service selectors.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    },
    "QQConfig": {
      "description": "QQ Official Bot configuration (Tencent QQ Bot SDK)",
      "properties": {
        "app_id": {
          "description": "App ID from QQ Bot developer console",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "app_secret": {
          "description": "App Secret from QQ Bot developer console",
          "type": "string",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Whether this channel is active. The runtime only loads channels whose\n`enabled = true`. Default: `false` so an operator who pastes a partial\n`[channels.<type>.<alias>]` block doesn't accidentally bring a channel\nlive before the rest of its config is filled in.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "excluded_tools": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Tools excluded from this channel's tool spec. When set, these tools\nare not exposed to the model when responding via this channel.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "proxy_url": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Per-channel proxy URL (http, https, socks5, socks5h).\nOverrides the global `[proxy]` setting for this channel only.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "app_id",
        "app_secret"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    "QdrantStorageConfig": {
      "description": "Qdrant vector database backend (`[storage.qdrant.<alias>]`).\n\nURL, collection, and API key are typed config values. Use schema-mirror env\noverrides such as `ZEROCLAW_storage__qdrant__<alias>__url=...` for runtime\nenv injection.",
      "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "API key for Qdrant Cloud or secured instances.\nUse `ZEROCLAW_storage__qdrant__<alias>__api_key=...` for env injection.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "collection": {
          "default": "zeroclaw_memories",
          "description": "Collection name for storing memories.\nUse `ZEROCLAW_storage__qdrant__<alias>__collection=...` for env injection.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "url": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Qdrant server URL (e.g. `\"http://localhost:6333\"`).\nUse `ZEROCLAW_storage__qdrant__<alias>__url=...` for env injection.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "QianfanModelProviderConfig": {
      "description": "Named model_provider profile definition.",
      "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "description": "Secret API token for this model_provider. Grab it from the model_provider's dashboard (OpenAI platform, Anthropic console, OpenRouter keys page, etc.). Stored via the OS keyring when possible; never commit it to config.toml directly.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "chat_template_kwargs": {
          "description": "Arbitrary key/value pairs forwarded verbatim as `chat_template_kwargs`\nin the request body (llama.cpp-specific). Use this to pass model-family\ntemplate variables that control behaviour not exposed by other fields.\nExample (Qwen3 thinking suppression):\n  `chat_template_kwargs = { enable_thinking = false }`"
        },
        "context_window": {
          "description": "Context window size (max input tokens) for this model.\nAuto-populated on setup from provider's /models endpoint if available.\nOverride manually for custom endpoints or when auto-detection fails.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "extra_headers": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "description": "Extra HTTP headers sent with every request. Niche: used for auth bridges, corporate proxies, or custom gateways that demand a tracing header. Most users never touch this; edit `config.toml` directly if you need it.",
          "type": "object",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "fallback": {
          "description": "Ordered list of other provider aliases to try when every model on this\nalias has failed. Each entry is a dotted `<type>.<alias>` reference into\n`providers.models` and resolves with its own credentials, endpoint, and\nmodel. A fallback never inherits this alias's key. The walk is\ndepth-first: this alias's models are exhausted first, then each fallback\nalias is descended in turn (applying its own `fallback_models` and\n`fallback`). Empty means no provider-level fallback.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/ModelProviderRef"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "fallback_models": {
          "description": "Ordered alternate models to try on THIS provider before falling over to\nthe `fallback` aliases. Same endpoint, key, and headers as the primary\n`model`. Only the model identifier changes. Use this when a provider\nserves a backup model (e.g. a smaller or older variant) that should be\ntried before leaving the provider entirely. Empty means only `model` is\ntried.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "kind": {
          "description": "Provider implementation to instantiate for this profile. Use this\nwhen a canonical typed slot should run through a compatible\nimplementation, e.g. `[providers.models.openai.proxy] kind =\n\"openai-compatible\"`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "live_pricing": {
          "description": "Pull live token prices for this provider's models from its own\nOpenAI-compatible `/models` listing (the gateway is the source of truth\nfor its prices), filling cost-tracking rates for models the operator\nhas NOT priced under `[cost.rates]` / `pricing`. Models the gateway does\nnot price (or providers with no HTTP `/models` listing at all, such as\na subprocess gateway like `kilocli`) fall back to the public models.dev\ncatalog. Configured rates always win; live prices only fill gaps. A\nbackground task refreshes the price snapshot hourly; the cost-recording\npath reads the cached snapshot and never blocks on the network. Default\n`false`: off means no fetching and behavior identical to a build\nwithout the feature.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "max_tokens": {
          "description": "Hard cap on response length in tokens. Most models enforce sensible built-in limits already; leave unset unless you specifically need to clip long outputs for cost or latency reasons.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "merge_system_into_user": {
          "description": "ModelProvider-specific quirk: fold the system prompt into the first user message instead of sending a separate system role. Only needed for models that reject (or mishandle) a standalone system role, e.g. certain older Mistral variants.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "model": {
          "description": "Model identifier to send with each request: the ID string from the model_provider's catalog (e.g. `gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `llama-3.3-70b`). Must match a model the model_provider actually serves on this account.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "native_tools": {
          "description": "Override the provider's default for native tool calling.\n`None` (default) honors the provider's built-in choice. `Some(true)`\nforces native tool calls on, `Some(false)` forces text-fallback.\nCurrently consulted only by the Groq factory, which defaults to\ntext-fallback because llama-family Groq models reject native tool\ncalls with HTTP 400. Setting `native_tools = true` re-enables native\ntool calling for Groq models that support it.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "pricing": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "format": "double",
            "type": "number"
          },
          "description": "Per-model pricing for cost tracking, USD per 1M tokens.\n\nFree-form key/value map. Keys are user-defined model identifiers; an\noptional `.input` / `.output` suffix encodes pricing dimension when\nthe operator wants to split rates. A bare key without a suffix is\nused as a flat per-token rate when neither dimension is specified.\nDefault is empty: cost tracking falls back to \"unknown\" rates and\nonly token usage is recorded.\n\nExample: `pricing = { opus = 15.0, sonnet = 3.0 }`\nOr split: `pricing = { \"opus.input\" = 15.0, \"opus.output\" = 75.0 }`",
          "type": "object"
        },
        "provider_extra": {
          "description": "Extra JSON parameters to include in API requests.\nMerged at the top level of the request body, allowing provider-specific\nfeatures (routing, transforms, etc.) without code changes.\nExample: `provider_extra = { model_provider = { only = [\"Anthropic\"] } }`"
        },
        "replay_assistant_reasoning": {
          "description": "Whether stored assistant reasoning should be replayed on outbound\nassistant history messages. `Some(false)` strips `reasoning_content`\nand `reasoning` before sending. `None` (default) honours the provider's\nbuilt-in default (true for most compat providers, false for Groq).",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "requires_openai_auth": {
          "description": "When true, the client pulls credentials from ZeroClaw's stored `openai-codex` auth profile instead of the `api_key` field above. Import an existing Codex CLI login with `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json`, or run `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex`. Turn on only for the OpenAI Codex model_provider; leave off for standard API-key model_providers.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "temperature": {
          "description": "Sampling temperature passed to the model. Lower values (0.0–0.3) give\ndeterministic, near-verbatim output, which fits code, routing, summarization.\nHigher values (0.7–1.2) give more varied output, which fits open-ended chat.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "think": {
          "description": "Enable or disable chain-of-thought thinking for models that support it\n(e.g. Qwen3, GLM-4). `true` turns thinking on, `false` turns it off.\n`None` (default) lets the model decide. Forwarded as `enable_thinking`\nin the request body; mirrors the Ollama provider's `think` field.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "description": "HTTP request timeout in seconds. Bump this for slow local model_providers (Ollama on CPU, big local models) or high-latency networks; leave unset otherwise.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "tls_ca_cert_path": {
          "description": "Path to a PEM-encoded CA certificate for TLS connections to this provider.\nMust be an absolute path; shell expansion (e.g. `~`) is not performed.\nLeave unset to use the system's default trust store.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "uri": {
          "description": "Endpoint URI the client hits. Override the family's default endpoint when pointing at a self-hosted gateway (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama), a custom proxy, or any non-standard URL. Leave unset to use the family's default URI from its `ModelEndpoint` impl. Set this to the FULL endpoint URL; there is no separate path-suffix field.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "vision": {
          "description": "Override the provider's vision (image input) capability.\n`None` (default) uses the provider family's built-in default. Several\nfamilies (llama.cpp, the generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint, etc.)\nassume vision-capable because they can serve multimodal models. Set\n`vision = false` for a text-only model served by such a family (e.g. a\ntext LLM behind llama.cpp) so image messages are routed to a configured\n`[multimodal] vision_model_provider` instead of being sent to a model\nthat rejects them. `Some(true)` forces vision on.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "wire_api": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/WireApi"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Wire protocol flavor: `responses` for OpenAI's Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`), `chat_completions` for the legacy chat wire and most OpenAI-compatible gateways. New OpenAI provider slots default to `responses`; other families default to chat-completions (or ignore the field). Only override if you're forcing an unusual combination."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },

Set\n`vision = false` for a text-only model served by such a family (e.g. a\ntext LLM behind llama.cpp) so image messages are routed to a configured\n`[multimodal] vision_model_provider` instead of being sent to a model\nthat rejects them. `Some(true)` forces vision on.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "wire_api": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/WireApi"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Wire protocol flavor: `responses` for OpenAI's Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`), `chat_completions` for the legacy chat wire and most OpenAI-compatible gateways. New OpenAI provider slots default to `responses`; other families default to chat-completions (or ignore the field). Only override if you're forcing an unusual combination."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "RedditConfig": {
      "description": "Reddit channel configuration (OAuth2 bot).",
      "properties": {
        "client_id": {
          "description": "Reddit OAuth2 client ID.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "client_secret": {
          "description": "Reddit OAuth2 client secret.",
          "type": "string",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Whether this channel is active. The runtime only loads channels whose\n`enabled = true`. Default: `false` so an operator who pastes a partial\n`[channels.<type>.<alias>]` block doesn't accidentally bring a channel\nlive before the rest of its config is filled in.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "excluded_tools": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Tools excluded from this channel's tool spec. When set, these tools\nare not exposed to the model when responding via this channel.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "refresh_token": {
          "description": "Reddit OAuth2 refresh token for persistent access.",
          "type": "string",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "subreddits": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Subreddits to filter messages (without `r/` prefix). Empty = accept\nfrom any subreddit the bot has access to. Migrated from the legacy\n`subreddit` singular field.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "username": {
          "description": "Reddit bot username (without `u/` prefix).",
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "client_id",
        "client_secret",
        "refresh_token",
        "username"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    "RekaModelProviderConfig": {
      "description": "Named model_provider profile definition.",
      "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "description": "Secret API token for this model_provider. Grab it from the model_provider's dashboard (OpenAI platform, Anthropic console, OpenRouter keys page, etc.). Stored via the OS keyring when possible; never commit it to config.toml directly.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "chat_template_kwargs": {
          "description": "Arbitrary key/value pairs forwarded verbatim as `chat_template_kwargs`\nin the request body (llama.cpp-specific). Use this to pass model-family\ntemplate variables that control behaviour not exposed by other fields.\nExample (Qwen3 thinking suppression):\n  `chat_template_kwargs = { enable_thinking = false }`"
        },
        "context_window": {
          "description": "Context window size (max input tokens) for this model.\nAuto-populated on setup from provider's /models endpoint if available.\nOverride manually for custom endpoints or when auto-detection fails.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "extra_headers": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "description": "Extra HTTP headers sent with every request. Niche: used for auth bridges, corporate proxies, or custom gateways that demand a tracing header. Most users never touch this; edit `config.toml` directly if you need it.",
          "type": "object",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "fallback": {
          "description": "Ordered list of other provider aliases to try when every model on this\nalias has failed. Each entry is a dotted `<type>.<alias>` reference into\n`providers.models` and resolves with its own credentials, endpoint, and\nmodel. A fallback never inherits this alias's key. The walk is\ndepth-first: this alias's models are exhausted first, then each fallback\nalias is descended in turn (applying its own `fallback_models` and\n`fallback`). Empty means no provider-level fallback.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/ModelProviderRef"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "fallback_models": {
          "description": "Ordered alternate models to try on THIS provider before falling over to\nthe `fallback` aliases. Same endpoint, key, and headers as the primary\n`model`. Only the model identifier changes. Use this when a provider\nserves a backup model (e.g. a smaller or older variant) that should be\ntried before leaving the provider entirely. Empty means only `model` is\ntried.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "kind": {
          "description": "Provider implementation to instantiate for this profile. Use this\nwhen a canonical typed slot should run through a compatible\nimplementation, e.g. `[providers.models.openai.proxy] kind =\n\"openai-compatible\"`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "live_pricing": {
          "description": "Pull live token prices for this provider's models from its own\nOpenAI-compatible `/models` listing (the gateway is the source of truth\nfor its prices), filling cost-tracking rates for models the operator\nhas NOT priced under `[cost.rates]` / `pricing`. Models the gateway does\nnot price (or providers with no HTTP `/models` listing at all, such as\na subprocess gateway like `kilocli`) fall back to the public models.dev\ncatalog. Configured rates always win; live prices only fill gaps. A\nbackground task refreshes the price snapshot hourly; the cost-recording\npath reads the cached snapshot and never blocks on the network. Default\n`false`: off means no fetching and behavior identical to a build\nwithout the feature.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "max_tokens": {
          "description": "Hard cap on response length in tokens. Most models enforce sensible built-in limits already; leave unset unless you specifically need to clip long outputs for cost or latency reasons.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "merge_system_into_user": {
          "description": "ModelProvider-specific quirk: fold the system prompt into the first user message instead of sending a separate system role. Only needed for models that reject (or mishandle) a standalone system role, e.g. certain older Mistral variants.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "model": {
          "description": "Model identifier to send with each request: the ID string from the model_provider's catalog (e.g. `gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `llama-3.3-70b`). Must match a model the model_provider actually serves on this account.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "native_tools": {
          "description": "Override the provider's default for native tool calling.\n`None` (default) honors the provider's built-in choice. `Some(true)`\nforces native tool calls on, `Some(false)` forces text-fallback.\nCurrently consulted only by the Groq factory, which defaults to\ntext-fallback because llama-family Groq models reject native tool\ncalls with HTTP 400. Setting `native_tools = true` re-enables native\ntool calling for Groq models that support it.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "pricing": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "format": "double",
            "type": "number"
          },
          "description": "Per-model pricing for cost tracking, USD per 1M tokens.\n\nFree-form key/value map. Keys are user-defined model identifiers; an\noptional `.input` / `.output` suffix encodes pricing dimension when\nthe operator wants to split rates. A bare key without a suffix is\nused as a flat per-token rate when neither dimension is specified.\nDefault is empty: cost tracking falls back to \"unknown\" rates and\nonly token usage is recorded.\n\nExample: `pricing = { opus = 15.0, sonnet = 3.0 }`\nOr split: `pricing = { \"opus.input\" = 15.0, \"opus.output\" = 75.0 }`",
          "type": "object"
        },
        "provider_extra": {
          "description": "Extra JSON parameters to include in API requests.\nMerged at the top level of the request body, allowing provider-specific\nfeatures (routing, transforms, etc.) without code changes.\nExample: `provider_extra = { model_provider = { only = [\"Anthropic\"] } }`"
        },
        "replay_assistant_reasoning": {
          "description": "Whether stored assistant reasoning should be replayed on outbound\nassistant history messages. `Some(false)` strips `reasoning_content`\nand `reasoning` before sending. `None` (default) honours the provider's\nbuilt-in default (true for most compat providers, false for Groq).",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "requires_openai_auth": {
          "description": "When true, the client pulls credentials from ZeroClaw's stored `openai-codex` auth profile instead of the `api_key` field above. Import an existing Codex CLI login with `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json`, or run `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex`. Turn on only for the OpenAI Codex model_provider; leave off for standard API-key model_providers.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "temperature": {
          "description": "Sampling temperature passed to the model. Lower values (0.0–0.3) give\ndeterministic, near-verbatim output, which fits code, routing, summarization.\nHigher values (0.7–1.2) give more varied output, which fits open-ended chat.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "think": {
          "description": "Enable or disable chain-of-thought thinking for models that support it\n(e.g. Qwen3, GLM-4). `true` turns thinking on, `false` turns it off.\n`None` (default) lets the model decide. Forwarded as `enable_thinking`\nin the request body; mirrors the Ollama provider's `think` field.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "description": "HTTP request timeout in seconds. Bump this for slow local model_providers (Ollama on CPU, big local models) or high-latency networks; leave unset otherwise.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "tls_ca_cert_path": {
          "description": "Path to a PEM-encoded CA certificate for TLS connections to this provider.\nMust be an absolute path; shell expansion (e.g. `~`) is not performed.\nLeave unset to use the system's default trust store.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "uri": {
          "description": "Endpoint URI the client hits. Override the family's default endpoint when pointing at a self-hosted gateway (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama), a custom proxy, or any non-standard URL. Leave unset to use the family's default URI from its `ModelEndpoint` impl. Set this to the FULL endpoint URL; there is no separate path-suffix field.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "vision": {
          "description": "Override the provider's vision (image input) capability.\n`None` (default) uses the provider family's built-in default. Several\nfamilies (llama.cpp, the generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint, etc.)\nassume vision-capable because they can serve multimodal models. Set\n`vision = false` for a text-only model served by such a family (e.g. a\ntext LLM behind llama.cpp) so image messages are routed to a configured\n`[multimodal] vision_model_provider` instead of being sent to a model\nthat rejects them. `Some(true)` forces vision on.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "wire_api": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/WireApi"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Wire protocol flavor: `responses` for OpenAI's Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`), `chat_completions` for the legacy chat wire and most OpenAI-compatible gateways. New OpenAI provider slots default to `responses`; other families default to chat-completions (or ignore the field). Only override if you're forcing an unusual combination."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "ReliabilityConfig": {
      "description": "Reliability and supervision configuration (`[reliability]` section).\n\nControls model_provider retries, API key rotation, and channel restart backoff.",
      "properties": {
        "api_keys": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Additional API keys for round-robin rotation on rate-limit (429) errors.\nThe primary `api_key` is always tried first; these are extras.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "channel_initial_backoff_secs": {
          "default": 2,
          "description": "Initial backoff for channel/daemon restarts.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "channel_max_backoff_secs": {
          "default": 60,
          "description": "Max backoff for channel/daemon restarts.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "provider_backoff_ms": {
          "default": 500,
          "description": "Base backoff (ms) for model_provider retry delay.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "provider_retries": {
          "default": 2,
          "description": "Retries per model_provider before bailing.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "scheduler_poll_secs": {
          "default": 15,
          "description": "Scheduler polling cadence in seconds.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "scheduler_retries": {
          "default": 2,
          "description": "Max retries for cron job execution attempts.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "RiskProfileConfig": {
      "description": "Named risk/autonomy profile (`[risk_profiles.<alias>]`).\n\nUnified policy surface. Agents reference a profile by alias and the\nruntime resolves through it for shell command allowlists, approval gates,\nsandbox/resource limits, and delegation guardrails. The conventional\n`risk_profiles[\"default\"]` is the resolution target for non-agent\ncontexts (orchestrator init, cron worker startup); the `Default` impl\nbelow mirrors the legacy safety-first defaults so a fresh install\nbehaves the same as a config from before the per-profile split.",
      "properties": {
        "allowed_commands": {
          "default": [
            "git",
            "npm",
            "cargo",
            "ls",
            "cat",
            "grep",
            "find",
            "echo",
            "pwd",
            "wc",
            "head",
            "tail",
            "date",
            "df",
            "du",
            "uname",
            "uptime",
            "hostname",
            "python",
            "python3",
            "pip",
            "node",
            "free"
          ],
          "description": "Allowlist of executable names for shell execution.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "allowed_roots": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Extra directory roots the agent may access.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "allowed_tools": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Tools the agent may call in agentic mode. Empty = inherit / no\nauthorization constraint. Authorization decision: which tools is\nthe agent permitted to invoke at all. See `excluded_tools` for\nthe inverse denylist scoped to non-CLI channels.\n\nThe TOML config does not distinguish an omitted field from\n`allowed_tools = []`; both deserialize to `Vec::new()` and\n`SecurityPolicy::from_profiles` maps that to \"no authorization\nconstraint\" at this layer. If you need an explicit deny-all gate,\napply it on the caller-supplied per-run `allowed_tools` (cron\njobs and other narrowers pass that list in directly to\n`ToolAccessPolicy`, which honors `Some(vec![])` as deny-all) or\nvia `excluded_tools` covering the specific tools you want blocked.\n\nMCP exception: when the list is non-empty, runtime-discovered MCP\ntools (any name containing `__`, which is the `<server>__<tool>`\nconvention used by the MCP wrapper) are auto-admitted into the\neffective allow-list without needing to be listed here individually.\nThis keeps the post-change eager-MCP default usable for agents with an\nexplicit allow-list. Block individual MCP tools via `excluded_tools`.\n\nScope of the exception: the `__` auto-admit applies only to this\nrisk-profile allow-list, **not** to caller-supplied per-run\n`allowed_tools` (cron job `allowed_tools`, narrowed delegate\ninvocations, etc.). Per-run lists are still strict explicit-list\nintersections, so a job that narrows `allowed_tools = [\"cron_add\"]`\nwill not see runtime-discovered MCP tools unless it names them.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "always_ask": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Tools that always require approval in this profile.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "approval_route": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/ApprovalRoute"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Route this profile's tool approvals to a DISTINCT approver channel instead of the\nchannel that triggered the run (closes the cross-channel-HITL gap). Absent ⇒ the\noriginating channel approves (today's behavior). See [`crate::autonomy::ApprovalRoute`].\n\nHonored on both the interactive channel-driven path and the non-interactive turn path\n(gateway chat/webhook dispatch and agent-to-agent peer messages). On the non-interactive\npath the approver is resolved from the live daemon channel registry; if no registry is\navailable or the approver is not live, the gate keeps the non-interactive default\n(fail-closed deny under the default `on_no_approver`)."
        },
        "auto_approve": {
          "default": [
            "file_read",
            "memory_recall",
            "web_search_tool",
            "web_fetch",
            "calculator",
            "glob_search",
            "content_search",
            "image_info",
            "weather",
            "tool_search",
            "browser",
            "browser_open"
          ],
          "description": "Tools that never require approval in this profile.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "block_high_risk_commands": {
          "default": true,
          "description": "Block high-risk commands even when allowlisted.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "delegation_policy": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/DelegationPolicy",
          "default": {
            "mode": "forbidden"
          },
          "description": "Whether agents using this profile may initiate delegation. Defaults to\n`Forbidden`. Reachable delegate targets and bounded/independent mode\nare resolved from each caller agent's config."
        },
        "excluded_tools": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Tools excluded from non-CLI channels under this profile.\n\nAlso subtracts from the agentic-delegate allow-list resolved at\nruntime, which is the only way to block individual\n`<server>__<tool>` MCP names that would otherwise be auto-admitted\nby the `allowed_tools` MCP exception described above.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "firejail_args": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Extra arguments forwarded to firejail when sandbox_backend = \"firejail\".",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "forbidden_paths": {
          "default": [
            "/etc",
            "/root",
            "/home",
            "/usr",
            "/bin",
            "/sbin",
            "/lib",
            "/opt",
            "/boot",
            "/dev",
            "/proc",
            "/sys",
            "/var",
            "/tmp",
            "~/.ssh",
            "~/.gnupg",
            "~/.aws",
            "~/.config"
          ],
          "description": "Explicit path denylist.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "level": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/AutonomyLevel",
          "default": "supervised",
          "description": "Autonomy level applied to this profile. Default: `supervised`."
        },
        "require_approval_for_medium_risk": {
          "default": true,
          "description": "Require approval for medium-risk operations.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "sandbox_backend": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Sandbox backend identifier (e.g. `\"firejail\"`, `\"landlock\"`). `None` inherits.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "sandbox_enabled": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Whether the sandbox is enabled for this profile. `None` inherits global.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "shell_env_passthrough": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Environment variable names passed through to shell subprocesses.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "workspace_only": {
          "default": true,
          "description": "Restrict filesystem access to workspace-relative paths. Default: `false`.",
          "type": "boolean"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "RiskProfileRef": {
      "description": "Reference to a configured `[risk_profiles.<type>.<alias>]` entry.\nEmpty value means \"no preference\" (opt-out). Non-empty values must\nresolve to a configured alias; `Config::validate()` enforces this.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "RuntimeConfig": {
      "description": "Runtime adapter configuration (`[runtime]` section).",
      "properties": {
        "docker": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/DockerRuntimeConfig",
          "default": {
            "allowed_workspace_roots": [],
            "cpu_limit": 1.0,
            "image": "alpine:3.20",
            "memory_limit_mb": 512,
            "mount_workspace": true,
            "network": "none",
            "read_only_rootfs": true
          },
          "description": "Docker runtime settings (used when `kind = \"docker\"`)."
        },
        "kind": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/RuntimeKind",
          "default": "native",
          "description": "Runtime kind: native | docker | cloudflare."
        },
        "reasoning_effort": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Optional reasoning effort for model_providers that expose a level control.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "reasoning_enabled": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Global reasoning override for model_providers that expose explicit controls.\n- `None`: model_provider default behavior\n- `Some(true)`: request reasoning/thinking when supported\n- `Some(false)`: disable reasoning/thinking when supported",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "shell": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Shell binary the native runtime uses for command execution.\n\nApplies only to `runtime.kind = \"native\"`; other runtimes ignore it.\nWhen unset or `null`, the system default `sh` is used. The shell is\ninvoked as `<shell> -c \"<command>\"`, so it must be a POSIX-compatible\nshell binary.\n\nAccepted forms (Unix):\n- a bare command name resolved via `PATH` (e.g. `\"bash\"`), or\n- an absolute path (e.g. `\"/bin/bash\"`, `\"/usr/bin/zsh\"`).\n\nThe value is validated when the native runtime is constructed, so a bad\nvalue is reported up front rather than failing on the first shell\ncommand. Rejected: empty/whitespace; a relative path with separators\n(e.g. `\"./sh\"`, `\"bin/sh\"` — use a bare `PATH` name or an absolute path\ninstead); a bare name not found on `PATH`; and a path that does not\nexist or is not executable.\n\n**Ignored on Windows and Android** (and not validated there): Windows\nalways uses `cmd.exe`, and Android always uses `/system/bin/sh`\n(its shell is not on `PATH` for spawned processes).\n\n**Examples:**\n```toml\n[runtime]\nshell = \"bash\" # resolves via PATH\nshell = \"/bin/zsh\" # absolute path\n```",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "RuntimeKind": {
      "description": "Runtime adapter kind.",
      "enum": [
        "native",
        "docker",
        "cloudflare"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    },
    "RuntimeProfileConfig": {
      "description": "Named runtime/LLM execution profile (`[runtime_profiles.<alias>]`).\n\nReusable operational tuning: agentic mode, iteration caps, context\nbudget, parallel dispatch, resource ceilings, recursion depth, and\nthe budget knobs that `SecurityPolicy` enforces with subagent\nparent-subset discipline. Anything authorization-shaped (allowed\ncommands/tools/paths, approval gates, sandbox) lives on\n`[risk_profiles.<alias>]`. Anything model-provider shaped (model,\ntemperature, max_tokens, timeout_secs) lives on\n`[providers.models.<type>.<alias>]`.",
      "properties": {
        "agentic": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Enable agentic (multi-turn tool-call loop) mode.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "agentic_timeout_secs": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Agentic delegate run timeout in seconds. `None` inherits global.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "auto_classify": {

            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/AutoClassifyConfig"

              "type": "null"

        },
        "compact_context": {
          "default": null,

            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "context_compression": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/ContextCompressionConfig",

            "enabled": false,
            "identifier_policy": "strict",
            "max_passes": 3,
            "protect_first_n": 3,
            "protect_last_n": 4,
            "source_max_chars": 50000,
            "summary_max_chars": 4000,
            "summary_model": null,
            "summary_provider": "",
            "threshold_ratio": 0.5,
            "timeout_secs": 60,
            "tool_result_retrim_chars": 2000,
            "tool_result_trim_exempt": []
          }
        },
        "delegation_timeout_secs": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Delegate call timeout in seconds. `None` inherits global delegate timeout.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "eval": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/EvalConfig",
          "default": {
            "enabled": false,
            "max_retries": 1,
            "min_quality_score": 0.5
          }
        },
        "history_pruning": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/HistoryPrunerConfig",
          "default": {
            "collapse_tool_results": true,
            "enabled": false,
            "keep_recent": 4,
            "max_tokens": 8192
          }
        },
        "keep_tool_context_turns": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Number of recent turns whose full tool context is preserved. `None` inherits.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "max_actions_per_hour": {
          "default": 20,
          "description": "Maximum actions allowed per hour. `0` is a hard zero budget — the\nper-sender rate tracker treats a max of 0 as always exhausted\n(`PerSenderTracker::is_exhausted`), blocking every action. For an\neffectively-unlimited budget use a high value (e.g. `u32::MAX`), not 0.\n`SecurityPolicy::ensure_no_escalation_beyond` rejects subagents\nthat try to raise this above the parent's value.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "max_context_tokens": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Maximum estimated tokens for context before compaction. `None` inherits.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "max_cost_per_day_cents": {
          "default": 500,
          "description": "Maximum cost per day in cents. `0` inherits the global limit.\nParent-subset enforced for subagents.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "max_delegation_depth": {
          "default": 0,
          "description": "Maximum delegation recursion depth. `0` inherits the default.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "max_history_messages": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Maximum conversation history messages retained per session. `None` inherits.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "max_system_prompt_chars": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Maximum characters for the assembled system prompt. `None` inherits.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "max_tool_iterations": {
          "default": 0,
          "description": "Maximum tool-call iterations in agentic mode. `0` inherits the global default.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "max_tool_result_chars": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Maximum characters for a single tool result. `None` inherits.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "memory_recall_limit": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Maximum memory entries injected per turn. `None` inherits global default (5).\nSet to `0` for unlimited.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"

        "parallel_tools": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Enable parallel tool execution per iteration. `None` inherits.",

            "boolean",

        "prompt_injection_mode": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/SkillsPromptInjectionMode"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "default": null,
          "description": "How skills are injected into the system prompt for agents on this\nprofile. `None` inherits the global `[skills] prompt_injection_mode`;\n`compact` inlines only compact skill metadata and registers the\n`read_skill` tool, `full` inlines full skill instructions. Resolved\nthrough [`Config::effective_skills_prompt_mode`], the single point both\nthe system-prompt builder and the `read_skill` tool-registration gate\nconsult so they always agree on the effective mode."
        },
        "shell_timeout_secs": {
          "default": 60,
          "description": "Shell subprocess timeout in seconds. `0` inherits the global timeout.\nParent-subset enforced for subagents.",
          "format": "uint64",

        },

            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"

          "default": null,

          "default": [],

            "$ref": "#/$defs/ToolFilterGroup"
          },

    },
    "RuntimeProfileRef": {
      "description": "Reference to a configured `[runtime_profiles.<type>.<alias>]` entry.\nEmpty value means \"no preference\" (opt-out). Non-empty values must\nresolve to a configured alias; `Config::validate()` enforces this.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "SambanovaModelProviderConfig": {
      "description": "Named model_provider profile definition.",
      "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "description": "Secret API token for this model_provider. Grab it from the model_provider's dashboard (OpenAI platform, Anthropic console, OpenRouter keys page, etc.). Stored via the OS keyring when possible; never commit it to config.toml directly.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "chat_template_kwargs": {
          "description": "Arbitrary key/value pairs forwarded verbatim as `chat_template_kwargs`\nin the request body (llama.cpp-specific). Use this to pass model-family\ntemplate variables that control behaviour not exposed by other fields.\nExample (Qwen3 thinking suppression):\n  `chat_template_kwargs = { enable_thinking = false }`"
        },
        "context_window": {
          "description": "Context window size (max input tokens) for this model.\nAuto-populated on setup from provider's /models endpoint if available.\nOverride manually for custom endpoints or when auto-detection fails.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "extra_headers": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "description": "Extra HTTP headers sent with every request. Niche: used for auth bridges, corporate proxies, or custom gateways that demand a tracing header. Most users never touch this; edit `config.toml` directly if you need it.",
          "type": "object",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "fallback": {
          "description": "Ordered list of other provider aliases to try when every model on this\nalias has failed. Each entry is a dotted `<type>.<alias>` reference into\n`providers.models` and resolves with its own credentials, endpoint, and\nmodel. A fallback never inherits this alias's key. The walk is\ndepth-first: this alias's models are exhausted first, then each fallback\nalias is descended in turn (applying its own `fallback_models` and\n`fallback`). Empty means no provider-level fallback.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/ModelProviderRef"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "fallback_models": {
          "description": "Ordered alternate models to try on THIS provider before falling over to\nthe `fallback` aliases. Same endpoint, key, and headers as the primary\n`model`. Only the model identifier changes. Use this when a provider\nserves a backup model (e.g. a smaller or older variant) that should be\ntried before leaving the provider entirely. Empty means only `model` is\ntried.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "kind": {
          "description": "Provider implementation to instantiate for this profile. Use this\nwhen a canonical typed slot should run through a compatible\nimplementation, e.g. `[providers.models.openai.proxy] kind =\n\"openai-compatible\"`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "live_pricing": {
          "description": "Pull live token prices for this provider's models from its own\nOpenAI-compatible `/models` listing (the gateway is the source of truth\nfor its prices), filling cost-tracking rates for models the operator\nhas NOT priced under `[cost.rates]` / `pricing`. Models the gateway does\nnot price (or providers with no HTTP `/models` listing at all, such as\na subprocess gateway like `kilocli`) fall back to the public models.dev\ncatalog. Configured rates always win; live prices only fill gaps. A\nbackground task refreshes the price snapshot hourly; the cost-recording\npath reads the cached snapshot and never blocks on the network. Default\n`false`: off means no fetching and behavior identical to a build\nwithout the feature.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "max_tokens": {
          "description": "Hard cap on response length in tokens. Most models enforce sensible built-in limits already; leave unset unless you specifically need to clip long outputs for cost or latency reasons.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "merge_system_into_user": {
          "description": "ModelProvider-specific quirk: fold the system prompt into the first user message instead of sending a separate system role. Only needed for models that reject (or mishandle) a standalone system role, e.g. certain older Mistral variants.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "model": {
          "description": "Model identifier to send with each request: the ID string from the model_provider's catalog (e.g. `gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `llama-3.3-70b`). Must match a model the model_provider actually serves on this account.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "native_tools": {
          "description": "Override the provider's default for native tool calling.\n`None` (default) honors the provider's built-in choice. `Some(true)`\nforces native tool calls on, `Some(false)` forces text-fallback.\nCurrently consulted only by the Groq factory, which defaults to\ntext-fallback because llama-family Groq models reject native tool\ncalls with HTTP 400. Setting `native_tools = true` re-enables native\ntool calling for Groq models that support it.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "pricing": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "format": "double",
            "type": "number"
          },
          "description": "Per-model pricing for cost tracking, USD per 1M tokens.\n\nFree-form key/value map. Keys are user-defined model identifiers; an\noptional `.input` / `.output` suffix encodes pricing dimension when\nthe operator wants to split rates. A bare key without a suffix is\nused as a flat per-token rate when neither dimension is specified.\nDefault is empty: cost tracking falls back to \"unknown\" rates and\nonly token usage is recorded.\n\nExample: `pricing = { opus = 15.0, sonnet = 3.0 }`\nOr split: `pricing = { \"opus.input\" = 15.0, \"opus.output\" = 75.0 }`",
          "type": "object"
        },
        "provider_extra": {
          "description": "Extra JSON parameters to include in API requests.\nMerged at the top level of the request body, allowing provider-specific\nfeatures (routing, transforms, etc.) without code changes.\nExample: `provider_extra = { model_provider = { only = [\"Anthropic\"] } }`"
        },
        "replay_assistant_reasoning": {
          "description": "Whether stored assistant reasoning should be replayed on outbound\nassistant history messages. `Some(false)` strips `reasoning_content`\nand `reasoning` before sending. `None` (default) honours the provider's\nbuilt-in default (true for most compat providers, false for Groq).",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "requires_openai_auth": {
          "description": "When true, the client pulls credentials from ZeroClaw's stored `openai-codex` auth profile instead of the `api_key` field above. Import an existing Codex CLI login with `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json`, or run `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex`. Turn on only for the OpenAI Codex model_provider; leave off for standard API-key model_providers.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "temperature": {
          "description": "Sampling temperature passed to the model. Lower values (0.0–0.3) give\ndeterministic, near-verbatim output, which fits code, routing, summarization.\nHigher values (0.7–1.2) give more varied output, which fits open-ended chat.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "think": {
          "description": "Enable or disable chain-of-thought thinking for models that support it\n(e.g. Qwen3, GLM-4). `true` turns thinking on, `false` turns it off.\n`None` (default) lets the model decide. Forwarded as `enable_thinking`\nin the request body; mirrors the Ollama provider's `think` field.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "description": "HTTP request timeout in seconds. Bump this for slow local model_providers (Ollama on CPU, big local models) or high-latency networks; leave unset otherwise.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "tls_ca_cert_path": {
          "description": "Path to a PEM-encoded CA certificate for TLS connections to this provider.\nMust be an absolute path; shell expansion (e.g. `~`) is not performed.\nLeave unset to use the system's default trust store.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "uri": {
          "description": "Endpoint URI the client hits. Override the family's default endpoint when pointing at a self-hosted gateway (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama), a custom proxy, or any non-standard URL. Leave unset to use the family's default URI from its `ModelEndpoint` impl. Set this to the FULL endpoint URL; there is no separate path-suffix field.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "vision": {
          "description": "Override the provider's vision (image input) capability.\n`None` (default) uses the provider family's built-in default. Several\nfamilies (llama.cpp, the generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint, etc.)\nassume vision-capable because they can serve multimodal models. Set\n`vision = false` for a text-only model served by such a family (e.g. a\ntext LLM behind llama.cpp) so image messages are routed to a configured\n`[multimodal] vision_model_provider` instead of being sent to a model\nthat rejects them. `Some(true)` forces vision on.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "wire_api": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/WireApi"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Wire protocol flavor: `responses` for OpenAI's Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`), `chat_completions` for the legacy chat wire and most OpenAI-compatible gateways. New OpenAI provider slots default to `responses`; other families default to chat-completions (or ignore the field). Only override if you're forcing an unusual combination."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "SchedulerConfig": {
      "description": "Scheduler configuration for periodic task execution (`[scheduler]` section).\n\nOwns the cron-runtime knobs: per-job declarations live on\n`Config.cron: HashMap<String, CronJobDecl>` (alias-keyed), while the\nscheduler loop's runtime behavior (`enabled`, polling cap, catch-up) lives here.",
      "properties": {
        "catch_up_on_startup": {
          "default": true,
          "description": "Run all overdue jobs at scheduler startup. Default: `true`.\n\nWhen the daemon restarts late, jobs whose `next_run` is in the past\nfire once before normal polling resumes. Disable to wait for the\nnext scheduled occurrence instead.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": true,
          "description": "Enable the built-in scheduler loop. When false, no cron jobs run.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "max_concurrent": {
          "default": 4,
          "description": "Maximum tasks executed in parallel within a single polling cycle.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "max_run_history": {
          "default": 50,
          "description": "Maximum number of historical cron run records to retain. Default: `50`.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "max_tasks": {
          "default": 64,
          "description": "Maximum number of persisted scheduled tasks per polling cycle.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },

        },
        "fallback_models": {
          "description": "Ordered alternate models to try on THIS provider before falling over to\nthe `fallback` aliases. Same endpoint, key, and headers as the primary\n`model`. Only the model identifier changes. Use this when a provider\nserves a backup model (e.g. a smaller or older variant) that should be\ntried before leaving the provider entirely. Empty means only `model` is\ntried.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "kind": {
          "description": "Provider implementation to instantiate for this profile. Use this\nwhen a canonical typed slot should run through a compatible\nimplementation, e.g. `[providers.models.openai.proxy] kind =\n\"openai-compatible\"`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "live_pricing": {
          "description": "Pull live token prices for this provider's models from its own\nOpenAI-compatible `/models` listing (the gateway is the source of truth\nfor its prices), filling cost-tracking rates for models the operator\nhas NOT priced under `[cost.rates]` / `pricing`. Models the gateway does\nnot price (or providers with no HTTP `/models` listing at all, such as\na subprocess gateway like `kilocli`) fall back to the public models.dev\ncatalog. Configured rates always win; live prices only fill gaps. A\nbackground task refreshes the price snapshot hourly; the cost-recording\npath reads the cached snapshot and never blocks on the network. Default\n`false`: off means no fetching and behavior identical to a build\nwithout the feature.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "max_tokens": {
          "description": "Hard cap on response length in tokens. Most models enforce sensible built-in limits already; leave unset unless you specifically need to clip long outputs for cost or latency reasons.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "merge_system_into_user": {
          "description": "ModelProvider-specific quirk: fold the system prompt into the first user message instead of sending a separate system role. Only needed for models that reject (or mishandle) a standalone system role, e.g. certain older Mistral variants.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "model": {
          "description": "Model identifier to send with each request: the ID string from the model_provider's catalog (e.g. `gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `llama-3.3-70b`). Must match a model the model_provider actually serves on this account.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "native_tools": {
          "description": "Override the provider's default for native tool calling.\n`None` (default) honors the provider's built-in choice. `Some(true)`\nforces native tool calls on, `Some(false)` forces text-fallback.\nCurrently consulted only by the Groq factory, which defaults to\ntext-fallback because llama-family Groq models reject native tool\ncalls with HTTP 400. Setting `native_tools = true` re-enables native\ntool calling for Groq models that support it.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "pricing": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "format": "double",
            "type": "number"
          },
          "description": "Per-model pricing for cost tracking, USD per 1M tokens.\n\nFree-form key/value map. Keys are user-defined model identifiers; an\noptional `.input` / `.output` suffix encodes pricing dimension when\nthe operator wants to split rates. A bare key without a suffix is\nused as a flat per-token rate when neither dimension is specified.\nDefault is empty: cost tracking falls back to \"unknown\" rates and\nonly token usage is recorded.\n\nExample: `pricing = { opus = 15.0, sonnet = 3.0 }`\nOr split: `pricing = { \"opus.input\" = 15.0, \"opus.output\" = 75.0 }`",
          "type": "object"
        },
        "provider_extra": {
          "description": "Extra JSON parameters to include in API requests.\nMerged at the top level of the request body, allowing provider-specific\nfeatures (routing, transforms, etc.) without code changes.\nExample: `provider_extra = { model_provider = { only = [\"Anthropic\"] } }`"
        },
        "replay_assistant_reasoning": {
          "description": "Whether stored assistant reasoning should be replayed on outbound\nassistant history messages. `Some(false)` strips `reasoning_content`\nand `reasoning` before sending. `None` (default) honours the provider's\nbuilt-in default (true for most compat providers, false for Groq).",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "requires_openai_auth": {
          "description": "When true, the client pulls credentials from ZeroClaw's stored `openai-codex` auth profile instead of the `api_key` field above. Import an existing Codex CLI login with `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json`, or run `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex`. Turn on only for the OpenAI Codex model_provider; leave off for standard API-key model_providers.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "temperature": {
          "description": "Sampling temperature passed to the model. Lower values (0.0–0.3) give\ndeterministic, near-verbatim output, which fits code, routing, summarization.\nHigher values (0.7–1.2) give more varied output, which fits open-ended chat.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "think": {
          "description": "Enable or disable chain-of-thought thinking for models that support it\n(e.g. Qwen3, GLM-4). `true` turns thinking on, `false` turns it off.\n`None` (default) lets the model decide. Forwarded as `enable_thinking`\nin the request body; mirrors the Ollama provider's `think` field.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "description": "HTTP request timeout in seconds. Bump this for slow local model_providers (Ollama on CPU, big local models) or high-latency networks; leave unset otherwise.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "tls_ca_cert_path": {
          "description": "Path to a PEM-encoded CA certificate for TLS connections to this provider.\nMust be an absolute path; shell expansion (e.g. `~`) is not performed.\nLeave unset to use the system's default trust store.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "uri": {
          "description": "Endpoint URI the client hits. Override the family's default endpoint when pointing at a self-hosted gateway (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama), a custom proxy, or any non-standard URL. Leave unset to use the family's default URI from its `ModelEndpoint` impl. Set this to the FULL endpoint URL; there is no separate path-suffix field.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "vision": {
          "description": "Override the provider's vision (image input) capability.\n`None` (default) uses the provider family's built-in default. Several\nfamilies (llama.cpp, the generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint, etc.)\nassume vision-capable because they can serve multimodal models. Set\n`vision = false` for a text-only model served by such a family (e.g. a\ntext LLM behind llama.cpp) so image messages are routed to a configured\n`[multimodal] vision_model_provider` instead of being sent to a model\nthat rejects them. `Some(true)` forces vision on.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "wire_api": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/WireApi"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Wire protocol flavor: `responses` for OpenAI's Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`), `chat_completions` for the legacy chat wire and most OpenAI-compatible gateways. New OpenAI provider slots default to `responses`; other families default to chat-completions (or ignore the field). Only override if you're forcing an unusual combination."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "ShellToolConfig": {
      "description": "Shell tool configuration (`[shell_tool]` section).\n\nControls the behaviour of the `shell` execution tool. The main\ntunable is `timeout_secs` — the maximum wall-clock time a single\nshell command may run before it is killed.",
      "properties": {
        "timeout_secs": {
          "default": 60,
          "description": "Maximum shell command execution time in seconds (default: 60).",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "SignalConfig": {
      "properties": {
        "account": {
          "description": "E.164 phone number of the signal-cli account (e.g. \"+1234567890\").",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "approval_timeout_secs": {
          "default": 300,
          "description": "Seconds to wait for operator approval on `always_ask` tools before auto-denying.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "dm_only": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "When true, only accept direct messages and ignore all group traffic.\nMutually exclusive with `group_ids` (which is ignored when this is\nset). Migrated from the legacy `group_id = \"dm\"` sentinel.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Whether this channel is active. The runtime only loads channels whose\n`enabled = true`. Default: `false` so an operator who pastes a partial\n`[channels.<type>.<alias>]` block doesn't accidentally bring a channel\nlive before the rest of its config is filled in.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "excluded_tools": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Tools excluded from this channel's tool spec. When set, these tools\nare not exposed to the model when responding via this channel.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "group_ids": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Group IDs to filter messages. Empty = accept all messages (DMs and\ngroups). When non-empty, only messages from listed groups are\naccepted (DMs are still accepted unless `dm_only` flips the policy\nto DMs-only). Migrated from the legacy `group_id` singular field.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "http_url": {
          "description": "Base URL for the signal-cli HTTP daemon (e.g. `\"http://127.0.0.1:8686\"`).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "ignore_attachments": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Skip messages that are attachment-only (no text body).",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "ignore_stories": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Skip incoming story messages.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "proxy_url": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Per-channel proxy URL (http, https, socks5, socks5h).\nOverrides the global `[proxy]` setting for this channel only.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "reply_min_interval_secs": {
          "default": 0,
          "description": "Per-(channel, recipient) outbound pacing floor in seconds.\nRange: `0..=REPLY_MIN_INTERVAL_MAX_SECS` (0 disables).",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "reply_queue_depth_max": {
          "default": 0,
          "description": "Per-(channel, recipient) outbound pacing queue depth.\nRange: `0..=REPLY_QUEUE_DEPTH_CEILING`. When `reply_min_interval_secs > 0`\nand this value is `0`, the pacing wrapper substitutes\n`DEFAULT_REPLY_QUEUE_DEPTH` (16). When the queue is full, the\nnewest send is dropped and a `WARN` is logged.",
          "format": "uint16",
          "maximum": 65535,
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "http_url",
        "account"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
