    "SkillBundleConfig": {
      "description": "Named skill bundle (`[skill_bundles.<alias>]`).\n\nA reusable group of skills that can be attached to an agent or channel\nby alias, controlling which skills are loaded and from where.",
      "properties": {
        "directory": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Directory path (relative to workspace root) to load skills from.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "exclude": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Skill names to exclude from this bundle.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "include": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Skill names to include. Empty means include all skills in `directory`.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "SkillCreationConfig": {
      "description": "Autonomous skill creation configuration (`[skills.skill_creation]` section).",
      "properties": {
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Enable automatic skill creation after successful multi-step tasks.\nDefault: `false`.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "max_final_answer_chars": {
          "default": 2000,
          "description": "Maximum characters of the final assistant answer fed into the\nreflection prompt. Bounds prompt size so a long answer cannot blow up\nthe reflection request. Default: `2000`.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "max_skills": {
          "default": 500,
          "description": "Maximum number of auto-generated skills to keep.\nWhen exceeded, the oldest auto-generated skill is removed (LRU eviction).",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "max_task_chars": {
          "default": 1000,
          "description": "Maximum characters of the task description fed into the reflection\nprompt. Default: `1000`.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "max_tool_trace_chars": {
          "default": 4000,
          "description": "Maximum characters of the rendered tool-call trace fed into the\nreflection prompt. Default: `4000`.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "reflection_enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Synthesize a canonical `SKILL.md` from the execution trace via a\nbounded model-provider reflection call instead of the deterministic\n`SKILL.toml` generator. Requires `enabled = true`. Falls back to\n`SKILL.toml` whenever the reflection call or its output is invalid, so\nturning this on never leaves a skill un-created. This is distinct from\nthe `[skills.skill_improvement]` background review fork, which patches\nexisting skills after use rather than creating new ones from a trace.\nDefault: `false`.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "similarity_threshold": {
          "default": 0.85,
          "description": "Embedding similarity threshold for deduplication.\nSkills with descriptions more similar than this value are skipped.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "SkillImprovementConfig": {
      "description": "Skill self-improvement configuration (`[skills.skill-improvement]` section).\n\nControls the post-turn background review fork that may patch, expand, or\narchive skills based on what the conversation revealed. The fork runs in a\nrestricted toolset (only `skills_list`, `skill_view`, `skill_manage`) and\nnever touches the user-visible conversation.",
      "properties": {
        "cooldown_secs": {
          "default": 3600,
          "description": "Minimum interval (in seconds) between reviews for the same skill.\nActs as a durable rate limit on patches to any one skill. Default: `3600`.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Enable the background skill-review fork. Default: `false`.\nOpt-in: users must explicitly enable this to allow post-turn skill\nmutations.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "max_review_iterations": {
          "default": 8,
          "description": "Maximum tool-call iterations the review fork itself is allowed to make.\nCaps the fork's LLM cost. Default: `8`.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "nudge_interval_iterations": {
          "default": 10,
          "description": "Spawn a review fork once at least this many tool-call iterations have\naccumulated in the current run. `0` disables iteration-based triggering.\nDefault: `10`.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "SkillInstallSuggestionsConfig": {
      "description": "Prompt-triggered skill install suggestions (`[skills.install_suggestions]` section).",

    },

      "description": "Skills loading configuration (`[skills]` section).",

        "allow_scripts": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Allow script-like files in skills (`.sh`, `.bash`, `.ps1`, shebang shell files).\nDefault: `false` (secure by default).",
          "type": "boolean"

        "extra_registries": {
          "description": "Additional user-configured skill registries, installed via\n`registry:<name>/<skill>`. Each reuses the git-clone registry path and\nis cloned to its own `extra-registry-<name>/` workspace directory.",

        "install_suggestions": {

            "enabled": false

        },
        "open_skills_dir": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Optional path to a local open-skills repository.\nIf unset, defaults to `$HOME/open-skills` when enabled.",

        "open_skills_enabled": {

        "prompt_injection_mode": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/SkillsPromptInjectionMode",

        },

    "SkillsPromptInjectionMode": {
      "description": "Skills loading configuration (`[skills]` section).",

          "type": "string"

    "SlackConfig": {
      "description": "Slack bot channel configuration.",
      "properties": {
        "app_token": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Slack app-level token for Socket Mode (xapp-...). When unset or empty,\nresolved at channel construction from `ZEROCLAW_SLACK_APP_TOKEN`, then\n`SLACK_APP_TOKEN`. `#[serde(default)]` makes omission explicit (an\n`Option` field is already omittable, but this keeps it consistent with\n`bot_token`).",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "approval_timeout_secs": {
          "default": 300,
          "description": "Seconds to wait for operator approval on `always_ask` tools before auto-denying.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "bot_token": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Slack bot OAuth token (xoxb-...). Optional in config: when unset or\nempty it is resolved at channel construction from\n`ZEROCLAW_SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`, then `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`. `#[serde(default)]`\nso a config that omits it still deserializes - the env fallback then\nsupplies it - instead of failing with `missing field 'bot_token'`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "cancel_reaction": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Emoji reaction name (without colons) that cancels an in-flight request.\nFor example, `\"x\"` means reacting with `:x:` cancels the task.\nLeave unset to disable reaction-based cancellation.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "channel_ids": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Explicit list of channel IDs to watch.\nEmpty = listen across all accessible channels.\nMigrated from the legacy `channel_id` singular field.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "draft_update_interval_ms": {
          "default": 1200,
          "description": "Minimum interval (ms) between draft message edits to avoid Slack rate limits.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Whether this channel is active. The runtime only loads channels whose\n`enabled = true`. Default: `false` so an operator who pastes a partial\n`[channels.<type>.<alias>]` block doesn't accidentally bring a channel\nlive before the rest of its config is filled in.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "excluded_tools": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Tools excluded from this channel's tool spec. When set, these tools\nare not exposed to the model when responding via this channel.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "interrupt_on_new_message": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "When true, a newer Slack message from the same sender in the same channel\ncancels the in-flight request and starts a fresh response with preserved history.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "mention_only": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "When true, only respond to messages that @-mention the bot in groups.\nDirect messages remain allowed.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "proxy_url": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Per-channel proxy URL (http, https, socks5, socks5h).\nOverrides the global `[proxy]` setting for this channel only.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "reply_min_interval_secs": {
          "default": 0,
          "description": "Per-(channel, recipient) outbound pacing floor in seconds.\nRange: `0..=REPLY_MIN_INTERVAL_MAX_SECS` (0 disables).",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "reply_queue_depth_max": {
          "default": 0,
          "description": "Per-(channel, recipient) outbound pacing queue depth.\nRange: `0..=REPLY_QUEUE_DEPTH_CEILING`. When `reply_min_interval_secs > 0`\nand this value is `0`, the pacing wrapper substitutes\n`DEFAULT_REPLY_QUEUE_DEPTH` (16). When the queue is full, the\nnewest send is dropped and a `WARN` is logged.",
          "format": "uint16",
          "maximum": 65535,
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "stream_drafts": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Enable progressive draft message streaming via `chat.update`.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "strict_mention_in_thread": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "When true (and `mention_only` is also true), messages inside a Slack\nthread must also @-mention the bot to trigger a response. By default,\nthread replies are allowed through without a mention so the bot can\nkeep a back-and-forth going without the user repeating @-mentions.\nSet this to true in channels shared with human discussion where the\nbot should stay silent unless explicitly addressed.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "thread_replies": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "When true (default), replies stay in the originating Slack thread.\nWhen false, replies go to the channel root instead.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "use_markdown_blocks": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Use the newer Slack `markdown` block type (12 000 char limit, richer formatting).\nDefaults to false (uses universally supported `section` blocks with `mrkdwn`).\nEnable this only if your Slack workspace supports the `markdown` block type.",
          "type": "boolean"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "SlashCommandScope": {
      "description": "Where a channel registers its skill slash commands. `global` (default)\nregisters application-wide - the commands work everywhere the bot is, but\nDiscord takes up to ~1h to propagate changes. `guild` registers to each\nguild in `guild_ids`, which propagates instantly (the right choice for fast\niteration and single-server bots). When `guild` is set with an empty\n`guild_ids`, the channel logs a warning and falls back to global.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "global",
          "description": "Application-wide commands (propagate in up to ~1h). Default.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "guild",
          "description": "Commands registered to each guild in `guild_ids` (instant propagation).",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    },
    "SopApprovalConfig": {
      "description": "`[sop.approval]` - approval broker policy config. A permanent identity source\nfor channel-provided approvers (not a stopgap): the approval broker consumes it\nfor group-membership and quorum checks. Empty = no broker policy applies.",
      "properties": {
        "groups": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/ApprovalGroupConfig"
          },
          "description": "Named approver groups: `group name -> members`. A member is matched against\nthe transport-derived (channel-authenticated) `ApprovalPrincipal` identity.\nA member may be source-qualified (`<source>:<identity>`, e.g. `http:ZeroClawOperator`,\n`ws:<subject>`, `agent:<alias>`) to grant rights on one transport only, or a\nbare identity (`alice`) to grant from any non-channel source. Channel members\nmust include the channel namespace (`channel:<channel-key>:<sender>`) so sender\nids from different channel aliases cannot collide. A future auth system adds a\nsecond resolver alongside this one; it does not replace channel identities.",
          "type": "object"
        },
        "policies": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/ApprovalPolicyConfig"
          },
          "description": "Named approval policies a SOP step may reference by name.",
          "type": "object"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "SopConfig": {
      "description": "Standard Operating Procedures engine configuration (`[sop]`).\n\nThe `default_execution_mode` field uses the `SopExecutionMode` type from\n`sop::types` (re-exported via `sop::SopExecutionMode`). To avoid circular\nmodule references, config stores it using the same enum definition.",
      "properties": {
        "approval": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/SopApprovalConfig",
          "default": {},
          "description": "Approval broker policy config (`[sop.approval]`): named approver groups and\nper-name approval policies (required group + quorum + escalation route) the\napproval broker consumes for group-membership and quorum checks. Members are\nchannel-provided identities (a gateway user, a forge login), so this is a\npermanent identity source, not a stopgap; a future auth system adds another\nresolver alongside it rather than replacing it. An empty block means no broker\npolicy applies (`approval_mode` alone governs a gate, unchanged behavior)."
        },
        "approval_mode": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/ApprovalMode",
          "default": "both",
          "description": "WHO may clear a SOP approval gate. Layered with execution_mode / priority /\nrequires_confirmation (those still apply). Default `both` keeps today's\nbehavior (the agent tool OR an out-of-band principal can clear a gate)."
        },
        "approval_timeout_action": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/ApprovalTimeoutAction",
          "default": "escalate",
          "description": "What happens to a SOP gate that times out (after `approval_timeout_secs`).\nDefault `escalate` is fail-closed: re-surface to the out-of-band approver and\nkeep waiting, never self-approve. (The SOP-gate analog of the channel\napproval-routing fail-closed default; reconcile with that model if both land.)"
        },
        "approval_timeout_secs": {
          "default": 300,
          "description": "Approval timeout in seconds. When a run waits for approval longer than\nthis, the configured `approval_timeout_action` is applied (default\n`escalate`: re-surface the gate to the out-of-band approver and never\nself-approve). Set to 0 to disable the timeout sweep.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "default_execution_mode": {
          "default": "supervised",
          "description": "Default execution mode for SOPs that omit `execution_mode`.\nValues: `auto`, `supervised` (default), `step_by_step`,\n`priority_based`, `deterministic`.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "maintenance_interval_secs": {
          "default": 60,
          "description": "How often (seconds) the daemon runs the SOP maintenance tick: fire\nfail-closed approval timeouts (per `approval_timeout_secs` /\n`approval_timeout_action`), reap expired concurrency-claim leases, and\nprune terminal runs past `max_finished_runs`. Default `60`; set to `0` to\ndisable the tick entirely. The tick itself self-approves nothing - timeout\nhandling is governed by `approval_timeout_action` (default `escalate`).",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "max_concurrent_total": {
          "default": 4,
          "description": "Maximum total concurrent SOP runs across all SOPs.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "max_finished_runs": {
          "default": 100,
          "description": "Maximum number of finished runs kept in memory for status queries.\nOldest runs are evicted when over capacity. 0 = unlimited.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "max_step_retries": {
          "default": 2,
          "description": "Maximum retries allowed by a step failure policy.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "max_step_visits": {
          "default": 256,
          "description": "Maximum times a routed SOP run can visit one step.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "persist_runs": {
          "default": true,
          "description": "Persist run state durably across restarts. Default `true`: `build_sop_engine`\nselects the configured backend (`sqlite`) and in-flight runs - including runs\nparked at a HITL approval - survive a restart. This is the durable substrate\nthe HITL admission model relies on so a pending approval is not lost when the\ndaemon restarts. Set to `false` to opt back into ephemeral in-memory state.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "procedural_memory_enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Enable SOP procedural-memory proposal tooling. Default false keeps\nself-modifying SOP write-back opt-in while the SOP subsystem is\nExperimental.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "run_state_dir": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Directory for the durable run store (created mode-0700). When omitted,\n`<data_dir>/sop`. Never OS-temp.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "run_store_backend": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/SopRunStoreBackend",
          "default": "sqlite",
          "description": "Durable run-state backend when `persist_runs` is true: `sqlite` (default,\ndurable) or `memory` (explicitly non-durable, for tests/degraded)."
        },
        "sops_dir": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Directory containing SOP definitions (subdirs with SOP.toml + SOP.md).\nOptional override. When omitted, the runtime and CLI both resolve the\ndefault `<workspace>/sops`; SOPs load from there whenever it exists.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "step_mandatory_tools": {
          "default": [
            "sop_advance",
            "sop_approve",
            "sop_status"
          ],
          "description": "Tool names that remain available while step scope is enforced.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "step_schema_enforce": {
          "default": true,
          "description": "Enforce per-step input/output schemas when a step declares them.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "step_scope_enforce": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Enforce per-step tool scope. Default false keeps `tools:` advisory.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "untrusted_frame_warning": {
          "default": true,
          "description": "Include the explanatory warning text inside untrusted-content frames.\nBoundary framing itself is always on once wired.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "untrusted_guard_sensitivity": {
          "default": 0.7,
          "description": "Prompt-guard and outbound-redaction sensitivity for untrusted SOP content.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        },
        "untrusted_input_guard": {
          "default": "warn",
          "description": "Prompt-guard action for untrusted SOP trigger input: warn, block, or sanitize.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "untrusted_outbound_redact": {
          "default": true,
          "description": "Redact outbound SOP content before persistence/audit consumers write it.\nIntended to converge with the shared B/F redaction switch once those consumers land.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "untrusted_payload_max_bytes": {
          "default": 8192,
          "description": "Maximum bytes accepted from untrusted SOP trigger payload/topic content\nbefore char-boundary truncation. 0 disables the cap.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "SopDispatch": {
      "description": "Generic AMQP 0-9-1 channel configuration (RabbitMQ, Fedora Messaging, etc.).\n\nSubscribes to an exchange via routing keys and lifts each delivery into an\ninbound `ChannelMessage`. The mapping from a JSON delivery body to message\nfields is config-driven (`content_template`, `thread_id_field`) so a new\nsource — Anitya, an internal bus, anything publishing JSON — is onboarded by\nconfiguration rather than code.\nWhere a fan-in delivery is routed once consumed. Used by AMQP, which carries\nthis field to choose between the agent loop, the SOP engine, or both.\nAgent-loop channels (Telegram, Discord, Slack, ...) do not carry a `dispatch`\nfield: their fan-in is trigger-driven, opting in via a SOP `channel` trigger\nwhile the normal agent turn always runs. The mode is source-agnostic.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "agent_loop",
          "description": "Drive a normal agent turn: the delivery becomes a `ChannelMessage`.\nThis is the default and preserves each channel's original behavior.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "sop",
          "description": "Dispatch the delivery to the SOP engine as a `SopEvent` (`topic` =\nsource identifier, `payload` = body), matching SOPs whose trigger for\nthis source matches. No agent turn is started.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "sop_and_agent_loop",
          "description": "Do both: dispatch to the SOP engine and drive an agent turn from the\nsame delivery.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    },
    "SopRunStoreBackend": {
      "description": "Durable SOP run-state backend selector. A closed, compile-time-known set, so it\nis a serde enum rather than free text (mirrors `SandboxBackend` /\n`ObservabilityBackend` in this file); unknown values are rejected at parse time.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "sqlite",
          "description": "Durable WAL-mode SQLite store (default).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "memory",
          "description": "Ephemeral in-memory store: explicitly non-durable, for tests / degraded boot.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    },
    "SqliteStorageConfig": {
      "description": "SQLite storage backend (`[storage.sqlite.<alias>]`).",
      "properties": {
        "open_timeout_secs": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Maximum seconds to wait when opening the DB if it's locked.\n`None` waits indefinitely. Recommended max: 300.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "path": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Optional override for the SQLite database path.\nWhen unset, defaults to `<workspace_dir>/brain.db`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "StepfunEndpoint": {
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "cn",
          "description": "Mainland China endpoint.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "intl",
          "description": "International endpoint.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    },
    "StepfunModelProviderConfig": {
      "description": "Named model_provider profile definition.",
      "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "description": "Secret API token for this model_provider. Grab it from the model_provider's dashboard (OpenAI platform, Anthropic console, OpenRouter keys page, etc.). Stored via the OS keyring when possible; never commit it to config.toml directly.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "chat_template_kwargs": {
          "description": "Arbitrary key/value pairs forwarded verbatim as `chat_template_kwargs`\nin the request body (llama.cpp-specific). Use this to pass model-family\ntemplate variables that control behaviour not exposed by other fields.\nExample (Qwen3 thinking suppression):\n  `chat_template_kwargs = { enable_thinking = false }`"
        },
        "context_window": {
          "description": "Context window size (max input tokens) for this model.\nAuto-populated on setup from provider's /models endpoint if available.\nOverride manually for custom endpoints or when auto-detection fails.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "endpoint": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/StepfunEndpoint",
          "default": "intl"
        },
        "extra_headers": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "description": "Extra HTTP headers sent with every request. Niche: used for auth bridges, corporate proxies, or custom gateways that demand a tracing header. Most users never touch this; edit `config.toml` directly if you need it.",
          "type": "object",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "fallback": {
          "description": "Ordered list of other provider aliases to try when every model on this\nalias has failed. Each entry is a dotted `<type>.<alias>` reference into\n`providers.models` and resolves with its own credentials, endpoint, and\nmodel. A fallback never inherits this alias's key. The walk is\ndepth-first: this alias's models are exhausted first, then each fallback\nalias is descended in turn (applying its own `fallback_models` and\n`fallback`). Empty means no provider-level fallback.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/ModelProviderRef"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "fallback_models": {
          "description": "Ordered alternate models to try on THIS provider before falling over to\nthe `fallback` aliases. Same endpoint, key, and headers as the primary\n`model`. Only the model identifier changes. Use this when a provider\nserves a backup model (e.g. a smaller or older variant) that should be\ntried before leaving the provider entirely. Empty means only `model` is\ntried.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "kind": {
          "description": "Provider implementation to instantiate for this profile. Use this\nwhen a canonical typed slot should run through a compatible\nimplementation, e.g. `[providers.models.openai.proxy] kind =\n\"openai-compatible\"`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "live_pricing": {
          "description": "Pull live token prices for this provider's models from its own\nOpenAI-compatible `/models` listing (the gateway is the source of truth\nfor its prices), filling cost-tracking rates for models the operator\nhas NOT priced under `[cost.rates]` / `pricing`. Models the gateway does\nnot price (or providers with no HTTP `/models` listing at all, such as\na subprocess gateway like `kilocli`) fall back to the public models.dev\ncatalog. Configured rates always win; live prices only fill gaps. A\nbackground task refreshes the price snapshot hourly; the cost-recording\npath reads the cached snapshot and never blocks on the network. Default\n`false`: off means no fetching and behavior identical to a build\nwithout the feature.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "max_tokens": {
          "description": "Hard cap on response length in tokens. Most models enforce sensible built-in limits already; leave unset unless you specifically need to clip long outputs for cost or latency reasons.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "merge_system_into_user": {
          "description": "ModelProvider-specific quirk: fold the system prompt into the first user message instead of sending a separate system role. Only needed for models that reject (or mishandle) a standalone system role, e.g. certain older Mistral variants.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "model": {
          "description": "Model identifier to send with each request: the ID string from the model_provider's catalog (e.g. `gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `llama-3.3-70b`). Must match a model the model_provider actually serves on this account.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "native_tools": {
          "description": "Override the provider's default for native tool calling.\n`None` (default) honors the provider's built-in choice. `Some(true)`\nforces native tool calls on, `Some(false)` forces text-fallback.\nCurrently consulted only by the Groq factory, which defaults to\ntext-fallback because llama-family Groq models reject native tool\ncalls with HTTP 400. Setting `native_tools = true` re-enables native\ntool calling for Groq models that support it.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "pricing": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "format": "double",
            "type": "number"
          },
          "description": "Per-model pricing for cost tracking, USD per 1M tokens.\n\nFree-form key/value map. Keys are user-defined model identifiers; an\noptional `.input` / `.output` suffix encodes pricing dimension when\nthe operator wants to split rates. A bare key without a suffix is\nused as a flat per-token rate when neither dimension is specified.\nDefault is empty: cost tracking falls back to \"unknown\" rates and\nonly token usage is recorded.\n\nExample: `pricing = { opus = 15.0, sonnet = 3.0 }`\nOr split: `pricing = { \"opus.input\" = 15.0, \"opus.output\" = 75.0 }`",
          "type": "object"
        },
        "provider_extra": {
          "description": "Extra JSON parameters to include in API requests.\nMerged at the top level of the request body, allowing provider-specific\nfeatures (routing, transforms, etc.) without code changes.\nExample: `provider_extra = { model_provider = { only = [\"Anthropic\"] } }`"
        },
        "replay_assistant_reasoning": {
          "description": "Whether stored assistant reasoning should be replayed on outbound\nassistant history messages. `Some(false)` strips `reasoning_content`\nand `reasoning` before sending. `None` (default) honours the provider's\nbuilt-in default (true for most compat providers, false for Groq).",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "requires_openai_auth": {
          "description": "When true, the client pulls credentials from ZeroClaw's stored `openai-codex` auth profile instead of the `api_key` field above. Import an existing Codex CLI login with `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json`, or run `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex`. Turn on only for the OpenAI Codex model_provider; leave off for standard API-key model_providers.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "temperature": {
          "description": "Sampling temperature passed to the model. Lower values (0.0–0.3) give\ndeterministic, near-verbatim output, which fits code, routing, summarization.\nHigher values (0.7–1.2) give more varied output, which fits open-ended chat.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "think": {
          "description": "Enable or disable chain-of-thought thinking for models that support it\n(e.g. Qwen3, GLM-4). `true` turns thinking on, `false` turns it off.\n`None` (default) lets the model decide. Forwarded as `enable_thinking`\nin the request body; mirrors the Ollama provider's `think` field.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "description": "HTTP request timeout in seconds. Bump this for slow local model_providers (Ollama on CPU, big local models) or high-latency networks; leave unset otherwise.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "tls_ca_cert_path": {
          "description": "Path to a PEM-encoded CA certificate for TLS connections to this provider.\nMust be an absolute path; shell expansion (e.g. `~`) is not performed.\nLeave unset to use the system's default trust store.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "uri": {
          "description": "Endpoint URI the client hits. Override the family's default endpoint when pointing at a self-hosted gateway (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama), a custom proxy, or any non-standard URL. Leave unset to use the family's default URI from its `ModelEndpoint` impl. Set this to the FULL endpoint URL; there is no separate path-suffix field.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "vision": {
          "description": "Override the provider's vision (image input) capability.\n`None` (default) uses the provider family's built-in default. Several\nfamilies (llama.cpp, the generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint, etc.)\nassume vision-capable because they can serve multimodal models. Set\n`vision = false` for a text-only model served by such a family (e.g. a\ntext LLM behind llama.cpp) so image messages are routed to a configured\n`[multimodal] vision_model_provider` instead of being sent to a model\nthat rejects them. `Some(true)` forces vision on.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "wire_api": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/WireApi"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Wire protocol flavor: `responses` for OpenAI's Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`), `chat_completions` for the legacy chat wire and most OpenAI-compatible gateways. New OpenAI provider slots default to `responses`; other families default to chat-completions (or ignore the field). Only override if you're forcing an unusual combination."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "StorageConfig": {
      "description": "Persistent storage configuration (`[storage]` section).\n\nStorage is a two-tier alias-keyed map: `[storage.<backend>.<alias>]`,\nparallel to `[providers.models.<type>.<alias>]`. Each backend has its own typed\nconfig struct. `MemoryConfig.backend` carries a dotted reference (`\"sqlite.default\"`,\n`\"postgres.work\"`) that resolves to one of these entries via\n[`Config::resolve_active_storage`].",
      "properties": {
        "lucid": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/LucidStorageConfig"
          },
          "description": "Lucid CLI sync instances (`[storage.lucid.<alias>]`).",
          "type": "object"
        },
        "markdown": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/MarkdownStorageConfig"
          },
          "description": "Markdown storage instances (`[storage.markdown.<alias>]`).",
          "type": "object"
        },
        "postgres": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/PostgresStorageConfig"
          },
          "description": "PostgreSQL storage instances (`[storage.postgres.<alias>]`).",
          "type": "object"
        },
        "qdrant": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/QdrantStorageConfig"
          },
          "description": "Qdrant storage instances (`[storage.qdrant.<alias>]`).",
          "type": "object"
        },
        "sqlite": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/SqliteStorageConfig"
          },
          "description": "SQLite storage instances (`[storage.sqlite.<alias>]`).",
          "type": "object"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "StreamMode": {
      "description": "Streaming mode for channels that support progressive message updates.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "off",
          "description": "No streaming -- send the complete response as a single message (default).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "partial",
          "description": "Update a draft message with every flush interval.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "multi_message",
          "description": "Send the response as multiple separate messages at paragraph boundaries.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    },
    "SyntheticModelProviderConfig": {
      "description": "Named model_provider profile definition.",
      "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "description": "Secret API token for this model_provider. Grab it from the model_provider's dashboard (OpenAI platform, Anthropic console, OpenRouter keys page, etc.). Stored via the OS keyring when possible; never commit it to config.toml directly.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "chat_template_kwargs": {
          "description": "Arbitrary key/value pairs forwarded verbatim as `chat_template_kwargs`\nin the request body (llama.cpp-specific).           "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "extra_headers": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "type": "string"

          "description": "Extra HTTP headers sent with every request. Niche: used for auth bridges, corporate proxies, or custom gateways that demand a tracing header. Most users never touch this; edit `config.toml` directly if you need it.",
          "type": "object",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "fallback": {
          "description": "Ordered list of other provider aliases to try when every model on this\nalias has failed. The walk is\ndepth-first: this alias's models are exhausted first, then each fallback\nalias is descended in turn (applying its own `fallback_models` and\n`fallback`). Empty means no provider-level fallback.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/ModelProviderRef"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "fallback_models": {
          "description": "Ordered alternate models to try on THIS provider before falling over to\nthe `fallback` aliases. Same endpoint, key, and headers as the primary\n`model`. Empty means only `model` is\ntried.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "kind": {
          "description": "Provider implementation to instantiate for this profile. Use this\nwhen a canonical typed slot should run through a compatible\nimplementation, e.g. `[providers.models.openai.proxy] kind =\n\"openai-compatible\"`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "live_pricing": {
          "description": "Pull live token prices for this provider's models from its own\nOpenAI-compatible `/models` listing (the gateway is the source of truth\nfor its prices), filling cost-tracking rates for models the operator\nhas NOT priced under `[cost.rates]` / `pricing`. Models the gateway does\nnot price (or providers with no HTTP `/models` listing at all, such as\na subprocess gateway like `kilocli`) fall back to the public models.dev\ncatalog. Configured rates always win; live prices only fill gaps. A\nbackground task refreshes the price snapshot hourly; the cost-recording\npath reads the cached snapshot and never blocks on the network. Default\n`false`: off means no fetching and behavior identical to a build\nwithout the feature.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "max_tokens": {
          "description": "Hard cap on response length in tokens. Most models enforce sensible built-in limits already; leave unset unless you specifically need to clip long outputs for cost or latency reasons.",

    "TailscaleTunnelConfig": {
      "properties": {
        "funnel": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Use Tailscale Funnel (public internet) vs Serve (tailnet only)",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "hostname": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Optional hostname override",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "TelegramConfig": {
      "description": "Telegram bot channel configuration.",
      "properties": {
        "ack_reactions": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Override for the top-level `ack_reactions` setting. When `None`, the\nchannel falls back to `[channels].ack_reactions`. When set\nexplicitly, it takes precedence.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "api_base_url": {
          "default": "https://api.telegram.org",
          "description": "Telegram Bot API base URL. Defaults to the official Telegram endpoint;\nset to a local Bot API server URL when self-hosting Telegram's bot API.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "approval_timeout_secs": {
          "default": 120,
          "description": "How long (seconds) to wait for the operator to tap an inline-keyboard\nbutton on a tool approval prompt before auto-denying. Default: 120.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "bot_token": {
          "default": "",
          "description": "Telegram Bot API token (from @BotFather). `#[serde(default)]` so a\nconfig that omits or later has it pruned (e.g. a freshly created\nalias with an empty token, stripped by `prune_empty_leaves` before\nwrite) still deserializes as an empty string - instead of failing\nwith `missing field 'bot_token'` and getting dropped by the resilient\nsalvage pass. `validate_bot_token` below still requires a real token\nonce `enabled = true`.",
          "type": "string",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "debounce_ms": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Inbound message debounce window in milliseconds for this Telegram alias.\nWhen set, overrides the global `[channels].debounce_ms` for this channel\nonly. `0` or unset falls back to the global value.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "draft_update_interval_ms": {
          "default": 1000,
          "description": "Minimum interval (ms) between draft message edits to avoid rate limits.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Whether this channel is active. The runtime only loads channels whose\n`enabled = true`. Default: `false` so an operator who pastes a partial\n`[channels.<type>.<alias>]` block doesn't accidentally bring a channel\nlive before the rest of its config is filled in.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "excluded_tools": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Tools excluded from this channel's tool spec. When set, these tools\nare not exposed to the model when responding via this channel.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "interrupt_on_new_message": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "When true, a newer Telegram message from the same sender in the same chat\ncancels the in-flight request and starts a fresh response with preserved history.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "mention_only": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "When true, only respond to messages that @-mention the bot in groups.\nDirect messages are always processed.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "proxy_url": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Per-channel proxy URL (http, https, socks5, socks5h).\nOverrides the global `[proxy]` setting for this channel only.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "reply_min_interval_secs": {
          "default": 0,
          "description": "Per-(channel, recipient) outbound pacing floor in seconds.\nRange: `0..=REPLY_MIN_INTERVAL_MAX_SECS` (0 disables).",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "reply_queue_depth_max": {
          "default": 0,
          "description": "Per-(channel, recipient) outbound pacing queue depth.\nRange: `0..=REPLY_QUEUE_DEPTH_CEILING`. When `reply_min_interval_secs > 0`\nand this value is `0`, the pacing wrapper substitutes\n`DEFAULT_REPLY_QUEUE_DEPTH` (16). When the queue is full, the\nnewest send is dropped and a `WARN` is logged.",
          "format": "uint16",
          "maximum": 65535,
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "stream_mode": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/StreamMode",
          "default": "off",
          "description": "Streaming mode for progressive response delivery via message edits."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },

          "description": "Hard cap on response length in tokens. Most models enforce sensible built-in limits already; leave unset unless you specifically need to clip long outputs for cost or latency reasons.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "merge_system_into_user": {
          "description": "ModelProvider-specific quirk: fold the system prompt into the first user message instead of sending a separate system role. Only needed for models that reject (or mishandle) a standalone system role, e.g. certain older Mistral variants.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "model": {
          "description": "Model identifier to send with each request: the ID string from the model_provider's catalog (e.g. `gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `llama-3.3-70b`). Must match a model the model_provider actually serves on this account.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "native_tools": {
          "description": "Override the provider's default for native tool calling.\n`None` (default) honors the provider's built-in choice. `Some(true)`\nforces native tool calls on, `Some(false)` forces text-fallback.\nCurrently consulted only by the Groq factory, which defaults to\ntext-fallback because llama-family Groq models reject native tool\ncalls with HTTP 400. Setting `native_tools = true` re-enables native\ntool calling for Groq models that support it.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "pricing": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "format": "double",
            "type": "number"
          },
          "description": "Per-model pricing for cost tracking, USD per 1M tokens.\n\nFree-form key/value map. Keys are user-defined model identifiers; an\noptional `.input` / `.output` suffix encodes pricing dimension when\nthe operator wants to split rates. A bare key without a suffix is\nused as a flat per-token rate when neither dimension is specified.\nDefault is empty: cost tracking falls back to \"unknown\" rates and\nonly token usage is recorded.\n\nExample: `pricing = { opus = 15.0, sonnet = 3.0 }`\nOr split: `pricing = { \"opus.input\" = 15.0, \"opus.output\" = 75.0 }`",
          "type": "object"
        },
        "provider_extra": {
          "description": "Extra JSON parameters to include in API requests.\nMerged at the top level of the request body, allowing provider-specific\nfeatures (routing, transforms, etc.) without code changes.\nExample: `provider_extra = { model_provider = { only = [\"Anthropic\"] } }`"
        },
        "replay_assistant_reasoning": {
          "description": "Whether stored assistant reasoning should be replayed on outbound\nassistant history messages. `Some(false)` strips `reasoning_content`\nand `reasoning` before sending. `None` (default) honours the provider's\nbuilt-in default (true for most compat providers, false for Groq).",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "requires_openai_auth": {
          "description": "When true, the client pulls credentials from ZeroClaw's stored `openai-codex` auth profile instead of the `api_key` field above. Import an existing Codex CLI login with `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json`, or run `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex`. Turn on only for the OpenAI Codex model_provider; leave off for standard API-key model_providers.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "temperature": {
          "description": "Sampling temperature passed to the model. Lower values (0.0–0.3) give\ndeterministic, near-verbatim output, which fits code, routing, summarization.\nHigher values (0.7–1.2) give more varied output, which fits open-ended chat.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "think": {
          "description": "Enable or disable chain-of-thought thinking for models that support it\n(e.g. Qwen3, GLM-4). `true` turns thinking on, `false` turns it off.\n`None` (default) lets the model decide. Forwarded as `enable_thinking`\nin the request body; mirrors the Ollama provider's `think` field.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "description": "HTTP request timeout in seconds. Bump this for slow local model_providers (Ollama on CPU, big local models) or high-latency networks; leave unset otherwise.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "tls_ca_cert_path": {
          "description": "Path to a PEM-encoded CA certificate for TLS connections to this provider.\nMust be an absolute path; shell expansion (e.g. `~`) is not performed.\nLeave unset to use the system's default trust store.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "uri": {
          "description": "Endpoint URI the client hits. Override the family's default endpoint when pointing at a self-hosted gateway (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama), a custom proxy, or any non-standard URL. Leave unset to use the family's default URI from its `ModelEndpoint` impl. Set this to the FULL endpoint URL; there is no separate path-suffix field.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "vision": {
          "description": "Override the provider's vision (image input) capability.\n`None` (default) uses the provider family's built-in default.           "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "wire_api": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/WireApi"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }

      "type": "object"

    "TextBrowserConfig": {
      "description": "Text browser tool configuration (`[text_browser]` section).\n\nUses text-based browsers (lynx, links, w3m) to render web pages as plain\ntext. Designed for headless/SSH environments without graphical browsers.",
      "properties": {
        "allowed_private_hosts": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Private/internal hosts allowed to bypass SSRF protection.\nExact and subdomain matches are supported; `[\"*\"]` permits **all** private/local\nhosts (RFC 1918, loopback, link-local, `.local`). Default: empty (deny).\nWarning: `[\"*\"]` also reaches link-local addresses, including the cloud metadata\nendpoint (`169.254.169.254`) — list specific hosts unless you accept that exposure.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Enable `text_browser` tool",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "preferred_browser": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Preferred text browser (\"lynx\", \"links\", or \"w3m\"). If unset, auto-detects.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "default": 30,
          "description": "Request timeout in seconds (default: 30)",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "ThinkingConfig": {
      "description": "Configuration for thinking/reasoning level control.",

          "additionalProperties": {
            "format": "uint32",

        "default_level": {

          "type": "boolean"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"

      "description": "How deeply the model should reason for a given message.",

        "off",
        "minimal",
        "low",
        "medium",
        "high",
        "max"

      "type": "string"
    },
    "TodoTrackerConfig": {
      "description": "ZeroCode live task tracker configuration (`[todotracker]` section).\n\nRead-only visual tracker driven by the model's `TodoWrite` tool.",
      "properties": {
        "enabled": {
          "default": true,
          "description": "Master switch. When `false` the tracker never renders and never\nauto-pops. Default: `true`.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "enabled_at_start": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Whether the panel is visible at launch (when `enabled`). When\n`false` it stays hidden until toggled or auto-popped by the first\nplan. Default: `false`.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "location": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/TodoTrackerLocation",
          "default": "right",
          "description": "Panel location: `bottom` (between transcript and input), `left`,\nor `right` (default)."
        },
        "max_height": {
          "default": 5,
          "description": "Bottom-strip maximum height in rows (grows up to this). Ignored for\nleft/right. Default: `5`.",
          "format": "uint16",
          "maximum": 65535,
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "width": {
          "default": 32,
          "description": "Side-panel target column width (left/right). Runtime-clamped to at\nmost half the terminal width. Ignored for `bottom`. Default: `32`.",
          "format": "uint16",
          "maximum": 65535,
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"

      "description": "Location of the ZeroCode TodoWrite tracker panel.",

          "const": "left",
          "description": "Vertical side panel on the left.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {

          "description": "Vertical side panel on the right (OpenCode style). Default.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    },

        "api_key": {

The walk is\ndepth-first: this alias's models are exhausted first, then each fallback\nalias is descended in turn (applying its own `fallback_models` and\n`fallback`). Empty means no provider-level fallback.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/ModelProviderRef"

          "type": "array"
        },
        "fallback_models": {

          "items": {
            "type": "string"

          "type": "array"
        },
        "kind": {

    "ToolCostRates": {
      "description": "Rates for a tool that hits a paid external API. Keyed in\n`[cost.rates.tools.<name>]` by the tool's registered name.",
      "properties": {
        "per_call": {
          "description": "Per-call cost (USD).",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "ToolFilterGroup": {
      "description": "A named group of MCP tool patterns with an activation mode.\n\nEach group lists glob patterns for MCP tool names and an optional set of\nkeywords that trigger inclusion in `dynamic` mode. MCP tools are named\n`<server>__<tool>` (double-underscore separator, e.g. `filesystem__read_file`).\n\nClassification is by origin, not name shape: only tools that actually came\nfrom the MCP registry are subject to these groups. Built-in tools AND skill\ntools — which share the `<x>__<y>` naming convention (`{skill}__{tool}`) —\nalways pass through and are never affected by `tool_filter_groups`.\n\nUnder `[mcp] deferred_loading = true`, `mode = \"always\"` entries are\npre-activated at assembly time so matching tools are live from the first\nturn without a `tool_search` round-trip.\n\n# Example\n```toml\n[[runtime_profiles.default.tool_filter_groups]]\nmode = \"always\"\ntools = [\"filesystem__*\"]\nkeywords = []\n\n[[runtime_profiles.default.tool_filter_groups]]\nmode = \"dynamic\"\ntools = [\"browser__*\"]\nkeywords = [\"browse\", \"website\", \"url\", \"search\"]\n```",
      "properties": {
        "keywords": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Keywords that activate this group in `dynamic` mode (case-insensitive substring).\nIgnored when `mode = \"always\"`.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "mode": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/ToolFilterGroupMode",
          "default": "dynamic",
          "description": "Activation mode: `\"always\"` or `\"dynamic\"`."
        },
        "tools": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Glob patterns matching MCP tool names (single `*` wildcard supported).",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "ToolFilterGroupMode": {
      "description": "Determines when a `ToolFilterGroup` is active.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "always",
          "description": "Tools in this group are always included in every turn.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "dynamic",
          "description": "Tools in this group are included only when the user message contains\nat least one of the configured `keywords` (case-insensitive substring match).",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    },
    "ToolReceiptsConfig": {
      "description": "HMAC tool execution receipt configuration, per agent\n(`[agents.<alias>.tool_receipts]`).\n\nReceipts are short HMAC-SHA256 tags appended to tool results so the model\ncannot claim it ran a tool that never actually executed. See\n`docs/book/src/security/tool-receipts.md`.",
      "properties": {
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Generate HMAC receipts on every tool execution. Default: `false`.\nWhen false, the entire receipt subsystem is inert (no key, no\ngeneration, no append, no system-prompt addendum).",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "inject_system_prompt": {
          "default": true,
          "description": "Inject the receipt-echo instruction into the system prompt so the\nmodel carries receipts verbatim into its response. Default: `true`.\nNo effect when `enabled = false`.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "show_in_response": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Append a trailing `Tool receipts:` block to user-visible replies so\nreceipts are auditable from the channel surface, not just the\ninternal history. Default: `false`.",
          "type": "boolean"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "TranscriptionConfig": {
      "description": "Voice transcription configuration with multi-provider support.\n\nThe top-level `api_url`, `model`, and `api_key` fields remain for backward\ncompatibility with existing Groq-based configurations.",

          "default": null,

          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "api_url": {
          "default": "https://api.groq.com/openai/v1/audio/transcriptions",
          "description": "Whisper API endpoint URL (Groq transcription provider).",
          "type": "string"
        },

          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/AssemblyAiSttConfig"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }

          "default": null,
          "description": "AssemblyAI STT model_provider configuration."
        },
        "deepgram": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/DeepgramSttConfig"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "default": null,
          "description": "Deepgram STT model_provider configuration."
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Enable voice transcription for channels that support it.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "google": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/GoogleSttConfig"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
