    "TunnelConfig": {
      "description": "Tunnel configuration for exposing the gateway publicly (`[tunnel]` section).\n\nSupported model_providers: `\"none\"` (default), `\"cloudflare\"`, `\"tailscale\"`, `\"ngrok\"`, `\"openvpn\"`, `\"pinggy\"`, `\"custom\"`.",
      "properties": {
        "cloudflare": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/CloudflareTunnelConfig"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "default": null,
          "description": "Cloudflare Tunnel configuration (used when `tunnel_provider = \"cloudflare\"`)."
        },
        "custom": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/CustomTunnelConfig"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "default": null,
          "description": "Custom tunnel command configuration (used when `tunnel_provider = \"custom\"`)."
        },
        "ngrok": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/NgrokTunnelConfig"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "default": null,
          "description": "ngrok tunnel configuration (used when `tunnel_provider = \"ngrok\"`)."
        },
        "openvpn": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/OpenVpnTunnelConfig"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "default": null,
          "description": "OpenVPN tunnel configuration (used when `tunnel_provider = \"openvpn\"`)."
        },
        "pinggy": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/PinggyTunnelConfig"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "default": null,
          "description": "Pinggy tunnel configuration (used when `tunnel_provider = \"pinggy\"`)."
        },
        "tailscale": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/TailscaleTunnelConfig"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "default": null,
          "description": "Tailscale Funnel/Serve configuration (used when `tunnel_provider = \"tailscale\"`)."
        },
        "tunnel_provider": {
          "default": "none",
          "description": "How the gateway gets exposed to the public internet so webhooks (Telegram, Slack, etc.) can reach it. `none` = keep it local, no tunnel; `cloudflare` = Cloudflare Tunnel via cloudflared (needs a Zero Trust account and token); `tailscale` = Tailscale Funnel/Serve (tailnet-only or public, no account beyond tailscale); `ngrok` = ngrok agent with auth token; `openvpn` = bring-your-own OpenVPN egress; `pinggy` = Pinggy SSH tunnels (quick one-shot URLs); `custom` = run an arbitrary command you define under `[tunnel.custom]`.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "TwitchConfig": {
      "description": "Twitch chat channel configuration. A thin adapter over IRC\n(`irc.chat.twitch.tv:6697` over TLS); see the `twitch` channel module.",
      "properties": {
        "bot_username": {
          "description": "Twitch login name of the bot account (case-insensitive — lowercased\nbefore send).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "channels": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Twitch channels to join. Each entry receives a `#` prefix if missing\nand is lowercased before send (Twitch channel names are\ncase-insensitive). E.g. `[\"mychannel\", \"#anotherchannel\"]`.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Whether this channel is active. The runtime only loads channels whose\n`enabled = true`. Default: `false`.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "mention_only": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "When true, only respond to messages that mention the bot's login\nname. Default: `false`.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "oauth_token": {
          "description": "Twitch OAuth user-access token. The `oauth:` prefix is added\nautomatically if missing, so both `\"oauth:abcdef\"` and `\"abcdef\"`\nwork. Mint via <https://twitchapps.com/tmi/> or the Twitch CLI.",
          "type": "string",
          "x-secret": true
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "bot_username",
        "oauth_token"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    "TwitterConfig": {
      "description": "X/Twitter channel configuration (Twitter API v2)",
      "properties": {
        "bearer_token": {
          "description": "Twitter API v2 Bearer Token (OAuth 2.0)",
          "type": "string",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Whether this channel is active. The runtime only loads channels whose\n`enabled = true`. Default: `false` so an operator who pastes a partial\n`[channels.<type>.<alias>]` block doesn't accidentally bring a channel\nlive before the rest of its config is filled in.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "excluded_tools": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Tools excluded from this channel's tool spec. When set, these tools\nare not exposed to the model when responding via this channel.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "bearer_token"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    "UpstageModelProviderConfig": {
      "description": "Named model_provider profile definition.",
      "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "description": "Secret API token for this model_provider. Grab it from the model_provider's dashboard (OpenAI platform, Anthropic console, OpenRouter keys page, etc.). Stored via the OS keyring when possible; never commit it to config.toml directly.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "chat_template_kwargs": {
          "description": "Arbitrary key/value pairs forwarded verbatim as `chat_template_kwargs`\nin the request body (llama.cpp-specific). Use this to pass model-family\ntemplate variables that control behaviour not exposed by other fields.\nExample (Qwen3 thinking suppression):\n  `chat_template_kwargs = { enable_thinking = false }`"
        },
        "context_window": {
          "description": "Context window size (max input tokens) for this model.\nAuto-populated on setup from provider's /models endpoint if available.\nOverride manually for custom endpoints or when auto-detection fails.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "extra_headers": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "description": "Extra HTTP headers sent with every request. Niche: used for auth bridges, corporate proxies, or custom gateways that demand a tracing header. Most users never touch this; edit `config.toml` directly if you need it.",
          "type": "object",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "fallback": {
          "description": "Ordered list of other provider aliases to try when every model on this\nalias has failed. Each entry is a dotted `<type>.<alias>` reference into\n`providers.models` and resolves with its own credentials, endpoint, and\nmodel. A fallback never inherits this alias's key. The walk is\ndepth-first: this alias's models are exhausted first, then each fallback\nalias is descended in turn (applying its own `fallback_models` and\n`fallback`). Empty means no provider-level fallback.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/ModelProviderRef"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "fallback_models": {
          "description": "Ordered alternate models to try on THIS provider before falling over to\nthe `fallback` aliases. Same endpoint, key, and headers as the primary\n`model`. Only the model identifier changes. Use this when a provider\nserves a backup model (e.g. a smaller or older variant) that should be\ntried before leaving the provider entirely. Empty means only `model` is\ntried.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "kind": {
          "description": "Provider implementation to instantiate for this profile. Use this\nwhen a canonical typed slot should run through a compatible\nimplementation, e.g. `[providers.models.openai.proxy] kind =\n\"openai-compatible\"`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "live_pricing": {
          "description": "Pull live token prices for this provider's models from its own\nOpenAI-compatible `/models` listing (the gateway is the source of truth\nfor its prices), filling cost-tracking rates for models the operator\nhas NOT priced under `[cost.rates]` / `pricing`. Models the gateway does\nnot price (or providers with no HTTP `/models` listing at all, such as\na subprocess gateway like `kilocli`) fall back to the public models.dev\ncatalog. Configured rates always win; live prices only fill gaps. A\nbackground task refreshes the price snapshot hourly; the cost-recording\npath reads the cached snapshot and never blocks on the network. Default\n`false`: off means no fetching and behavior identical to a build\nwithout the feature.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "max_tokens": {
          "description": "Hard cap on response length in tokens. Most models enforce sensible built-in limits already; leave unset unless you specifically need to clip long outputs for cost or latency reasons.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "merge_system_into_user": {
          "description": "ModelProvider-specific quirk: fold the system prompt into the first user message instead of sending a separate system role. Only needed for models that reject (or mishandle) a standalone system role, e.g. certain older Mistral variants.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "model": {
          "description": "Model identifier to send with each request: the ID string from the model_provider's catalog (e.g. `gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `llama-3.3-70b`). Must match a model the model_provider actually serves on this account.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "native_tools": {
          "description": "Override the provider's default for native tool calling.\n`None` (default) honors the provider's built-in choice. `Some(true)`\nforces native tool calls on, `Some(false)` forces text-fallback.\nCurrently consulted only by the Groq factory, which defaults to\ntext-fallback because llama-family Groq models reject native tool\ncalls with HTTP 400. Setting `native_tools = true` re-enables native\ntool calling for Groq models that support it.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "pricing": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "format": "double",
            "type": "number"
          },
          "description": "Per-model pricing for cost tracking, USD per 1M tokens.\n\nFree-form key/value map. Keys are user-defined model identifiers; an\noptional `.input` / `.output` suffix encodes pricing dimension when\nthe operator wants to split rates. A bare key without a suffix is\nused as a flat per-token rate when neither dimension is specified.\nDefault is empty: cost tracking falls back to \"unknown\" rates and\nonly token usage is recorded.\n\nExample: `pricing = { opus = 15.0, sonnet = 3.0 }`\nOr split: `pricing = { \"opus.input\" = 15.0, \"opus.output\" = 75.0 }`",
          "type": "object"
        },
        "provider_extra": {
          "description": "Extra JSON parameters to include in API requests.\nMerged at the top level of the request body, allowing provider-specific\nfeatures (routing, transforms, etc.) without code changes.\nExample: `provider_extra = { model_provider = { only = [\"Anthropic\"] } }`"
        },
        "replay_assistant_reasoning": {
          "description": "Whether stored assistant reasoning should be replayed on outbound\nassistant history messages. `Some(false)` strips `reasoning_content`\nand `reasoning` before sending. `None` (default) honours the provider's\nbuilt-in default (true for most compat providers, false for Groq).",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "requires_openai_auth": {
          "description": "When true, the client pulls credentials from ZeroClaw's stored `openai-codex` auth profile instead of the `api_key` field above. Import an existing Codex CLI login with `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json`, or run `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex`. Turn on only for the OpenAI Codex model_provider; leave off for standard API-key model_providers.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "temperature": {
          "description": "Sampling temperature passed to the model. Lower values (0.0–0.3) give\ndeterministic, near-verbatim output, which fits code, routing, summarization.\nHigher values (0.7–1.2) give more varied output, which fits open-ended chat.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "think": {
          "description": "Enable or disable chain-of-thought thinking for models that support it\n(e.g. Qwen3, GLM-4). `true` turns thinking on, `false` turns it off.\n`None` (default) lets the model decide. Forwarded as `enable_thinking`\nin the request body; mirrors the Ollama provider's `think` field.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "description": "HTTP request timeout in seconds. Bump this for slow local model_providers (Ollama on CPU, big local models) or high-latency networks; leave unset otherwise.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "tls_ca_cert_path": {
          "description": "Path to a PEM-encoded CA certificate for TLS connections to this provider.\nMust be an absolute path; shell expansion (e.g. `~`) is not performed.\nLeave unset to use the system's default trust store.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "uri": {
          "description": "Endpoint URI the client hits. Override the family's default endpoint when pointing at a self-hosted gateway (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama), a custom proxy, or any non-standard URL. Leave unset to use the family's default URI from its `ModelEndpoint` impl. Set this to the FULL endpoint URL; there is no separate path-suffix field.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "vision": {
          "description": "Override the provider's vision (image input) capability.\n`None` (default) uses the provider family's built-in default. Several\nfamilies (llama.cpp, the generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint, etc.)\nassume vision-capable because they can serve multimodal models. Set\n`vision = false` for a text-only model served by such a family (e.g. a\ntext LLM behind llama.cpp) so image messages are routed to a configured\n`[multimodal] vision_model_provider` instead of being sent to a model\nthat rejects them. `Some(true)` forces vision on.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "wire_api": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/WireApi"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Wire protocol flavor: `responses` for OpenAI's Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`), `chat_completions` for the legacy chat wire and most OpenAI-compatible gateways. New OpenAI provider slots default to `responses`; other families default to chat-completions (or ignore the field). Only override if you're forcing an unusual combination."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "VeniceModelProviderConfig": {
      "description": "Named model_provider profile definition.",
      "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "description": "Secret API token for this model_provider. Grab it from the model_provider's dashboard (OpenAI platform, Anthropic console, OpenRouter keys page, etc.). Stored via the OS keyring when possible; never commit it to config.toml directly.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "chat_template_kwargs": {
          "description": "Arbitrary key/value pairs forwarded verbatim as `chat_template_kwargs`\nin the request body (llama.cpp-specific). Use this to pass model-family\ntemplate variables that control behaviour not exposed by other fields.\nExample (Qwen3 thinking suppression):\n  `chat_template_kwargs = { enable_thinking = false }`"
        },
        "context_window": {
          "description": "Context window size (max input tokens) for this model.\nAuto-populated on setup from provider's /models endpoint if available.\nOverride manually for custom endpoints or when auto-detection fails.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "extra_headers": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "description": "Extra HTTP headers sent with every request. Niche: used for auth bridges, corporate proxies, or custom gateways that demand a tracing header. Most users never touch this; edit `config.toml` directly if you need it.",
          "type": "object",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "fallback": {
          "description": "Ordered list of other provider aliases to try when every model on this\nalias has failed. Each entry is a dotted `<type>.<alias>` reference into\n`providers.models` and resolves with its own credentials, endpoint, and\nmodel. A fallback never inherits this alias's key. The walk is\ndepth-first: this alias's models are exhausted first, then each fallback\nalias is descended in turn (applying its own `fallback_models` and\n`fallback`). Empty means no provider-level fallback.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/ModelProviderRef"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "fallback_models": {
          "description": "Ordered alternate models to try on THIS provider before falling over to\nthe `fallback` aliases. Same endpoint, key, and headers as the primary\n`model`. Only the model identifier changes. Use this when a provider\nserves a backup model (e.g. a smaller or older variant) that should be\ntried before leaving the provider entirely. Empty means only `model` is\ntried.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "kind": {
          "description": "Provider implementation to instantiate for this profile. Use this\nwhen a canonical typed slot should run through a compatible\nimplementation, e.g. `[providers.models.openai.proxy] kind =\n\"openai-compatible\"`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "live_pricing": {
          "description": "Pull live token prices for this provider's models from its own\nOpenAI-compatible `/models` listing (the gateway is the source of truth\nfor its prices), filling cost-tracking rates for models the operator\nhas NOT priced under `[cost.rates]` / `pricing`. Models the gateway does\nnot price (or providers with no HTTP `/models` listing at all, such as\na subprocess gateway like `kilocli`) fall back to the public models.dev\ncatalog. Configured rates always win; live prices only fill gaps. A\nbackground task refreshes the price snapshot hourly; the cost-recording\npath reads the cached snapshot and never blocks on the network. Default\n`false`: off means no fetching and behavior identical to a build\nwithout the feature.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "max_tokens": {
          "description": "Hard cap on response length in tokens. Most models enforce sensible built-in limits already; leave unset unless you specifically need to clip long outputs for cost or latency reasons.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "merge_system_into_user": {
          "description": "ModelProvider-specific quirk: fold the system prompt into the first user message instead of sending a separate system role. Only needed for models that reject (or mishandle) a standalone system role, e.g. certain older Mistral variants.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "model": {
          "description": "Model identifier to send with each request: the ID string from the model_provider's catalog (e.g. `gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `llama-3.3-70b`). Must match a model the model_provider actually serves on this account.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "native_tools": {
          "description": "Override the provider's default for native tool calling.\n`None` (default) honors the provider's built-in choice. `Some(true)`\nforces native tool calls on, `Some(false)` forces text-fallback.\nCurrently consulted only by the Groq factory, which defaults to\ntext-fallback because llama-family Groq models reject native tool\ncalls with HTTP 400. Setting `native_tools = true` re-enables native\ntool calling for Groq models that support it.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "pricing": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "format": "double",
            "type": "number"
          },
          "description": "Per-model pricing for cost tracking, USD per 1M tokens.\n\nFree-form key/value map. Keys are user-defined model identifiers; an\noptional `.input` / `.output` suffix encodes pricing dimension when\nthe operator wants to split rates. A bare key without a suffix is\nused as a flat per-token rate when neither dimension is specified.\nDefault is empty: cost tracking falls back to \"unknown\" rates and\nonly token usage is recorded.\n\nExample: `pricing = { opus = 15.0, sonnet = 3.0 }`\nOr split: `pricing = { \"opus.input\" = 15.0, \"opus.output\" = 75.0 }`",
          "type": "object"
        },
        "provider_extra": {
          "description": "Extra JSON parameters to include in API requests.\nMerged at the top level of the request body, allowing provider-specific\nfeatures (routing, transforms, etc.) without code changes.\nExample: `provider_extra = { model_provider = { only = [\"Anthropic\"] } }`"
        },
        "replay_assistant_reasoning": {
          "description": "Whether stored assistant reasoning should be replayed on outbound\nassistant history messages. `Some(false)` strips `reasoning_content`\nand `reasoning` before sending. `None` (default) honours the provider's\nbuilt-in default (true for most compat providers, false for Groq).",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "requires_openai_auth": {
          "description": "When true, the client pulls credentials from ZeroClaw's stored `openai-codex` auth profile instead of the `api_key` field above. Import an existing Codex CLI login with `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json`, or run `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex`. Turn on only for the OpenAI Codex model_provider; leave off for standard API-key model_providers.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "temperature": {
          "description": "Sampling temperature passed to the model. Lower values (0.0–0.3) give\ndeterministic, near-verbatim output, which fits code, routing, summarization.\nHigher values (0.7–1.2) give more varied output, which fits open-ended chat.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "think": {
          "description": "Enable or disable chain-of-thought thinking for models that support it\n(e.g. Qwen3, GLM-4). `true` turns thinking on, `false` turns it off.\n`None` (default) lets the model decide. Forwarded as `enable_thinking`\nin the request body; mirrors the Ollama provider's `think` field.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "description": "HTTP request timeout in seconds. Bump this for slow local model_providers (Ollama on CPU, big local models) or high-latency networks; leave unset otherwise.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "tls_ca_cert_path": {
          "description": "Path to a PEM-encoded CA certificate for TLS connections to this provider.\nMust be an absolute path; shell expansion (e.g. `~`) is not performed.\nLeave unset to use the system's default trust store.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "uri": {
          "description": "Endpoint URI the client hits. Override the family's default endpoint when pointing at a self-hosted gateway (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama), a custom proxy, or any non-standard URL. Leave unset to use the family's default URI from its `ModelEndpoint` impl. Set this to the FULL endpoint URL; there is no separate path-suffix field.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "vision": {
          "description": "Override the provider's vision (image input) capability.\n`None` (default) uses the provider family's built-in default. Several\nfamilies (llama.cpp, the generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint, etc.)\nassume vision-capable because they can serve multimodal models. Set\n`vision = false` for a text-only model served by such a family (e.g. a\ntext LLM behind llama.cpp) so image messages are routed to a configured\n`[multimodal] vision_model_provider` instead of being sent to a model\nthat rejects them. `Some(true)` forces vision on.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "wire_api": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/WireApi"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Wire protocol flavor: `responses` for OpenAI's Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`), `chat_completions` for the legacy chat wire and most OpenAI-compatible gateways. New OpenAI provider slots default to `responses`; other families default to chat-completions (or ignore the field). Only override if you're forcing an unusual combination."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },

Import an existing Codex CLI login with `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json`, or run `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex`. Turn on only for the OpenAI Codex model_provider; leave off for standard API-key model_providers.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "temperature": {
          "description": "Sampling temperature passed to the model. Lower values (0.0–0.3) give\ndeterministic, near-verbatim output, which fits code, routing, summarization.\nHigher values (0.7–1.2) give more varied output, which fits open-ended chat.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "think": {
          "description": "Enable or disable chain-of-thought thinking for models that support it\n(e.g. Qwen3, GLM-4). `true` turns thinking on, `false` turns it off.\n`None` (default) lets the model decide. Forwarded as `enable_thinking`\nin the request body; mirrors the Ollama provider's `think` field.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "description": "HTTP request timeout in seconds. Bump this for slow local model_providers (Ollama on CPU, big local models) or high-latency networks; leave unset otherwise.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "tls_ca_cert_path": {
          "description": "Path to a PEM-encoded CA certificate for TLS connections to this provider.\nMust be an absolute path; shell expansion (e.g. `~`) is not performed.\nLeave unset to use the system's default trust store.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "uri": {
          "description": "Endpoint URI the client hits. Override the family's default endpoint when pointing at a self-hosted gateway (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama), a custom proxy, or any non-standard URL. Leave unset to use the family's default URI from its `ModelEndpoint` impl. Set this to the FULL endpoint URL; there is no separate path-suffix field.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "vision": {
          "description": "Override the provider's vision (image input) capability.\n`None` (default) uses the provider family's built-in default. Several\nfamilies (llama.cpp, the generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint, etc.)\nassume vision-capable because they can serve multimodal models. Set\n`vision = false` for a text-only model served by such a family (e.g. a\ntext LLM behind llama.cpp) so image messages are routed to a configured\n`[multimodal] vision_model_provider` instead of being sent to a model\nthat rejects them. `Some(true)` forces vision on.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "wire_api": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/WireApi"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Wire protocol flavor: `responses` for OpenAI's Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`), `chat_completions` for the legacy chat wire and most OpenAI-compatible gateways. New OpenAI provider slots default to `responses`; other families default to chat-completions (or ignore the field). Only override if you're forcing an unusual combination."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "VoiceCallConfig": {
      "properties": {
        "account_id": {
          "type": "string"
        },
        "auth_token": {
          "type": "string"
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Whether this channel is active. The runtime only loads channels whose\n`enabled = true`. Default: `false` so an operator who pastes a partial\n`[channels.<type>.<alias>]` block doesn't accidentally bring a channel\nlive before the rest of its config is filled in.",

    "VoiceDuplexConfig": {

          "default": false,

          "type": "boolean"
        },

    "VoiceWakeConfig": {
      "description": "Voice wake word detection channel configuration.\n\nListens on the default microphone for a configurable wake word,\nthen captures the following utterance and transcribes it via the\nexisting transcription API.",
      "properties": {
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Whether this channel is active. The runtime only loads channels whose\n`enabled = true`. Default: `false` so an operator who pastes a partial\n`[channels.<type>.<alias>]` block doesn't accidentally bring a channel\nlive before the rest of its config is filled in.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "energy_threshold": {
          "default": 0.009999999776482582,
          "description": "RMS energy threshold for voice activity detection. Samples below\nthis level are treated as silence. Default: `0.01`.",
          "format": "float",
          "type": "number"
        },
        "excluded_tools": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Tools excluded from this channel's tool spec. When set, these tools\nare not exposed to the model when responding via this channel.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "max_capture_secs": {
          "default": 30,
          "description": "Maximum capture duration in seconds before forcing transcription.\nDefault: `30`.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "silence_timeout_ms": {
          "default": 2000,
          "description": "Silence timeout in milliseconds: how long to wait after the last\nenergy spike before finalizing a capture window. Default: `2000`.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "wake_word": {
          "default": "hey zeroclaw",
          "description": "Wake word phrase to listen for (case-insensitive substring match).\nDefault: `\"hey zeroclaw\"`.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },

    "WeComWsConfig": {
      "description": "WeCom AI Bot WebSocket configuration.\n\nThis is distinct from webhook-based [`WeComConfig`] and uses the WeCom AI\nBot long-connection API for inbound messages and active-session replies.",
      "properties": {
        "allowed_groups": {

          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Whether this channel is active. The runtime only loads channels whose\n`enabled = true`. Default: `false` so an operator who pastes a partial\n`[channels.<type>.<alias>]` block doesn't accidentally bring a channel\nlive before the rest of its config is filled in.",

        },

        },

    "WebAuthnConfig": {
      "description": "WebAuthn / FIDO2 hardware key authentication configuration (`[security.webauthn]`).\n\nEnables registration and authentication via hardware security keys\n(YubiKey, SoloKey, etc.) and platform authenticators (Touch ID, Windows Hello).",

          "description": "Relying Party display name. Default: \"ZeroClaw\".",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "rp_origin": {
          "default": "http://localhost:42617",
          "description": "Relying Party origin URL (e.g. `\"https://example.com\"`). Default: `\"http://localhost:42617\"`.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "WebFetchConfig": {
      "description": "Web fetch tool configuration (`[web_fetch]` section).\n\nFetches web pages and converts HTML to plain text for LLM consumption.\nDomain filtering: `allowed_domains` controls which hosts are reachable (use `[\"*\"]`\nfor all public hosts). `blocked_domains` takes priority over `allowed_domains`.\nIf `allowed_domains` is empty, all requests are rejected (deny-by-default).",
      "properties": {
        "allowed_domains": {
          "default": [
            "*"
          ],
          "description": "Allowed domains for web fetch (exact or subdomain match; `[\"*\"]` = all public hosts)",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "allowed_private_hosts": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Private/internal hosts allowed to bypass SSRF protection (e.g. `[\"192.168.1.10\", \"internal.local\"]`).\nExact and subdomain matches are supported. Listing a host skips the\nresolved-IP SSRF check for it; a *literal* private/local host (IP literal,\nlocalhost, .local) listed here also bypasses `allowed_domains`. The `*`\nwildcard permits any literal private/local host and lets a name already in\n`allowed_domains` resolve to a private IP, but it does NOT widen\n`allowed_domains` — a non-private host (matched explicitly or via `*`) still\nneeds `allowed_domains`, so `*` cannot reach an arbitrary public host.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "blocked_domains": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Blocked domains (exact or subdomain match; always takes priority over allowed_domains)",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": true,
          "description": "Enable `web_fetch` tool for fetching web page content",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "firecrawl": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/FirecrawlConfig",
          "default": {
            "api_key_env": "FIRECRAWL_API_KEY",
            "api_url": "https://api.firecrawl.dev/v1",
            "enabled": false,
            "mode": "scrape"
          },
          "description": "Firecrawl fallback configuration (`[web_fetch.firecrawl]`)"
        },
        "max_response_size": {
          "default": 500000,
          "description": "Maximum response size in bytes (default: 500KB, plain text is much smaller than raw HTML)",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "default": 30,
          "description": "Request timeout in seconds (default: 30)",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "WebSearchConfig": {
      "description": "Web search tool configuration (`[web_search]` section).",
      "properties": {
        "bocha_api_key": {
          "default": null,

        },
        "jina_api_key": {
          "default": null,

            "string",

          ],

        },
        "search_provider": {
          "default": "duckduckgo",
          "description": "Search provider: \"duckduckgo\" (free), \"brave\" (requires API key), \"tavily\" (requires API key), \"searxng\" (self-hosted), \"jina\" (requires API key), or \"bocha\" (Bocha AI, requires API key — Chinese-friendly, <https://open.bochaai.com>)",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "searxng_instance_url": {
          "default": null,

          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "tavily_api_key": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Tavily Search API key (required if search_provider is \"tavily\")",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "default": 15,

          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,

        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "WebhookAuditConfig": {
      "description": "Configuration for the webhook-audit builtin hook.\n\nSends an HTTP POST with a JSON body to an external endpoint each time\na tool call matches one of the configured patterns. Useful for\ncentralised audit logging, SIEM ingestion, or compliance pipelines.",
      "properties": {
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Enable the webhook-audit hook. Default: `false`.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "include_args": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Include tool call arguments in the audit payload. Default: `false`.\n\nBe mindful of sensitive data — arguments may contain secrets or PII.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "max_args_bytes": {
          "default": 4096,
          "description": "Maximum size (in bytes) of serialised arguments included in a single\naudit payload. Arguments exceeding this limit are truncated.\nDefault: `4096`.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "tool_patterns": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Glob patterns for tool names to audit (e.g. `[\"Bash\", \"Write\"]`).\nAn empty list means **no** tools are audited.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "url": {
          "default": "",
          "description": "Target URL that will receive the audit POST requests.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "WebhookConfig": {
      "description": "Webhook channel configuration.\n\nReceives messages via HTTP POST and sends replies to a configurable outbound URL.\nThis is the \"universal adapter\" for any system that supports webhooks.",
      "properties": {
        "auth_header": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Optional `Authorization` header value for outbound requests.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Whether this channel is active. The runtime only loads channels whose\n`enabled = true`. Default: `false` so an operator who pastes a partial\n`[channels.<type>.<alias>]` block doesn't accidentally bring a channel\nlive before the rest of its config is filled in.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "excluded_tools": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Tools excluded from this channel's tool spec. When set, these tools\nare not exposed to the model when responding via this channel.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "listen_path": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "URL path to listen on (default: `/webhook`).",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "max_retries": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Maximum number of retry attempts for outbound sends on transient failures\n(network errors, 429, 5xx). Set to `0` to disable retries. Default: `3`.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "port": {
          "default": 8090,
          "description": "Port to listen on for incoming webhooks.",
          "format": "uint16",
          "maximum": 65535,
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "reply_min_interval_secs": {
          "default": 0,
          "description": "Per-(channel, recipient) outbound pacing floor in seconds.\nRange: `0..=REPLY_MIN_INTERVAL_MAX_SECS` (0 disables).",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "reply_queue_depth_max": {
          "default": 0,
          "description": "Per-(channel, recipient) outbound pacing queue depth.\nRange: `0..=REPLY_QUEUE_DEPTH_CEILING`. When `reply_min_interval_secs > 0`\nand this value is `0`, the pacing wrapper substitutes\n`DEFAULT_REPLY_QUEUE_DEPTH` (16). When the queue is full, the\nnewest send is dropped and a `WARN` is logged.",
          "format": "uint16",
          "maximum": 65535,
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "retry_base_delay_ms": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Base delay in milliseconds for exponential backoff between retries. Default: `500`.\nValues below `1` are clamped to `1ms` at runtime to avoid busy-retry loops.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "retry_max_delay_ms": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Maximum delay cap in milliseconds for any single retry wait. Default: `30000` (30s).\nValues below `1` are clamped to `1ms` at runtime to avoid busy-retry loops.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "secret": {
          "description": "Shared secret for webhook signature verification (HMAC-SHA256).\nThe channel will refuse to start without one. Set\n`[channels.webhook.<alias>].secret` in config.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "send_method": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "HTTP method for outbound messages (`POST` or `PUT`). Default: `POST`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "send_url": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "URL to POST/PUT outbound messages to.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "WhatsAppChatPolicy": {
      "description": "Policy for a particular WhatsApp chat type (DMs or groups) when\n`mode = \"personal\"`.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "allowlist",
          "description": "Only respond to senders on the `allowed_numbers` list (default).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "ignore",
          "description": "Ignore all messages in this chat type.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "all",
          "description": "Respond to every message regardless of allowlist.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    },
    "WhatsAppConfig": {
      "description": "WhatsApp channel configuration (Cloud API or Web mode).\n\nSet `phone_number_id` for Cloud API mode, or `session_path` for Web mode.",
      "properties": {
        "access_token": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Access token from Meta Business Suite (Cloud API mode)",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "allowed_groups": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Allowed group chats by JID (Web mode). An empty list (the default)\npermits all groups; a non-empty list drops every group message whose\nchat JID matches no entry. Each entry matches either the full group\nJID (`123456789012345@g.us`) or the JID user part - the segment before\n`@` (`123456789012345`) - compared exactly, not as a string prefix.\nDirect messages bypass this filter regardless of list contents.\nModeled on the Matrix channel's `allowed_rooms`; it gates group\nidentity, which `dm_policy`/`group_policy` (chat type) and the\nsender allowlist (sender) do not.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "app_secret": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "App secret from Meta Business Suite (for webhook signature verification)\nCan also be set via `ZEROCLAW_WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET` environment variable\nOnly used in Cloud API mode",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "approval_timeout_secs": {
          "default": 300,
          "description": "Seconds to wait for operator approval on `always_ask` tools before auto-denying.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "dm_mention_patterns": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Regex patterns for DM mention gating (case-insensitive).\nWhen non-empty, only direct messages matching at least one pattern are\nprocessed; matched fragments are stripped from the forwarded content.\nExample: `[\"@?ZeroClaw\", \"\\\\+?15555550123\"]`",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "dm_policy": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/WhatsAppChatPolicy",
          "default": "allowlist",
          "description": "Policy for direct messages when mode = \"personal\".\n\"allowlist\" (default) | \"ignore\" | \"all\"."
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Whether this channel is active. The runtime only loads channels whose\n`enabled = true`. Default: `false` so an operator who pastes a partial\n`[channels.<type>.<alias>]` block doesn't accidentally bring a channel\nlive before the rest of its config is filled in.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "excluded_tools": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Tools excluded from this channel's tool spec. When set, these tools\nare not exposed to the model when responding via this channel.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "group_mention_patterns": {
          "default": [],
          "description": "Regex patterns for group-chat mention gating (case-insensitive).\nWhen non-empty, only group messages matching at least one pattern are\nprocessed; matched fragments are stripped from the forwarded content.\nExample: `[\"@?ZeroClaw\", \"\\\\+?15555550123\"]`",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "group_policy": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/WhatsAppChatPolicy",
          "default": "allowlist",
          "description": "Policy for group chats when mode = \"personal\".\n\"allowlist\" (default) | \"ignore\" | \"all\"."
        },
        "interrupt_on_new_message": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Cancel an in-flight response from this channel sender when a newer\nWhatsApp message arrives. Default: `false`.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "mention_only": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "When true, only respond to messages that @-mention the bot in groups (Web mode only).\nDirect messages are always processed.\nBot identity is resolved from the wa-rs device at runtime; `pair_phone` seeds it on first connect.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "mode": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/WhatsAppWebMode",
          "default": "business",
          "description": "Usage mode for WhatsApp Web: \"business\" (default) or \"personal\".\nIn personal mode the bot applies dm_policy, group_policy, and\nself_chat_mode to decide which chats to respond in."
        },
        "pair_code": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Custom pair code for linking (Web mode, optional)\nLeave empty to let WhatsApp generate one",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "pair_phone": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Phone number for pair code linking (Web mode, optional)\nFormat: country code + number (e.g., \"15551234567\")\nIf not set, QR code pairing will be used",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "passive_group_context": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "When true in WhatsApp Web group chats, unaddressed messages that pass\nsender/chat authorization are recorded as passive conversation context\nwithout starting an agent turn. Default: `false`.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "phone_number_id": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Phone number ID from Meta Business API (Cloud API mode)",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "proxy_url": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Per-channel proxy URL (http, https, socks5, socks5h).\nOverrides the global `[proxy]` setting for this channel only.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "reply_min_interval_secs": {
          "default": 0,
          "description": "Per-(channel, recipient) outbound pacing floor in seconds.\nRange: `0..=REPLY_MIN_INTERVAL_MAX_SECS` (0 disables).",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "reply_queue_depth_max": {
          "default": 0,
          "description": "Per-(channel, recipient) outbound pacing queue depth.\nRange: `0..=REPLY_QUEUE_DEPTH_CEILING`. When `reply_min_interval_secs > 0`\nand this value is `0`, the pacing wrapper substitutes\n`DEFAULT_REPLY_QUEUE_DEPTH` (16). When the queue is full, the\nnewest send is dropped and a `WARN` is logged.",
          "format": "uint16",
          "maximum": 65535,
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "self_chat_mode": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "When true and mode = \"personal\", always respond to messages in the\nuser's own self-chat (Notes to Self). Defaults to false.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "session_path": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Session database path for WhatsApp Web client (Web mode)\nWhen set, enables native WhatsApp Web mode with wa-rs",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "verify_token": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Webhook verify token (you define this, Meta sends it back for verification)\nOnly used in Cloud API mode",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "ws_url": {
          "default": null,
          "description": "Override the WhatsApp Web WebSocket URL (Web mode, optional). Used\nby integration tests and proxy setups; leave unset to use the\ndefault endpoint that ships with `wa-rs`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "WhatsAppWebMode": {
      "description": "WhatsApp Web usage mode.\n\n`Personal` treats the account as a personal phone — the bot only responds to\nincoming messages that pass the DM/group/self-chat policy filters.\n`Business` (default) responds to all incoming messages, subject only to the\n`allowed_numbers` allowlist.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "business",
          "description": "Respond to all messages passing the allowlist (default).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "personal",
          "description": "Apply per-chat-type policies (dm_policy, group_policy, self_chat_mode).",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    },
    "WireApi": {
      "description": "Wire protocol flavor for the model_provider client. `responses` routes\nthrough OpenAI's Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`);\n`chat_completions` routes through the legacy `/v1/chat/completions` (or\nthe family's chat-completions-compatible endpoint). New OpenAI provider\nslots default to `responses`; other families default to chat-completions\n(or ignore the field) when unset.",
      "enum": [
        "responses",
        "chat_completions"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    },
    "WssConfig": {
      "description": "WebSocket Secure (WSS) transport for remote TUI-to-daemon connections (`[wss]`).\n\nWhen enabled, the daemon listens for TLS-encrypted WebSocket connections\non the configured bind address and port. TUI clients connect via\n`--connect wss://host:port`.",
      "properties": {
        "bind": {
          "default": "0.0.0.0",
          "description": "Bind address for the WSS listener (default: \"0.0.0.0\").",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "cert_path": {
          "default": "",
          "description": "Path to the PEM-encoded server certificate file.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "enabled": {
          "default": false,
          "description": "Enable the WSS listener (default: false).",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "key_path": {
          "default": "",
          "description": "Path to the PEM-encoded server private key file.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "port": {
          "default": 9781,
          "description": "Port for the WSS listener (default: 9781).",
          "format": "uint16",
          "maximum": 65535,
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "XaiModelProviderConfig": {
      "description": "Named model_provider profile definition.",
      "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "description": "Secret API token for this model_provider. Grab it from the model_provider's dashboard (OpenAI platform, Anthropic console, OpenRouter keys page, etc.). Stored via the OS keyring when possible; never commit it to config.toml directly.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "chat_template_kwargs": {
          "description": "Arbitrary key/value pairs forwarded verbatim as `chat_template_kwargs`\nin the request body (llama.cpp-specific). Use this to pass model-family\ntemplate variables that control behaviour not exposed by other fields.\nExample (Qwen3 thinking suppression):\n  `chat_template_kwargs = { enable_thinking = false }`"
        },
        "context_window": {
          "description": "Context window size (max input tokens) for this model.\nAuto-populated on setup from provider's /models endpoint if available.\nOverride manually for custom endpoints or when auto-detection fails.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "extra_headers": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "description": "Extra HTTP headers sent with every request. Niche: used for auth bridges, corporate proxies, or custom gateways that demand a tracing header. Most users never touch this; edit `config.toml` directly if you need it.",
          "type": "object",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "fallback": {
          "description": "Ordered list of other provider aliases to try when every model on this\nalias has failed. Each entry is a dotted `<type>.<alias>` reference into\n`providers.models` and resolves with its own credentials, endpoint, and\nmodel. A fallback never inherits this alias's key. The walk is\ndepth-first: this alias's models are exhausted first, then each fallback\nalias is descended in turn (applying its own `fallback_models` and\n`fallback`). Empty means no provider-level fallback.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/ModelProviderRef"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "fallback_models": {
          "description": "Ordered alternate models to try on THIS provider before falling over to\nthe `fallback` aliases. Same endpoint, key, and headers as the primary\n`model`. Only the model identifier changes. Use this when a provider\nserves a backup model (e.g. a smaller or older variant) that should be\ntried before leaving the provider entirely. Empty means only `model` is\ntried.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "kind": {
          "description": "Provider implementation to instantiate for this profile. Use this\nwhen a canonical typed slot should run through a compatible\nimplementation, e.g. `[providers.models.openai.proxy] kind =\n\"openai-compatible\"`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "live_pricing": {
          "description": "Pull live token prices for this provider's models from its own\nOpenAI-compatible `/models` listing (the gateway is the source of truth\nfor its prices), filling cost-tracking rates for models the operator\nhas NOT priced under `[cost.rates]` / `pricing`. Models the gateway does\nnot price (or providers with no HTTP `/models` listing at all, such as\na subprocess gateway like `kilocli`) fall back to the public models.dev\ncatalog. Configured rates always win; live prices only fill gaps. A\nbackground task refreshes the price snapshot hourly; the cost-recording\npath reads the cached snapshot and never blocks on the network. Default\n`false`: off means no fetching and behavior identical to a build\nwithout the feature.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "max_tokens": {
          "description": "Hard cap on response length in tokens. Most models enforce sensible built-in limits already; leave unset unless you specifically need to clip long outputs for cost or latency reasons.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "merge_system_into_user": {
          "description": "ModelProvider-specific quirk: fold the system prompt into the first user message instead of sending a separate system role. Only needed for models that reject (or mishandle) a standalone system role, e.g. certain older Mistral variants.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "model": {
          "description": "Model identifier to send with each request: the ID string from the model_provider's catalog (e.g. `gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `llama-3.3-70b`). Must match a model the model_provider actually serves on this account.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "native_tools": {
          "description": "Override the provider's default for native tool calling.\n`None` (default) honors the provider's built-in choice. `Some(true)`\nforces native tool calls on, `Some(false)` forces text-fallback.\nCurrently consulted only by the Groq factory, which defaults to\ntext-fallback because llama-family Groq models reject native tool\ncalls with HTTP 400. Setting `native_tools = true` re-enables native\ntool calling for Groq models that support it.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "pricing": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "format": "double",
            "type": "number"
          },
          "description": "Per-model pricing for cost tracking, USD per 1M tokens.\n\nFree-form key/value map. Keys are user-defined model identifiers; an\noptional `.input` / `.output` suffix encodes pricing dimension when\nthe operator wants to split rates. A bare key without a suffix is\nused as a flat per-token rate when neither dimension is specified.\nDefault is empty: cost tracking falls back to \"unknown\" rates and\nonly token usage is recorded.\n\nExample: `pricing = { opus = 15.0, sonnet = 3.0 }`\nOr split: `pricing = { \"opus.input\" = 15.0, \"opus.output\" = 75.0 }`",
          "type": "object"
        },
        "provider_extra": {
          "description": "Extra JSON parameters to include in API requests.\nMerged at the top level of the request body, allowing provider-specific\nfeatures (routing, transforms, etc.) without code changes.\nExample: `provider_extra = { model_provider = { only = [\"Anthropic\"] } }`"
        },
        "replay_assistant_reasoning": {
          "description": "Whether stored assistant reasoning should be replayed on outbound\nassistant history messages. `Some(false)` strips `reasoning_content`\nand `reasoning` before sending. `None` (default) honours the provider's\nbuilt-in default (true for most compat providers, false for Groq).",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "requires_openai_auth": {
          "description": "When true, the client pulls credentials from ZeroClaw's stored `openai-codex` auth profile instead of the `api_key` field above. Import an existing Codex CLI login with `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json`, or run `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex`. Turn on only for the OpenAI Codex model_provider; leave off for standard API-key model_providers.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "temperature": {
          "description": "Sampling temperature passed to the model. Lower values (0.0–0.3) give\ndeterministic, near-verbatim output, which fits code, routing, summarization.\nHigher values (0.7–1.2) give more varied output, which fits open-ended chat.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "think": {
          "description": "Enable or disable chain-of-thought thinking for models that support it\n(e.g. Qwen3, GLM-4). `true` turns thinking on, `false` turns it off.\n`None` (default) lets the model decide. Forwarded as `enable_thinking`\nin the request body; mirrors the Ollama provider's `think` field.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "description": "HTTP request timeout in seconds. Bump this for slow local model_providers (Ollama on CPU, big local models) or high-latency networks; leave unset otherwise.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "tls_ca_cert_path": {
          "description": "Path to a PEM-encoded CA certificate for TLS connections to this provider.\nMust be an absolute path; shell expansion (e.g. `~`) is not performed.\nLeave unset to use the system's default trust store.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "uri": {
          "description": "Endpoint URI the client hits. Override the family's default endpoint when pointing at a self-hosted gateway (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama), a custom proxy, or any non-standard URL. Leave unset to use the family's default URI from its `ModelEndpoint` impl. Set this to the FULL endpoint URL; there is no separate path-suffix field.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "vision": {
          "description": "Override the provider's vision (image input) capability.\n`None` (default) uses the provider family's built-in default. Several\nfamilies (llama.cpp, the generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint, etc.)\nassume vision-capable because they can serve multimodal models. Set\n`vision = false` for a text-only model served by such a family (e.g. a\ntext LLM behind llama.cpp) so image messages are routed to a configured\n`[multimodal] vision_model_provider` instead of being sent to a model\nthat rejects them. `Some(true)` forces vision on.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "wire_api": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/WireApi"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Wire protocol flavor: `responses` for OpenAI's Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`), `chat_completions` for the legacy chat wire and most OpenAI-compatible gateways. New OpenAI provider slots default to `responses`; other families default to chat-completions (or ignore the field). Only override if you're forcing an unusual combination."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },

        },
        "model": {
          "description": "Model identifier to send with each request: the ID string from the model_provider's catalog (e.g. `gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `llama-3.3-70b`). Must match a model the model_provider actually serves on this account.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "native_tools": {
          "description": "Override the provider's default for native tool calling.\n`None` (default) honors the provider's built-in choice. `Some(true)`\nforces native tool calls on, `Some(false)` forces text-fallback.\nCurrently consulted only by the Groq factory, which defaults to\ntext-fallback because llama-family Groq models reject native tool\ncalls with HTTP 400. Setting `native_tools = true` re-enables native\ntool calling for Groq models that support it.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "pricing": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "format": "double",
            "type": "number"
          },
          "description": "Per-model pricing for cost tracking, USD per 1M tokens.\n\nFree-form key/value map. Keys are user-defined model identifiers; an\noptional `.input` / `.output` suffix encodes pricing dimension when\nthe operator wants to split rates. A bare key without a suffix is\nused as a flat per-token rate when neither dimension is specified.\nDefault is empty: cost tracking falls back to \"unknown\" rates and\nonly token usage is recorded.\n\nExample: `pricing = { opus = 15.0, sonnet = 3.0 }`\nOr split: `pricing = { \"opus.input\" = 15.0, \"opus.output\" = 75.0 }`",
          "type": "object"
        },
        "provider_extra": {
          "description": "Extra JSON parameters to include in API requests.\nMerged at the top level of the request body, allowing provider-specific\nfeatures (routing, transforms, etc.) without code changes.\nExample: `provider_extra = { model_provider = { only = [\"Anthropic\"] } }`"
        },
        "replay_assistant_reasoning": {
          "description": "Whether stored assistant reasoning should be replayed on outbound\nassistant history messages. `Some(false)` strips `reasoning_content`\nand `reasoning` before sending. `None` (default) honours the provider's\nbuilt-in default (true for most compat providers, false for Groq).",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "requires_openai_auth": {
          "description": "When true, the client pulls credentials from ZeroClaw's stored `openai-codex` auth profile instead of the `api_key` field above. Import an existing Codex CLI login with `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex --import ~/.codex/auth.json`, or run `zeroclaw auth login --model-provider openai-codex`. Turn on only for the OpenAI Codex model_provider; leave off for standard API-key model_providers.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "temperature": {
          "description": "Sampling temperature passed to the model. Lower values (0.0–0.3) give\ndeterministic, near-verbatim output, which fits code, routing, summarization.\nHigher values (0.7–1.2) give more varied output, which fits open-ended chat.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": [
            "number",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "think": {
          "description": "Enable or disable chain-of-thought thinking for models that support it\n(e.g. Qwen3, GLM-4). `true` turns thinking on, `false` turns it off.\n`None` (default) lets the model decide. Forwarded as `enable_thinking`\nin the request body; mirrors the Ollama provider's `think` field.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "timeout_secs": {
          "description": "HTTP request timeout in seconds. Bump this for slow local model_providers (Ollama on CPU, big local models) or high-latency networks; leave unset otherwise.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "tls_ca_cert_path": {
          "description": "Path to a PEM-encoded CA certificate for TLS connections to this provider.\nMust be an absolute path; shell expansion (e.g. `~`) is not performed.\nLeave unset to use the system's default trust store.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "uri": {
          "description": "Endpoint URI the client hits. Override the family's default endpoint when pointing at a self-hosted gateway (LiteLLM, vLLM, Ollama), a custom proxy, or any non-standard URL. Leave unset to use the family's default URI from its `ModelEndpoint` impl. Set this to the FULL endpoint URL; there is no separate path-suffix field.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "vision": {
          "description": "Override the provider's vision (image input) capability.\n`None` (default) uses the provider family's built-in default. Several\nfamilies (llama.cpp, the generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint, etc.)\nassume vision-capable because they can serve multimodal models. Set\n`vision = false` for a text-only model served by such a family (e.g. a\ntext LLM behind llama.cpp) so image messages are routed to a configured\n`[multimodal] vision_model_provider` instead of being sent to a model\nthat rejects them. `Some(true)` forces vision on.",
          "type": [
            "boolean",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "wire_api": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/WireApi"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "Wire protocol flavor: `responses` for OpenAI's Responses API (`POST /v1/responses`), `chat_completions` for the legacy chat wire and most OpenAI-compatible gateways. New OpenAI provider slots default to `responses`; other families default to chat-completions (or ignore the field). Only override if you're forcing an unusual combination."
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "ZaiEndpoint": {
      "enum": [
        "cn",
        "global"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    },
    "ZaiModelProviderConfig": {
      "description": "Named model_provider profile definition.",
      "properties": {
        "api_key": {
          "description": "Secret API token for this model_provider. Grab it from the model_provider's dashboard (OpenAI platform, Anthropic console, OpenRouter keys page, etc.). Stored via the OS keyring when possible; never commit it to config.toml directly.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ],
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "chat_template_kwargs": {
          "description": "Arbitrary key/value pairs forwarded verbatim as `chat_template_kwargs`\nin the request body (llama.cpp-specific). Use this to pass model-family\ntemplate variables that control behaviour not exposed by other fields.\nExample (Qwen3 thinking suppression):\n  `chat_template_kwargs = { enable_thinking = false }`"
        },
        "context_window": {
          "description": "Context window size (max input tokens) for this model.\nAuto-populated on setup from provider's /models endpoint if available.\nOverride manually for custom endpoints or when auto-detection fails.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "endpoint": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/ZaiEndpoint",
          "default": "global"
        },
        "extra_headers": {
          "additionalProperties": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "description": "Extra HTTP headers sent with every request. Niche: used for auth bridges, corporate proxies, or custom gateways that demand a tracing header. Most users never touch this; edit `config.toml` directly if you need it.",
          "type": "object",
          "x-secret": true
        },
        "fallback": {
          "description": "Ordered list of other provider aliases to try when every model on this\nalias has failed. Each entry is a dotted `<type>.<alias>` reference into\n`providers.models` and resolves with its own credentials, endpoint, and\nmodel. A fallback never inherits this alias's key. The walk is\ndepth-first: this alias's models are exhausted first, then each fallback\nalias is descended in turn (applying its own `fallback_models` and\n`fallback`). Empty means no provider-level fallback.",
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/ModelProviderRef"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "fallback_models": {
          "description": "Ordered alternate models to try on THIS provider before falling over to\nthe `fallback` aliases. Same endpoint, key, and headers as the primary\n`model`. Only the model identifier changes. Use this when a provider\nserves a backup model (e.g. a smaller or older variant) that should be\ntried before leaving the provider entirely. Empty means only `model` is\ntried.",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        "kind": {
          "description": "Provider implementation to instantiate for this profile. Use this\nwhen a canonical typed slot should run through a compatible\nimplementation, e.g. `[providers.models.openai.proxy] kind =\n\"openai-compatible\"`.",
          "type": [
            "string",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "live_pricing": {
          "description": "Pull live token prices for this provider's models from its own\nOpenAI-compatible `/models` listing (the gateway is the source of truth\nfor its prices), filling cost-tracking rates for models the operator\nhas NOT priced under `[cost.rates]` / `pricing`. Models the gateway does\nnot price (or providers with no HTTP `/models` listing at all, such as\na subprocess gateway like `kilocli`) fall back to the public models.dev\ncatalog. Configured rates always win; live prices only fill gaps. A\nbackground task refreshes the price snapshot hourly; the cost-recording\npath reads the cached snapshot and never blocks on the network. Default\n`false`: off means no fetching and behavior identical to a build\nwithout the feature.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "max_tokens": {
          "description": "Hard cap on response length in tokens. Most models enforce sensible built-in limits already; leave unset unless you specifically need to clip long outputs for cost or latency reasons.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "merge_system_into_user": {
          "description": "ModelProvider-specific quirk: fold the system prompt into the first user message instead of sending a separate system role. Only needed for models that reject (or mishandle) a standalone system role, e.g. certain older Mistral variants.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "model": {
          "description": "Model identifier to send with each request: the ID string from the model_provider's catalog (e.g. `gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `llama-3.3-70b`). Must match a model the model_provider actually serves on this account.",
          "type": [

Setting `native_tools = true` re-enables native\ntool calling for Groq models that support it.",

A bare key without a suffix is\nused as a flat per-token rate when neither dimension is specified.\nDefault is empty: cost tracking falls back to \"unknown\" rates and\nonly token usage is recorded.\n\nExample: `pricing = { opus = 15.0, sonnet = 3.0 }`\nOr split: `pricing = { \"opus.input\" = 15.0, \"opus.output\" = 75.0 }`",
