<file path="op-state-store/src/public_state.rs">
//! Plugin-authored policy for projecting internal state into shared public views.
//!
//! The full state remains authoritative elsewhere. This module only derives a
//! least-privilege outbound view from the exact sealed [`PluginSchema`].

use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet, HashMap};

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize, Serializer};
use simd_json::prelude::*;
use simd_json::OwnedValue as Value;
use thiserror::Error;

use crate::plugin_schema::{FieldSchema, FieldType, PluginSchema};

const MAX_PUBLIC_PATHS: usize = 256;
const MAX_PUBLIC_PATH_DEPTH: usize = 32;

/// Explicit state paths a plugin publishes to unaffiliated shared consumers.
///
/// Object-field components use RFC 6901 escaping. A `*` component selects
/// every item of a schema-declared array while retaining only the selected
/// fields within each item. The empty policy publishes no state. A path cannot
/// select the document root, use a numeric array index, or terminate at an
/// opaque [`FieldType::Any`]. Maps require explicit literal keys in the policy;
/// neither a whole map nor a map wildcard can reveal runtime key membership.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct PublicStatePolicy {
    #[serde(
        default,
        skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty",
        serialize_with = "serialize_paths_sorted"
    )]
    pub paths: Vec<String>,
}

impl PublicStatePolicy {
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.paths.is_empty()
    }
}

fn serialize_paths_sorted<S>(paths: &[String], serializer: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error>
where
    S: Serializer,
{
    let mut sorted: Vec<&str> = paths.iter().map(String::as_str).collect();
    sorted.sort_unstable();
    sorted.serialize(serializer)
}

#[derive(Debug, Error, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PublicStateProjectionError {
    #[error("invalid public-state policy: {0}")]
    InvalidPolicy(String),
    #[error("internal state does not match the public-state contract: {0}")]
    InvalidState(String),
}

#[derive(Debug, Default)]
struct SelectionNode {
    terminal: bool,
    children: BTreeMap<String, SelectionNode>,
}

impl PluginSchema {
    /// Validate the plugin-authored public state policy without reading state.
    pub fn validate_public_state_policy(&self) -> Result<(), PublicStateProjectionError> {
        self.public_selection_tree().map(|_| ())
    }

    /// Whether the policy publishes any part of one top-level field.
    ///
    /// Consumers use this to distinguish an approved-but-currently-absent
    /// property from a field the plugin did not publish. The complete policy
    /// is validated first, so callers never need their own pointer parser.
    pub fn public_state_exposes_top_level(
        &self,
        field: &str,
    ) -> Result<bool, PublicStateProjectionError> {
        Ok(self.public_selection_tree()?.children.contains_key(field))
    }

    /// Derive the only state view suitable for the shared public namespace.
    ///
    /// `None` means the plugin publishes no public state. A configured policy
    /// returns `Some({})` when its approved fields are currently absent, which
    /// lets consumers distinguish fail-closed policy from field deletion and
    /// issue tombstones against an earlier non-empty view.
    pub fn project_public_state(
        &self,
        state: &Value,
    ) -> Result<Option<Value>, PublicStateProjectionError> {
        if self.public_state.is_empty() {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let selection = self.public_selection_tree()?;
        let source = state.as_object().ok_or_else(|| {
            PublicStateProjectionError::InvalidState("plugin root must be an object".into())
        })?;
        let projected = project_selected_object(source, &self.fields, &selection, "")?;
        Ok(Some(Value::Object(Box::new(projected))))
    }

    fn public_selection_tree(&self) -> Result<SelectionNode, PublicStateProjectionError> {
        if self.public_state.paths.len() > MAX_PUBLIC_PATHS {
            return Err(invalid_policy(format!(
                "more than {MAX_PUBLIC_PATHS} paths"
            )));
        }
        let mut seen = BTreeSet::new();
        let mut root = SelectionNode::default();
        for pointer in &self.public_state.paths {
            if !seen.insert(pointer.as_str()) {
                return Err(invalid_policy(format!("duplicate path {pointer:?}")));
            }
            let components = decode_pointer(pointer)?;
            validate_schema_path(&self.fields, &components, pointer)?;
            insert_selection(&mut root, &components, pointer)?;
        }
        Ok(root)
    }
}

fn invalid_policy(message: impl Into<String>) -> PublicStateProjectionError {
    PublicStateProjectionError::InvalidPolicy(message.into())
}

fn invalid_state(message: impl Into<String>) -> PublicStateProjectionError {
    PublicStateProjectionError::InvalidState(message.into())
}

fn decode_pointer(pointer: &str) -> Result<Vec<String>, PublicStateProjectionError> {
    if pointer.is_empty() {
        return Err(invalid_policy("the document root cannot be public"));
    }
    if !pointer.starts_with('/') {
        return Err(invalid_policy(format!(
            "path {pointer:?} is not an RFC 6901 pointer"
        )));
    }
    let components = pointer[1..]
        .split('/')
        .map(|component| decode_pointer_component(component, pointer))
        .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;
    if components.len() > MAX_PUBLIC_PATH_DEPTH {
        return Err(invalid_policy(format!(
            "path {pointer:?} exceeds depth {MAX_PUBLIC_PATH_DEPTH}"
        )));
    }
    Ok(components)
}

fn decode_pointer_component(
    component: &str,
    pointer: &str,
) -> Result<String, PublicStateProjectionError> {
    let mut output = String::with_capacity(component.len());
    let mut chars = component.chars();
    while let Some(character) = chars.next() {
        if character != '~' {
            output.push(character);
            continue;
        }
        match chars.next() {
            Some('0') => output.push('~'),
            Some('1') => output.push('/'),
            _ => {
                return Err(invalid_policy(format!(
                    "path {pointer:?} contains invalid RFC 6901 escaping"
                )))
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(output)
}

fn validate_schema_path(
    root_fields: &HashMap<String, FieldSchema>,
    components: &[String],
    pointer: &str,
) -> Result<(), PublicStateProjectionError> {
    let Some((field_name, remaining)) = components.split_first() else {
        return Err(invalid_policy("the document root cannot be public"));
    };
    let field = root_fields.get(field_name).ok_or_else(|| {
        invalid_policy(format!(
            "path {pointer:?} names undeclared field {field_name:?}"
        ))
    })?;
    validate_type_path(&field.field_type, remaining, pointer)
}

fn validate_type_path(
    field_type: &FieldType,
    remaining: &[String],
    pointer: &str,
) -> Result<(), PublicStateProjectionError> {
    let Some((component, tail)) = remaining.split_first() else {
        return if is_closed_public_type(field_type) {
            Ok(())
        } else {
            Err(invalid_policy(format!(
                "path {pointer:?} terminates at an opaque type"
            )))
        };
    };
    match field_type {
        FieldType::Object(fields) => {
            let field = fields.get(component).ok_or_else(|| {
                invalid_policy(format!(
                    "path {pointer:?} names undeclared field {component:?}"
                ))
            })?;
            validate_type_path(&field.field_type, tail, pointer)
        }
        FieldType::Map(item_type) if component != "*" => {
            validate_type_path(item_type, tail, pointer)
        }
        FieldType::Map(_) => Err(invalid_policy(format!(
            "path {pointer:?} must name an explicit map key; wildcards disclose keys"
        ))),
        FieldType::Array(item_type) if component == "*" => {
            validate_type_path(item_type, tail, pointer)
        }
        FieldType::Array(_) => Err(invalid_policy(format!(
            "path {pointer:?} must use '*' for array items"
        ))),
        _ => Err(invalid_policy(format!(
            "path {pointer:?} traverses through a non-container field"
        ))),
    }
}

fn is_closed_public_type(field_type: &FieldType) -> bool {
    match field_type {
        FieldType::Any | FieldType::Map(_) | FieldType::JsonSchema(_) => false,
        FieldType::Array(item) => is_closed_public_type(item),
        FieldType::Object(fields) => fields
            .values()
            .all(|field| is_closed_public_type(&field.field_type)),
        FieldType::OneOf(branches) => {
            !branches.is_empty() && branches.iter().all(is_closed_public_type)
        }
        FieldType::String
        | FieldType::Integer
        | FieldType::Float
        | FieldType::Boolean
        | FieldType::Enum(_) => true,
    }
}

fn insert_selection(
    root: &mut SelectionNode,
    components: &[String],
    pointer: &str,
) -> Result<(), PublicStateProjectionError> {
    let mut current = root;
    for component in components {
        if current.terminal {
            return Err(invalid_policy(format!(
                "path {pointer:?} is already covered by an ancestor"
            )));
        }
        current = current.children.entry(component.clone()).or_default();
    }
    if current.terminal || !current.children.is_empty() {
        return Err(invalid_policy(format!(
            "path {pointer:?} overlaps another public path"
        )));
    }
    current.terminal = true;
    Ok(())
}

fn project_selected_object(
    source: &simd_json::value::owned::Object,
    fields: &HashMap<String, FieldSchema>,
    selection: &SelectionNode,
    parent: &str,
) -> Result<simd_json::value::owned::Object, PublicStateProjectionError> {
    let mut output = simd_json::value::owned::Object::new();
    for (name, selected) in &selection.children {
        let schema = fields.get(name).ok_or_else(|| {
            invalid_policy(format!("selection contains undeclared field {name:?}"))
        })?;
        let Some(value) = source.get(name) else {
            continue;
        };
        if !schema.required && value.is_null() {
            continue;
        }
        let path = format!("{parent}/{}", encode_pointer_component(name));
        let projected = project_selected_value(value, &schema.field_type, selected, &path)?;
        output.insert(name.clone(), projected);
    }
    Ok(output)
}

fn project_selected_value(
    value: &Value,
    field_type: &FieldType,
    selection: &SelectionNode,
    path: &str,
) -> Result<Value, PublicStateProjectionError> {
    if selection.terminal {
        return project_closed_value(value, field_type, path);
    }
    match field_type {
        FieldType::Object(fields) => {
            let source = value
                .as_object()
                .ok_or_else(|| invalid_state(format!("field {path:?} must be an object")))?;
            Ok(Value::Object(Box::new(project_selected_object(
                source, fields, selection, path,
            )?)))
        }
        FieldType::Map(item_type) => {
            let source = value
                .as_object()
                .ok_or_else(|| invalid_state(format!("field {path:?} must be an object map")))?;
            let mut output = simd_json::value::owned::Object::new();
            // Iterate the sealed allowlist, never the private runtime keys.
            for (key, selected) in &selection.children {
                if key == "*" {
                    return Err(invalid_policy("map wildcards are not public"));
                }
                let Some(value) = source.get(key) else {
                    continue;
                };
                let child_path = format!("{path}/{}", encode_pointer_component(key));
                output.insert(
                    key.clone(),
                    project_selected_value(value, item_type, selected, &child_path)?,
                );
            }
            Ok(Value::Object(Box::new(output)))
        }
        FieldType::Array(item_type) => {
            if selection.children.len() != 1 || !selection.children.contains_key("*") {
                return Err(invalid_policy(format!(
                    "path {path:?} has an invalid array selection"
                )));
            }
            let item_selection = &selection.children["*"];
            let items = value
                .as_array()
                .ok_or_else(|| invalid_state(format!("field {path:?} must be an array")))?;
            items
                .iter()
                .enumerate()
                .map(|(index, item)| {
                    project_selected_value(
                        item,
                        item_type,
                        item_selection,
                        &format!("{path}/{index}"),
                    )
                })
                .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()
                .map(Value::Array)
        }
        _ => Err(invalid_policy(format!(
            "path {path:?} traverses through a non-container field"
        ))),
    }
}

fn project_closed_value(
    value: &Value,
    field_type: &FieldType,
    path: &str,
) -> Result<Value, PublicStateProjectionError> {
    if !value_matches_type(value, field_type) {
        return Err(invalid_state(format!(
            "field {path:?} has an unexpected type"
        )));
    }
    match field_type {
        FieldType::String
        | FieldType::Integer
        | FieldType::Float
        | FieldType::Boolean
        | FieldType::Enum(_) => Ok(value.clone()),
        FieldType::Array(item_type) => value
            .as_array()
            .expect("type checked")
            .iter()
            .enumerate()
            .map(|(index, item)| project_closed_value(item, item_type, &format!("{path}/{index}")))
            .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()
            .map(Value::Array),
        FieldType::Object(fields) => {
            let source = value.as_object().expect("type checked");
            let mut output = simd_json::value::owned::Object::new();
            for (name, field) in fields {
                if let Some(child) = source.get(name) {
                    if !field.required && child.is_null() {
                        continue;
                    }
                    let child_path = format!("{path}/{}", encode_pointer_component(name));
                    output.insert(
                        name.clone(),
                        project_closed_value(child, &field.field_type, &child_path)?,
                    );
                }
            }
            Ok(Value::Object(Box::new(output)))
        }
        FieldType::OneOf(branches) => {
            let branch = branches
                .iter()
                .find(|branch| value_matches_type(value, branch))
                .expect("type checked");
            project_closed_value(value, branch, path)
        }
        FieldType::Any | FieldType::Map(_) | FieldType::JsonSchema(_) => Err(invalid_policy(
            format!("path {path:?} selects an opaque value"),
        )),
    }
}

fn value_matches_type(value: &Value, field_type: &FieldType) -> bool {
    match field_type {
        FieldType::String => value.is_str(),
        FieldType::Integer => value.is_i64() || value.is_u64(),
        FieldType::Float => value.is_f64() || value.is_i64() || value.is_u64(),
        FieldType::Boolean => value.is_bool(),
        FieldType::Array(item_type) => value
            .as_array()
            .is_some_and(|items| items.iter().all(|item| value_matches_type(item, item_type))),
        FieldType::Map(item_type) => value.as_object().is_some_and(|object| {
            object
                .values()
                .all(|item| value_matches_type(item, item_type))
        }),
        FieldType::Object(fields) => value.as_object().is_some_and(|object| {
            fields.iter().all(|(name, field)| {
                object
                    .get(name)
                    .map(|value| {
                        (!field.required && value.is_null())
                            || value_matches_type(value, &field.field_type)
                    })
                    .unwrap_or(!field.required)
            })
        }),
        FieldType::Enum(values) => value
            .as_str()
            .is_some_and(|value| values.iter().any(|candidate| candidate == value)),
        FieldType::OneOf(branches) => branches
            .iter()
            .any(|branch| value_matches_type(value, branch)),
        FieldType::JsonSchema(_) => false,
        FieldType::Any => true,
    }
}

fn encode_pointer_component(component: &str) -> String {
    component.replace('~', "~0").replace('/', "~1")
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::plugin_schema::{Constraint, FieldSchema};
    use simd_json::json;

    fn field(field_type: FieldType, required: bool) -> FieldSchema {
        FieldSchema {
            field_type,
            required,
            description: String::new(),
            default: None,
            example: None,
            constraints: Vec::<Constraint>::new(),
            read_only: false,
            read_only_when: None,
        }
    }

    fn schema(fields: HashMap<String, FieldSchema>, paths: &[&str]) -> PluginSchema {
        let mut builder = PluginSchema::builder("fixture");
        for (name, field) in fields {
            builder = builder.field(&name, field);
        }
        builder.public_state_paths(paths).build()
    }

    #[test]
    fn absent_policy_exposes_no_state() {
        let schema = PluginSchema::builder("fixture")
            .string_field("status", false, "")
            .build();
        assert_eq!(
            schema
                .project_public_state(&json!({"status":"ok","secret":"no"}))
                .unwrap(),
            None
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn typed_parent_drops_unknown_nested_and_top_level_fields() {
        let nested = HashMap::from([
            ("enabled".into(), field(FieldType::Boolean, false)),
            ("label".into(), field(FieldType::String, false)),
        ]);
        let schema = schema(
            HashMap::from([
                ("config".into(), field(FieldType::Object(nested), false)),
                ("private".into(), field(FieldType::String, false)),
            ]),
            &["/config"],
        );
        let projected = schema
            .project_public_state(&json!({
                "config":{"enabled":true,"label":"public","token":"hidden"},
                "private":"hidden",
                "unknown":{"credential":"hidden"}
            }))
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            projected,
            Some(json!({"config":{"enabled":true,"label":"public"}}))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn nested_path_selects_only_that_declared_child() {
        let nested = HashMap::from([
            ("status".into(), field(FieldType::String, false)),
            ("details".into(), field(FieldType::Any, false)),
        ]);
        let schema = schema(
            HashMap::from([("provider".into(), field(FieldType::Object(nested), false))]),
            &["/provider/status"],
        );
        assert_eq!(
            schema
                .project_public_state(&json!({
                    "provider":{"status":"ready","details":{"token":"hidden"}}
                }))
                .unwrap(),
            Some(json!({"provider":{"status":"ready"}}))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn opaque_terminal_and_overlapping_rules_are_rejected() {
        let opaque = schema(
            HashMap::from([("config".into(), field(FieldType::Any, false))]),
            &["/config"],
        );
        assert!(matches!(
            opaque.validate_public_state_policy(),
            Err(PublicStateProjectionError::InvalidPolicy(_))
        ));

        let nested = HashMap::from([("status".into(), field(FieldType::String, false))]);
        let overlapping = schema(
            HashMap::from([("provider".into(), field(FieldType::Object(nested), false))]),
            &["/provider/status", "/provider"],
        );
        assert!(matches!(
            overlapping.validate_public_state_policy(),
            Err(PublicStateProjectionError::InvalidPolicy(_))
        ));
    }

    #[test]
    fn runtime_type_drift_fails_closed_without_echoing_value() {
        let schema = schema(
            HashMap::from([("status".into(), field(FieldType::String, false))]),
            &["/status"],
        );
        let error = schema
            .project_public_state(&json!({"status":{"token":"must-not-appear"}}))
            .unwrap_err();
        assert!(matches!(error, PublicStateProjectionError::InvalidState(_)));
        assert!(!error.to_string().contains("must-not-appear"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn configured_but_absent_fields_produce_empty_public_object() {
        let schema = schema(
            HashMap::from([("status".into(), field(FieldType::String, false))]),
            &["/status"],
        );
        assert_eq!(
            schema.project_public_state(&json!({})).unwrap(),
            Some(json!({}))
        );
        assert!(schema.public_state_exposes_top_level("status").unwrap());
        assert!(!schema.public_state_exposes_top_level("private").unwrap());
    }

    #[test]
    fn optional_null_is_withheld_instead_of_causing_or_widening_projection() {
        let schema = schema(
            HashMap::from([("status".into(), field(FieldType::String, false))]),
            &["/status"],
        );
        assert_eq!(
            schema
                .project_public_state(&json!({"status":null,"other":"hidden"}))
                .unwrap(),
            Some(json!({}))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn typed_arrays_filter_unknown_object_members() {
        let item = FieldType::Object(HashMap::from([(
            "name".into(),
            field(FieldType::String, true),
        )]));
        let schema = schema(
            HashMap::from([(
                "items".into(),
                field(FieldType::Array(Box::new(item)), false),
            )]),
            &["/items"],
        );
        assert_eq!(
            schema
                .project_public_state(&json!({
                    "items":[{"name":"one","credential":"hidden"}]
                }))
                .unwrap(),
            Some(json!({"items":[{"name":"one"}]}))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn array_item_rules_preserve_order_length_and_drop_unselected_fields() {
        let item = FieldType::Object(HashMap::from([
            ("name".into(), field(FieldType::String, false)),
            ("status".into(), field(FieldType::String, false)),
            ("details".into(), field(FieldType::Any, false)),
        ]));
        let schema = schema(
            HashMap::from([(
                "items".into(),
                field(FieldType::Array(Box::new(item)), false),
            )]),
            &["/items/*/name", "/items/*/status"],
        );
        assert_eq!(
            schema
                .project_public_state(&json!({
                    "items":[
                        {"name":"one","status":"up","details":{"token":"hidden"},"unknown":"hidden"},
                        {"name":"two","details":{"password":"hidden"}}
                    ]
                }))
                .unwrap(),
            Some(json!({
                "items":[
                    {"name":"one","status":"up"},
                    {"name":"two"}
                ]
            }))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn nested_arrays_project_only_selected_typed_leaves() {
        let child = FieldType::Object(HashMap::from([
            ("id".into(), field(FieldType::String, false)),
            ("opaque".into(), field(FieldType::Any, false)),
        ]));
        let parent = FieldType::Object(HashMap::from([(
            "children".into(),
            field(FieldType::Array(Box::new(child)), false),
        )]));
        let schema = schema(
            HashMap::from([(
                "parents".into(),
                field(FieldType::Array(Box::new(parent)), false),
            )]),
            &["/parents/*/children/*/id"],
        );
        assert_eq!(
            schema
                .project_public_state(&json!({
                    "parents":[{"children":[{"id":"c1","opaque":{"secret":"hidden"}}]}]
                }))
                .unwrap(),
            Some(json!({"parents":[{"children":[{"id":"c1"}]}]}))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn array_rule_rejects_indexes_and_type_drift_before_returning_a_view() {
        let item = FieldType::Object(HashMap::from([(
            "name".into(),
            field(FieldType::String, false),
        )]));
        let indexed = schema(
            HashMap::from([(
                "items".into(),
                field(FieldType::Array(Box::new(item.clone())), false),
            )]),
            &["/items/0/name"],
        );
        assert!(matches!(
            indexed.validate_public_state_policy(),
            Err(PublicStateProjectionError::InvalidPolicy(_))
        ));

        let selected = schema(
            HashMap::from([(
                "items".into(),
                field(FieldType::Array(Box::new(item)), false),
            )]),
            &["/items/*/name"],
        );
        let error = selected
            .project_public_state(&json!({
                "items":[{"name":"ok"},{"name":{"secret":"must-not-appear"}}]
            }))
            .unwrap_err();
        assert!(matches!(error, PublicStateProjectionError::InvalidState(_)));
        assert!(!error.to_string().contains("must-not-appear"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn star_is_a_literal_name_when_traversing_an_object() {
        let schema = schema(
            HashMap::from([("*".into(), field(FieldType::String, false))]),
            &["/*"],
        );
        assert_eq!(
            schema
                .project_public_state(&json!({"*":"visible","other":"hidden"}))
                .unwrap(),
            Some(json!({"*":"visible"}))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn rfc6901_escaped_field_names_are_supported() {
        let schema = schema(
            HashMap::from([("a/b~c".into(), field(FieldType::String, false))]),
            &["/a~1b~0c"],
        );
        assert_eq!(
            schema
                .project_public_state(&json!({"a/b~c":"visible"}))
                .unwrap(),
            Some(json!({"a/b~c":"visible"}))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn policy_is_plugin_schema_owned_and_roundtrips_canonically() {
        let withheld = PluginSchema::builder("withheld")
            .string_field("status", false, "")
            .build();
        let withheld_json = serde_json::to_value(&withheld).unwrap();
        assert!(withheld_json.get("public_state").is_none());
        let withheld_roundtrip: PluginSchema = serde_json::from_value(withheld_json).unwrap();
        assert!(withheld_roundtrip.public_state.is_empty());

        let exposed = PluginSchema::builder("exposed")
            .string_field("status", false, "")
            .string_field("alpha", false, "")
            .public_state_paths(&["/status", "/alpha"])
            .build();
        let first = serde_json::to_vec(&exposed).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            serde_json::from_slice::<serde_json::Value>(&first).unwrap()["public_state"]["paths"],
            serde_json::json!(["/alpha", "/status"])
        );
        let roundtrip: PluginSchema = serde_json::from_slice(&first).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            roundtrip.public_state,
            PublicStatePolicy {
                paths: vec!["/alpha".into(), "/status".into()]
            }
        );
        assert_eq!(
            serde_json::to_vec(&exposed.public_state).unwrap(),
            br#"{"paths":["/alpha","/status"]}"#
        );
        assert_eq!(
            serde_json::to_value(&exposed).unwrap(),
            serde_json::to_value(&roundtrip).unwrap()
        );
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod typed_map_privacy_tests {
    use super::*;
    use simd_json::json;
    fn field(field_type: FieldType) -> FieldSchema {
        FieldSchema {
            field_type,
            required: false,
            description: String::new(),
            default: None,
            example: None,
            constraints: vec![],
            read_only: false,
            read_only_when: None,
        }
    }
    fn schema(paths: &[&str]) -> PluginSchema {
        let item = FieldType::Object(HashMap::from([
            ("status".into(), field(FieldType::String)),
            ("secret".into(), field(FieldType::Any)),
            (
                "children".into(),
                field(FieldType::Map(Box::new(FieldType::Object(HashMap::from(
                    [
                        ("ready".into(), field(FieldType::Boolean)),
                        ("private".into(), field(FieldType::Any)),
                    ],
                ))))),
            ),
        ]));
        PluginSchema::builder("fixture")
            .field("jobs", field(FieldType::Map(Box::new(item))))
            .public_state_paths(paths)
            .build()
    }
    #[test]
    fn explicit_key_and_grandchild_projection_never_enumerates_private_keys() {
        let schema = schema(&["/jobs/public/status", "/jobs/public/children/a~1b~0c/ready"]);
        let state = json!({"jobs":{
            "public":{"status":"ok","secret":"HIDDEN","children":{"a/b~c":{"ready":false,"private":"HIDDEN"},"PRIVATE_CHILD":{"private":"HIDDEN"}}},
            "PRIVATE_JOB":false
        }});
        assert_eq!(
            schema.project_public_state(&state).unwrap(),
            Some(json!({"jobs":{"public":{"status":"ok","children":{"a/b~c":{"ready":false}}}}}))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            schema
                .project_public_state(&json!({"jobs":{"PRIVATE_JOB":false}}))
                .unwrap(),
            Some(json!({"jobs":{}}))
        );
        assert!(schema
            .project_public_state(&json!({"jobs":{"public":{"status":false}}}))
            .is_err());
    }
    #[test]
    fn whole_maps_wildcards_and_opaque_values_are_not_public() {
        for paths in [
            vec!["/jobs"],
            vec!["/jobs/*/status"],
            vec!["/jobs/public"],
            vec!["/jobs/public/secret"],
            vec!["/jobs/public/children/*/ready"],
        ] {
            assert!(schema(&paths).validate_public_state_policy().is_err());
        }
        // Even a closed scalar map cannot disclose all keys by selecting its parent.
        let scalar = PluginSchema::builder("fixture")
            .field("labels", field(FieldType::Map(Box::new(FieldType::String))))
            .public_state_path("/labels")
            .build();
        assert!(scalar.validate_public_state_policy().is_err());
    }
}

<file path="op-state-store/src/schema_projection.rs">
//! Schema-described projection of a method's arguments (OD-64).
//!
//! The sealed plugin schema is the noise filter for retrieval: only the
//! fields a method's `args` schema *describes* are worth embedding, rendered
//! with the description the schema author wrote; fields marked `x-secret`
//! are dropped with their whole subtree; anything the schema does not
//! declare (hashes, transport metadata, stray keys) is left out. The chain
//! block stays lossless — this is the retrieval view of it, not a replacement.

use serde_json::Value;

/// One argument field the schema describes, with the value it carried.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct DescribedField {
    /// Dotted path from the args root, arrays as `[i]`.
    pub path: String,
    /// `description` from the schema (or `title`), empty when absent.
    pub description: String,
    /// `x-oscal-subid` when declared.
    pub subid: Option<String>,
    /// Scalar rendering of the value (bounded by the caller).
    pub value: String,
}

const MAX_DEPTH: usize = 32;
const MAX_FIELDS: usize = 256;

/// Walk `value` under `schema`, emitting described scalar leaves.
pub fn described_fields(schema: &Value, value: &Value) -> Vec<DescribedField> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    walk(schema, schema, value, "", &mut out, 0);
    out
}

fn is_secret(schema: &Value) -> bool {
    schema.get("x-secret").and_then(Value::as_bool) == Some(true)
}

fn resolve<'a>(root: &'a Value, schema: &'a Value) -> &'a Value {
    if let Some(reference) = schema.get("$ref").and_then(Value::as_str) {
        if let Some(pointer) = reference.strip_prefix('#') {
            if let Some(target) = root.pointer(pointer) {
                return target;
            }
        }
    }
    schema
}

/// Merge `allOf` branches' properties view: the first branch that declares
/// the property wins; combinators are searched for property declarations.
fn property_schema<'a>(root: &'a Value, schema: &'a Value, key: &str) -> Option<&'a Value> {
    let schema = resolve(root, schema);
    if let Some(found) = schema.get("properties").and_then(|p| p.get(key)) {
        return Some(found);
    }
    for combinator in ["allOf", "anyOf", "oneOf"] {
        if let Some(branches) = schema.get(combinator).and_then(Value::as_array) {
            for branch in branches {
                if let Some(found) = property_schema(root, branch, key) {
                    return Some(found);
                }
            }
        }
    }
    None
}

fn description_of(root: &Value, schema: &Value) -> (String, Option<String>) {
    let schema = resolve(root, schema);
    let description = schema
        .get("description")
        .or_else(|| schema.get("title"))
        .and_then(Value::as_str)
        .unwrap_or_default()
        .to_string();
    let subid = schema
        .get("x-oscal-subid")
        .and_then(Value::as_str)
        .map(str::to_string);
    (description, subid)
}

fn scalar_text(value: &Value) -> Option<String> {
    match value {
        Value::Null => None,
        Value::Bool(b) => Some(b.to_string()),
        Value::Number(n) => Some(n.to_string()),
        Value::String(s) => Some(s.clone()),
        _ => None,
    }
}

fn walk(
    root: &Value,
    schema: &Value,
    value: &Value,
    path: &str,
    out: &mut Vec<DescribedField>,
    depth: usize,
) {
    if depth > MAX_DEPTH || out.len() >= MAX_FIELDS {
        return;
    }
    let schema = resolve(root, schema);
    if is_secret(schema) {
        return;
    }
    match value {
        Value::Object(map) => {
            for (key, child) in map {
                // Undeclared keys are noise: not described, not embedded.
                let Some(child_schema) = property_schema(root, schema, key) else {
                    continue;
                };
                let child_path = if path.is_empty() {
                    key.clone()
                } else {
                    format!("{path}.{key}")
                };
                walk(root, child_schema, child, &child_path, out, depth + 1);
            }
        }
        Value::Array(items) => {
            let Some(item_schema) = schema.get("items") else {
                return;
            };
            for (index, item) in items.iter().enumerate() {
                walk(
                    root,
                    item_schema,
                    item,
                    &format!("{path}[{index}]"),
                    out,
                    depth + 1,
                );
            }
        }
        scalar => {
            if let Some(text) = scalar_text(scalar) {
                let (description, subid) = description_of(root, schema);
                out.push(DescribedField {
                    path: path.to_string(),
                    description,
                    subid,
                    value: text,
                });
            }
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use serde_json::json;

    #[test]
    fn only_described_non_secret_fields_survive_with_their_descriptions() {
        let schema = json!({
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "message": {"type": "string", "description": "What the user asked", "x-oscal-subid": "obs.x.message@v1"},
                "api_key": {"type": "string", "x-secret": true, "description": "never"},
                "route": {"$ref": "#/$defs/Route"},
                "tags": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string", "description": "A tag"}},
                "nested": {"allOf": [{"properties": {"depth": {"type": "integer", "title": "Depth"}}}]}
            },
            "$defs": {
                "Route": {"type": "object", "properties": {
                    "provider": {"type": "string", "description": "Upstream provider"},
                    "token": {"type": "string", "x-secret": true}
                }}
            }
        });
        let value = json!({
            "message": "hello",
            "api_key": "sk-live-123",
            "route": {"provider": "anthropic", "token": "t0k"},
            "tags": ["a", "b"],
            "nested": {"depth": 3},
            "event_hash": "deadbeef",
            "extra": {"stray": true}
        });
        let fields = described_fields(&schema, &value);
        let rendered: Vec<String> = fields
            .iter()
            .map(|f| format!("{}={} ({})", f.path, f.value, f.description))
            .collect();
        assert_eq!(
            rendered,
            // Sorted key order: deterministic on origin and replica alike.
            vec![
                "message=hello (What the user asked)",
                "nested.depth=3 (Depth)",
                "route.provider=anthropic (Upstream provider)",
                "tags[0]=a (A tag)",
                "tags[1]=b (A tag)",
            ]
        );
        assert_eq!(fields[0].subid.as_deref(), Some("obs.x.message@v1"));
        let joined = rendered.join("\n");
        assert!(!joined.contains("sk-live"));
        assert!(!joined.contains("t0k"));
        assert!(!joined.contains("deadbeef"));
        assert!(!joined.contains("stray"));
    }
}
</file>

<file path="op-state-store/src/schema_validator.rs">
//! Schema Validation Module
//!
//! Provides validation of:
//! - Generated schemas against JSON Schema meta-schemas
//! - Instance data against plugin schemas
//! - Expansion of propertyDependencies to if/then for broader compatibility

use crate::plugin_schema::{PluginSchema, SchemaCatalog, DEFAULT_SCHEMA_DIALECT};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use simd_json::prelude::*;
use simd_json::{json, OwnedValue as Value};
use std::collections::HashMap;

/// Validation report with detailed error information
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ValidationReport {
    /// Whether validation passed
    pub valid: bool,
    /// List of validation errors
    pub errors: Vec<ValidationError>,
    /// List of validation warnings (non-fatal)
    pub warnings: Vec<String>,
    /// Schema dialect used
    pub dialect: String,
    /// Hash of the validated content (for audit trail)
    pub content_hash: Option<String>,
}

impl ValidationReport {
    /// Create a successful validation report
    pub fn success(dialect: &str) -> Self {
        Self {
            valid: true,
            errors: Vec::new(),
            warnings: Vec::new(),
            dialect: dialect.to_string(),
            content_hash: None,
        }
    }

    /// Create a failed validation report with errors
    pub fn failure(dialect: &str, errors: Vec<ValidationError>) -> Self {
        Self {
            valid: false,
            errors,
            warnings: Vec::new(),
            dialect: dialect.to_string(),
            content_hash: None,
        }
    }

    /// Add a content hash for audit trail
    pub fn with_content_hash(mut self, hash: String) -> Self {
        self.content_hash = Some(hash);
        self
    }
}

/// A single validation error
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ValidationError {
    /// JSON Pointer path to the error location
    pub path: String,
    /// Error message
    pub message: String,
    /// The keyword that caused the error (e.g., "type", "required")
    pub keyword: Option<String>,
    /// The schema path where the error originated
    pub schema_path: Option<String>,
}

impl ValidationError {
    pub fn new(path: &str, message: &str) -> Self {
        Self {
            path: path.to_string(),
            message: message.to_string(),
            keyword: None,
            schema_path: None,
        }
    }

    pub fn with_keyword(mut self, keyword: &str) -> Self {
        self.keyword = Some(keyword.to_string());
        self
    }
}

/// Schema validator that uses the jsonschema crate
pub struct SchemaValidator {
    /// Cached compiled validators
    validators: HashMap<String, jsonschema::Validator>,
}

impl SchemaValidator {
    /// Create a new schema validator
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            validators: HashMap::new(),
        }
    }

    /// Validate a generated schema against the meta-schema
    pub fn validate_schema_against_meta(
        &mut self,
        schema: &Value,
        schema_catalog: &SchemaCatalog,
    ) -> Result<ValidationReport, ValidatorError> {
        let dialect = schema
            .get("$schema")
            .and_then(|s| s.as_str())
            .unwrap_or(DEFAULT_SCHEMA_DIALECT);

        // Get or load the meta-schema
        let meta_schema = schema_catalog
            .get_meta_schema(dialect)
            .ok_or_else(|| ValidatorError::MetaSchemaNotLoaded(dialect.to_string()))?;

        // Compile the meta-schema validator if not cached
        let validator = self.get_or_compile_validator(dialect, meta_schema)?;

        // Convert simd_json::Value to serde_json::Value for jsonschema
        let serde_schema: serde_json::Value = serde_json::to_value(schema)
            .map_err(|e| ValidatorError::CompilationError(e.to_string()))?;

        // Validate
        match validator.validate(&serde_schema) {
            Ok(_) => Ok(ValidationReport::success(dialect)),
            Err(error) => {
                // Single error returned, but we can get all errors via iter_errors
                let validation_errors: Vec<ValidationError> = validator
                    .iter_errors(&serde_schema)
                    .map(|e| ValidationError::new(&e.instance_path.to_string(), &e.to_string()))
                    .collect();
                if validation_errors.is_empty() {
                    // Fallback if iter_errors returns empty but validate failed
                    Ok(ValidationReport::failure(
                        dialect,
                        vec![ValidationError::new("", &error.to_string())],
                    ))
                } else {
                    Ok(ValidationReport::failure(dialect, validation_errors))
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /// Validate instance data against a plugin schema
    pub fn validate_instance(
        &mut self,
        schema: &PluginSchema,
        instance: &Value,
    ) -> Result<ValidationReport, ValidatorError> {
        let json_schema = schema.to_json_schema();
        let dialect = &schema.dialect;

        // Convert to serde_json for jsonschema
        let serde_json_schema: serde_json::Value = serde_json::to_value(&json_schema)
            .map_err(|e| ValidatorError::CompilationError(e.to_string()))?;
        let serde_instance: serde_json::Value = serde_json::to_value(instance)
            .map_err(|e| ValidatorError::CompilationError(e.to_string()))?;

        // Compile the schema validator
        let validator = jsonschema::validator_for(&serde_json_schema)
            .map_err(|e| ValidatorError::CompilationError(e.to_string()))?;

        // Validate
        match validator.validate(&serde_instance) {
            Ok(_) => {
                let mut report = ValidationReport::success(dialect);
                // Add content hash for audit trail
                report.content_hash = Some(compute_content_hash(instance));
                Ok(report)
            }
            Err(error) => {
                // Get all errors via iter_errors
                let validation_errors: Vec<ValidationError> = validator
                    .iter_errors(&serde_instance)
                    .map(|e| ValidationError::new(&e.instance_path.to_string(), &e.to_string()))
                    .collect();
                if validation_errors.is_empty() {
                    Ok(ValidationReport::failure(
                        dialect,
                        vec![ValidationError::new("", &error.to_string())],
                    ))
                } else {
                    Ok(ValidationReport::failure(dialect, validation_errors))
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /// Expand propertyDependencies to if/then for validators that don't support it natively
    ///
    /// Transforms:
    /// ```json
    /// {
    ///   "propertyDependencies": {
    ///     "status": {
    ///       "locked": { "properties": { "id": { "readOnly": true } } }
    ///     }
    ///   }
    /// }
    /// ```
    ///
    /// To:
    /// ```json
    /// {
    ///   "allOf": [
    ///     {
    ///       "if": { "properties": { "status": { "const": "locked" } } },
    ///       "then": { "properties": { "id": { "readOnly": true } } }
    ///     }
    ///   ]
    /// }
    /// ```
    pub fn expand_property_dependencies(schema: &Value) -> Result<Value, ValidatorError> {
        let mut result = schema.clone();

        if let Some(obj) = result.as_object_mut() {
            if let Some(prop_deps) = obj.remove("propertyDependencies") {
                let mut all_of = obj
                    .get("allOf")
                    .and_then(|a| a.as_array())
                    .cloned()
                    .unwrap_or_default();

                if let Some(deps_obj) = prop_deps.as_object() {
                    for (prop_name, value_map) in deps_obj {
                        if let Some(values) = value_map.as_object() {
                            for (value, then_schema) in values {
                                let if_schema = json!({
                                    "properties": {
                                        prop_name: { "const": value }
                                    },
                                    "required": [prop_name]
                                });

                                all_of.push(json!({
                                    "if": if_schema,
                                    "then": then_schema
                                }));
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }

                if !all_of.is_empty() {
                    obj.insert("allOf".to_string(), json!(all_of));
                }
            }
        }

        // Recursively expand nested schemas
        if let Some(obj) = result.as_object_mut() {
            for (_key, value) in obj.iter_mut() {
                if value.is_object() {
                    *value = Self::expand_property_dependencies(value)?;
                } else if let Some(arr) = value.as_array_mut() {
                    for item in arr.iter_mut() {
                        if item.is_object() {
                            *item = Self::expand_property_dependencies(item)?;
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        Ok(result)
    }

    fn get_or_compile_validator(
        &mut self,
        key: &str,
        schema: &Value,
    ) -> Result<&jsonschema::Validator, ValidatorError> {
        if !self.validators.contains_key(key) {
            let serde_schema: serde_json::Value = serde_json::to_value(schema)
                .map_err(|e| ValidatorError::CompilationError(e.to_string()))?;
            let validator = jsonschema::validator_for(&serde_schema)
                .map_err(|e| ValidatorError::CompilationError(e.to_string()))?;
            self.validators.insert(key.to_string(), validator);
        }
        self.validators.get(key).ok_or_else(|| {
            ValidatorError::CompilationError(format!(
                "validator for {} not found after compilation",
                key
            ))
        })
    }
}

impl Default for SchemaValidator {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

/// Errors that can occur during validation
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum ValidatorError {
    MetaSchemaNotLoaded(String),
    CompilationError(String),
    InvalidSchema(String),
}

impl std::fmt::Display for ValidatorError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        match self {
            Self::MetaSchemaNotLoaded(d) => write!(f, "Meta-schema not loaded for dialect: {}", d),
            Self::CompilationError(e) => write!(f, "Schema compilation error: {}", e),
            Self::InvalidSchema(e) => write!(f, "Invalid schema: {}", e),
        }
    }
}

impl std::error::Error for ValidatorError {}

/// Compute a hash of the content for audit trail
fn compute_content_hash(value: &Value) -> String {
    // Canonicalize the JSON for consistent hashing
    let canonical = canonicalize_json(value);
    let canonical_str = simd_json::to_string(&canonical).unwrap_or_default();
    format!("{:x}", md5::compute(canonical_str.as_bytes()))
}

/// Canonicalize JSON for consistent hashing
/// - Sort object keys
/// - Normalize numbers
/// - Remove optional whitespace variance
pub fn canonicalize_json(value: &Value) -> Value {
    match value {
        Value::Object(map) => {
            // Sort keys for consistent ordering
            let mut sorted: Vec<_> = map.iter().collect();
            sorted.sort_by(|a, b| a.0.cmp(b.0));

            let canonical_map: simd_json::value::owned::Object = sorted
                .into_iter()
                .map(|(k, v)| (k.clone(), canonicalize_json(v)))
                .collect();

            Value::Object(Box::new(canonical_map))
        }
        Value::Array(arr) => Value::Array(arr.iter().map(canonicalize_json).collect()),
        Value::Static(s) => {
            if let Some(f) = s.as_f64() {
                if f.fract() == 0.0 && f.abs() < i64::MAX as f64 {
                    // It's an integer
                    json!(f as i64)
                } else {
                    json!(f)
                }
            } else {
                value.clone()
            }
        }
        _ => value.clone(),
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn test_canonicalize_json() {
        let input = json!({
            "z": 1,
            "a": 2,
            "m": [3, 2, 1]
        });

        let canonical = canonicalize_json(&input);
        let output = simd_json::to_string(&canonical).unwrap();

        // Keys should be sorted
        assert!(output.find("\"a\"").unwrap() < output.find("\"m\"").unwrap());
        assert!(output.find("\"m\"").unwrap() < output.find("\"z\"").unwrap());
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_expand_property_dependencies() {
        let schema = json!({
            "type": "object",
            "propertyDependencies": {
                "status": {
                    "locked": {
                        "properties": {
                            "id": { "readOnly": true }
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        });

        let expanded = SchemaValidator::expand_property_dependencies(&schema).unwrap();

        // Should have allOf with if/then
        assert!(expanded.get("allOf").is_some());
        assert!(expanded.get("propertyDependencies").is_none());

        let all_of = expanded.get("allOf").unwrap().as_array().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(all_of.len(), 1);

        let first = &all_of[0];
        assert!(first.get("if").is_some());
        assert!(first.get("then").is_some());
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_content_hash_consistency() {
        let value1 = json!({"b": 2, "a": 1});
        let value2 = json!({"a": 1, "b": 2});

        // Same content, different order should produce same hash
        let hash1 = compute_content_hash(&value1);
        let hash2 = compute_content_hash(&value2);

        assert_eq!(hash1, hash2);
    }
}
</file>

<file path="op-state-store/src/state_schema_shape.rs">
//! Bounded producer preflight for the finite FieldType representation.
//!
//! This is not a second schema. It rejects shapes the state adapters cannot
//! represent instead of silently converting typed dynamic keys into Object({}).
//! Method arguments/results keep their original JSON Schema and do not use it.
use serde_json::Value;

const MAX_DEPTH: usize = 64;
const MAX_EXPANDED_NODES: usize = 65_536;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, thiserror::Error)]
#[error("unsupported plugin state schema: {reason}")]
pub struct StateSchemaShapeError {
    pub reason: &'static str,
}

fn error(reason: &'static str) -> StateSchemaShapeError {
    StateSchemaShapeError { reason }
}

/// Normalize the one finite reference intersection emitted for internally
/// tagged struct variants: an open object reference plus one disjoint required
/// string-constant tag. This is a derived producer view; the authored JSON is
/// untouched. Arbitrary intersections and closed objects remain unsupported.
pub fn prepare_state_schema(root: &Value) -> Result<Value, StateSchemaShapeError> {
    crate::exact_schema::bound_json(root)
        .map_err(|_| error("state schema raw document exceeds bounds"))?;
    let mut prepared = root.clone();
    let mut count = 0;
    normalize_tagged_refs(root, &mut prepared, 0, &mut count)?;
    validate_state_schema(&prepared)?;
    Ok(prepared)
}

fn normalize_tagged_refs(
    root: &Value,
    node: &mut Value,
    depth: usize,
    count: &mut usize,
) -> Result<(), StateSchemaShapeError> {
    *count += 1;
    if depth > MAX_DEPTH || *count > MAX_EXPANDED_NODES {
        return Err(error("normalized state schema exceeds bounds"));
    }
    if node
        .get("x-opdbus-exact-json-schema")
        .and_then(Value::as_bool)
        == Some(true)
    {
        // Close exact fields over the ORIGINAL definitions before preparing
        // finite views. Shared definitions may be normalized elsewhere; their
        // derived representation is never substituted into an exact field.
        *node = crate::exact_schema::self_contained_field_schema(
            node,
            root.get("$defs")
                .or_else(|| root.get("definitions"))
                .and_then(Value::as_object),
        )
        .map_err(|_| error("explicit exact field schema is invalid or unsupported"))?;
        return Ok(());
    }
    if let Some(reference) = node.get("$ref").and_then(Value::as_str) {
        let has_intersection = node.as_object().is_some_and(|object| {
            object
                .keys()
                .any(|key| key != "$ref" && !annotation(key) && !key.starts_with("x-"))
        });
        if has_intersection {
            match merge_tagged_object(root, node, reference) {
                Ok(merged) => *node = merged,
                // Only the reachable finite graph is admitted below. An
                // unsupported intersection in a definition used exclusively
                // by an exact field retains its original semantics there.
                Err(_) => return Ok(()),
            }
        }
    }
    let Some(object) = node.as_object_mut() else {
        return Ok(());
    };
    for key in [
        "properties",
        "$defs",
        "definitions",
        "patternProperties",
        "dependentSchemas",
    ] {
        if let Some(fields) = object.get_mut(key).and_then(Value::as_object_mut) {
            for field in fields.values_mut() {
                normalize_tagged_refs(root, field, depth + 1, count)?;
            }
        }
    }
    for key in ["oneOf", "anyOf", "allOf", "prefixItems"] {
        if let Some(items) = object.get_mut(key).and_then(Value::as_array_mut) {
            for item in items {
                normalize_tagged_refs(root, item, depth + 1, count)?;
            }
        }
    }
    for key in [
        "items",
        "additionalProperties",
        "unevaluatedProperties",
        "contains",
        "not",
        "if",
        "then",
        "else",
        "propertyNames",
    ] {
        if let Some(child) = object.get_mut(key) {
            normalize_tagged_refs(root, child, depth + 1, count)?;
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn merge_tagged_object(
    root: &Value,
    extension: &Value,
    reference: &str,
) -> Result<Value, StateSchemaShapeError> {
    let invalid = || error("reference intersection is not a disjoint open-object string tag");
    let extension_object = extension.as_object().ok_or_else(invalid)?;
    if extension_object.keys().any(|key| {
        key != "$ref"
            && !annotation(key)
            && !key.starts_with("x-")
            && !matches!(key.as_str(), "type" | "properties" | "required")
    }) || extension.get("type").and_then(Value::as_str) != Some("object")
    {
        return Err(invalid());
    }
    let tags = extension
        .get("properties")
        .and_then(Value::as_object)
        .ok_or_else(invalid)?;
    if tags.len() != 1 {
        return Err(invalid());
    }
    let (tag, value) = tags.iter().next().ok_or_else(invalid)?;
    if extension.get("required") != Some(&Value::Array(vec![Value::String(tag.clone())]))
        || value.get("type").and_then(Value::as_str) != Some("string")
        || value.get("const").and_then(Value::as_str).is_none()
        || value.as_object().is_none_or(|object| {
            object.keys().any(|key| {
                !matches!(key.as_str(), "type" | "const")
                    && !annotation(key)
                    && !key.starts_with("x-")
            })
        })
    {
        return Err(invalid());
    }
    let tail = reference
        .strip_prefix("#/$defs/")
        .or_else(|| reference.strip_prefix("#/definitions/"))
        .ok_or_else(invalid)?;
    if tail.is_empty() || tail.contains('/') || tail.contains('%') {
        return Err(invalid());
    }
    let key = decode_component(tail)?;
    let target = root
        .get("$defs")
        .or_else(|| root.get("definitions"))
        .and_then(Value::as_object)
        .and_then(|defs| defs.get(&key))
        .ok_or_else(invalid)?;
    let target_object = target.as_object().ok_or_else(invalid)?;
    // Closed targets would reject the new tag in the original intersection.
    // Other constraints/recursive references need an explicit exact field.
    if target.get("type").and_then(Value::as_str) != Some("object")
        || target_object.keys().any(|key| {
            !matches!(key.as_str(), "type" | "properties" | "required")
                && !annotation(key)
                && !key.starts_with("x-")
        })
    {
        return Err(invalid());
    }
    let properties = target
        .get("properties")
        .and_then(Value::as_object)
        .ok_or_else(invalid)?;
    if properties.contains_key(tag) {
        return Err(invalid());
    }
    let mut required = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
    if let Some(names) = target.get("required") {
        for name in names.as_array().ok_or_else(invalid)? {
            required.insert(name.as_str().ok_or_else(invalid)?.to_owned());
        }
    }
    required.insert(tag.clone());
    let mut merged = target_object.clone();
    let mut fields = properties.clone();
    fields.insert(tag.clone(), value.clone());
    merged.insert("properties".into(), Value::Object(fields));
    merged.insert(
        "required".into(),
        Value::Array(required.into_iter().map(Value::String).collect()),
    );
    for (key, value) in extension_object {
        if annotation(key) || key.starts_with("x-") {
            merged.insert(key.clone(), value.clone());
        }
    }
    Ok(Value::Object(merged))
}

/// Check only the schema-bearing graph, never defaults/examples or live state.
/// Recursive schemas (including recursive definitions) are outside FieldType's
/// finite tree contract. Bounded expansion catches them before recursive adapters.
/// A map's keys cannot carry pattern/property-count constraints in Map(Box<_>),
/// and its immediate value has no FieldSchema metadata slot; reject such losses.
pub fn validate_state_schema(root: &Value) -> Result<(), StateSchemaShapeError> {
    // node, expansion depth, inside map, has FieldSchema metadata slot
    let mut pending = vec![(root, 0usize, false, true)];
    let mut visited = 0usize;
    while let Some((node, depth, in_map, field_slot)) = pending.pop() {
        visited += 1;
        if depth > MAX_DEPTH || visited > MAX_EXPANDED_NODES {
            return Err(error("recursive or excessively expanded state type"));
        }
        if node
            .get("x-opdbus-exact-json-schema")
            .and_then(Value::as_bool)
            == Some(true)
        {
            crate::exact_schema::self_contained_field_schema(
                node,
                root.get("$defs")
                    .or_else(|| root.get("definitions"))
                    .and_then(Value::as_object),
            )
            .map_err(|_| error("explicit exact field schema is invalid or unsupported"))?;
            continue;
        }
        if node == &Value::Bool(true) {
            continue;
        }
        if node == &Value::Bool(false) {
            return Err(error("false schema has no FieldType representation"));
        }
        let object = node
            .as_object()
            .ok_or_else(|| error("schema node is not an object or boolean"))?;
        if let Some(reference) = node.get("$ref") {
            let reference = reference
                .as_str()
                .ok_or_else(|| error("invalid local reference"))?;
            let tail = reference
                .strip_prefix("#/$defs/")
                .or_else(|| reference.strip_prefix("#/definitions/"))
                .ok_or_else(|| error("only local definition references are supported"))?;
            if tail.contains('/') || tail.contains('%') || tail.is_empty() {
                return Err(error("unsupported definition pointer"));
            }
            let key = decode_component(tail)?;
            let target = root
                .get("$defs")
                .or_else(|| root.get("definitions"))
                .and_then(Value::as_object)
                .and_then(|defs| defs.get(&key))
                .ok_or_else(|| error("unresolved local reference"))?;
            if object
                .keys()
                .any(|key| key != "$ref" && !annotation(key) && !key.starts_with("x-"))
            {
                return Err(error("reference siblings change the referenced type"));
            }
            pending.push((target, depth + 1, in_map, field_slot));
            continue;
        }
        // Numeric-key maps emit this even with additionalProperties:false.
        if object.contains_key("patternProperties") {
            return Err(error(
                "pattern-keyed objects require an explicit exact field schema",
            ));
        }
        if let Some(constant) = node.get("const") {
            if !constant.is_string() || node.get("type").and_then(Value::as_str) != Some("string") {
                return Err(error(
                    "non-string const requires an explicit exact field schema",
                ));
            }
            if node.get("enum").is_some_and(|values| {
                values
                    .as_array()
                    .is_none_or(|values| !values.contains(constant))
            }) {
                return Err(error(
                    "conflicting const and enum require an explicit exact field schema",
                ));
            }
        }
        let properties = node.get("properties").and_then(Value::as_object);
        let additional = node.get("additionalProperties");
        let dynamic = additional.is_some_and(|value| value != &Value::Bool(false));
        if dynamic && properties.is_some_and(|fields| !fields.is_empty()) {
            return Err(error(
                "mixed named properties and additionalProperties are not representable",
            ));
        }
        let is_map = dynamic && properties.is_none_or(|fields| fields.is_empty());
        if is_map
            && object.keys().any(|key| {
                matches!(
                    key.as_str(),
                    "propertyNames"
                        | "patternProperties"
                        | "minProperties"
                        | "maxProperties"
                        | "dependentRequired"
                        | "dependentSchemas"
                        | "unevaluatedProperties"
                )
            })
        {
            return Err(error(
                "map key or cardinality constraints are not representable",
            ));
        }
        if in_map {
            if node.get("type").is_some_and(|kind| kind == "null") && !field_slot {
                return Err(error(
                    "null map values or array items are not representable",
                ));
            }
            if node
                .get("enum")
                .and_then(Value::as_array)
                .is_some_and(|values| values.iter().any(|value| !value.is_string()))
            {
                return Err(error("non-string map enums are not representable"));
            }
            for key in object.keys() {
                if annotation(key) || key.starts_with("x-") {
                    continue;
                }
                if matches!(
                    key.as_str(),
                    "type"
                        | "properties"
                        | "required"
                        | "additionalProperties"
                        | "items"
                        | "enum"
                        | "const"
                        | "anyOf"
                        | "oneOf"
                ) {
                    continue;
                }
                if field_slot && matches!(key.as_str(), "minimum" | "maximum" | "pattern") {
                    continue;
                }
                return Err(error(
                    "constraint inside map has no faithful FieldType representation",
                ));
            }
            // Optional named fields can omit null. A map entry or array item has
            // no required/nullable bit; silently removing its null branch is wrong.
            if !field_slot
                && (node
                    .get("type")
                    .and_then(Value::as_array)
                    .is_some_and(|types| types.iter().any(|kind| kind == "null"))
                    || ["anyOf", "oneOf"].iter().any(|key| {
                        node.get(key)
                            .and_then(Value::as_array)
                            .is_some_and(|branches| {
                                branches.iter().any(|branch| {
                                    branch.get("type").is_some_and(|kind| kind == "null")
                                })
                            })
                    }))
            {
                return Err(error(
                    "nullable map values or array items are not representable",
                ));
            }
        }
        if let Some(properties) = properties {
            for value in properties.values() {
                pending.push((value, depth + 1, in_map, true));
            }
        }
        if let Some(value) = additional.filter(|_| dynamic) {
            pending.push((value, depth + 1, true, false));
        }
        if let Some(value) = node.get("items") {
            if value.is_array() {
                return Err(error("tuple array items are not representable"));
            }
            pending.push((value, depth + 1, in_map, false));
        }
        for key in ["anyOf", "oneOf"] {
            if let Some(branches) = node.get(key).and_then(Value::as_array) {
                for branch in branches {
                    // Optional named null branch is already handled by field.required.
                    if field_slot && branch.get("type").is_some_and(|kind| kind == "null") {
                        continue;
                    }
                    let concrete = branches
                        .iter()
                        .filter(|branch| !branch.get("type").is_some_and(|kind| kind == "null"))
                        .count();
                    pending.push((branch, depth + 1, in_map, field_slot && concrete == 1));
                }
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn annotation(key: &str) -> bool {
    matches!(
        key,
        "title"
            | "description"
            | "default"
            | "examples"
            | "example"
            | "readOnly"
            | "writeOnly"
            | "deprecated"
            | "$comment"
            | "$schema"
            | "$id"
            | "$defs"
            | "definitions"
    )
}

pub fn decode_component(component: &str) -> Result<String, StateSchemaShapeError> {
    let mut output = String::with_capacity(component.len());
    let mut chars = component.chars();
    while let Some(c) = chars.next() {
        if c != '~' {
            output.push(c);
            continue;
        }
        output.push(match chars.next() {
            Some('0') => '~',
            Some('1') => '/',
            _ => return Err(error("invalid definition pointer escape")),
        });
    }
    Ok(output)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use serde_json::json;

    #[test]
    fn tagged_object_normalization_retains_intersection_and_authored_source() {
        let original = json!({"type":"object","properties":{
            "device":{"$ref":"#/$defs/Base","type":"object","properties":{"type":{"type":"string","const":"nic"}},"required":["type"],"description":"native tagged device"}
        },"$defs":{"Base":{"type":"object","properties":{"parent":{"type":"string"}},"required":["parent"]}}});
        let preserved = original.clone();
        let prepared = prepare_state_schema(&original).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(original, preserved);
        assert!(prepared["properties"]["device"].get("$ref").is_none());
        assert_eq!(
            prepared["properties"]["device"]["properties"]["type"]["const"],
            "nic"
        );
        let before = jsonschema::validator_for(&original).unwrap();
        let after = jsonschema::validator_for(&prepared).unwrap();
        for value in [
            json!({"device":{"type":"nic","parent":"ovsbr0"}}),
            json!({"device":{"type":"nic","parent":"ovsbr0","arbitrary_open_key":5}}),
            json!({"device":{"type":"nic"}}),
            json!({"device":{"type":"disk","parent":"ovsbr0"}}),
            json!({"device":{"parent":"ovsbr0"}}),
        ] {
            assert_eq!(before.is_valid(&value), after.is_valid(&value));
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn tagged_normalization_rejects_closed_intersecting_or_extra_constraints() {
        let original = json!({"type":"object","properties":{
            "device":{"$ref":"#/$defs/Base","type":"object","properties":{"type":{"type":"string","const":"nic"}},"required":["type"]}
        },"$defs":{"Base":{"type":"object","properties":{"parent":{"type":"string"}}}}});
        let mut closed = original.clone();
        closed["$defs"]["Base"]["additionalProperties"] = json!(false);
        assert!(prepare_state_schema(&closed).is_err());
        let mut overlapping = original.clone();
        overlapping["$defs"]["Base"]["properties"]["type"] = json!({"type":"string"});
        assert!(prepare_state_schema(&overlapping).is_err());
        let mut constraint = original.clone();
        constraint["properties"]["device"]["maxProperties"] = json!(2);
        assert!(prepare_state_schema(&constraint).is_err());
        let mut numeric = original.clone();
        numeric["properties"]["device"]["properties"]["type"] = json!({"type":"integer","const":1});
        assert!(prepare_state_schema(&numeric).is_err());
        let scalar = json!({"type":"object","properties":{"value":{"$ref":"#/$defs/N","minimum":4}},"$defs":{"N":{"type":"integer"}}});
        assert!(prepare_state_schema(&scalar).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn finite_typed_maps_allow_nested_fields_but_not_lost_constraints() {
        let valid = json!({"type":"object","additionalProperties":{"type":"object","properties":{
            "revision":{"type":"integer","minimum":0},
            "nested":{"type":"object","additionalProperties":{"type":"boolean"}}
        },"required":["revision"]}});
        validate_state_schema(&valid).unwrap();
        for invalid in [
            json!({"type":"object","properties":{"tag":{"type":"string","const":"nic","enum":["disk"]}}}),
            json!({"type":"object","patternProperties":{"^\\d+$":{"type":"string"}},"additionalProperties":false}),
            json!({"type":"object","properties":{"fixed":{"type":"string"}},"additionalProperties":{"type":"boolean"}}),
            json!({"type":"object","additionalProperties":{"type":"integer","minimum":0}}),
            json!({"type":"object","additionalProperties":{"type":["string","null"]}}),
            json!({"type":"object","additionalProperties":{"type":"object","properties":{"x":{"type":"string","minLength":1}}}}),
            json!({"type":"object","additionalProperties":{"type":"string"},"propertyNames":{"pattern":"a"}}),
        ] {
            assert!(validate_state_schema(&invalid).is_err(), "{invalid}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn cycles_unresolved_and_reference_constraints_fail_before_expansion() {
        for invalid in [
            json!({"$ref":"#/$defs/Cycle","$defs":{"Cycle":{"$ref":"#/$defs/Cycle"}}}),
            json!({"type":"object","properties":{"x":{"$ref":"#/$defs/Cycle"}},"$defs":{"Cycle":{"type":"object","additionalProperties":{"$ref":"#/$defs/Cycle"}}}}),
            json!({"type":"object","properties":{"x":{"$ref":"#/$defs/Missing"}}}),
            json!({"$ref":"https://example.invalid/schema"}),
            json!({"$ref":"#/$defs/T","minimum":3,"$defs":{"T":{"type":"integer"}}}),
        ] {
            assert!(validate_state_schema(&invalid).is_err());
        }
    }
}

use crate::error::Result;
use crate::execution_job::ExecutionJob;
use crate::{CanonicalDbExport, StoredObject};
use async_trait::async_trait;
use uuid::Uuid;

/// Tool record from database
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ToolRecord {
    pub tool_name: String,
    pub definition_json: String, // Serialized ToolDefinition
    pub category: String,
    pub namespace: String,
    pub schema_version: String, // JSON Schema version
    pub source: String,         // "builtin", "dbus-session.v1", "dbus-system.v1", "mcp", "agent"
    pub created_at: String,
    pub updated_at: String,
}

#[async_trait]
pub trait StateStore: Send + Sync {
    async fn save_job(&self, job: &ExecutionJob) -> Result<()>;
    async fn get_job(&self, id: Uuid) -> Result<Option<ExecutionJob>>;
    async fn update_job(&self, job: &ExecutionJob) -> Result<()>;

    async fn get_object(&self, id: &str) -> Result<Option<StoredObject>>;
    async fn upsert_object(
        &self,
        id: &str,
        object_type: &str,
        namespace: &str,
        data: &simd_json::OwnedValue,
    ) -> Result<()>;
    async fn export_canonical(&self) -> Result<CanonicalDbExport>;

    // Tool persistence (READ on startup, WRITE only on onboarding/upgrade/migration)
    async fn save_tools(&self, tools: Vec<ToolRecord>) -> Result<()>;
    async fn load_tools(&self) -> Result<Vec<ToolRecord>>;
    async fn is_tools_empty(&self) -> Result<bool>;
    async fn clear_tools(&self) -> Result<()>;
}
</file>

<file path="op-tools/src/bin/op-packagekit-install.rs">
//! Install packages via PackageKit D-Bus (no CLI fallbacks).

use anyhow::{Context, Result};
use clap::Parser;
use futures::StreamExt;
use zbus::Connection;
use zbus::Proxy;

#[derive(Parser, Debug)]
#[command(name = "op-packagekit-install")]
#[command(about = "Install packages via PackageKit D-Bus using zbus")]
struct Args {
    /// Package names to install
    #[arg(required = true)]
    packages: Vec<String>,

    /// PackageKit resolve filters
    #[arg(long, default_value_t = 0)]
    resolve_filters: u64,

    /// PackageKit transaction flags
    #[arg(long, default_value_t = 0)]
    transaction_flags: u64,
}

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<()> {
    let args = Args::parse();
    let connection = Connection::system().await?;

    let package_ids = resolve_packages(&connection, args.resolve_filters, &args.packages)
        .await
        .context("Failed to resolve package IDs")?;

    if package_ids.is_empty() {
        anyhow::bail!(
            "No packages resolved for requested names: {:?}",
            args.packages
        );
    }

    install_packages(&connection, args.transaction_flags, &package_ids)
        .await
        .context("PackageKit install failed")?;

    println!(
        "Installed packages via PackageKit: {}",
        package_ids.join(", ")
    );

    Ok(())
}

async fn create_transaction(connection: &Connection) -> Result<zbus::zvariant::OwnedObjectPath> {
    let proxy = Proxy::new(
        connection,
        "org.freedesktop.PackageKit",
        "/org/freedesktop/PackageKit",
        "org.freedesktop.PackageKit",
    )
    .await?;

    let path: zbus::zvariant::OwnedObjectPath = proxy.call("CreateTransaction", &()).await?;
    Ok(path)
}

async fn resolve_packages(
    connection: &Connection,
    filters: u64,
    packages: &[String],
) -> Result<Vec<String>> {
    let tx_path = create_transaction(connection).await?;
    let tx_proxy = Proxy::new(
        connection,
        "org.freedesktop.PackageKit",
        &tx_path,
        "org.freedesktop.PackageKit.Transaction",
    )
    .await?;

    let mut package_stream = tx_proxy.receive_signal("Package").await?;
    let mut finished_stream = tx_proxy.receive_signal("Finished").await?;

    let _: () = tx_proxy
        .call("Resolve", &(filters, packages.to_vec()))
        .await?;

    let mut resolved = Vec::new();

    loop {
        tokio::select! {
            Some(signal) = package_stream.next() => {
                if let Ok((_, package_id, _)) = signal.body().deserialize::<(u32, String, String)>() {
                    resolved.push(package_id);
                }
            }
            Some(_) = finished_stream.next() => {
                break;
            }
        }
    }

    resolved.sort();
    resolved.dedup();
    Ok(resolved)
}

async fn install_packages(
    connection: &Connection,
    flags: u64,
    package_ids: &[String],
) -> Result<()> {
    let tx_path = create_transaction(connection).await?;
    let tx_proxy = Proxy::new(
        connection,
        "org.freedesktop.PackageKit",
        &tx_path,
        "org.freedesktop.PackageKit.Transaction",
    )
    .await?;

    let mut finished_stream = tx_proxy.receive_signal("Finished").await?;

    let _: () = tx_proxy
        .call("InstallPackages", &(flags, package_ids.to_vec()))
        .await?;

    // Wait for installation to complete
    if let Some(signal) = finished_stream.next().await {
        if let Ok((exit_code, _runtime)) = signal.body().deserialize::<(u32, u32)>() {
            if exit_code != 1 {
                // 1 = PK_EXIT_ENUM_SUCCESS
                anyhow::bail!("Package installation failed with exit code: {}", exit_code);
            }
        }
    }

    Ok(())
}
